# Baku personnel inquiry: a duplicated-block reconstruction

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p185 B contains a conditional reading of an inquiry about the fate of
army personnel in **Baku**, addressed through General von Kress in Tiflis.
The printed body has **279 slots** against an advertised **268**, including
an exact repeated ten-coordinate block. The reconstruction excludes one
occurrence of that block and one further coordinate. Its readable wording
requires **10 observed-coordinate substitutions** and **1 source-mask fill**
in addition to the **11 excluded observed coordinates**.

The unchanged published **Nov13–15a** key fixes **125/134 raw positions** in
the stated frame. The edited output fixes **129/134** and preserves five
unknown reference positions. Two equally priced frame alternatives give the
same displayed words but different relations among those unknown labels;
both remain part of the result. Period-key recovery retains the published
credit to George Lasry and collaborators.


**Reviewed source crops:** [p185_B_reviewed.png](../../experiments/baku_personnel_inquiry/sources/p185_B_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).
## p185 B

[Reviewed source image — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/baku_personnel_inquiry/inputs.json).

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — literal header:**

```text
B) NKJ v LP (07.57 p.m., November 13th)
FUER COS
SS GENERAL V KRESS TIFLIS 19.59 (13/11)
RICHI-268
```

</details>

The source's final row is:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — final row, excerpt:**

```text
GGDAX XFVVF DXXVG XFVVF DXXVG VDDXA FXAVV DXXD
```

</details>

The two identical **`XFVVF DXXVG`** blocks occupy source ranges **245–254**
and **255–264**, using zero-based indices. They remain in the complete
literal transcription. The primary 268-slot model excludes the first block
and the final D at source index **278**. No visible cancellation or free OCR
correction is claimed. The full native 279-slot decode and its unpaired
coordinate remain in the certificate.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 268-slot frame after the eleven-coordinate exclusion; 125/134 fixed positions:**

```text
FU?KUNFTXUEBERXSCHICKSALXHEIRESANGEHOERIGERXJNX?AKUXERBET?NXKRIEGSMINISTERIUMXABTGILUNGXFUERXVNRBDENDENEXHEEREXNR????STRIC?A?XGEHXAXWX
```

**Edited output — same conditional frame; ten observed-coordinate substitutions and one source-mask fill; 129/134 fixed positions:**

```text
AUSKUNFTXUEBERXSCHICKSALXHEERESANGEHOERIGERXINXBAKUXERBETENXKRIEGSMINISTERIUMXABTEILUNGXFUERXVERBUENDETEXHEEREXNR????STRICHA?XGEHXAXWX
```

</details>

The observed substitutions, in zero-based source coordinates, are
**74 V→X**, **90 X→D**, **92 G→A**, **94 D→F**, **112 A→X**, **136 A→X**,
**138 X→F**, **139 F→X**, **143 F→V**, and **274 V→X**. The literal invalid
**E** in `XGVEX`, at source index **228**, is masked in the raw frame and
filled with **F** in the proposal. These changes are additional to the
source exclusions and do not assign a missing square cell.

**Readable German — complete edited stream under the conditional frame:**

> Auskunft ueber Schicksal Heeresangehoeriger in Baku erbeten. Kriegsministerium, Abteilung fuer verbuendete Heere. Nr ????STRICHA?. Geh. A W.

The proposed text requests information; it does not explain what happened
to those people or identify particular individuals. **`????STRICHA?`**
remains literal. `STRICH` is a decoded word proposal, not a display instruction
to replace that substring by punctuation. `A W` and the reference's A are
not expanded into names or offices.

## Competing exclusions and reference relations

The verifier compares both possible exclusions of the identical printed
ten-coordinate block, followed by **each of the 269 remaining source
coordinates** as the additional exclusion. That is **538 labelled source
maps**, with overlap between the two duplicate-block branches; it is not
538 independent historical observations.

For the stated letter pattern, with its five question marks left as
wildcards, the minimum is **10 observed-coordinate substitutions**. It is
attained by precisely six maps:

| Removed ten-coordinate block starts at | Additional excluded source index | Distinct retained frame |
|---:|---:|---|
| 245 or 255 | 276 or 277 | The two adjacent X choices give one retained stream |
| 245 or 255 | 278 | Excluding the final D gives a second retained stream |

All six maps give the same displayed raw and edited text. They do **not**
give the same square-cell relations for the unknown reference. In the table
below, Greek letters name unknown values; they are not inserted plaintext.

| Additional exclusion | Linked reference pattern | Unknown cells |
|---|---|---|
| Source 276 or 277 | `α β γ α STRICH A δ` | `α=GG`, `β=DX`, `γ=GX`, `δ=GD` |
| Source 278 | `α β γ α STRICH A γ` | `α=GG`, `β=DX`, `γ=GX` |

Each of these cells has the domain **`0123456789QY`** under the published
partial square. Repeated use of one cell has one shared value; distinct
cells must receive distinct values. In particular, the last unknown is
equal to the third unknown in the second frame but distinct from it in the
first. The current evidence does not choose between them.

The minimum-cost statement is confined to one declared letter pattern and
the duplicated-block-plus-one-exclusion family. It does not prove unique
historical wording, identify the damage mechanism, or justify deleting any
other source coordinates without a new account.

## Evidence and verification

[Inputs](../../experiments/baku_personnel_inquiry/inputs.json) ·
[Certificates](../../experiments/baku_personnel_inquiry/certificates.json) ·
[Reproduction notes](../../experiments/baku_personnel_inquiry/README.md).

```sh
python experiments/baku_personnel_inquiry/verify.py --verify
python experiments/baku_personnel_inquiry/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
```

The optional PDF check reproduces the inspected crop and compares its
pixels. The verifier checks the literal duplicate, every source exclusion,
independent coordinate costs for all 538 labelled maps, both surviving
reference relations, complete readable-label preservation and exact
re-encryption with globally injective square-completion witnesses. Those
completion witnesses are explicitly nonhistorical. Earlier OCR and its
unchanged-key output remain separate from the present source reconstruction;
no universal first-decipherment priority is asserted.

# Caucasus ammunition: a request for loading instructions

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

The native p102 C frame asks whether ammunition still held at the reporting location should be loaded for the destination. The quantity is the literal **5280625** under the published Nov1–3 key. This source edition resolves three unknown labels in the earlier OCR reading; it uses no coordinate repair.

Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Source: J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed p102 (PDF page105). The Nov1–3 square and column ranks are the published key credited to George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker. Earlier OCR bodies are retained in [prior evidence](../../experiments/nov1_ammunition_and_leave/prior_evidence.json); this is not a claim of first historical body recovery.

## p102 C

### Source and frame

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — literal cleartext header:**

```text
C) POT v NKJ (1.00 a.m., November 3rd)
DEUTSCHE DELEG KAUK 1622 (1)
RICHI-262
```

</details>

The [full page](../../experiments/nov1_ammunition_and_leave/sources/p102_full.png) and [native C/D detail](../../experiments/nov1_ammunition_and_leave/sources/p102_C_D_detail.png) show all 262 coordinates, matching the advertised length. The source frame contains no masks, added slots or excluded coordinates.

| Layer | Fixed plaintext positions | Observed substitutions | Source fills | Added / excluded coordinates |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Raw output, native 262-coordinate frame | 131 / 131 | 0 | 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Edited output | Same as raw | 0 | 0 | 0 / 0 |

### Raw output

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — published Nov1–3 key, native source frame:**

```text
ZUDORTASRM1NR2078XLAGERNHIERNOCH5280625RUSSXISXDRAHTETOBMUNXNACHDORTVERLADENWERDENSOLLXMUVVERMITTLXSTELLESUEDOSTNR6829HITTMERXHPTMX
```

</details>

### Readable German

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation only; umlauts display their literal two-letter equivalents:**

> Zu dort. A. S. R. M. 1 Nr. 2078. Lagern hier noch 5280625 russ. I. S. Drahtet, ob Mun. nach dort verladen werden soll. M. U. V. Vermittl. Stelle Südost Nr. 6829. Hittmer, Hptm.

`ASRM1`, `RUSSXIS`, and `MUV` are retained literally. The readable display separates their letters but does not expand these abbreviations or identify an ammunition type. It does not insert thousands separators into `5280625`. The references `2078` and `6829`, and the signature `HITTMER`, require no digit or letter repair. No external identity is assigned to Hittmer.

The earlier OCR had coordinate masks at source indices 3, 12 and 256. Native inspection reads `G`, `D` and `G` there. These restore the missing labels in `52?0625`, `WERDE?` and `H?TTMER`. They are corrections to the earlier OCR transcription, not historical ciphertext fills.

### Evidence and limits

The [input transcription](../../experiments/nov1_ammunition_and_leave/inputs.json) preserves every source row, the published key and the exact readable display. The [certificate](../../experiments/nov1_ammunition_and_leave/certificates.json) maps each plaintext position to its two source coordinates, preserves all numeral labels, and checks every non-`X` label in the displayed German. The [standalone verifier](../../experiments/nov1_ammunition_and_leave/verify.py) re-encrypts the native plaintext to the full observed ciphertext. Its optional PDF mode also reproduces the source images exactly.

No historical inference changes the source, key, numerals or personal-name spellings. Punctuation and abbreviation segmentation are editorial choices, so grammatical attachment and full abbreviations may remain uncertain even when all cipher labels are fixed.

# Caucasus delegation and radio transmitters at Tiflis

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p88 A1/A2, PDF p91, form the two-part message headed
`NKJ v LP (05.56 a.m., November 2nd)` and
`FUER COS SSD BLITZ GR H Q 1330 (1.11) 2 TEILE`. Both parts use the
unchanged published **Nov1–3** key. The message discusses tube radio
transmitters at Tiflis and General von Kress. It does not establish that
the proposed transport actually took place.

## p88 A1

The [first-part crop](../../experiments/caucasus_radio_transmitters/sources/p88_A1.png)
contains **172 visible slots**, matching `1 TL RICHI-172`. Source slot
**57** contains a printed **Q** in `DVQXX`. It is masked as one invalid
coordinate, with no change to the frame.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — native 172-coordinate frame:**

```text
DTSCHEKAUKASDELEGAXER?TTETRANSPORRTX800WATTROEHRENSENDTIFLISZURTAFUNKBERLINVERANLASSEN
```

</details>

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation, with the malformed words retained:**

> Dtsche. Kaukas. Delega. ER?TTE TRANSPORRT, 800 Watt Röhrensend.
> Tiflis zur TAFUNK Berlin veranlassen.

The verb-like field is incomplete. The message nevertheless preserves
`800 WATT ROEHRENSEND`, `TIFLIS`, `BERLIN` and `VERANLASSEN` directly.
**ZURTAFUNK** is displayed as “zur TAFUNK”; no institutional expansion of
TAFUNK is claimed.

The unknown plaintext position **21** has domain **248CIM**, not every
letter. Supplying an apparently obvious B would also require a change to
its other, observed coordinate. More broadly, normalizing the whole field
to `ERBITTETRANSPORT` requires **20 observed-coordinate substitutions plus
one fill** in this native frame. That expensive editorial possibility is
certified separately and **not adopted**. The main reading retains
**85 / 86 fixed positions**, including the doubled R in `TRANSPORRT`.

## p88 A2

The [second-part crop](../../experiments/caucasus_radio_transmitters/sources/p88_A2.png)
contains **134 visible slots**, matching `2 TL RICHI-134`. Source **53**
is a [y-like non-coordinate glyph](../../experiments/caucasus_radio_transmitters/sources/p88_A2_y_glyph.png),
recorded as Y in the literal transcript and masked without deleting it.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 134-coordinate typed frame:**

```text
UOBER1500WETTDOEHRENSENDVERFUEGTG?NERALVONKRESSXNACHCHEFRM4BX49523X
```

**Edited output — three observed-coordinate substitutions and one invalid-glyph fill:**

```text
UEBER1500WATTROEHRENSENDVERFUEGTGENERALVONKRESSXNACHCHEFRM4BX49523X
```

</details>

The changes are source **22 A→V**, **37 G→D**, **107 V→X**, and the
fill **53 Y→V**. The first three repair `UOBER`, `DOEHREN` and `WETT`;
the fill supplies E in `GENERAL`. The edited stream fixes **67 / 67
positions** and re-encrypts exactly.

**Readable German — spacing, punctuation and umlauts:**

> Über 1500 Watt Röhrensend. verfügt General von Kress.
> Nach Chef RM. 4. B. 49523.

The power, name and reference retain their literal values. No independent
biographical identity or expansion of the reference is inferred.

## Conditional interpretation and the supralinear source layer

The scan contains [four marks above typed coordinates](../../experiments/caucasus_radio_transmitters/sources/p88_A2_annotations.png).
Their author, date and purpose are unknown. Interpreting each as a
replacement of the aligned typed glyph gives the following independently
reproducible effects; all indices are zero-based.

| Source slot | Typed → aligned mark | Plaintext effect when applied alone |
|---|---|---|
| 107 | V → X | Position 10: `WETT` → `WATT` |
| 115 | G → F | Position 23: `SEND` → `SEN0` |
| 116 | F → A | Position 32: `G?NERAL` → `0?NERAL` |
| 119 | X → V | Position 61: `49523` → `M9523` |

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — all four aligned replacements, with the same native frame:**

```text
UOBER1500WATTDOEHRENSEN0VERFUEGT0?NERALVONKRESSXNACHCHEFRM4BXM9523X
```

</details>

The certificate retains **all 16 combinations** of these four source
choices. The primary edited candidate uses only the first annotation;
the other three effects are kept as source evidence rather than silently
accepted or suppressed. They are variants of the same physical A2
record, not extra recovered messages. No numerical relabeling follows.

Across both parts there are **306 visible slots**, **304 valid source
coordinates**, and **153 plaintext positions**. The typed layer fixes
**151 / 153** positions; the conservative edited layer fixes **152 / 153**.
The summary counts only three observed substitutions and one fill, with
one invalid source glyph still unresolved. It excludes the expensive A1
normalization and the alternative annotation layers. Six full A1
completion witnesses demonstrate the remaining ambiguity without naming
one as the historical text.

Both bodies already appeared in earlier unreviewed repository candidates.
Published key credit and the bounded prior-paper/comment check are kept
explicitly; this edition makes no historical first-solution claim. See
[inputs](../../experiments/caucasus_radio_transmitters/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/caucasus_radio_transmitters/certificates.json)
and [verification instructions](../../experiments/caucasus_radio_transmitters/README.md).

# Falkenhausen followup: a surviving second-part ending

[Case index](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

## p86 B2

**Status:** 39/39 native raw positions fixed; 0 coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills. No frame change.

**Source and dates:** Page heading: 31st OCTOBER, 1918; B) POT, COS v NKJ (9.00 p.m., October 31st); 2 TL RICHI-78.

![Source p86 B2](../../experiments/oct31_armistice_and_followup/sources/p86_B2.png)

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FOLGENBALMOEGLIHSTXFALKENHAUSENX8274X18
```

</details>

**Readable German — the same candidate labels with spacing and punctuation:**

> Folgen BAL MOEGLIHST. Falkenhausen. 8274 / 18.

**Meaning:** The surviving ending appears to promise that something will follow as soon as possible, with Falkenhausen and reference 8274/18. The subject of folgen is not present in this part. The literal defective words BAL and MOEGLIHST are preserved; the interpretation as bald moeglichst is not an additional cryptographic recovery.

**Conditional interpretation and source details:** All 78 received coordinates decode directly. The first part has not been identified here. No missing D or C is inserted to normalize BAL MOEGLIHST, and no link to the neighboring food dispatch is asserted.

### Explicit source changes

No source-coordinate substitution or source-mask fill is used.

### Reproducibility and attribution

The [input](../../experiments/oct31_armistice_and_followup/inputs.json) binds each literal source to exact PDF crops. The [certificate](../../experiments/oct31_armistice_and_followup/certificates.json) contains the raw paired-coordinate domains, each source change and the forward checks. The [verifier](../../experiments/oct31_armistice_and_followup/verify.py) checks the unchanged published keys and the live German quotations, retaining all numerical and letter labels.

Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro (2026). Childs supplies the historical collection; published reconstruction and key provenance credit Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker. Earlier repository OCR and body readings are retained in the [attribution record](../../experiments/oct31_armistice_and_followup/prior_candidates.json).

# Oil stocks and production: the Nobel and Hagelin message

**Prior body and interpretation:** George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal
and Arno Wacker, *Deciphering ADFGVX messages from the Eastern Front of
World War I* (2016), **§6.6 and Table 5**, author PDF pp25–26,
[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461). · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Current source edition and exact repair audit: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The paper already publishes this complete two-part oil inquiry and
discusses the Hagelin name. This case supplies its literal source frames,
quantified repairs and qualification of marked or faded characters.
It is not a first-decipherment or new personal-identification claim.

Childs printed p64 A, PDF p67, is headed
`--- v NKJ (3.23 a.m., October 5th)` and **Beginning lost**. Its first
surviving body has length 346 and no printed part number; this edition
calls it A1. The following body explicitly says `2 TL / RICHI-354`.
Both native lengths agree with their headers and use the unchanged
published **Oct4–6** key.

## p64 A1

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 346-coordinate frame:**

```text
HP?MXBENEDIKTXVERTRETERKUKAOKXINATORXATOMXXERSUCHEDRINGENEZUSTELLUNGFOLGENDENTELEGRXUXVERANLASSUNGDASSANTWXTELEGRXANHERUEBYRMITTELTWIRDXXGEBRSEDERNOBELXATOMXXDRAHTETVOURAETE
```

**Edited output — four observed-coordinate substitutions and one
printed-dash fill:**

```text
HPTMXBENEDIKTXVERTRETERKUKAOKXINATOMXATOMXXERSUCHEDRINGENEZUSTELLUNGFOLGENDENTELEGRXUXVERANLASSUNGDASSANTWXTELEGRXANHERUEBERMITTELTWIRDXXGEBRUEDERNOBELXATOMXXDRAHTETVORRAETE
```

</details>

**Readable German — spacing, punctuation and the two bracketed
editorial expansions noted below:**

> [Hauptmann] Benedikt, Vertreter k.u.k. A.O.K. in Atom. Atom. Ersuche
> [dringende] Zustellung folgenden Telegr. u. Veranlassung, dass Antw.
> telegr. anher übermittelt wird. Gebrüder Nobel, Atom: Drahtet Vorräte …

`HPTM` is expanded in brackets. The bracketed **dringende** is a
grammatical normalization of the exact stream's **DRINGENE**; the
additional D is not claimed as a recovered encoded character. The
ellipsis means that the source message continues in A2 below. The
repeated `ATOM` remains visible and is not replaced with another place.

The [source crop](../../experiments/p64_oil_and_radio/sources/p64_A1.png)
has one printed dash. Three faded right-edge glyphs have primary readings
V, X and F, documented in an enlarged crop. A separate variant masks
those three readings and quantifies the resulting uncertainty. It does
not change the accepted transcript or conceal a length adjustment.

## p64 A2

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 354-coordinate frame, including both parenthesized
X coordinates:**

```text
NAPHTAXPRODUKTIONSAEMTLICHERSORTENBEIUNSUND6NDERENFIRMENATOMXFERNERWIEVIELBISJETZTGELIEFERTXDIEUELBENDATEQBETREFFENNQVOROSSISKFALLSSOLCHEIHNENBEKANNTXHAGELINXXXLSTARMEEOXQU12059
```

**Edited output — five observed-coordinate substitutions:**

```text
NAPHTAXPRODUKTIONSAEMTLICHERSORTENBEIUNSUNDANDERENFIRMENATOMXFERNERWIEVIELBISJETZTGELIEFERTXDIESELBENDATENBETREFFENNOVOROSSISKFALLSSOLCHEIHNENBEKANNTXHAGELINXXXOSTARMEEOXQU12059
```

</details>

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation of that candidate:**

> Naphta-Produktion sämtlicher Sorten bei uns und anderen Firmen Atom.
> Ferner, wieviel bis jetzt geliefert. Dieselben Daten betreffen
> Novorossisk, falls solche Ihnen bekannt. Hagelin. Ostarmee O. Qu. 12059.

The native word **BETREFFEN** remains. The paper's table prints
**BETREFFEND**; its extra D is not inserted into this exact stream.
The inquiry seeks oil-related figures rather than reporting actual
stock or delivery amounts. The reference number is qualified below.

The name **HAGELIN** is directly present in the raw reading. Lasry and
colleagues propose Karl Wilhelm Hagelin and also note uncertainty about
the name's role in the message. This edition does not independently
identify the person or determine who authored the quoted request.

## Parentheses and the reference number

The [source](../../experiments/p64_oil_and_radio/sources/p64_A2.png)
prints **`(X)XVVG`** and **`GFD(X)`**. Those marked X values occupy
source coordinates **90** and **353**. They count as one coordinate
each; the qualification punctuation is retained in the literal rows.

The primary edition accepts both printed X values. Its word repair
changes source 90 from X to A. If this marked coordinate is instead
treated as unknown, that same change is a mask fill and the remaining
observed-substitution count is four. Both prices are recorded.

**Conditional interpretation — the final reference:** The `5` in
`12059` depends on the parenthesized X at source 353. Masking it leaves
the field **`120?9`**, whose unknown has domain **57DSTU**. Requiring a
decimal reference would leave **12059 or 12079**. That field-type
assumption does not choose one, and the sensitivity edition does not
silently retain the primary 5. Every complete coordinate alternative
has an exact re-encryption witness.

## Exact scope

The two parts have **700 source slots**, **699 valid coordinates**, and
**350 plaintext positions**. The primary raw readings fix **349 / 350**
positions; the edited candidates fix **350 / 350**, with **nine
observed-coordinate substitutions and one printed-dash fill**. There
is no insertion, deletion, group movement or key change. The source
qualification variants are not additional physical records.

[Inputs](../../experiments/p64_oil_and_radio/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/p64_oil_and_radio/certificates.json)
and [verification instructions](../../experiments/p64_oil_and_radio/README.md)
preserve every printed row, coordinate price, alternative domain and
prior attribution.

# October Caucasus traffic — Kress, Westernhagen and a shipment for Poti

[All readings](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Source and verification](../../experiments/october_caucasus/README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and repair analysis:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. **Earlier key:** the published October 4–6 square and 22-column transposition, credited to Childs and George Lasry / Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker in the [key catalogue](../../data/keys.json).

Twelve source records cover seven exchanges about the Caucasus: personnel and money for Kress's delegation, price instructions to Westernhagen, electrical equipment sent to Tiflis, a cargo leaving Braila for Poti, radio timings, a liaison officer and equipment procurement. The p68 procurement pair has a **provisional, heavily repaired first part and a partially extended second part**; it is not a direct recovery of the complete exchange. Another interrupted continuation is retained separately without an accepted reading. The German readings below use explicit editorial repairs. Every received coordinate, surviving garble, ambiguous layout and repair cost is retained in the [certificate](../../experiments/october_caucasus/certificates.json). This is a new reproducible edition in this repository, without a first-historical-decipherment claim.

**Display notes:** The German readings use the stated edited witnesses. Square brackets identify a supplied spelling, a proposed value or an explicitly described unresolved passage; the nearby record notes give the category. Uninterpreted literal fields are shown in code, not promoted to names or quantities. A bracketed whole value does not mean that all its characters are unknown.

## p72 A — Reinforcements, administrative personnel and money for Kress

**Source:** printed p. 72 / PDF p. 75, section A, three parts. `COS v OSM (--------, October 9th); NR 294 KRESS (6) 2040 3 TLE`. The heading is **6 October 1918**. The clear route is OSM to COS, with Kress named in the header; it does not make Kress the sender.

### Most likely readable German

**Readable German:**

> Zu Tel. 30.9. `NATEKS` Nr. 8557. 1. Verstärkung der Deleg. von O.H.L. ohne Beteiligung [des] K.M. angeordnet. 2. Mit Bericht vom 8.[?], `4A` Nr. 553 angeford. Verw.-Pers. wird mit Ausnahme der Garnison-Verw.-Beamten — vergl. Tel. 26.[?], [unresolved reference] — zur Verfügung gestellt werden. 3. Notwendiges Geld ist sichergestellt.

**Meaning:** Reinforcement of the delegation has been ordered by Supreme Army Command, without the participation of the office denoted literally by `K.M.`, under the separately priced article completion below. Requested administrative personnel will be made available, except for garrison-administration officials. Necessary money has been secured.

`Deleg.`, `O.H.L.`, `Verw.-Pers.` and `Garnison-Verw.-Beamten` are expanded only in the explanation. The reference text `NATEKS` and several dates and numbers remain unresolved. The article completion below reads raw `X?S` as `DES` before literal `K.M.`; it does not identify a particular ministry or assign the damaged reference digits.

### What the three source parts preserve

| Part | Literal / interpreted coordinates | Fixed raw positions | Source issue | Additional editorial cost |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| A1 | 203 / 178 | 88/89 | The second copy of an identical 25-coordinate run is visibly struck out. | Earlier: 1 substitution, no fill; with conditional article: 2 substitutions, 1 fill |
| A2 | 251 / 226 | 108/113 common to both models; 109/113 in one model | An unmarked 25-slot near-repeat; two deletion alternatives remain. | 6 substitutions; 1 or 2 asserted fills |
| A3 | 124 / 124 | 60/62 | Two invalid/missing source coordinates; unchanged geometry | 4 substitutions; 2 fills |

The A1 strikeout is a source instruction. The A2 deletion is a reconstruction hypothesis: its adjacent copies differ only by a printed `X` versus a non-coordinate `S`. Removing either copy gives the same raw text except for `GARNISON` versus `G?RNISON`. Both are kept; the latter does not become an independently witnessed `A`.

The raw core is already recognizable as `VERSTAER1UNGDERDELEGXVONOXHXLXOHNEBETEILIGUNG...ANGEORDNET`, and A3 directly contains `ZURVERFUEGUN...GESTELLT...` and most of `NOTWENDIGESGELDISTSICHERGESTELLT`. The stated costs account for making those words readable; the uncorrected strings remain in the certificate.

### Conditional article before K.M.

The unchanged inverse ends `OHNEBETEILIGUNGX?SKXMXANGEORDNET`.
A grammatical proposal reads `X?S` as **DES**: “ohne Beteiligung des K.M.
angeordnet”. It adds no plaintext position and changes no source frame.
The source still has D at coordinate 136 and the invalid printed U at 185;
neither glyph is silently retranscribed.

| Plaintext index | Raw pair / label | Proposed label | Additional source operation |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 72 | `GD` / X | D (`GG`) | source 136 D → G; one observed substitution |
| 73 | `F?` / domain `1EKLOS` | E (`FA`) | source 185 U → A; one invalid-glyph fill |

The 88/89 raw count is unchanged. Including the existing `VERSTAERKUNG`
repair, the conditional first-part layer has **89/89 positions**, at
**two observed-coordinate substitutions and one mask fill**. The printed
25-coordinate strikeout and published key remain exactly as before.

**Readable German — conditional article bracketed, abbreviations retained:**

> Zu Tel. 30.9. NATEKS Nr. 8557. 1. Verstaerkung der Deleg. von O.H.L. ohne Beteiligung [des] K.M. angeordnet.

<details>
<summary>Complete conditional first-part machine string</summary>

**Edited output — the existing word repair plus one observed substitution and one invalid-glyph fill for DES:**

```text
ZUTELX30X9XNATEKSNRX8557X1XVERSTAERKUNGDERDELEGXVONOXHXLXOHNEBETEILIGUNGDESKXMXANGEORDNET
```

</details>

The [extension certificate](../../experiments/p72_article_completion/README.md)
prices all 216 combinations of the first label and the six source-compatible
second labels. **Sixty** have the same one-additional-substitution cost as
`DE`. The grammar motivates this proposal; the cipher does not make it
unique. `K.M.`, `NATEKS`, `8557` and the reference date remain literal, and
no institution or separate received copy is asserted.

## p70 A — Westernhagen, price limits and an urgent return

**Source:** printed p. 70 / PDF p. 73, section A, two parts. `POT, COS v NKJ (3.10 a.m., October 7th); FUR COS DEUTSCHE DELEGATO WIRTCHI ABTLG 2305 (6) 2 TLE`.

### Most likely readable German

**Readable German:**

> An Westernhagen. Bestätigen Telegr. 28.9. Euer früheres Telegr. nicht erhalten. Da von euch ohne Bericht und Kenntnis dortiger Marktlage gelassen, können Preisgrenzen nicht aufgeben. Mdl. Rücksprache sofort erforderlich. Bitten Rück[k]ehr beschleunigen. Drahten Gleiches über ASTO Constanza. Bestätigt Empfang. Deutkauf.

**Meaning:** A telegram of 28 September is acknowledged, but an earlier one was not received. Without the requested report or knowledge of local market conditions, the sender cannot give price limits. An immediate personal discussion is needed; Westernhagen is asked to hasten his return. The same instruction is being telegraphed via `ASTO Constanza`, and receipt is to be acknowledged.

The source names only **Westernhagen**. `MDL` is interpreted as *mündliche*; `ASTO` and the signature `DEUTKAUF` are retained without an institutional expansion. The encrypted spelling is `RUECKEHR` with one `K`; ordinary German spelling in the displayed reading supplies the second `k` as a prose normalization. The unusual but directly decoded `AUFGEBEN` remains; the edition does not silently substitute a more idiomatic verb.

| Part | Literal / interpreted coordinates | Fixed raw positions | Source issue | Additional editorial cost |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| A1 | 332 / 322 | 156/161 | Two separate identical five-coordinate pairs: `AAAAA AAAAA` and `DAAGG DAAGG` | 7 substitutions; 5 fills |
| A2 | 246 / 246 | 121/123 | Header says `RICHI-256`; the printed 246-slot body decodes at its actual length | 4 substitutions; 2 fills |

Removing one copy of each repeated A1 group gives four source-index aliases and **one identical 322-coordinate stream**. Those deletions are conditional, despite the visible repetition. A2 is not padded by ten invented coordinates to force its length to match the header: its raw reading already begins `MDLXRUECKSPRACHEDOFORTERFORDERLICH...` and ends `...EMPFANGXDEUTKAUF` at 246 slots.

## p71 A1 — Electrical equipment sent to Tiflis

**Source:** printed p. 71 / PDF p. 74, section A, first of two parts. `POT v OSM (01.17 a.m., October 8th); FUR COS (6) 1230 2 TEILE; 1 TL RICHI-170`. The page heading is **6 October 1918**.

### Most likely readable German

**Readable German:**

> Nach Tiflis abgegangen 28.9., mit 2 Begleiter: 2 Stück 16-kW-Maschinensätze und 1 [20]-kW-Umformer.

**Meaning:** Two machine sets rated at 16 kW and one converter, provisionally read as rated at 20 kW, were dispatched to Tiflis on 28 September with two accompanying people. The directly decoded telegraphic form is `BEGLEITER`; no grammatical final `N` is inserted into the cipher edition.

The literal **170 slots** have unchanged geometry and fix **72/85 raw positions**. Twelve printed dashes and one damaged `C`-shaped glyph in row one's last group are treated as erasures. That glyph may be an incomplete `G`, but the raw letter domain remains open. The proposed reading fills all **13 erasures** and changes **one known coordinate**, source slot 40 from `G` to `X`, to repair the raw `GEGA?BEN` fragment to `GEGANGEN`. All slot and plaintext positions in the certificate are zero-based.

The two equipment counts, the **16-kW** rating, and the date digits `28` and `9` survive directly. The **2** in the proposed **20-kW** rating is an erasure fill, so the exact second rating is conditional. The raw ending is `...UND1??0KX?XUMFORMER`, not a fully recovered numerical specification.

Part A2 advertises **192 coordinates** but stops after **85**, followed by the printed note `(interference)`. Under the simple hypothesis that the lost suffix supplies the remaining 107 slots, no complete plaintext letter is fixed: each surviving symbol supplies only one side of a coordinate pair. Its literal fragment and conditional letter domains are preserved separately. A [conditional partial edition](../radio/p71_dc_machines_fragment.md) now proposes a 47-position technical clause with 51 added-slot fills and no observed-coordinate substitutions. Both SCHALTEN and ERHALTEN alternatives remain compatible; the other 49 positions are unread. This proposal does not change the native 0/96 fixed-position count or infer additional equipment specifications.

## p69 B — Violetta's cargo from Braila to Poti

**Source:** printed p. 69 / PDF p. 72, section B, two parts. `COS v NKJ (---- October 11th); NR 298 FUR COS HPTM GEMOLL (6) 2330 2 TLE`. The page heading says **5 October**, while the individual clear header says `(6)`; both are preserved.

### Most likely readable German

**Conditional interpretation — readable German with the separately bracketed cargo/date hypotheses:**

> Ab Braila [4.10.] mit D. Violetta: [10 000] Eierhandgranaten, 3 Wagen Masch.-Gew., `04WLI` russ. Gew., 9 Wag. Mun., `94TS6` Lebensmittel, 16 Faß Benzin, 2 Kisten Kuriergepäck, 10 Wag. Mun. für Mun.-Dep. Poti und mehrere Wag. für dort. Truppen.

**Meaning:** A cargo sent from Braila aboard the vessel *Violetta* includes hand grenades, machine guns, Russian rifles, ammunition, food, petrol and courier luggage. Poti's ammunition depot and troops there are named as destinations. Two damaged quantity fields are unresolved. The proposed **10 000** hand grenades is also conditional: the common raw reading is `100?0`, and the fourth digit depends on the declared alignment and an erased-coordinate fill. It is not an independently established exact quantity.

The displayed **4.10.** date and several words are editorial repairs. `04WLI` and `94TS6` are raw garbles, not accepted quantities; no numerical expansion is supplied for them. `D.`, `Masch.-Gew.`, `russ. Gew.`, `Wag.` and `Mun.-Dep.` are interpreted in their cargo context. The text does not independently establish the ship's registry or the nature of the wagons carried.

| Part | Literal / interpreted coordinates | Raw positions fixed across every tested placement | Source issue | Minimum additional editorial cost |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| B1 | 329 / 330 | 159/165 | Four-letter group `VXFX`; insert one erased slot at any of its five boundaries | 9 substitutions; 2 fills |
| B2 | 65 / 66 | 28/33 | Four-letter group `(X)FFF`; insert one erased slot at any of its five boundaries | 1 substitution; 1 fill |

These models supply a slot because a printed group is short and the header is one longer. They do not prove that the historical loss occurred there. In B1 the editorial template has two tied minimum-cost placements. In B2, the proposed complete continuation is

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — conditional missing-slot frame for the short printed group:**

```text
UNDMEHREREWAGXFUERDORTXTRUPPENXXX
```

</details>

It replaces the short printed `XFFF` by `GDFFF`: either insert `G` before the printed `X` and change that `X` to `D`, or change `X` to `G` and insert `D` after it. Both have exactly one known-coordinate substitution and one missing-coordinate fill. All five within-group placements, including the more expensive ones, remain in the certificate.

## p72 B — Radio timings and reception

**Source:** printed p. 72 / PDF p. 75, section B. `POT v OSM (---------, October 9th); FUR POT (6) 0830; RIZI-274`. The source prints `RIZI`; that label is not silently rewritten as `RICHI`.

### Most likely readable German

**Readable German:**

> Zu dort Nr. 479: 20.00, 20.30 für OSM ungeeignet. Sind Sie mit RICHI `M98`, 30.9., mitgeteilten Zeiten einverstanden? Wie ist dort Empfang OSM, Welle 2800 und 3500? Schlee.

**Meaning:** The proposed times are unsuitable for OSM. The recipient is asked whether the previously notified times are acceptable and how OSM is received at two wavelengths.

The unchanged 274-coordinate geometry fixes **136/137 raw positions**. The displayed `NR`, `2000`, `SIE` and `3500` require **four known-coordinate substitutions**, with one additional erased-coordinate fill for `ZU`. The first time and second wavelength are plausible editorial values, not independently recovered numerical facts. `2030`, `2800` and `SCHLEE` are directly decoded; the damaged reference `RICHIM98` is left unresolved.

## p69 A — A liaison officer from Army Group Kiev

**Source:** printed p. 69 / PDF p. 72, section A. `NKJ v --- (---- October 11th); NR 44 0628 (5.10); RICHI-220`. The sender is not identified in the clear header.

### Most likely readable German

**Readable German:**

> Mit Einverständnis O.H.L. wird Rittm. [Tellner], [Tellner], als Verbdgs.-Offz. der Heeresgr. nach Tiflis entsandt. Heergr. Kjew.

**Meaning:** With Supreme Army Command's approval, a cavalry captain is being sent to Tiflis as the army group's liaison officer. The signature names Army Group Kiev; the cipher's literal spelling is `KJEW`. The two bracketed names are an editorial name reconstruction, not one-position question marks. The damaged surname is repeated and is provisionally read as **Tellner**, without assigning a forename or identifying a person outside the telegram.

The actual body has **220 coordinates**, matching the header. Three parenthesized `X` values are retained as recorded source coordinates, including the final printed run `FDX(X)-X(X)VGX`. Parentheses remain visible in the literal row edition. Removing those annotated letters or treating the ten-slot run as one five-letter group would change the frame.

The literal inverse fixes **109/110 raw positions**:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
MITEINVERSTAEWDNISXOXHXLXWIRDRITTMXTELLNEIXTELLN1RXA?SVERBDGSXXBFZDERHEERELGRXNACHXTIKLCSXEN5SAND6XHEERGRXKJEW
```

</details>

The displayed ordinary words require **10 known-coordinate substitutions and one erased-coordinate fill**. The two raw surname copies, `TELLNEI` and `TELLN1R`, preserve complementary letters: `TELLNER` combines the sixth letter of the first copy with the seventh of the second. That is still an editorial reconstruction, not an independent personnel identification. `RITTM`, `VERBDGS` and `OFFZ` are expanded only in the explanation.

## p68 A — Provisional procurement text carrying CHI labels

**Source:** printed p. 68 / PDF p. 71, section A, two parts. `COS, POT v NKJ (9.19 p.m., October 5th); VON THO 1640 (5) 2 TEILE`. The first part visibly says **CHI-220**. The second says **CHI-186** and then **RICHI-186** on the next line. Those labels are preserved exactly.

The published October 4–6 key gives a recognizable Kress/Tiflis address and equipment vocabulary. This is another warning that the printed `CHI` label alone does not identify the separate key family used by the open/previously open CHI challenges. These parts are not companions under the recovered p153 key.

### Provisional first-part reading

**Readable German:**

> General v. Kress, Tiflis. Zu T-Spruch Nr. [?159; damaged reference]. Betr. Entsendung 2 Offz. nach Tiflis zum Ankauf von Ausrüstungsstücken [continued in part 2]

**Meaning under the proposed repairs:** The message concerns sending two officers to Tiflis to purchase equipment. Its reference number and date cannot be completed responsibly from this edition.

The literal **220-slot** body has **22 coordinate erasures**, including the non-coordinate letters `W` and `K`, and fixes **89/110 raw positions**. Two erased coordinates fall in the same plaintext pair. Its unchanged inverse is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
G?NE??LOKR?SSXTIFL?LXX?1TSP?UC6NR?159F????9XBZTRW?NT?1?DU?G2OFFX0NAUHDTCFSISXZU??XKAUFVONA5SR5?STUNAS?TS?CKENX
```

</details>

The displayed ordinary wording needs **24 known-coordinate substitutions and 17 erased-coordinate fills**. This substantial editorial cost is why the reading remains **provisional**. The `T` in `TSPRUCH` survives directly and is not expanded to an asserted original abbreviation. Five date/reference positions and the first position after `NR` remain unassigned in the proposed template. No precise reference date is supplied.

### Limited second-part continuation

Part 2 has exactly **186 slots**, with **41 coordinate erasures** and **56/93 fixed raw positions**. Its beginning `??DARTILLER??T7QITJO?` supports the provisional continuation:

**Readable German:**

> [continued from part 1] und Artilleriemunition [remaining text unresolved]

The bracketed continuation and unresolved-text notices are display descriptions, not recovered German words or a new gap-length hypothesis. The earlier template asserts only `UNDARTILLERIEMUNITION`, requiring **four known-coordinate substitutions and five erasure fills**. The remaining **72 plaintext positions are unasserted**. The certificate retains their raw domains, and its arbitrary coordinate fillers for a complete arithmetic roundtrip are not promoted to a further sentence, quantity, date or signature.

A [separately priced continuation](../../experiments/p68_procurement_continuation/README.md)
now proposes `DONREGIERUNG`, `DORTEINGE?ANGEN`, `HGRUKIEW` and `ROSTOW`.
Retaining the other raw letters, the earlier opening fixes **61/93 positions**;
the common extension reaches **76/93**, with **one additional observed
substitution and 15 printed-mask fills**. All fifteen newly assigned positions
retain an observed half-coordinate. The wholly missing internal verb letter
admits both `EINGEGANGEN` and `EINGELANGEN` at the same two-fill price, giving
77/93 only under either optional completion. `F??`, the fields `?0` and `1??8`,
and the intervening damaged text remain literal. Native messages attest three
individual words; no complete independent copy of this clause is claimed.

## Relation to the open p73 challenge

These messages add readable traffic from the Kress/Caucasus route, with explicit October origin and later interception dates. They supply neither p73's key nor a matching plaintext passage. **p73 remains open**; the source-level repairs here do not decide between its conflicting 26 October and 8 November date layers.

# October routing, weather and personnel requests

[All cases](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** Four source-reviewed records under the previously published
**Oct4–6 key**, with different levels of certainty. The Sofia record is an
exact reading. The Westernhagen request uses five explicit coordinate repairs.
The weather instruction depends on two unmarked source deletions. The
inspector request is only partially edited; a difficult 21-character expression
remains unassigned. Source review: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Earlier
key credit: **J. Rives Childs, George Lasry, and Lasry–Niebel–Kopal–Wacker**.

The [source package](../../experiments/october_requests/README.md) preserves
842 literal slots, every invalid glyph and header, all coordinate domains,
costed editorial changes and re-encrypted witnesses. No new key or first
historical decipherment is claimed.

## p62 A — Sofia leaves the Ringbahnverkehr

Header: `ASO v LP (04.50 p.m., October 4th); 1030 (4.10); RICHI-124`.
The heading is October 4, 1918. All 62 plaintext positions are directly fixed:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
SOFIAXAUSRINGBAHNVERKEHRAUSGESCHIEDENXXNACHRICHTENCHEF4BX49287
```

</details>

**Readable German:**

> Sofia. Aus Ringbahnverkehr ausgeschieden. Nachrichtenchef 4B. 49287.

The notice says that Sofia has left the `Ringbahnverkehr`. The radio-traffic
context suggests a circuit-service meaning, but an independent contemporary
definition of the term has not been established here. The German token is
therefore retained without a definite technical expansion. The reference
`4BX49287` is literal and is not expanded into an unprinted formation or date.
There is no coordinate substitution, erasure fill or layout change.

The source separately prints `QUITTUNG VON WAU` and `NKJ OSM ASO LP UM`.
These are clear service annotations, outside the encrypted body. They are
preserved without inferring an unprinted acknowledgment time.

Source: [p62 A](../../experiments/october_requests/sources/childs_p62_A.png).

## p65 A — Accelerate Westernhagen's return

Header: `COS v NKJ (3.18 a.m., October 5th); DEUTSCHE DELEGATION 2355 (4/10);
RICHI-260`. The heading is October 4, 1918.

**Readable German — editorial reading:**

> Hptm. v. Westernhagen. [0] Bitten Rückkehr beschleunigen, da über dortige
> Marktlage dringend Bericht benötigen, mit Einkauf beginnen wollen.
> Deutkauf.

The request asks the captain to return sooner because an urgent report on
the local market is needed before purchases begin. The `0` after the
addressee remains the literal source-derived symbol; it is not silently
converted to punctuation. `DEUTKAUF` is retained as the signature token.

The raw 130-character inverse is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
HPTMXVXWESTERNHA5ENX0BITTENRUECLKEHRBESCHLEUNIGENDAUEBERDOUTIGEHARKTLAGEDRINGENDBERICHTBENOETIGENMITEINLAUFBEGINNENWOLLENXDEUTKAUF
```

</details>

Five single-coordinate substitutions give `WESTERNHAGEN`, `RUECKKEHR`,
`DORTIGE`, `MARKTLAGE` and `EINKAUF`. All five printed glyphs were checked
against the scan; they are explicit editorial repairs, not corrected manual
transcription errors. The source independently fixes the rank and `V` before
the surname. The later [p70 A1/A2 request](october_caucasus.md) supplies a
separate Westernhagen surname and market-report witness. No forename or
identity beyond the source is assigned.

| Source index, zero-based | Printed group / character | Coordinate repair | Resulting word |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 132 | 27 / 3 | `X→V` | `RUECKKEHR` |
| 170 | 35 / 1 | `G→F` | `DORTIGE` |
| 202 | 41 / 3 | `G→X` | `WESTERNHAGEN` |
| 222 | 45 / 3 | `X→V` | `EINKAUF` |
| 242 | 49 / 3 | `A→F` | `MARKTLAGE` |

Source: [p65 A](../../experiments/october_requests/sources/childs_p65_A.png).

## p62 B — Date groups before weather-observation telegrams

**Readable German — conditional two-deletion frame; reference field unresolved:**

> Frontwetterwarte. Bitte Obs. Telegr. stets Datumgruppen voranzustellen,
> sonst Meldg. wertlos. FEWEWA?10.

The instruction asks for date groups to precede observation telegrams,
warning that the reports are otherwise worthless. The closing label
`FEWEWA?10` retains one unknown character.

The source is headed `COS v NKJ (03.40 a.m., October 6th); 1540 (5);
RICHI-186`, beneath the October 5 page heading. It contains **188 slots**.
The reading retains the two established conditional layouts: delete either
index 79 or 80, one of the adjacent `FF` across `FFDGF FGAFRG`, and the
final `X` at 187. Both give the same 186-coordinate frame.

### Corrected glyph position and reference uncertainty

The second source group reads **`FVFEF`**, correcting the earlier
transcription `FVEFF`. The printed `E` is at source index **8**, not 7.
Consequently the `L` in `WERTLOS` is directly observed, while the first
character of the closing `?10` is not. The source's `R` in the six-character
`FGAFRG` group remains a separate mask.

The reference unknown has pair `?F` and domain **`018MRV`**. A decimal-only
interpretation still permits **`010`, `110` or `810`**. The previously
printed `FEWEWA110` is one compatible completion; the current edition
leaves the field open. It fixes **92/93 proposed positions**, with two
observed-coordinate substitutions and one mask fill. The conditional raw
frame fixes **91/93**.

<details>
<summary>Raw reading, source changes and layout comparison</summary>

**Raw output — conditional deletion of source 79 or 80, and final source 187:**

```text
FRONTWETTERWARTEXLITTEOBSXTELEGRXSTETKDATUMGRUPPENVORANZUSTELLENSONSTME?DGXWERTLOSXXFEWEWA?10
```

`LITTE→BITTE` changes source 45 from `F` to `G`; `STETK→STETS` changes
157 from `V` to `G`. Filling the `R` mask at 84 with coordinate `F` supplies
the `L` in `MELDG`. The `E` mask at 8 stays unfilled.

| Operation | Original source index | Printed location |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Delete one adjacent `F` | 79 or 80 | Group 16 / 5 or group 17 / 1 |
| Delete final `X` | 187 | Group 38 / 2 |
| `F→G` for `BITTE` | 45 | Group 10 / 1 |
| `V→G` for `STETS` | 157 | Group 32 / 2 |
| Fill literal `R` as coordinate `F` | 84 | Group 17 / 5 |
| Retain literal `E` as an unfilled mask | 8 | Group 2 / 4 |

The verifier checks all **17,578** ways to delete two source slots against
this partial template and the published key. The two layouts above remain
the only minima at two observed substitutions. The source marks neither
deletion. The comparison leaves the reference character unasserted; it
also preserves all six source-compatible completions and their exact
additional one-mask-fill cost.

Printed locations follow the actual six-character group rather than
uniform groups of five. The [input review](../../experiments/october_requests/inputs.json)
retains the earlier transcription and reference proposal.

</details>

Source: [p62 B](../../experiments/october_requests/sources/childs_p62_B.png).

## p63 A — A partially readable inspector request

Header: `LP v NKJ (12.53 p.m., October 6th); 1754 (5.10) POT FÜR OHL AN
DEUTSCHEN FEZDEIRENBAHNCHEF (4.10); RICHI-54`. The heading is October 4, 1918.
The literal spelling `FEZDEIRENBAHNCHEF` is preserved. The body has **54
groups of five slots**, or 270 slots; the source field remains `RICHI-54`.

The raw inverse is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
E?BITTEUEBER?EID5OGJEEINESBESRIEBSUNDVASCHIWNENMECH8ISCHENKONTROLLEWRSGENERALVSNKRESSEINVERSTAODENDEUTSCHEDELXKASKXABTXZXNRX474DG1MOOLX
```

</details>

A limited editorial reading, costing **12 known-coordinate substitutions
and two erasure fills**, is:

**Readable German:**

> Erbitte Übersendung je eines Betriebs- und [21-character technical
> expression unresolved] Kontrolleurs. General von Kress einverstanden.
> Deutsche Del. Kauk. Abt. Z. Nr 474D. Gemoll.

The request concerns inspectors, states Kress's agreement, and carries a
German Caucasus delegation reference. The middle raw span,
`VASCHIWNENMECH8ISCHEN`, suggests a technical qualification, but normalizing
it to `MASCHINENMECHANISCHEN` would raise the total to **28** known-coordinate
substitutions. That full normalization is not accepted. All 21 positions are
left as `?` in the published partial template, and no witness filler is
presented as recovered text.

The proposed surname `GEMOLL` has an independent clear-header witness in
**p69 B1/B2**, which explicitly addresses `HPTM GEMOLL`. Here the raw ending
is `474DG1MOOLX`; the two letter repairs are costed. The proposed division
`474D | GEMOLL` is retained as an editorial division; it does not create a
first initial or expand the reference.

Source: [p63 A](../../experiments/october_requests/sources/childs_p63_A.png).

A [separately priced technical-word proposal](../../experiments/p63_optional_technical_reading/README.md)
reads `MASCHINENTECHNISCHEN` after treating one raw W as a surplus interim
pair. It keeps both printed D coordinates in the full transmitted witness
and adds three observed substitutions to the existing twelve. The optional
model therefore costs 15 substitutions, two dash fills and two surplus
interim coordinates. Its unique minimum is conditional on a retrospective
word template; the primary 21-position unresolved span above remains unchanged.

## Attribution and limits

These source editions use an earlier published period key. The adjacent p64
Hagelin/Nobel body is explicitly interpreted in Lasry and colleagues' §6.6
and Table 5 and is not part of this package. Absence of an individually
printed interpretation of the four records above is not a first-decipherment
claim. The differing headings, origin fields and reception dates remain
separate source fields. None of these records establishes p73's date,
plaintext or key.

# October staffing, manganese purchases and service traffic

[All cases](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** Six source-reviewed records under the previously published
**Oct4–6 key**. The principal result is a two-part Bavarian personnel order;
four other records concern Tiflis unit information, medical retransmission,
manganese purchases and a telegram acknowledgment. Source review:
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Earlier key credit belongs to **J. Rives
Childs**, **George Lasry**, and **Lasry–Niebel–Kopal–Wacker**.

All six printed frames have their advertised lengths. Across 1,264 received
slots, the raw key inverse fixes 630 of 632 plaintext positions. The edition
uses **four explicit known-coordinate substitutions and two erasure fills**;
626 proposed characters need neither. The
[reproducible source package](../../experiments/october_staffing/README.md)
contains every source row, domain, coordinate origin, edit and re-encryption.
There is no new key claim or proposed p73 plaintext.

## p66 C1 and p67 A2 — Bavarian command appointments

The source explicitly joins these parts: both carry `NR40 DEUTSCHE DELEGATION
KAUKASUS1723(5)2TLE`, with `1TL RICHI-286` on p66 and `2TL RICHI-220` on p67.
Both travel `COS v NKJ`; the reception times are 03.15 and 03.21 a.m. on
October 6. The page heading is October 5, and the shared origin field is
`1723(5)`.

**Readable German — most likely reading, with abbreviation and reference fields retained:**

> Oberst und Kdeur des 4. bayr. Chev.-Regt., Graf von Seyboltstorff, als
> Kdeur der 4. bayr. Kav.-Brig. bestimmt, ist sofort zu dieser Brig. zu
> beordern. Abreisetag umgehend drahten.
>
> Als Ersatz ist bereits Oberstlt. Karl von Grundherr, röm.I, des 4.
> Chev.-Regts dorthin beordert. Bayr. Kriegsministerium Nr 249774P.

**Display notes:** Abbreviations remain abbreviated. The displayed `röm.I` renders the literal name discriminator `ROEM1`; it is a formatting interpretation, not an additional unit number or a new personal identification.

The order directs the named colonel to the 4th Bavarian Cavalry Brigade and
requests the departure date. The second part says that the named lieutenant
colonel has already been ordered there as the replacement. Both brigade and
regiment numerals **4**, `KARLVONGRUNDHERR`, and the name discriminator `ROEM1`
are directly fixed by the received coordinates. The text alone does not locate
the brigade or identify a later telegram's unknown brigade numeral.

The raw first part spells the surname `SEYBOLTSTORF0`; its final `0` becomes
`F` through one coordinate substitution. The second part has `BEORSERT`;
`BEORDERT` costs one coordinate substitution. The reference `249774P` is
preserved without adding punctuation or interpreting its final character.

The institutional
[SLUB catalogue](https://katalog.slub-dresden.de/en/id/0-165780514X) records a 1922
history of the 4th Chevaulegers with contributors **Karl von Grundherr** and
**August Graf von Freyen-Seyboltstorff**. This supplies bibliographic support
for the names. Its linked WLB scan was unavailable to automated access during
this review; no command date or troop movement from that book is asserted.
The telegram's shorter surname form remains the form used in the reading.

Sources: [p66 C1](../../experiments/october_staffing/sources/childs_p66_C1.png)
and [p67 A2](../../experiments/october_staffing/sources/childs_p67_A2.png).

## p67 B — Suspend further manganese-ore purchases

Header: `COS v NKJ (10.32 p.m., October 5th); NR48 1916(5); RICHI-224`.

**Readable German:**

> An BV.K.M.KA Tiflis. Weitere Käufe Manganerze bis auf Weiteres
> unterlassen. Rittm.[F]ischer, Comm[i]ssar des Kriegsministeriums.

**Display notes:** `[F]` in the surname and `[i]` in `Comm[i]ssar` are proposed fills of two printed erasures. They are not abbreviation expansions. The former remains a name proposal; the latter is an ordinary-word completion. Their different evidential force is retained below.

The instruction to stop further manganese-ore purchases is directly fixed;
it requires no known-coordinate substitution. The address abbreviation
`BVXKXMXKA` remains unexpanded. The two printed dashes are in one source group,
`AAG--`, and affect separate plaintext positions.

The first signature letter has raw domain **`0BDFXZ`**. `[F]ISCHER` is the
proposed surname, not a uniquely recovered or independently identified person.
The other domain is **`3CIRUW`**, filled with `I` for `COMMISSAR`. Both are
explicit erasure fills. The raw signature is
`RITTMX?ISCHERCOMM?SSARDESKRIEGSMINISTERIUMS`.

Source: [p67 B](../../experiments/october_staffing/sources/childs_p67_B.png).

## p66 B — Repeat the garbled medical telegram

Header: `--- v NKJ (3.11 a.m., October 6th); DEUTSCHE DELEGATION KAUKASUS
1812(5); RICHI-284`.

**Readable German:**

> An leitenden Sanitätsoffz. Dortiges Telegr. Nr 131X232 ist verstümmelt.
> Bitte nochmals drahten. Armeearzt Oberkommando Besatzungsheeres Rumänien
> Nr 8586X3.

The recipient is asked to retransmit a garbled message. The raw text has
`DORTIGZS` and `BESATZUNGSHEERZS`; the edition changes each `Z` to `E`, costing
one received-coordinate substitution each. All numerals are directly fixed.
`131X232` and `8586X3` remain literal reference fields; the edition does not
turn the former into a date.

Source: [p66 B](../../experiments/october_staffing/sources/childs_p66_B.png).

## p66 A — An abbreviated Tiflis unit response

Header: `ASO v NKJ (9.27 p.m., October 5th); COS1615(5); RICHI-190`.

This record is fully determined, with no edit or fill:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
KDTURXTIFLISXXZUDORTXNRX80XREITXABTLGXBAYRX5OHNEERSTEBATTXBEIBXKXBXGEGENXKIEWXXGXUVXSEWASTOPOLX
```

</details>

A conservative division into words is:

**Readable German:**

> Kdtur. Tiflis. Zu dort Nr 80. Reit. Abtlg. Bayr. 5 ohne erste Batt. bei
> B.K.B. gegen Kiew. G.U.V. Sewastopol.

It addresses the Tiflis commandant's office, cites No. 80, and connects an
abbreviated mounted unit and battery exception with Kiew and Sewastopol. The
literal `5`, `BEIBXKXBX`, and `GXUVX` are preserved. No exact regiment, expanded
brigade designation, added verb or movement order is inferred from these
abbreviations.

Source: [p66 A](../../experiments/october_staffing/sources/childs_p66_A.png).

## p67 C — Telegram acknowledgment and a separate clear instruction

Header: `NKJ v OSM (--.-- October 7th); 2030; RICHI-60`. The sheet remains
headed October 5; no origin day is printed in this record's own `2030` field.

The 60 coordinates directly fix all 30 plaintext characters:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
TELXREISENOX1AVOM20X9XERHALTEN
```

</details>

A conservative reading is “Tel. Reise No. 1A vom 20.9. erhalten.” The exact token
`REISENO` and the reference `1A` remain visible; the interpretation does not
add an unprinted destination or sender.

The source separately prints **`BITTE JETZT ODER RAT ZU QUITTIEREN`** beneath
the ciphertext. This is a clear service instruction asking for acknowledgment;
it is not the plaintext of the 60-coordinate body. `RAT` remains unexpanded.

Source: [p67 C](../../experiments/october_staffing/sources/childs_p67_C.png).

## Explicit repair ledger

Source indices below are zero-based; group and character numbers are one-based.
The complete certificate also gives the plaintext positions and both received
coordinate origins.

| Record | Source index | Printed group / character | Proposed coordinate | Purpose |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| p66 B |11 |3 /2 |`G→F` |`HEERZS→HEERES` |
| p66 B |41 |9 /2 |`G→F` |`DORTIGZS→DORTIGES` |
| p66 C1 |251 |51 /2 |`F→V` |Final surname `0→F` |
| p67 A2 |106 |22 /2 |`F→G` |`BEORSERT→BEORDERT` |
| p67 B |118 |24 /4 |`?→V` |Proposed `[F]ISCHER` |
| p67 B |119 |24 /5 |`?→X` |Proposed `COMM[I]SSAR` |

The literal source is unchanged in every record. The proposed texts and their
re-encrypted witnesses are separate certificate fields.

# A truncated copy of the Tiflis armistice notice

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and cross-copy analysis: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** Newly edited record: Childs p212 A2. Earlier full witness: p218 A2, already in the [Tiflis armistice edition](p218_A.md). Published `Nov25-28` key, unchanged. [Inputs](../../experiments/p212_p218_crosscopy/inputs.json), [exact certificate](../../experiments/p212_p218_crosscopy/certificates.json), [method and limits](../../experiments/p212_p218_crosscopy/README.md).

The fragment is part of the previously known notice concerning withdrawal from territory that belonged to Russia before the war and the Allies' assessment of its internal situation. Its role is established by the close ciphertext correspondence with the complete p218 part, not by joining it to the medical passages printed around p212.

**The date conflict remains unresolved:** p212 is headed 22 November, while p218's full witness is headed and received 25 November. The edition changes neither date and makes no claim about the cause of the discrepancy.

## p212 A2

[Short-fragment source crop](../../experiments/p212_p218_crosscopy/sources/p212_A2.png); [full p218 A2 witness](../../experiments/p212_p218_crosscopy/sources/p218_A2.png). The p212 source advertises 284 coordinates but prints 160. Of those, 157 are identical to the corresponding p218 prefix. The differences are source indices 46 (`F/G`), 67 (`A/printed dash`) and 103 (`G/X`).

In the 284-coordinate frame, with the absent tail left as 124 erasures, only 30 plaintext positions have both source coordinates visible:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 284-slot frame with 124 absent tail coordinates left unknown:**

```text
?????????K??E????U??L?N?????????N??A????S??A?D?????????R??7????R??R?E?????????U??D????N??E?L?????????G??I????E??U?E?????????R??K????N??A?H????
```

</details>

### A conditional tail from the full printed witness

Borrowing p218's 124 literal tail coordinates, while preserving every p212 coordinate, gives:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional cross-copy tail completion from p218:**

```text
DIEVORDEMKRIEGZURUSZLANDGEHOERTENXHABENXSOBALDDIEALLIIERTE7UNTERBERUECKSICHTIGUNGDERJNNERENLAGEDIESERGEBIETEDENAUGENBLICKFUERGEKOMMENERACHTENX
```

</details>

This is a **source-copy reconstruction**, not a reading derived from the fragment alone. All borrowed coordinates have individual provenance in the certificate. Exhausting the 161 possible positions of one contiguous 124-coordinate loss gives the tail placement a unique minimum of two valid-coordinate disagreements. That supports the alignment under the copy assumption; it does not prove that an unseen historical tail was identical.

The copies are complementary. p212's F at index 46 independently supports the earlier `DPN → DEN` correction. Its A at index 67 supplies the missing coordinate in p218's `BERUEC?SICHTIGUNG`. In the other direction, p218's X at index 103 corrects p212's `ALLIIERTE7 → ALLIIERTEN`.

### Conservative readable candidate

Using that one p218 witness correction in the observed p212 prefix, then separately changing borrowed coordinate 217 `X → F` for `JNNEREN → INNEREN`, gives:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — conditional cross-copy tail completion, followed by the stated repairs:**

```text
DIEVORDEMKRIEGZURUSZLANDGEHOERTENXHABENXSOBALDDIEALLIIERTENUNTERBERUECKSICHTIGUNGDERINNERENLAGEDIESERGEBIETEDENAUGENBLICKFUERGEKOMMENERACHTENX
```

</details>

The received `RUSZLAND` spelling is retained. This is a continuation: “… die vor dem Krieg zu Russland gehörten, haben, sobald die Alliierten unter Berücksichtigung der inneren Lage dieser Gebiete den Augenblick für gekommen erachten …”. The surrounding withdrawal context belongs to the earlier complete three-part p218 notice; no complete p212 medical message is inferred.

Relative to p212's actual source, the candidate uses one observed-coordinate substitution and 124 missing-coordinate fills. Of those fills, 123 are literal p218 values; one is the explicitly separate ordinary-word correction. Thirty plaintext positions use two p212 coordinates, 100 use one coordinate from each copy, and 12 use only borrowed coordinates.

## The neighboring medical fragment

p212 A4 now has a separate [conditional medical edition](../military/p212_medical_fragment.md): its primary reading fills 129/151 positions, and an optional transport-doctor reading reaches 148/151. Both depend on a proposed 302-coordinate frame; three positions in the opening remain unresolved.

The earlier copy search found no nonself exact ten-coordinate window among 788 frozen OCR blocks. That result is retained in this package's certificate. It concerns repeated source coordinates, not the later recovery within the proposed frame; the search did not span OCR block boundaries.

## Attribution and scope

The full p218 A2 body was already edited and catalogued; its earlier work is not recounted as a new message or a new physical record. The present contribution is recognition of the truncated p212 copy, a conditional tail restoration, and complementary source evidence for earlier repairs. Only p212 A2 is newly proposed for the catalog. No first historical decipherment or changed key/date is claimed.

# p218 A - Kress, Tiflis and the armistice withdrawal condition [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source records](../../experiments/corpus_readings/selected_sources.json) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md) **Records:** p218 A1-A3, three parts of one message dated 25 November 1918. **Result:** the treaty reference supports a conditional interpretation of two Nov25–28 numeral cells. It reduces the reading's source cost from **16 to 13 observed-coordinate substitutions**, with the same three erasure fills. The two final digits of the opening telegram reference remain unknown. The message concerns German troops in former Russian territory and the German guard at Tiflis. ## Most likely reading **Readable German — conditional treaty numeral interpretation:** > General von Kress, Tiflis. Auf Tel. Nr. 2??. Artikel roem. 12 > Waffenstillstandsvertrages bestimmt: Alle deutschen Truppen, die sich > gegenwaertig in Gebieten befinden, die vor dem Krieg zu Russland > gehoerten, haben, sobald die Alliierten unter Beruecksichtigung der > inneren Lage dieser Gebiete den Augenblick fuer gekommen erachten, > in die deutschen Grenzen zurueckzukehren. > > Die Alliierten haben bisher die Zurueckziehung der deutschen > Schutzwache aus Tiflis nicht verlangt. Auswaertiges Amt. The article is XII. The transmitted instruction `ROEM12` expresses that Roman-number reference; spacing and punctuation are editorial. **Meaning:** Replying to telegram 163, the Foreign Office informs General von Kress in Tiflis that the armistice requires German troops in territory that belonged to Russia before the war to return within Germany's borders when the Allies judge the moment suitable in light of local conditions. The telegram adds that the Allies have not yet demanded withdrawal of the German guard from Tiflis. The wording identifies **Article XII** in the independently published [German armistice text](https://germanhistorydocs.org/de/die-weimarer-republik-1918-1933/waffenstillstandsbedingungen-11-november-1918) and the [U.S. diplomatic documentary edition](https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1919Parisv02/d1). The two received numeral pairs in `RO?MJ1` are complete: `FX` and `VG`. Reading them as 1 and 2 gives `ROEM12`, after the existing missing `E` fill. This [conditional shared-square interpretation](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/README.md) preserves three coordinates that the earlier numeral repair changed. It also changes the opening raw-label reference `163` to `2??`; its remaining two values are not established. The same `FX=1` assignment gives the headquarters designation `AOK11` in the [Breslau staff order](../people/breslau_staff_transfer.md) and both 11th-Army addresses in the [crown requests](../finance/crown_cash_requests.md). These are consistent consequences of the treaty identification. The published square, source transcriptions and earlier edition remain intact. The telegram paraphrases the treaty. The final statement about the Tiflis guard belongs to this telegram, not to Article XII. No conclusion about a later withdrawal date is inferred from it. ## Baseline reading and the reduced source cost The unchanged published key fixes 419/422 raw positions. Its earlier edition priced the article number as a source repair: | Source part | Coordinates | Raw fixed positions | Candidate cost | |---|---:|---:|---| | [A1](../../sources/excerpts/other_p218_A1.png) | 282 | 140/141 | 10 valid-coordinate substitutions; one printed dash filled | | [A2](../../sources/excerpts/other_p218_A2.png) | 284 | 141/142 | Four valid-coordinate substitutions; one printed dash filled | | [A3](../../sources/excerpts/other_p218_A3.png) | 278 | 138/139 | Two valid-coordinate substitutions; one printed dash filled |
Raw decoded text **Raw output:** ```text G9NERALVONKRESSTIFLISXAUFTELXNRX163XART4KELRO?MJ1WAFFENSTILLSFANDSVERTRAGESBESTIMMTXALLEDEUTSCHAZTRUPPENDIESICHGEGE8CAERTIGINGEBIETENBEFINDEN DIEVORDEMKRIEGZURUSZLANDGEHOERTENXHABENXSOBALDDIEALLIIERTENUNTERBERUEC?SICHTIGUNGDERJNNERENLAGEDIESERGEBIETEDPNAUGENBLICKFUERGEKOMMENERACHTENX INDIEDEUTSCHENGRENZENZURUECKZUKEHRWNXDIEALLIIERTENHABENBISHERDIEZURUECKZIEHUNGDERKEUTSCHENSCHUTZWACHEAU?TIFLISNICHTVERLANGTXAUSWAERTIGESAMT ```
The earlier candidate preserves **825 valid source coordinates**. Under the treaty interpretation, p218 A1 needs seven observed-coordinate changes and one fill; A2 and A3 keep their previous costs. The new combined reading therefore preserves **828** valid coordinates. Its [certificate](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/certificates.json) records all three removed numeral substitutions and checks the German reading above against the revised coordinate stream. Ordinary-word repairs, including `G9NERAL`, `RUSZLAND`, `JNNEREN` and `KEUTSCHENSCHUTZWACHE`, retain their earlier costs. ## Source, route and credit Printed p218 / PDF p221, heading **25 November 1918**: `NKJ v LP (02.10 p.m., November 25th); FUER COS 0950 (11/25) 3 TLE`. The three parts are separately labelled RICHI-282, RICHI-284 and RICHI-278. Using the established recipient-first header convention, the transmission is LP to NKJ, for onward delivery to COS. This is an additional Kress-route record; it does not determine the key or disputed date of [p73](../p73.md). The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, in the [public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view). The published period key keeps its external attribution in [data/keys.json](../../data/keys.json). Source inspection, assembly, coordinate audit and this annotated edition are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment priority is claimed. ```sh python3 experiments/corpus_readings/verify.py --verify ``` The [literal source records](../../experiments/corpus_readings/selected_sources.json) and [certificate](../../experiments/corpus_readings/certificates.json) include the source PDF hash, reproducible image rectangles, the complete unchanged key, all raw position domains and both re-encryption checks.
