# Poti horse transport: a conditional first-part edition

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This is a conditional partial edition of the previously uncounted first part of the [Poti horse-delivery exchange](poti_horse_delivery.md). The original source has **225 positions** under the printed label **RICHI-220**. Its two transport clauses and footer can be repaired at a small explicit cost. A separate repeated-field extension now supplies three conditional letters, reaching **108/110** positions while retaining the original frame alternatives, unread opening and competing vessel-like labels.

## Source and complete frame comparison

The [existing public source crop](../../experiments/poti_horse_delivery/sources/p59_A1.png) retains every printed group and dash. Header: `SSD, COS v ASO (07.50 a.m., September 22nd); 2250 (21.9) 3 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-220`. The [literal inputs](../../experiments/poti_first_part_conditional/inputs.json) bind the earlier source edition without altering it.

The exact search prices **all 4,595,146,920 ways to exclude five of the 225 positions**, using dynamic programming. Only six ordinary transport-word spans are constrained; the opening, names and numbers are left free. The minimum is **five changed observed coordinates and two printed-mask fills**, after the separately declared **five exclusions**. There are **21 minimum source maps and eight distinct raw streams**. All are preserved, including their different prefix labels and first date-like fields. This is a bounded model result, not a proof that any five-coordinate deletion occurred historically.

The representative below excludes source indices 200–204, the visible `AFFDD` group. No cancellation mark on the source licenses that choice. It is retained because it was already one of the earlier illustrative frames, not because its prefix digits look more plausible.

## Representative raw and limited repair

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 220-coordinate frame after the five disclosed exclusions; unchanged Sep19–21 key:**

```text
6X??FFQ274XHG6AM11X9XAUF9AMPF?RXVUR?A4VA?NAX5XBATTAAM15X9XAUFDAM?FZRXBURDALXBYRDA?XINSGYSAWT52PFERDENAUHXPOTI0
```

**Edited output — the same conditional frame, five observed-coordinate substitutions and two printed-mask fills; all other labels retained:**

```text
6X??FFQ274XHG6AM11X9XAUFDAMPFERXVUR?A4VA?NAX5XBATTAAM15X9XAUFDAMPFERXBURDALXBYRDA?XINSGESAMT52PFERDENACHXPOTI0
```

</details>

**Readable German — all representative candidate labels retained; no vessel identification or date normalization:**

> 6 X ??FFQ274 X HG6 am 11 X 9 X auf Dampfer X VUR?A4VA?NA X 5 X BATT A am 15 X 9 X auf Dampfer X BURDAL X BYRDA? X insgesamt 52 Pferde nach X POTI0.

The two `AUF DAMPFER` clauses and the `INSGESAMT52PFERDENACH` footer support a limited horse-transport interpretation toward the literal `POTI0` ending. The separately printed second and third parts concern horses and Poti, which supplies context but does not identify the names or restore the opening. In this earlier 105/110 layer, `VUR?A4VA?NA`, `BURDAL` and `BYRDA?` remain opaque. The separate extension below transfers three missing letters; it does not identify either vessel with certainty.

## Conditional repeated-field completion

Each `AUF DAMPFER` clause is followed by two similar short fields. If each
pair repeats one label, and extra observed-coordinate changes are minimized,
three missing letters are common to every minimum-cost reconstruction:
**N at position 35**, **R at 40**, and **L at 81**. The corresponding letters
are directly present in the other copy at positions 41, 34 and 74.

| Raw pair in every retained frame | Minimum equal-copy alternatives | Common missing-letter transfers |
|---|---|---|
| `VUR?A` / `VA?NA` | `VARNA` or `VURNA` | N into the first copy; R into the second |
| `BURDAL` / `BYRDA?` | `BURDAL` or `BYRDAL` | L into the second copy |

These are conditional repetition inferences. The source itself still fixes
103/110 positions under the five-exclusion frame. Transferring just the
three common letters gives **108/110**, at **four additional printed-mask
fills and no additional observed-coordinate substitutions**. N and R each
need one missing half; L needs both halves. The totals are **five observed
substitutions, six mask fills and five separately declared source
exclusions**. All 21 previously minimizing source maps remain represented.

**Readable German — the common extension, with the three conditional letters bracketed:**

> 6 X ??FFQ274 X HG6 am 11 X 9 X auf Dampfer X VUR[N]A4VA[R]NA X 5 X BATT A am 15 X 9 X auf Dampfer X BURDAL X BYRDA[L] X insgesamt 52 Pferde nach X POTI0.

The differing U/A and U/Y letters and the raw `4` remain literal in this
common layer. Enforcing identical complete copies costs one further observed
substitution for each pair and leaves **four joint minimum variants**; all
are retained. The extension does not silently choose `VARNA`, replace `4`
with a separator, or turn `BURDAL`/`BYRDAL` into a different ship name. The
two opening unknowns still permit **36** complete strings in each frame.

<details>
<summary>Common conditional extension and exact machine labels</summary>

**Edited output — three repetition-based letters; five substitutions and six mask fills after the existing five exclusions:**

```text
6X??FFQ274XHG6AM11X9XAUFDAMPFERXVURNA4VARNAX5XBATTAAM15X9XAUFDAMPFERXBURDALXBYRDALXINSGESAMT52PFERDENACHXPOTI0
```

</details>

For limited context, the shipping company's own
[history](https://navibulgar.com/en/company/history/index.php) records a
steamer *Varna* among deliveries in 1903–1906 and wartime mobilization of its
vessels in 1916–1918. A separate public
[photograph caption](https://www.flickr.com/photos/39631091@N03/15359293270/)
is titled *Poti, Ship Varna* and attributed by its uploader to a German
officer in winter 1918. Only the caption was inspected; this metadata does
not verify a September voyage or identify the telegram's vessel. These
contextual sources make `VARNA` plausible without selecting it by arithmetic.

The [extension package](../../experiments/p59_repeated_vessel_labels/README.md)
records all label costs, all four equal-copy variants and exact source
ledgers for every retained frame. The original first-part edition and its
source inputs are preserved.

## Alternative frames and withheld constraints

The complete certificate preserves every minimizing source map, raw stream, repaired stream and source-coordinate ledger. It does not collapse numerically different branches into the representative display.

| Constraints used | Minimum observed substitutions | Printed-mask fills | Minimum maps |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Both steamer clauses only |2|2|812|
| Transport footer, with NACH withheld |1|0|359630|
| All spans except NACH |4|2|1146|
| All six spans |5|2|21|

The five exclusions are a separate structural cost in every row. Withholding words leaves more possible maps; the retained 21 are conditional on the declared word stencil. The unchanged native 225-coordinate stream is also recorded with its orphan coordinate and no hidden truncation.

## Reproduce and credit

```sh
python experiments/poti_first_part_conditional/verify.py --verify
python experiments/poti_first_part_conditional/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf
```

Childs source p59 and the published Sep19–21 key; earlier source transcription and A2/A3 edition retained. Joint frame pricing, constrained partial edition and complete alternative accounting: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. No first-decipherment claim.

# Horses for a cavalry brigade: Poti shipment and handover inquiry

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p59 A, PDF p62, contains three numbered parts under the header
`SSD, COS v ASO (07.50 a.m., September 22nd)`, followed by
`2250 (21.9) 3 TLE`. The second and third parts recover coherent passages
about a shipment at Poti for a cavalry brigade, an abteilung ordered
elsewhere, horses handed over at Poti, and an urgent request for a reply.
The incomplete preceding clause leaves the precise assertion or question
about the handover uncertain.

The **Sep19–21** key is unchanged. This edition counts **two** physical
records, with **225 plaintext positions**. The first part is preserved as
context outside this package's two-record totals because its 225 visible
source slots disagree with its printed length of 220. It now has a separate
[conditional catalogue entry](poti_first_part_conditional.md), with its
own declared frame model. It is not silently forced into the continuation.

## p59 A2

The [source crop](../../experiments/poti_horse_delivery/sources/p59_A2.png)
has **220 slots**, including seven printed dashes, exactly matching
`2 TL RICHI-220`.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 220-coordinate frame:**

```text
POTIXVERLADEBXDIEFUER7GBA8?BRIGXBE7THMMTXXDAABTEILUNGKNDERSHINBEO4DHGTXDRING?NDDRAHTEO?ERBRTVEXO0?NDWME??EL?XX
```

**Edited output — 11 observed-coordinate substitutions and three printed-dash fills:**

```text
POTIXVERLADENXDIEFUER7XKAVXBRIGXBESTIMMTXXDAABTEILUNGANDERSHINBEORDERTXDRINGENDDRAHTEODERBRTVEXO0?NDWME??EL?XX
```

</details>

**Readable German — spacing of the conservative partial candidate, with its opaque ending retained:**

> ... Poti verladen, die für 7. Kav. Brig. bestimmt. Da Abteilung
> andershin beordert. Dringend drahte oder BRTVE. O0?NDWME??EL? ...

The leading ellipsis marks missing syntactic context from the unresolved
first part, not an added coordinate gap in A2. The closing ellipsis marks
the unfinished syntax; it does not hide further decoded A2 labels. This reading fixes
**106 / 110 positions** after the disclosed edits. The abbreviation
`KAV` is an editorial word repair; its leading **7** is the unchanged
raw label. The final fragment remains unresolved and is not polished into
a complete sentence.

### Conditional interpretation of the opaque ending

One contextually plausible extension is shown below. It requires **25
observed substitutions and seven dash fills in total**, or **14 additional
substitutions and four additional fills** beyond the conservative candidate.

**Conditional interpretation — costly full A2 hypothesis, excluded from the main reading counts:**

```text
POTIXVERLADENXDIEFUER7XKAVXBRIGXBESTIMMTXXDAABTEILUNGANDERSHINBEORDERTXDRINGENDDRAHTEODERBRIEFXOBUNDWEMDIESEXX
```

This would produce “... Brief ... ob und wem diese ...” before the next
part. It is guided by the following part and by language, with substantial
changes to observed source coordinates. It is not independent evidence
for the damaged letters. Its final `DIESE` and the next part's initial
`DIESE` are both retained; neither is deleted to smooth the join. The
certificate records its exact round trip and all additional costs separately.

## p59 A3

The [source crop](../../experiments/poti_horse_delivery/sources/p59_A3.png)
contains **230 slots**, with **31 printed dashes**, matching
`3 TL RICHI-230`. Restoring the dash groups omitted by the earlier OCR
is essential to preserving the source's frame.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 230-coordinate frame:**

```text
D?ES?4?FER1E??X???I?EBERGE?E?WUGWE?XF?R?ERBALQIG?T?ANTWIRTA??UNSE?ZNFU??S1RZCH?79??7070V9?15X?XXXGEN?DOX?2XTBXP?47?
```

**Edited output — nine observed-coordinate substitutions and 23 printed-dash fills:**

```text
DIESEXPFERDEINXPOTIUEBERGEBENWURDENXFERNERBALDIGSTXANTWORTAUFUNSERENFUNKSPRUCH?79??7070V9?15X?XXXGENKDOX?2XTBXP?47?
```

</details>

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation, with the unresolved reference fields kept literal:**

> ... diese Pferde in Poti übergeben wurden. Ferner baldigst Antwort
> auf unseren Funkspruch ?79??7070V9?15X?XXX. Gen. Kdo. ?2. TB. P?47?

The ellipsis marks the unfinished preceding clause. The fragment can be
part of a question about delivery; it does not independently prove that
the delivery occurred. The main reading fixes **107 / 115 positions**.
All eight unresolved positions are in the reference/footer portion. The
literal `V`, repeated `70`, and other surviving labels are preserved;
there is no guessed date, time, corps number or reference.

## Domains, source costs and first-part conflict

The [certificate](../../experiments/poti_horse_delivery/certificates.json)
lists every source-coordinate pair, raw domain, substitution, fill and
changed plaintext position. Raw fixed-position totals count single-symbol
algebraic domains, including erroneous received letters; they are not an
accuracy score for the historical reading.

The four remaining A2 erasures independently allow **1,296** complete
plaintexts. The eight remaining A3 erasures independently allow
**1,679,616**. These are exact factorized counts under the unchanged
complete square and the stated main edits, with finite re-encryption
witnesses retained. No completion is selected as historical.

The [first-part crop](../../experiments/poti_horse_delivery/sources/p59_A1.png)
shows **225 slots** under `RICHI-220`. All **221** possible consecutive
five-slot deletions are retained as diagnostic frames. Two illustrative
placements expose transport-related fragments, but neither establishes
a complete clean reading or a unique historical geometry. A1 remains outside
this package's A2/A3 totals. Its separate
[conditional first-part edition](poti_first_part_conditional.md) is now
included in the catalogue and preserves the unresolved frame alternatives.

The counted two records use **450 source slots**, **412 valid source
coordinates**, **20 observed-coordinate substitutions** and **26 dash
fills**, with **12 dashes still unfilled**. There is no length change,
source deletion or key change in these two records.

The published key and the earlier partial A2 repository candidate retain
their credit. No historical first-solution claim is made. The
[inputs](../../experiments/poti_horse_delivery/inputs.json),
[earlier candidates](../../experiments/poti_horse_delivery/prior_candidates.json)
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/poti_horse_delivery/README.md)
preserve the full source and the limits of this reading.

# The Caucasus K.M. representative is to remain

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This p142 B telegram replies to an earlier message and says the `BEV K.M.`
representative in the Caucasus, at Tiflis, is to remain. The closing names
the `KRIEGSAMT KRIEGSROHSTOFFABTLG`. The abbreviated office `K.M.` is left
unexpanded; the closing alone is not used to assign it a different title.

## Source and reading

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [printed p142, PDF p145](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [B crop](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p142_B.png)
is under a November 6 heading:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
B) NKJ v LP (08.30 p.m., November 6th)
FUER COS EINMAL 1250 (6/11)
RICHI-286
```

</details>

All **286 coordinates** are visible and valid, matching the printed length.
The earlier 280-slot OCR extraction omitted source content and is not the
analysis frame. The unchanged published `Nov4-6` key fixes all 143 raw labels:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FUERXBEVXKMXKAUKASUCXT9FLISXZU4TELEGRAMMVOMX29X10X18XPOTX44XNRX2331XBEVXKXMXSOLLBLEIBENXKRIEGSAMTKRIEGSROHSTOFFABTLGXNRXZXROEMX1XAX23X11X18XKRA
```

</details>

Three observed-coordinate substitutions give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
FUERXBEVXKMXKAUKASUSXTIFLISXZUMTELEGRAMMVOMX29X10X18XPOTX44XNRX2331XBEVXKXMXSOLLBLEIBENXKRIEGSAMTKRIEGSROHSTOFFABTLGXNRXZXROEMX1XAX23X11X18XKRA
```

</details>

Readable core:

**Readable German:**

> Für Bev. K.M. Kaukasus, Tiflis. Zum Telegramm vom 29.10.18,
> POT 44, Nr. 2331. Bev. K.M. soll bleiben.

The source uses `BEVXKMX` in the address and `BEVXKXM` later; both exact
separator patterns remain in the encoded edition. The following reference
is retained verbatim and **not silently interpreted as a November date**:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — unchanged reference-field excerpt:**

```text
KRIEGSAMTKRIEGSROHSTOFFABTLGXNRXZXROEMX1XAX23X11X18XKRA
```

</details>

| Source index, zero-based | Printed group / position, one-based | Change | Effect |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 52 | 11 / 3 | `F` → `V` | `T9FLIS` → `TIFLIS` |
| 53 | 11 / 4 | `V` → `F` | `ZU4TELEGRAMM` → `ZUMTELEGRAMM` |
| 171 | 35 / 2 | `D` → `G` | `KAUKASUC` → `KAUKASUS` |

The raw `9` and `4` within words are separately preserved in the numerical
ledger. Their local repairs do not reassign square digits. All actual date,
number and reference fields remain unchanged. There are no erasure fills,
coordinate insertions, deletions or square changes.

## Reproduce and prior credit

The [source inputs](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/inputs.json)
and [certificate](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/certificates.json)
retain raw domains, changes and the complete forward witness.

```sh
python experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/verify.py --verify
```

The published key is credited to **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**, [DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461).
Earlier unreviewed OCR-derived candidates existed. No universal first-reading
priority is asserted. The exact repaired witness establishes its stated
three-coordinate cost, not the identity of the representative or proof that
the instruction was carried out.

# A Polish representative in Tiflis — p199 preamble and p192 parts 2 and 3

[Case index](../README.md) · [November 14 retransmissions](../radio/nov14_radio_retransmissions.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition, missing-group recovery and historical comparison: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The two unheaded parts at the top of printed page 192 describe an appointment
to represent the Polish government in the Caucasus. The first is directly
readable under the published November 13–15b key. The second becomes readable
after an explicitly certified missing five-coordinate group. Its courier
surname provides independent historical support for the conditional key
assignment **FX = Y**.

A later source check recovered a matching preamble on printed p199. It asks
General von Kress in Tiflis to forward the Polish Foreign Ministry's message
to **Waclaw v. Ostrowski**. The text supplies the recipient directly. Its
association with the unheaded p192 parts is strong, but their conflicting
page/header dates are not silently reconciled.

## Readable meaning

**Readable German — the base edited text, with the courier name still unresolved:**

> An General von Kress, Tiflis. Nr. `?1?`. Bitte Weiterleitung folgenden Telegramms des Ministerium des Aeusseren in Warschau an Herrn Waclaw v. Ostrowski, Tiflis: Sie sind zum Vertrauensmann der polnischen Regierung fuer die Republiken Grusien, Armenien und Aserbejnzan mit Sitz in Tiflis ernannt. Ernennung und Instruktion bereits durch `T?DE?SKI` an Sie abgesandt. Ministerium des Aeussern. Bussche.

**Display notes:** This combines the separately identified parts under the cross-page association discussed below. It supplies word spacing, capitalization and punctuation; the colon renders the transmitted word `DOPPELPUNKT`. The spellings `ASERBEJNZAN`, `AEUSSERN` and the missing genitive S in `DESMINISTERIUM` remain unnormalized in the base text. The reference and both name positions remain unknown.

**English meaning with a conditional historical-name interpretation:**

> To General von Kress, Tiflis: Please forward the following telegram from
> the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Warsaw to Mr. Waclaw v. Ostrowski,
> Tiflis: You have been appointed the Polish government's trusted
> representative for the republics of Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan,
> with your seat in Tiflis. The appointment and instructions have already
> been sent to you through [Tydelski]. Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Bussche.

The bracketed surname `[Tydelski]` is a historical identification, not an abbreviation expansion or a direct rendering of the unresolved base name. It uses the historical identification described below.
The opening uses the newly sourced p199 preamble and its explicit cross-page
association. Its source header is dated November 15, 1918, while p192 is
headed November 14. Neither is established as the appointment telegram's
original issue date; a forwarding date need not be an issue date.

### Part 1 on p199: the recipient and a floating group

The unlettered message following p199 A is headed `NKJ v LP (08.32 p.m.,
November 15th)`, `FUER COS 18.56 (15/11)`, `3 TLE`, and `1 TL RICHI-262`.
It has 257 valid coordinates in the main grid and a separate printed `FGFFF`
above it. All 262 valid coordinates are preserved. The main grid also has a blank cell
at row 6, column 5; the blank is not silently supplied with five erasures.

Reading the floating group first, in physical top-to-bottom order, gives:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — floating group read first in physical top-to-bottom order:**

```text
ANGENERALVO?KRESSTI5LISXNRXZ1?XBITTEWEITERLEITUNGFODGENDENTILEGRAMM6DESMTNISTERIUMDESAEUSSELSNINWARSCHAUANHERRNXWACLAWXVXOSTROWSKIX
```

</details>

The source's unusual layout is resolved independently of the personal names.
The certificate places the five observed floating coordinates at all **258**
boundaries of the main grid and compares a declared ordinary-word stencil.
It masks `KRESS`, `TIFLIS`, `WARSCHAU`, the entire `WACLAW V OSTROWSKI` field,
and the reference. The unique minimum places `FGFFF` after the first **10**
main-grid coordinates, as the third group. It needs only two changes to
ordinary-word coordinates; the literal top-first placement needs seven under
the same masked stencil. This movement adds and removes no coordinate.

The selected geometry gives 129 fixed raw positions out of 131:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional placement of the floating group after ten main-grid coordinates:**

```text
ANGENERALVONKRESSTIFLISXNRX?1?XBITTEWEITERLEITUNGFOLGENDENTELEGRAMMSDESMTNISTERIUMDESAEUSSERSNINWARSCHAUANHERRNXWACLAWXVXOSTROWSKIX
```

</details>

Two observed-coordinate substitutions restore `MINISTERIUM` and
`AEUSSEREN`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional floating-group placement, followed by the stated repairs:**

```text
ANGENERALVONKRESSTIFLISXNRX?1?XBITTEWEITERLEITUNGFOLGENDENTELEGRAMMSDESMINISTERIUMDESAEUSSERENINWARSCHAUANHERRNXWACLAWXVXOSTROWSKIX
```

</details>

The received `MINISTERIUM` lacks the genitive `S` expected in this formula.
The [shared conditional VG=2 reading](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md#the-award-class)
completes the first reference digit: **`21?`**, giving **130/131** labels in
the preamble. This uses the existing floating-group placement and its two
word repairs, with no new source edit. The baseline quotation and streams
above retain `?1?` for comparison.

The association with p192 is supported by complementary part numbers,
the same published key, and continuous address/appointment syntax: p199 ends
with Ostrowski, while p192 part 2 begins `TIFLISDOPPELPUNKT` followed by the
appointment. It remains a cross-page association, not a surviving common
header. The November 14/15 discrepancy is real. The separate p192 A and B
records also combine November 14 receipt dates with `15/11` originating
dates, so the anomaly is documented elsewhere on that page as well. Mądzik's
study of Ostrowski in Tbilisi is corroborating context after this source
reading, and supplies no name crib to the group-placement test.

### Part 2: the appointment and its geographic scope

All 230 source coordinates are valid. Their unmodified decryption is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
TIFLISDOPPELPUNKTXSIESINDZUMVSRTRAUENSMANNDERPOLNISCHENREGIERUNGFUERDIEREPUBLIKENXGRUSIENXARMENIENXUNDXASERBEJNZANX
```

</details>

The ordinary-word candidate changes one source coordinate to give
`VERTRAUENSMANN`. The exact country spelling `ASERBEJNZAN` is retained in the
base reading. A separate same-length `ASERBEJDZAN` proposal costs one
additional coordinate change; neither spelling is silently expanded to
modern German. The interpretation as Azerbaijan follows the country list
and recognizable transmitted name, rather than a claim that every letter
is correct.

### Part 3: a missing group established without the surname

The source prints **227 valid coordinates** under a `RICHI-232` heading.
The certificate tests insertion of one five-coordinate gap at **all 228
possible boundaries**. Its ordinary-word stencil masks the entire eight-slot
courier name and the seven-slot signature. Neither `TYDELSKI` nor `BUSSCHE`
helps choose the gap.

The unique minimum is **source boundary 150**, before the printed group
`AAAFF`: exactly one observed coordinate must change to fit the surrounding
words. Four other boundaries require two changes. This is an exact result
for the stated single-group-loss model and displayed stencil, rather than a
proof of the historical copying error.

Under that geometry, before word repairs, the unchanged key gives:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional five-coordinate gap at source boundary 150; before word repairs:**

```text
MITSITZINEIFLISERNANNTXXERNENNUNGUNDINST?UKTIONB?REITSDU?CHXT?DE?SKIXANS?EABGESANDTXXMINISTERIUMDESAEUSSERNXXBUSSCHE
```

</details>

Ordinary words supply four missing coordinates, and one observed-coordinate
change corrects `EIFLIS` to `TIFLIS`. The result fixes **114/116 positions**:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional gap, with four added-slot fills and one observed substitution:**

```text
MITSITZINTIFLISERNANNTXXERNENNUNGUNDINSTRUKTIONBEREITSDURCHXT?DE?SKIXANSIEABGESANDTXXMINISTERIUMDESAEUSSERNXXBUSSCHE
```

</details>

The unknown name letter at position 61 is a complete observed `FX` pair,
made from **original source indices 80 and 138**. Both coordinates precede
the gap and remain unchanged throughout every repair. The other unknown,
at position 64, has an observed F and one missing coordinate.

## The separate historical-name inference

Marek Mądzik's [archival study](https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/texts/rocznik-lubelski/1987-1988-tom-29-30/rocznik_lubelski-r1987_1988-t29_30-s77-87.pdf#page=3),
printed p78 note 3, names engineer Tadeusz Tydelski as chairman of the Polish
Caucasus council, citing CAW relacje 400.2500, appendix 2, p3. Pages 78–79
also connect him with Ostrowski's Baku office. The article and
[short name crop](../../experiments/tiflis_appointment/sources/madzik_p78_name.png)
were checked; the underlying manuscript was not. Identifying this courier
with that person remains a separate inference.

Under that identification, `T?DE?SKI` becomes `TYDELSKI`. It supplies the
missing L coordinate and sets **FX = Y** in the November 13–15b square.
The full candidate then reads:

**Conditional interpretation — historical TYDELSKI identification, missing-coordinate fill and FX = Y:**

```text
MITSITZINTIFLISERNANNTXXERNENNUNGUNDINSTRUKTIONBEREITSDURCHXTYDELSKIXANSIEABGESANDTXXMINISTERIUMDESAEUSSERNXXBUSSCHE
```

Its exact repair certificate has **one observed-coordinate substitution**
and **five inserted coordinates**, `GFGFA`, at the declared gap. Full
reencryption reproduces that repaired ciphertext exactly. The historical
key file remains unchanged.

This check alone does not prove Y: the same repaired ciphertext can encode
`T2DELSKI`, `T3DELSKI`, `T4DELSKI`, `T7DELSKI`, `T8DELSKI`, `T9DELSKI`,
`TQDELSKI` or `TYDELSKI` under the eight possible cell assignments. The
independent historical surname supplies the reason to select Y.

## Consequences for the pilot notices

Two inference layers are kept distinct:

| Layer | Assignment | Additional assumption | Complete-pair effects in these editions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Historical courier name | Nov13–15b FX = Y | The damaged courier name identifies Tydelski with correct spelling | p192 part 3 position 61; p190 A position 37 becomes FRYE |
| Cross-key pilot-name transfer | Nov13–15a DG = Y | The p190 A and p194 B FR?E fields contain the same correctly copied name | p194 B position 54 and interrupted p193 B position 54 |

Positions are zero-based. The first assignment does not depend on the pilot's
identity. The second remains conditional even if the Tydelski identification
is accepted. The machine-readable report includes every before/after raw
text and marginal-domain change across the three Tiflis records and all seven
[November 14 records](../radio/nov14_radio_retransmissions.md), including changes that
do not create another fixed letter.

## Evidence and reproduction

- [Literal source and historical-reference metadata](../../experiments/tiflis_appointment/inputs.json)
- [All 228 gap models, exact repairs and conditional key-layer effects](../../experiments/tiflis_appointment/certificates.json)
- [Preamble source with floating group](../../experiments/tiflis_appointment/sources/p199_B1.png)
- [Part 2 source](../../experiments/tiflis_appointment/sources/p192_2.png)
- [Part 3 source](../../experiments/tiflis_appointment/sources/p192_3.png)
- [Verification instructions](../../experiments/tiflis_appointment/README.md)

The three records contain 719 valid source coordinates. The declared
724-coordinate frame fixes 354/362 raw positions before repairs, 358/362
after the ordinary-word layer, and 360/362 under the historical-name layer.
The p192 subset is unchanged at 225/231, 229/231 and 231/231. The further
VG=2 interpretation leaves one unresolved reference symbol in the p199
preamble and is compatible with the separate historical-name layer.
Raw fixed positions include source garbles; these counts describe the
mathematical consequences of each explicitly stated layer.

cases/caucasus/tiflis_pioneer_detachment.text:
# A pioneer detachment may remain in Tiflis

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** Childs p81 B (PDF p84), 30 October 1918; published `Oct28-31` key, unchanged. [Source crop](../../experiments/deutzitag_dispatch_inquiries/sources/p81_B.png), [inputs](../../experiments/deutzitag_dispatch_inquiries/inputs.json), [exact certificate](../../experiments/deutzitag_dispatch_inquiries/certificates.json).

The clear header addresses General von Kress in Tiflis: `NKJ v LP (3.53 p.m., October 30th); FUER COS SS DD GR HQ OP 1400 (30/10); FUER GENERAL VON KRESS, TIFLIS`. This is a separate military message, unrelated to the commercial inquiries around it on the page.

## p81 B

All 132 source coordinates are observed. They decrypt directly to 66 fixed labels with no repair:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ZUXNRX4452XPIONXABTXKANNINTIFLISBELASZENWERDENXGROENERXBX103830XO9
```

</details>

Reading: “Zu Nr. 4452: Pion.-Abt. kann in Tiflis belassen werden. Groener. B. 103830 O9.”

The received `BELASZEN`, `4452`, `BX103830XO9` and the final `O9` remain unchanged. The last field is not silently expanded to `OP`. The text permits the detachment to remain; it does not independently show what the unit subsequently did.

An earlier unreviewed repository candidate already contained this body. The present edition adds visual source checking, all coordinate and plaintext indices, re-encryption and an unchanged-reference inventory. It does not claim first historical decipherment.

cases/context/benzol_pump_query.md.text:
# Benzol-pump inquiry with an explicit missing-coordinate model

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The p189 D reading asks whether a benzol pump is available and requests a prompt answer. Its 102-coordinate analysis is conditional: the printed body contains 101 occupied positions, including one non-coordinate glyph, and the first row ends with a four-coordinate group. Every missing-slot assumption and textual repair is priced below.

## Source and context

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed query and neighboring reply](../../experiments/benzol_pump_query/sources/p189_reviewed.png) · [Inputs](../../experiments/benzol_pump_query/inputs.json) · [Position certificates and all 102 insertion prices](../../experiments/benzol_pump_query/certificates.json)

**Source transcription — header:** `D) CM v CZ (9.30 a.m., November 15th); RIZI-102`

The source says RIZI-102 but has **101 occupied slots**, with `XVGF` as the four-coordinate last group of the first row. The K-like final glyph of `DXXGK` occupies a separate source slot; it is masked, not discarded. All other observed coordinates stay in order.

The neighboring p189 E reverses the direction to `CZ v CM`, is timed 10.00 a.m. after D's 9.30 a.m., and begins with an answer about a pump. Its [existing edition](transport.md#independent-transport-context) supports the topic. It is not a parallel ciphertext and cannot supply D's missing coordinate or certify the exact closing surname.

## p189 D

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — native 101-position diagnostic, before any length change:**

```text
ISEEIDEBENNOLPUMPE?OR1XBESKHLE?NIGTEANTWORTXSSIF??
```

</details>

This odd-length diagnostic has one unpaired intermediate coordinate. The certificate retains its intermediate position, source index and literal coordinate; it is not silently removed from the source account.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 102-coordinate frame with one masked insertion at source boundary 38; 47/51 fixed positions:**

```text
IS?EIDEBENZOLPUMPEDOR1XBESAHLE?NIGTEANTWORTXSSIF??T
```

**Edited output — the same conditional frame; six observed-coordinate substitutions, one source-glyph fill and one inserted-coordinate fill:**

```text
ISTEINEBENZOLPUMPEDORTXBESCHLEUNIGTEANTWORTXSEIFERT
```

</details>

**Readable German — labels from the edited output, with editorial word spacing and punctuation:**

> Ist eine Benzolpumpe dort. Beschleunigte Antwort. Seifert.

**Meaning:** The sender asks whether a benzol pump is available there and requests an expedited answer. The closing is the explicitly reconstructed surname Seifert, with no first name or biographical identification added.

The first sentence is a question by its wording. Its raw numeral-like `1` in DOR1 is not silently treated as T: that change is part of the recorded substitution cost. Unknown square labels in the raw body are not freely assigned letters to obtain familiar words.

## Local and global insertion alternatives

All indices are zero-based. The five boundaries around XVGF have these costs for the displayed complete word proposal:

| Insertion boundary | Observed substitutions | Existing source-mask fills | Inserted-slot fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 35 | 8 | 1 | 1 |
| 36 | 7 | 1 | 1 |
| 37 | 6 | 1 | 1 |
| 38 | 6 | 1 | 1 |
| 39 | 7 | 1 | 1 |

All 102 boundaries in the entire received stream were also tested against the same disclosed candidate. Only **37 and 38** attain the minimum of six observed substitutions. Both choices produce the same completed ciphertext under the fixed key, but their source-to-model maps and missing-slot values differ. The primary display uses boundary 38; the alternative is not suppressed. This is a conditional minimum within the 102-coordinate model and chosen wording, not an exhaustive proof over other message lengths or plaintexts.

For the primary frame, the exact observed substitutions are source **31 V→F, 32 F→V, 34 D→X, 37 G→X, 53 V→X and 79 D→X**. The K-like source glyph at **24** is filled with X; the additional coordinate at boundary **38** is D. At the equal boundary-37 alternative, the inserted value is X, with its different observed repair map retained in the certificate.

| Primary scope | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| New physical source records | 1 |
| Occupied source slots / valid coordinates | 101 / 100 |
| Modeled coordinates / plaintext positions | 102 / 51 |
| Fixed conditional raw / edited labels | 47 / 51 |
| Observed substitutions | 6 |
| Source-glyph fills / additional-coordinate fills | 1 / 1 |
| Observed-coordinate deletions or moves | 0 |

The source and candidate permit the restored question, but the edition does not add a first name for Seifert, identify a historical person, specify the pump's later use, or establish that it was delivered.

## Credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The earlier OCR body and its unchanged-key decoding remain in [separate provenance files](../../experiments/benzol_pump_query/prior_candidates.json). The missing coordinate is a source-length issue, not a claim that the earlier OCR simply omitted a visible fifth glyph. Verification replays all insertion prices, every source/model mapping and edit, the complete roundtrip, and exact readable-label preservation.

```sh
python experiments/benzol_pump_query/verify.py --verify
python experiments/benzol_pump_query/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf
```

The optional PDF check verifies the original scan digest and exact crop pixels. Successful re-encryption proves compatibility with the stated source model and proposed wording; it does not establish a unique historical loss location.

# p155: Asgard's return to Poti

[Case index](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Asgard is expected at Poti to collect troops. The same message reports that
Asgard and Tresivolus arrived at the sender's port on 7 November and asks for
acknowledgment. The port is not named in the ciphertext. Hopman's diary
places the two ships at Sevastopol on that date, with orders to return to
Poti; its spelling *Tresivolos* differs from the telegram's `TRESIVOLUS`.
[Diary passages and source references](../../data/reviews/hopman_context.json).

## Completed reading

**Readable German — the two-part conditional completion:**

> Dampfer Asgard eintrifft Poti Poti voraussichtlich in nächsten Tagen, um dort befindliche Truppen abzuholen. Asgard Asgard, Tresivolus Tresivolus, 7.11. hier eingelaufen. Empfang bestätigen. BQZ K.

The earlier bracketed reconstruction is now accompanied by exact repaired
streams and coordinate costs. Part A1 retains its native frame. Part A2
requires one missing coordinate; **two equally priced placements** give the
same complete stream. The repeated names, `7.11`, and `BQZ K` closing remain
as transmitted.

| Part | Received / modeled coordinates | Raw fixed positions | Completed positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills | Added-slot fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| p155 A1 | 170 / 170 | 84/85 | 85/85 | 2 | 1 | 0 |
| p155 A2 | 185 / 186 | 90/93 | 93/93 | 3 | 2 | 1 |
| Total | 355 / 356 | 174/178 | 178/178 | 5 | 3 | 1 |

<details>
<summary>Completed two-part stream</summary>

**Edited output — complete two-part proposal; 5 observed substitutions, 3 source-mask fills and 1 added-slot fill:**

```text
DAMPFERASGARDEINTRIFFTPOTIPOTIVORAUSSICHTLICHINNAECHSTENTAGENUMDORTBEFINDLICHETRUPPENABZUHOLENXASGARDXASGARDXTRESIVOLUSXTRESIVOLUSX7X11XHIEREINGELAUFENXEMPFANGBESTAETIGENXXBQZXKX
```

The part boundary falls between `TRUPPEN` and `ABZUHOLEN`. Nothing is added
to join the two plaintexts.

</details>

### Source-supported wording

A1 already supplies **ASGARD** from complete observed pairs. A2 has both a
complete occurrence and `A?GARD`; the repeated name supports the S fill.
Three other telegrams provide the vocabulary in their raw readings:

| Proposed wording | Independent observed wording | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `VORAUSSICHTLICH` | `RUECKUNFT VORAUSSICHTLICH 0100` | [p182 B](../radio/return_time_and_vehicle_attempt.md#p182-b) |
| `BEFINDLICHE` | `BEFINDLICHEN TRUPPEN` | [p222 A2](../military/liman_troop_reports.md#a2-special-requirements-and-acknowledgment) |
| `EMPFANG BESTAETIGEN` | `EMPFANGBESTAETIGEN` | [p129 A8](../military/transylvania_situation_report.md#p129-a8) |

These witnesses establish vocabulary used elsewhere in the collection.
They are not copies of this telegram. The [completion certificate](../../experiments/p155_shipping_completion/certificates.json)
records every observed pair in the cited words and in the repeated name.

### Coordinate costs and tied gap placements

All source indices are zero-based. In A1, source 97 `G`→`A` and source 118
`X`→`G` repair `IO?AUSSICHTLICH` and `BEFINDLBCHE`; source 88, printed `C`,
is filled with `D` to supply R in `VORAUSSICHTLICH`.

For A2, the completed body requires source 174 `V`→`A`, source 175 `A`→`D`,
and fills at the two printed dashes: 177→`X`, 178→`D`. The final repair has
two equivalent source accounts:

| Added coordinate before source | Added value | Further observed substitution |
| ---: | :---: | --- |
| 183 | `A` | Source 183 `D`→`X` |
| 184 | `X` | Source 183 `D`→`A` |

Each produces the same 186-coordinate witness with 3 observed substitutions,
2 printed-mask fills and 1 added-slot fill. Pricing this fixed body at all
186 gap positions gives exactly these two minima. The earlier raw variants
at 183, 185, 184 and 0 remain in the original certificate; the new comparison
is conditional on the proposed body.

## Most likely reading

<details>
<summary>Earlier bracketed reconstruction</summary>

**Readable German — conditional reconstructed body; the source-frame assumption remains explicit:**

> Dampfer Asgard eintrifft Poti Poti [voraussichtlich] in naechsten Tagen, um dort [befindliche] Truppen [abzuholen]. Asgard Asgard, Tresivolus Tresivolus, 7.11. hier eingelaufen. [Empfang bestaetigen]. BQZ K.

The earlier reading already proposed the ordinary words and repeated
Asgard name. The present supplement verifies those choices without claiming
a newly discovered shipping event.

</details>

## Literal readings

The [source](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p155_A.png) gives `POT v NKJ`,
onward to `COS GENERAL V KRESS`, origin `2035 (7)`, and interception on
8 November at 02:28. The two parts have advertised lengths170 and 186.
A1's invalid `C` and A2's two printed dashes remain in the literal record.

A1, without insertion, deletion, or valid-coordinate substitution:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DAMPFERASGARDEINTRIFFTPOTIPOTIIO?AUSSICHTLICHINNAECHSTENTAGENUMDORTBEFINDLBCHETRUPPEN
```

</details>

A2, conditional on inserting one unknown coordinate before original position 183:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional insertion before original source position 183:**

```text
ABZUHOLE?XASGARDXA?GARDXTRESIVOLUSXTRESIVOLUSX7X11XHIEREINGELAUFENXE?4FANGBESTLUTIGENXXBQZXKX
```

</details>

The [original certificate](../../data/certificates/p155.json) preserves all
four earlier source-frame variants. The [new supplement](../../experiments/p155_shipping_completion/inputs.json)
adds the explicitly repaired readings; it leaves the original transcription,
raw outputs and published Nov7–9 square unchanged.

## Consequence for p73

This message follows the same radio route as p73 and was received five
minutes later, but the origin dates differ. p73 has an October 26 heading
and `0911 (26)`; p155 has `2035 (7)`. Reception-time proximity therefore
does not establish a common original-date key. The [p73 source-context record](../../data/reviews/p73_source_context.json)
retains the dating evidence and the unsuccessful search for an October 25–27
companion.

## Reproduction and credit

```sh
python -m adfgvx.context155
python experiments/p155_shipping_completion/verify.py --verify
```

Source edition, comparison and conditional completion: **icekylinx and
GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The Nov7–9 period key retains the published credit of
Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker. The original source certificate and
bracketed reading remain available alongside the new coordinate account.

# p164 A4 — cavalry report

[Case index](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** Conditional editorial reconstruction of a contextual sibling, outside the 22-target challenge. **Contribution:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. It does not change the partial status of [p164a](../p164a.md) or [p164b](../p164b.md).

## Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> Vorstoss der abgesessenen 4./1. G. Drag. stiess westl. MIRCO auf staerkeren Gegner. MIRCO wurde vom Gegner besetzt.

**Meaning:** An advance by dismounted cavalry met stronger opposition west of `MIRCO`; `MIRCO` was occupied by the enemy.

**Notes:** The entire sentence is an editorial reconstruction requiring **nine known-coordinate substitutions and thirteen erasure fills**. The nine printed glyphs were independently rechecked and support the literal transcription. These proposed changes therefore alter historical source evidence. `MIRCO` remains unidentified; it is not silently replaced by `MIROC` or a modern place name.

## Source reading

The source has 198 coordinate slots, including 13 erasures, although its header advertises 188. Under the audited November 7–9 key, with no repairs, **87 of 99 plaintext characters are fixed**:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
VORG?OSSDX?A?GESESSEK?NX4X1XGXD?AGXGTIESSWES?LX?IRCOAUFGTAER0EREFGEGNERX?IY?OWURDE?OMGEGNER??SETSTX
```

</details>

## Unit interpretation

Expanding `4./1. G. Drag.` as the 4th Squadron of the 1st Guard Dragoon Regiment is a contextual inference. The unit is attested in the US War Department's [1920 divisional history, p. 689](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/55620/55620-h/55620-h.htm#Page_689), under the 218th Division: its 1917 column names the Guard Dragoon regiment, while its 1918 column omits “Guard.” This association does not verify the wording or locate the squadron on the intercept date.

## Exact edit certificate

All indices below are zero-based positions in the original 198-slot source.

| Source index | Printed | Proposed | Plaintext effect |
|---:|:---:|:---:|---|
| 39 | G | X | G → S in VORSTOSS |
| 51 | V | X | K → N in ABGESESSENEN |
| 115 | D | G | 0 → K in STAERKEREN |
| 128 | X | F | S → Z in BESETZT |
| 135 | X | G | F → N in STAERKEREN |
| 136 | G | D | Y → R in the second MIRCO |
| 172 | G | X | G → S in STIESS |
| 174 | G | X | G → S in AUF STAERKEREN |
| 179 | V | D | X → E in DER |

Erasure fillings are `1:G, 7:A, 8:G, 9:D, 14:A, 50:A, 61:D, 68:G, 69:G, 73:G, 141:V, 142:D, 176:D`. No coordinate is inserted or deleted.

The exact unspaced proposed plaintext is:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
VORSTOSSDERABGESESSENENX4X1XGXDRAGXSTIESSWESTLXMIRCOAUFSTAERKERENGEGNERXMIRCOWURDEVOMGEGNERBESETZTX
```

</details>

Its exact re-encryption is:

<details>
<summary>Re-encryption witness</summary>

**Re-encryption witness — ciphertext for the stated edited proposal:**

```text
AGXXDXAAGDDDVGAXDADGFDVDDDDFDGVVVXDDVDVXGVGXVVGXXGAXXDFVAXAFXDAAFDVDGGDVVGXXAADDDFGVGDFDDVXGVGVGVGVDXGDVDDFAVADGVXDGDVDXVGVVVVXVFVVAVVXGDFVXDVDXXVVVXDDVDDADGFDXXVGFDGXGVXXVXDXGDGVDDVDAADADXDDDGDXAXV
```

</details>

An eight-substitution alternative omits the change at source 179 and leaves source 50 erased. It therefore reads `VORSTOSSDX?ABGESESSENEN...`, with the remaining plaintext character restricted to `02ACLR`. The certificate retains all six conditional completions.

## What this changes

The source fragment `A?GESESSEK?N` can be reconstructed as `ABGESESSENEN` with one known-coordinate substitution and three erasure fills. Consequently, its internal `ESSEK` substring is not sufficient evidence for identifying Osijek. MIRCO remains unidentified; no geographic substitution or expansion is adopted. The apparent height 828 in part 5 does not determine the interpretation.

The [certificate](../../data/certificates/p164_A4_editorial.json) and [standalone verifier](../../adfgvx/editorial164.py) reproduce the raw reading, each explicit edit, all six partial completions, and the complete proposed plaintext's re-encryption. The verifier uses coordinate arithmetic only. Successful verification confirms the consequences of the proposed edits, not their historical truth.

```sh
python3 -m adfgvx.editorial164
```

Source: [Childs p164](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p164_ACD.png).

## Geographic lead

[The geographic review](../../data/reviews/p164_geography.json) records Martin's 1920 regimental history: on October 24 it places twenty men of a closely matching 4th Squadron/1st Prussian Dragoon designation at Mosnac, near the later Miroc fighting. Its subsequent chronology and the different report date prevent a firm identification. Changing both `MIRCO` occurrences to `MIROC` would additionally alter three known source coordinates and one guessed fill. No such normalization is adopted. The relevant French daily journal is identified as an archive lead, with its entries still uninspected.

# p186 A1/A2 — Earlier Russian and Polish traffic instruction

[Case guide](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Source image](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p186_A.png) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** Earlier corpus reading, source-checked under `Nov13-15b`.
**Present source and coordinate review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

Norbert's [comment 53, 3 May 2017](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-878079)
identifies this earlier transmission and says it had already been deciphered
by the Lasry team. Both its known status and that attribution are retained.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German — body interpretation; the final ellipsis omits the unresolved administrative ending shown in Part 2:**

> Russischen und poln. Heereverkehr voll erfassen. Wichtiges, besond. aus poln.
> Verkehr, ueber OHL-Station verziffert funken. Soweit Fernschreiber-Verbdg.
> nicht arbeitet, Rest schriftlich. [Nachchef] […]

**Meaning:** Monitor Russian and Polish army traffic comprehensively. Radio
important material, especially Polish traffic, in cipher through the Supreme
Army Command station. Where the teleprinter connection is not working, send
the rest in writing. The administrative ending remains incomplete.

Word divisions and punctuation are editorial. Part 1's readable completion
uses three erasure fills supported by corresponding words in [p187](../p187.md).
The source's abbreviated `BESOND` and `HEEREVERKEHR` are retained here; this
transmission is not identical to p187/p187b.

## Part 1 — RICHI-170

The 170 received positions contain three printed erasures. The raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
RUSS?SCHENUN?POLNHEEREVERKEHRVOLLERFASSENWICHTIGESBESONDAUSPOLNVERKEHRUEBEROHLSTA?ION
```

</details>

Filling received indices 147, 148 and 149 with `DAA` gives the displayed body
without changing any known coordinate. This is a source-supported word
proposal under the fixed key, not an observation of the missing glyphs.

## Part 2 — RICHI-174

Two ambiguous printed glyphs are kept unknown in the conservative layer.
It fixes **80 of 87 positions**:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
VERZIFFERTFUNKENSOWEITFERNSCHREIBERVERBDGNICHTARBEITETXRESTSCHRIFTLICH?ACHCHEF??1???1?X
```

</details>

The repeated known numeral `1` belongs to this reading. It cannot simply be
copied into the [p187b](../p187b.md) suffix, which has a different length and
different shared-cell constraints. This published-key layer supplies no
additional numerical label.

### Conditional shared-key reference labels

The [shared Nov13–15b interpretation](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/coverage.md)
(`XX=Q`, `VG=2`) fixes **82 of 87 positions** in the conservative source,
with the administrative ending **`CHEF??1??212X`**. Its number remains
unidentified.

The two added digits use intact `VG` pairs at plaintext positions 83 and 85,
from source positions `[173, 10]` and `[64, 107]` (zero-based). The source
masks at 20 and 29 remain, and the coordinate-edit cost is unchanged. These
labels inherit the shared-key interpretation; five positions remain unresolved.

## Evidence

The header is `SU v LP (06.33 a.m., November 13th); 20.50 (13/11); 2 TLE`.
The records are printed p186 / PDF page 189. Their full transcriptions and
earlier credit are in [the source record](../../data/reviews/p186_chi_parallel.json).
The [conservative source audit](../../experiments/source_followup/p186_source_and_suffix_delta.json)
contains the two glyph masks, the three proposed fills and exact word maps.

```sh
python3 experiments/source_followup/audit_p186.py --verify
python3 experiments/nov13_joint_completion/verify_coverage.py --verify
```

# p189 C — December-key instruction

[Case guide](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Source image](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p189_C.png) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** A supplementary contextual message, outside the 22-target challenge.
The unchanged published `Nov13-15b` key fixes **61 of 62 raw plaintext positions**.
**Source transcription and present review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.
The period key retains [George Lasry's published attribution](../../data/keys.json).

## Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> [Unloesbare Funksprueche] nach Dezemberschluessel entziffern. Irrtum.

**Meaning:** “Decipher unreadable radio messages using the December key.”
The separate closing word `IRRTUM` means “error” or “mistake.” Its precise
function in this transmission is not established. Word spacing, punctuation
and capitalization are editorial.

The two bracketed words need **two known-coordinate substitutions**, with no
erasure fills or changes to the key. The rest of the proposed text is directly
decoded. In particular, **DEZEMBER and IRRTUM are source-supported** despite the
printed **15 November 1918** date. The edition does not replace December with
November, correct the date, or infer a cancellation procedure.

## Unchanged source reading

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
UNLOESBA?EHUNKSPRUECHENACHDEZEMBERSCHLUESSELENTZIFFERNXXIRRTUM
```

</details>

The unknown at plaintext index 8 uses square cell `VG`, whose remaining domain
is `234789QY`. `R` already occupies `FG`. The proposed `UNLOESBARE` therefore
requires a received-coordinate change; assigning `R` to the unknown cell would
violate the square's injectivity. The raw `HUNKSPRUECHE` likewise needs an
explicit change to become `FUNKSPRUECHE`.

| Source index, zero based | Printed | Proposed | Plaintext effect |
| ---: | :---: | :---: | --- |
| 23 | V | F | `VG` becomes `FG`, giving `R` at plaintext index 8. |
| 62 | A | D | `AA` becomes `DA`, giving `F` instead of `H` at index 10. |

The other **122 source coordinates are unchanged**. The candidate has the same
62 positions as the direct reading and re-encrypts exactly to the stated
two-substitution reconstruction. No missing square cell is completed.

## Source

Printed p189 / PDF p192, section C:
`NKJ v LP (9.14 a.m., November 15th); 1000 (15); RIZI-124`.
The route is LP to NKJ. The 124 legible coordinates agree with the declared
length:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription:**

```text
XXVFV FFDVG VGFFV AGVAA XDAVF XXGXX VXAAF GDFGV
XXFVV AFAFA FFAGV DVAXV DFAXF GXDFF DFFFA AVXGG
VFFAA XVAVA XFAGF AVXDV AFXAG FAGFA AFAFG XGAXX
XFXX
```

</details>

The retrieval corpus omitted the final visible `XFXX` and contained only 120
coordinates. Restoring that row corrects the OCR transcription; it does not
insert conjectural characters into the historical source. The crop was
independently inspected, and an independent column-offset implementation
reproduces the direct decode and candidate edit map.

## Relationship to the challenge

This source was retrieved as a short local ciphertext resemblance to
[p132](../p132.md). Both messages concern the handling of radio traffic, but
their instructions and keys differ. The match does **not** establish a repeated
transmission or supply new fixed letters to p132's damaged wording.

It is also distinct from the [p189 challenge fragment](../p189.md), whose
transport context comes from a p185 near-parallel. Page number alone does not
identify a message.

## Verify and credit

The [source and edit certificate](../../experiments/source_similarity_extension/source_inspection.json)
retains all 62 coordinate maps, the unassigned-cell domain, the literal source,
the OCR comparison and direct decodes under three published November keys.
The [retrieval report](../../experiments/source_similarity_extension/README.md)
explains how this witness was selected.

```sh
python3 experiments/source_similarity_extension/check_source.py --verify
```

George Lasry's period-key publication is credited separately from this source
inspection, OCR correction and editorial audit by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.
No first-decipherment priority is claimed for this supplementary corpus message.

# Radio instructions: p77 B and p134 B

[Case index](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** Two source-checked contextual records, outside the 22-target challenge. The established period keys are credited to the earlier corpus researchers. Source transcription, comparison, and verification: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first decipherment priority is claimed for these wider-corpus messages.

## p77 B — call-sign instruction for Konia

**Readable German — most likely reading:**

> Nachrichtenchef drahtet mit 4 B 49338: Funkerabtlg. Osmanie. Zu dort 2032: [Funkerabtlg.] Konia erhaelt Rufnamen Nathan Otto Karl. Wellen von dort festlegen. Admiralstab 17830 D 2.

**Meaning:** The signals chief reports that the radio detachment at Konia receives the call sign spelled Nathan–Otto–Karl. The recipient is to determine the wavelengths. Administrative references and the Admiralty Staff signature are retained.

All **350 received coordinates** give **175 plaintext characters** and re-encrypt exactly under `Oct28-31`. The raw `FUNKERABT3G` is normalized in brackets; no source coordinate is silently changed. The directly decoded formula `ERHAELT RUFNAMEN` followed by spelling words independently supports the revised interpretation of [p146](../p146.md). This October message concerns Konia and does not establish Kerch's November date.

Source: [Childs p77 B](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p77_B.png), PDF page 80; header `OSM v LP (6.47 a.m., October 30th); SS BERLIN 29/10 1922; RICHI-350`. Under the source's header convention, LP is the sender and OSM the recipient.

## p134 B — repeat a fourth-period telegram in the fifth

**Readable German — most likely reading:**

> [Eilvese]. [Telegr.] [der] 4. [Periode] in 5. wiederholen. OSM.

**Meaning:** A message apparently directed to Eilvese asks for a fourth-period telegram to be repeated in the fifth period.

The **102 source slots** yield **50 of 51 fixed characters** under `Nov4-6`:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
EGLV2SSEXT?LEGRXDE8X4XPORIODEINX5XWIEDERHOLENXOSMXX
```

</details>

The malformed final glyph of group 16, source index 79, remains unknown. The place name and other corrected words are editorial. The repeated instruction independently supports the corresponding vocabulary in [p132](../p132.md); it is not an identical copy, does not establish `VORHER`, and does not explain what the numbered periods denote.

Source: [Childs p134 B](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p134_B.png), PDF page 137; header `LP v NKJ (4.02 a.m., November 6th); 0530 (6); RIZI-102`.

## Evidence and verification

# Transport traffic — p185/p189 and parallel messages

[Case index](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status: source-preserving partial reading under a plausible, unproved gap geometry.** This supplementary **p185 D** intercept is outside the 22-message challenge. Its header reads `CM v CZ (20.15 p.m., November 13th), 21.00, RIZI-198`, but the body contains 193 slots: 192 valid ADFGVX coordinates and one literal `Y`. The raw `Y` is retained in the source layer and treated as one unknown coordinate in analysis.

**Current transcription, comparison and verification:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. Historical keys and source witnesses retain the provenance recorded in the certificate.

## Most likely readings

| Record | Readable German text | Meaning and uncertainty |
|---|---|---|
| p185 D, conditional word completion | […] marschiert Lastautos morgen 1500 ueber DHFN. Abmarschbereit sein. […] Seifert. | The reconstructed clause concerns trucks moving tomorrow via `DHFN` and orders readiness to depart. Three coordinate substitutions and three fills complete the words; the opening and closing instruction remain damaged. |
| p193 E | Kleiner Federwagen zu[m] Anhaengen hier. Kommt Auto. | A small sprung cart for attachment is available; the message mentions a car. Punctuation and the `M` are editorial. |
| p194 A / p196 B composite | Abtransport in verabredeter Weise Freitag DHFN 1?00. Wagen bereithalten. Marschziel Hanau. Seifert. | Departure as arranged on Friday; keep vehicles ready; Hanau is the destination. Every selected coordinate is attested in one of the two witnesses, but one time digit remains unknown. |
| p197 E / p198 C | Lastauto 1?00 abgefahren. Ich bleibe mit ? Mann bis Sonntag. Alles Gute, auf Wiedersehen. [Seifert]. Gruss Bocho. | The truck has departed; the sender remains with an unknown number of men until Sunday. The signature is normalized editorially; neither witness spells it exactly this way. |
| p189 E, conditional shared digit | Ja, Hebepumpe aus Blech. Kommen 2 Autos. Hier 2 Anhaenger. | Two vehicles and two trailers; VG=2 and one invalid-coordinate fill complete the short message. |

Brackets mark editorial interpretations; `?` retains an unresolved character. `DHFN`, `STATMET` and `BOCHO` are not expanded or geographically identified. The exact readings and witness disagreements follow below.

### Two vehicles and two trailers — p189 E

**Readable German — conditional shared VG=2, with one invalid-coordinate fill:**

> Ja, Hebepumpe aus Blech. Kommen 2 Autos. Hier 2 Anhaenger.

The [award-class interpretation](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md#the-award-class)
supplies **VG=2** to both count fields, at plaintext positions **26 and 37**.
The word `ANH?ENGER` has the partial pair `V?`, with the invalid printed `B`
at source position **81**. Filling it as **V** gives `ANHAENGER`. This takes
the native 94-slot message from **44 to 47/47** fixed positions: two digits
from the shared square and one ordinary-word fill, with **no observed-coordinate
substitution**. The source's `B` remains visible in the literal transcription.
Indices are zero-based. [Exact completion and source mapping](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/transport_certificate.json).

## p185 D source and gap model

![Literal p185 D source excerpt](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p185_D.png)

We enumerated all 194 possible positions for a contiguous block of five missing coordinates under the audited November 13–15b key. Every valid received coordinate remains unchanged and in its original order. No missing coordinate or unknown square cell is filled.

## Conditional result

Inserting five erasures before source index **55**, a printed group boundary, gives this exact partial plaintext:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional five-coordinate gap before source index 55:**

```text
STATMETXMARSCHIERTLCST?UT?SMORGEN1500UEBERDHFNXAB?A6SCHBE?EITSEIN?VS6GROV?AN?IERE?XBITTEF6EXSEIFERT
```

</details>

Under this geometry, **91 of 99 characters are fixed**. The eight unresolved positions consist of six positions touched by uncertain coordinates and two positions using unassigned square cells. The fixed portions include `MARSCHIERT`, `MORGEN1500UEBERDHFN`, and `SEIFERT`; malformed portions are retained literally. `DHFN` and `STATMET` are not expanded into place or station names.

This is a conditional result. The strongest composite language score selects position 55, but a conventional plaintext quadgram score selects position 57:

| Gap before source index | Composite ranking score | Plaintext quadgram mean |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 55 | 24.910328 | -6.041730 |
| 56 | 22.691041 | -6.070230 |
| 57 | 22.641029 | -5.987314 |

These are heuristic scores, not confidence probabilities. All 194 positions are arithmetically compatible with the received symbols. Positions 159 and 160 produce the same masked ciphertext because the inserted gap can exchange places with the existing unknown `Y` slot. There are 193 distinct masked ciphertexts. No plaintext character is fixed across all 194 geometries. The three leading composite-score candidates share 89 fixed characters, but that selected subset is not a confidence set.

### Truck movement and readiness

The [word-completion certificate](../../experiments/p185_readiness_completion/README.md)
restores the vehicle noun and readiness instruction within the existing gap-55
frame:

**Readable German — conditional excerpt; the ellipses omit the damaged opening and closing instruction:**

> […] marschiert Lastautos morgen 1500 ueber DHFN. Abmarschbereit sein. […] Seifert.

The wording concerns trucks moving the following day via `DHFN` and instructs
the recipient to be ready to depart. `STATMET`, the transmitted `1500` and the
closing command remain unexpanded in the exact text. The unusual word order
is preserved.

`LCST?UT?S → LASTAUTOS` costs two observed-coordinate substitutions and a fill
of the printed `Y`. `AB?A6SCHBE?EITSEIN → ABMARSCHBEREITSEIN` costs one
substitution and two fills inside the five-coordinate gap. The edition fixes
**95/99 positions**, up from 91; three inserted coordinates remain unknown.
The same conversation has native `LASTAUTO` in p198 C, `ABMARSCH` in p193 C
and `BEREIT` in p196 B. These support the vocabulary without establishing an
identical sentence in another reception.

<details>
<summary>Exact conditional word completion</summary>

**Edited output — gap 55, three observed-coordinate substitutions, one printed-glyph fill and two missing-slot fills:**

```text
STATMETXMARSCHIERTLASTAUTOSMORGEN1500UEBERDHFNXABMARSCHBEREITSEIN?VS6GROV?AN?IERE?XBITTEF6EXSEIFERT
```

</details>

A separate lexical check masks the numerical field, opening designation and
closing instruction. Among all 194 gap positions, **52–55** tie at the minimum
of three observed substitutions. The readable clause therefore remains
conditional on the retained gap-55 frame; the word repairs do not prove its
geometry.

```sh
python experiments/p185_readiness_completion/verify.py --verify
```

## Independent transport context

Six additional source-checked intercepts decrypt directly with the same historical key. They retain every literal garble and unresolved square cell:

- **p193 E, November 14:** `KLEINERFEDERWAGENZU?ANHAENGENHIERXKOMMTAUTOX`
- **p194 A, November 14, header `CM v CZ`:** `ABTRANSPORTINVERABREDETERWEISEFREITCGDHFN1?00XWAGENBERE?THALTENXMARSCHZIELHANAUXSEIFERT`
- **p196 B, November 15, header `CM v CZ`:** `ABTRANSPORTINVERABREDETERWEISEFREITAGDHFN1?00XWAGENBEREITHALTENXMARSCHZIELHANAUXSEI?ERT`
- **p197 E, November 15, header `CM v CZ`:** `LASTAUTO1?00A?GEFAHRENXICHBLEIBEMIT?MANNBISSOHNTAGXALLESGUTEAUFWIEDERSEHENXSE?FERTXGRUSSBOCHO`
- **p198 C, November 15, header `CM v CZ`:** `LASTAUTO1?00ABGEFAHRENXICHBLEIBEMIT?MANNBISSONNTAGXALLESGUTEAUFWIEDERSEHENXSEHFERTXGRUSSBOCHO`
- **p189 E, November 15, header `CZ v CM`:** `JAHEBEPUMPEAUSBLECHXKOMMEN?AUTOSXHIER?ANH?ENGER`. This is a different intercept from the p189 challenge target.

The p194/p196 pair repeats `DHFN` and names `HANAU` as the march destination. It has 171 of 174 raw coordinates in common; disagreements are at indices 82 (`K/X`), 167 (`X/V`), and 173 (`D/G`). The p197/p198 pair agrees at 183 of 186 coordinates, differing at indices 59 (`V/A`), 63 (`A/V`), and 67 (`G/A`). Neither lorry-message copy supplies an exact `SEIFERT` signature; `SEHFERT` is not silently corrected.

For the transport-order pair, a separately labelled source-supported composite takes `X` at index 82 and `V` at index 167 from p196 while retaining p194's `D` at index 173. It reads:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional source-supported composite of the p194 and p196 witnesses:**

```text
ABTRANSPORTINVERABREDETERWEISEFREITAGDHFN1?00XWAGENBEREITHALTENXMARSCHZIELHANAUXSEIFERT
```

</details>

This composite fixes 86 of 87 characters. It makes an editorial choice
between disagreeing source witnesses, with every chosen value attested in
at least one. The certificate retains all four combinations of the two
disagreements between valid coordinates. The planned-time cell `FV`
remains unassigned.

Under the separate shared VG=2 interpretation, the reported-hour cell
`AF` cannot also be 2. If the departure occurred on the report's date
before its `13.45` origin time, `1?00` therefore becomes **13:00**. That
chronological assumption is kept separate from the source-supported
composite. The [linked-field comparison](transport_197_198.md#linked-number-fields)
also shows why this reading cannot be combined with the earlier extra
assumption that the reported departure was no earlier than the planned one.

The [certificate](../../data/certificates/p185_D_transport.json) contains every gap geometry, its full plaintext domains, exact source-to-plaintext mapping, all six direct context readings, both near-parallel comparisons, and the conditional composite. The [standalone verifier](../../adfgvx/transport.py) recomputes all 194 constraint sets and exact coordinate roundtrips without a language model. It checks the consistency of the stored ranking order but does not recompute the heuristic scores. The [portable ranking script](../../experiments/known_key/README.md) reproduces both complete rankings from a pinned upstream model; every stored score matched exactly in the recorded environment.

```sh
python3 -m adfgvx.transport
```

This analysis does not fully solve p189 and does not add a solved item to the 22-message total.

Four [additional p197/p198 witnesses](transport_197_198.md) now connect the
conversation with equipment for Darmstadt, a lorry, a trailer and a petrol
pump. Their duplicate-group and missing-coordinate hypotheses have separate
source and arithmetic certificates.

Source images: [p189](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p189_context.png), [p193](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p193_context.png), [p194](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p194_context.png), [p196](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p196_context.png), [p197](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p197_context.png), [p198](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p198_context.png). Header order is `recipient v sender`; see [source conventions](../../sources/README.md).
