# Odessa consular routing and a Magdeburg wagon-sale instruction

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Two native parts give the consular and export-company routing of an instruction involving the sale of a railway wagon. The primary edition retains the opaque DAMM LADWIG phrase and all incomplete references. More fluent cargo-word proposals are priced separately rather than silently treated as source wording.

## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p201 excerpt](../../experiments/odessa_wagon_sale/sources/p201_reviewed.png) · [Inputs](../../experiments/odessa_wagon_sale/inputs.json) · [Position and change certificates](../../experiments/odessa_wagon_sale/certificates.json)

The published `Nov16-18` key is unchanged. [Original OCR records](../../experiments/odessa_wagon_sale/ocr_snapshot.json) and [reproducible comparisons with that earlier evidence](../../experiments/odessa_wagon_sale/prior_candidates.json) are preserved separately. The present edition supplies checked source framing, exact costs and readable passages; it makes no first-public-decipherment claim.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [p201 A1](#p201-a1) | 254 | 124 / 127 | 0 | 0 |
| [p201 A2](#p201-a2) | 236 | 117 / 118 | 1 | 0 |

## p201 A1

**Source transcription — header:** `A) NKJ FUER RAT (6.50 a.m., November 16th); 0700 (16) 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-254`

Under the [existing November date constraint](../../experiments/nov16_18_reference_completion/README.md),
the opening reference becomes **Nr. 8?**, raising the conditional reading
to **125/127** positions. The other reference cells remain distinct and
unassigned; no source coordinate changes.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
DEUTSCHESGENERALKONSULATODESSAXNRX??XAUSSENUKRAANDEUTSCHEENBEVOLLMAECHTIGTENODESSAXFUERAUSFUHRGESELLSCHAFTXABTXRMX?IHRTELEGRAMM
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the unchanged raw output:**

> Deutsches Generalkonsulat Odessa. Nr. ?? AUSSENUKRA. An DEUTSCHEEN Bevollmaechtigten Odessa. Fuer Ausfuhrgesellschaft. Abt. RM ? Ihr Telegramm

**Meaning:** The first part gives the German consulate at Odessa, an unresolved numbered reference, the Odessa representative and an export company as address or routing information. It then begins a reference to a previous telegram. The spelling DEUTSCHEEN and AUSSENUKRA are retained without silently normalizing them.

**Editorial limits.**

- All 254 coordinates are present in the printed source and decode without repair. The earlier OCR split the first row from the rest; the complete native body is now used.
- DEUTSCHEEN is retained with both E letters. AUSSENUKRA, ABT and RM remain unexpanded, and RM is not treated as a currency amount.
- The baseline question marks use three different cells, FD, GF and GD. The conditional layer fixes FD=8; GF and GD retain distinct values from `034679`.

## p201 A2

**Source transcription — header:** `A) NKJ FUER RAT (6.50 a.m., November 16th); 0700 (16) 2 TLE; 2 TL RICHI-236`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
?WEITAUSENDUNDACHTZIGERSUCHENWAGGONMAGDEBURGNEUNTAUSENDNEUNHUNDERTZEHNXDAMMXLADWIGBESTMOEGLICHSTZUVERKAUFENXAUSWAERTIG
```

**Edited output — 1 observed-coordinate substitution and 0 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
ZWEITAUSENDUNDACHTZIGERSUCHENWAGGONMAGDEBURGNEUNTAUSENDNEUNHUNDERTZEHNXDAMMXLADWIGBESTMOEGLICHSTZUVERKAUFENXAUSWAERTIG
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Zweitausendundachtzig. Ersuchen Waggon Magdeburg neuntausendneunhundertzehn. DAMM LADWIG bestmoeglichst zu verkaufen. Auswaertig.

**Meaning:** The continuation refers to the telegram with the spelled-out number zweitausendundachtzig and requests a sale on the best possible terms involving the wagon identified by Magdeburg and neuntausendneunhundertzehn. DAMM LADWIG remains opaque in the primary edition; it is not treated as a confirmed person, cargo description or instruction to sell the contents.

**Editorial limits.**

- The native 236-coordinate body is preserved. The initial unresolved square label is changed to Z in ZWEITAUSEND as one observed-coordinate substitution; this is not a free fill of an unknown square cell.
- Both long numbers remain spelled out exactly as recovered. No wagon identity is independently established from those words.
- The primary reading retains DAMM LADWIG. Conditional LADUNG, SAMT LADUNG and DANN LADUNG alternatives are separately priced, and none is silently substituted into the primary meaning.
- SAMT LADUNG and DANN LADUNG each require nine observed changes from the source, including the initial Z proposal; coordinate cost alone does not choose between them.

## Conditional interpretation: cargo wording

The primary reading leaves DAMM LADWIG unresolved. Replacing LADWIG with LADUNG would make a cargo reading possible, but costs four further observed-coordinate changes. The longer phrase SAMT LADUNG would suggest selling the wagon together with its load; DANN LADUNG is an equally costly alternative under the same coordinate metric. These are proposals, not independent source recoveries.

| Phrase retained or proposed | Total observed substitutions from the native source, including initial Z | Additional substitutions beyond the primary edition |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DAMM LADWIG — primary | 1 | 0 |
| DAMM LADUNG | 5 | 4 |
| SAMT LADUNG | 9 | 8 |
| DANN LADUNG | 9 | 8 |

All three conditional streams and their exact coordinate edits re-encrypt under the unchanged published key. Equal cost does not select the historical phrase. The edition therefore does not present the sale of the wagon’s contents as established. The spelled-out references remain the source’s words; neither consular routing nor a plausible commercial sentence identifies the particular wagon independently.

## Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates independently reconstruct column positions and domains, compare them with the cipher implementation, replay every priced change, and check all readable nonseparator labels. Partial readings have one consistent injective square/source-mask completion witness that re-encrypts exactly; those witness choices are not historical identifications. Source images are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/odessa_wagon_sale/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to check the original PDF and exact source-crop pixels.

The source prints `RICHI 224` but **no visible “3 TL” label**. `A3` is the catalog's positional identifier for the block between numbered parts 2 and 4. The query is kept separate from the surrounding medical passages; a shared subject or complete seven-part assembly is not assumed.

All 224 coordinates are observed. Raw, 112 positions:

```text
OELKARTELLVIFLISXNUMM3R2XDRAHTETWANNWOHINWOLCHEADRESSEMITWELCHEMSCHCFFUNSEREPARTIENVONPOTIVERLADENSINDXXDEUTKAUF
```

</details>

Five observed-coordinate substitutions yield the conservative candidate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
OELKARTELLTIFLISXNUMMER2XDRAHTETWANNWOHINWELCHEADRESSEMITWELCHEMSCHIFFUNSEREPARTIENVONPOTIVERLADENSINDXXDEUTKAUF
```

</details>

The candidate repairs `VIFLIS`, `NUMM3R`, `WOLCHE` and `SCHCFF`. The reference label `2`, `POTI` and `DEUTKAUF` remain unchanged. The raw 3 in the damaged word is retained in the certificate; no digit is globally relabeled.

# A request for thirty million kroner

[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source and verification](../../experiments/corpus_joint/README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Record:** p205 A, four parts, intercepted on 17 November 1918 with an internal `1600 (16)` time/date. **Result:** the published Nov16–18 partial key fixes **481 of 486 plaintext positions** from all **972 printed coordinates**. The financial instructions are readable; five characters in the closing references remain unknown.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> Zur Geldanforderung bei OHL: Sendung von dreißig Millionen Kronen angesichts starken Notenmangels nur in Teilbeträgen möglich. Wiener Bankverein, Wien, überweist heute telegraphisch an Oesterr.-Ungarische Bank, Kronstadt, zur Verfügung deutscher Etappenverwaltung zunächst fünf Millionen gemischter Stückelung. Drahtet, ob glatte Auszahlung erfolgte und ob dieser Betrag vorläufig gemügt [genügt]. Sonst anfordert weitere Summe bei General-Kriegskasse, Zweigstelle Berlin. K `?` BD Nr. `1???` Strich 11 `B?`.

**English meaning:** Concerning the request to the Supreme Army Command for money: a shipment of thirty million kroner can only be made in installments because banknotes are in short supply. The Wiener Bankverein in Vienna is transferring an initial five million, in mixed denominations, to the Austro-Hungarian Bank at Kronstadt for the German rear-area administration. The recipient should telegraph whether payment went smoothly and whether the amount is sufficient for the time being; otherwise, further funds should be requested from the General War Treasury's Berlin branch.

Word spacing, punctuation and capitalization are editorial. Three obvious-looking word repairs still require changes to valid printed coordinates: `Z2R → ZUR`, `ETAPPENVWRWALTUNG → ETAPPENVERWALTUNG`, and `BERL2N → BERLIN`. They are kept separate from the raw decipherment. No value is supplied for any of the five unknown closing-reference characters.

The literal A3 spelling is `GEMUEGT`, displayed as **gemügt**. The bracketed
**[genügt]** is a prose-only normalization, not a fourth coordinate repair.
The closing fields display all five unresolved positions explicitly:
one after `K`, three in `1???`, and one in `B?`. Their separator `X`
characters are represented by spacing; none of those unknown positions is
replaced by an ellipsis or a guessed digit.

## The four parts

| Part | Printed coordinates | Fixed plaintext positions | Direct result and qualification |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| A1 | 236 | 118/118 | The thirty-million-kroner request and shortage of notes; begins with literal `Z2R`. |
| A2 | 304 | 152/152 | Vienna bank, telegraphic transfer, Kronstadt and German administration; literal `ETAPPENVWRWALTUNG`. |
| A3 | 234 | 117/117 | Initial five million in mixed denominations; asks about payment and sufficiency. No editorial change. |
| A4 | 198 | 94/99 | Further requests to the General War Treasury's Berlin branch; literal `BERL2N` and five unknown reference characters. |

### Direct decipherment

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
Z2RXGELDANFORDERUNGXBEIXOHLXSENDUNGXVONXDREISSIGXMILLIONENXKRONENXANGESICHTSXSTARKENXNOTENMANGELSXNURXINXTEILBETRAEGEN
MOEGLICHXWIENERXBANKVEREINXWIENXUEBERWEISTXHEUTEXTELEGRAPHISCHXANXOESTERRXUNGARISCHEBANKXKRONSTADTXZURXVERFUEGUNGXDEUTSCHERXETAPPENVWRWALTUNGXZUNAECHSTX
FUENFXMILLIONENXGEMISCHTERXSTUECKELUNGXDRAHTETXOBXGLATTEXAUSZAHLUNGXERFOLGTEXUNDXOBXDIESERXBETRAGXVORLAEUFIGXGEMUEGTX
SONSTXANFORDERTXWEITEREXSUMMEXBEIXGENERALXKRIEGSKASSEXZWEIGSTELLEXBERL2NXKX?XBDXNRX1???STRICH11XB?X
```

</details>

The proposed word corrections cost one transmitted-coordinate substitution each: A1 index 162 `V → F`; A2 index 77 `A → G`; A4 index 90 `D → A`. Indices restart at zero for each part. All other printed coordinates are retained. The [certificate](../../experiments/corpus_joint/p205_readings.json) records every character's domain and its source offsets, including the dependencies imposed by one common injective partial square.

## Source assembly and credit

The four printed parts are reproduced in the [p205 A crop](../../experiments/corpus_joint/sources/p205_A.png). The OCR split A1 after its first eight groups and appended a nonexistent extra unknown character to A4. Joining the source's A1 lines and removing that OCR artifact restores the printed geometries of 236 and 198 coordinates; neither operation deletes a printed coordinate. A2's source group 16 is visibly `FXAFF`, replacing an OCR question mark but retaining the printed `A` that causes the `VWRWALTUNG` garble.

The historical source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed p. 205, PDF p. 208 in the [complete scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view). Its header is `NKJ v LP`, with `FUER UKS` and `O K M HERMANNSTADT`; these routing details do not change the supplied plaintext.

The period key retains the attribution in [data/keys.json](../../data/keys.json) to **George Lasry** and the historical/research work of **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**. Source assembly, review, exact coordinate audit and this edition are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment priority is claimed.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 experiments/corpus_joint/build_readings.py \
  experiments/corpus_joint/p205_inputs.json \
  experiments/corpus_joint/p205_readings.json --verify
python3 experiments/corpus_joint/verify_p205.py
```

# Order to stop premium payments and inform subordinate offices

`SSD BERLIN M GST 29/10 AN BVS BEIM BVG KOSPOLI`; `0940 2 TLE`.

## p78 A1

```text
GEMAESSXFECHXROEMISCHXNEUNX52021STRICH2949XSINDMITABLAUFOKTOBER18SAEMTLICHEPRAEMIENZAHLUNGENAUSLANDESMITTELNEINZUSTELLEN
```

</details>

> Gemäß FECH, römisch neun, 52021 Strich 2949, sind mit Ablauf Oktober 18
> sämtliche Prämienzahlungen aus Landesmitteln einzustellen.

The continuous sequence **AUSLANDESMITTELN** supports the displayed word
boundary “aus Landesmitteln.” It is not changed to “Auslandsmitteln.”

## p78 A2

The [second part](../../experiments/premium_payment_stop/sources/p78_A2.png)

## Conditional interpretation and scope

The two-part header and consecutive part labels establish this assembly.
Across both records, **410 visible coordinates** give **205 / 205 fixed
plaintext positions**. Both unchanged outputs re-encrypt exactly, with
zero source repairs or frame changes. The message gives instructions to
stop payments and notify offices; it does not show that either step was
carried out.

Both exact bodies were already present in earlier unreviewed repository
screens. The present contribution is visual source verification,

# Ruble prices and payments above par: companions to p171 A1

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Companion source editions: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The second and third parts of the telegram whose first part was read by
**Norbert in 2017** report prices for Tsar rubles in Kiev and Warsaw, then
recommend allowing more than par for `BONS` if necessary. They complete
the subject of the earlier first-part reading without changing its priority
or its source accounting. The second part requires a substantial, explicitly
conditional layout reconstruction; the third part needs only two printed
erasure fills.

The source is Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
[printed p171 A2–A3, PDF p174](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [three-part section](../../experiments/ruble_rate_companions/sources/p171_A.png)
is headed:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
9th NOVEMBER, 1918.
A) COS v NKJ (1.58 a.m., November 10th)
COS POT FUR GENERAL VON KRESS 1425 (9/11) 3 TLE
```

</details>

Only A2 and A3 are new physical source records in this package. A1 remains
in [the canonical challenge case](../p171.md), credited to Norbert, with
Max Baertl's later editorial `KURSE STARK` separately identified.

## A2: what the telegram reports about ruble prices

Under the conditional layout described below, the direct reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 252-slot layout after two group exclusions and one added slot:**

```text
GEMEINS0MXXINKIEWXKIEWW?RDENFUERHUNDERTZAYENRUBEL?UNDERTVIERZIGMARKGEZAHLTXINWARSCHAUSO2LENBISHUNDERTNEUNZINMAR?GEZAHATWE?XENX
```

</details>

Six observed-coordinate substitutions, three fills of retained printed
dashes, and one fill of the added unknown coordinate give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional layout, with observed substitutions and separately priced fills:**

```text
GEMEINSAMXXINKIEWXKIEWWURDENFUERHUNDERTZARENRUBELHUNDERTVIERZIGMARKGEZAHLTXINWARSCHAUSOLLENBISHUNDERTNEUNZIGMARKGEZAHLTWERDENX
```

</details>

The opening `GEMEINSAM` continues A1's reference to Germany and the Entente.
The message reports that **140 marks were paid for 100 Tsar rubles in Kiev**,
and that **up to 190 marks were reportedly being paid in Warsaw**. These
amounts are spelled out as words, so they do not require filling the period
key's unknown digit cells. They remain reports made by this telegram, not
independently verified market-price observations. The repeated `KIEW` is
preserved.

### The source is 261 slots; the working frame is 252

The [source crop](../../experiments/ruble_rate_companions/sources/p171_A2.png)
prints `RICHI-252`, but its literal transcription contains **261 slots**.
The adopted model makes three explicit layout decisions:

1. Exclude source group 6, **`---DD`**, at positions 25–29.
2. Exclude the visibly struck-through source group 19, **`G-VFA`**, at
   positions 90–94.
3. Add one unknown coordinate within the four-character group **`DVAX`**, at
   source positions 200–203, to make a five-coordinate group.

All indices here are zero-based. Both excluded groups remain visible in the
literal transcript. Their ten slots include **six observed coordinates and
four printed erasures**. The `G-VFA` cancellation is visible; excluding
`---DD` is a further model decision and is not claimed to be uniquely
required by the typography. The source itself does not certify the added
coordinate's exact boundary.

With those two exclusions held fixed, the verifier examines **all five
boundaries** in `DVAX`:

| Source boundary for the added unknown | Known-coordinate substitutions for the full proposed text | Substitutions with places and spelled quantities masked |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 200 | 8 | 6 |
| 201 | 7 | 6 |
| 202 | 6 | 5 |
| 203 | 6 | 5 |
| 204 | 7 | 5 |

The full text has two tied minima, **202 and 203**. Both produce the same
corrected ciphertext, since the supplied `A` can lie before or after an
already observed `A`. The record uses boundary 202 as a representative and
preserves boundary 203 equally. Removing the place and quantity words from
the stencil leaves **three** ties, 202–204. This is a local check of a model
selected after the earlier readable candidate was seen, not an independent
control or a global proof of the original geometry.

## A3: authorize more than par if necessary

The third part is source-exact at **152 slots** and has two printed dashes.
Its direct reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
EMPFEHLEDAHERNOTFALLSFUE?BONSAUCHMEHRALSPARIXPARIB?WILLIGENXXWALLERXWALLERXX
```

</details>

Filling those two dashes, with no observed-coordinate change, yields:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
EMPFEHLEDAHERNOTFALLSFUERBONSAUCHMEHRALSPARIXPARIBEWILLIGENXXWALLERXWALLERXX
```

</details>

The sender, `WALLER` repeated, therefore recommends authorizing more than
par for `BONS` if needed. `Bons` is retained as the message's term; the
edition does not identify a particular issuer or financial instrument.
The duplicated **`PARI X PARI`** is also preserved, without deduplication.

## Exact accounting

| Part | Literal source slots | Analysis-frame slots | Raw fixed labels | Edition fixed labels | Known-coordinate substitutions | Printed fills | Added-coordinate fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A2 | 261 | 252 | 122 / 126 | 126 / 126 | 6 | 3 | 1 |
| A3 | 152 | 152 | 74 / 76 | 76 / 76 | 0 | 2 | 0 |
| **Total** | **413** | **404** | **196 / 202** | **202 / 202** | **6** | **5** | **1** |

The table's substitutions are **additional to** A2's ten excluded slots,
six of which are observed coordinates, and its one added unknown. There
is no period-key change, source-group reordering or alteration of A1.

The [inputs](../../experiments/ruble_rate_companions/inputs.json) and
[certificate](../../experiments/ruble_rate_companions/certificates.json)
retain literal rows, all five local models, both minimizing placements,
every source exclusion and repair, complete raw/edited texts and explicit
global consistency witnesses. Re-encryption establishes costs and
compatibility, not unique historical wording.

## Prior credit

The period key is credited to **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**. Norbert's
[2017 comment 20](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-852668)
supplies A1's earlier body and repairs. Both companion bodies had already
appeared in unreviewed OCR-derived computations, and A3 was in the frozen
p73 retrieval corpus. The new work supplies source review and explicit
conditional editions; no universal first-decipherment claim is made.

```sh
python experiments/ruble_rate_companions/verify.py --verify
```

With `--pdf`, the verifier additionally checks the pinned source PDF and
regenerates all delivered crop pixels.

# State-bank accounting request and dispatched cheques

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The two-part message addresses Staatsbank Berlin, asks for an accounting amount connected to the Generalkriegskasse, and requests notice of arrival of dispatched cheques. It contains no recovered payment amount. The first part needs one explicitly modeled missing coordinate; the second part uses its complete native frame.

## Conditional digit reading

The [shared Nov7–9 digit interpretation](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) reads **am 6. gesandte Cheks** in part 2. The opposite square gives am 5.; the selected date is conditional on the cross-period reference relation and adds no source repair.

## Source and frame

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p172 excerpt](../../experiments/staatsbank_accounting_cheques/sources/p172_reviewed.png) · [Inputs](../../experiments/staatsbank_accounting_cheques/inputs.json) · [All coordinate and insertion certificates](../../experiments/staatsbank_accounting_cheques/certificates.json)

The source page heading says November 10. Section D has an interception header dated November 11 and an originating line `VON UKS LP 2127 (9/11) 2 TLE`. The published Nov7–9 key is retained with its two unresolved square cells; none of these date layers is silently normalized.

The first part advertises 198 coordinates but contains 197 occupied slots. Its sixth group is the four-coordinate `ADAX`. The model adds one unknown coordinate at one of that group’s five boundaries. It does not add a complete plaintext letter or change the period key. The second part has exactly its advertised 204 positions.

| First-part insertion boundary | Observed substitutions for displayed proposal | Printed-mask fills | Additional-slot fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 25 | 4 | 3 | 1 |
| 26 | 3 | 3 | 1 |
| 27 | 2 | 3 | 1 |
| 28 | 2 | 3 | 1 |
| 29 | 3 | 3 | 1 |

All indices are zero-based. Boundaries **27 and 28 tie**, and inserting the proposed A at either side of the already printed A gives the same completed ciphertext. The primary display uses boundary 28. This equality leaves the precise loss location unresolved; a minimum against proposed German words is not a unique historical diagnosis. The native 197-coordinate diagnostic, including its unpaired intermediate coordinate and source provenance, remains in the certificate.

## p172 D1

**Source transcription — header:** `D) LP v NKJ (6.06 p.m., November 11th); VON UKS LP 2127 (9/11) 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-198`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 198-coordinate frame after one modeled insertion; 95/99 fixed positions:**

```text
STAATSBANKBERLINXERBITTENDRINLICHOTFUNKSPRU?HFUERBEST?RREICHERABRECHNUNGBETRAGD?RGENE?ALKRIEGSKASSE
```

**Edited output — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions, 3 printed-mask fills and one additional-slot fill; the insertion remains conditional.**

```text
STAATSBANKBERLINXERBITTENDRINLICHSTFUNKSPRUCHFUEROESTERREICHERABRECHNUNGBETRAGDERGENERALKRIEGSKASSE
```

</details>

**Readable German — preserves the exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Staatsbank Berlin. Erbitten DRINLICHST Funkspruch fuer OESTERREICHER Abrechnung Betrag der Generalkriegskasse

**Meaning:** The first part addresses Staatsbank Berlin and asks urgently by radio for an accounting amount concerning the Generalkriegskasse. The proposed word OESTERREICHER is left unexpanded; it is not used to identify a person or prove an Austrian institutional connection. The request continues in part 2.

**Editorial limits.**

- The source has 197 slots against the printed 198, with the four-coordinate group ADAX. One additional modeled slot is required for the disclosed 198-coordinate frame.
- All five insertion boundaries around ADAX are retained. Boundaries 27 and 28 tie for the lowest observed-change cost under the stated word proposal and yield the same completed ciphertext; neither is asserted as the unique historical loss location.
- DRINLICHOT to DRINLICHST and BEST?RREICHER to OESTERREICHER are explicitly priced lexical proposals. DRINLICHST remains a source-length spelling without inserting a G.
- The two printed dashes in DVX-- and C-shaped glyph in ACAXA occupy source slots and are filled separately from the additional coordinate.
- The page heading says November 10, this section's interception header says November 11, and its originating line says 9/11. All three source layers are retained; the Nov7–9 key is unchanged.

## p172 D2

**Source transcription — header:** `D) LP v NKJ (6.06 p.m., November 11th); VON UKS LP 2127 (9/11) 2 TLE; 2 TL RICHI-204`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 204-coordinate frame; 97/102 fixed positions:**

```text
VOM18XBISENDEOOTOBERGEZAHLTENYAYKXFERNERA?KUNFTSANZ?IGEUEBERA??XGESANDTECHEKSXHAUPTWECHSE?AMT89240911X
```

**Edited output — 3 observed-coordinate substitutions, 4 printed-mask fills; no source coordinate inserted, removed or moved.**

```text
VOM18XBISENDEOCTOBERGEZAHLTENMARKXFERNERANKUNFTSANZEIGEUEBERAM?XGESANDTECHEKSXHAUPTWECHSELAMT89240911X
```

</details>

**Readable German — preserves the exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Vom 18 bis Ende October gezahlten Mark. Ferner Ankunftsanzeige ueber am ? gesandte CHEKS. Hauptwechselamt 89240911.

**Meaning:** The continuation concerns the amount of marks paid in the period represented by 18 through the end of October, and asks for notice of arrival of cheques dispatched on an unresolved date. The closing is Hauptwechselamt followed by the literal reference 89240911; that reference is not treated as the requested payment amount.

**Editorial limits.**

- The native 204-slot second part needs no length adjustment. OOTOBER to OCTOBER and YAYK to MARK are priced observed-coordinate changes; four printed dashes are filled explicitly.
- CHEKS is retained without supplying an extra letter. The footer 89240911 is not silently split into a date or interpreted as a currency quantity.
- The unresolved date-like position after AM is square cell VF, whose remaining domain is {5, 6}. The value is not inferred from the source date or the earlier baseline completion.
- No amount paid is recovered: the telegram asks for an amount. The first part and this continuation must not be read as reporting that the footer is a monetary total.

## Joint meaning and unresolved labels

Read together, the parts ask for a radio report of an accounting amount connected with marks paid by the Generalkriegskasse in the period represented by `18` through the end of October, followed by a request for arrival information about cheques. The prose does not turn the closing reference `89240911` into either a payment amount or a reconstructed date.

The proposed OESTERREICHER reading costs a source change and a separately disclosed erasure fill. Its administrative referent is unresolved. DRINLICHST and CHEKS remain source-length spellings; no omitted G or extra C is supplied as formatting. The question mark after AM is cell VF with domain `{5, 6}`. Choosing either digit would also constrain the other unresolved Nov7–9 square cell; no such historical assignment is made. Specifically, VF must be the opposite label from the three shared XA positions in the [p155 C1/C2 repetition edition](../radio/nov7_eighth_part_repetition.md).

| Joint account | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| Physical source records | 2 |
| Printed source slots | 401 |
| Modeled coordinates | 402 |
| Plaintext positions | 201 |
| Fixed raw labels under the stated frames | 192 |
| Fixed edited labels | 200 |
| Observed-coordinate substitutions | 5 |
| Printed-mask fills | 7 |
| Inserted-coordinate fills | 1 |

## Credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The [earlier unreviewed candidates](../../experiments/staatsbank_accounting_cheques/prior_candidates.json) and [original OCR snapshot](../../experiments/staatsbank_accounting_cheques/ocr_snapshot.json) retain their attribution separately. Verification reconstructs the source-to-model mapping, replays all five local insertion choices, prices every edit and fill, and checks all plaintext domains and readable labels. Complete candidates and an injective completion witness for the partial second part re-encrypt exactly; the witness assigns no historical digit value.

```sh
python experiments/staatsbank_accounting_cheques/verify.py --verify
python experiments/staatsbank_accounting_cheques/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf
```

Optional PDF verification checks the original scan digest and exact source-crop pixels. No chronological or monetary claim is established merely by a numerical-looking decoded label.

**Later copy evidence.** The [p172 D2 / p175 B2 reconciliation](../../experiments/accounting_copy_reconciliation/README.md)
compares the two native second parts without changing this edition. They
agree at 185 of 190 jointly observed source coordinates and have disjoint
masks. This supplies two previously unknown labels to the conservative
p175 reading; the final X remains a separately priced change in that copy.
Neither complete source pair supports the proposed M in MARK or L in
HAUPTWECHSELAMT, and the unresolved AM label remains VF in `{5, 6}`.

# A complete ZITAG stop order with reporting instruction and literal footer

[Case index](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

## p96 A

**Status:** 160/160 native raw positions fixed; 0 coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills. No frame change.

**Source and dates:** Page heading: 1st NOVEMBER, 1918; A) OSM v LP (8.45 p.m., November 1st); 1820 (1/11) BEVOLLMAECHTIGTEN PREUSS KRIEGSMINISTERIUMS KONSTANTINOPEL; RICHI-320.

![Source p96 A](../../experiments/nov1_nov2_native_dispatches/sources/p96_A.png)

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FUERXZITAGXOHNENUMMERNICHTSWEITERKAUFENUNDNICHTSWEITERVERLADENXALLESMOEGLICHSTSICHERNXZITAGXXVERANLASSTESANXKXMXDRAHTENXQXMXALLQXKRXDEPXNOX2439STRICH18XGXANCHXX
```

</details>

**Readable German — the same candidate labels with spacing and punctuation:**

> Fuer ZITAG, ohne Nummer: nichts weiter kaufen und nichts weiter verladen, alles moeglichst sichern. ZITAG. Veranlasstes an K. M. drahten. Q. M. ALLQ. KR. DEP. No. 2439 Strich 18, G. ANCH.

**Meaning:** The message instructs ZITAG to stop further purchases and loading, secure everything as far as possible, and telegraph the action taken to K.M. Its longer closing includes the literal office-like field Q M ALLQ KR DEP and reference 2439 STRICH 18 G ANCH. Those fields are preserved without silently normalizing Q to K or ALLQ to ALLG.

**Conditional interpretation and source details:** All 320 received coordinates and 160 plaintext positions decode directly. The procurement-stop body was already read from shorter p102/p103 witnesses; this newly reviewed physical record supplies a complete longer native text, including the reporting instruction. The certificate compares the nonseparator body labels with the earlier composite candidate while preserving different X separators and different transposition lengths.

### Explicit source changes

No source-coordinate substitution or source-mask fill is used.

The [shorter ZITAG witnesses](../finance/zitag_purchase_orders.md) already supplied the procurement-stop body. This additional physical record directly retains the longer instruction and closing; the older witnesses are not counted again.

### Reproducibility and attribution

The [input](../../experiments/nov1_nov2_native_dispatches/inputs.json) binds each literal source to exact PDF crops. The [certificate](../../experiments/nov1_nov2_native_dispatches/certificates.json) contains the raw paired-coordinate domains, each source change and the forward checks. The [verifier](../../experiments/nov1_nov2_native_dispatches/verify.py) checks the unchanged published keys and the live German quotations, retaining all numerical and letter labels.

Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro (2026). Childs supplies the historical collection; published reconstruction and key provenance credit Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker. Earlier repository OCR and body readings are retained in the [attribution record](../../experiments/nov1_nov2_native_dispatches/prior_candidates.json).

# ZITAG stop-orders and cancellation of procurement contracts

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source:** J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
printed pp102, 103 and 106, PDF pp105, 106 and 109. **Edition:** icekylinx
and GPT-6 Astra Pro. The [experiment](../../experiments/zitag_purchase_orders/README.md)
contains the exact crops, literal coordinates, key provenance and repair
certificates.

Three 180-coordinate messages are almost identical copies of a short
stop-order. A separate two-part message on p103 deals with a request for
rubles, permits loading already paid consignments, orders cancellation
of other contracts and asks again for Westernhagen's prompt return.
The two orders have different scopes and are not merged into one text.

All five records use the unchanged published Nov1–3 square and ranks.
There are no geometry changes or newly assigned key cells.

## p102 A

The source heading is 1 November 1918; the receipt header says November 2
without a time. It addresses the Prussian War Ministry representative
at Constantinople. All **180 coordinates** are observed. The raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FUERXZITAGVOHNENUMMERNICHTSWEITERKAUFENUNDNICHTSWEITERVERLADENALLESMOEGLICHSTSIVHERNXZITAG
```

</details>

The common readable candidate replaces source coordinates **29 G→X**
and **55 G→D**. Both replacements are observed in the other copies.

## p103 D

Header: `OSM v LP (7.08 a.m., November 2nd); 2210 (1/11)`, with the same
War Ministry representative addressee. The source prints the different
forms `VFFAX` and `FDGAG`; neither is silently changed in the transcript.
Its raw **90-character** reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FUERXZITAGXOENENUMMERNICHTSWEITERKAUFENUNDNICHTSWEITERVERLADENALLESMOEGLICHSTSICHERNXZITAG
```

</details>

Only **source index 162 G→F** is changed for the common candidate,
repairing `OENE` to `OHNE`. Both other copies witness that coordinate.

## p106 B

Header: `NKJ v LP (8.11 p.m., November 2nd); 1/11 2210`, again with the
same addressee. The printed group `XGGGG` has five characters; the earlier
OCR form `XXGGGG` was not an actual extra source coordinate. The raw body is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FUERXZITAGVOHNENUMMERNICHTSWEITERKAUFENUNDNICHTSWEITERVERLADENALLESMOEGLICHSTSICHERNXZITAG
```

</details>

The common candidate changes only **source index 29 G→X**, witnessed by
p103 D. The three literal copies differ at exactly three source positions:

| Source index | p102 A | p103 D | p106 B | Candidate |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 29 | G | X | G | X |
| 55 | G | D | D | D |
| 162 | F | G | F | F |

The candidate is:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
FUERXZITAGXOHNENUMMERNICHTSWEITERKAUFENUNDNICHTSWEITERVERLADENALLESMOEGLICHSTSICHERNXZITAG
```

</details>

**Readable German:**

> Für Zitag. Ohne Nummer. Nichts weiter kaufen und nichts weiter verladen. Alles möglichst sichern. Zitag.

Every candidate coordinate has an observed witness. This supports a
common original but does not prove which printed version is closest to
the transmission. In particular, the `X` at index 29 is a minority
reading selected for its ordinary wording, not by majority vote.

The [complete p96 A source edition](zitag_full_stop_order.md) independently
gives the same 87 nonseparator labels as this common stop-order body
without any source edit, and continues with a reporting instruction and
closing fields. Its 320-coordinate frame and separator placement differ
from these 180-coordinate copies, so this is plaintext-label corroboration,
not another vote at their source-coordinate indices.

## p103 B1

This separate message has header `FÜR COS v NKJ (0.43 a.m., November 3rd)`
and `HPTM WESTGRNHAGEN ODER KARL MÜLLER DTSCH WIRTSCHAFTS ABTLG;
1845 (1) 2 TLE`. B1 advertises and prints **274 coordinates**. Its last
group is the observed four-letter `DXGV`; the five-slot OCR version
previously spoiled its frame.

The source-aligned raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DEUTSCHKAUFDRAHTETNRX5XXBEXTAETIQEN4TEWEGRXINDEDENBESCHAFBUNG6MILLIONENRUBE1ERSUCHGXXERLEDIGTDURCHUNSERTELEGRXNRX3XDASSNUR5EREITSBEZAHLTE
```

</details>

The explicit ordinary-word candidate is:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
DEUTSCHKAUFDRAHTETNRX5XXBESTAETIGENXTELEGRXINDENENBESCHAFFUNG6MILLIONENRUBELERSUCHTXXERLEDIGTDURCHUNSERTELEGRXNRX3XDASSNURBEREITSBEZAHLTE
```

</details>

It costs **10 observed-coordinate substitutions** and no fills. Its nine
changed plaintext positions are all listed in the certificate, including
the inconvenient raw digits within damaged words. `TELEGR` remains an
abbreviation. No absent preposition, article or additional word is
inserted to regularize the syntax.

The separate fields `NR X 5`, `6 MILLIONEN` and `NR X 3` are unchanged,
with complete observed pairs. They are retained as raw square labels;
the edition does not infer a new numerical map from a plausible amount.

## p103 B2

The second part advertises and prints **254 slots**. The first group is
`GG-VF`, source group `FCXGD` contains an invalid `C`, and a later group is
`AVG-G`. The raw text is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
PARTIENVERLADENWERDENSOL?ENXSTORNIERETSAEMTLXA?DEREKONTRAKTE?EGENALLGEMEINERLAGEXERSUCHENWESTERNHAGENNOCHMALSSOFORTIGERUECKKEHR
```

</details>

The candidate fills those three printed erasures and changes no observed
coordinate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
PARTIENVERLADENWERDENSOLLENXSTORNIERETSAEMTLXANDEREKONTRAKTEWEGENALLGEMEINERLAGEXERSUCHENWESTERNHAGENNOCHMALSSOFORTIGERUECKKEHR
```

</details>

Continuing B1 with editorial spacing:

**Readable German — continuation excerpt; the preceding words are outside this display:**

> … dass nur bereits bezahlte Partien verladen werden sollen. Stornieret sämtl. andere Kontrakte wegen allgemeiner Lage. Ersuchen Westernhagen nochmals sofortige Rückkehr.

The received form `STORNIERET` and the telegraphic wording of the final
request are preserved. `WESTERNHAGEN` is complete in the uncorrected
plaintext. The heading's different `WESTGRNHAGEN` form is kept literally,
and no particular person is identified from the name alone.

The final `SOFORTIGERUECKKEHR` is spaced as **sofortige Rückkehr**. No extra
`R` or connecting preposition is supplied to regularize the telegram's
grammar. The leading ellipsis marks words before this continuation excerpt,
not an unresolved plaintext position.

## Scope and attribution

The short copies and B2 were already present as readable but unreviewed
repository screen candidates. B1 had a degraded candidate under the
wrong OCR length. Their prior bodies are frozen in the inputs file.
The source edition adds precise transcription, frame correction,
cross-copy evidence and reversible edits. A bounded check of the paper,
dissertation chapter and cached 55-comment thread located no explicit
discussion of these bodies; that does not establish first decipherment.

Together the five records contain **1,068 source slots**, **1,065 valid
coordinates** and **534 plaintext positions**. The raw models fix 531
positions; the explicit candidates fix all 534. Total cost is 14 observed
coordinate substitutions plus three printed-erasure fills. These are
edition coverage figures, not a count of newly solved cryptographic
symbols. Neither the stop-order nor the cancellation request proves
that the requested action was carried out.

```bash
python experiments/zitag_purchase_orders/verify.py --verify
python experiments/zitag_purchase_orders/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
```

# An airfield and German troops: the surviving third part on p154

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

A native third-part fragment reports an apparent airfield and German troops providing security along a named line. The exact text, three occupied source masks and two proposed coordinate corrections are retained; preceding parts and the geographical referents are not supplied from context.

## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p154 excerpt](../../experiments/airfield_german_troop_fragment/sources/p154_reviewed.png) · [Inputs](../../experiments/airfield_german_troop_fragment/inputs.json) · [Position and change certificates](../../experiments/airfield_german_troop_fragment/certificates.json)

The published `Nov4-6` key is unchanged. [Original OCR records](../../experiments/airfield_german_troop_fragment/ocr_snapshot.json) and [reproducible comparisons with that earlier evidence](../../experiments/airfield_german_troop_fragment/prior_candidates.json) are preserved separately. The present edition supplies checked source framing, exact costs and readable passages; it makes no first-public-decipherment claim.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [p154 B3](#p154-b3) | 172 | 83 / 86 | 2 | 3 |

## p154 B3

**Source transcription — header:** `B) ZON v UKS (10.04 p.m., November 7th); 3 TL RICHI-172`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
ANSCHEINENDDORT?LUGPLATZXXX2XINLINIEXMIROCXBR?APALANKA?SICHERNNURNOCHDEUTSCHETRUPPELXX
```

**Edited output — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions and 3 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
ANSCHEINENDDORTFLUGPLATZXXX2XINLINIEXMIROCXBRZAPALANKAXSICHERNNURNOCHDEUTSCHETRUPPENXX
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Anscheinend dort Flugplatz. 2. In Linie MIROC BRZAPALANKA sichern nur noch deutsche Truppen.

**Meaning:** This surviving third part says there apparently is an airfield at the previously mentioned place. Its next item says that only German troops still provide security along the line designated MIROC and the proposed BRZAPALANKA label. The earlier place reference and precise geographical identification are not supplied.

**Editorial limits.**

- The printed body is explicitly 3 TL and has exactly its advertised 172 occupied slots. This edition identifies no preceding first or second part and does not join the fragment to a different report by geographical resemblance.
- The source has ADX-F and DXU-X: two printed dashes and a U-like non-coordinate glyph occupy three slots. All three are masked in the raw layer and filled explicitly.
- The BR?APALANKA proposal is not a free fill: the raw pair G? has domain {0, 3, 6, O, Q, Y}, which excludes Z. BRZAPALANKA additionally requires source 107 G→F, together with the source-glyph fill. The place spelling remains an editorial proposal.
- TRUPPEL to TRUPPEN is the other observed-coordinate substitution. The item label 2 and MIROC remain literal.
- The Nov4–6 key is unchanged. Its successful decryption does not alter the printed November 7 header or establish the original drafting date.

## Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates independently reconstruct column positions and domains, compare them with the cipher implementation, replay every priced change, and check all readable nonseparator labels. Partial readings have one consistent injective square/source-mask completion witness that re-encrypts exactly; those witness choices are not historical identifications. Source images are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/airfield_german_troop_fragment/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to check the original PDF and exact source-crop pixels.

# Arad provisions and reported strength: the restored copies [Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md) **The second reception turns an uncertain strength field into an observed 80000 MANN.** The report addresses provisions, trains to Arad and an approach to the Hungarian government; it also gives 30000 TIERE. Its two durations, 14 and 10 days, remain in the transmitted order without an invented explanation of how they relate. The p159 A source is damaged by repeated groups and missing coordinates. The independently received [p168 E copy](danube_arad_witnesses.md#p168-e) now supplies all eleven missing values and fixes the duration separator as X, replacing the earlier optional U. The current source-linked reading has **135 of 136 fixed labels under the published partial square**. The last uncertainty in that layer is a shared footer cell, not the strength figure. **Source recovery and edition:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. The unchanged Nov7–9 key is credited to George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker. Earlier OCR and the original reconstruction remain attributed in their evidence packages. ## Conditional digit reading The [shared Nov7–9 reference interpretation](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) supplies **6** in the footer, giving **RM 1C 186 GEH** and **136/136 conditional edited labels**. The opposite assignment gives 185 GEH. This adds no coordinate change or fill to the current seven-substitution collation. The pair is originally observed in all eight retained source maps; raw p159 still ends 186 GLH before the separately priced GEH repair. ## What can be read, and under which model **Readable German — current p159 common reading; seven observed substitutions, source-supported fills, footer unresolved:** > An OHL. Verpflegung noch 14 Tage. 10 Tage. Verpfleg. Zuege nach Arad. Arad bei ungar. Regierung erwirken. STAEKE 80000 Mann, 30000 Tiere. AOK11. RM 1C18?GEH. The message asks for provision trains to Arad and for something to be obtained through the Hungarian government. It records the military and administrative work of sustaining movement: food, trains, permission and reported manpower and animals appear in one compact telegram. It does not establish that the trains arrived or independently authenticate the strength as an actual headcount. `STAEKE` stays as its six transmitted labels; no R is inserted. The repeated `ARAD` and the separate 14-day/10-day statements are retained. The common edited footer is `18?GEH`, with ?={5,6}; adopting the p168 E spelling in p159 costs one of the seven observed-coordinate substitutions. Raw p159 ends `GLH`, and that disagreement remains in the source-linked stream below.
Current p159 source-linked and explicitly repaired streams **Raw output — p159 primary geometry with all 11 missing coordinates supplied from observed p168 pairs:** ```text 0NOHLXVERPOLEGUNGNOCH14TAGEX10TAGEXXVERPFLEGXEUEGENACHARADXARADNEIUNGARXREGIERUNGERWIRKENXSTAEKE80000MANNX30000TISREXAOK11XRMX1CX18?GLHX ``` **Edited output — current p159 collation; seven observed substitutions and eleven source-supported added-coordinate fills:** ```text ANOHLXVERPFLEGUNGNOCH14TAGEX10TAGEXXVERPFLEGXZUEGENACHARADXARADBEIUNGARXREGIERUNGERWIRKENXSTAEKE80000MANNX30000TIEREXAOK11XRMX1CX18?GEHX ```
## Explicit structural cost The copy supplies source evidence for the missing values; it does not erase the reconstruction’s structural assumptions. The current collation uses the same finite family of duplicated groups and gaps, now compared against observed coordinates in the second reception. | Operation in the current p159 collation | Count or result | |---|---| | Native p159 source | 271 observed coordinates; header advertises 272 | | Exclude one copy of each repeated `VDAGG` and `FFXDF` | 10 observed coordinates | | Add two five-slot gaps and one slot in `GDDA` | 11 slots; model length 272 | | Supply those additions from directly observed p168 coordinates | All 11; no donation uses p168’s borrowed or missing values | | Minimum source-to-source disagreement | 5 differences across 258 jointly observed comparisons | | Retained source-origin maps | 8, all producing the same completed ciphertext | | Common word proposal | 7 observed p159 substitutions; 135/136 fixed labels | The source-only comparison examines 173,580 canonical layouts and 694,320 source-origin maps. The eight minima replace the earlier 64 word-conditioned maps and remove their P0000 alternatives. This is a minimum within a declared source-edit family, not proof of a unique historical transmission failure. The [cross-copy certificate](../../experiments/danube_arad_witnesses/certificates.json) records every origin, price and both globally consistent footer assignments. ## Native source and literal header
Original p159 header, literal ciphertext and odd-frame diagnostic **Literal header:** `A) UKS? v ZON (11.12 p.m., November 8th); AN LP 2000 KR; RICHI-272; following control: ZON` The question mark after `UKS` is present in the source header. The reception time is **11.12 p.m.**, not the earlier OCR's 11.18. The final `ZON` is a source control, separate from the cipher body. **Source transcription — all 271 printed coordinates, including both copies of each repeated group:** ```text FDVDD FXAAX XGVDD XADVV XFVXD VDAGG VDAGG ADVDV VADDA VDDGV DDGGX GVVGX GVXVG XDDVF VGXXA ADDVV FFXDF FFXDF XDXXV DGAGF VDAXV VXDDG VXAAV GDDA DVFDX GDGVG VGDDX VXVAG VDVDD DDGVG DXXVX GDDGX DDGAA GVAVD VVGAA VGDVD VVDVG GGGDF XGDGD DDDVV VFVGF VDGDD VXDAD XDADV GVVVV GDVDD DDVGG VVDGG DVVVV VAFVA DXXXV VVVFA FFADV DAXVV FV ``` **Raw output — native odd-frame diagnostic, before any exclusions or additions:** ```text HAQSTYKGWPOG3IRIDD1CXCKETTPUC0BCEEQXUEYPNCLK0L0XEEAAQFEYTKKAREAGYIEAEAYQRUN2GQYNSDRSKUP0AXLZADKE3A000DNGAXXLH0KNTWZE10QK8?KLSXLEH18EL0I ``` The last unpaired intermediate coordinate is `V` at source index **40**. This diagnostic and the complete unaltered source remain in the certificate; they are not replaced by the conditional readable frame.
## Earlier reconstruction, before the complete-copy evidence
Superseded word-conditioned baseline — exact displays and historical tests The sections in this drawer document the earlier reconstruction before p168 supplied the missing source values. They remain available for comparison; their U, unresolved strength and P0000 alternatives are not the current reading. ## Raw output — conditional 272-coordinate frame **Raw output — ten valid exclusions and eleven unfilled additions:** ```text 0NOHLXVERPOLEGUNG?OCH14TAGE?10TAGEXX??RPFLEGXEU?GENACHAR??XARADNEI?NGARXREGI?RUNGERWIR?ENXSTAEKE?0000MANNX30000TISREXAOK11XRMX1CX18?GLHX ``` The early frame fixed 124 of 136 positions while all eleven additions were left unknown. ## Edited output — primary partial proposal **Edited output — six observed substitutions and ten added-slot fills; one added slot remains unknown:** ```text ANOHLXVERPFLEGUNGNOCH14TAGEU10TAGEXXVERPFLEGXZUEGENACHARADXARADBEIUNGARXREGIERUNGERWIRKENXSTAEKE?0000MANNX30000TIEREXAOK11XRMX1CX18?GLHX ``` The early proposal changed observed source indices 60, 65, 68, 69, 210 and 235, filled ten added coordinates, and left the strength and footer open. Its exact readable display was: **Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the primary partial proposal:** > An OHL. Verpflegung noch 14 Tage U10 Tage. Verpfleg. Zuege nach Arad. Arad bei ungar. Regierung erwirken. STAEKE ?0000 Mann, 30000 Tiere. AOK11. RM. 1C. 18?GLH. Its duration U was a lexical supply. It should no longer compete on equal evidence with the directly observed p168 separator X. ## Every tied source map is retained The earlier text-conditioned search covered 173,580 canonical layouts and 694,320 source-origin maps: either instance of each duplicated group could be excluded, a single slot was added around GDDA, and two five-slot gaps were placed at the remaining boundaries. It retained 64 minimum source maps at six observed-coordinate changes. Those old prices and every map remain in the [original certificate](../../experiments/arad_provisions_partial/certificates.json). The new coordinate-only comparison retains eight maps with one completed stream. Its five-disagreement objective compares two sources, rather than a supplied plaintext template; these are different costs, not competing claims about the same repair count. ## The first quantity and footer stay linked Before the complete copy was inspected, the primary strength pair had domain {3,4,5,6,8,P,V}. Sixteen word-minimum maps left it open; forty-eight produced literal P0000 and filled all eleven additions. The latter display was: **Conditional interpretation — one tied map retaining literal P0000; six substitutions and eleven added-slot fills:** ```text ANOHLXVERPFLEGUNGNOCH14TAGEU10TAGEXXVERPFLEGXZUEGENACHARADXARADBEIUNGARXREGIERUNGERWIRKENXSTAEKEP0000MANNX30000TIEREXAOK11XRMX1CX18?GLHX ``` These were alternative maps, not independent witnesses or votes for P. The new observed p168 pairs fix 80000 and eliminate those P0000 alternatives within the tested source family. Only the footer’s shared VF={5,6} choice remains unresolved. The original twelve global completion witnesses and map-specific compatibility records remain historical calculation evidence. ## Exploration, verification and credit The original vocabulary search followed a provisions/strength lead; it was not a blind test. Its [portable script](../../experiments/arad_provisions_partial/explore.py) and [retained results](../../experiments/arad_provisions_partial/exploration.json) remain reproducible, alongside the fixed-template audit: **Reproduction commands:** ```sh python experiments/arad_provisions_partial/verify.py --verify python experiments/arad_provisions_partial/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf python experiments/arad_provisions_partial/explore.py --verify ```
The [current witness edition](danube_arad_witnesses.md#arad-cross-copy-restoration) explains the source relationship; the [original experiment](../../experiments/arad_provisions_partial/README.md) keeps the earlier search and candidate unchanged. The reviewed [p159 crop](../../experiments/arad_provisions_partial/sources/p159_A_reviewed.png) and p168 crop are bound to the authenticated Childs PDF. ```sh python experiments/danube_arad_witnesses/verify.py --verify python experiments/danube_arad_witnesses/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf ```

# Citadel surrender, local armistice terms and home leave

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source editions: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Four physical parts on Childs p179 concern surrender terms, a request for
the armistice conditions applicable to Mackensen's front, and postponement
of discharge and urgent home leave. The source's dates, abbreviated words,
unresolved reference fields and unusual year form are preserved separately
from the ordinary-word repairs.

The source is Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
[printed p179, PDF p182](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The adjacent A record is a separate
[radio-equipment transfer order](../radio/right_rhine_equipment.md).

## Conditional shared digits

The citadel instruction gains **KM 2583 18G ANCH**, fixing **79/79 labels** after the earlier single word repair. The suffix remains a literal administrative reference. The [joint reconstruction](../../experiments/nov10_joint_completion/README.md) combines the earlier Marineamt and formation interpretations with the army-number constraint and the mobilization decree; the reversed 7/9 assignment is retained there.

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the joint square:**

> Zitadelle: Widerstand aufgeben, Uebergabebedingungen dort festsetzen. K M 2583 18G ANCH.

<details>
<summary>Exact conditional labels</summary>

**Edited output — p179_B, conditional shared square; 79/79 fixed positions:**

```text
ZITADELLEXWIDERSTANDAUFGEBENUEBERGABEBEDINGUNGENDORTFESTSETZENXKMX2583X18GXANCH
```

</details>


## B: abandon resistance and determine surrender terms

The [158-coordinate telegram](../../experiments/november_armistice_orders/sources/p179_B.png)
has `WAU v LP (15.50, November 11th); KR (15.53)` and a separate `NF NF NF`
postamble outside the ciphertext. Its direct reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ZITADELLEXWIDERSTANDAUFGEBENUEBERGABEBEDINGUNGENGORTFESTSETZENXKMX2??3X1?GXANCH
```

</details>

One observed-coordinate substitution proposes `DORT` for `GORT`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ZITADELLEXWIDERSTANDAUFGEBENUEBERGABEBEDINGUNGENDORTFESTSETZENXKMX2??3X1?GXANCH
```

</details>

The instruction is to abandon resistance at the citadel and set surrender
terms there. The message does not name the citadel's city. Its final
`KMX2??3X1?GXANCH` reference remains unresolved; the three question marks
come from the partial square, with all source coordinates present.

## C: what armistice conditions apply to this front?

The [232-coordinate source](../../experiments/november_armistice_orders/sources/p179_C.png)
has `--- v ZO'N (10.25 p.m., November 11th)` and several routing lines,
including `2000 FUER LP KK 11 KK (11) KR`. The full routing text and the
interstitial `WP WP WP FF NKJ v ZO'N` are preserved in the input record.

The raw output is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ANOHLXOBERKOMMANDOMACKE1SENUND11XARMEEERBITTENMITTEILUNGDERBESONDERENWAFFENSTILLSTANDSBESINGXFUERHIESIGEFRONTXAOK11X
```

</details>

Three observed-coordinate substitutions repair the two word fragments
`MACKE1SEN→MACKENSEN` and `BESING→BEDING`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ANOHLXOBERKOMMANDOMACKENSENUND11XARMEEERBITTENMITTEILUNGDERBESONDERENWAFFENSTILLSTANDSBEDINGXFUERHIESIGEFRONTXAOK11X
```

</details>

Mackensen's high command and the 11th Army ask OHL to communicate the
particular armistice conditions for their front. The abbreviation
`BEDING` is retained, without inserting letters to spell out *Bedingungen*.
B and C use the unchanged published Nov10–12 key.

## D: discharge delayed, and urgent home leave suspended

The [two-part source](../../experiments/november_armistice_orders/sources/p179_D.png)
is separately headed:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
12th NOVEMBER, 1918.
D) FUER UKS (18.50, November 12th) 2 TLE
```

</details>

Its actual part lengths are **190 and 212 coordinates**, matching their
printed labels. The earlier D1 OCR stream had 191 slots. Manual
retranscription restores the received 190-slot frame, with no insertion
or deletion of the printed source itself.

Both parts read under the unchanged published key labelled **Nov13–15b**.
That label differs from the source's **November 12** heading. The dates
and the successful working-key identity remain recorded together; their
chronology is unresolved.

D1's direct output, with **zero source repairs**, is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
INFLGTRANSPTSCHWIERIGKINHEIMATISTDURCHKMDX????AMANGEORDNENTLASSGLDSTURMJAHRGX1560U61VERSCHOBENX
```

</details>

It reports that transport difficulties at home have caused a previously
ordered discharge of Landsturm year groups to be postponed. The reference
after `KMD` remains unknown. The year-like text **`1560U61`** is preserved
literally. The edition does not normalize it to a historically plausible
year or assign a new digit value.

D2's direct output, also with **zero source repairs**, is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DRINGENDEHEIMATSURLAUBEHABENBISAUFWEITERESGAENZLICHZUUNTERBLEIBENXCHEFDESGENSTABESNRXRM1A11???GEHOPEZ??0?X
```

</details>

Urgent home leave is to cease entirely until further notice. The signatory
is the chief of the general staff; the remaining reference string is not
completed. The question marks in these two parts are unassigned key cells,
not printed erasures, and their domains share one global square bijection.

The separate [p193 award-class interpretation](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md)
assigns `VG=2`, giving `RM1A11?2?` in D2. This fixes one further position,
**101/106**, while leaving the reference incomplete and adding no source
repair.

## Exact accounting and attribution

| Part | Received coordinates | Raw fixed labels | Edition fixed labels | Known-coordinate substitutions | Source insertions/deletions/fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| B | 158 | 76 / 79 | 76 / 79 | 1 | 0 |
| C | 232 | 116 / 116 | 116 / 116 | 3 | 0 |
| D1 | 190 | 91 / 95 | 91 / 95 | 0 | 0 |
| D2 | 212 | 100 / 106 | 100 / 106 | 0 | 0 |
| **Total for these four parts** | **792** | **383 / 396** | **383 / 396** | **4** | **0** |

The arithmetic certificate additionally contains the separate p179 A
record, whose printed five-coordinate cancellation is counted explicitly.
It must not be confused with the zero geometry changes in B–D above.

The [inputs](../../experiments/november_armistice_orders/inputs.json) and
[certificate](../../experiments/november_armistice_orders/certificates.json)
retain full source rows, header differences, all source images and every
digit/`J/Q/Y` occurrence, including changes made only by priced ordinary-word
repairs. Global re-encryption witnesses check compatibility and costs;
their arbitrary missing-key assignments are not proposed original numbers.

The keys are prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**. B, C and D2 already had unreviewed OCR-derived body candidates,
also represented in the frozen p73 retrieval corpus. D1 gains a coherent
source reading from the corrected transcription length. The bounded
publication check is recorded, with no universal priority claim.

```sh
python experiments/november_armistice_orders/verify.py --verify
```

The optional `--pdf` check regenerates all source crops from the pinned scan
and compares their pixels.

# Two additional witnesses to the armistice-planning traffic

**Source comparison and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Printed p137 preserves two fragments already represented in the
[pp125–126 armistice-planning edition](armistice_transit_planning.md). · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)
Their actual coordinate strings distinguish an independently supported
source-mask fill from two corrupt words repeated by both copies.
Neither case changes the published **Nov4–6** key.

## p137 B4

The source explicitly labels this block `4 TL RICHI-212`; `LP v NKJ`
appears after its final `GV`. All 212 observed coordinates give:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
XDIEBESTIMMUNGXDASSENTENTERECHTZURBEFOERDERUNGIHRERTRUPPENASAEMTLICHENEISENBAHNENUNDRECHTDERBESETZUNGALLER
```

</details>

This is the clause about Entente rights to transport troops on the railways
and occupy places described in the following part. Its literal
`TRUPPENASAEMTLICHEN` is retained; the edition does not add missing letters
to make that phrase smoother.

Compared with p125 A4, **211 coordinates are identical**. At source index
30, p125 has a noncoordinate 2/Z-shaped glyph that the earlier edition
masked; p137 plainly has X. That observed X independently supplies the
earlier fill and gives the N in `BEFOERDERUNG`. This new physical witness
fixes all **106 plaintext positions without any source repair**.

The preceding p137 B `RIZI-138` block has a different layout and surrounding
call signs. It is not silently treated as part 3 of the p125 message.

## p137 C

The header reads `LP v NKJ 464 (12.01 November 5th), RICHI-134`.
Its **134 coordinates are exactly identical** to p126 B, including the
two values responsible for the damaged words:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
OXHXL0XDRBHTUNGRM1XAX11118XOPGEH02XANGXORHALTENXOXK0M0RM1A011232XOP
```

</details>

The same conservative ordinary-word candidate remains available:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
OXHXL0XDRAHTUNGRM1XAX11118XOPGEH02XANGXERHALTENXOXK0M0RM1A011232XOP
```

</details>

It changes source indices **27 and 56, both G→F**, giving `DRAHTUNG` and
`ERHALTEN`. Because both copies repeat the same corrupt values, the new
witness **does not independently confirm those repairs**. All numerical
and reference labels remain untouched.

## Scope and sources

The p137 page heading says November 6 while both receiving timestamps
refer to November 5. These labels are preserved. The earlier source texts,
repairs and catalogue rows remain intact; this adds two physical witnesses,
not two new unique message bodies or a new decipherment of the period key.

| New physical record | Source slots | Raw fixed labels | Observed-coordinate substitutions | Source fills or geometry changes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| p137 B4 | 212 | 106 / 106 | 0 | 0 |
| p137 C | 134 | 67 / 67 | 2 | 0 |

See the [source page](../../experiments/retrieved_copy_editions/sources/p137.png),
[transcribed inputs](../../experiments/retrieved_copy_editions/inputs.json),
and [independent certificate](../../experiments/retrieved_copy_editions/certificates.json).
The page is from Childs,
[complete scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).

# Armistice-departure report: the p151/p157 copy relation

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source comparison and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The truncated first part on p157 shares substantial ciphertext with p151 A1.
It supplies a coordinate that changes the latter's opaque `STUR3FSS` ending
to **STURZFSS** under an explicit common-copy model. The complete p157
reading below copies its missing material from p151 and prices every
disagreement. **The p157 source alone fixes 0 of 95 plaintext positions in
this conditional frame.** The copied reading is not an independent native
decryption of the 83 surviving slots.

This supplement leaves the [earlier p151 edition](nov7_fragment_and_acknowledgment.md#p151-a1)
and [p157 parts 2–5](romanian_pacification_consultation.md) unchanged. A
further **STURZ DES** interpretation is priced separately below; two of its
letters have no surviving p157 coordinate support.

## Sources and the copy assumption

The [p151 source](../../experiments/nov7_fragments_and_council/sources/p151_A.png)
has `LP v NKJ (6.42 p.m., November 7th)`, `KR 1215 UKS 5 TLE`, and
`1 TL RICHI-190`. It contains 189 coordinates and the visibly short `AVVG`.
Its earlier conditional edition adds D before that group to read
GEMELDETEN; that lexical assumption remains explicit here.

The [p157 first-part source](../../experiments/romanian_pacification_consultation/sources/p157_A1.png)
has `LP v NKJ (--- November 8th)`, `5 TLE` and blank `RICHI----`, beneath
the [7 November page heading](../../experiments/romanian_pacification_consultation/sources/p157_overview.png).
It preserves **83 slots: 78 coordinates and five printed dashes**. Its
four-symbol groups are `XDDV` and `XXXA`; no advertised length survives.
These headers and date layers are retained.

Two long exact coordinate runs establish the close source relation
without using German word guesses. All indices in this edition are
zero-based, and the endpoints below are inclusive.

| p151 source positions | p157 source positions | Exact length |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| 118–141 | 13–36 | 24 |
| 143–175 | 38–70 | 33 |

The reconstruction assumes the same 190-slot transposition frame as p151:
**105 absent prefix slots plus one absent coordinate in each short group**.
Thus 83 surviving slots plus 107 modeled absent slots give 190. This length
and prefix are copy assumptions, not values printed on p157.

All 25 combinations of the two local insertion boundaries are replayed.
Four share the minimum **six disagreements among 78 observed coordinates**:
`(3, 71)`, `(3, 72)`, `(4, 71)` and `(4, 72)`. Each has 72 observed agreements
with the p151 witness. The primary display uses `(3, 71)`; the other three
remain equally economical local alignments. No unique loss position or
exhaustive optimum over other total lengths is claimed.

## p157 A1

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — p157 coordinates only, with 105 absent prefix slots and two local gaps masked; conditional 190-slot frame, 0/95 fixed positions:**

```text
???????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????
```

</details>

Every pair still depends on at least one missing coordinate in this frame.
The certificate retains the individual domains; the question marks do not
mean that all 36 symbols are possible at every position.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — fill the 112 masked or absent slots from the stated p151 candidate, before changing any observed p157 coordinate:**

```text
OHLXBPHXNACHRICHBVONABREISSDEUTSCHERUAFFENSTILLSTANDSKOMMISSIONHATANSAHEINENDGEMELDETENSTURZFSS
```

</details>

The 112 fills comprise **105 prefix fills, two short-group fills and five
printed-mask fills**. Of these, 111 have actual p151 coordinate counterparts;
one is the earlier conditional D supplying GEMELDETEN. Fixed positions in
this copy-assisted layer are never counted as fixed raw p157 positions.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same copy-conditioned frame, five observed p157 substitutions plus the 112 separately accounted fills; opaque ending retained:**

```text
OHLXBPXXNACHRICHTVONABREISEDEUTSCHERWAFFENSTILLSTANDSKOMMISSIONHATANSCHEINENDGEMELDETENSTURZFSS
```

</details>

The primary p157 substitutions are **9 X→V, 10 X→V, 11 X→V, 12 V→X,
71 X→F**. The local gap values are V at source boundary 3 and D at boundary
71; the five printed dashes, source positions 73–77, become AXFDX. In the
equally economical second-group boundary 72 alignment, the local value is
F and source position 71 changes X→D instead. Both complete candidates
re-encrypt to the same stated ciphertext after their separately mapped
changes.

**Readable German — copy-conditioned reconstruction; spacing and punctuation only, with STURZFSS retained:**

> OHL. BP. Nachricht von Abreise deutscher Waffenstillstandskommission hat anscheinend gemeldeten STURZFSS

**Meaning:** The shared fragment concerns news of the departure of a German
armistice commission and an apparent effect. Its closing remains opaque in
the primary reading. BP is not expanded, and the missing predicate is not
supplied as an established event.

## The six disagreements and their plaintext effects

The table shows the primary `(3, 71)` alignment. Each pair combines the
listed coordinate with its other coordinate from the stated p151 frame;
these are conditional paired readings, not independently fixed p157 letters.

| p151 source | p157 source | Other p151 coordinate | p151 pair → label | Pair with p157 coordinate → label | Displayed choice and reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 114: V | 9: X | 76: V | VV → X | VX → H | p151 separator after BP; the p157 H remains an alternative. |
| 115: V | 10: X | 77: G | GV → T | GX → B | p151 T gives NACHRICHT rather than NACHRICHB. |
| 116: V | 11: X | 78: D | DV → E | DX → S | p151 E gives ABREISE rather than ABREISS. |
| 117: X | 12: V | 79: A | AX → W | AV → U | p151 W gives WAFFEN rather than UAFFEN. |
| 142: A | 37: F | 65: D | DA → 3 | DF → Z | p157 F supplies the Z in STURZFSS; the remaining FSS is retained. |
| 177: F | 71: X | 34: D | FD → C | XD → A | p151 C gives ANSCHEINEND rather than ANSAHEINEND. |

With second-group boundary 72, the last row instead compares p151 source
176 D with the same p157 source 71 X: pair DX → S versus XX → F, in
KOMMISSION/KOMMISFION. The other five rows are unchanged.

The five selected p151 coordinates are editorial choices supported by
ordinary word forms and the p151 witness; p151 is not assumed infallible.
The certificate retains **all 64 combinations** of choosing p151 or p157
at the six primary-frame conflicts. Every combination roundtrips and has
the same combined cost of six observed-coordinate changes across the two
witnesses. Coordinate cost alone does not select the displayed wording.

For p151 itself, the Z proposal costs **one observed substitution, source
142 A→F**, in addition to its already declared missing D. Its other paired
coordinate is printed on p151. The p157 coordinate therefore supports a
specific correction under the copy model; it does not independently decode
the whole closing.

## Conditional interpretation: STURZ DES

The already edited p157 A2 begins `MINISTERIUMSHERBEIGEFUEHRT`. Joining
that continuation to a proposed STURZ DES ending would read “Sturz des
Ministeriums herbeigeführt.” This is a contextual proposal about the fall
of a ministry, with the following additional cost.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — further contextual STURZ DES proposal; two additional observed p151 substitutions, neither observed on the surviving p157 source:**

```text
OHLXBPXXNACHRICHTVONABREISEDEUTSCHERWAFFENSTILLSTANDSKOMMISSIONHATANSCHEINENDGEMELDETENSTURZDES
```

</details>

Relative to the primary STURZFSS reading, this changes p151 source
**103 X→V** for F→D and **46 X→V** for S→E. Both counterpart positions lie
inside the 105 absent p157 prefix slots. Hence the p151 total becomes
**three observed substitutions plus its one missing-slot fill**. The p157
observed cost stays five only because these two altered values occur in its
copied prefix; they are not free source support. Across both witnesses the
observed-change cost rises from six to eight.

The continuation is itself the explicitly edited p157 A2 reading, not a
literal uncorrected source. The full interpretation does not establish
which ministry fell or that the inferred event happened. In particular,
p151 A2 has a different 186-slot body from p157 A2's 200 slots: the complete
five-part telegrams are not silently equated.

## Accounting, attribution and reproduction

| Quantity for the newly cataloged p157 A1 record | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| Surviving printed slots / valid coordinates | 83 / 78 |
| Conditional modeled coordinates / plaintext positions | 190 / 95 |
| Fixed raw p157 positions / proposed complete positions | 0 / 95 |
| Observed p157 substitutions | 5 |
| Printed-mask fills | 5 |
| Absent-prefix fills / short-group fills | 105 / 2 |
| Observed-coordinate deletions or moves | 0 |

The already cataloged p151 record is a comparison witness and is excluded
from new-record totals. All counts use the primary opaque-ending candidate;
the additional STURZ DES interpretation is separate.

Published period-key recovery retains the credit of George Lasry, Ingo
Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry's 2017 key list.
Earlier repository candidates and both source editions remain frozen.
This supplement supplies explicit source correspondence and bounded
interpretations; it claims no first historical decipherment.

[Inputs](../../experiments/armistice_departure_copy/inputs.json),
[all alignments, conflict choices and position certificates](../../experiments/armistice_departure_copy/certificates.json),
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/armistice_departure_copy/README.md)
preserve the exact evidence and counts.

```sh
python experiments/armistice_departure_copy/verify.py --verify
python experiments/armistice_departure_copy/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf
```
