# Armistice conditions and urgent provisions requests on Childs p188

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and exact repair accounting: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro (2026).** Published Nov13–15b partial key: Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker. Earlier unreviewed machine readings are retained in the evidence package; no universal decipherment-priority claim is made.

Three physical records are kept separate. A is a **conditional edited reading**, requiring exclusion of an extra visible mark, 14 observed-coordinate substitutions and seven source-mask fills. B2 and C1 use their native frames. Their matching `20.05 (13/11)` references, complementary part labels and provisions subject make them likely companions, without proving their complete source history.

## Source and accounting

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed p188, PDF p191. The page is headed 13 November 1918. Six delivered crops preserve the headers, literal glyphs and three enlarged source details. Dates and intercept times are not harmonized by plausibility.

| Record | Source slots → analysis-frame slots | Positions | Raw fixed → edited fixed | Observed substitutions | Mask fills | Additional geometry |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| p188 A | 225 → 224 | 112 | 104 → 112 | 14 | 7 | One extra visible K/X-like mark excluded; 0–1 known-coordinate deletion depending on its interpretation |
| p188 B2 | 176 → 176 | 88 | 84 → 88 | 10 | 0 | Native frame; printed “jammed to end” note retained |
| p188 C1 | 268 → 268 | 134 | 130 → 130 | 4 | 0 | Native frame; literal E remains a mask |

Across all three records there are 669 source slots, 668 analysis-frame slots and 334 plaintext positions, of which 318 are fixed in the raw readings. The edited proposals use 28 observed-coordinate substitutions and seven fills. B2/C1 alone comprise 444 source slots, including one noncoordinate E glyph, and 222 positions, 214 raw fixed positions and 218 edited fixed positions, with 14 substitutions and no fills. These separate counts prevent A's conditional geometry from being hidden in the aggregate.

## A: request for armistice conditions

The conditional proposal asks OHL for the special armistice conditions applying to this theatre. `BESX` remains an abbreviation. The raw body has `AVK1P`; the edition changes the ordinary letter V to O but preserves the suffix `1P` as `AOK1P`. Its footer separately reads `A X O X K X 11`. The thematic request on p179 C is not used to normalize these unit labels.

The second source row ends `DDFXXK`: the final slot is a crossed/overtyped K- or X-like mark, not a certain extra coordinate. It is retained in the literal transcription at zero-based source index 80 and excluded from the 224-coordinate working frame. If it is a noncoordinate overprint, no known coordinate is deleted; if read as X, the exclusion costs one observed-coordinate deletion. Neither this geometry nor the wording has been shown globally optimal or unique. Under the X interpretation, neighboring identical X values can also make the identity of an excluded mark ambiguous.

The third source row ends `GDGAG AV?XF`. The [enlarged source crop](../../experiments/armistice_provisions_requests/sources/p188_A_damaged_glyph.png) preserves the vertical/overlapping strokes in the third glyph of the last group, source index 118. The complete row and the original embedded image pixels do not establish an unqualified X. The earlier frozen OCR also recorded `AV?XF`; that is another transcription of the same witness, not an independent copy. No literal M is asserted. The source mark therefore remains `?`, alongside the five printed dashes and the B-shaped glyph at source index 165: seven source masks in total.

Source index 118 maps to working index 117 and pairs with source index 90 at plaintext position 42. Its raw `?V` pair has domain `234789ACMQVXY`, so the former raw C in `BESCNZ` is now `?` in `BES?NZ`. The edition still proposes D at that source slot, producing `DV = X` in `BESX`; this is a mask fill. The certificate separately retains the **conditional X interpretation**: `XV = C`, 105 raw fixed positions, 15 observed substitutions and six fills, with the identical edited stream. Reclassifying this damaged glyph reduces the number of observed substitutions by one and increases fills by one; it does not recover a letter or reduce the total number of proposed coordinate changes.

## B2: provisions available for only five days

The edited text says that the need is very urgent and provisions last at most five more days. `LAENGSTENSOCH` and `FELDINTENTENDANT` are retained exactly in the edited stream: no missing-looking N is inserted and no duplicated-looking syllable is deleted. The V before AOK11 and the reference `6011` remain baseline labels. This is a statement in the telegram, not independent verification of the supply situation.

All 176 received slots are present, yet the source explicitly says “jammed to end.” That interference note remains part of the record; no unprinted tail is invented. Four raw question marks here arise from unassigned square cells, not source erasures; their proposed letters require the counted coordinate changes.

## C1: flour and oats to Szolnok

**Readable German — conditional headquarters and award-class assignments:**

> Generalintendant Feldheeres. Gr. H. Qu. Bitte alle 2 Tage VV Zug mit ??0000 vollen Portionen einschl. Mehl, Rest Hafer, nach Szolnok an der Theiss absenden.

The request asks the Generalintendant of the field army for a train of
provisions to Szolnok on the Theiss. The quantity remains unresolved;
`VVZUG` is retained. Four earlier substitutions supply `EINSCHL`, `SZOLNOK`
and `ANDER`.

Two independent readings in the shared square complete the address and
interval. The native [p202 B3 intendant address](military_intendant_remit.md#b3-the-headquarters-supply-office)
has `GENERALINTENDANT GRHQU`; reading the p188 destination as the same
headquarters gives **XX=Q**. Separately, interpreting `EK?` in the
[p193 congratulation](../people/nov13_conditional_congratulation.md)
as an Iron Cross class while retaining numerical **DD=1** gives **VG=2**,
hence **every two days** here. The independent p186 `10X11` field supports
DD=1 only under its explicit date interpretation, as the linked account explains.
These assignments raise C1 from **130 to 132/134** positions without
adding a source change. Their assumptions and propagation are checked in
the [joint certificate](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/certificates.json).

The clearly printed E in `EFXGF` remains unfilled at source index 140.
The four baseline uncertainties and their present treatment are:

| Position | Field | Source pair | Baseline domain | Conditional treatment |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | `GR X H X ?U` headquarters label | XX | 234789QY | Q from the headquarters interpretation |
| 45 | `ALLE ? TAGE` interval | VG | 234789QY | 2 from the award-class interpretation |
| 58 | First character of `??0000` portions | ?D, literal ED | 1234789JKQTY | Still unresolved |
| 59 | Second character of `??0000` portions | FV | 234789QY | Still unresolved |

The remaining values share one square. The historical quantity is not
selected from a presumed ration requirement.

## Literal and edited streams

### p188 A

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 224-slot frame excluding the separately priced extra mark:**

```text
A?O?LXX6A?UNDAVK1PSRB?ITENMIK?EILUNGDERBES?NZFFENSTIL5STANDSBLDINGUNGENFUERNIESI?ENK?IEGSSCHAUPRATZMXAXOXKX11XXX
```

**Edited output — same conditional extra-mark exclusion; fourteen substitutions and seven fills:**

```text
ANOHLXXOKMUNDAOK1PERBITTENMITTEILUNGDERBESXWAFFENSTILLSTANDSBEDINGUNGENFUERHIESIGENKRIEGSSCHAUPLATZXXAXOXKX11XXX
```

</details>

### p188 B2

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
BEDARF?EHRDRINGENDVVGLPFLEGUNGREICHTLAENGSTE?SOC?HUENFTAGEXFELDINTENTENDWNTVA?K11X6011XX
```

**Edited output:**

```text
BEDARFSEHRDRINGENDXVERPFLEGUNGREICHTLAENGSTENSOCHFUENFTAGEXFELDINTENTENDANTVAOK11X6011XX
```

</details>

### p188 C1

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
GENERALINTENDANTFELDHEERESXGRXHX?UXXBITTEALLE?TAGEVVZUGMIT??0000VOLLENPORTIONENEIN6CHLXMEHLXRESTHAFERXNACHSCOLNOKANDCRTHEISSXABSENDENX
```

**Edited output:**

```text
GENERALINTENDANTFELDHEERESXGRXHX?UXXBITTEALLE?TAGEVVZUGMIT??0000VOLLENPORTIONENEINSCHLXMEHLXRESTHAFERXNACHSZOLNOKANDERTHEISSXABSENDENX
```

</details>

## Evidence, reproduction and limits

The [inputs](../../experiments/armistice_provisions_requests/inputs.json) contain every literal source row, header, image rectangle/scale and excluded-slot interpretation. The [certificates](../../experiments/armistice_provisions_requests/certificates.json) identify every changed coordinate, every source-mask fill, every remaining domain and every plaintext pair's original source slots. The [earlier candidate snapshot](../../experiments/armistice_provisions_requests/prior_candidates.json) preserves the preexisting unreviewed readings and the bounded publication check. This is a source and repair edition, not a claim that these message bodies were first identified here.

The package [README](../../experiments/armistice_provisions_requests/README.md) gives verification commands. The verifier checks the unchanged published partial square and ranks, compares an independent physical-column inverse with the project decoder, recomputes every cost, and supplies an injective completion/re-encryption witness. Such a witness is only a consistency example, not the original key or a uniquely authenticated message. Optional PDF verification checks both the full-source digest and all delivered crop pixels.

# Armistice transit and withdrawal planning

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

A six-part report on Childs pp125-126 discusses reported armistice conditions
for Austria-Hungary and their effect on German troop movements. It says
that the terms learned from Hungarian newspapers allow only fifteen days'
transit, describes plans for the **11th Army**, and urgently requests the
actual agreement. Five parts are readable in their ordinary cipher frames.
Part five has an odd 267-slot source and a useful, explicitly conditional
recovery of its latter half. A separate adjacent receipt note is included
as a seventh source record.

## Source and headers

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [printed pp125-126, PDF pp128-129](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
Both [p125](../../experiments/armistice_transit_planning/sources/childs_p125_full.png)
and [p126](../../experiments/armistice_transit_planning/sources/childs_p126_full.png)
are preserved. The page heading is `4th NOVEMBER, 1918.`, and the report's
repeated header reads:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) --- v NKJ (6.52 p.m., November 5th)
2345 (4/11) AN LP 6 TLE
```

</details>

Parts 1-4 occur on p125 and parts 5-6 continue on p126. The missing addressee
in the reception line is retained as `---`; `AN LP` remains in the origin
line. No date, callsign, reference or numerical label is silently normalized.
The complete published `Nov4-6` square and 17-column rank order are unchanged.

## A1-A3: transit rights and the 11th Army

The [first part](../../experiments/armistice_transit_planning/sources/childs_p125_A1.png)
has exactly 244 valid coordinates and reads without repair:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
OXHXLXOPXXNACHSOEBENHIERAUSUNGARISCHENZEITUNGENBEKANNTWERDENDENWAFFENSTILLSTANDSBEDINGUNGENFUEROESTUNGXISTDEUTSCHENTRUPPEN
```

</details>

The [second part](../../experiments/armistice_transit_planning/sources/childs_p125_A2.png)
has 238 valid coordinates. Its raw `FUENFXEHN` is repaired to `FUENFZEHN`
by one coordinate substitution:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
NURFUENFZEHNTAEGIGESDURCHZUGSRECHTZUGESTANDENXXOXKXMXHATTEBEABSICHTIGTX11XARMEEZUNAECHSTANDONAUZUBELASSENXSIEDEMNAECHST
```

</details>

The [third part](../../experiments/armistice_transit_planning/sources/childs_p125_A3.png)
has 200 valid coordinates. One coordinate substitution changes the raw
`RGEUMT` to `RAEUMT`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
FALLSBESATZUNGSHEERWALACHEIRAEUMTXALSSCHUTZRECHTERFLANKEZWISCHENTHEISSUNDGEBIRGEZURUECKGEHENZULASSEN
```

</details>

With spaces and ordinary punctuation, the three parts read:

**Readable German:**

> O.H.L. Op. Nach soeben hier aus ungarischen Zeitungen bekannt werdenden
> Waffenstillstandsbedingungen für Oest.-Ung. ist deutschen Truppen nur
> fünfzehntägiges Durchzugsrecht zugestanden. O.K.M. hatte beabsichtigt,
> 11. Armee zunächst an Donau zu belassen, sie demnächst, falls Besatzungsheer
> Walachei räumt, als Schutz rechter Flanke zwischen Theiss und Gebirge
> zurückgehen zu lassen.

The report says that German troops have only fifteen days' passage under
the conditions just learned from Hungarian newspapers. It describes an
intention to leave the 11th Army on the Danube initially and, if the occupation
army evacuates Wallachia, let it retreat between the Theiss and the mountains
to protect the right flank. This is the report's stated information and
plan; the edition does not independently verify the newspaper terms or
assert that the proposed movement occurred. The raw army label `11` is
preserved exactly.

## A4: Entente transport and occupation rights

The [fourth part](../../experiments/armistice_transit_planning/sources/childs_p125_A4.png)
has 212 slots. A printed noncoordinate `2`/Z-like glyph is one erasure. It
leaves only the `N` in `BEFOERDERUNG` unknown; filling that position gives:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
XDIEBESTIMMUNGXDASSENTENTERECHTZURBEFOERDERUNGIHRERTRUPPENASAEMTLICHENEISENBAHNENUNDRECHTDERBESETZUNGALLER
```

</details>

The clause describes a provision giving the Entente the right to transport
its troops on the railways and occupy strategic points. The source literally
has `TRUPPENASAEMTLICHEN`; interpreting its `A` as an abbreviation for *auf*
is an editorial expansion, not recovered `UF` coordinates. The sentence
continues into the damaged fifth part.

## A5: conditional recovery of the odd frame

The [fifth part](../../experiments/armistice_transit_planning/sources/childs_p126_A5.png)
is explicitly marked `RICHI-267` and contains exactly **267 slots**, including
two printed dashes. Its original untransposed coordinate stream is odd.
The direct paired reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — original odd frame; paired prefix with an unpaired coordinate reported separately:**

```text
STRATEGISCHWICHTIGENPU?K?HABENSOLLXWUERDEFUERDIEMIT1A11204GRMELDETEN3L4QL3LCZWFFQ7K7I7I4IQFNCIC9Z9J6WLNL6JQFCX94A2FYZ6KZL6JY94ALFWLFL
```

</details>

One final coordinate remains unpaired. The first portion is readable; the
latter portion becomes readable under the opposite pairing phase. This
motivates the following **conditional error model**: a coordinate was lost
from the fractionated intermediate stream before the sender transposed its
267 remaining coordinates.

Keeping the received frame and its ranks intact, insert one unknown at
interim index 136 after untransposition. The conditional raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional insertion at interim index 136 after untransposition:**

```text
STRATEGISCHWICHTIGENPU?K?HABENSOLLXWUERDEFUERDIEMIT1A11204GRMELDETEN?ONBESONDRERBEDEUTUNGSEINUNDMACHTENTSCHEIDDNGXOBABMKRSCHANGETRETRN
```

</details>

The two printed-dash fills, the inserted interim coordinate `F`, and four
observed-coordinate substitutions give this 134-character proposal:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same interim-insertion model, with the stated fills and substitutions:**

```text
STRATEGISCHWICHTIGENPUNKTHABENSOLLXWUERDEFUERDIEMIT1A11204GEMELDETENVONBESONDRERBEDEUTUNGSEINUNDMACHTENTSCHEIDUNGXOBABMARSCHANGETRETEN
```

</details>

It continues the strategic-points clause, invokes the literal reference
`1A11204`, calls the matter of particular significance, and says that a
decision on beginning the march is needed. The grammar around
`FUERDIEMIT1A11204GEMELDETEN` is elliptical; no missing noun is invented.
`PUNKT` and `BESONDRER` also remain as encoded, without adding a plural ending
or an unencoded vowel.

To verify the source-shaped witness, fractionate this proposal, remove its
coordinate at interim index 136, and transpose the remaining 267 coordinates
with the original rank order. That reproduces the source after exactly
the four substitutions and two dash fills. The proposed interim coordinate
has no received source index; all actual received coordinates retain theirs.

The [finite geometry audit](../../experiments/armistice_transit_planning/geometry_audit.json)
preserves 1,070 evaluated candidates: all single insertions and deletions
at both the transmitted and interim stages. The two frozen language models
favor interim insertion positions 136 and 137. For the retrospectively
assembled proposed text, position 136 uniquely minimizes substitutions
among all 268 interim insertion positions. This is a conditional consistency
result. It does not prove the original omission's location or exclude other
multi-error mechanisms, and the recovered tail is not classified as a
direct reading of an ordinary even frame.

## A6: request for the actual agreement

The [sixth part](../../experiments/armistice_transit_planning/sources/childs_p126_A6.png)
returns to an ordinary 242-slot frame. Its raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
WERDENSOLLXAEUSSERSTDRINGDXXUMANGABEDERTATSAECGLICHENVEREINBARUNGENUEBERWAFFENSTILLSTANDWIRDGEBET?NXXOXKXMX1BNOX11230OPXX
```

</details>

Two coordinate substitutions repair the single plaintext `G` in
`TATSAECGLICHEN` to `H`; a printed `T` erasure is filled to give the missing
`E` in `GEBETEN`. Readable wording, continuing A5:

**Readable German — continuation excerpt; the preceding words are outside this display:**

> … werden soll, äußerst dringd. Um Angabe der tatsächlichen Vereinbarungen
> über Waffenstillstand wird gebeten. O.K.M. `1BNOX11230OPXX`

The report requests the actual armistice agreement because the decision
whether to begin the march is extremely urgent. `DRINGD` is retained as an
abbreviation. The footer's numerical and letter labels remain literal.

## B: separate receipt note

The [adjacent B record](../../experiments/armistice_transit_planning/sources/childs_p126_B.png)
is a separate 134-coordinate message, not a seventh part of A:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
B) LP v NKJ (6.28 p.m., November 5th)
1201 (4)
RICHI-134
```

</details>

All 67 raw positions are fixed. The literal reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
OXHXL0XDRBHTUNGRM1XAX11118XOPGEH02XANGXORHALTENXOXK0M0RM1A011232XOP
```

</details>

Two observed-coordinate substitutions give `DRAHTUNG` and `ERHALTEN`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
OXHXL0XDRAHTUNGRM1XAX11118XOPGEH02XANGXERHALTENXOXK0M0RM1A011232XOP
```

</details>

It is a receipt notification with reference labels including `11118` and
`11232`. All `0`, `1`, other numeral labels and the `RM` strings are retained;
the edition does not turn them into a reconstructed historical numbering
system or infer that B acknowledges the six-part report.

## Exact costs and provenance

| Record | Source slots | Fixed positions | Observed-coordinate substitutions | Source-erasure fills | Other geometry |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| A1 | 244 | 122 / 122 | 0 | 0 | Ordinary |
| A2 | 238 | 119 / 119 | 1 | 0 | Ordinary |
| A3 | 200 | 100 / 100 | 1 | 0 | Ordinary |
| A4 | 212 | 105 / 106 | 0 | 1 | Ordinary |
| A5 | 267 | 131 / 134, conditional | 4 | 2 | One interim insertion before transposition |
| A6 | 242 | 120 / 121 | 2 | 1 | Ordinary |
| B | 134 | 67 / 67 | 2 | 0 | Ordinary |

The [inputs](../../experiments/armistice_transit_planning/inputs.json) preserve
the seven manual transcriptions, literal headers and nine source images.
The [certificate](../../experiments/armistice_transit_planning/certificates.json)
records every plaintext domain and coordinate origin, every change's printed
row/group/position, and the complete re-encrypted witnesses. All transmitted
lengths match the source. The total is 1,537 slots, ten valid-coordinate
substitutions, four source-erasure fills and one conditional interim insertion.
There are no changes to the published square or rank order.

The key is prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno
Wacker**, [2016, DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
also published in George Lasry's [2017-02-24 comment 4](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1).
Earlier unreviewed OCR-derived candidates and selected retrieval strings
existed. The bounded author-paper audit found no explicit p125/p126 body
example; this edition makes no universal first-decipherment claim.

```sh
python experiments/armistice_transit_planning/verify.py --verify
python experiments/armistice_transit_planning/geometry_audit.py --verify
```

## Later receipt and clause witnesses

The [p137 B4 and C source editions](armistice_clause_witnesses.md) preserve
copies of p125 A4 and p126 B. B4 independently witnesses the previously
masked coordinate in `BEFOERDERUNG`; C reproduces the two corrupt words
in the receipt, so their existing repairs remain editorial. Neither copy
changes the conditional geometry or uncertainty of p126 A5.

# An instruction to avoid fighting, with further orders to follow

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

An instruction to OKM requires avoidance of all fighting, compliance with demands abbreviated FRANZ, and attention to further orders. A joint reading with p225 recovers JEDER from its original coordinate pair. Only the word repair ZT to ZU remains, reducing the cost from four observed-coordinate substitutions to two.

## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p227 excerpt](../../experiments/avoid_fighting_instruction/sources/p227_reviewed.png) · [Inputs](../../experiments/avoid_fighting_instruction/inputs.json) · [Position and change certificates](../../experiments/avoid_fighting_instruction/certificates.json)

The published `Nov28-Dec1` key is unchanged. [Original OCR records](../../experiments/avoid_fighting_instruction/ocr_snapshot.json) and [reproducible comparisons with that earlier evidence](../../experiments/avoid_fighting_instruction/prior_candidates.json) are preserved separately. The present edition supplies checked source framing, exact costs and readable passages; it makes no first-public-decipherment claim.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [p227 D](#p227-d) | 272 | 136 / 136 | 4; **2 with shared J** | 0 |

## p227 D

**Source transcription — header:** `D) UKS v BSL (09.29 a.m., November 28th); KR 0912 (11/28); RICHI-272`

**Conditional interpretation — shared FA=J, with the two-coordinate ZT to ZU repair:**

> OKM. Auf Befehl der REICHSLEITG ist jeder Kampf zu vermeiden. Eingehen
> auf FRANZ Forderungen notwendig. Weitere Befehle folgen.
> OHL1A1136?GEH. OP2ANG.

The J at plaintext position 31 comes from the complete observed pair `FA`
at source positions 3 and 105. [p225 B2](regimental_journey_report.md#p225-b2)
provides a second native instance in `JEDE UNTERSTUETZUNG`.
The shared letter interpretation fixes **135/136 positions** in this message,
leaving the reference `1136?`; `FRANZ` remains abbreviated.
It extends the existing Nov28–Dec1 interpretation, including its historical
numeral assumptions. [Joint evidence and 24 square witnesses](../../experiments/late_november_joint_completion/README.md).

The subsequent [calendar and unit comparison](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/README.md)
also fixes the original `VG` pair in the reference as `7`:

| Field | After the shared J | After the unit interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| OHL reference | `1136?` | **11367** |

The conditional reading now fixes **136/136 positions**. Its two-coordinate
`ZT→ZU` repair is unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
OKMYAUFBEFEHLDERREICHSLEITGYIST1EDERKAMPFZTVERMEIDENYEINGEHENAUFFRANZYFORDERUNGENNOTWENDIGYWEITEREBEFEHLEFOLGENYYOHLXAXX280GEHYOPJANGYYY
```

**Edited output — earlier unchanged-key wording; 4 observed-coordinate substitutions:**

```text
OKMYAUFBEFEHLDERREICHSLEITGYISTJEDERKAMPFZUVERMEIDENYEINGEHENAUFFRANZYFORDERUNGENNOTWENDIGYWEITEREBEFEHLEFOLGENYYOHLXAXX280GEHYOPJANGYYY
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> OKM. Auf Befehl der REICHSLEITG ist jeder Kampf zu vermeiden. Eingehen auf FRANZ Forderungen notwendig. Weitere Befehle folgen. OHLXAXX280GEH. OPJANG.

**Meaning:** The message instructs OKM, on the order of the authority labeled REICHSLEITG, to avoid any fighting, says compliance with demands labeled FRANZ is necessary, and promises further orders. FRANZ is read as an abbreviation for French in this context; the source does not spell that word out. The message records an instruction, not proof that fighting stopped or that the demands were fulfilled.

**Editorial limits.**

- All 272 printed coordinates are present and legible, with no source erasures. The source photograph includes a complete group absent from the earlier OCR; restoring that visible group is a transcription correction, not an inserted historical coordinate.
- The high-resolution source reads FFFVD, including the third F with its middle bar. It is not treated as an invented missing coordinate or a T-shaped source mask.
- Under the published square, 1EDER to JEDER and ZT to ZU cost four substitutions. The shared FA=J interpretation removes the two J repairs; ZT to ZU still costs two. REICHSLEITG and FRANZ remain abbreviated.
- Y is the separator in this period key. The closing OHLXAXX280GEH and OPJANG are preserved literally; 280 is not turned into a calendar date or a reference number with an inferred format.

## Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates independently reconstruct column positions and domains, compare them with the cipher implementation, replay every priced change, and check all readable nonseparator labels. Partial readings have one consistent injective square/source-mask completion witness that re-encrypts exactly; those witness choices are not historical identifications. Source images are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and pixel digest.

Reproduce the source edition with `python experiments/avoid_fighting_instruction/verify.py --verify` and the joint extension with `python experiments/late_november_joint_completion/verify.py --verify`. The source verifier accepts `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` for the original PDF and exact crop pixels.

# p98 — disembarkation at Odessa and a repeated shipping instruction

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** Three complete source transcriptions and readable editions. The two versions of part 2 retain their separate lengths and place spellings. No missing-coordinate model is imposed.

Source edition and exact repair accounting: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Published **Nov1–3** square and ranks: Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker, unchanged. An earlier unreviewed candidate already identified the body of A1, including its appearance in the frozen p73 retrieval corpus. A2 and B were unreadable in the earlier OCR screen, which omitted their first source rows. Those candidates are preserved in [the prior-work record](../../experiments/black_sea_disembarkation/prior_candidates.json); the new full source transcriptions do not establish universal first-decipherment priority.

## Source records

All three records occur on Childs printed page 98 / PDF page 101. A is headed `OSM v LP (-------, November 1st)`, `BVG KOSPOLI (1/11) 0400 2 TEILE`. Its first and second parts carry `RICHI-252` and `RICHI-264`. B is headed `OSM v LP (9.37 a.m., November 2nd)`, `BVG KOSPOLI (1.11) 0400`, `2 TL`, `RICHI-266`.

| Record | Literal coordinates | Fixed plaintext positions | Proposed coordinate substitutions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A1 |252|126|3|
| A2 |264|132|1|
| B, repeated part 2 |266|133|3|
| **Total physical records** |**782**|**391**|**7**|

The source has no erased slots. Source transcription restores the full printed rows omitted by OCR; it does not insert coordinates into the historical ciphertext. The 391-position total includes both versions of the second part and is not a count of 391 distinct message characters.

## p98 A1

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FECHXROEMX2XGROSSXBFRX52751XISTDAHINABZUAENDERNXDYSSAUCHSIEGFRIEDTZUPPENNICHTMEHRI5KONSTANZAXSONDERNINODESSAAUSZUSCHIFFENSINDX
```

</details>

Edition, with three coordinate substitutions:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
FECHXROEMX2XGROSSXBFRX52751XISTDAHINABZUAENDERNXDASSAUCHSIEGFRIEDTRUPPENNICHTMEHRINKONSTANZAXSONDERNINODESSAAUSZUSCHIFFENSINDX
```

</details>

The cited instruction is to be amended so that the Siegfried troops, too, are to disembark at Odessa instead of Constanza. The three local proposals are `DYSS→DASS`, `TZUPPEN→TRUPPEN`, and `I5→IN`. Each changes one observed ciphertext coordinate. The last is a source repair in this word, not a reassignment of the key's digit5.

`FECH`, `ROEM`, `GROSS`, `B`, `FR` and the reference digits remain literal source labels. Their codebook or procedural meanings are not supplied.

## p98 A2

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DEMNACHGEHENNUMEHRSAEMTLICHESCHIFFEVONKOSPOLINACHODESSABEZWXNIKILJEWXVERTEILTWIEFRX52751XUNDXBVGXRUMXXF7CHXROEMX2XGROSSXBXFRX52787XX
```

</details>

The edition changes only `F7CH→FECH`, for one observed-coordinate substitution. The corresponding `E` is directly present in B. The text says that all ships from `KOSPOLI` are consequently to go to Odessa or the place written `NIKILJEW`, distributed according to the referenced instructions.

The source form `NUMEHR` is retained, and `NIKILJEW` is not silently replaced by the longer spelling in B.

## p98 B — second witness of part2

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DEMNACHGEHENNUMEGRSAEMTLFCHESCHIFFVVONKOSPOLINACHODESSABEZWXNIKOLAJEWXVERTEILTWIEFRX52751XUNDXBVGXRUMXXFECHXROEMX2XGROSSXBXFRX52787XX
```

**Edited output:**

```text
DEMNACHGEHENNUMEHRSAEMTLICHESCHIFFEVONKOSPOLINACHODESSABEZWXNIKOLAJEWXVERTEILTWIEFRX52751XUNDXBVGXRUMXXFECHXROEMX2XGROSSXBXFRX52787XX
```

</details>

The three proposed letters in `NUMEHR`, `SAEMTLICHES` and `SCHIFFE` are each directly observed in A2. The raw `NIKOLAJEW` spelling is retained in B and supports identifying the destination as Nikolaiev in the reading of this witness. It does not prove which spelling appeared in an earlier original transmission.

## Witness checks and limits

The certificate identifies all four A2/B cross-supported letters by plaintext index and by the two original source-coordinate indices in both copies. The proposed target pair equals an entirely observed pair in the other copy. The three A1 repairs are separately identified as ordinary-word proposals without this second-copy evidence.

The published key and column ranks remain unchanged. There are **no fills, coordinate additions, deletions, reorders or new numeral assignments**. A2 and B retain their264/266-coordinate frames; no forced common message, restored extra `N`, or added letter in the shorter place spelling is claimed.

Complete source rows, raw and edited round trips, repair ledgers and retained numerical labels are in [the certificate](../../experiments/black_sea_disembarkation/certificates.json). [The experiment README](../../experiments/black_sea_disembarkation/README.md) documents reproduction and PDF crop authentication.

# Black Sea evacuation routes, the Braila prohibition and onward rail movement

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**New source editions and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**
**Existing part2 body: Ayush Agarwal (@AyushAg1002), 2026-10-28.**

Childs pp88–90, PDF pp91–93, preserve a source-labeled five-part order.
The repeated header is `OSM de LP (01.18 p.m., November 1st)`, followed
by `SSD BVG KOSPOLI (1/11) 1400 5 TEILE`. The explicit sequence is
**p88 C1, p89 A2, p89 A3, p89 A4, p90 A5**. The source time fields
remain unchanged. All parts use the published **Nov1–3** key.

This edition adds **four physical records**. The already reviewed p89 A2
is included only as credited context. A3 contains a source-declared loss
of 20 groups, so its restored prefix is presented with its full missing
coordinate cost and its unresolved tail.

## p88 C1

The [first-part crop](../../experiments/black_sea_evacuation_routes/sources/p88_C1.png)
contains **298 valid coordinates**, matching `1 TL RICHI-298`.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 298-coordinate frame:**

```text
ERSTENSXZUXFECHXRMX2XGROSSXBXFRX50749XXFUERABSCHUBGELTENFOLGENREZIELEDOPPELPUNKTXSIEGFRIEDXNACHXKONSTANZAXALLESUEBRIGEXODESSAXUNDFALLSDIESESNICHTMEHR
```

**Edited output — one observed-coordinate substitution, with no fills:**

```text
ERSTENSXZUXFECHXRMX2XGROSSXBXFRX50749XXFUERABSCHUBGELTENFOLGENDEZIELEDOPPELPUNKTXSIEGFRIEDXNACHXKONSTANZAXALLESUEBRIGEXODESSAXUNDFALLSDIESESNICHTMEHR
```

</details>

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation; the clause continues into part 2:**

> Erstens. Zu FECH RM. 2. Gross B. FR. 50749. Für Abschub gelten
> folgende Ziele, Doppelpunkt: Siegfried nach Konstanza, alles übrige
> Odessa, und falls dieses nicht mehr ...

Source **288 D→G** changes `FOLGENRE` to `FOLGENDE`. The name
`SIEGFRIED` remains a literal source name, without a new identification
of a particular vessel or formation.

## Existing p89 A2 — earlier credited context

This part's body is credited to **Ayush Agarwal**, and its prior
[conservative source edition](../supplementary/p89_A2.md) is unchanged.
It has **290 source slots**, **145 plaintext positions**, and
**142 fixed positions** in that conservative layer. It is **not** one
of the four new records or part of their totals.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — existing credited conservative source reading, unchanged:**

```text
AUFNAHMEFAEHIGXNIKOLAJEWXAUFWUNSCHXEZXKIEWXBESTIMMTXHPTMXJOELXVXOXFECHXODESSAX?ELCHES?HI?FEETWAXWEGENXEISENBAHNLAGEXNACHXNIKOLAJEWXZUGEHENHABENXX
```

</details>

This continues the Odessa capacity clause and gives Nikolajew as another
destination, naming Hptm. Joel and railway-related routing from Odessa.
The three uncertainties and source-glyph qualifications remain exactly as
in the earlier edition; the assembly does not silently fill them.

## p89 A3

**Readable German — current conditional proposal; each ? is one unresolved position:**

> Zweitens. Nach Braila geht nichts. Dorthin unterwegs befindliche
> Dampfer abdrehen. Drittens. Weiterleitung in geschlossenen Zügen.
> Ziel für MILI? DIENSTELLEN: Ers. Batl. 2 Garderegts. z. F?sz? Berlin.

**English meaning:** Nothing is to go to Braila, and steamers already on
that route are to turn back. Onward transport is to use whole trains.
The conditional continuation names a destination for apparently military
offices, followed by a replacement-battalion designation and Berlin.
The last clause still has three unresolved labels.

The new reading supplies ten positions beyond the
[guard-battalion extension](../../experiments/p89_guard_battalion_extension/README.md),
reaching **176/179 fixed positions under the conditional model**. All ten
new assignments have one observed coordinate half and require only the
missing half to be filled. Their complete cost and independent witnesses
are in the [destination continuation](../../experiments/p89_destination_continuation/README.md).

The proposed spelling `DIENSTELLEN` is deliberately retained. The normal
word `DIENSTSTELLEN` is thirteen characters long, while this target span
has eleven. The hypothesis is an omitted `ST` within `STST`. A separate
raw message, **p78 A2**, supplies `DIENSTSTELLEN` with all 26 coordinate
halves observed; the target spelling agrees with its own **16 observed
halves**. This is a constrained textual proposal, not the recovery of the
two additional letters or a change to the source frame.

A contemporary [1918 Berlin directory](../../experiments/p89_destination_continuation/HISTORY.md)
lists **2. Garderegiment zu Fuß** in Berlin. It supports the proposed unit
name and city, but does not determine the replacement battalion's November
location or any missing cipher labels. The T in `BATL` remains wholly
absent, and the numeral 2 is supported by one observed half.

The [third-part crop](../../experiments/black_sea_evacuation_routes/sources/p89_A3.png)
prints `3 TL RICHI-358` and **`(missed 20 groups)`** after five
40-coordinate rows. There are **258 visible slots**, including one
printed dash. Inserting **100 unknown coordinate slots at source
boundary 200** gives the source-declared 358-coordinate frame. The page
supplies the gap's size and placement.

<details>
<summary>Source, exact candidate and cumulative repair account</summary>

**Raw output — source-declared frame with 100 missing coordinates:**

```text
???ITE??NA???BR?I?A???HTN??HT???O??H?N???ERL??SB???ND?I?H???MPF??AB???HE?X?D???TEN??WE???RL?I?U???NGE??HL???EN?N?U???NXZ???F???MI?I?D???STE???N???SX?A?L???GAR???E???XZ?F?SZ??ERL??
```

**Edited output — current conditional proposal in that same frame:**

```text
ZWEITENSNACHXBRAILAXGEHTNICHTSXDORTHINUNTERWEGSBEFINDLICHEDAMPFERABDREHENXXDRITTENSXWEITERLEITUNGINGESCHLOSSENENZUEGENXZIELFUERMILI?DIENSTELLENXERSXBATLX2XGARDEREGTSXZXF?SZ?BERLIN
```

All prices are cumulative. A fixed position can be an editorially supplied
letter, separator or numeral under the indicated layer.

| Layer | Fixed positions | Observed substitutions | Printed-dash fills | Lost-coordinate fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Raw source-declared frame | 81/179 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Original prefix | 151/179 | 1 | 1 | 69 |
| Guard designation and Berlin | 166/179 | 1 | 1 | 85 |
| Current destination proposal | **176/179** | **1** | **1** | **95** |

The inherited observed substitution is **source 243 A→G**, giving the W
in `UNTERWEGS`. The printed dash at **source 242** is filled with A.
The subsequent layers add no observed substitutions or printed-mask fills.
All machine indices are zero-based.

</details>

The remaining plaintext positions are **131**, **169** and **172**. The
first two have both coordinates missing. Position 172, immediately before
`BERLIN`, has the pair `X?` and admits only **1, 3, 4, 6, A or Y** under
the published key. Reading it as a separator X would require another
observed-coordinate substitution. The five remaining coordinate masks
permit exactly **6^5 = 7,776** complete strings under this candidate model;
this count does not select the historical wording.

## p89 A4

The [fourth-part crop](../../experiments/black_sea_evacuation_routes/sources/p89_A4.png)
has **360 valid coordinates**, matching `4 TL RICHI-360`. Detail
crops confirm the G in `GVGAG` and the X in `XDXFX`, which can look
misleading at lower resolution; neither requires an editorial source edit.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 360-coordinate frame:**

```text
XIVILPERSONENBERLINXZIELFUERGESCHLOSSENETRUPPENTEILEHIER7RFRAGENXXVIERTENSXUMUNTERBRINGUNGUNDWEITERLEITUNGSICHERZUSTELLENXSORGTXSXMXSTXFUERMOEQLICHSTFRUEHZEITIQEUNDGENAUEVORMELDUNG
```

**Edited output — four observed-coordinate substitutions, with no fills:**

```text
ZIVILPERSONENBERLINXZIELFUERGESCHLOSSENETRUPPENTEILEHIERERFRAGENXXVIERTENSXUMUNTERBRINGUNGUNDWEITERLEITUNGSICHERZUSTELLENXSORGTXSXMXSTXFUERMOEGLICHSTFRUEHZEITIGEUNDGENAUEVORMELDUNG
```

</details>

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation:**

> Zivilpersonen Berlin. Ziel für geschlossene Truppenteile hier
> erfragen. Viertens. Um Unterbringung und Weiterleitung sicherzustellen,
> sorgt S. M. St. für möglichst frühzeitige und genaue Vormeldung.

The first raw X is repaired to the Z of `ZIVILPERSONEN`; it is not
automatically treated as a separator. The raw 7 in `HIER7RFRAGEN`
is another explicitly priced word repair. The key and all numerical
reference fields remain unchanged.

## p90 A5

The [fifth-part crop](../../experiments/black_sea_evacuation_routes/sources/p90_A5.png)
contains **398 valid coordinates**, matching `5 TL RICHI-398`.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 398-coordinate frame:**

```text
ANEMPFANGSSTELLENINXUKRAINEXGLEICHESANXETRAXOSTXSUEDOSTXBVGXKOSPOLIXEZXKI7WXSXMXSTXDTSCHXSTABXSXAXBERLINXNATEKOXNACHRXRXMXAXADMIRALSTABXSEEKRIEGSLEITUNGXFELDEISENBAHNCHEFXRMX2XQROSSXBXFRX52751X31X10X
```

**Edited output — two observed-coordinate substitutions, with no fills:**

```text
ANEMPFANGSSTELLENINXUKRAINEXGLEICHESANXETRAXOSTXSUEDOSTXBVGXKOSPOLIXEZXKIEWXSXMXSTXDTSCHXSTABXSXAXBERLINXNATEKOXNACHRXRXMXAXADMIRALSTABXSEEKRIEGSLEITUNGXFELDEISENBAHNCHEFXRMX2XGROSSXBXFRX52751X31X10X
```

</details>

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation, keeping abbreviations literal:**

> An Empfangsstellen in Ukraine. Gleiches an Etra Ost, Südost, BVG
> Kospoli, Ez. Kiew, S. M. St., Dtsch. Stab, S. A. Berlin, Nateko,
> Nachr. R. M. A., Admiralstab, Seekriegsleitung, Feldeisenbahnchef.
> RM. 2. Gross B. FR. 52751. 31.10.

The source continues with the following **printed cleartext**, which
is outside the encrypted body and all plaintext-position counts.

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — printed cleartext outside the encrypted body:**

```text
BITTE JETZT NUR QUITTUNG FALLS FUNKSPRUECHE VORLIEGEN
SENDEN SIE DIESE VON 1830 BIS 20,25 H v OSM v LP UM
```

</details>

## Conditional interpretation and unresolved space

The four newly edited records comprise **1,314 visible source slots**,
**1,313 valid observed coordinates** and **707 modeled plaintext positions**.
Including the current A3 continuation, their proposed readings use **eight
observed substitutions**, **one printed-dash fill** and **95 fills of
explicitly lost coordinates**. The earlier Ayush part 2 remains outside
these totals. A3 is the only part of this new group with a source-declared
large loss; three of its plaintext positions remain unresolved in the
current conditional reading.

The complete order distinguishes the route of evacuation, onward movement
by whole trains, and destinations for different groups. Its next part
specifies Berlin for civilians and requires an enquiry about destinations
for formed troop units. Those source-numbered adjacent clauses give the
A3 continuation a useful context without supplying its missing characters.
The order records intended movements; it does not establish that the
steamers turned back or that the personnel reached the stated destinations.

The [original source inputs](../../experiments/black_sea_evacuation_routes/inputs.json),
[baseline certificates](../../experiments/black_sea_evacuation_routes/certificates.json),
[credited part 2 snapshot](../../experiments/black_sea_evacuation_routes/existing_part2.json)
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/black_sea_evacuation_routes/README.md)
retain the source, loss placement and earlier editorial operations.
The [current A3 package](../../experiments/p89_destination_continuation/README.md)
adds the exact continuation, independent word witnesses, historical source
and bounded retrieval checks.

# Bridges and the wire connection through Budapest

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p100 B reports that bridges have been blown up and attributes an
interruption of the wire lines through Budapest to the Hungarian National
Council. It ends with the literal headquarters label `A.O.K.11`.
The edition establishes what this telegram reports; it does not independently
verify those events or identify the location meant by `DORT`.

## Source and body

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [printed p100, PDF p103](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [B crop](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p100_B.png)
is under a November 1 heading:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
B) UKS v ZÖN (------ November 2nd)
RICHI-194
```

</details>

Manual transcription finds **194 valid coordinates**, matching the printed
length. An earlier 195-slot OCR extraction produced a garbled result; its
extra slot is not treated as a historical cipher error. The unchanged
published `Nov1-3` key fixes all 97 raw plaintext positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
BRUECKENXDORTXGESPRENGTXDRAHTLEITUNGENXUEBERXBUDAPESTXDURCHSUNGXNATIONALRATXUNTERBJOCHENXAXOXKX11
```

</details>

Two observed-coordinate substitutions give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
BRUECKENXDORTXGESPRENGTXDRAHTLEITUNGENXUEBERXBUDAPESTXDURCHXUNGXNATIONALRATXUNTERBROCHENXAXOXKX11
```

</details>

Readable German, expanding only the explicit abbreviation in brackets:

**Readable German:**

> Brücken dort gesprengt. Drahtleitungen über Budapest durch
> ung[arischen] Nationalrat unterbrochen. A.O.K. 11.

| Source index, zero-based | Printed group / position, one-based | Change | Effect |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 118 | 24 / 4 | `V` → `X` | `DURCHSUNG` → `DURCHXUNG` |
| 130 | 27 / 1 | `V` → `D` | `UNTERBJOCHEN` → `UNTERBROCHEN` |

There are no source erasures, inserted coordinates or square changes. The
final **11** is unchanged in both the raw and repaired readings.

The adjacent [p100 C](../radio/radio_contacts_and_keys.md#p100-c-direct-contact-while-the-wire-is-broken)
asks about direct communication and also says the wire is interrupted.
The separately printed B body is not merged with the earlier
[p100 challenge](../p100.md); that challenge's Belgrade reading retains
**Armin's 2017 comment 13** priority. A multipart relationship is not required
to verify this independent source frame.

## Reproduce

The [inputs](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/inputs.json) and
[certificate](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/certificates.json)
preserve the source groups and exact forward witness.

```sh
python experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/verify.py --verify
```

The key is credited to **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**,
[DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
with full prior-key provenance in the input record. Earlier unreviewed OCR
candidates existed. No first-decipherment priority is claimed from the
bounded absence of an explicit body example in the author-paper review.

# Railway message: Laz. Zug 42 from Chemnitz and Zug 34 to VERBETZ

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p107 B1/B2, PDF p110, form the two-part message headed
`UKS v ZÖN (4.48 a.m., November 3rd)` and
`VEVE 1905 (2) AN LP 2 TLE`. The consecutive labels and repeated railway
subject support the assembly. Both use the unchanged published
**Nov1–3** key.

## p107 B1

The [source crop](../../experiments/p107_railway_and_dragoman/sources/p107_B.png)
contains **164 valid coordinates**, matching `1 TL RICHI-164`.
The earlier OCR omitted the final **FDGD** row and masked source **152 D**.
Restoring those visible glyphs recovers the native frame; the exact old
OCR is retained in a [frozen snapshot](../../experiments/p107_railway_and_dragoman/ocr_snapshot.json).

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 164-coordinate frame:**

```text
EISMNBAHNTRANB6ORTABTLGXSXOXPFESSXGXHX1XQXXBEILINIEN1DTXGXLAZXZUGX42XVONXCHEMNITZX
```

**Edited output — five observed-coordinate substitutions, with no fills:**

```text
EISENBAHNTRANSPORTABTLGXSXOXPFESSXGXHX1XQXXBEILINIENKDTXGXLAZXZUGX42XVONXCHEMNITZX
```

</details>

The changes are source **43 D→G**, **44 G→D**, **62 X→V**, **66 X→V** and
**160 F→V**. The last is a genuine proposed source change within the
restored final row; it is counted separately from correcting the OCR.
The candidate repairs the railway-transport wording and `LINIEN1DT`;
the opaque **PFESS** and **G H 1 Q** fields remain unchanged.

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation, keeping abbreviations and opaque fields literal:**

> Eisenbahntransportabtlg. S. O. PFESS. G. H. 1. Q. Bei Linienkdt.
> G. Laz. Zug 42 von Chemnitz.

The routing abbreviations, including **G** before **LAZ**, are not
expanded. This part fixes **82 / 82 positions**; its complete edited
candidate re-encrypts exactly.

## p107 B2

The same crop has **110 visible slots** for `2 TL RICHI-110`, including
the printed dash in **DGFG-** at source index **39**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 110-coordinate frame:**

```text
WAZXZUGX34XNACHXVERBETZXA5ROLIENLASSENXX?BAXAEK11X10502
```

**Edited output — three observed-coordinate substitutions, with no fills:**

```text
LAZXZUGX34XNACHXVERBETZXABROLLENLASSENXX?BAXAEK11X10502
```

</details>

The changes are source **12 G→A**, **21 D→F** and **54 X→V**. The printed
dash remains unresolved. No character in the closing is supplied merely
to produce a familiar command abbreviation.

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation:**

> Laz. Zug 34 nach VERBETZ abrollen lassen. ?BA. AEK11. 10502.

**VERBETZ** is the literal decoded destination; no independent location
identification or spelling correction is imposed. The dispatch wording
is an instruction, not proof that either train moved.

## Conditional interpretation and remaining ambiguity

The candidate for B2 fixes **54 / 55 positions**. Its unknown position
**40** has pair **?V**, source indices **39** and **67**, and domain
**3BFKQS**. All six possible complete ciphertexts and plaintexts are
retained as exact re-encryption witnesses; none is selected as the
historical closing.

Across these two records there are **274 visible slots**, **273 valid
coordinates** and **136 / 137 fixed plaintext positions**. The main
edition uses **eight observed-coordinate substitutions and no fills**,
with no frame, length or key change. Local changes to `TRANB6ORT`,
`LINIEN1DT` and `A5ROLIEN` do not establish global numeral mappings.

The package retains earlier unread OCR frames and candidate readings,
along with the published key's provenance. It makes no historical
first-solution claim. See [inputs](../../experiments/p107_railway_and_dragoman/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/p107_railway_and_dragoman/certificates.json)
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/p107_railway_and_dragoman/README.md).

# November 9: Danube report and Arad provisions [Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md) These reports received on 9 November concern a Danube crossing and provisions at Arad for **80,000 men and 30,000 animals**. Source comparison restores a misread Danube-report glyph and eleven coordinates missing from the earlier Arad copy. The readings use the published **Nov7–9** key. ## p164 C1 **Readable German — conditional date and army completion:** > AOK11. Abendmeldung 8.11.18. Lage der 11 Armee am 7.11 abends. Donauuebergang 219 I D beendet. Belgrad SEMUM. Lebhafter Uebersetzverkehr. This first part of a five-part report describes the Eleventh Army's evening situation on 7 November: the 219th Infantry Division has completed its Danube crossing, with busy crossing traffic at `BELGRAD` and `SEMUM`. The proposed report date is 8 November 1918; interception followed early on 9 November. `SEMUM` retains the transmitted spelling. The completion reads `8XC1X1?` as a day.month.year date and identifies `?1 ARMEE` with the `AOK11` already named at the start. The nearby [p155 report](nov7_derailment_and_trains.md#p155-d) uses the fully observed date form `7X11X18`. These two contextual assumptions complete **124/124 positions** at a total cost of **five observed substitutions and five source-mask fills**. | Field | Additional source changes, zero-based | Basis | | --- | --- | --- | | `8XC1X1?` → `8X11X18` | 139 `D` → `G`; 164 dash → `A` | Day.month.year interpretation within the 1918 sequence | | `?1 ARMEE` → `11 ARMEE` | 52 invalid `C` → `G` | The same message opens with native `AOK11` | Literal header: `C) ZON v UKS (1.57 a.m., November 9th); 2101 5 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-248`. [Source crop](../../experiments/danube_arad_witnesses/sources/p164_C1.png).
p164 source, earlier word layer and exact conditional completion The direct source supplies 119 of 124 raw labels. Two mask values from the parallel p153 passage raise this to 121 before lexical repair. The earlier word proposal costs four observed substitutions and three printed-mask fills, leaving the date and army fields unresolved: **Readable German — complete edited stream, preserving the unresolved fields and literal labels:** > AOK11. Abendmeldung 8. C1 1?. Lage der ?1 Armee am 7 11 abends. Donauuebergang 219 I D beendet. Belgrad SEMUM. Lebhafter Uebersetzverkehr. **Source transcription — literal printed rows:** ```text V-VVA XGVDV XDAGD XAVXX GDAAD FAVVF XDXGA DDGVX VX-DV DVXGV DGCFX VGVXX VVXXF GDDAF XXGDD FAFDX XDGXX VAVFX FFVVA VVDGG XXDXF FXVDA AGVAG FDDGV GDVDG VVDFV XVFVD -DDVD VVVVG GDXVV DGDDG XDVVV DAGV- GVVDV VVVVX FGVDG VFVVX DXVDF FFDDG GDXDV XGDDV GGXDF VVGVV VGVGV XFVFX VDDGA GDADG VDFDA XXDDD DDA ``` **Raw output — native source, before word repair:** ```text AOKX11ABENDM?LDUNG8XC1X1?XLAGSTE0?1XARMEEAM7X11XABENDSXDONA?UEBERGANG219XIXDXBEENDZTXBELGRADXSEMUMLEBHAFTERUEBER?ETZVERKEHRX ``` **Raw output — two mask values supported by the parallel p153 passage; zero observed-coordinate substitutions:** ```text AOKX11ABENDM?LDUNG8XC1X1?XLAGSTE0?1XARMEEAM7X11XABENDSXDONAUUEBERGANG219XIXDXBEENDZTXBELGRADXSEMUMLEBHAFTERUEBERSETZVERKEHRX ``` **Edited output — from the unfilled source: four observed substitutions and three printed-mask fills; two fields remain unresolved:** ```text AOKX11ABENDMELDUNG8XC1X1?XLAGEDER?1XARMEEAM7X11XABENDSXDONAUUEBERGANG219XIXDXBEENDETXBELGRADXSEMUMLEBHAFTERUEBERSETZVERKEHRX ``` The source’s fourth-row group is GDXVV, correcting earlier OCR/edition GDXXV. Its printed V at source 148 restores the E in UEBER, with zero historical coordinate-repair cost. p153 directly supplies U in DONAU and S in SETZ; p164 in turn supports the E/A/E repairs in p153’s U3BER, BELGR4D and UEBSR. The native unit labels are 219 and 21B. The corresponding p164 pair now supports a separately priced [219 proposal for p153](nov7_danube_and_message_reports.md#p153-b1). LAGE DER and BEENDET are word repairs. ABENDMELDUNG uses one lexical mask fill beyond the two independent-passage fills. Every price is measured from the unfilled native source. **Conditional interpretation — date and army completed; 5 observed substitutions and 5 source-mask fills:** ```text AOKX11ABENDMELDUNG8X11X18XLAGEDER11XARMEEAM7X11XABENDSXDONAUUEBERGANG219XIXDXBEENDETXBELGRADXSEMUMLEBHAFTERUEBERSETZVERKEHRX ``` The two newly supplied digits use printed masks. The month correction changes an observed `D`; all three source appearances remain unchanged in the transcription. Both completions of the unused 5/6 square cells reproduce this same full reading and ciphertext.
## Conditional digit reading The [shared Nov7–9 reference interpretation](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) supplies **6** in the Arad footer, giving **RM 1C 186 GEH** and **136/136 conditional edited labels** in p168 E. The opposite assignment gives 185 GEH. Both coordinates of this VF pair are original observations. The four word substitutions, two printed-mask fills and one supplied gap coordinate remain unchanged. ## p168 E **Readable German — complete edited stream, preserving the unresolved fields and literal labels:** > An OHL. Verpflegung noch 14 Tage. 10 Tage. Verpfleg. Zuege nach Arad. Arad bei ungar. Regierung erwirken. STAEKE 80000 Mann, 30000 Tiere. AOK11. RM 1C18?GEH. The report requests provision trains to Arad and action through the Hungarian government. Both strength figures come directly from observed ciphertext pairs. The relationship between “14 Tage” and “10 Tage” remains unclear; the transmitted `STAEKE`, repeated Arad and closing labels are retained. Literal header: `E) UKS v ZON (11.05 p.m., November 9th);AN LP 2000 KR; RICHI-272`. [Source crop](../../experiments/danube_arad_witnesses/sources/p168_E.png). The source prints 271 slots. In the conditional 272-slot frame, the short group DDGX lacks one G present in p159’s DDGGX. Either insertion boundary 52 or 53 gives the same completed group. p159 also supplies the two printed masks in VF--F. These three borrowed values change no observed p168 coordinate and raise the reading from 132 to 135 fixed positions out of 136.
p168 source, source-linked reading and four-repair proposal **Source transcription — literal printed rows:** ```text FDVDD FXAAX XGVDD XVDDX XADVV XFVXD VDAGG ADVDV VADDA VDDGV DDGX GVVGX GVXVG VDVXX VGXXA ADDVV FFXDF XDXXV DGAGF VDAXV VXDDG VXAAV GDDGA XADVF DVFDX GDGXG VGDDX VXVAG VDVDD DDGVG DXXVX GDDGX DDGAA GVAVD VVGAA VGDVD VVDVG GGGDF XGDGD DDDVV VF--F VDGDD VXDAD XDADV GVVVV GDVDD DDVGG VVDGG DVVVV VAFVA DXXXV VVVFA FFADV DAXVV FV ``` **Raw output — conditional 272-slot frame; one unfilled coordinate in DDGX, with printed masks unfilled:** ```text ANOHLXVERPFLEGUNGNOCH14TAGEX10TAGEXXVERPFLEGXEUEGENACHARADHARADNEIUNGARXREGIERUNGERWIRKENXSTAEKE80000MANNX30000?IEREXAO?1?XRMX1CX18?GEHX ``` **Raw output — three source-linked coordinate values, with every borrowed value bound to a directly observed p159 origin:** ```text ANOHLXVERPFLEGUNGNOCH14TAGEX10TAGEXXVERPFLEGXEUEGENACHARADHARADNEIUNGARXREGIERUNGERWIRKENXSTAEKE80000MANNX30000TIEREXAOK11XRMX1CX18?GEHX ``` **Edited output — four observed substitutions, two printed-mask fills and one added-slot fill; footer cell unassigned:** ```text ANOHLXVERPFLEGUNGNOCH14TAGEX10TAGEXXVERPFLEGXZUEGENACHARADXARADBEIUNGARXREGIERUNGERWIRKENXSTAEKE80000MANNX30000TIEREXAOK11XRMX1CX18?GEHX ``` The p168 pairs independently fix 80000 and the X in 14 TAGE X 10 TAGE. The old p159 optional U is not imported. The common edited stream costs four observed p168 substitutions, its two mask fills and the one supplied gap coordinate. The remaining VF footer cell has the shared domain {5,6}, giving 18{5,6}GEH; p159’s raw footer instead ends GLH.
## Arad cross-copy restoration The p168 witness raises the earlier p159 primary frame from **124 to 135 fixed positions**. Its eleven supplied coordinates are all directly observed in p168, independent of the three values p168 borrows in the reverse comparison. This establishes the formerly uncertain strength field from surviving source pairs.
Restored p159 stream and complete source-family comparison **Raw output — p159 primary geometry with all 11 missing coordinates supplied from observed p168 pairs:** ```text 0NOHLXVERPOLEGUNGNOCH14TAGEX10TAGEXXVERPFLEGXEUEGENACHARADXARADNEIUNGARXREGIERUNGERWIRKENXSTAEKE80000MANNX30000TISREXAOK11XRMX1CX18?GLHX ``` The coordinate-only comparison covers 173,580 canonical layouts and 694,320 source-origin maps. Five disagreements across 258 jointly observed positions are the minimum. Only two canonical layouts remain: short-slot boundary 118 with five-slot boundaries (15,110) or (16,110). The four choices of duplicated group origin give eight minimizing maps, all with one completed ciphertext and 135/136 fixed labels. Each supplies its eleven additions from native p168 observations. Within this error family, coordinate comparison reduces the earlier 64 word-conditioned minima to eight and excludes all 48 P0000 alternatives. The earlier six-change objective fitted a word template; the present five-disagreement objective compares the received coordinates.
The common edited reading costs **seven observed substitutions in p159** and **four in p168**. The extra p159 repair beyond its earlier six-word layer adopts p168’s GEH footer spelling. Both copies keep the globally coupled unknown digit. The [current p159 case](arad_provisions_partial.md) now presents this improved collation first, with the superseded U and P0000 hypotheses in a historical comparison drawer. ## Source and prior work Childs printed pp164 and 168 correspond to PDF pp167 and 171. # Request for a position on a Dobrudscha report

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p142 C asks for a response to an Entente report of renewed Romanian
occupation of the Dobrudscha. The message is addressed to the literal
`N.O. MACKENSEN` field and closes with `ABT FREMDE HEERE`. This edition
recovers the report's wording; it does not independently establish the
military event or expand the abbreviated addressee's office.

## Source and reading

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [printed p142, PDF p145](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [C crop](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p142_C.png)
is under a November 6 heading:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
C) NKJ v LP (09.00 p.m., November 6th)
FUER UKS 1915 (6/11)
RICHI-242
```

</details>

The 242-slot source contains two printed dashes. The unchanged published
`Nov4-6` key fixes 119 of 121 raw positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
?NXNXOXMACKENSENXENTENTEMELDETX5011XERNEUTRUMAENISCHE?ESETZUNGDERXDOBRU2SCHAXSTELLUNGSNAHMEERBETENXABTXFREMDEHEERED17U560
```

</details>

One known-coordinate substitution and two dash fills give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ANXNXOXMACKENSENXENTENTEMELDETX5011XERNEUTRUMAENISCHEBESETZUNGDERXDOBRUDSCHAXSTELLUNGSNAHMEERBETENXABTXFREMDEHEERED17U560
```

</details>

Readable core, with the reference retained literally:

**Readable German:**

> An N.O. Mackensen. Entente meldet `5011` erneut rumänische Besetzung
> der Dobrudscha. Stellungsnahme [Stellungnahme] erbeten. Abt. Fremde Heere `D17U560`.

The numerical/reference labels **`5011`** and **`D17U560`** remain as read.
They are not normalized into dates or message numbers. The raw `2` within
`DOBRU2SCHA` is retained in the raw reading and explicitly repaired locally
to `D`; this does not reassign the square's digit `2`.

Both machine layers retain `STELLUNGSNAHME`. The bracketed
**[Stellungnahme]** is a prose-only spelling normalization: its omitted `S`
is not an additional source-coordinate repair or a change to the edited
output above.

| Source index, zero-based | Printed group / position, one-based | Change | Treatment |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | 2 / 4 | `G` → `F` | Known-coordinate substitution: `2` → `D` in the place name |
| 34 | 7 / 5 | printed dash → `V` | Source-erasure fill: `B` in `BESETZUNG` |
| 84 | 17 / 5 | printed dash → `V` | Source-erasure fill: initial `A` in `AN` |

The source length, transposition and full published square are unchanged.
The [certificate](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/certificates.json)
includes every source-coordinate origin and the exact reconstructed witness.

```sh
python experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/verify.py --verify
```

The key is prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno
Wacker**, [DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
with provenance in the [inputs](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/inputs.json).
Earlier unreviewed OCR-derived candidates existed. The bounded paper review
does not establish universal first-decipherment priority; exact arithmetic
does not prove unique historical wording or independent truth of the report.

# p83 B — dissolution of formations and return of personnel

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** Complete direct source reading, with no coordinate repairs. This page prints the second part of a message. Subsequent review of an exact p79 second-part witness supplies its first-part context; see the linked source edition below.

Source edition and reproducible verification: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The unchanged **Oct28–31** period key is credited to Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker. An earlier unreviewed OCR-derived reading already contained this body and was included in the frozen p73 retrieval corpus; this edition resolves its three OCR erasures from the visible printed coordinates. It does not claim first decipherment.

## Source and scope

Childs, printed page 83 / PDF page 86, labels the item `B) OSM v LP (4.09 p.m., October 30th)`, `2 TL`, `RICHI-336`. The source contains exactly 336 valid coordinates, giving 168 fixed plaintext positions under the published key. The source crop and all manual rows are in [the input record](../../experiments/formation_dissolution/inputs.json).

The p83 page itself contains no first part. Subsequent source review identified [p79 A1/A2](palestine_medical_dissolution.md): A2 repeats all 336 coordinates of this second part, while A1 names the medical formations lost in Palestine apart from their remaining personnel. The complete first-part text, literal unit labels and source-header differences are preserved in that edition. This supplies the previously missing antecedent without changing the p83 source or repair count. `K.M.` remains an unexpanded abbreviation.

## Literal plaintext

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
BEIMXKXMXISTBEANTRAGTSIEFUERAUFGELOESTZUERKLAERENXXNOCHVORHANDENESPERSONALDIESERFORMATIONENISTZUDENHEIMISCHENERSATZTRUPPENTEILENINMARSCHZUSETZENXOHLXRMX1XCXNRX103577XOP
```

</details>

**Readable German:**

> Beim K.M. ist beantragt, sie fuer aufgeloest zu erklaeren. Noch vorhandenes Personal dieser Formationen ist zu den heimischen Ersatztruppenteilen in Marsch zu setzen. OHL. RM 1 C Nr103577 Op.

The telegram says a request has been made to declare the formations dissolved, and orders their remaining personnel to proceed to replacement units at home. The closing reference is retained as printed-key labels, without a new numerical interpretation.

## Verification and limits

The literal source, analysis frame and re-encrypted reading all have336 coordinates. There are **zero substitutions, source erasures, fills, additions, deletions or reorders**. All 168 positions are fixed under the unchanged published key.

[The certificate](../../experiments/formation_dissolution/certificates.json) records source-coordinate pairs, the complete digit/J/Q/Y inventory and a round trip. # A second-part instruction on security measures at own discretion

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

A complete native second-part body directs security measures according to one’s own discretion. Its first part is not supplied. Six explicitly priced coordinate changes recover the ordinary-word clause while the opening label, two irregular spellings and three coupled reference positions remain literal or unresolved.


**Reviewed source crops:** [p184_reviewed.png](../../experiments/group_security_measures_fragment/sources/p184_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).
## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p184 excerpt — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/group_security_measures_fragment/inputs.json) · [Inputs](../../experiments/group_security_measures_fragment/inputs.json) · [Position and change certificates](../../experiments/group_security_measures_fragment/certificates.json)

The published `Nov13-15b` key is unchanged. [Original OCR records](../../experiments/group_security_measures_fragment/ocr_snapshot.json) and [reproducible comparisons with that earlier evidence](../../experiments/group_security_measures_fragment/prior_candidates.json) are preserved separately. The present edition supplies checked source framing, exact costs and readable passages; it makes no first-public-decipherment claim.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [p184 A2](#p184-a2) | 202 | 96 / 101 | 6 | 0 |

## p184 A2

**Source transcription — header:** `Page heading 13th November 1918; A) 2 TL; RICHI-202`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
HIFUERUALLEFUERDIESIMHERHEITDE6GRUPPENOTIGENMASSREGLNNACHEIG?NEMERMASSENZUTR?FFENXOHLRM1ANR11???GEHOP
```

**Edited output — 6 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
HIFUERUALLEFUERDIESICHERHEITDERGRUPPENOTIGENMASSREGLNNACHEIGENEMERMESSENZUTREFFENXOHLRM1ANR11???GEHOP
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> HIFUERU. Alle fuer die Sicherheit der Gruppe NOTIGEN MASSREGLN nach eigenem Ermessen zu treffen. OHL RM1A NR11??? GEH OP.

**Meaning:** The surviving second part calls for taking the necessary measures for the security of the group according to one’s own discretion. The opening HIFUERU remains unexplained, and the particular group and reference number are not identified. This is an instruction fragment, not evidence that the measures were carried out.

**Editorial limits.**

- The printed second-part body has 202 valid source coordinates and matches its RICHI-202 header. High-resolution inspection confirms five glyphs in the last complete five-coordinate group FXVFA, followed by DG and a clear final G in DXGFG. No source erasure, insertion or deletion is introduced.
- The first part is not supplied. HIFUERU remains a literal unexplained opening, rather than being shortened or rewritten into a familiar introductory word.
- NOTIGEN and MASSREGLN are retained exactly; missing vowel letters in familiar spellings are not silently inserted.
- The proposal repairs SIMHERHEIT, DE6 to DER, EIG?NEM, ERMASSEN and ZUTR?FFEN at six observed-coordinate substitutions. The 6 in DE6 is a known label and its change is paid for. The two question marks in EIG?NEM and ZUTR?FFEN come from the fully observed unassigned AF square cell; proposing E at each position is separately paid for by coordinate changes, not by changing the key.
- The first and third unknowns in the final NR11??? field are the same fully observed GA square cell, at plaintext 93 and 95. The middle unknown is the distinct GD cell at 94. The two cells must receive different members of {2,3,4,7,8,9,Q,Y}; no assumption that the labels are digits is imposed.

## Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates independently reconstruct column positions and domains, compare them with the cipher implementation, replay every priced change, and check all readable nonseparator labels. Partial readings have one consistent injective square/source-mask completion witness that re-encrypts exactly; those witness choices are not historical identifications. Source images are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/group_security_measures_fragment/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to check the original PDF and exact source-crop pixels.
