# Wishing to travel home and uncertainty over Baltic transport

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Two native source bodies describe soldiers wishing to travel home without authorization and transport difficulty linked to uncertainty in the Baltic Sea. The second begins an incomplete statement about Graf Goltz. One damaged source glyph in that body is retained as unknown; its unchanged edited reading requires one explicit source-mask fill. The shared unknown GA cell remains globally coupled across their separate references. Missing context and abbreviated source spellings stay explicit.

## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p186 excerpt](../../experiments/home_departures_baltic_transport/sources/p186_reviewed.png) · [Damaged C1 glyph](../../experiments/home_departures_baltic_transport/sources/p186_C1_damaged_glyph.png) · [Exact inputs](../../experiments/home_departures_baltic_transport/inputs.json) · [Position-by-position certificates](../../experiments/home_departures_baltic_transport/certificates.json)

The unchanged published keys are `Nov13-15b`. The [earlier unreviewed candidates](../../experiments/home_departures_baltic_transport/prior_candidates.json) and [original OCR records](../../experiments/home_departures_baltic_transport/ocr_snapshot.json) are preserved. The present work supplies an image-reviewed source edition and a reproducible repair account; it does not claim that every body is a first public decipherment.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Coordinate substitutions | Source-mask fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [p186 B2](#p186-b2) | 242 | 120 / 121 | 0 | 0 |
| [p186 C1](#p186-c1) | 182 | 88 / 91 | 0 | 1 |

## p186 B2

**Source transcription — header:** `B) NKJ v LP (06.23 a.m., November 13th); FUER WAU 07.00 2 TLE; 2 TL RICHI-242`

**Readable German** — based on the unchanged raw output.

> Die Schwierigkeiten, dass Mannschaften eigenmaechtig nach Hause fahren wollen, sind ueberall die gleichen. OHL. RM 1A Nr. 11?01 Geh. Op.

**Meaning:** The second part states that the difficulty is the same everywhere: soldiers want to travel home on their own authority. It closes with OHL and an unresolved office reference. It reports the problem; it does not itself authorize those departures.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
DIESCHWIERIGKEITENXDASSMANNSCHAFTENEIGENMAECHTIGNACHHAUSEFAHRENWOLLENXSINDUEBERALLDIEGLEICHENXOHLXRMX1AXNRX11?01XGEHXOPXX
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- All 242 printed coordinates are preserved and decode without repairs. The earlier OCR separated the first row and omitted additional source material; those OCR defects are not historical ciphertext losses.
- The heading explicitly identifies this as part 2. The independently handled first part has two group-width obliterations and a conditional exclusion model; this native part does not rely on that model.
- The literal reference 11?01 retains one globally coupled unknown square cell. No historical file number or date is inferred.
- The unknown in 11?01 is the same GA square cell as the first unknown in p186 C1's DRTRM1A?5?; both must have the same unresolved label. The second unknown in that C1 field is AF and must have a different label.

## p186 C1

**Source transcription — header:** `C) KOW v LP (06.26 a.m., November 13th); 17.40 (13/11) 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-182; (Continued)`

**Readable German** — based on the edited output with one disclosed source-mask fill.

> Zu DRTRM1A?5?. ABTRSPRT z. Zt. wegen unklarer Lage in Ostsee UNMOGLCH. Gen. Graf Goltz hat jedoch VORBEREITG

**Meaning:** This first part concerns transport that is currently described as impossible because the situation in the Baltic Sea is unclear. It then begins a statement about preparations associated with the literal name and title GEN GRAF GOLTZ. The statement is incomplete in this source body, so no completed plan or action is supplied.

<details>
<summary>Raw and edited decoded text</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
ZUDRTRM1A?5?XABTRSPRTXZXZTWEGENUNKLARERLAGEINOSTSEEUNMOGLCHXG?NGRAFGOLTZHATJEDOCHVORBEREITG
```

**Edited output** — the E in `GEN` depends on the disclosed F interpretation of the damaged source glyph.

```text
ZUDRTRM1A?5?XABTRSPRTXZXZTWEGENUNKLARERLAGEINOSTSEEUNMOGLCHXGENGRAFGOLTZHATJEDOCHVORBEREITG
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- All 182 source slots are preserved. In the third cipher row, the first glyph of the seventh group has an F/R-like outline with an attached lower-right diagonal. The [original-PDF crop](../../experiments/home_departures_baltic_transport/sources/p186_C1_damaged_glyph.png) supports masking it as `?FAFF`, without assigning the competing literal letter R. At zero-based source index 110 it combines with source index 64 to give pair `X?` and plaintext position 61, whose domain is `234789CEGIQTY`.
- The edited E in `GEN` fills source index 110 with F. The main reading therefore has 88 fixed raw positions and 89 fixed edited positions out of 91, with no observed-coordinate substitutions and one source-mask fill. The certificate retains the former F interpretation as an explicit sensitivity assumption: 89 raw positions and no fill. It is excluded from observed-source totals; the change records uncertainty, not a repair-cost reduction or a new recovery.
- The scan labels two parts and prints “Continued,” but only this first body is included here. No missing continuation is reconstructed from context.
- DRTRM1A?5?, ABTRSPRT, UNMOGLCH and VORBEREITG are retained literally. The English meaning interprets the abbreviated transport statement; no missing I, vowel or grammatical ending is added to the decoded stream.
- The two question marks in the opening reference come from different unresolved square cells; their labels remain globally injective rather than being independently guessed.
- The literal name GRAF GOLTZ is not used to add a first name or identify a historical biography.

## Evidence and credit

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates replay every coordinate alteration, compare the independent column/domain reconstruction with the cipher implementation, and re-encrypt every complete edited output. For a partial output, an injective global completion of the square and residual source masks supplies an explicitly nonhistorical roundtrip witness. Each readable passage preserves every nonseparator output label; literal protected fields are also checked without removing their internal separators. Source crops are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and RGB-pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/home_departures_baltic_transport/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to regenerate and compare the delivered source pixels.

A roundtrip proves compatibility with a stated reading. Editorial spelling repairs remain proposals, and literal number labels are not automatically historical dates, quantities or reference numbers.

# Hungarian armistice negotiations: troop departure and instructions requested

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p124 A1/A2/A3, PDF p127, are one source-labeled three-part message:
`LP v NKJ (7.17 p.m., November 5th)`; `1715 (4/11) 3 TLE`.
The consecutive part labels and native lengths **352 / 266 / 48** establish
the assembly. All three use the unchanged published **Nov4–6** key.

## p124 A1

The [first-part crop](../../experiments/hungarian_armistice_instructions/sources/p124_A1.png)
contains **352 valid coordinates** and **176 / 176 fixed plaintext positions**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 352-coordinate frame:**

```text
ANOXHXLXOPXHEERESGRUPPEKOOVESHATWAFFENSTILLSTANDSVERHANDLUNGENFDERUNGARISCHETRUPPENEINGELEITETXDEUTSCHETRUPPENSOLLENSOBALDALSMOEGLICHPNGARISCHENUNDSUEDSLAVISC3ENBODENVERLASSEN0
```

**Edited output — three observed-coordinate substitutions, with no fills:**

```text
ANOXHXLXOPXHEERESGRUPPEKOOVESHATWAFFENSTILLSTANDSVERHANDLUNGENFUERUNGARISCHETRUPPENEINGELEITETXDEUTSCHETRUPPENSOLLENSOBALDALSMOEGLICHUNGARISCHENUNDSUEDSLAVISCHENBODENVERLASSEN0
```

</details>

The changes are source **80 G→A**, **110 F→V** and **306 X→V**. They
repair `FDER`, `PNGARISCHEN` and `SUEDSLAVISC3EN`. The name string
**KOOVES** and the final **0** are unchanged.

**Readable German — spacing, punctuation and umlauts; the literal closing 0 is retained:**

> An O. H. L. Op. Heeresgruppe KOOVES hat Waffenstillstandsverhandlungen
> für ungarische Truppen eingeleitet. Deutsche Truppen sollen sobald
> als möglich ungarischen und südslavischen Boden verlassen. 0.

The final 0 remains an uninterpreted label. The edition does not turn
KOOVES into an independently identified person's name. The message
reports negotiations and says German troops are to leave; it does not
show that the departure occurred.


**Cross-key phrase witness.** The unchanged [p117 C3 reading](nov3_withdrawal_and_night_report.md#p117-c3)
supplies the 59-letter phrase from `SOBALD` through `VERLASSEN` under the
separate Nov1–3 key. It independently supports A1's `UNGARISCHEN` and
`SUEDSLAVISCHEN` repairs: source **306 X→V** and **80 G→A** respectively.
The [paired-source certificate](../../experiments/hungarian_armistice_instructions/withdrawal_parallel.json)
records all 59 positions and the original coordinate pairs. The verb remains
`SOLLEN` here and `WERDEN` in p117; the headers also differ. This is a
parallel phrase, with no extra recovered position or physical message.
The separate `FDER`→`FUER` repair remains a word proposal.

## p124 A2

The [second-part crop](../../experiments/hungarian_armistice_instructions/sources/p124_A2.png)
contains **266 valid coordinates** and **133 / 133 fixed plaintext positions**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 266-coordinate frame:**

```text
AXOXKX11NSTBEAUFTRAGTXZWEIGENERLSTABSOFFIZIEREZUDENVERHANDLUNGENZUENTSENDENXWEISUNGENANAXJXKX11UNDHIER3ERFUERDIEVERHANDLUNGENERBETENX
```

**Edited output — three observed-coordinate substitutions, with no fills:**

```text
AXOXKX11ISTBEAUFTRAGTXZWEIGENERLSTABSOFFIZIEREZUDENVERHANDLUNGENZUENTSENDENXWEISUNGENANAXOXKX11UNDHIERHERFUERDIEVERHANDLUNGENERBETENX
```

</details>

The changes are source **16 X→V**, **88 D→G** and **106 G→A**. They
repair `11NST`, the second `A J K` sequence, and `HIER3ER`. The first
`A O K 11` and both occurrences of 11 remain as already decoded.

**Readable German — spacing, punctuation and one explicitly supplied spelling letter in brackets:**

> A. O. K. 11 ist beauftragt, zwei Gener[a]lstabsoffiziere zu den
> Verhandlungen zu entsenden. Weisungen an A. O. K. 11 und hierher für
> die Verhandlungen erbeten.

The source-derived string is **GENERLSTABSOFFIZIERE**, with no A between
R and L. The bracketed A appears only in the readable display. It is not
a recovered plaintext position, an insertion into the cipher, or part of
the repair count. The message reports an assignment and requests
instructions; it does not state that the officers had already arrived.

## p124 A3

The [third-part crop](../../experiments/hungarian_armistice_instructions/sources/p124_A3.png)
contains **48 valid coordinates** and **24 / 24 fixed plaintext positions**.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — native 48-coordinate frame:**

```text
OXKXMXROEMX1XAX11222XOPX
```

</details>

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation, with abbreviations unexpanded:**

> O. K. M. Röm. 1. A. 11222. Op.

## Conditional interpretation and source-defined OCR correction

Earlier OCR merged the second part with the first 40 coordinates of the
third part, introduced extra symbols into two groups, and omitted A3's
final **VDFFA FAA** row. The scan explicitly labels separate **2 TL**
and **3 TL** frames and supplies the eight omitted coordinates. The
[frozen OCR snapshot](../../experiments/hungarian_armistice_instructions/ocr_snapshot.json)
and [certificate](../../experiments/hungarian_armistice_instructions/certificates.json)
replay the exact correction: two OCR-only symbol deletions, two resolved
OCR masks, the part boundary after 266 coordinates, and the visible A3
final row. A1's separate masked F at source index 194 is also resolved
visually. The old shared OCR corpus is unchanged.

These transcript corrections are distinct from the six proposed changes
to visible historical coordinates. Across the three records, **666 valid
coordinates** give **333 / 333 fixed positions** in the source-defined
frames. All three edited streams re-encrypt exactly. There are **six
observed-coordinate substitutions, zero fills and no historical source
insertions, deletions or key changes**. A2's bracketed display letter
adds nothing to those counts. The damaged separate p124 B is excluded.

A1's body already appeared in an earlier unreviewed repository candidate;
the old A2/A3 OCR artifacts and published key credit are also preserved.
This source edition makes no historical first-solution claim. See the
[inputs](../../experiments/hungarian_armistice_instructions/inputs.json)
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/hungarian_armistice_instructions/README.md).

# Transports from Romania: warning against entry into Hungary

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** Childs printed p184 (PDF p187), 13 November 1918; published `Nov13-15a` key, unchanged. [Inputs](../../experiments/hungary_transport_warning/inputs.json), [exact certificates](../../experiments/hungary_transport_warning/certificates.json), [method and limits](../../experiments/hungary_transport_warning/README.md).

Two three-part transmissions address the Mackensen command's mineral-oil department and warn that transports from Romania should not be allowed into Hungary because they would be lost there. This is what the message says; the edition supplies no independent evidence that this outcome happened.

Both origin headers give LP for UKS, `13.40 (13/11)`, three parts. The different receipt headers give `02.51 a.m.` and `02.15 a.m.` on the same date, an unresolved chronological inconsistency. The addresses and bodies differ in length. They are compared by explicit shared passages, not treated as identical whole messages.

## p184 B1

[Source crop](../../experiments/hungary_transport_warning/sources/p184_B1.png). All 146 printed coordinates give 73 fixed positions without repair:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ANXOBERKOMMANDOXMACKENSENXWIRTSCHAFTSSTABXMINERALOELABTEILUNGXBUCKARESTXX
```

</details>

Reading: “An Oberkommando Mackensen, Wirtschaftsstab, Mineralölabteilung, Buckarest.” The received city spelling `BUCKAREST` is retained.

## p184 B2

[Source crop](../../experiments/hungary_transport_warning/sources/p184_B2.png). The source advertises 192 coordinates but prints 187. With five unknown coordinates inserted before source index 35, the 96-position raw text is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional five-coordinate gap before source index 35:**

```text
TRANSPOR?EXVONXRUM?ENIENXNIC?TXNACHXUNGARNXHEREINLASSENXDAXSIEXINXUNGARNXRESTLO?XVERLOREN?SINDXX
```

</details>

The corresponding C2 text independently determines the missing group `DXDVA`. No observed B2 coordinate changes:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — missing group supplied by the independently identified C2 witness:**

```text
TRANSPORTEXVONXRUMAENIENXNICHTXNACHXUNGARNXHEREINLASSENXDAXSIEXINXUNGARNXRESTLOSXVERLORENXSINDXX
```

</details>

Reading: “Transporte von Rumänien nicht nach Ungarn hereinlassen, da sie in Ungarn restlos verloren sind.” The gap is uniquely located among all 188 placements of one contiguous five-coordinate gap, using only 92 matching raw C2 positions. The certificate lists every gap score and the five individual witnesses. It does not assert uniqueness outside this recorded model.

## p184 B3

[Source crop](../../experiments/hungary_transport_warning/sources/p184_B3.png). All 110 coordinates are observed. The 55-position raw text retains 15 unknown reference positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
KRIEGSAMTXROEMX?X???STRICH????XKRAX???STRICH????XANCHXX
```

</details>

The office and reference syntax are readable; the number labels remain unassigned. No guessed reference number is supplied.

## p184 C1

[Source crop](../../experiments/hungary_transport_warning/sources/p184_C1.png). The shorter 136-coordinate address gives 68 fixed raw positions without repair:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ANXOBERKOMMANDOXMKENSENXWIRTSCHAFTSSTABXMINERALOLABTEILUNGXBUMARESTX
```

</details>

The received forms `MKENSEN`, `MINERALOL` and `BUMAREST` remain explicit. Their likely relation to B1's address is clear from the message context, but the edition does not invent missing ciphertext to make the addresses identical.

## p184 C2

[Source crop](../../experiments/hungary_transport_warning/sources/p184_C2.png). All 190 coordinates are observed. The 95-position raw text is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
TRANSTORTEXVONXRUMAENIENXNICHTXNACHXUNGARNXHE?REINLASSENXDAXSIEXINXUNGARNXRESTLOSVERLORENXTINDX
```

</details>

Two observed-coordinate substitutions, source index 75 `V → F` and index 86 `D → G`, yield:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
TRANSPORTEXVONXRUMAENIENXNICHTXNACHXUNGARNXHE?REINLASSENXDAXSIEXINXUNGARNXRESTLOSVERLORENXSINDX
```

</details>

Both corrected letters are witnessed by unchanged B2 positions that were excluded from the gap-selection mask. The extra position in `HE?REIN` remains unknown: plaintext index 45, pair `DX`, source indices 90 and 137, domain `0123456789QY`. The missing separator after `RESTLOS` and the shorter ending remain as received.

## p184 C3

[Source crop](../../experiments/hungary_transport_warning/sources/p184_C3.png); [enlargement of faint final-column groups](../../experiments/hungary_transport_warning/sources/p184_C3_faint.png). All 108 coordinates are retained:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
KRIEGSAMTXROEMX?X???STRICH????XKRAX???STRICH????XANCHX
```

</details>

Every one of these 54 positions has the same coordinate pair as the corresponding B3 position; B3 only adds a final X. All 15 unknown positions remain unknown in each copy. Exact pair agreement confirms the relationship and the preserved reference structure, but supplies no new digit assignment.

## Attribution and scope

Earlier unreviewed repository candidates already recognized much of the address, warning and footer. This edition adds source-checked coordinates and boundaries, an exact missing-group reconstruction, and explicit costed ordinary-word corrections. No claim of first historical decipherment is made. All fixed letters remain labels under the published key, and all unknown domains are available in the certificate.

# A Jaeger division's accommodation area near Huy

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This message reports an accommodation area for a German Jaeger division near Huy. A prewar illustrated guide supplies the spelling **Vierset-Barse**, supporting one correction in its place list. The complete source body matches its advertised 230 slots, with no change to its frame.

## Vierset-Barse in the accommodation list

The received `VIERSWT X BARSE` is proposed as **VIERSET X BARSE**. A plate in
*Huy-pittoresque*, dated about 1885–1890 by the Rijksmuseum, prints the caption
**CHATEAU DE VIERSET-BARSE**. The two fields can therefore be read together as
the place-name **Vierset-Barse**. The intervening X remains the transmitted
separator; the hyphen belongs to the readable display.

The correction costs **one additional observed substitution**, source **170 D→X**.
It changes plaintext position 88 from W to E (`VD→VX`) and leaves the other
114 labels untouched. Including the earlier JAEGER repair and two dash fills,
this place-name layer costs **two substitutions and two source-mask fills**.
It adds no fixed positions: the corrected letter was already a known W.

**Readable German — place-name correction, with the published partial square:**

> An AOK 1?. Zu dort 11140 OP. Unterbringungsraum DT JAEGER DIV 13?11: MARCHE, SUEDL HUY, VIERSET-BARSE, SOHEIT. AOK 1? 1 AM.

<details>
<summary>Exact place-name proposal</summary>

**Edited output — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions and 2 source-mask fills:**

```text
ANXAOKX1?XZUXDORTX11140XOPXUNTERBRINGUNGSRAUMXDTXJAEGERXDIVX13?11XMARCHEXSUEDLXHUYXVIERSETXBARSEXSOHEITXAOKX1?X1XAM
```

</details>

The [source plate and exact check](../../experiments/p183_vierset_place/README.md)
support this spelling independently of the conditional numeral interpretation
below. MARCHE, SOHEIT and the intermediate reference remain unchanged.

## Conditional shared digits

The accommodation report gains **AOK 17** at the opening and **AOK 18** at the close, reaching **115/115 labels** under the shared interpretation. The intermediate field becomes the literal **13711**. Its 7 is coupled to AOK 17 and is not replaced by a separator. The earlier JAEGER repair and two source-mask fills are retained. The [joint reconstruction](../../experiments/nov10_joint_completion/README.md) combines the earlier Marineamt and formation interpretations with the army-number constraint and the mobilization decree; the reversed 7/9 assignment is retained there.

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the joint square:**

> An AOK 17. Zu dort 11140 OP. Unterbringungsraum DT JAEGER DIV 13711: MARCHE, SUEDL HUY, VIERSWT, BARSE, SOHEIT. AOK 18 1 AM.

<details>
<summary>Exact conditional labels</summary>

**Edited output — p183_F, conditional shared square; 115/115 fixed positions:**

```text
ANXAOKX17XZUXDORTX11140XOPXUNTERBRINGUNGSRAUMXDTXJAEGERXDIVX13711XMARCHEXSUEDLXHUYXVIERSWTXBARSEXSOHEITXAOKX18X1XAM
```

</details>


## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p183 excerpt](../../experiments/jaeger_accommodation_area/sources/p183_reviewed.png) · [Inputs](../../experiments/jaeger_accommodation_area/inputs.json) · [Position and change certificates](../../experiments/jaeger_accommodation_area/certificates.json)

The published `Nov10-12` key is unchanged. [Original OCR records](../../experiments/jaeger_accommodation_area/ocr_snapshot.json) and [reproducible comparisons with that earlier evidence](../../experiments/jaeger_accommodation_area/prior_candidates.json) are preserved separately. The present edition supplies checked source framing, exact costs and readable passages; it makes no first-public-decipherment claim.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [p183 F](#p183-f) | 230 | 110 / 115 | 1 | 2 |

## p183 F

**Source transcription — header:** `F) -- v -- (14.05 p.m., November 12th); 12.10; RICHI-230`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
ANXAOKX1?XZUXDORTX11140XOPXUNTERBRINGUNGSRAUMXDTXJAEGE1XDIVX13?11XMARC?EXSUEDL?HUYXVIERSWTXBARSEXSOHEITXAOKX1?X1XAM
```

**Edited output — 1 observed-coordinate substitution and 2 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
ANXAOKX1?XZUXDORTX11140XOPXUNTERBRINGUNGSRAUMXDTXJAEGERXDIVX13?11XMARCHEXSUEDLXHUYXVIERSWTXBARSEXSOHEITXAOKX1?X1XAM
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> An AOK 1?. Zu dort 11140 OP. Unterbringungsraum DT JAEGER DIV 13?11: MARCHE, SUEDL HUY, VIERSWT, BARSE, SOHEIT. AOK 1? 1 AM.

**Meaning of this earlier layer:** The message reports an accommodation area for a German Jaeger division, followed by a partially unresolved label and a list of place-like fields. SUEDL HUY means south of Huy. This layer preserves VIERSWT, BARSE and the three unresolved numeral positions; the place-name correction and shared digits are presented separately above.

**Editorial limits.**

- The native body has all 230 printed slots, including two printed dashes in XF--F. No source coordinate is inserted, excluded or reordered.
- The single observed-coordinate proposal JAEGE1 to JAEGER is priced. The two dash fills propose MARC?E to MARCHE and SUEDL?HUY to SUEDLXHUY. These supply readable words and a separator without changing the key.
- VIERSWT and SOHEIT remain literal in this earlier layer. The Vierset proposal above carries its additional substitution explicitly.
- The unknown at plaintext index 8 in the opening AOK1? and at 62 in 13?11 comes from the same fully observed GF square cell. Those two occurrences must take the same digit from {5,6,7,8,9}.
- The final AOK1? unknown at plaintext index 109 is a different fully observed XG square cell and must take a different member of {5,6,7,8,9}. No choice is made merely to make the two AOK labels agree.
- The header retains the literal 14.05 p.m. and 12.10. Neither is used to resolve the date-like or reference labels inside the body.

## Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates independently reconstruct column positions and domains, compare them with the cipher implementation, replay every priced change, and check all readable nonseparator labels. Partial readings have one consistent injective square/source-mask completion witness that re-encrypts exactly; those witness choices are not historical identifications. Source images are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/jaeger_accommodation_area/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to check the original PDF and exact source-crop pixels.

# Kiew morning report and pioneer-park loading request

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

These are two separate messages on Childs p110, both marked NKJ v LP and
forwarded for UKS on November 3. They are not assembled into one telegram.
Both use the unchanged published Nov1–3 square and ranks.

## Morning report

### p110 B

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
OXKXMACKENSENXXMORGENMELDU?GXVX3X11X18XNICHTSN?UESXXHRGXKIEWXROMX1AX6915X18
```

**Edited output:**

```text
OXKXMACKENSENXXMORGENMELDUNGXVX3X11X18XNICHTSNEUESXXHRGXKIEWXROMX1AX6915X18
```

</details>

Cost: **0 observed-coordinate substitutions** and **2 source-mask fills**. Source length and transposition are unchanged.

The message addresses Mackensen and reports `NICHTS NEUES`—nothing new—in
the morning report of `3X11X18`. The Kiew/office/reference ending remains
literal. Two printed glyphs at source indices 67 and 104 are C-shaped;
they are preserved as C in the diplomatic transcript and treated as masks
in the arithmetic. Filling the two word positions gives `MORGENMELDUNG`
and `NICHTSNEUES` without changing an observed coordinate. Independent enlarged-glyph review identifies source 62 as G in `VAGGF`;
its coordinate pair directly supplies the final reference digit5. The raw
reference `6915` is preserved as a published-square label sequence, without
a new historical numerical assignment. [The independent glyph audit](../../experiments/nov3_radio_and_pioneer/source_glyph_audit.json) retains the rejected preliminary C reading and the comparison crops.

## Pioneer-park request

### p110 C

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ANDENSTABSOFFIZIERDERPIONIEREDESXAXOXKXSCHOLTVXXPIONPARKKAMPX13XFIEGTBEI26X10INXPETREXVERLADEBEREITERBITTEPARKNUM2ERDES1AGGONGESTELLUNGVERANLASSETDASONSTJINFORTKOMMENUNMOEGLICHXXBAYXPIONXPARKXKOMPX13
```

**Edited output:**

```text
ANDENSTABSOFFIZIERDERPIONIEREDESXAXOXKXSCHOLTZXXPIONPARKKOMPX13XLIEGTBEI26X10INXPETREXVERLADEBEREITERBITTEPARKNUMMERDESWAGGONGESTELLUNGVERANLASSENDASONSTEINFORTKOMMENUNMOEGLICHXXBAYXPIONXPARKXKOMPX13
```

</details>

Cost: **8 observed-coordinate substitutions** and **0 source-mask fills**. Source length and transposition are unchanged.

The request addresses the staff officer of pioneers of Army Command Scholtz.
It says that a pioneer-park company is ready for loading at the literal
place field `PETRE` and requests wagon provision, without which onward
movement is impossible. These are readings of the message, not confirmation
that the shipment occurred or a new identification of the place.

Seven equal-length word/name repairs cost eight observed-coordinate changes:
`SCHOLTV`→`SCHOLTZ`, `PARKKAMP`→`PARKKOMP`, `FIEGT`→`LIEGT`,
`NUM2ER`→`NUMMER`, `1AGGON`→`WAGGON`, `VERANLASSET`→`VERANLASSEN`,
and `SONSTJIN`→`SONSTEIN`. The two numerical-looking symbols repaired inside
words are local edits; they do not relabel those square cells elsewhere.

The awkward `BEI26X10`, `ERBITTEPARKNUMMERDES` and the unit labels `13`
are retained. A precise intended date or a smoother grammatical sentence
is not imposed. The source has exactly **398 coordinates**. Earlier OCR
had 399 because it inserted a spurious V at source boundary 277 and also
masked two visible letters. Restoring the literal source frame is not an
original-message deletion or an erasure fill.

## Notation and evidence

The fixed-width strings preserve every plaintext position. `?` means one
unresolved position, `X` is a literal decoded symbol that may serve as a
separator, and digits retain the published square's labels. Word spacing,
calendar values and numerical identities are not silently inferred. A source
mask fill is separate from a change to an observed ADFGVX coordinate.

[Source rows and image metadata](../../experiments/nov3_radio_and_pioneer/inputs.json),
[coordinate and domain certificate](../../experiments/nov3_radio_and_pioneer/certificates.json),
and [method, prior credit and reproduction](../../experiments/nov3_radio_and_pioneer/README.md).

# Rail stoppage, motor columns and aviation replenishment

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and recovery: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Three telegrams on Childs's printed p229 concern transport during the final
withdrawal period: halted railway traffic, a request for motor-transport
columns, and an aviation unit's destination and replenishment. Their six
physical parts provide **721 plaintext positions** under the unchanged
published Nov28–Dec1 key. The separate editorial readings require **14
observed-coordinate substitutions and 39 erasure fills**, leaving five
plaintext positions unresolved. The shared calendar and unit interpretation
now supplies **30 November**, formations **219/217**, and **seven motor columns**
in the passages below.

The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
[printed p229, PDF p232](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view),
under `30th NOVEMBER, 1918.`. The page's parenthetical receiving times are
in December: **A, 04.59 p.m. on December 1; B, 01.50 a.m. on December 1;
C, 01.15 a.m. on December 1**. These differ from several earlier OCR header
guesses. The photographed callsign has two small marks over `ZON`; searchable
metadata uses `ZON` without making a new callsign identification.

## A: the evening report and halted railway transports

The [three-part source](../../experiments/late_transport_dispatches/sources/p229_A.png)
has the header `HP v ZON; 1930 (30/11) FUR OKM 3 TEILE` and exact part lengths
228, 192 and 176. The raw body was already recognizable in an earlier
unreviewed OCR-derived computation. The present work verifies every source
slot and records the limited word repairs explicitly.

**Conditional interpretation — readable German with the shared calendar and unit assignments:**

> Abendmeldg. v. 30.11. 6. R. D. ist mit Anfang bis Tiszafoeldvar aufgerueckt.
> Unterbringungsraum der 219. u. 217. I. D. unveraendert. Seit 29.11. abends
> sind alle Transporte auf Strecke Arad, Szolnok auf Weisung der ung. Z. T. L.
> angehalten worden. Die fuer heute beabsichtigten Verladungen haben daher
> bisher nicht stattgefunden. A. O. K. 11. 1. A.

The 6th Reserve Division's leading element has reached Tiszafoeldvar;
the accommodation areas of the 219th and 217th divisions are unchanged.
Railway transports on the Arad–Szolnok route have been stopped since the
evening of 29 November, preventing the planned loadings.

The [joint interpretation](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/README.md)
uses the valid November date `3?/11` to fix **GA=0** and the independently
documented 217th Division and 7th Bavarian cavalry brigade to support **VG=7**.
Part A1 reaches **114/114 interpreted positions** with its existing one-coordinate
word repair. Barkóczy-Klopsch's account also places the transport-stop decision
on 29 November; it corroborates the earlier assignment of the final digit in
`29/11`. The abbreviation `Z T L` remains unexpanded.

### Earlier source edition

Part A1, after the one-coordinate `M3T→MIT` repair:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ABENDMELDGYVY26YXXYY8YRYDYISTMITANFANGBISTISZAFOELDVARAUFGERUECKTYUNTERBRINGUNGSRAUMDERJX5YUYJX0YIYDYUNVERAENDERTY
```

</details>

The literal `26`, `8`, `JX5` and `JX0` in this earlier display are
published-key labels. Their conditional numerical interpretation appears above.

Part A2, with one substitution proposing `SWOLNOK→SZOLNOK` and the printed
dash filled to give `ANGEHALTEN`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
SEITJ5YXXYABENDSSINDALLETRANSPORTEAUFSTRECKEARADSZOLNOKAUFWEISUNGDERUNGYZYTYLYANGEHALTENWORDENYY
```

</details>

The unchanged-key display retains the date-like field `J5YXX`.

Part A3, with two substitutions restoring `NICHT` and `GEFUNDEN`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
DIEFUERHEUTEBEABSICHTIGTENVERLADUNGENHABENDAHERBISHERNICHTSTATTGEFUNDENYYAYOYKYXXYXYAYYY
```

</details>

As a consequence, the loadings intended for that day have not yet taken place.
The three parts form a continuous operational report. No missing part,
coordinate insertion or reordering is needed.

## B: how many motor columns can the army release?

The [two-part source](../../experiments/late_transport_dispatches/sources/p229_B.png)
has `ZON v BSL; NR 153 1900 (30/11) 2 TLE`, with exact lengths 268 and 248.
In B1, two previously uncertain words are filled from printed dashes, and
one observed coordinate repairs the office abbreviation `OH4→OHL`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
AOKXXYOKMHATBEIOHL0KRAFTWAGENKOLONNENBEANTRAGTOHLDRAHTETMIRRMX?X63282ESWIRDGEBETENMITXXARMEEUNMITTELBARINVERBINDUNGZUTRETENOBVONDIESER
```

</details>

OKM has requested motor columns from OHL. OHL asks the sender to contact
the army directly to establish whether further columns can be made available.
The shared interpretation reads the requested quantity as **seven** and the
army as the **11th Army**. The source edition above retains the baseline
labels `0`, `XX` and the damaged reference `RMX?X63282`.

B2 continues the question, after six substitutions and five erasure fills:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
NOCHWEITEREAKKSABGEGEBENWERDENKOENNENYTELRAMMSCHLUSSUMMITTEILUNGWIRDGEBETENWIEVIELKONNENABGEGEBENWERDENKOENNENYOKMRMXCX0?40Y
```

</details>

The body asks how many additional `AKKS` can be released. That abbreviation
is retained, as are the shortened **`TELRAMM`** and six-character **`KONNEN`**.
The edition does not silently add letters to make `TELEGRAMM` or a second
`KOENNEN`. The closing `OKM` is an explicitly priced office-label repair;
its context is supported by the unchanged `OKM` in B1. The final numerical
reference remains `0?40` in baseline labels.

The same two new square assignments supply four numeral positions across
B1 and B2. They add no source edits:

| Field | Published-key labels | Joint interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| B1: requested motor columns | `0` | **7** |
| B1: OHL reference | `RMX?X63282` | `RM1?10?363` |
| B2: closing reference | `0?40` | **7?87** |

B1 has **132/134** and B2 **123/124** positions fixed in this interpretation;
their remaining reference characters stay unresolved.

Visual retranscription also resolves two earlier OCR erasures without changing
the source: B1 source index 195 is the first `F` of `FFGFD`, and B2 index 161
is the `F` of `GFDGG`. These source readings are distinct from editorial
coordinate substitutions.

## C: an aviation unit and a park at Craiova

**Readable German — conditional shared-square interpretation, with one additional separator fill:**

> Kofl 11. Wo bleibt Fliegerabtl. 38. Marschziel ist Craiova, da hier eigener Park errichtet wird. Bitte nach HK? versetzte Fliegerverbaende bestimmungsgemaess auffuellen. Kofl Mack. ??18OP.

The message asks for the flight detachment's whereabouts, sets **Craiova**
as its march destination, and requests that the transferred aviation units
be brought up to their prescribed strength. The shared late-November square
reads the existing unit labels as **Kofl 11** and **Fliegerabtl. 38**.
The boundary `WIRD?BITTE` admits separator `X`: filling one printed mask,
source position 277, with `A` gives the pair `AX`. The revised edition has
**3 observed-coordinate substitutions and 32 mask fills**; its conditional
interpretation fixes **162/165** plaintext positions.

`HK?` remains incomplete. The closing `??18OP` contains a source erasure
followed by the still-interchangeable **4/5** square cell. The
[additional-traffic certificate](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/traffic_certificate.json)
checks the quote and both surviving squares.

The [aviation source](../../experiments/late_transport_dispatches/sources/p229_C.png)
has `ZON v BSL; NO 151 2100 (11/30)` and `RICHI-330`. Its **330 actual slots**
include **33 printed dashes** and a **Q-shaped glyph**, transcribed `Q` and
conservatively masked, at source index 154. A
[close view](../../experiments/late_transport_dispatches/sources/p229_C_glyph.png)
preserves that decision for review. The earlier unreviewed OCR candidate
stream contained only 323 slots.
Reading the omitted printed slots from the image restores the actual frame;
it is not a seven-coordinate insertion into the historical ciphertext.

The resulting direct reading under the published Nov28–Dec1 key is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
K?FLXXYYW?BLEIBTF?IEGER???LY24Y?A?SCHZIEL?STC?0IO?ADA?IER?IGE?ERP?RKE?RIC?TET?IR??BIT?ENA??HK?VER?ETZ?EFLIEGE?VERBAEN?EBESTIM?UNGSGEM?ESSAUFF??LLENYK?FLMACKY?3X4OPYY
```

</details>

Three observed-coordinate substitutions and 31 erasure fills support this
separate conditional edition:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — conditional partial-source reconstruction with the stated erasure fills:**

```text
KOFLXXYYWOBLEIBTFLIEGERABTLY24YMARSCHZIELISTCRAIOVADAHIEREIGENERPARKERRICHTETWIRD?BITTENACHHK?VERSETZTEFLIEGERVERBAENDEBESTIMMUNGSGEMAESSAUFFUELLENYKOFLMACKY?3X4OPYY
```

</details>

`FLIEGERABTL` and the damaged ordinary words are editorial restorations;
the complete repair ledger is retained. No second reception independently
supplies the restored wording.

The earlier published-key edition leaves three source positions unresolved:

| Position | Context | Baseline-key domain | Treatment |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 81 | `WIRD?BITTE` | `39WXYZ` | The new conditional edition fills the separator; the earlier stream is retained above |
| 93 | `NACHHK?VERSETZTE` | `BCKMSW` | Destination left as `HK?`; no silent repair to `OKM` |
| 157 | `MACKY?3X4OPYY` | `278GPY` | Closing reference remains incomplete |

The baseline unit label `24`, army label `XX` and raw `Y` separators remain
in the recorded stream. Their interpretation in the opening quote follows
the [shared date and unit analysis](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/README.md);
this telegram supplies no independent identification of the detachment.

## Source accounting and reproducibility

The table records the earlier published-key editions; the additional C
separator raises that edition to **163/165** labels and **32** mask fills.
The shared interpretation above has a further unresolved 4/5 cell.

| Part | Slots | Printed dashes / invalid glyphs | Raw fixed labels | Edition fixed labels | Known-coordinate changes | Erasure fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A1 | 228 | 0 / 0 | 114 / 114 | 114 / 114 | 1 | 0 |
| A2 | 192 | 1 / 0 | 95 / 96 | 96 / 96 | 1 | 1 |
| A3 | 176 | 0 / 0 | 88 / 88 | 88 / 88 | 2 | 0 |
| B1 | 268 | 3 / 0 | 131 / 134 | 133 / 134 | 1 | 2 |
| B2 | 248 | 6 / 0 | 118 / 124 | 123 / 124 | 6 | 5 |
| C | 330 | 33 / 1 | 131 / 165 | 162 / 165 | 3 | 31 |
| **Total** | **1,442** | **43 / 1** | **677 / 721** | **716 / 721** | **14** | **39** |

There are no source-coordinate insertions, deletions, block moves or key
changes. Fixed-label totals do not authenticate historical numerals. The
[inputs](../../experiments/late_transport_dispatches/inputs.json) preserve
manual rows, full render metadata, protected fields and separate recipes;
the [certificate](../../experiments/late_transport_dispatches/certificates.json)
lists every change, its source and plaintext position, all numeral/`J/Q/Y`
occurrences, and global round-trip witnesses. Arbitrary witnesses certify
consistency, not original wording.

The published key is credited to **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**, [2016, DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461).
Earlier unreviewed A/B candidates are retained in the package, including
their use in the frozen p73 retrieval corpus. No explicit p229 body was
located in the bounded author-paper, supplementary-reading and catalog
check; this does not establish universal decipherment priority.

```sh
python experiments/late_transport_dispatches/verify.py --verify
```

With the pinned source PDF, the optional `--pdf` argument also regenerates
and compares the delivered crop pixels.

# Reports requested from General von Liman

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This two-part telegram requests regular information about troops near
Constantinople and Haidarpascha: their return transport, strength, condition
and special requirements. It also requests acknowledgment. Almost the whole
ordinary-language body is readable directly from the received coordinates.

The later [Article XII numeral interpretation](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/README.md)
reads the closing field as `OHLXROEMX1AX11??2XGEHXOPXX`, with four newly
interpreted numeral positions and no added source change. The two middle
digits of the reference remain unassigned. The ordinary-word `JEDE`
reading has its own earlier [letter constraint](../../experiments/nov25_letter_constraint/README.md).

The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
[printed p222, PDF p225](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [preserved source image](../../experiments/liman_troop_reports/sources/childs_p222_A.png)
shows the heading `26th NOVEMBER, 1918.`, followed by:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) XY v LP (02.56 a.m., December 18th, G.H.Q.American E.F.)
0900 (26/11) 2 TEILE
```

</details>

The November heading and origin date and the December reception-line date
are all retained. The edition does not resolve that chronological distinction.

## A1: the requested reports

The first part has exactly 214 valid coordinates, matching `RICHI-214`.
Under the unchanged published `Nov25-28` square and ranks, its direct
107-position reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
GENERALVONLIMANXXBITTEREGELMAESSIG9EDEWOCHEABTRANSPORTESTAERKEUNDZUSTANDDERBEIKONSTANTINOPELUNDHAIDARPASCHA
```

</details>

There is **no source repair** in this part. In ordinary words, it addresses
General von Liman and asks for regular reports on troop transport, strength
and condition at the two named places. Reading `9EDE WOCHE` as *jede Woche*
(every week) is a separate lexical interpretation.

The raw `9` is at plaintext index 34, coordinate pair `VD`, supplied by
received indices 114 and 189. The source-certified p224 C1 personnel order
also has `MA9OR` at this same square cell; see the
[separate staff-transfer edition](../people/breslau_staff_transfer.md). These two
lexical contexts suggest an intended `J`, but this edition retains the
published labels. Simply replacing `9` by `J` in the complete square would
duplicate its existing `J`; a full historical interpretation must also
account for the old `J` cell and the remaining labels.

## A2: special requirements and acknowledgment

The second part has exactly 200 valid coordinates, matching `RICHI-200`.
Its direct reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
BEFINDLICHENTRUPPENUNDBESOXDEREWUENSCHEMELDENXXBITTEEMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNGXXOHLXROEMXJAXJJ201XGEHXOPXX
```

</details>

One observed-coordinate substitution gives:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
BEFINDLICHENTRUPPENUNDBESONDEREWUENSCHEMELDENXXBITTEEMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNGXXOHLXROEMXJAXJJ201XGEHXOPXX
```

</details>

The change is received index **132**, printed group **27**, coordinate **3**:
`V` to `A`. It replaces the `X` in `BESOXDERE` with `N`. The text then asks
for reports about the troops present and any special requirements, followed
by a request to acknowledge receipt. The footer `OHL ROEM JA JJ201 GEH OP`
retains every raw label; no order number or numeral interpretation is supplied.

## Evidence, scope and credit

| Quantity | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| Physical source parts | 2 |
| Received valid coordinates | 414 |
| Raw positions fixed as published-square labels | 207 / 207 |
| Observed-coordinate substitutions | 1 |
| Erasure fills, insertions, deletions or block moves | 0 |
| Changes to the published square | 0 |

The [inputs](../../experiments/liman_troop_reports/inputs.json) retain the manual
rows, exact header and image hash. The
[certificate](../../experiments/liman_troop_reports/certificates.json) records
all source-position pairs, the one repair and every untouched numeral or
`J/Q/Y` field. Both raw readings and both edition readings reencrypt exactly.
The numerical count of fixed labels does not certify the original values
of unresolved numeral or rare-letter labels.

The period key is credited to **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**, [2016, DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461).
Both bodies already existed as unreviewed OCR-derived candidates; A2 is
also in the frozen p73 retrieval corpus. No explicit p222/Liman body example
was located in the bounded author-paper, supplementary-reading and catalog
check. This source edition makes no universal first-decipherment claim.

```sh
python experiments/liman_troop_reports/verify.py --verify
```

# Mackensen's appeal over disarmament and internment

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Prior body identification:** Childs; summarized by George Lasry, Ingo
Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016). **Source edition and exact repair
audit:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

This six-part message reports Berthelot's communication of Foch's refusal
to apply the Western armistice conditions to the German southeastern front,
and a demand for disarmament and internment of Mackensen's army group.
The proposed German edition distinguishes acknowledging receipt while a
decision is pending, disarmament by Hungary, and a request to forgo
internment. Its fifth part is a conditional reconstruction of a genuinely
short source frame. The closing warns of mass flight, misery and open
resistance.

The [conditional Article XII numeral interpretation](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/README.md)
clarifies four positions in the closing reference: raw `JAJJ6J4` becomes
`1A11?1?`. It adds no source change. The earlier repairs of raw
`MITGETEILJ` and `SOLLJE` remain necessary; those received `J` labels would
otherwise become 1 under the same assignment.

The source is [Childs's collection](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view),
printed **p220 C1–C4 and p221 A5–A6**, PDF pages 223–224. The repeated header
links the six parts:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
NKJ v UKS (05.24 p.m., November 25th)
1620 (11/25) KR MIM 6 TLE
FUR LP
```

</details>

Both pages are headed 25 November 1918. The scan's `1620` differs from the
`16:30` time in the earlier research-paper summary; the source time is
preserved without resolving that difference. The published `Nov25-28`
square and transposition are unchanged.

## p220 C1: Berthelot's notification

All **222** printed slots are retained. The `C` in `ADCAV` is outside the
coordinate alphabet. The literal-source reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
OHLOPXXKMXXVOLKSREGXBERLI7XXGENXBERTHELOTHATMITGETEILJKDASSGENXFOCHANWENDUNGDERWESTWAFFEN?TILLSTANDSBEDINGUNGEN
```

</details>

Four observed-coordinate substitutions and one invalid-glyph fill give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
OHLOPXXKMXXVOLKSREGXBERLINXXGENXBERTHELOTHATMITGETEILTXDASSGENXFOCHANWENDUNGDERWESTWAFFENSTILLSTANDSBEDINGUNGEN
```

</details>

With editorial spacing: “OHL, Op. KM. Volksreg. Berlin. Gen. Berthelot hat
mitgeteilt, dass Gen. Foch Anwendung der Westwaffenstillstandsbedingungen …”
The `7` and `J` repaired inside ordinary words remain visible in the raw
layer and the complete numeral/rare-letter inventory.

## p220 C2: southeastern front and pending decision

The source contains exactly **264 valid coordinates**. Its raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FUERDEUTSCHESUEDOSTFRONTABLEHNTUNDENTWAFFNUNGUNDINTERNIERUNGHGRMAPKENSENFORDERTXOKMWIRDIMPFANGDERNOTEBISZUMEINTREFFENDERENTSCHEIDUNG
```

</details>

Two observed-coordinate substitutions repair `MAPKENSEN` and `IMPFANG`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
FUERDEUTSCHESUEDOSTFRONTABLEHNTUNDENTWAFFNUNGUNDINTERNIERUNGHGRMACKENSENFORDERTXOKMWIRDEMPFANGDERNOTEBISZUMEINTREFFENDERENTSCHEIDUNG
```

</details>

This continues: “… für deutsche Südostfront ablehnt und Entwaffnung und
Internierung Hgr. Mackensen fordert. OKM wird Empfang der Note bis zum
Eintreffen der Entscheidung …”

## p220 C3: limited acknowledgment and conditional proposal

The page prints **206 valid coordinates**. Earlier OCR omitted the complete
final `DDADF D`, producing an incorrect 200-coordinate frame. Restoring
those six observed coordinates gives:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
OHLXLEDIGLICHBESTAETIGENXSOLLJEALLGEMXLAGEERFUELLUNGFRANZXFORDERUNGVERLANGEBXMUESSTEERREICHTWERDENKDASU
```

</details>

Five observed-coordinate substitutions give the same-length candidate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
OHLXLEDIGLICHBESTAETIGENXSOLLTEALLGEMXLAGEERFUELLUNGFRANZXFORDERUNGVERLANGENXMUESSTEERREICHTWERDENXDASS
```

</details>

With editorial spacing: “… OHL lediglich bestätigen. Sollte allgem. Lage
Erfüllung franz. Forderung verlangen, müsste erreicht werden, dass …”
In particular, `SOLLJE` becomes `SOLLTE`; an extra letter is not added to
turn it into `SOLL DIE`.

Parts C2–C3 support **merely acknowledging receipt pending OHL's decision**.
That limited acknowledgment is distinct from accepting the demands. The
earlier paper paraphrases the timing differently; this edition presents
the German wording and its costs so the distinction can be assessed.

## p220 C4: Hungary and the internment clause

The source contains **244 valid coordinates**. Its final `XGGG` was omitted
by earlier OCR. With that observed group restored, the raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ENTWAFFNUNGDURCHINGARNXNICHTDURCHENTENTEERFOLTUXDVONWNTERNI9RUNGXDIEAUCHAUIVERPFLEGUNGSGRUENDENHOECHSTENSINUNGARNMOEGLICHX
```

</details>

Five observed-coordinate substitutions give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ENTWAFFNUNGDURCHUNGARNXNICHTDURCHENTENTEERFOLTUNDVONINTERNIERUNGXDIEAUCHAUSVERPFLEGUNGSGRUENDENHOECHSTENSINUNGARNMOEGLICHX
```

</details>

The clause asks for disarmament by Hungary, rather than the Entente, and
continues into the next part's internment proposal. The apparent omission
in `ERFOLT` is retained: no `G` is inserted into this complete source frame.
Changing `UXD` to `UND` has its own explicit coordinate cost.

The raw `9` inside `WNTERNI9RUNG` is an unchanged-source `VD` pair; its
ordinary-word repair to `E` is separately recorded. It is not evidence that
every `VD` means `E`, and remains an inconvenient example when considering
the separate conditional `VD=J` interpretation.

## p221 A5: conditional missing-prefix reconstruction

The source advertises **232** coordinates but actually prints **222 slots**,
including three dashes. This discrepancy is present in the scan. Under
the representative model of ten absent coordinates at the beginning, the
raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 232-slot frame with ten absent leading coordinates:**

```text
ABS?AN0GE?OMME?WIRDKINTERN?ERUNGWUERD?NACH5EMSOEB?NKAR?ATHTN?NTERGROESST?NANSTRENGU?GENUEBERSCH?ITTENUNDAB?U?NSPORTE
```

</details>

Six observed-coordinate substitutions, three printed-dash fills and ten
inserted-coordinate fills give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional leading-gap frame, with the stated repairs and fills:**

```text
ABSTANDGENOMMENWIRDXINTERNIERUNGWUERDENACHDEMSOEBENKARPATHENUNTERGROESSTENANSTRENGUNGENUEBERSCHRITTENUNDABTRANSPORTE
```

</details>

With editorial spacing: “… Abstand genommen wird. Internierung würde,
nachdem soeben Karpathen unter grössten Anstrengungen überschritten und
Abtransporte …” The received formulation has no article before `Karpathen`;
none is inserted.

Read with C4, the stated candidate asks that internment be **forgone**,
while its intervening clause says that provisioning would make Hungary
the only feasible location. The wording is more specific than a summary
that merely proposes internment in Hungary. This interpretation inherits
the explicit missing-prefix and ordinary-word assumptions; the absent
coordinates are not independently witnessed by another transmission.

### All declared loss placements are retained

The audit checks all **223** placements of one ten-coordinate gap and all
**24,976** ordered placements of two five-coordinate gaps. The complete
retrospective candidate has a unique minimum of six observed-coordinate
changes when both missing groups precede source index 0.

That is not independent proof of the location. Masking `ABSTANDGENOMMENWIRD`,
`INTERNIERUNG` and `KARPATHEN` leaves five two-group minima, each with four
changes on the remaining template: **(0,0), (1,1), (1,2), (2,2), (3,3)**.
All are preserved. Their raw readings share **100 of 116 fixed positions**.
The book and radio scores also rank the leading gap first, but language
ranking is used only to find a candidate. Other loss mechanisms and an
incorrect length indicator are not excluded by these bounded comparisons.

## p221 A6: the warning and signature

All **194 source coordinates** are valid. The raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
EINGELEITETZUMASSENF8UC0TMITUNSAEGLICHEMELENDUNDZUOFFENERAUFLEHNUNGFUEHRENXFELDMXMACKENSENJAJJ6J4
```

</details>

Two observed-coordinate substitutions give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
EINGELEITETZUMASSENFLUCHTMITUNSAEGLICHEMELENDUNDZUOFFENERAUFLEHNUNGFUEHRENXFELDMXMACKENSENJAJJ6J4
```

</details>

The message warns that internment, after the stated crossing and start of
return transports, would lead to mass flight, unspeakable misery and open
resistance. `FELDMXMACKENSEN` and the complete raw reference `JAJJ6J4` are
retained. No numerical value is assigned to that reference.

## Exact accounting and prior work

| Part | Printed slots | Working frame | Raw fixed positions | Observed substitutions | Printed-erasure fills | Inserted-coordinate fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| C1 | 222 | 222 | 110 / 111 | 4 | 1 | 0 |
| C2 | 264 | 264 | 132 / 132 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| C3 | 206 | 206 | 103 / 103 | 5 | 0 | 0 |
| C4 | 244 | 244 | 122 / 122 | 5 | 0 | 0 |
| A5 | 222 | 232, conditional | 103 / 116 | 6 | 3 | 10 |
| A6 | 194 | 194 | 97 / 97 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| **Total** | **1,352** | **1,362** | **667 / 681** | **24** | **4** | **10** |

The candidate fixes all 681 **labels in the declared model**. That count
does not certify the historical meanings of the numerical reference or
turn the fifth-part reconstruction into direct source text. There are no
source deletions, block rearrangements or changes to the published key.

The earlier [Lasry et al. author manuscript](https://www.apprendre-en-ligne.net/crypto/bibliotheque/PDF/adfgvx.pdf),
p21, already identifies and summarizes this message and explicitly credits
Childs. Its key is likewise prior work. The present contribution is the
complete German source edition, corrected OCR frames, conditional loss
audit and exact repair accounting. Earlier unreviewed repository candidates
are frozen separately; none is presented as a new historical discovery.

The [experiment and verifier](../../experiments/mackensen_armistice_appeal/README.md)
preserve both source-page crops, every coordinate-to-plaintext map,
all 24,976 two-group costs, raw numeral/rare-letter occurrences and every
supplied coordinate.

# Internment letter to Mackensen's soldiers' council — p226 C / p227 A

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Prior reading: J. Rives Childs; George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker. Source edition and exact repair audit: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The four-part letter says that efforts to avoid internment have failed, asks the soldiers to maintain order, and expresses the hope of their return to Germany. This body is already published in [Lasry et al., Table 4](https://www.apprendre-en-ligne.net/crypto/bibliotheque/PDF/adfgvx.pdf), printed p. 22, and in [Lasry's dissertation, Table 6.4](https://www.uni-kassel.de/upress/online/OpenAccess/978-3-7376-0458-1.OpenAccess.pdf), p. 108. The source edition explains a two-location defect in part 3. An independent Berlin copy now supports the signature repairs and exposes differences between the transmitted and archival wording.

## Meaning

Addressed to the soldiers' council of the Mackensen army, the letter reports that the Entente insists on internment. It says that maintaining the marching order would be treated as a breach of the armistice, giving the Entente grounds to enter Germany. The sender promises to seek tolerable internment conditions and a safe return home after peace is concluded, then urges calm and order to avoid internal disintegration.

The closing names the executive council of the workers' and soldiers' councils of Greater Berlin. The raw signatures are `SOLKENBUHR` and `MNELLER`. The archival counterpart signs Molkenbuhr and Richard Müller, supporting the two surname repairs described below.

The source is headed `ZON v BSL` (the O has two marks), `04.20 a.m., December 2nd`, with origin field `NR 132 2200 (11/29) 4 TLE`. Parts 1–3 appear on printed p226 and part 4 on p227. These are different date fields, not an interchangeable date of composition. All four parts use the unchanged published **Nov28–Dec1** key.

| Part | Printed coordinates | Fixed raw positions, including garbles | Additional readable-text repairs |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| p226 C1 | 344 | 172/172 | 6 substitutions with the damaged word retained; 8 if `STATIONEN` is proposed |
| p226 C2 | 324 | 162/162 | 11 known-coordinate substitutions |
| p226 C3 | 338 | 168/169 under the explicit group-restoration model | 4 substitutions and 1 supplied coordinate |
| p227 A4 | 392 | 196/196 | 12 substitutions; 13 if `MOLKENBUHR` is also proposed |

## An independent Berlin copy

Document 96 in Engel, Holtz and Materna, eds., *Groß-Berliner Arbeiter- und
Soldatenräte in der Revolution 1918/19* (Akademie Verlag, 1993), pp. 461–462,
preserves a typescript carbon copy of the same letter. Its 28 November
dateline and the editor's 29 November dispatch date distinguish composition
from transmission; Childs records `2200 (11/29)` in the originating line.
[Published source and comparison](../../experiments/mackensen_archival_comparison/README.md).

The independent signatures support the existing cipher-side proposals:

| Raw surname | Signature in the Berlin copy | Required source-coordinate change |
|---|---|---|
| `SOLKENBUHR` | Molkenbuhr | 71: V→F |
| `MNELLER` | Richard Müller | 269: G→D |

Indices are zero based. Each surname needs one substitution. The complete
fourth-part edition with both names still costs **13 substitutions**; the
new evidence strengthens those earlier repairs. Richard belongs to the
archival attribution, while the ciphertext supplies only the surname.

The copy also has *Faktoren* where the received first part yields
`SMUTIONEN`, and a longer armistice term in part 2. These are distinct
textual witnesses. The comparison uses the published transcription;
the archival original has not been inspected.

## Part 3: restoring two malformed groups

The source visibly prints a six-letter group **`VFFGDV`** at group 34 and a four-letter group **`XFVA`** at group 56. The total remains the advertised 338 coordinates. Decrypting those coordinates in their printed sequence gives a garbled result; that identity result is retained in the certificate.

A separate model restores five-letter grouping at those two locations: remove one coordinate from group 34 and add one slot inside group 56. Among all **30** local layouts, the readable 169-position candidate needs the fewest further known-coordinate substitutions in two equivalent cases:

- Remove either of the adjacent `F` characters in group 34, producing `VFGDV`.
- Supply `V` after the initial `X` of group 56, producing `XVFVA`.

The two deletion indices are aliases of one reconstructed stream. Before supplying the new coordinate or changing any remaining source symbol, its raw plaintext is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional deletion-and-insertion frame; equivalent deletion aliases retained:**

```text
ESIVTUNSE?BEMUEHENEUREINTERNIERUNGSOZUGESTALTENDASSIHRWEDERNHTNOCHMANGELLEIDETUNDNACHDEMMOJGLICHSTRASCHENFRIEDENSCHLUSSGLUECKLICHUNDGESUNDINDIEHEIMATZUJUECKKEHRENKOENNTY
```

</details>

Four explicit coordinate substitutions and the one supplied `V` give:

**Readable German — conditional reconstructed third part:**

> Es ist unser Bemühen, eure Internierung so zu gestalten, dass ihr weder Not noch Mangel leidet und nach dem möglichst raschen Friedenschluss glücklich und gesund in die Heimat zurückkehren könnt.

The source-length spelling `FRIEDENSCHLUSS` is retained in the exact candidate; the additional S of modern `FRIEDENSSCHLUSS` is not silently inserted. The local optimum is conditional on this candidate and the stated two-group model. It establishes a small exact repair certificate, not historical certainty about every error.

## A word in part 1 remains unsettled

The directly decrypted token after `INBEDRACHTKOQMENDEN` is **`SMUTIONEN`**, occupying nine positions. The prior publication prints **`SITUATIONEN`**, which has eleven. That normalization therefore requires two extra plaintext positions and is not an unchanged or same-length decryption.

The present certificate prices two same-length alternatives. `STATIONEN` adds two coordinate substitutions to the six otherwise proposed in part 1; `INSTANZEN` raises that total to seventeen. The archival counterpart has `FAKTOREN`, eight letters. That wording explains the reference to the bodies concerned but does not fit the nine received positions. The conservative cipher edition therefore retains `SMUTIONEN`; `STATIONEN` remains a separately priced alternative, and the earlier `SITUATIONEN` normalization remains attributed to its publication.

## Literal source and reproducibility

The complete raw strings, source-index maps and every proposed edit are in [inputs.json](../../experiments/corpus_extension/inputs.json) and [certificates.json](../../experiments/corpus_extension/certificates.json). The focused source images are [part 1](../../experiments/corpus_extension/sources/p226_C1.png), [part 2](../../experiments/corpus_extension/sources/p226_C2.png), [part 3](../../experiments/corpus_extension/sources/p226_C3.png) and [part 4](../../experiments/corpus_extension/sources/p227_A4.png).

```sh
python experiments/corpus_extension/verify.py --verify
python experiments/mackensen_archival_comparison/verify.py --verify
```

Raw `X`, `Y`, `J` and digits remain labels from the published square. Ordinary spelling proposals and source layout repairs do not change that square.

cases/military/mackensen_subordination.m.text:
# Eleventh Army subordination to Mackensen

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

A two-part telegram on Childs pp100–101 reports that the 11th Army and all
its German elements have been placed under `O.K. MACKENSEN` and asks for
orders. A second copy of the ending provides useful letter evidence but has
an extra five-coordinate group and a weak source glyph. The native reading
and the conditional copy analysis remain distinct.

## p100 D1

The [D1 source](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p100_D1.png)
reads `UKS v ZON`, received at an unspecified time on November 2, origin
`2312 (1) 2 TLE`, and `1 TL RICHI-136`. There are 136 slots, including the
printed `L` at source 39 and `C` at 56. The following page is explicitly
marked as a continuation.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame**

```text
OXKXMACKENSENX11XARMEE?ITALLENDEUTSCHENTEILENISTLAUT?XHXLXRMX1A11127
```

`C56` as `A` gives 68/68 fixed positions with **no observed-coordinate
substitutions**. It ends in reference `RM 1A11127`, with the sentence
continuing in A2. The source does not supply additional words between the
reference and that continuation.

## p101 A2

The [A2 source](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p101_A2_B2.png)
has the same `UKS v ZON`, `2312 (1) 2 TLE` heading and is explicitly
`2 TL RICHI-132`. All 132 native coordinates are valid.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame**



</details>

> dem O.K. Mackensen unterstellt und bittet um Befehle. A.O.K. 11. RM 1A7011.

All 66 raw labels are fixed. The single change is source 65 `V`→`F`, giving
`BITTET` in place of `BITTEP`. The second copy below directly supports the
`T` coordinate. The reference `7011` and the two appearances of `11` across
these parts remain literal. The [p99 receipt acknowledgment](../radio/nov1_contact_and_mail.md#p99-d-acknowledgment-of-an-ohl-message)
also names reference `11127`; it remains a separate telegram rather than
an additional part of this text.

## p101 D2

The [D2 source](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p101_C1_D2.png)
reads `UKS v ZON`, `2.15 a.m., November 2nd`, origin `2352 (1)`, and
`2 TL RIZI-137`. Its origin differs from A2's `2312`. This edition reserves
**137 source slots**, including printed `S` at 19 and an illegible fifth
slot after `XDVV` at 119. The latter is not transcribed as the copy's expected
`X`. The [14× detail](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p101_D2_illegible.png)
shows a separate upper stroke and lower ink trace in that slot. The advertised
137 supports this interpretation but is not its only evidence. In the source
JSON, `?` at this one location explicitly denotes an illegible ink remnant,
not a printed question mark.

The common-frame model excludes the **five observed coordinates** in
`XDDAF`, source 10–14, to obtain 132 slots. Those exclusions have a cost of
five observed-coordinate operations; they are not free padding removal.
All native 137-slot diagnostics, including the unpaired coordinate, remain
in the certificate.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 132-slot copy-alignment frame**

```text
?EMOXKXMACKENSENUNTERSTELLTUNDBI?TETUMBEFEHLEXAXOXKX11XRMX1A70G1XX
```

**Edited output — same conditional frame; separately priced exclusions**

```text
DEMOXKXMACKENSENUNTERSTELLTUNDBITTETUMBEFEHLEXAXOXKX11XRMX1A7011XX
```

</details>

**Readable German — from the conditional edited layer**

> dem O.K. Mackensen unterstellt und bittet um Befehle. A.O.K. 11. RM 1A7011.

This model has 64/66 raw fixed positions. The selected edited text fills
`S19`→`G` and the illegible source 119→`X`, and changes source 136 `F`→`X`.
The last substitution changes the raw reference `70G1` to `7011`, supported
by A2's unchanged coordinate. Its price is **1 observed substitution,
2 source-mask fills and 5 observed-coordinate exclusions**.

### Equal-cost copy readings

After the declared alignment, the two endings have 128 identical observed
coordinates, two complementary masks, and two observed conflicts. At common
frame index 65, A2 has `V` and D2 has `F`; at 131, A2 has `X` and D2 has `F`.
There are four equally minimum common streams:

| Common word / reference | A2 substitutions | D2 substitutions | Combined substitutions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `BITTEP / 7011` | 0 | 2 | 2 |
| **`BITTET / 7011`** | **1** | **1** | **2** |
| `BITTEP / 70G1` | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| `BITTET / 70G1` | 2 | 0 | 2 |

Every row additionally uses the same two D2 source-mask fills and the
separately stated five exclusions. The chosen readable row combines the
`T` supported by D2 and the numeric reference supported by A2. Equal edit
cost alone does not select it, and the two physical copies do not prove
independent transmission histories.

### Geometry and weak-glyph limits

All **133 contiguous five-coordinate exclusions** in the 137-slot source
were evaluated against the selected common text. Starts **8, 9, 10, 11 and
12** tie at one observed substitution and give exactly the same raw and
edited streams. Their source-origin maps differ. Start 10 is the printed
group boundary used for presentation, not a unique historical loss or
insertion location. This finite test does not exhaust arbitrary five-coordinate
exclusions or alternative plaintexts.

The old OCR's **136-slot interpretation** is retained as an alternate
reading of the weak ink trace. Under that interpretation, the equivalent
132-slot copy model needs five observed exclusions, one newly supplied
coordinate, one source-mask fill and one substitution. It produces the same
final text. The text therefore cannot decide whether the weak fifth slot
was a printed character or a missing coordinate; the primary slot choice
comes from the image review.

## Evidence and attribution

The published `Nov1-3` square and ranks retain the credit of **George Lasry,
Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**. The current source and arithmetic
review is by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Earlier unreviewed OCR
candidates are retained in the [prior-evidence snapshot](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/prior_evidence.json).
No first historical decipherment priority is claimed. The existing
[p100 challenge](../p100.md) is a separate A message and keeps Armin's earlier
body credit; its status is unchanged.

[Literal rows, key and source images](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/inputs.json),
[recomputed domains and complete ledgers](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/certificates.json)
and [verification commands](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/README.md)
make the stated frames and repairs reproducible. The verifier also checks
that each readable passage preserves every non-`X` label in its cited stream.
