# The Warsaw query and its later quotation — p181 A / p214 B

[Case guide](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** A 92-character query on p181 is quoted inside a later message on
p214 under a different key. The two direct readings agree at **85 of 92**
aligned positions; their complementary evidence supports a complete query
with every proposed source change recorded. **Source comparison and edition:**
icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. This is a supplementary message, not a new
solution to an open challenge.

## Reading

**Readable German:**

> Erbitten umgehend Nachricht, ob Geruecht vom Anmarsch Mackensens auf
> Warschau wahr. Soldatenrat Warschau.

**Meaning:** The Warsaw Soldiers' Council asks for an immediate report on
whether the rumor of Mackensen's advance on Warsaw is true. The query does
not itself establish that such an advance occurred.

The later message includes the query in its forwarding body:

**Readable German — earlier cross-key repairs, with one additional separator fill:**

> An OKM. Hier einging folgender Funkspruch: Erbitten umgehend Nachricht, ob Geruecht vom Anmarsch Mackensens auf Warschau wahr. Soldatenrat Warschau.

The address and introductory sentence are directly decoded. The display
treats the erased character after `FUNKSPRUCHX` as a second separator,
filling source **3** with **A** to make **AX=X**. This adds one mask fill
to the earlier cross-key edition and completes the 130-position introduction
and quotation. The whole source now has **145/146** fixed labels, at **three
observed substitutions and four mask fills**. The remaining erasure is in
the closing reference.

The boundary fill is editorial: the source permits `1GJKWX`, so X is not
cipher-forced. [Exact fill, quotation mapping and retained footer domain](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/p214_completion_certificate.json).

## Prior publication and date discrepancy

Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker already discuss the Warsaw query in section
6.4 of [*Deciphering ADFGVX messages from the Eastern Front of World War I*](https://www.apprendre-en-ligne.net/crypto/bibliotheque/PDF/adfgvx.pdf),
DOI [10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461).
Their narrative assigns it to **13 November**. The inspected p181 page heading
and intercept header both print **12 November**. The source date is retained
here; the discrepancy is not silently resolved.

The present contribution is the cross-key quotation link, direct source
transcription and exact repair accounting. It does not claim first
decipherment of the query or treat the previously published interpretation
as independent cryptographic evidence.

The same prior body credit applies to the quoted query within **p214 B**.
Its forwarding introduction, cross-key source relationship and damaged footer
are assessed separately in this edition.

## Sources and direct readings

| Witness | Source header | Published key | Direct reading |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| [p181 A / PDF p184](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/sources/childs_p181_selected.png) | `NKJ v LP (06.43 p.m., November 12th); 15.50; RICHI-184` | `Nov10-12` | 91/92 positions fixed |
| [p214 B / PDF p217](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/sources/childs_p214_selected.png) | `--- v UKS (07.05 p.m., November 22d); 1630 (11/22); RICHI-292` | `Nov22-24` | 141/146 positions fixed |

The unmodified p181 reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ERBITTENUMGEHENDNACHRICHTOBGERUECHTVOMANMARSCHMACKEN?ENSAUFWARSCHAUWAHRXSOLDATENRATWARSCHAUX
```

</details>

Its only unknown plaintext position comes from the printed invalid coordinate
`C` in group `AACDD`. The later quote supplies the missing `S` in
`MACKENSENS`. Filling source index **17** with `G` preserves all **183 valid
coordinates**; the resulting 92-character text re-encrypts exactly. No
unknown square cell is assigned.

The p214 source decodes as:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ANOKMXHIEREINGINGFOLGENDERFUNKSPRUCHX?ERBI3TENUM?EHEN?NACHRICHTOBGERUECHT?OMANMARSCHMACKENSENSAUFWARACHAUWAHRXSOLDATENRATWARSCHA8XXAOKYYXRMYAQY?5X
```

</details>

Its 92-position quotation starts at plaintext index **38**. The p181 text
supports three changes to fixed p214 characters and three erasure fills:

| Quote position, zero based | p181 | Direct p214 | Consequence |
| ---: | :---: | :---: | --- |
| 4 | T | 3 | One known-coordinate substitution in p214. |
| 10 | G | ? | One p214 erasure fill. |
| 15 | D | ? | One p214 erasure fill. |
| 35 | V | ? | Fill the invalid printed `S` coordinate in p214. |
| 52 | ? | S | Fill the invalid printed `C` coordinate in p181. |
| 62 | S | A | One known-coordinate substitution in p214. |
| 90 | U | 8 | One known-coordinate substitution in p214. |

The p214 substitutions are source indices **242: F→V**, **208: X→D** and
**170: X→V**. The fills are **4: –→G**, **56: –→G** and **165: S→V**.
The earlier quote reconstruction changes no other source slot. Of its two
remaining erasures, the optional boundary completion above fills source 3;
source 78 in the ending `XAOKYYXRMYAQY?5X` remains unknown. The questionable
fixed closing labels are retained.

## Verification

The [input package](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/inputs.json)
contains the literal groups, prior-publication note, headers and source image
hashes. The [certificate](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/certificates.json)
reproduces the quote alignment and each coordinate cost with an independent
column-offset inverse, checked against the project decoder.

```sh
python3 experiments/open_targets_continuation/verify.py --verify
```

George Lasry's period-key publication is credited separately from this source
review and comparison by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

## Later conditional reading of the p214 closing label

The independent [late-key interpretation](../../experiments/late_key_interpretation/README.md) applies the p217-derived Nov22–24 numeral hypothesis to the unchanged p214 B source. Its baseline `AOKYY` becomes `AOK11`, consistent with the 11th Army headquarters. The remaining reference stays damaged, and this optional map does not alter the earlier quoted body or its repair costs.

# Mackensen's withdrawal report: the separately received second part

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Printed p118 explicitly identifies this record as the **second part of the
thirteen-part message sent at 20:00 on 11/3**. It supplies the source witness
missing from the earlier [twelve-part repository edition](mackensen_withdrawal_report.md).
The header, source number and unchanged Nov1–3 key bind the second part to
that report; no historical English translation is back-translated into
cipher evidence.

The source has 377 valid coordinates against `RICHI-378`. Its eighth ciphertext
row begins with the visibly short four-glyph group **FGAD**. The conditional
378-coordinate frame below inserts one unknown coordinate inside that group,
then separately prices its fill and every observed-coordinate change.

## p118 A2

Childs p118, PDF p121; [full source crop](../../experiments/mackensen_withdrawal_part2/sources/p118_A2.png)
and [short-group detail](../../experiments/mackensen_withdrawal_part2/sources/p118_A2_short_group.png).
The page heading gives 3 November, reception is 6 November, and the explicit
assembly note gives 20:00 on 11/3. These source date layers remain separate.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — literal header:**

```text
3rd NOVEMBER, 1918.
A) LP v UKS (04.06 a.m., November 6th)
(Following is 2nd TLE of 13 TLE message sent at 20:00 11/3)
2 TL RICHI-378
```

**Raw output — conditional one-slot insertion at source boundary 283; 188/189 fixed positions:**

```text
SEIT1X11X18ERGIBTSICGJEDOCHDASBILDXDASSDIESERBIZC?ENARMEANMIT3LRANCXDMVXIMVO0MARSCHGE7ENBELGRADXSHMENDRIABEWRIFFENSINDUNDDERBEITVID8NUNDOO2PALANKAFEABSICHTIGTEANGRIFFAUF7EGEBENZUSEINVCHEINT
```

**Edited output — same frame, 13 observed-coordinate substitutions and one inserted-slot fill; 189/189 fixed positions:**

```text
SEIT1X11X18ERGIBTSICHJEDOCHDASBILDXDASSDIESERBISCHENARMEENMIT3FRANZXDIVXIMVORMARSCHGEGENBELGRADXSHMENDRIABEGRIFFENSINDUNDDERBEIXVID8NUNDOO2PALANKABEABSICHTIGTEANGRIFFAUFGEGEBENZUSEINSCHEINT
```

</details>

Observed coordinate changes, with zero-based source indices: **6 F→V**, **45 F→V**, **47 D→F**, **48 F→D**, **49 G→F**, **62 F→V**, **112 F→D**, **114 A→G**, **138 G→V**, **164 X→V**, **215 G→F**, **225 V→A**, **229 G→F**.

The modeled slot at source boundary 283 is filled **V**, reconstructing
`FGAD` as `FGAVD`. It has no source index and is not counted as a printed-mask
fill. All 377 observed source positions remain in order; no observed position is deleted. The complete
edited stream re-encrypts exactly to this declared frame and these changes.

**Readable German — complete baseline edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Seit 1 / 11 / 18 ergibt sich jedoch das Bild, dass die serbischen Armeen mit 3 franz. Div. im Vormarsch gegen Belgrad, SHMENDRIA begriffen sind und der bei VID8N und OO2PALANKA beabsichtigte Angriff aufgegeben zu sein scheint.

**Meaning:** For the period beginning 1/11/18, the report assesses that the Serbian armies with 3 French divisions are advancing toward Belgrade and the literal place label SHMENDRIA; the attack planned near the literal labels VID8N and OO2PALANKA appears to have been abandoned. This is the report's assessment, not independent evidence of the actual movements.

## The source geometry supports the selected local frame

All 378 possible single-insertion boundaries were tested against the exact
baseline template. Boundary 283 is the unique minimum at 13 observed
substitutions plus one missing-coordinate fill. The five possible boundaries
in or immediately after the four-letter group give:

| Source boundary | Missing coordinate supplied | Observed substitutions |
|---:|:---:|---:|
|280|F|16|
|281|G|15|
|282|A|14|
|283|V|13|
|284|D|14|

This is a bounded comparison under a fixed proposed reading and unchanged
published key. It does not prove that no different historical damage model
could explain the record. The original 377-coordinate odd frame, its raw
pair decoding and the final orphan coordinate are also retained in the
certificate; the orphan is never silently discarded from the source.

## Place labels and numerical labels

The baseline deliberately retains the source-derived names **SHMENDRIA**,
**VID8N** and **OO2PALANKA**. Their familiar geographical interpretations are
kept out of the baseline coordinate count.

**Conditional interpretation — optional geographical spellings:**

Changing those three labels to **SEMENDRIA**, **VIDIN** and **LOMPALANKA**
costs four additional observed-coordinate substitutions:

| Source index | Observed change |
|---:|:---:|
|113|G→F|
|228|F→G|
|271|G→A|
|371|F→V|

That optional complete stream has 17 observed substitutions and the same
one-coordinate insertion/fill. Its re-encryption is certified separately;
these plausible names are not independent geographical identifications.

The baseline keeps the exact date labels **1/11/18** and count **3**. Changes
from 0 to R in `VORMARSCH` and from 7 to G in `GEGEN` and `AUFGEGEBEN` are
ordinary-word proposals with explicit coordinate costs. The raw forms are
shown above, so no numeral reassignment is hidden in the readable layer.

## Attribution and evidence

Historical decipherment of the withdrawal report belongs to **J. Rives
Childs**. **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker** published
a reconstruction in 2016; the earlier repository edition records that
attribution and the published-key credit. An unreviewed merged OCR screen
already suggested much of this second part. The present contribution is
its primary-source review, exact short-group geometry, exhaustive local
insertion pricing and complete qualified reading. No first-decipherment
priority is claimed.

[Inputs](../../experiments/mackensen_withdrawal_part2/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/mackensen_withdrawal_part2/certificates.json),
[prior candidate](../../experiments/mackensen_withdrawal_part2/prior_candidates.json)
and [reproduction](../../experiments/mackensen_withdrawal_part2/README.md)
provide the complete evidence.

# Mackensen's November 3 withdrawal report and its separately received ninth part

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and assembly audit: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This thirteen-part report assesses threats to the occupation army's rear
communications and proposes immediate withdrawal from Romania if a general
armistice is not expected soon. Its historical decipherment belongs to
**J. Rives Childs**; **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**
published most of the reconstructed body in their 2016 paper, Table 3.
The present contribution is an exact source edition, repair accounting,
and the recovery of the report's assembly from separately received pieces.

The original package below retains **twelve physical parts**: eleven readable
editions and one heavily jammed ending. The separately received
[second part, p118 A2](mackensen_withdrawal_part2.md), has now been located
and source-reviewed, so all thirteen numbered parts have a source entry.
Its 189-position reading uses one explicitly modeled missing coordinate
and thirteen observed-coordinate substitutions; its place-name defects
remain literal. The original twelve-record evidence and totals below stay
unchanged, and the second part has its own repair certificate.
The period square and column ranks remain the published **Nov1–3** key.

## Why part 9 belongs here

The consecutive copy on printed pp114–116 explicitly marks its ninth part
missing. Table 3 in the 2016 paper also leaves it missing. But the previous
source page contains **p113 B, explicitly labelled `9 TL`**. It shares the
`2000 (3)` message reference, the OHL destination, the Nov1–3 cipher key,
and the exact grammatical join from part 8 to part 10. Its receiving time is
9.38pm on November 5, after the November 4 main copy; the later receipt
explains why it is treated as a separate physical witness rather than
silently inserted into the page image.

Part 8 ends with the communications that had so far been disabled only
because of something; part 9 supplies the complete collapse of the Hungarian
army and disorganization of its railway system; part 10 continues with a
threat of enemy attack. The new ninth-part edition needs **zero changes
to its 216 observed coordinates** and yields 108 fixed plaintext labels.
This is a source-and-assembly result, not a claim of universal decipherment
priority over earlier historical work or the earlier unreviewed OCR candidate.

## Read the surviving parts

Spaces below are editorial word breaks. Literal `X` separators, abbreviations,
repetitions, unresolved `?` positions and the named defects are preserved.
Removing spaces from each displayed reading reproduces its certified
plaintext exactly. Ordinary word repairs are priced in the table below;
the complete unchanged raw strings remain in the certificate.

### p114 A1

**Part 1: Assessment of the situation.**

**Readable German:**

> BEURTEILUNG DER LAGE X BISHER MUSSTE DAMIT GERECHNET WERDEN X DASS FEIND MIT DEN BEI VIDIN X LOEPALANKA UND IN GEGEND RUTSCHUK IN VERSAMMLUNG BEGRIFFENEN KRAEFTEN EINEN DONAUUEBERGANG VERSUCHEN WIRD MIT DEM ZIEL X DIE BAHN ORSOVA X CRAIOVA ZU UNTERBRECHEN UND AUF BUKAREST VORZUSTOSSEN

The source spelling `LOEPALANKA` is retained. Two observed-coordinate changes repair `MCT` and `KRNEFTE`; six source masks are filled. No modern geographical spelling is imposed.

### p113 A3

**Part 3: Forces south of the Danube.**

**Readable German:**

> MIT DEM AUFMARSCH STAERKERER KRAEFTE AN DER DONAU SUEDLICH X SVISTOV X RUSTSCHUK MUSS BESONDERS NACH FRIEDENSSCHLUSS DER X TUERKEI WEITER GERECHNET WERDN

Five observed-coordinate changes supply ordinary words. The defective final `WERDN` is retained; an extra E is not silently inserted.

### p114 A4

**Part 4: Possible Serbian advance.**

**Readable German:**

> ES IST SOMIT DURCHAUS WAHRSCHEINLICH X DASS DIE DURCH FRANZOSEN VERSTAERKTEN SERBISCHEN ARMEEN DEN UEBERGANG UEBER DIE

Two observed-coordinate substitutions and one masked-glyph fill produce this continuation. The final glyph of source group `VADG-` remains conservatively masked in the source layer.

### p115 A5

**Part 5: Crossing into southern Hungary.**

**Readable German:**

> DONAU BEI X BELGRAD X SEMENDIA X UND DEN EINMARSCH IN SUE X SUE UNGARN BEABSICHTIGEN X WAEHREND DIE AUFGABE DER SUEDL X

Four coordinate substitutions repair three plaintext letters. The repeated `SUE X SUE` is in the source-derived body and remains in the edition.

### p115 A6

**Part 6: French offensive toward Bucharest.**

**Readable German:**

> SVISTOV X RUSTSCHUK AUFMARSCHIERENDEN FRANZOES X ARMEE X OFFENSIVE RICHTUNG BUKAREST X BESTEHEN BLEIBT X IM ZUSAMMENHANG MIT DIESER

**All 113 positions are directly fixed by the unchanged received coordinates.** No substitution, fill or length adjustment is needed.

### p115 A7

**Part 7: Romanian movement through the passes.**

**Readable German:**

> OPERATION IST ES NICHT AUSGESCHLOSSEN X DASS RUMAEN X KRAEFTE AUS DER MOLDAU DURCH DEN TOELGYES X GIMES X UND X OITOS PASS X IN

Four coordinate substitutions support the three character repairs, including the prior-reading place-name correction `GJMES→GIMES`. This is a priced editorial choice, not independent geographical identification.

### p115 A8

**Part 8: Threatened rear communications.**

**Readable German:**

> SIEBENBUERGEN X EINRUECKEN X X DADURCH WERDEN DIE RUECKWAERTIGEN VERBINDUNGEN DES BESATZUNGSHEERES X DIE BISHER NUR IN FOLGE

Two observed-coordinate substitutions repair `DEF` and `BIVHER`. The last words lead directly into the separately received part 9.

### p113 B9

**Part 9: The separately received ninth part.**

**Readable German:**

> DER VOELLIGEN AUFLOESUNG DES UNGAR X HEERES UND DER DESORGANISATION DES UNGAR X BAHNWESENS AUSGESCHALTET WAREN X DURCH FEINDL X

**All 108 positions are directly fixed by the unchanged source.** There are no masks, word repairs, missing coordinates or key changes in this part. Its full raw body was already present as an unreviewed OCR candidate; the new work certifies its source and joins it to the report.

### p116 A10

**Part 10: Occupation and supply constraints.**

**Readable German:**

> ANGRIFF BEDOHT UND DIE WEITERE BESETZUNG DER X WALACHEI X WIE IN X O X K X 2 X RM1 X A X NR X 1??6?O6? AUSGEFUEHRT ZWEIFLOS UND IM HINBLICK

Three observed-coordinate changes and eleven source-mask fills give this conservative edition. The literal defects `BEDOHT` and `ZWEIFLOS` remain. Four unresolved reference positions and the observed reference labels are not replaced by the smoother number printed in the later reconstruction.

### p116 A11

**Part 11: Ammunition, food and coal.**

**Readable German:**

> AUF MUNITIONS X VERPFLEGUNGS X UND KOHLEN VORRAETE UNDURCHFUEHRBAR X FALLS DER ALLGEMEINE WAFFENSTILLSTAND NICHT IN ABSEHBARER

This is conditional on one missing transmitted coordinate at source boundary 102. It preserves every observed coordinate, fills sixteen source masks and supplies the missing coordinate. The visible four-character group occurs elsewhere, at 110; the geometry tension is discussed below.

### p116 A12

**Part 12: Proposed immediate withdrawal.**

**Readable German:**

> ZEIT ZU ERWARTEN IST X WIRD DESHALB VORGESCHLAGEN X DAS BESATZUNSHEER SOFORT AUS X RUMAENIEN HERAUS ZU ZIEHEN UND GEMEINSAM MIT DEN DEUTSCHEN

Three observed-coordinate substitutions, six source-mask fills and one modeled missing-coordinate fill are explicit. All four minimum-cost boundaries 141–144 are retained. The literal `BESATZUNSHEER` is not silently expanded by adding G.

### p116 A13

**Part 13: Jammed final part, left partial.**

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
??????DERX?????MEED??M???CHDU?????GARN??F???R?CH??????A?Z??????N?EI?????T??N??????R?ET?????XK????M???A?1G?????X
```

</details>

The source prints 160 slots against RICHI-222 and explicitly says “Balance jammed.” The stated tail-loss model appends 62 unknown coordinates. Only 38 of 111 plaintext positions are fixed, and **no source mask, lost coordinate or word is filled**. The existing historical translation is not converted into invented cipher evidence.

A [separately priced optional route fragment](../../experiments/p116_optional_route_fragment/README.md)
tests five word spans under this same tail-loss model. It fixes 75 of 111
positions through five printed-mask fills and 32 lost-tail fills, without
changing any observed coordinate. Each of the 37 selected letters retains
one observed half-pair. The historical English translation guided the word
choices; it is not an independent German coordinate witness. The army label,
approval clause and footer are unfilled in that layer, and the raw-only edition
above is unchanged.

**Approval-request extension.** A further [conditional word layer](../../experiments/p116_optional_route_fragment/APPROVAL.md)
adds `EINVERSTAENDNIS?ERBETEN`, raising the reading to **90/111 positions**
with zero observed-coordinate changes, 11 printed-mask fills and 43 lost-tail
fills in total. Of the 15 newly fixed letters, 13 have an observed half-pair;
V at 68 and N at 87 are wholly missing and supplied by the word proposal.
Position 80 stays unresolved. An optional additional S gives 91/111 for one
more lost-tail fill; the army label and footer remain open.

**Optional footer fields.** The [joined field proposal](../../experiments/p116_optional_route_fragment/FOOTER.md)
adds `XKXMXRMX1XA` from overlapping original fields in p164 D and p105 C1,
reaching **97/111 positions** with 12 printed-mask fills and 49 lost-tail fills.
A separate closing proposal, guided by the historical signature, adds
`GR?XOPX` and reaches **101/111**, with 12 printed-mask fills and 53 lost-tail
fills. All eleven new labels have an observed half-coordinate; no observation
changes. The preceding position, intervening labels and army designation remain
unfilled. These are contextual proposals, not repeated-message identifications.

## The two short frames require different qualifications

Part 11 actually prints 219 slots, although its header says 220. An independent
manual retranscription confirms the four-character group `VGGV` at source
index 110. Testing **all 220 one-coordinate insertion boundaries** against
the readable template yields a unique zero-observed-substitution fit at
boundary 102. Masking the whole `WAFFENSTILLSTAND` word leaves the same minimum.
The five boundaries in or after the visibly short group,110–114, need 8,8,9,9
and 10 observed-coordinate changes under the complete template.

Thus the chosen model is arithmetically economical, but its missing-coordinate
location is **not visually witnessed by the short group**. A separate source
review found no transcription correction that removes this tension. The
edition does not infer how the historical printer or operator produced it.

Part 12 actually prints 237 against 238. Its short group `DDGF` starts at 140.
All 238 single-loss boundaries were evaluated. Boundaries141,142,143 and 144
tie at three observed-coordinate changes; these positions fall within or
at the end of that short group. After masking `BESATZUNSHEER`, three of those
boundaries remain tied at two observed changes. None is promoted to a
uniquely witnessed missing-symbol location.

Both templates were formed after reading the source and the prior report.
These are exact conditional cost comparisons, not blind confirmation of
the missing-coordinate mechanism or historical wording. The certificate
retains all 458 gap comparisons, all tied raw readings, and the separate
short-group comparisons.

The source-derived part 12 wording is `ZEIT ZU ERWARTEN IST`, where Table 3
uses `ZEIT EINTRITT`. This edition follows the received coordinate evidence.
Similarly, source defects and the uncertain part 10 reference are retained
instead of importing every normalization from the later reconstruction.

## Coverage and exact repair accounting

| Physical part | Source slots | Modeled positions | Raw fixed labels | Edition fixed labels | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills | Missing-coordinate fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| p114 A1 | 482 | 241 | 235 | 241 | 2 | 6 | 0 |
| p113 A3 | 262 | 131 | 131 | 131 | 5 | 0 | 0 |
| p114 A4 | 204 | 102 | 101 | 102 | 2 | 1 | 0 |
| p115 A5 | 194 | 97 | 97 | 97 | 4 | 0 | 0 |
| p115 A6 | 226 | 113 | 113 | 113 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| p115 A7 | 206 | 103 | 103 | 103 | 4 | 0 | 0 |
| p115 A8 | 214 | 107 | 107 | 107 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| p113 B9 | 216 | 108 | 108 | 108 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| p116 A10 | 218 | 109 | 95 | 105 | 3 | 11 | 0 |
| p116 A11 | 219 | 110 | 94 | 110 | 0 | 16 | 1 |
| p116 A12 | 237 | 119 | 112 | 119 | 3 | 6 | 1 |
| p116 A13 | 160 | 111 | 38 | 38 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| **Total** | **2838** | **1451** | **1334** | **1374** | **25** | **40** | **2** |

The 62 modeled tail coordinates of part 13 remain unknown, as do20 source-mask
coordinates across parts 10 and 13. Raw-label coverage is not a claim that
every printed letter, numeral or editorial word is historically correct.
There is no source deletion, block reordering or baseline-key change.

## Sources and reproduction

- Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed pp113–116:
  [complete scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
- Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker, *Deciphering ADFGVX messages from the Eastern Front of World War I* (2016), Table 3:
  [author paper](https://www.apprendre-en-ligne.net/crypto/bibliotheque/PDF/adfgvx.pdf).
- Delivered page images: [p113](../../experiments/mackensen_withdrawal_report/sources/p113.png),
  [p114](../../experiments/mackensen_withdrawal_report/sources/p114.png),
  [p115](../../experiments/mackensen_withdrawal_report/sources/p115.png),
  [p116](../../experiments/mackensen_withdrawal_report/sources/p116.png).

The [inputs](../../experiments/mackensen_withdrawal_report/inputs.json) preserve
the headers and manually transcribed coordinate groups. The
[certificate](../../experiments/mackensen_withdrawal_report/certificates.json)
contains each source-to-plaintext coordinate map, raw domains, all repairs,
and exact forward witnesses. Arbitrary full fills used for round-trip checks
are labelled as validation witnesses and are not historical readings.

```sh
python experiments/mackensen_withdrawal_report/verify.py --verify
python experiments/mackensen_withdrawal_report/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
```

The default verifier uses the standard library. The optional PDF check
regenerates all six delivered source images and compares their pixels.

# Heated sick wagons, cooking equipment and hot tea

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** Childs pp212–213, 22 November 1918; published `Nov22-24` key, unchanged. [Inputs](../../experiments/medical_return_transports/inputs.json), [exact certificates](../../experiments/medical_return_transports/certificates.json), [method and limits](../../experiments/medical_return_transports/README.md).

The readable medical passages concern preparations for transports coming through from Turkey. They recommend a sick wagon fitted with stoves, cooking equipment and continuously available hot tea. The final paragraph asks for action as far as possible from Constantinople because the received place `NIKOLA9EW` may lack sufficient capacity. The text records recommendations and a forwarding request, not proof that the equipment or supplies were provided.

The source has a nominal seven-part frame. Parts 2 and 4 were retained as unassigned context in this medical package and are excluded from its restored-reading count. A subsequent [cross-copy audit](../caucasus/p212_p218_crosscopy.md) identifies the printed part 2 as a truncated copy of a separate Caucasus/Russia withdrawal message on p218. The [conditional part-4 edition](p212_medical_fragment.md) now recovers 129/151 positions in its primary reading and 148/151 in an optional transport-doctor reading. The latter fills 102 missing coordinates without changing an observed coordinate; the 302-coordinate frame remains a hypothesis, and three opening positions remain unresolved. An unnumbered oil-cartel query between them is [edited separately](../finance/oil_cartel_dispatch_query.md). The relation of the seven printed parts remains unresolved.

## p212 A1

[Source crop](../../experiments/medical_return_transports/sources/p212_A1.png). The source advertises 344 coordinates but prints 339, including Y at source index 248. The primary 344-coordinate model inserts five erasures before source index 105 and treats the invalid Y as an erasure. Raw, 172 positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional five-coordinate gap before source 105; invalid source Y masked:**

```text
FUERM?LITAHRMISZIONKONSTANTENO?ELXXSTA0SARZTBEIMOSANOFFMILMIYZHATQUSODESSAFOLGENDESANDEUTSCHENGOUVERNEURNIKOLA9EWGERICHTHTQURBEKANNTG?BEANVONTUE?KEIDURCHGE?ENDETRANSP?RTEXX
```

</details>

A costed candidate, requiring nine observed-coordinate substitutions and six fills, is:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional gap and source-mask interpretation:**

```text
FUERMILITAERMISZIONKONSTANTINOPELXXSTABSARZTBEIMOSANOFFMILMISZHATAUSODESSAFOLGENDESANDEUTSCHENGOUVERNEURNIKOLA9EWGERICHTETZURBEKANNTGABEANVONTUERKEIDURCHGEHENDETRANSPORTEXX
```

</details>

Reading: for the military mission in Constantinople; a staff doctor, followed by the unexpanded received abbreviation `BEIMOSANOFFMILMISZ`, has sent the following from Odessa to the German governor at `NIKOLA9EW`, for communication to transports coming through from Turkey.

**The gap location is not unique.** All 340 possible single five-coordinate gaps were checked against the recorded candidate. Gaps 104, 105, 107 and 108 tie at nine observed-coordinate changes. Gap 105 is presented first because it lies at a five-coordinate source-group boundary. All four raw variants and exact repair certificates remain available; the proposed reading is conditional and is not described as a uniquely restored source.

## p212 A5

[Source crop](../../experiments/medical_return_transports/sources/p212_A5.png). All 280 source slots are printed, including invalid C at index 231. Raw, 140 positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
EINENMITOEFENVERSEHENVNREVIEVWA?ENFUERKRANKEEINRICHTENX2XXFELDKUECHEODEREINDEBAUTENHERGMITNEHMENXAUFDEMDAUERNDWARMERTEEVORRAETIGZUHALTENISTX
```

</details>

Five observed-coordinate substitutions and the single C-to-G fill yield:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
EINENMITOEFENVERSEHENENREVIERWAGENFUERKRANKEEINRICHTENX2XXFELDKUECHEODEREINGEBAUTENHERDMITNEHMENXAUFDEMDAUERNDWARMERTEEVORRAETIGZUHALTENISTX
```

</details>

Reading: arrange a sick wagon fitted with stoves; take a field kitchen or built-in stove on which warm tea is to be continuously available. The received instruction marker `2` remains unchanged and is not used to infer a missing preceding instruction.

## p213 A6

[Source crop](../../experiments/medical_return_transports/sources/p213_A6.png). The source has 318 slots, including a dash at index 39. Raw, 159 positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
KEINEWASSERSTELLENUNTERWEGSODEHOFTNICHTIMUETRIEBXXXGARNISONARZTNIKOLA9EWHA3GEBETENXDI2SENSPRUCH5TMILMISZWEINERZUGEBENX?DEPARTEMENTBITTETXVORSTEHENDENANREGUNGEN
```

</details>

Five observed-coordinate substitutions yield this conservative candidate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
KEINEWASSERSTELLENUNTERWEGSODEROFTNICHTIMBETRIEBXXXGARNISONARZTNIKOLA9EWHATGEBETENXDIESENSPRUCH5TMILMISZWEITERZUGEBENX?DEPARTEMENTBITTETXVORSTEHENDENANREGUNGEN
```

</details>

The text says water points are absent or often out of operation en route; the garrison doctor at `NIKOLA9EW` has requested that the message be passed on to the military mission, with the received bridge `5T` still unexplained. The following department request continues into part 7.

The `5T` bridge is not silently rewritten. The erased position before `DEPARTEMENT` also remains unresolved: plaintext index 118, pair `?X`, source indices 39/242, domain `1GJKWX`. It may not be assigned solely to make the surrounding text smoother.

## p213 A7

[Source crop](../../experiments/medical_return_transports/sources/p213_A7.png). The source has 276 slots with printed C at index 232. Raw, 138 positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
SCHONMOEGLICHSTVONKONSTANTINOPELAUSZUENTSPRECHENXDAANGENOMMENWER?ENKANNXDASSNIKOLA9EWNICHTLEISTUNGSFAEHIGGENUGISTXXKMXAXDXNRQJ0XXYYXY5XAYY
```

</details>

Filling the invalid C as G gives `WERDEN` without changing any observed valid coordinate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
SCHONMOEGLICHSTVONKONSTANTINOPELAUSZUENTSPRECHENXDAANGENOMMENWERDENKANNXDASSNIKOLA9EWNICHTLEISTUNGSFAEHIGGENUGISTXXKMXAXDXNRQJ0XXYYXY5XAYY
```

</details>

Reading: meet the preceding recommendations as far as possible from Constantinople, since `NIKOLA9EW` may not have sufficient capacity. The complete raw footer `KMXAXDXNRQJ0XXYYXY5XAYY` is unchanged; no number or date is supplied by conjecture.

## Attribution and retained gaps

The sick-wagon and final medical passages already had recognizable unreviewed repository candidates. This edition records the exact source and all local repairs; it makes no first historical decipherment claim. The two initially unassigned frames and all four tied first-part geometries remain preserved in this package's frozen evidence; the later part-2 identification has its own certificate and counting scope. No baseline square or later-period relabeling is applied to the medical readings.

# Inventory query for German MG08 machine guns

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p86 A asks how many German `MG08` with tripod mounts are available
in the recipient's area and what caliber they have. It is a request for an
inventory, not a report giving the number available. The source's address,
office and reference fields remain literal.

## Source and reading

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [printed p86, PDF p89](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [source crop](../../experiments/inventory_and_medical_return/sources/childs_p86_A.png)
is under an October 31 heading:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) OSM v NKJ (3.35 a.m., November 1st)
1207 (31/10)
RICHI-298
```

</details>

All 298 printed coordinates are valid and give 149 fixed labels under the
unchanged published `Oct28-31` key:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
MGKOMMANDEUROSMANHGRXOSTXWIEVIELDEUTSCHEMG08MITDREIFUSSLAFETTEIMDORTIGEXBER4ICHVORHANDENXWELCHESKALIBERHABENSIEXOSMAN19ABTLGXGRXHXQUXNO835C120X10X18X
```

</details>

Two known-coordinate substitutions repair ordinary words:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
MGKOMMANDEUROSMANHGRXOSTXWIEVIELDEUTSCHEMG08MITDREIFUSSLAFETTEIMDORTIGENBEREICHVORHANDENXWELCHESKALIBERHABENSIEXOSMAN19ABTLGXGRXHXQUXNO835C120X10X18X
```

</details>

Readable core, preserving the telegram's abbreviated grammar:

**Readable German:**

> Wie viel deutsche MG08 mit Dreifußlafette im dortigen Bereich
> vorhanden? Welches Kaliber haben sie?

The address field `MGKOMMANDEUROSMANHGRXOST` is not expanded into an
identified individual or a formally established command title. The closing
also remains unexpanded:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — unchanged closing-field excerpt:**

```text
OSMAN19ABTLGXGRXHXQUXNO835C120X10X18X
```

</details>

In particular, the **08** in `MG08`, the **19** in `OSMAN19`, and the complete
reference `NO835C120X10X18` are unchanged published-square labels. No unit,
office or date reassignment is inferred from a plausible reading.

## Exact costs

| Source index, zero-based | Printed group / position, one-based | Change | Effect |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 223 | 45 / 4 | `V` → `F` | `BER4ICH` → `BEREICH` |
| 289 | 58 / 5 | `A` → `X` | `DORTIGEX` → `DORTIGEN` |

The raw `4` inside `BER4ICH` remains visible in the original string and
numerical ledger. Its local word repair does not reassign the square's
digit `4`. There are no source erasures, inserted coordinates, deletions or
square changes. The complete 298-coordinate repaired witness is retained
in the [certificate](../../experiments/inventory_and_medical_return/certificates.json).

```sh
python experiments/inventory_and_medical_return/verify.py --verify
```

The [inputs](../../experiments/inventory_and_medical_return/inputs.json)
preserve the manual rows, source images and key provenance. The period key
is prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**,
[DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
also reproduced in Lasry's 2017 key comment. Earlier unreviewed OCR candidates
existed. The bounded author-paper review does not establish universal
first-decipherment priority; this source edition does not supply an answer
to the inventory question it recovers.

# Military-intendant addresses and responsibilities

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and recovery: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

A four-part message distinguishes the work of the **Generalintendant in
Berlin** from that of the **Generalintendant at `GRHQU`**. It supplies a new
Berlin address on Augsburger Strasse, assigns organization, personnel and
administrative-finance questions to Berlin, and assigns supply transport,
delivery, clothing and related matters to the headquarters office. The
address number and several reference fields remain unresolved.

The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
[printed p202, PDF p205](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
Its [preserved section image](../../experiments/military_intendant_remit/sources/p202_B.png)
has this header:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
B) NKJ v LP (4.00 p.m., November 16th)
FUER UKS 1200 (16) 4 TEILE SS GRHQU 14/11 FLUGPOST O K M
HERMANNSTADT (16)
```

</details>

The page heading is `16th NOVEMBER, 1918.`. The published `Nov16-18` key
is used unchanged, including all eight unassigned square cells.

## B1: new address and Berlin responsibilities

The first part advertises `RICHI-228` but contains only **223 valid
coordinates**. A 228-coordinate working frame with five consecutive missing
coordinates produces a clear body. The representative below puts that gap
before received index **145**, before printed group **30**. Its raw reading
is conditional on that placement:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional five-coordinate gap before source 145; representative placement:**

```text
NEUBADRESSEX?XGENERALI?TENDANTB?RLINAUGSB?RGERSTRX??XFUERKRIEGSGL?EDERUNGENPERSONALIENFUERREINEVERWALTUNG?SACHENIW
```

</details>

Four observed-coordinate substitutions and three fills of added slots give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same representative gap model, with the stated substitutions and added-slot fills:**

```text
NEUEADRESSEX?XGENERALINTENDANTBERLINAUGSBURGERSTRX??XFUERKRIEGSGLIEDERUNGENPERSONALIENFUERREINEVERWALTUNGSSACHENIN
```

</details>

This announces a new address and names the Berlin Generalintendant on
Augsburger Strasse. The street number and the field before the office name
are not supplied. The duties begin with war organization, personnel, and
purely administrative matters; the sentence continues in B2.

The five added coordinates are `?DGD?` in this representative. The two
question marks remain unknown. Every one of the 223 received coordinates
remains in its original order, and the four observed-coordinate changes
are recorded separately from added-coordinate fills.

### Competing placements are retained

The [gap audit](../../experiments/military_intendant_remit/gap_audit.json)
enumerates all **224** places to insert five unknown coordinates. Using an
ordinary-word template with the address and reference fields masked gives
a minimum of two observed-coordinate changes at **142 and 143**. Including
the proposed address gives three changes at **143 and 144**. Among the
**46** printed-group boundaries or final end position, the full proposed
body has its minimum of four changes at **145**; the masked comparison
instead favors **140**.

The templates were constructed after reading the candidates. These are
conditional edit-cost comparisons, not independent plaintext evidence.
The earlier book and radio language scores both favored position **146**,
and their full score rows are retained. Because marginal scores can favor
unknown characters, that ranking does not establish the original geometry.
The edition therefore uses an explicit representative and makes no unique
loss-location or loss-mechanism claim. The ordinary-language body is much
better constrained than the number fields and the precise placement.

## B2: administrative, cash and levy matters

The second part contains exactly **220 slots**, agreeing with `RICHI-220`.
At received index 86 the source prints the non-coordinate letter `Q` in
`XQFDG`. A heavily overprinted final glyph in `GAAD?`, index 169, is also
left undecided. Both are masked before decryption. The raw body is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
VERPFLEGUNGSANGELEGENHEIRENFUERGELDXKASSENXGEBUEHRNISANGELE?ENHEITENFUE?KONTRIBUTIONSGELDERUNDZWANGSAUFLAGENXX
```

</details>

One observed-coordinate change and two masked-slot fills give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
VERPFLEGUNGSANGELEGENHEITENFUERGELDXKASSENXGEBUEHRNISANGELEGENHEITENFUERKONTRIBUTIONSGELDERUNDZWANGSAUFLAGENXX
```

</details>

Together with B1, this assigns Berlin administrative victualling matters,
money and treasury business, pay or allowance matters, contribution money
and compulsory levies. No numeral is inserted into the body.

## B3: the headquarters supply office

The third part contains exactly **210 valid coordinates**, agreeing with
`RICHI-210`. Its raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
2XGENERALINTENDANTXGRHQUXALLENACHSCHUBANGELEGENHEITENSOWEITSIEMITTRANSPORT?NDHERANFUEHRUNNZUSAMMENHAENGEB
```

</details>

Four observed-coordinate substitutions give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
2XGENERALINTENDANTXGRHQUXALLENACHSCHUBANGELEGENHEITENSOWEITSIEMITTRANSPORTUNDHERANFUEHRUNGZUSAMMENHAENGEN
```

</details>

The message assigns the Generalintendant at `GRHQU` all supply matters
insofar as they concern transport and delivery. The direct published-square
label `2` at the beginning is retained.

## B4: clothing, meat, sutlery and wartime services

The final part contains exactly **224 slots**, agreeing with `RICHI-224`.
Three coordinates are masked: a faded `C/G`-shaped glyph in `VDA?D`, a
faded glyph in `XAA?D`, and the printed non-coordinate `R` in `ARFXD`.
Enlarged crops preserve the visible appearances. The raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
BEKL?IDUNGXUXA?SRUESTUNGFLEISCHVERSORGUNG?ARKETENDEREIWESENKRIEGSLEISTUNGENXGENERALIWTENDANTXRMX?XAX????XAX11X1?
```

</details>

One observed-coordinate change and three masked-slot fills give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
BEKLEIDUNGXUXAUSRUESTUNGFLEISCHVERSORGUNGMARKETENDEREIWESENKRIEGSLEISTUNGENXGENERALINTENDANTXRMX?XAX????XAX11X1?
```

</details>

The list continues with clothing and equipment, meat provision,
*Marketendereiwesen* (sutlery), and wartime services or requisitions.
The literal `UX` abbreviation is retained. The signature says
`GENERALINTENDANT`; six positions in its reference remain unresolved.

The [shared November date and order constraints](../../experiments/nov16_18_reference_completion/README.md)
fix three of those positions, giving `RM ? A 5?5? A 11 18` and
**109/112** conditional positions. Both fives use the same observed `VA`
pair; the final eight uses `FD`. This adds no source repair and does not
complete the reference number.

## Exact costs and limits

| Part | Received slots | Working frame | Raw fixed positions | Edition fixed positions | Known-coordinate changes | Masked-slot fills | Added-slot fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B1 | 223 | 228, conditional | 106 / 114 | 111 / 114 | 4 | 0 | 3 |
| B2 | 220 | 220 | 108 / 110 | 110 / 110 | 1 | 2 | 0 |
| B3 | 210 | 210 | 104 / 105 | 105 / 105 | 4 | 0 | 0 |
| B4 | 224 | 224 | 103 / 112 | 106 / 112 | 1 | 3 | 0 |
| **Total** | **877** | **882** | **421 / 441** | **432 / 441** | **10** | **5** | **3** |

The [inputs](../../experiments/military_intendant_remit/inputs.json) preserve
every manual row, ambiguous glyph, header and image hash. The
[certificates](../../experiments/military_intendant_remit/certificates.json)
map each plaintext position to both working-frame and original-source
coordinates, list all repairs and retain the complete unresolved domains.
There are no deletions, block moves or changes to the published square.
The two unknown inserted coordinates remain unknown.

Each partial reading has a globally consistent square/source completion
witness. Those witnesses choose arbitrary missing digits and coordinates
to demonstrate arithmetic consistency; they are explicitly **not proposed
original readings**. Repeated square cells couple the unresolved domains,
so their values cannot all be selected independently.

The period key is prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**, [2016, DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461).
B2 and B3 already appeared as unreviewed OCR-derived candidates in the
frozen p73 retrieval corpus. The present work supplies visual source
certification, the newly coherent opening and final-part bodies and their
explicit conditional models and costs. No explicit discussion of this

and catalog check; this does not establish universal historical priority.


# Namur arrival, Cassel transport and armistice-information requests

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

These four surviving source bodies report an arrival at Namur, direct prompt transport arrangements to Cassel, and request the local armistice conditions again. The Namur telegram explicitly lacks its second part; its first and third parts are presented without bridging that gap. Literal office labels, an opaque transport field and source-length spellings remain visible.

## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p172 excerpt](../../experiments/namur_cassel_armistice_requests/sources/p172_reviewed.png) · [Reviewed p180 excerpt](../../experiments/namur_cassel_armistice_requests/sources/p180_reviewed.png) · [Reviewed p181 excerpt](../../experiments/namur_cassel_armistice_requests/sources/p181_reviewed.png) · [Exact inputs](../../experiments/namur_cassel_armistice_requests/inputs.json) · [Position-by-position certificates](../../experiments/namur_cassel_armistice_requests/certificates.json)

The unchanged published keys are `Nov10-12`, `Nov13-15b`. The [earlier unreviewed candidates](../../experiments/namur_cassel_armistice_requests/prior_candidates.json) and [original OCR records](../../experiments/namur_cassel_armistice_requests/ocr_snapshot.json) are preserved. The present work supplies an image-reviewed source edition and a reproducible repair account; it does not claim that every body is a first public decipherment.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Coordinate substitutions | Source-mask fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [p172 C1](#p172-c1) | 116 | 58 / 58 | 1 | 0 |
| [p172 C3](#p172-c3) | 84 | 42 / 42 | 0 | 0 |
| [p180 E](#p180-e) | 224 | 110 / 112 | 3 | 0 |
| [p181 B](#p181-b) | 234 | 116 / 117 | 3 | 1 |

## p172 C1

**Source transcription — header:** `C) SY v ZM (13.40 p.m., November 10th); 1412 3 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-116`

**Readable German** — based on the explicitly repaired output below.

> Major Kroeger. GHQU. Soeben mit RXABLASS Namur eingetroffen.

**Meaning:** The first surviving part names Major Kroeger and reports a recent arrival at Namur. The opening may address Kroeger, so the arriving person is not securely identified. GHQU and RXABLASS remain opaque labels. The surviving third part closes with Hpt. Mannstaedt, and the source explicitly marks part 2 as missing.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
MAJORKROEGERXGHQUXIOEBENXMITXXRXABLASSXNAMURXEINGETROFFENX
```

**Edited output** — 1 observed-coordinate substitution and 0 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
MAJORKROEGERXGHQUXSOEBENXMITXXRXABLASSXNAMURXEINGETROFFENX
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The native 116-slot first part is complete. The source explicitly prints “2 TL (Missing)” before the separately preserved third part; no second part is supplied or counted.
- IOEBEN to SOEBEN is an explicitly priced lexical proposal. GHQU and RXABLASS remain literal and unexpanded; ABLASS is not asserted to be a person's name. The opening could be an address, and no arriving subject is supplied.
- The printed time is 13.40 p.m. and is retained without conversion. No historical identity beyond the literal surname KROEGER is inferred.

## p172 C3

**Source transcription — header:** `C) SY v ZM (13.40 p.m., November 10th); 1412 3 TLE; 3 TL RICHI-84`

**Readable German** — based on the unchanged raw output.

> Erbitten hierueber Bescheid. Hpt. Mannstaedt.

**Meaning:** The surviving third part asks for a response on the preceding matter and closes with the literal signature Hpt. Mannstaedt. The intervening second part is absent from the printed source.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
ERBITTENXHIERUEBERXBESCHEIDXHPTXMANNSTAEDT
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- All 84 printed coordinates decode without any observed substitution or mask fill. The earlier OCR block did not retain the complete native body.
- HPT is retained as the source abbreviation and the surname MANNSTAEDT is not expanded into a biographical identification.

## p180 E

**Source transcription — header:** `E) SY A v SY (10.09 p.m., November 12th); 10.45; RICHI-224`

**Readable German** — based on the explicitly repaired output below.

> Lt. Bauman. STATON sofort marschbereit 0 sein fuer M?TRANSPORT Cassel. Abtransport so schnell wie moeglich regeln. Kommandeur.

**Meaning:** The instruction addresses Lt. Bauman, calls for immediate readiness to move, and directs transport to Cassel to be arranged as quickly as possible. The spelling STATON and the literal fields 0 and M? TRANSPORT remain unresolved; the specific transport type is not identified.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
LTXBAUMANXSTATONSOFORTXMARSCHBERECT0SEINFUERXM?TRANSPORTXCASSELXABTRANSPORTSOSCHNELSWIEMOEGLICHRE?ELNXKOMMANDEUR
```

**Edited output** — 3 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
LTXBAUMANXSTATONSOFORTXMARSCHBEREIT0SEINFUERXM?TRANSPORTXCASSELXABTRANSPORTSOSCHNELLWIEMOEGLICHREGELNXKOMMANDEUR
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The source contains 224 slots, including all final groups; no coordinate is inserted, removed or moved.
- STATON is retained without inserting the absent I of STATION. BAUMAN remains the literal surname with one terminal N.
- MARSCHBERECT0 to MARSCHBEREIT0, SCHNELS to SCHNELL and RE?ELN to REGELN are separately priced lexical changes. The literal 0 is not silently changed into a separator.
- The Nov13–15b published key is used because it yields the demonstrated reading; the printed November 12 date is retained as a different evidence layer.
- The unknown position in M?TRANSPORT comes from an unresolved square cell and remains globally coupled. Its label is not chosen from historical expectations.

## p181 B

**Source transcription — header:** `B) LP v NKJ (01.00 a.m., November 12th); 23.10 (12/11); RICHI-234`

**Readable German** — based on the explicitly repaired output below.

> An OHL. OKM und AOK11. Erbitten nochmals Mitteilung der besonderen Waffenstillstandsbedingungen fuer hiesigen Kriegsschauplatz.

**Meaning:** The sender again asks OHL, OKM and the literal addressee AOK11 for the specific armistice conditions applying to the local theater of operations. The text is a request for information, not the conditions themselves.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
ANXOHLXXOKMXUNDAOK11XERBITTENNOCHMALSMITTEILU?GDERBESONDERENXWAFFENS2ILLSTAXDSBEDINGUNGENFQERHIESIGENKRIEGSSCHAUPLATZ
```

**Edited output** — 3 observed-coordinate substitutions and 1 source-mask fill; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
ANXOHLXXOKMXUNDAOK11XERBITTENNOCHMALSMITTEILUNGDERBESONDERENXWAFFENSTILLSTANDSBEDINGUNGENFUERHIESIGENKRIEGSSCHAUPLATZ
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The printed source has one non-coordinate glyph O in OADDG. It occupies a source slot, is masked in the raw model, and is filled explicitly for MITTEILUNG.
- The lexical proposals WAFFENS2ILLSTAXDS to WAFFENSTILLSTANDS and FQER to FUER are priced observed-coordinate changes. The raw numeral-like 2 remains available in the exact raw layer.
- Both header times and the separate 12/11 line remain literal. The label AOK11 is not used to prove a historical unit identification.

## Evidence and credit

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates replay every coordinate alteration, compare the independent column/domain reconstruction with the cipher implementation, and re-encrypt every complete edited output. For a partial output, an injective global completion of the square and residual source masks supplies an explicitly nonhistorical roundtrip witness. Each readable passage preserves every nonseparator output label; literal protected fields are also checked without removing their internal separators. Source crops are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and RGB-pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/namur_cassel_armistice_requests/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to regenerate and compare the delivered source pixels.

A roundtrip proves compatibility with a stated reading. Editorial spelling repairs remain proposals, and literal number labels are not automatically historical dates, quantities or reference numbers.

# Demobilization at Neuhof, south of Fulda

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and recovery: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The opening of this three-part telegram directs a Flak unit, whose number
remains unresolved, toward demobilization at **Neuhof, south of Fulda**.
The middle part now supports a conditional continuation naming the Hanau–Fulda
line, enclosures 1 and 2, and formations undergoing demobilization within a
deputy command's district. The final part explicitly directs the relevant
field-army items to Neuhof.

The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
[printed p228, PDF p231](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [preserved section](../../experiments/neuhof_demobilization/sources/p228_B.png)
appears under `30th NOVEMBER, 1918.` with the header:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
B) ZON v BSL (01.33 a.m., December 1st)
NO 152 1512 3 TLE
```

</details>

All three parts use the unchanged published `Nov28-Dec1` square and ranks.
The source edition retains raw `Y` separators, numeral labels and rare
letters. The separate shared interpretation below supplies part of B1's
numerical fields.

## B1: the destination instruction

The first part advertises `RICHI-246` and has exactly **246 slots**, including
six printed dashes. Its earlier OCR stream had 241 coordinates and did not
produce a coherent reading. The visual transcription gives:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
0OKXXYYZUMERLYVJXYXXZX4NRP680YX4GEHYAY3YANLGYXLF?YNRYX4SPALTE9FLAKABTEILUNG?0WIRDNI?L3NDARMJT?DTSONDERNINYNEU?OFYSUEDHFUL?A
```

</details>

Five observed-coordinate substitutions and five fills of printed dashes give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
AOKXXYYZUMERLYVJXYXXZX4NRP680YX4GEHYAY3YANLGYXLFDYNRYX4SPALTE9FLAKABTEILUNG?0WIRDNICHINDARMSTADTSONDERNINYNEUHOFYSUEDLFULDA
```

</details>

The ordinary body names a Flak unit and places its destination at Neuhof,
south of Fulda, with Darmstadt appearing in the negative part of the
instruction. It retains the shortened `NICHIN`: the expected German phrase
would normally contain `NICHT IN`, but no `T` is inserted into the fixed
source frame. The Flak unit field remains `?0`. Its number, the order
number, date-like fields and column-reference label remain uninterpreted.

The [joint calendar and unit interpretation](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/README.md)
adds `GA=0` and `VG=7`, fixing three more numeral positions without additional
source changes:

| Field | Published-key labels | Joint interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Order reference | `P680` | **P067** |
| Flak unit field | `?0` | **?7** |

This interpreted layer fixes **120/123 positions**. The leading unit character
remains an erasure, and two other fields retain the shared `4/5` ambiguity.
The body continues into the middle part with the demobilization wording.

## B2: the demobilization continuation

The [current B2 edition](p228_demobilization_fragment.md) reaches **125/132
positions** through a conditional relocation of five printed mask slots,
word proposals and two shared-reference transfers from B1. It preserves all
221 observed coordinates in their original relative order. Five observed
substitutions and 36 mask fills support the combined reading; seven positions,
including the command field and the prefix before `CKFORMATIONEN`, remain
unresolved.

<details>
<summary>Earlier native-frame opening</summary>

The second part advertises `RICHI-264` and has **264 slots**, including
**43 printed dashes**. Its direct label reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
A?ST??CKE?ANK?FUL?AD1?OBI?G5D??HT?I1??CHA?LL??UJD5S1??Y26U03??GEHX0Z??MBEDES??DESIT7???YYADA???MX8A8???OBPL2???ENREN???CKS?R???I4CEH
```

</details>

The proposed original-language span is limited to **positions 0-32**:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — partial proposed span only; positions 0–32:**

```text
ANSTRECKEHANAUFULDADEMOBILGEMACHT
```

</details>

It says “demobilized on the Hanau-Fulda line.” This is a conditional
editorial reconstruction requiring **five observed-coordinate changes and
ten erasure fills**. It joins the preceding location instruction coherently,
but its exact wording is not independently witnessed. All changes are
confined to these 33 plaintext positions.

The remaining **99 positions** retain their source-derived labels and
domains for later work. No original wording is proposed for that remainder,
and the label count below does not turn it into a recovered body.

</details>

## B3: routing to Neuhof

The source heading is literally **`RICHI-196?`**. Counting the received
groups gives **186 slots**, including one printed dash. The edition uses
that actual 186-slot frame and preserves the questioned header length.
It does not insert ten hypothetical coordinates. Its direct reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DESFELDHEERESSINDDAHERNICHTNACHDAR?SADTSONDERNNACHNEUHOFZULEITENYCMTRUPPENDEPY3025YXXYX4YAY3Y
```

</details>

Filling the one printed dash at source index **15**, group **4**, coordinate
**1**, with `X` gives:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
DESFELDHEERESSINDDAHERNICHTNACHDARMSADTSONDERNNACHNEUHOFZULEITENYCMTRUPPENDEPY3025YXXYX4YAY3Y
```

</details>

The final instruction says the relevant field-army items must therefore
be directed to Neuhof. The preceding plural subject lies in the unread
middle portion, so the edition does not invent a specific unit or equipment
category. The city string remains `DARMSADT`, without an added `T`.
The office label `CMTRUPPENDEP` and its numerical reference remain literal.

## Source accounting for the native-frame edition

| Part | Actual slots | Printed dashes | Raw fixed labels | Edition fixed labels | Known-coordinate changes | Erasure fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B1 | 246 | 6 | 117 / 123 | 122 / 123 | 5 | 5 |
| B2 | 264 | 43 | 89 / 132 | 99 / 132 | 5 | 10 |
| B3 | 186 | 1 | 92 / 93 | 93 / 93 | 0 | 1 |
| **Total** | **696** | **50** | **298 / 348** | **314 / 348** | **10** | **16** |

There are **no insertions, deletions, block moves or changes to the period
key**. The 314 fixed labels include untouched, uninterpreted values in B2's
unread remainder. The [certificate](../../experiments/neuhof_demobilization/certificates.json)
lists every repair, its source and plaintext positions, and every numeral
or `J/Q/Y` occurrence, including those changed by explicitly priced
ordinary-word repairs. This is not a silent numerical substitution.

The [inputs](../../experiments/neuhof_demobilization/inputs.json) preserve all
manual rows, headers, image hashes and the limited middle-part template.
Globally consistent source-fill witnesses prove arithmetic consistency of
the partial readings. Their arbitrary erased-coordinate values are
explicitly marked as nonhistorical witnesses.

The published key is credited to **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**, [2016, DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461).
B3 had already appeared as an unreviewed OCR-derived candidate. The present
work adds the exact source edition, the readable opening instruction and
the separately limited middle proposal. No explicit p228 B example was
located in the bounded author-paper, supplementary-reading and catalog
check; no universal first-decipherment claim is made.

```sh
python experiments/neuhof_demobilization/verify.py --verify
```

# The Danube field report: two companion parts, 10–11 November

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and exact repair audit: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs printed p176 B, PDF p179, labels a three-part message
`LP v ZÖN (3.38 a.m., November 11th); 2305 (10) 3 TLE`.
Its first part is the existing [p176b challenge](../p176b.md), credited
to **Prinz and GPT-6 Astra, 19 September 2026**. The two parts below
complete the source-labeled sequence; they do not solve the first
part's reconstructed 20-coordinate shortage or unknown unit digits.
Only these two physical records are new catalog entries.

These texts report French forces, a Danube crossing near the literal
place-name `RUSTUK`, and reserves north of `SLOBOZIE`. The edition treats
those statements as the sender's report; it does not independently
establish that the reported movements occurred. The two parts retain
their native source lengths and the unchanged published **Nov10–12**
square and ranks.

## p176 B2

The [252-coordinate source](../../experiments/nov10_delegates_and_field_report/sources/p176_B2.png)
directly reads:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FEHERTEMPLOMXFOLGENFRANZOSENXXBESATZUNSHEERXFEINDVORFUEHLTEGEGENNEUESTELLUNGENDONAUKNIEXSAMVITXNACHAGENTENSTARKMITENGLAEN?ERNX
```

</details>

A single observed-coordinate replacement gives:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
FEHERTEMPLOMXFOLGENFRANZOSENXXBESATZUNSHEERXFEINDVORFUEHLTEGEGENNEUESTELLUNGENDONAUKNIEXSAMVITXNACHAGENTENSTARKMITENGLAENDERNX
```

</details>

The final word becomes `ENGLAENDERN`, in a report attributed to agents.
The source-derived `BESATZUNSHEER`, unusual order `FEINDVORFUEHLTE`, and
`SAMVIT` remain untouched. No extra letter is inserted into the first
word, no phrase is reordered, and no place-name is silently modernized.

The original question mark is pair `FD`, whose domain is **56789** in
the partial square. Source coordinate **108** changes **F→G**, turning
that pair into a known `D`. This is an explicit ciphertext repair, not
a fill of an erased coordinate or an assignment of an unknown key cell.

## p176 B3

The [272-coordinate source](../../experiments/nov10_delegates_and_field_report/sources/p176_B3.png)
directly reads:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
MAROKANERNBELEG1XXSISTOWXZUGVERKEHRXXBEIXRUS2UKXSETZTENFRANZOSENRUMAENISCHUFERUEBERXXRESERVENBRACHTENSNENOERDLNCHXSLOBOZIEXZUMSTEHENXOKM
```

</details>

Four observed-coordinate replacements give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
MAROKANERNBELEGTXXSISTOWXZUGVERKEHRXXBEIXRUSTUKXSETZTENFRANZOSENRUMAENISCHUFERUEBERXXRESERVENBRACHTENSIENOERDLICHXSLOBOZIEXZUMSTEHENXOKM
```

</details>

This part mentions Moroccan troops and train traffic at `SISTOW`, then
reports French forces crossing to the Romanian bank near `RUSTUK` and
being stopped by reserves north of `SLOBOZIE`. Its opening depends on
the preceding part for context; no missing introductory phrase is
supplied. The spellings `MAROKANERN`, `RUSTUK`, `RUMAENISCHUFER` and
`SLOBOZIE` are left exactly as the candidate decodes.

The enlarged [five-letter group](../../experiments/nov10_delegates_and_field_report/sources/p176_B3_group.png)
confirms `VDVAV`. There is no source deletion or uncertain final frame.
The four replacements change `BELEG1`, `RUS2UK`, `SNE` and `NOERDLNCH`
as displayed. Both numerical-looking pre-repair labels remain in the
certificate; no global interpretation of `1` or `2` is imposed.

## Scope and attribution

These two parts total **524 observed coordinates**, **262 plaintext
positions**, **261 raw fixed labels**, and **262 candidate fixed labels**.
Their cost is **five observed-coordinate substitutions**, with no
coordinate fill, loss model, deletion or key change. All candidate
characters re-encrypt to the exact explicitly repaired streams.

Earlier unreviewed whole-corpus screening already produced readable
bodies for both parts. The contribution here is source transcription,
the complete coordinate and domain ledger, and verification of the
parts' printed relationship. A bounded review of the paper, thesis
and cached comments found no separate explicit discussion of these
two bodies; that absence does not establish historical priority.

The report shares geographical context with the already reviewed
Nov9 operational messages and the Nov3 Mackensen report. It is not
presented as an exact copy of either. The old p176b unit interpretation
also remains an independent conditional layer.

[Inputs](../../experiments/nov10_delegates_and_field_report/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/nov10_delegates_and_field_report/certificates.json)
and [verification instructions](../../experiments/nov10_delegates_and_field_report/README.md)
provide the literal source rows, all edits, historical-credit checks,
and the source-header crop.

# November 11: Romanian mobilization and a crossing report

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

The surviving second part on printed page 180 reports mobilization and a crossing. Its last line is followed by **“(jammed to end)”**. The source contains **235 printed slots**, including two dashes, under a **RICHI-240** header. Keeping every printed slot and appending five unknown coordinates produces a conditional 240-coordinate frame with **110 of 120 plaintext positions fixed** under the unchanged published Nov10–12 key.

Six narrow word proposals raise that count to **116 of 120**. They cost **four observed-coordinate substitutions, one printed-mask fill and four fills of added tail slots**. The remaining source dash, first added tail slot and two linked occurrences of an unknown square cell stay unresolved. Date-like fields, the shortened **KRIEGSZUSAND** and the literal **ZIMNICA** are preserved. This is a partial source edition of one surviving part; the absent first part and a unique original transmission are not reconstructed.

Research and editorial work: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The period key is credited to George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker, with its publication details retained in [inputs.json](../../experiments/nov11_romanian_mobilization_report/inputs.json). Earlier local native and terminal-mask trials already exposed this lead. Their transcription and reproducible outputs are retained in [prior_candidates.json](../../experiments/nov11_romanian_mobilization_report/prior_candidates.json); this edition does not claim first-decipherment priority.


**Reviewed source crops:** [p180_B2_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov11_romanian_mobilization_report/sources/p180_B2_reviewed.png) · [p180_D1_header_comparison.png](../../experiments/nov11_romanian_mobilization_report/sources/p180_D1_header_comparison.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).
## Conditional shared digits

The mobilization report gains the order date **9 November** and the linked **9 Uhr abends**, taking the existing edited layer from **116/120 to 118/120**. Decree 3179 is dated 27 October, one day before the poster’s first mobilization day of 28 October / 10 November. Identifying the report’s order with this decree selects the 9 branch. The two remaining masks and all prior source repairs remain explicit. The [joint reconstruction](../../experiments/nov10_joint_completion/README.md) combines the earlier Marineamt and formation interpretations with the army-number constraint and the mobilization decree; the reversed 7/9 assignment is retained there.

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the joint square:**

> Rumaen. Mobilmachung 9.11. angeordnet. 1. Tag 10 ?1L. Kriegszusand 10 1T, 9 Uhr abends. Feind 1? 11 Turnumagurele Zimnica uebergesetzt.

<details>
<summary>Exact conditional labels</summary>

**Edited output — p180_B2, conditional shared square; 118/120 fixed positions:**

```text
RUMAENXMOBILMACHUNG9X11XANGEORDNETXX1XTAG10X?1LXKRIEGSZUSAND10X1TX9UHRABENDSXFEIND1?X11XTURNUMAGURELEZIMNICAUEBERGESETZT
```

</details>


## p180 B2

Literal header: `B) LP v ZON (0[1/4].02 p.m. November 11th); -----; 2 TL RICHI-240`.

The damaged hour glyph remains ambiguous between `01.02` and `04.02`. The older OCR reads 01.02. An enlarged comparison with the same page’s clear 4 in the D1 header does not decisively exclude either reading. The complete alternatives are `B) LP v ZON (01.02 p.m. November 11th); -----; 2 TL RICHI-240` and `B) LP v ZON (04.02 p.m. November 11th); -----; 2 TL RICHI-240`. Neither is selected by the body’s date or hour fields.

[Printed page 180, B2 and its terminal-jamming note — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov11_romanian_mobilization_report/inputs.json)

[The neighboring D1 header used only for glyph comparison — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov11_romanian_mobilization_report/inputs.json) is not a second recovered body in this edition.

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — all 235 native printed slots, including both dashes:**

```text
GVGDA GAAFD GXGVA XVXAX ADXFX XGXGX GDXXG XDDXG
AAVVV VFXXD XGXFD XDVXV GVAGA GFGAV AADFF DAAXX
XXDGG XXADG AFDAA AAAGD GAADX VDDDX FDXAD XFVAX
ADAAV XDDAV DAADA DAAAG ADXAD AGFVA GFXXV XFDXX
DGFDD FAGDX DVGVX XVGXF XAXDV AGXDX XDDFG XGGDA
--AVG GAVAV XDXFX XFFFF XVGXV AGXVG GVGAD
```

**Separate contextual record:** [p217 A2](p217_A.md) directly decodes `OROSHAZA` in a later report without coordinate repairs. That occurrence supports recognizing the geographical name; it does not establish that the two reports refer to the same unit, the same position or the same event. It does not reduce any of the p215 edits above or verify the other proposed place names. The baseline unit label `2RXD` remains literal here; the separate numeral interpretation discussed in that older case is not imported into this edition.

![Page date heading](../../experiments/southern_hungary_positions_part2/sources/p215_date_heading.png)

The [input](../../experiments/southern_hungary_positions_part2/inputs.json) binds each literal source to exact PDF crops. The [certificate](../../experiments/southern_hungary_positions_part2/certificates.json) contains the raw paired-coordinate domains, each source change and the forward checks. The [verifier](../../experiments/southern_hungary_positions_part2/verify.py) checks the unchanged published keys and the live German quotations, retaining all numerical and letter labels.

Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro (2026). Childs supplies the historical collection; published reconstruction and key provenance credit Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker. number is assigned. The question marks are unresolved positions.

The source prints 204 slots, including 21 masks. It genuinely repeats `FXXXF`
at source indices 45–49 and 50–54. The conditional frame excludes the first
copy and inserts five unknown slots before retained-stream index 12. No
cancellation mark is printed, and neither operation is an established
