# Reduced provisioning strength and a separate evening report

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Two physically numbered parts request a complete stop to provisions after
a reduction in the strength being provisioned. The existing shared-square
interpretation identifies their army field as **11th Army**. Their association
is explicit across the p219/p220 page break. A separate evening report on
p220 now supports **Tiszafoeldvar, Nagymagocs and Kondoros** as places reached,
while its unit labels remain incomplete. All three retain their complete
native printed frames.

## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p219 excerpt](../../experiments/nov25_provisions_and_evening_report/sources/p219_reviewed.png) · [Reviewed p220 excerpt](../../experiments/nov25_provisions_and_evening_report/sources/p220_reviewed.png) · [Inputs](../../experiments/nov25_provisions_and_evening_report/inputs.json) · [Position and change certificates](../../experiments/nov25_provisions_and_evening_report/certificates.json)

The original editions use the published `Nov25-28` key. The later shared-square interpretation and witnessed place repair are separately priced below. [Original OCR records](../../experiments/nov25_provisions_and_evening_report/ocr_snapshot.json) and [reproducible comparisons with that earlier evidence](../../experiments/nov25_provisions_and_evening_report/prior_candidates.json) are preserved separately. The present edition supplies checked source framing, exact costs and readable passages; it makes no first-public-decipherment claim.

The earlier published-label editions have the following source accounts.
The later Tiszafoeldvar proposal adds one substitution to p220 B only.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [p219 D1](#p219-d1) | 166 | 83 / 83 | 3 | 0 |
| [p220 A2](#p220-a2) | 244 | 122 / 122 | 2 | 0 |
| [p220 B](#p220-b) | 220 | 110 / 110 | 1 | 0 |

## p219 D1

**Source transcription — header:** `D) UKS v ZÖN (10.11 p.m., November 25th); 1849 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-166`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
INFOLGEVERRINGERTERXVERPFLEGUNGSSTAERKEFUERJJXARMEEKEINEVERPFLEGNNGFEHRERFOGDERLICH
```

**Edited output — 3 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
INFOLGEVERRINGERTERXVERPFLEGUNGSSTAERKEFUERJJXARMEEKEINEVERPFLEGUNGMEHRERFORDERLICH
```

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Infolge verringerter Verpflegungsstaerke fuer JJ. Armee keine Verpflegung mehr erforderlich.

</details>

**Conditional interpretation — existing shared FX=1 interpretation and the same three word repairs:**

> Infolge verringerter Verpflegungsstaerke fuer 11. Armee keine Verpflegung mehr erforderlich.

**Meaning:** Under the existing shared-square interpretation, the message
states that the 11th Army's reduced provisioning strength makes further
provisions unnecessary. The next part requests an immediate, complete
halt to further supplies.

The two original `FX` pairs at plaintext positions 43–44 come from
source **10 F + 83 X** and **53 F + 133 X**. Neither was touched by the
three word repairs. Their `11` reading follows the already supported
`FX=1` assignment; this passage introduces no new numeral choice or
source change. The [separate follow-up certificate](../../experiments/nov25_evening_place_witness/certificate.json)
checks both pairs and the complete current quotation.

**Editorial limits.**

- All 166 observed coordinates are present, including the final printed VGGXA F omitted by the earlier 160-coordinate OCR block. Restoring those visible coordinates is a transcription correction, not a hypothetical lost-prefix or missing-slot fill.
- The word proposals VERPFLEGNNG → VERPFLEGUNG, FEHR → MEHR and ERFOGDERLICH → ERFORDERLICH have explicit observed-coordinate costs. All raw garbles remain displayed.
- JJ remains literal in both earlier label streams above. The separately certified shared-square interpretation supplies 11 in the current reading; no headcount or additional key assignment is inferred.
- The printed continued marker, identical UKS/ZÖN routing, 10.11 p.m. interception, 1849 internal reference and 2 TLE count associate this first part with p220 A2. The source changes its section label from D to A across the page break.

## p220 A2

**Source transcription — header:** `A) UKS v ZÖN (10.11 p.m., November 25th); 1849 2 TLE; 2 TL RICHI-244`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
BITTENACHSCHUBANVERPFLEGUNGSOFOR3GANZEINSTELLENXGLEICHESTELEGRAMMGEHTANGENENALINTENDANTUNDPROVIANTDEPOTDRESDENXXVIERAXU203
```

**Edited output — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
BITTENACHSCHUBANVERPFLEGUNGSOFORTGANZEINSTELLENXGLEICHESTELEGRAMMGEHTANGENERALINTENDANTUNDPROVIANTDEPOTDRESDENXXVIERAXU203
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Bitte Nachschub an Verpflegung sofort ganz einstellen. Gleiches Telegramm geht an Generalintendant und Proviantdepot Dresden. VIERA. U203.

**Meaning:** The continuation requests an immediate, complete halt to further provisions and states that the same telegram goes to the Generalintendant and the provisions depot at Dresden. It records a request and notification, without proving that deliveries actually stopped. The closing labels VIERA and U203 remain unexpanded.

**Editorial limits.**

- The complete native 244-coordinate body matches its header. Two earlier OCR blocks split this one physical source part; neither block alone gives its full geometry.
- SOFOR3 → SOFORT and GENENALINTENDANT → GENERALINTENDANT are separately priced ordinary-word proposals, with no global reinterpretation of the 3 label.
- VIERA and U203 remain literal closing fields. They are not silently converted to an office, a personal name, a number or an expanded date.
- The source explicitly marks this as part 2 and repeats the p219 D header. Its association with that first part is supported by printed metadata as well as the continued marker, not solely by similar meaning.

## p220 B

**Source transcription — header:** `B) UKS v ZÖN (09.54 p.m., November 25th); HATTE MR 20[4-like]7; RICHI-220`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
ABENDMELDUNG13XJJ22ALPEXKX16X1ZUIGEXESHABE7MITANFAENGENERREICHT1J0IDXTISHAFOELDVARXPRDXNAGQMAGOCS81J8XKONDOROS
```

**Edited output — 1 observed-coordinate substitution and 0 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
ABENDMELDUNG13XJJ22ALPEXKX16X1ZUIGEXESHABENMITANFAENGENERREICHT1J0IDXTISHAFOELDVARXPRDXNAGQMAGOCS81J8XKONDOROS
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Abendmeldung 13. JJ22 ALPE. K. 16. 1 ZUIGE. Es haben mit Anfaengen erreicht: 1J0ID, TISHAFOELDVAR. PRD, NAGQMAGOCS81J8. KONDOROS.

**Meaning:** The recoverable clause in this separate evening report states
that leading elements had reached the following listed entries. This earlier
label-based display preserves its unit, time-like and garbled place labels;
the two separate place readings below have additional evidence.

### A shared letter identifies Nagymágocs

The later [shared `AD=Y` interpretation](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/README.md#the-shared-y-in-strzemieczny-and-nagymagocs)
turns `NAGQMAGOCS` into **`NAGYMAGOCS`**. At plaintext position 90,
the pair comes from the originally observed **A at source 74 and D at
source 180**. This is the same cell that completes Strzemieczny's surname
in p224 C1; neither name requires an added source-coordinate repair.

The place spelling is independently printed in *Csongrád vármegye
Hivatalos Lapja*, **21 December 1912**, no. 59, p349, items 86–89, in
the municipality's proposed 1913 budgets.
[National-library scan](https://epa.hu/05200/05279/00539/pdf/EPA05279_csongradvarmegye_hivatalos_lapja_1912_059.pdf)
· [Masthead](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/sources/csongrad_1912_title.png)
· [Nagymágocs entries](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/sources/nagymagocs_1912.png).
The newly identified place is one location that leading elements
reportedly reached; the adjacent unit labels remain unresolved. The other
damaged place has the separate native witness described next.
The gazette supplies a geographical spelling, not a separate account
of the reported military movement.

### A native place witness under a different key

The November 30 evening report [p229 A1](late_transport_dispatches.md)
directly reads **`TISZAFOELDVAR`** at positions 41–53, using 26 untouched
observed coordinates under its different Nov28–Dec1 key. Its Z is `VX`,
from source 219 V and 148 X. That native spelling supports the earlier
`TISHAFOELDVAR` place repair.

In p220 B, H at position 72 comes from `AA`, source 6 and 150. The
proposed change **6 A→D**, retaining source 150 A, gives `DA=Z`.
The original image visibly has A; this is an observed-coordinate repair,
not a corrected transcription. The older `HABE7→HABEN` repair at source
157 remains separate, for **two total observed substitutions**, no fills
and the unchanged 220-coordinate frame.

**Conditional interpretation — shared Y and the witnessed place spelling, with unit labels retained:**

> Es haben mit Anfaengen erreicht: 21?ID, Tiszafoeldvar. PRD, Nagymagocs. ?21?, Kondoros.

This makes the place list readable as Tiszafoeldvar, Nagymagocs and
Kondoros while preserving its incomplete unit labels. The donor is a
separate later report, not a duplicate reception; it supports the
spelling without establishing this report's unit identities or movements.
The [cross-key place check](../../experiments/nov25_evening_place_witness/README.md)
prices all 98 possible starts of that spelling in the native recipient
frame. Position 69 is the only one-substitution minimum for this fixed
word and frame. The conditional fixed-position count stays **103/110**:
H was already observed, so this repair does not recover an erased position.

**Editorial limits.**

- All 220 observed coordinates remain in their native order. The earlier primary word proposal HABE7 → HABEN is priced as an observed-coordinate change, not as a free reading of a numeral; the new place repair adds one separately recorded change.
- 13, JJ22ALPE, K, 16, 1ZUIGE, 1J0ID, TISHAFOELDVAR, PRD, NAGQMAGOCS81J8 and KONDOROS keep their exact labels. Word spacing in the opening is editorial and does not establish its syntax or reference values.
- The original edition supplies no unit number or geographical correction. Its TISHAFOELDVAR and NAGQMAGOCS remain in the exact label stream. The separate shared-Y interpretation and one-coordinate witnessed repair identify those two places in the current reading.
- The HATTE MR heading contains a 4-like glyph rendered as [4-like] in the metadata. This is a header transcription qualification and does not add a source-ciphertext erasure or a decoded position.
- B has its own source label and reception time. It is not counted as a third part of the two-part provisioning message above.

## Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates independently reconstruct column positions and domains, compare them with the cipher implementation, replay every priced change, and check all readable nonseparator labels. Partial readings have one consistent injective square/source-mask completion witness that re-encrypts exactly; those witness choices are not historical identifications. Source images are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/nov25_provisions_and_evening_report/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to check the original PDF and exact source-crop pixels.

# November 30: aviation march destinations

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Printed **p228 A** reports proposed march destinations for an aviation staff and a numerically limited army aviation park. Its native body has **384 occupied slots**, although the questioned advertised count is **RICHI-374?**. A conditional 374-coordinate frame yields a largely readable body. Seven observed-coordinate substitutions and four printed-mask fills support the proposed word reading.

The ten-coordinate exclusion is a substantive model choice. All **ten** equally priced contiguous placements remain in the evidence. The primary representation removes two complete printed groups and preserves the source’s repetitions in the native layer; it does not establish how the surplus arose historically.

Research and editorial work: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The published Nov28–Dec1 key retains the credit of George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker. Earlier source surveys and OCR retain their attribution; no first historical decipherment is claimed.

## p228 A

Page heading: **30th NOVEMBER, 1918.** The reception header is dated **December 1st**; both dates remain literal.

Literal header: `A) ZÖN v BSL (01.00 a.m., December 1st); --------; RICHI-374?`.

The original source crop was reviewed locally. [inputs.json](../../experiments/nov30_aviation_march_destination/inputs.json) pins the original PDF, page 231, crop rectangle, render scale, dimensions and RGB digest. **Reviewed source crops:** [p228_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov30_aviation_march_destination/sources/p228_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify). `--pdf` verifies those pixels; ordinary verification explicitly reports that no source-pixel comparison was performed.

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — all 384 native slots, including all repeated groups and five non-coordinate glyphs:**

```text
VGXFV VGXXV -XVVG VGXXV XVVXG -AVFF XVDDD GFDVX
VDFVV DXVVA VVMFX AAMDX FGDFV DXVGX AGAGG GDFFG
VGFDD FFGFG GXXGV DFVFF GGDVG GAAVA FGVVV FF-FV
VFVGV GGAVF VFXXV XVVVX VXVXA DVVXG XDVGF DGADA
VFDVF FVDGF VDDVD XGVAG AVDVX GFFDG AADDD XXXFF
GGVVD XAXXV VXVGG FXGGX ADFXD GFVDD AFGGF GGDDF
FAXDX XFDDG XXVFD FVAGA FDFAV DVXXV VAFFA DGFFA
FADAD XGDAF DXXVG AXVFD DDDGA GAFVD FFGXD FAVFG
XFDXG DVXDF FDFVX AXAGV GXGGD VGXAA GFVVA XVFXD
VGGDD AGVXX XXDVA VXVGX XVDA
```

</details>

Source indices **10, 25, 52, 57 and 117** contain **-, -, M, M, -**. They remain occupied source slots and become coordinate masks in analysis. The first row includes VGXXV twice, with -XVVG between the two copies; neither repetition is removed from this transcription. The final group has four coordinates, XVDA.

## Native and conditional raw layers

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — all 384 source slots under the unchanged Nov28–Dec1 key:**

```text
FXLBR1JE5C?G6RU4FHPLXUJSS3A0O3XI?7U49XZZMAIMYVV03DKTTHVX1XZLAE7K6KHFKXRS?NF0CVD0AQ5TW2E?ZSLKW8UKQ418FAC0COF2R8ME8EAT8UR4MMSNRLBESHZRSERVANH0E0EMZDDGLEAKSHRWBDBJ0NAZMIAMXAHNA?WR6KBSQD0JN2EO7RKK
```

</details>

The native frame has **192 plaintext positions**, of which **187** have fixed labels. Those labels do not form a readable whole; fixing a label under a chosen key is distinct from confirming meaningful language.

For the primary conditional frame, exclude source interval **[5,15)**: VGXXV followed by -XVVG. This removes **nine observed coordinate glyphs and one masked slot**. All remaining slots keep their printed order. No coordinate is inserted, and the column permutation is then applied at length **374**.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 374-coordinate frame, before any substitutions or mask fills:**

```text
?OFLXXYZUDORTXJ43YX4OPISTANKOGENLNFTGEDRATETXYMARSCHZIBLFUERSTABKOFLMACKYBUCKARESTJYMARSCHZYFUERZ0HLENMAEMMIG?ESCHRAENKTENARMEE?LUGPARKPLOEMTIYANDERBAHNKR?NSTADTBUCARESTYKOFLMACKYJYX4OPYY
```

</details>

This frame fixes **183/187 positions**. It already exposes the staff wording, most of the army aviation park wording, the railway reference and much of the closing. The raw wordforms GEDRATET and BUCKAREST remain unchanged below. **Y is the separator** for this key; X and XX remain literal labels throughout this edition.

## What the geometry search establishes

The search uses eight retrospective word spans at the offsets listed below. It does not constrain the references, other surrounding words or the entire proposed body. It prices observed-coordinate conflicts, recording mask fills and source exclusions separately.

All **375 contiguous ten-slot exclusions** were tested. The minimum is **seven observed substitutions**, at starts **4–13** inclusive. These are all retained, not just the six source maps yielding the primary ciphertext.

A second, narrower source-group model tests all **2,850 pairs of complete five-coordinate groups** among the first 76 groups. The final four-coordinate group is retained. Exactly two pairs attain the same seven-substitution minimum: zero-based groups **[1,2]** and **[2,3]**, corresponding to source intervals **[5,15)** and **[10,20)**. # Flying units: should they depart or remain?

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p124 section B contains a short inquiry about whether flying units
should leave or remain. The source prints **183 slots**, including **25
masked coordinates**, against an advertised **184**. A visibly short
four-slot group constrains the proposed missing coordinate, and a conditional
184-slot frame yields **92 plaintext positions, 67 fixed raw**.

The edited reading repairs ordinary words in the body while leaving the
entire opening reference untouched. It has **83/92 fixed positions** and
requires **2 observed-coordinate substitutions, 16 source-mask fills and 1
inserted-slot fill**. The published **Nov4–6** key stays unchanged. The two
equally priced local gap positions are both retained.


**Reviewed source crops:** [p124_B_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov4_flying_unit_inquiry/sources/p124_B_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).


heading is a separate source layer. The [literal input](../../experiments/nov4_flying_unit_inquiry/inputs.json)
preserves every dash and the invalid printed `U` in `GXXGU`.

The short **XFVV** group occupies source indices **15–18**. The displayed
frame inserts an unknown coordinate at **source boundary 17**, before
original source index 17. No source slot is removed or reordered.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Meaning:** The proposed body says that a communication is not understood
and asks whether flying units should depart by air or remain here. It does

| Added-slot fill | F at source boundary 17, model index 17 |
| Unfilled printed masks | 9, retained in the opening fragment |

All listed mask fills except source 58 fill printed dashes. Source 58 is the
invalid printed `U`, retained literally in the source transcript. The
certificate records each event with its original glyph, source index,

## Both local gap minima

The verifier compares all five insertion boundaries within or at the edges
of the visibly four-slot group, against the same partial edited template:

| Source boundary | Observed substitutions | Printed-mask fills | Added-slot fills |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 15 | 3 | 16 | 1 |
| 16 | 2 | 16 | 1 |
| 17 | 2 | 16 | 1 |
| 18 | 3 | 16 | 1 |
| 19 | 3 | 16 | 1 |

Boundaries **16 and 17 tie**. Both add F next to the already printed F,
producing the same edited ciphertext group **XFFVV** and the same edited
plaintext. Their unfilled raw frames differ because the unknown slot lies
on opposite sides of the observed F.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — equally priced boundary-16 alternative; 67/92 fixed positions:**

```text
??ERX?K??1?2??OP??ICHT?E??T?ENDLI??XXSOLLEN?LI?GER???EI?UNGEN?B?LIEGENX?DERHIERRLEIBENXFRAGE
```

</details>

The displayed boundary-17 frame is a presentation choice. The certificate
preserves both mappings and all five price comparisons. The comparison is
limited to this stated short-group family and fixed body proposal; it
neither proves a unique historical reading nor identifies the historical
stage at which the coordinate was lost.

## Source restoration, attribution and reproduction

Earlier repository OCR contained **178 slots**: it omitted the printed
last-row `---AV` group and misread or masked several observed coordinates.
The reviewed **183-slot transcription** restores those actual source marks.
Those machine-input corrections are separate from the one missing
coordinate hypothesized in `XFVV`.

J. Rives Childs's scan is the historical source. The period-key work of
George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker, Lasry's 2017 key list,
and earlier repository work retain their credit. The frozen earlier OCR
and recomputed unchanged-key output are available in
[prior candidates](../../experiments/nov4_flying_unit_inquiry/prior_candidates.json).

# Troop crossing in boats: a fragmentary November 6 report

[Case index](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The 192-slot section B on Childs p144 supports a short passage concerning troops crossing in boats and a routine no-further-events ending. Its opening, one intervening token and the location remain garbled. The edition retains those labels and gives a limited ordinary-word proposal with its exact source cost.


**Reviewed source crops:** [p144_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov6_boat_crossing_fragment/sources/p144_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).
## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed source excerpt — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov6_boat_crossing_fragment/inputs.json) · [Literal inputs](../../experiments/nov6_boat_crossing_fragment/inputs.json) · [Position and repair certificates](../../experiments/nov6_boat_crossing_fragment/certificates.json)

The published `Nov4-6` key is unchanged. [Earlier OCR evidence](../../experiments/nov6_boat_crossing_fragment/ocr_snapshot.json) and its [recomputed decode](../../experiments/nov6_boat_crossing_fragment/prior_candidates.json) are retained. This edition adds checked framing, explicit reading limits and a readable display; it makes no first-public-decipherment claim.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [p144 B](#p144-b) | 192 | 93 / 96 | 5 | 2 |

## p144 B

**Source transcription — header:** `B) UKS v ZON (---- November 7th); RICHI-192; page heading 6th NOVEMBER, 1918`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order:**

```text
SOCSTDENVU4RONEE4HEXXLUHLEGKU?GXUEBERSETZECVONTRUPPEIXINBOOJENBEIBRFIRBD9SONSTNI?HTS?ESENELICWES
```

**Edited output — 5 observed-coordinate substitutions and 2 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
SOCSTDENVU4RONEE4HEXXLUHLEGKU?GXUEBERSETZENVONTRUPPENXINBOOTENBEIBRFIRBD9SONSTNICHTSWESENTLICHES
```

</details>

**Readable German — the same nonseparator labels as the edited output:**

> SOCSTDENVU4RONEE4HE. LUHLEGKU?G. Uebersetzen von Truppen in Booten bei BRFIRBD9. Sonst nichts Wesentliches.

**Meaning:** The ordinary-word proposal describes troops crossing in boats and ends with nothing further of significance. The preceding 19-label field, the LUHLEGKU?G token and the place-like BRFIRBD9 remain uninterpreted; no particular river, town, formation or successful crossing is independently established.

### Editorial limits

- The proposal repairs only five ordinary-word labels and fills two source-mask coordinates; the exact coordinate cost is listed in the certificate. No source position or key cell is changed without pricing.
- The opening, the apparent reconnaissance token and the place-like string remain exactly as decoded. Their appearance in the readable display does not turn them into accepted German words.
- The date heading and November 7 intercept header are both retained. The adjacent p144 C1 aerial report is a separate physical record; thematic proximity does not join their plaintexts.
- The literal 4 and 9 labels in the opaque fields are retained. They are not relabeled as letters, separators or historical numbers to make an assumed geographical interpretation fit.

### Exact repair account

The five observed-coordinate changes repair `UEBERSETZEC` to `UEBERSETZEN`, `TRUPPEI` to `TRUPPEN`, `BOOJEN` to `BOOTEN`, and two letters in `?ESENELICWES` to `WESENTLICHES`. Two separate mask fills supply the `C` in `NI?HTS` and the initial `W` of the last word. The remaining `?` in `LUHLEGKU?G` is kept.

| Source index, zero-based | Printed | Proposed | Cost |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 17 | `D` | `X` | Observed-coordinate substitution |
| 66 | `F` | `X` | Observed-coordinate substitution |
| 72 | `D` | `X` | Observed-coordinate substitution |
| 78 | `F` | `G` | Observed-coordinate substitution |
| 85 | `V` | `X` | Observed-coordinate substitution |
| 65 | `-` | `D` | Source-mask fill |
| 190 | `-` | `A` | Source-mask fill |

The resulting proposal fixes **95 / 96** positions. Fixed labels in an opaque string are not the same as understood words. The primary reading adopts neither an expansion of the first line nor a particular town. A separately priced opening hypothesis follows below. The nearby [aerial-reconnaissance record](nov6_horse_loading_reconnaissance.md) remains separate.

### An independently attested closing formula

The unedited [p127 A3 aerial-reconnaissance report](nov4_march_air_reconnaissance.md)
contains the exact phrase **NICHTSWESENTLICHES** in fixed raw output.
The verifier independently decodes that source and maps its letters against
the proposed ending here. This supports the ending as a formula actually
present elsewhere in the collection; it does not identify these reports as
copies or as descriptions of the same event. It supplies no evidence for
the optional opening below.

### Optional reading of the opening, outside the primary totals

**Conditional interpretation — a separately priced lexical hypothesis:**

The nineteen-position opening could be read as **SONST DONAUFRONT RUHE**.
This is an ordinary-language proposal, not a reading independently supplied
by another copy. It changes seven output labels at **eight additional
observed-coordinate substitutions**. The full optional candidate therefore
costs **13 observed substitutions and the same 2 source-mask fills**, with
no frame or key change. It remains outside the primary totals.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — optional opening proposal; 13 observed substitutions, 2 source-mask fills; 95/96 fixed positions:**

```text
SONSTDONAUFRONTRUHEXXLUHLEGKU?GXUEBERSETZENVONTRUPPENXINBOOTENBEIBRFIRBD9SONSTNICHTSWESENTLICHES
```

</details>

**Readable German — optional opening, with the remaining opaque fields unchanged:**

> Sonst Donaufront Ruhe. LUHLEGKU?G. Uebersetzen von Truppen in Booten bei BRFIRBD9. Sonst nichts Wesentliches.

The additional source changes are **11 F→V, 46 F→V, 68 G→F, 92 F→X,
114 D→X, 148 X→A, 159 F→G and 182 X→D**. These are changes to observed
coordinates, not newly resolved square cells. Both raw 4 labels in the
opening are affected only within this explicit proposal; the primary raw
and edited streams retain them.

**Meaning — conditional on the optional opening:** The first clause would
say that the Danube front is otherwise quiet. This does not identify the
place-like BRFIRBD9, restore LUHLEGKU?G, link the adjacent reconnaissance
telegram into this one, or establish the military events as historical
facts. The exact cost makes this possible interpretation reviewable without
promoting it to the primary reading.

## Reproduction and credit

Run `python experiments/nov6_boat_crossing_fragment/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to check the original PDF and the exact rendered pixels of the preserved source excerpt.

The verifier reconstructs source-coordinate pairs, checks raw domains, replays all priced changes, verifies the readable display without dropping unresolved labels, and checks a global completion witness where required. Such a completion is mechanical evidence, not a historical guess.

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

# November 7: Danube crossings and short message reports

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Five telegrams on Childs pp. 152–153 report a Serbian attack near Belgrad,
Danube crossing traffic, a prescribed march line and short service messages.
The [p164 C1 parallel report](danube_arad_witnesses.md#p164-c1) supports three
word repairs and a conditional **219 I. D.** reading in [p153 B1](#p153-b1).
Its native unit label is `21B`.

The page-153 first and third parts have separate reception headers; their
second part is absent from this edition. The later fifth and sixth parts

# Gomel route derailment and station-train forwarding

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Two source editions concern railway operations: a freight-train derailment blocking both tracks on the proposed Gomel–Bachmatsch route, and a message about forwarding a station train and construction train to Group Winterfeld. The wagon count, train labels, abbreviations and office references remain literal.

## Conditional shared digits

The [Siegfried reference comparison](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) supplies one shared conditional assignment, XA=5 and VF=6, to both railway records.

### p155 D

**Readable German — conditional shared digits, with the existing source edition retained:**

> OK Mackensen. Morgenmeldung vom 7.11.18: Auf Strecke Gomel, Bachmatsch entgleiste ein Gueterzug. 25 Wagen zertruemmert. Beide Gleise sind gesperrt. Hrgr. Kiew. RM 1 A 7097 18.

Under the shared-reference assignment XA=5, the original pair at source 294/56 gives **25 wagons**, completing **158/158** labels. The opposite assignment gives 26. The earlier three observed substitutions and five mask fills are unchanged.

### p169 B

**Readable German — conditional shared digits, with the existing source edition retained:**

> NACHRUEBGEL. FECH wird beschleunigt Stationszug S1152 und Bauzug 1924 der Gruppe Winterfeld zufuehren. Nachchef 1B16616.

The same assignment gives **S1152** and **1B16616**, completing **112/112** labels from 108/112, with no source edit. The opposite assignment gives S1162 and 1B15515. NACHRUEBGEL and FECH remain unexpanded.


## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed page excerpt](../../experiments/nov7_derailment_and_trains/sources/p155_reviewed.png) · [Second source excerpt](../../experiments/nov7_derailment_and_trains/sources/p169_reviewed.png) · [Exact inputs](../../experiments/nov7_derailment_and_trains/inputs.json) · [Position-by-position certificates](../../experiments/nov7_derailment_and_trains/certificates.json)

The unchanged published keys are `Nov7-9`. The [earlier unreviewed candidates](../../experiments/nov7_derailment_and_trains/prior_candidates.json) and [original OCR records](../../experiments/nov7_derailment_and_trains/ocr_snapshot.json) are preserved. The present work supplies an image-reviewed source edition and a reproducible repair account; it does not claim that every body is a first public decipherment.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Coordinate substitutions | Source-mask fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [p155 D](#p155-d) | 316 | 152 / 158 | 3 | 5 |
| [p169 B](#p169-b) | 224 | 108 / 112 | 0 | 0 |

## p155 D

**Source transcription — header:** `D) NKJ v LP (3.55 p.m., November 7th); FUER UKS 1355; RICHI-316`

**Readable German** — based on the explicitly repaired output below.

> OK Mackensen. Morgenmeldung vom 7X11X18: Auf Strecke Gomel, Bachmatsch entgleiste ein Gueterzug. 2? Wagen zertruemmert. Beide Gleise sind gesperrt. Hrgr. Kiew RMX1XAX7097X18.

**Meaning:** A morning report addressed to Oberkommando Mackensen says a freight train derailed on the proposed Gomel–Bachmatsch route, that a quantity written 2? of wagons was wrecked, and that both tracks are blocked. The unresolved wagon-count label and final reference remain literal.

<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

- Correct source groups FVXDD and VXDVG each have five slots. Earlier OCR strings with repeated X coordinates are not treated as source evidence.

## p169 B

**Source transcription — header:** `B) ZM v SY (10.00 p.m., November 9th); 2245 (9/11); RICHI-224`

**Readable German** — based on the unchanged raw output.

> NACHRUEBGEL. FECH wird beschleunigt Stationszug S11?2 und Bauzug 1924 der Gruppe Winterfeld zufuehren. Nachchef 1B1??1?.

**Meaning:** The station train labelled S11?2 and construction train labelled 1924 are to be forwarded promptly to Group Winterfeld. The opening NACHRUEBGEL and FECH are preserved without forcing an expansion, and the train and office labels are not independently numbered.

<details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The reference 1B1??1? and the station-train field retain all coupled unassigned square cells. A global witness is provided without claiming literal historical digit values.

## Coupled wagon and train labels

The unresolved symbols are linked by the unchanged Nov7–9 square. All indices below are zero-based plaintext positions.

| Square cell | Source occurrences | Shared constraint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| XA | p155 D position 89; p169 B position 47 | The unknown in wagon label `2?` is the same label as the unknown in train label `S11?2`. |
| VF | p169 B positions 107, 108 and 110 | All three unknowns in `1B1??1?` are the same label, and differ from XA. |

VF and XA carry the two remaining labels `{5, 6}` bijectively. There are therefore two global assignments, not five independent numerical guesses. Neither assignment is established as the historical numbering.

## Evidence and credit

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates replay every coordinate alteration, compare the independent column/domain reconstruction with the cipher implementation, and re-encrypt every complete edited output. For a partial output, an injective global completion of the square and residual source masks supplies an explicitly nonhistorical roundtrip witness. Each readable passage preserves every nonseparator output label; literal protected fields are also checked without removing their internal separators. Source crops are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and RGB-pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/nov7_derailment_and_trains/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to regenerate and compare the delivered source pixels.

A roundtrip proves compatibility with a stated reading. Editorial spelling repairs remain proposals, and literal number labels are not automatically historical dates, quantities or reference numbers.

</details>

The modeled missing coordinate at working index **55** is filled with D,
supplying E at plaintext position **80**. Its raw domain is **DEQTUX**.
The candidate fixes **95 / 95 positions** but retains the opaque ending
**STUR3FSS**; a fixed label is not necessarily an understood word.

**Readable German — spacing of an incomplete fragment, with the opaque closing retained:**

> OHL. BP. Nachricht von Abreise deutscher Waffenstillstandskommission
> hat anscheinend gemeldeten STUR3FSS

The predicate and closing are not reconstructed into a complete report.
The edition does not infer what effect the news of the commission's
departure had.

All five placements inside AVVG and all six coordinate values are
retained: **30 geometry-labeled witnesses**, **26 distinct complete
ciphertexts and plaintexts**. Requiring the lexical crib
**GEMELDETEN** at positions **77:87** leaves one candidate, the one above.
That uniqueness is conditional on both the one-loss model and the crib;
it is not an unconditional historical solution.

The later [p151/p157 copy comparison](armistice_departure_copy.md) supports
a separately priced A1 variant. Under the common-copy alignment, an
observed p157 coordinate supports p151 source index 142 `A` → `F`, giving
`STURZFSS` in place of `STUR3FSS`. The fuller `STURZDES` interpretation
still needs two additional p151 coordinate changes without observed p157
support. The truncated p157 source fixes **0/95 positions by itself** in
the declared frame; its copied prefix, competing alignments and conflicting
source choices remain explicit in the separate edition. The original
layers above retain their stated zero-observed-substitution candidate.

## p151 A2

The same source crop gives **186 valid coordinates** for
`2 TL RICHI-186`, fixing **93 / 93 positions**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 186-coordinate frame:**

```text
ANSCHEINENDXOMOLDOVAXUEBERGEGANGENERFEINDMARSCHIERTAUFXFEHERTEMPLOMXXARMEETRITTX8X11X0BMARSCH
```

**Edited output — one observed-coordinate substitution, with no fills:**

```text
ANSCHEINENDXOMOLDOVAXUEBERGEGANGENERFEINDMARSCHIERTAUFXFEHERTEMPLOMXXARMEETRITTX8X11XABMARSCH
```

</details>

Source **27 V→X** repairs `0BMARSCH` to `ABMARSCH`. No global numeral
relabeling follows, and the separate 8 and 11 remain literal.

**Readable German — spacing, punctuation and umlaut; the unfinished wording remains:**

> Anscheinend O MOLDOVA übergegangener Feind marschiert auf
> FEHERTEMPLOM. Armee tritt 8. 11. Abmarsch

The initial O is retained without geographical expansion. The ending is
not supplemented with “an,” a route, a time or a missing continuation.

## p151 B

The [separate source](../../experiments/nov7_fragments_and_council/sources/p151_B.png)
is headed `NKJ v UKS (11.30 p.m., November 7th)` and `AN LP 2150`.
Its **156 typed coordinates** match `RICHI-156`. Five additional
[handwritten glyphs](../../experiments/nov7_fragments_and_council/sources/p151_B_annotation.png)
read **VXXDV**, duplicating the immediately preceding typed group.
The combined visible layer has **161 slots** and is odd in length.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — 156-coordinate typed source layer, with the five handwritten glyphs retained separately:**

```text
OXOXLXOPXDHRTIGESTELEGRAMMROEMX1ANOX11212OPXGEHXERHFLTENHOXKXMXOPXROEMX1A11302
```

**Edited output — same typed source layer; three observed-coordinate substitutions, with no fills:**

```text
OXHXLXOPXDORTIGESTELEGRAMMROEMX1ANOX11212OPXGEHXERHALTENHOXKXMXOPXROEMX1A11302
```

</details>

The changes are composite-source **0 F→V**, **40 V→F** and **115 X→D**.
They repair the first `O O L`, `DHRTIGES` and `ERHFLTEN`. The additional
H between ERHALTEN and O K M remains literal. Both layers have
**78 / 78 fixed positions**, and the complete edited candidate re-encrypts
exactly within the typed frame.

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation, with abbreviation labels retained:**

> O. H. L. Op. Dortiges Telegramm Röm. 1 A No. 11212 Op. Geh. erhalten.
> H. O. K. M. Op. Röm. 1 A 11302.

The acknowledgment refers to the literal number **11212**. This edition
does not establish which other surviving message, if any, it answers.

## Conditional interpretation and source-layer accounting

B's primary reading selects the typed source layer, mapping each working
coordinate to the complete visible composite. The handwriting's author
and purpose are not established. If all 161 visible glyphs are instead
treated as transmitted material, reaching the typed frame requires
**five slot deletions**, involving five known coordinates under the
primary D reading. That is a separate conditional transmission model,
not a free repair. A hypothetical handwritten D→O sensitivity leaves
four known coordinates and one non-coordinate mask in those excluded
slots; it does not affect the typed output. The enlarged crop supports
D, so the O variant is not presented as equally certified.

The old B OCR omitted typed **XXVGF** and the final D, misread one typed
X and masked a handwritten D and typed V. Its exact reconstruction is
frozen in the [OCR snapshot](../../experiments/nov7_fragments_and_council/ocr_snapshot.json)
and [certificate](../../experiments/nov7_fragments_and_council/certificates.json).
The historical typed-layer choice is kept separate from those OCR fixes.

These three physical records have **536 visible glyph slots including
five handwritten annotations**, **531 typed coordinates**, and **532
modeled coordinates**, with **266 plaintext positions**. The raw layers
fix **265 / 266** and the edited layers **266 / 266** under their stated
frames/layers. The primary cost is **four observed substitutions and one
missing-coordinate fill**. Neither unresolved key symbol 5 nor 6 is
assigned: all used pairs are already resolved by the published baseline.

Earlier A1/A2 body candidates, B's unread OCR and key provenance are
preserved; no historical first-solution claim is made. See the
[inputs](../../experiments/nov7_fragments_and_council/inputs.json),
[reproduction instructions](../../experiments/nov7_fragments_and_council/README.md)
and the separate [Soldiers Council notice](soldiers_council_surrender.md).

cases/military/nov8_alpenkorps_report.md.text:
# Alpenkorps departure and march report

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

A conditional second-part reading concerns preparations to transport the Alpenkorps and the continuation of a march. The source is dated 8 November 1918; the receipt header is 11.44 p.m. on 8 November. The first part of this physical p160 transmission has not been identified. The place-like strings NAGYBESKEREK and WERGCHEEZ are left exactly as decoded.

Source: Childs, printed pp.160–161 (PDF pp.163–164). [Source images and inputs](../../experiments/nov8_radio_keys_and_reports/inputs.json), [certificates](../../experiments/nov8_radio_keys_and_reports/certificates.json), [method and limitations](../../experiments/nov8_radio_keys_and_reports/README.md). All indices below are zero-based.

## Conditional shared digits

**Readable German — conditional shared digits, with the existing source edition retained:**

> Alpenkorps wird Ujverbasz zum Abtransport bereitgestellt. 219 217 und 6 R D setzen 9.11. Marsch in Linie Nagybeskerek, Wergcheez fort.

The [shared-reference assignment](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) supplies **VF=6**, completing **119/119** labels in the selected word edition. The four observed substitutions, one printed-mask fill and two observed exclusions remain unchanged. The opposite assignment gives 5; both UJVERBASZ/UZVERBASZ frames and the separately priced WERSCHETZ proposal remain available.


## p160 A2

Header: `A) UKS v ZON (11.44 p.m., November 8th); 1915 (8/11) 2 TLE; 2 TL; RICHI-238`.

Literal 240 versus advertised 238. The two six-character groups occupy source 15–20 and 26–31; the primary conditional frame excludes 18 and 26. This is one of the two best alignments with the independently transcribed p170 B2 source. Both retain the observed coordinates that give `RD`; they differ between `UJVERBASZ` and `UZVERBASZ`, which the parallel's mask cannot resolve. The displayed reading retains the former branch. The first part of this physical p160 transmission is not identified. ZON is a separate cleartext footer. WERGCHEEZ and NAGYBESKEREK stay literal.

The source has **240 slots** (239 valid coordinates). The conditional model has 238 slots / 119 plaintext positions: 117 fixed raw, 118 fixed after the stated edits.

**Cost:** 4 observed-coordinate substitutions; 1 printed-mask fill; 2 observed-coordinate exclusions; 0 mask exclusions; no inserted coordinates.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — under the explicitly conditional exclusion frame:

```text
ALPENKOYPSW2RDUJVERBASZZUMABTRFNSPORTBEREIT?ESTELLTXX219X217XUNU?XRDXSETZEN9X11XMARSCHINLINIENAGYBESKEREKXWERGCHEEZFORT
```

**Edited output** — changes and source offsets are enumerated in the certificate:

```text
ALPENKORPSWIRDUJVERBASZZUMABTRANSPORTBEREITGESTELLTXX219X217XUND?XRDXSETZEN9X11XMARSCHINLINIENAGYBESKEREKXWERGCHEEZFORT
```

</details>

**Readable German** — spacing, case, punctuation and conventional umlaut rendering only; all non-`X` labels match the edited output:

> Alpenkorps wird Ujverbasz zum Abtransport bereitgestellt. 219, 217 und ? Rd. setzen 9.11 Marsch in Linie Nagybeskerek, Wergcheez fort.

## Parallel traffic and an additional interpretation

The previously reviewed [p170 B1/B2 and p166/p167 reports](nov9_operational_reports.md)
provide related earlier-part context and a near-identical second part. The
source headers differ: this p160 transmission is received on November 8,
while p170 B is received on November 9. The parallel does not identify the
missing physical first part of this particular p160 transmission.

The source-only audit compares **all 28,680 two-coordinate exclusion maps**
with the untouched 238-slot p170 B2 source. It uses no proposed German text,
word score or completed square to choose the maps. Exactly two maps attain
the minimum of five observed disagreements:

| Excluded p160 source positions | Known agreements / disagreements / masks | Native name-like token | Native abbreviation |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 18, 26 | 231 / 5 / 2 | `UJVERBASZ` | `RD` |
| 18, 27 | 231 / 5 / 2 | `UZVERBASZ` | `RD` |

The previous frame excluded 19 and 26 and had six disagreements. Both new
minimum maps instead exclude source 18 `D`, retaining source 19 `X`.
Together with source 199 `V`, that observed coordinate gives square cell
`XV` = `D` at plaintext position 67. **`RD` therefore needs no coordinate
substitution under either minimum map.** This sharpens the frame without
increasing the fixed-position count: each map fixes 117 of 119 raw positions,
and 116 positions have the same fixed label across both maps.

The second exclusion remains conditional. Retaining source 27 `X` gives
`J`; retaining source 26 `D` gives `Z`. P170 frame 25 is a mask, so the
source comparison cannot independently select `UJVERBASZ`. By contrast,
p170 frame 183 supplies `D` where p160 source 185 is a dash under both
maps, supporting the fill in `BEREITGESTELLT`. All five observed disagreements
remain recorded.

**Conditional interpretation:** substituting the parallel's `WERSCHETZ`
for the primary `WERGCHEEZ` costs **two additional observed-coordinate
substitutions**, at p160 source 48 G→X and source 192 D→G. Its total is
**six observed substitutions**, one printed-mask fill and two observed
exclusions: one fewer substitution than under the previous frame. This
separately priced interpretation is not substituted into the primary edited
or readable stream above. The shared `ABTRFNSPORT` raw spelling still needs
its stated editorial correction; agreement between copies does not correct it.

The [parallel certificate](../../experiments/nov8_radio_keys_and_reports/parallel_witnesses.json)
retains every source and plaintext difference, both minimum source-alignment
maps, prior record identity and both complete 5/6 key witnesses. The earlier operational case's historical unit
identification remains a separate context layer; no unknown digit is filled
in this source edition. No previously cataloged parallel is counted again.

## Shared uncertainty and credit

The two missing square cells `VF` and `XA` jointly contain `5` and `6`. Both complete assignments are retained as compatibility witnesses; every occurrence of a cell shares the same digit. The displayed `?` positions therefore must not be treated as independent digit choices. In p160 B2 one additional source coordinate remains unfilled; its domain can include letters as well as digits.

The published Nov7–9 period key and earlier OCR candidates are credited in the inputs. This edition adds source inspection, separate repair costs and exact readable-text mappings. It does not claim new recovery of the period key.

# November 8: a separate Serbian-cavalry report witness

Source review and editorial work: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Published
Nov7–9 key: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker; unchanged
here. The operational body and p170 word proposals were already edited in
[the p166/p167/p170 report study](nov9_operational_reports.md). This addition · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)
is a new physical witness and source-alignment audit, not a claim to a new
body decipherment or universal priority.


**Reviewed source crops:** [p158_E_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov8_serbian_cavalry_parallel/sources/p158_E_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).
## Conditional shared digits

**Readable German — conditional shared digits, with the existing source edition retained:**

> ANENMELDUNG. Serb. Kavallerie Peterwadein und Fehertemplom eingerueckt. Abmarsch 217 I D und 6 R D nach Norden ohne Feinberuehrung.

The [shared-reference assignment](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) supplies **VF=6** to the unchanged division pair, completing **118/118** labels in the selected word edition. The five observed substitutions and one source-linked added A are unchanged; the opposite square retains 5. This propagates a separately justified digit to this physical witness and does not count the earlier p170 unit identification again.


## What the additional source establishes

Printed p158 E1 has **235 coordinates against an advertised 236**. Its
third source row contains the four-coordinate group `XDGV`. The independent
p170 B1 copy has `AXDGV` in the corresponding position. Adding its observed
`A` restores a 236-coordinate frame while retaining all 235 p158 coordinates
in their printed order. The source-linked frame fixes **117 of 118
plaintext positions** and preserves three letter disagreements with p170.

The report describes Serbian cavalry entering the places transmitted as
`PETERWADEIN` and `FEHERTEMPLOM`, followed by a northward departure of
`217 I D` and `? R D`. The spelling `PETERWADEIN` lacks the R in the fuller
place-name used by another report. The final `FEINBERUEHRUNG` appears to
mean enemy contact but lacks the D of `FEIND`; the exact readable stream
retains both omissions. `ANENMELDUNG` remains unexpanded.

The conservative edited layer uses **five observed-coordinate
substitutions**: three are supported by the independent raw copy; two are
shared ordinary-word repairs. The added A is separately priced as **one
source-linked coordinate addition**, not represented as a coordinate
visible on p158. No source coordinate is excluded, reordered or masked.

## The two literal headers

| Witness | Printed header |
|---|---|
| p158 E1 | `E) UKS v ZON (11.44 p.m., November 8th); 1915 (8/11) 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-236; following control: ZON UM; page footer: (continued)` |
| p170 B1 | `UKS v ZON (11.44 p.m., November 9th); 1915 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-236` |

The same station pair, reception time and `1915` field recur. The reception
dates differ by one day, and p158 also supplies `(8/11)`. These observations
support a repeated body; they do not identify a specific copying or
reception mechanism. The p158 heading advertises two parts, but this edition
adds only the first. The next page's separate header is not silently joined
to it as its second part.

## Raw output — native 235-coordinate source

The literal source has odd length. Its diagnostic output, before adding
anything, is retained in full:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — native odd-frame diagnostic:**

```text
NDSGREXNRNL0LERBT4DVDLSDDI2YETEWU0EETDMNAFZSIRGSRPECYTXNASMULO0X2X7TYAUEQFD1X0TXN0RKN?YUXDFF1SFOINSNCXDXRENNTELWLHGU?
```

</details>

The final unpaired intermediate coordinate is
`D` from source index
**23**. This diagnostic is not the
readable report. Its native length and orphan remain in the certificate.

## Raw output — conditional source-linked 236-coordinate frame

Adding the independently printed A at primary source boundary **85** gives:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional frame with one source-linked A:**

```text
ANENMELDUNGXSERBXKAVALLERITPETERWADE2NUNDFEHERTEMPLOMEINGSRUECKTXXABMARSCH217XIXDXUND?XRXDNACHNOYDENOHNEFEINBELUEHRUNG
```

</details>

This frame has **117 fixed positions / 118**. If the added coordinate is
left unfilled, **116/118** positions are fixed. The other question mark is
the unchanged square cell `VF`, whose two global alternatives are **5/6**.

## Edited output — five observed substitutions

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — five observed-coordinate substitutions:**

```text
ANENMELDUNGXSERBXKAVALLERIEPETERWADEINUNDFEHERTEMPLOMEINGERUECKTXXABMARSCH217XIXDXUND?XRXDNACHNORDENOHNEFEINBERUEHRUNG
```

</details>

All source indices below are zero-based. The source-linked addition is
listed separately from the five substitutions.

| Source index | Printed coordinate | Edited coordinate | Support |
|---:|:---:|:---:|---|
| 70 | D | A | Shared ordinary-word proposal |
| 96 | G | D | Independent p170 raw coordinate |
| 144 | D | G | Independent p170 raw coordinate |
| 150 | G | D | Independent p170 raw coordinate |
| 194 | X | V | Shared ordinary-word proposal |

The added A comes from p170 B1 coordinate **85** and is inserted before
p158 source coordinate **85**. The unchanged p158 source group `XDGV`
therefore appears as `AXDGV` only in the explicit analysis frame.

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels preserved:**

> ANENMELDUNG. Serb. Kavallerie Peterwadein und Fehertemplom eingerueckt. Abmarsch 217 I D und ? R D nach Norden ohne Feinberuehrung.

**Conditional interpretation:** Serbian cavalry is reported as having
entered the two transmitted place-names. A northward departure of the
labelled formations follows. Reading the final phrase as “without enemy
contact” requires recognizing the missing D in the transmitted word; that
is a prose interpretation, not an extra recovered coordinate. The earlier
report study gives fuller place-name and operational context separately.

## What the independent copy supports

The p170 B1 raw source directly supports three p158 changes:

| Plaintext position | p158 source-linked raw | p170 raw | Proposed label |
|---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 26 | T | E | E |
| 36 | 2 | I | I |
| 96 | Y | R | R |

Those supply the E of `KAVALLERIE`, the I of the transmitted
`PETERWADEIN`, and the R of `NORDEN`. Both copies share raw
`EINGSRUECKT` and `FEINBELUEHRUNG`; their E/R corrections therefore remain
editorial and are not presented as independently corroborated letters.

Keeping both source values at every disagreement gives a conservative
**114/118-position** common template:

**Conditional interpretation — union of the two raw-source domains:**

```text
ANENMELDUNGXSERBXKAVALLERI?PETERWADE?NUNDFEHERTEMPLOMEINGSRUECKTXXABMARSCH217XIXDXUND?XRXDNACHNO?DENOHNEFEINBELUEHRUNG
```

Its per-position union domains are recorded in the certificate. Agreement
on a repeated body does not erase the disagreements between the two
physical witnesses.

## Every one-coordinate alignment

The verifier compares the 235 observed p158 coordinates with all **236**
possible one-coordinate omissions from the complete p170 source. This
comparison uses the two printed ciphertexts, with no desired plaintext or
language score.

| Source boundary receiving the parallel A | Observed agreements | Observed disagreements | Filled 236-coordinate stream |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 82 | 232 | 3 | Same as the other minima |
| 83 | 232 | 3 | Same as the other minima |
| 84 | 232 | 3 | Same as the other minima |
| 85 | 232 | 3 | Same as the other minima |

The A run makes all four placements equivalent after the coordinate is
supplied. Their raw unfilled outputs and source maps differ, and all are
retained. Boundary 85 is the primary display because it places the extra
coordinate at the start of the visibly short group. It is not a uniquely
recovered historical omission site. All prices and all frames within one
disagreement of the minimum are included in the certificate.

## Optional earlier headline proposal

The earlier p170 edition proposes `ABENMELDUNG` for raw `ANENMELDUNG`.
Applying that same proposal here adds **two observed-coordinate
substitutions**, for **seven total**:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — optional earlier headline, seven observed substitutions:**

```text
ABENMELDUNGXSERBXKAVALLERIEPETERWADEINUNDFEHERTEMPLOMEINGERUECKTXXABMARSCH217XIXDXUND?XRXDNACHNORDENOHNEFEINBERUEHRUNG
```

</details>

The D of `Aben[d]meldung` would still be a prose-only supplied letter. The
primary five-substitution reading retains `ANENMELDUNG`; both exact
candidate costs and round trips are verified.

## Reproduction and credit

[Inputs](../../experiments/nov8_serbian_cavalry_parallel/inputs.json) preserve
the native p158 groups, both headers, the source-linked addition, the
unchanged key and prior credits. The
[certificate](../../experiments/nov8_serbian_cavalry_parallel/certificates.json)
retains the native odd diagnostic, every gap price, competing source maps,
all edits, source-supported and shared-editorial letters, union domains and
both globally consistent 5/6 completions. Each complete square exactly
decrypts and re-encrypts the raw, edited, optional-headline and prior frames.
Neither completion is selected historically by this edition.

The existing p170 source record is hash-bound and its image has been
reviewed independently. Both its crop and the new p158 crop are checked by
exact RGB regeneration from the pinned Childs PDF. The
[README](../../experiments/nov8_serbian_cavalry_parallel/README.md) gives the
portable verification commands. Earlier OCR, unchanged-key diagnostics,
body readings and word proposals retain their distinct attribution; the
p170 witness is not counted as another new physical record.

cases/military/nov9_operational_reports..text:
# November 9 operational reports: Serbian cavalry and the retreat north

[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All cases](../README.md) · [Source certificate](../../experiments/p170_continuation/military_records.json) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

The three-part report on p166 and two-part report p170 B describe Serbian cavalry entering towns, German formations marching north and preparations to transport the Alpenkorps. Our comparison with the p167 reception restores the **twenty-coordinate prefix** missing from p166 part 3 and recovers its order footer. The readings use the published **Nov7–9** key.

## Read the reports

The German readings follow the edited witnesses. Brackets mark the expansions, repairs and unresolved numeral explained below.

### p166 A, with its p167 A continuation

**Readable German — the stated edited witness, with the linked 5/6 cell left unresolved:**

> O.H.L., O.P. Lage 11. Armee, 8.11., abends: Serb[ische] Kavallerie [in] Peterwardein und Fehertemplom eingerückt.
>
> Abmarsch 217. I.D. und **[5. oder 6.] R.D.** nach Norden ohne Feindberührung. Alpenkorps wird Umverbasz (Fragezeichen) zum Abtransport bereitgestellt.
>
> 219., 217. und **[5. oder 6.] R.D.** setzen 9.11. Marsch in Lin[i]e Nagybeskerek–Werschetz fort. O.K.M., 1a, No. 11319 op.

**Meaning.** An evening situation report describes Serbian cavalry entering Peterwardein and Fehertemplom. The 217th Infantry Division and a reserve division are marching north without enemy contact. The Alpenkorps is being assembled for onward transport at a place transmitted as `UMVERBASZ`, followed by the literal word `FRAGEZEICHEN` (“question mark”). The 219th and 217th divisions and the same reserve division continue their march on 9 November along the Nagybeskerek–Werschetz line. The footer is retained as `O.K.M., 1a, No.11319 op.`

The p170 parallel supports the conditional place reading **Ujverbasz**. The reserve-division numeral remains **5/6** in the key; the historical comparison below supports **6th Reserve Division**.

### p170 B, parts 1 and 2

**Readable German — the stated edited witness and prose-only additions identified below:**

> Aben[d]meldung: Serb[ische] Kavallerie [in] Peterwa[r]dein und Fehertemplom eingerückt. Abmarsch 217. I.D. und **[5. oder 6.] R.D.** nach Norden ohne Fein[d]berührung.
>
> Alpenkorps wird U[j]verbasz zum Abtransport bereitgestellt. 219., 217. und **[5. oder 6.] R.D.** setzen 9.11. Marsch in Linie Nagybeskerek–Werschetz fort.

**Meaning.** This reception repeats the operational account and directly confirms **217**, **219** and the onward-march date **9.11**. Its proposed J in `UJVERBASZ` fills an erasure; other bracketed letters expand the prose. The two cipher frames retain 118 and 119 positions.

| Display form | Editorial category | What remains separate |
|---|---|---|
| `Serb[ische]` | Abbreviation expansion | The extra prose letters are not encoded positions. |
| `[in]` | Supplied grammar | The exact streams do not acquire a new word. |
| `Aben[d]meldung`, `Peterwa[r]dein`, `Fein[d]berührung`, `Lin[i]e` | Prose-only spelling normalization | The same-length edited witnesses still retain their missing letters. |
| `U[j]verbasz` | Priced source-erasure fill | J is a candidate coordinate fill, not an abbreviation expansion. |
| `[5. oder 6.]` | Linked key-cell alternatives | Every occurrence uses the same unresolved cell; the choices are not independent. |

## Historical identification: most likely the 6th Reserve Division

General Franchet d'Esperey's telegram **5.956/3**, sent from Salonique to Clemenceau and Foch on **19 November 1918 at 22:40**, describes the situation on **11 November**. Its paragraph on the reconstituted German 11th Army names the Alpenkorps, the 217th and 219th divisions around Nagy-Backskerek–Verschatz, and explicitly the **6th Reserve Division**. The relevant short passage reads: “217° — 219° D.I. Nagy-Backskerek—Verschatz) 6° D.I. réserve”. The matching formations and geography support the same identification in these German reports of 9 November; the French telegram is two days later in its reported situation and ten days later in transmission.

The telegram appears as document 39, pp79–82, in *Documents diplomatiques français sur l'histoire du Bassin des Carpates, 1918–1932*, vol. I (1993). [Source PDF, p153](https://real-eod.mtak.hu/19844/13/documents.pdf).

The retrospective battle calendar *Ruhmeshalle unserer alten Armee*, vol. I, fifth revised edition, places the 6th Reserve Division on the return march from the Balkans through Hungary from 6 November (p385). It places the 5th Reserve Division at the Antwerp–Meuse position on 5–11 November (p382). [Calendar extract, PDF pp43 and 46](https://denstorekrig1914-1918.dk/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Ruhmeshalle_unsere_alten_Armee_5_Aufl_Bd-1_s_342-497s.pdf).

<details>
<summary>Bibliographic details and earlier use of the sources</summary>

The French document collection is vol. I, *Octobre 1918 – Août 1919*, collected by Magda Ádám, György Litván and Mária Ormos, edited by Ádám, Akadémiai Kiadó, Budapest, 1993, ISBN 963 05 6659 1. The telegram's archival reference, printed on p82, is **AG.4N58 c/63. d/10.** [Library catalogue](https://real-eod.mtak.hu/19844/).

# Ober Ost troop movements: a conditional reading across two obliterations

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The first part of p186 B proposes troop movements within the Ober Ost territory. This reading depends on explicitly excluding two obliterated group-width regions. The surviving second part independently describes soldiers wanting to travel home without authorization; it is published in the [native companion edition](home_departures_baltic_transport.md#p186-b2).

## Source geometry and its limits

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p186 excerpt](../../experiments/oberost_troop_movement_obliterations/sources/p186_reviewed.png) · [Inputs](../../experiments/oberost_troop_movement_obliterations/inputs.json) · [Position certificates and controls](../../experiments/oberost_troop_movement_obliterations/certificates.json)

**Source transcription — header:** `B) NKJ v LP (06.23 a.m., November 13th); FUER WAU 07.00 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-308`

The fourth ciphertext row has two heavily obliterated regions between GFDXG and the following C/G-ambiguous group. They occupy two ordinary group columns, but five separate original glyphs cannot be counted in either region. The disclosed **318-position composite layout** consists of **308 individually transcribed positions plus two regions modeled as five masks each**. It is not a claim that 318 separate original coordinate letters remain visible.

**Conditional interpretation — source-row layout with five inferred masks for each obliterated group column:**

```text
GFDXG ????? ????? FGCGA AFGFA GVXVD DXXXF AFFVF
```

The C/G-shaped glyph in FGCGA is transcribed C and masked; its ambiguity is independent of the two obliterated regions. The Y-like glyph in XYVXX is also masked. All other positions are retained in source order.

The primary frame excludes the ten modeled masks at composite source indices 125–134, yielding the advertised 308 coordinates. This costs **ten masked-layout-slot exclusions**. It deletes no observed coordinate. The agreement with the heading supports examining this geometry, but neither the heading nor a readable result proves that the obliterations were intended cancellations.

The certificate preserves all four choices: retain both regions (318 positions), exclude either region alone (313 positions), and exclude both (308 positions). Both odd-length controls explicitly identify their unpaired intermediate coordinate and its source index; their final coordinate is not silently discarded as source evidence. The two single-region controls happen to have identical streams because both regions are entirely masked.

## p186 B1

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — retain both five-mask regions in the 318-position composite layout; diagnostic only:**

```text
?0AMOVBM1ZRPVZR??LS?R5FDX?TXZO0SPX?5ICFJA??H?O6??R?K1CC6XP?PX?TK6V?MXV?I?F?Z0XENUF?6FVTPVC?EOHEPE??E?ZBIMA?INTCGMG?III???C?GZSELW?LUNMOB5XG?IMEDGS?EZ?EDNIBCLDP
```

**Raw output — conditional 308-coordinate frame after ten masked-layout-slot exclusions; 150 of 154 positions fixed:**

```text
GENXGOUVXWARSCHAUXZ0FORTX?MX1AXNRR6?1X15XGENXVX10X11XISTANOBOSTGEDRAHTETXXESWIRDVORGESCHLX?ENXTRUPPENVERSCHIEBUNG?NINNERHALBDESOBEROSTGEBIETSVORZUNEHMENXX
```

**Edited output — same conditional frame, one observed-coordinate substitution and two source-mask fills; 152 of 154 positions fixed:**

```text
GENXGOUVXWARSCHAUXZ0FORTX?MX1AXNRR6?1X15XGENXVX10X11XISTANOBOSTGEDRAHTETXXESWIRDVORGESCHLAGENXTRUPPENVERSCHIEBUNGENINNERHALBDESOBEROSTGEBIETSVORZUNEHMENXX
```

</details>

All indices below refer to the 318-position composite source layout. The observed substitution is **88 D→V**. The two source-mask fills are **91 Y-like glyph→X** and **137 C/G-shaped glyph→G**. The ten excluded masks do not receive guessed coordinate values and are not counted as fills.

**Readable German — conditional frame and explicitly priced changes; opaque fields retained:**

> Gen. Gouv. Warschau. Z0FORT. ?MX1AXNRR6?1X15XGENXVX10X11 ist an OBOST gedrahtet. Es wird vorgeschlagen, Truppenverschiebungen innerhalb des Oberostgebiets vorzunehmen.

**Meaning:** The body addresses GEN GOUV WARSCHAU, says that the referenced item has been wired to OBOST, and proposes troop movements within the Ober Ost territory. Z0FORT and the opening reference remain opaque literal fields. The text is a proposal, not evidence that the movements occurred.

The two remaining unknowns come from unresolved square cells: VG at plaintext index 25 and AF at index 35. The AF position is coupled to p186 C1 index 11; it must differ from GA, which is shared by p186 B2 index 109 and C1 index 9. All indices are zero-based, and none of these reference labels is historically assigned. The published Nov13–15b key is unchanged; its nonhistorical injective completion witness verifies compatibility without selecting historical numeral labels. Z0FORT is not silently normalized to SOFORT, and the reference `?MX1AXNRR6?1X15XGENXVX10X11` remains literal. The phrase “ist an OBOST gedrahtet” reports earlier transmission of the referenced item; the following sentence proposes movements. Neither establishes that troop movements occurred.

## Native date context and numerical labels

The unchanged field `GENXVX10X11XISTANOBOSTGEDRAHTET` provides a separate
contextual check on DD, which carries the published label 1. Within the
same conditional obliteration frame, the two final month labels use the
original **DD** pairs at composite source indices **170/122** and **305/6**.
All ten coordinates of `10X11` are observed; none uses a word repair or
mask fill. The [joint verifier](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md#the-award-class)
replays the complete field from the source transcription.

If `10X11` is a day/month date, 11 is the only valid repeated-digit month,
so this supports retaining **numerical DD=1** independently of the p193
award. The date reading is explicitly conditional, and the larger reference
remains opaque. This argument changes no source coordinate or fixed-label
count and does not resolve the obliteration geometry.

## Exact account

The separate [p193 award-class interpretation](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md)
propagates `VG=2` to the opening field, giving `2MX1AXNRR6?1`.
This raises the conditional label count to **153/154** but leaves the
opening opaque. It supplies no additional ordinary word or source repair.

| Quantity | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| New physical source records | 1 |
| Individually transcribed positions | 308 |
| Added layout masks for two obliterated group columns | 10 |
| Composite layout positions | 318 |
| Conditional analyzed coordinates / plaintext positions | 308 / 154 |
| Fixed conditional raw / edited labels | 150 / 152 |
| Excluded layout masks / excluded observed coordinates | 10 / 0 |
| Observed-coordinate substitutions / source-mask fills | 1 / 2 |
| Inserted coordinates or reordered source positions | 0 |

These counts exclude the already separate native second part. The certificate's `printed_source_slots` is 308, while `composite_layout_slots` is 318; `source_deletions` counts the ten modeled-mask exclusions, with `observed_coordinate_deletions` separately fixed at zero. This prevents the group-width model from being represented as ten legible original letters.

## Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

[Earlier OCR candidates](../../experiments/oberost_troop_movement_obliterations/prior_candidates.json) and the [original OCR snapshot](../../experiments/oberost_troop_movement_obliterations/ocr_snapshot.json) remain separately frozen. The new source analysis does not treat an OCR token count as a historical received length.

```sh
python experiments/oberost_troop_movement_obliterations/verify.py --verify
python experiments/oberost_troop_movement_obliterations/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf
```

Verification checks every source/model index, the four control frames, all position domains, each proposed change, exact readable-label preservation, an injective global completion witness, unchanged key provenance and the optional original-PDF crop pixels. A successful roundtrip establishes compatibility with the declared exclusion model, not a unique historical reading or cancellation intent.

# Orient intelligence: expected landings and fighting on the Tigris

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source:** J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
printed p92 B1, p93 A2–A4 and p94 A5–A6; PDF pp95–97.
**Edition:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

These six numbered parts share `OSM v LP (4.20 p.m., November 1st)`,
the clear addressee `SSD DEUTSCHER N O OSM OHL ZUGL FUER UNTERST N O`,
and the origin line `(1/11) 0415 6 TEILE`. The final plaintext signature
is `ABT FREMDE HEERE`. Their [source edition](../../experiments/orient_intelligence/README.md)
contains every literal coordinate and exact repair.

The report first corrects an earlier Orient note, then assesses reports
of shipping and expected landings around Alexandretta. It ends with an
English-reported attack against Turkish positions near `KALAT SHERGAT`
and a qualified claim about British cavalry. The source presents
observations, assessments and allegations; this edition preserves those
distinctions.

## p92 B1

The source advertises and prints **328 valid coordinates**. Its raw body is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DEUTSCQERNOOSMOHLZUGLFUERUNTERSTNOXBERICHTIGUNGZUVORTRXNOTORIENTVOMX30X10X2ABSATZSYRIENXMUSSAMSCHLUSSHEISSENXALSOANSCHEINENDX7XINDXDIVX60XGEMXDIVXODEDXFALLSX54XUSWX
```

</details>

The candidate repairs `DEUTSCQER` to `DEUTSCHER` and `ODED` to `ODER`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
DEUTSCHERNOOSMOHLZUGLFUERUNTERSTNOXBERICHTIGUNGZUVORTRXNOTORIENTVOMX30X10X2ABSATZSYRIENXMUSSAMSCHLUSSHEISSENXALSOANSCHEINENDX7XINDXDIVX60XGEMXDIVXODERXFALLSX54XUSWX
```

</details>

This costs **three observed-coordinate substitutions**. The clear
header independently contains `DEUTSCHER`. The report calls itself a
correction to the Orient presentation note of raw `30 X 10`, second
paragraph on Syria, and says the ending should read:

**Readable German:**

> Also anscheinend 7 X IND X DIV X 60 X GEM X DIV X oder X falls X 54 X usw.

Those unit labels and the fragmentary syntax are preserved. The earlier
note is not supplied or reconstructed from this correction alone.

## p93 A2

The source advertises and prints **252 coordinates**. Earlier OCR merged
this part with A3 and A4; applying the printed boundary gives the
following complete **126-position raw reading**, without any edit:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
VORTRAGSNOTIZENX31X10X1918XORIENTROEMX1XSYRIENBEVORSTEHENDELANDUNGINALEXANDRETTENACHFLIEGERMELUNGVOM29X10FUHREINGELEITZUGVONX2
```

</details>

This is headed presentation notes, raw `31 X 10 X 1918`, Orient,
`ROEM X 1`, Syria: an expected landing at Alexandretta. It attributes a
convoy report to an air observation of raw `29 X 10`. The received
`FLIEGERMELUNG` is left intact; an apparent omitted `D` is not inserted
into the ciphertext.

## p93 A3

The source advertises and prints **394 valid coordinates**. The
**197-position raw reading** is complete and unchanged:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
GROESZERENTRANSPORTERN1KREUZERXUX4XTORPEDOBOOTENX40XKMXSUEDWESTLXALEXANDRETTEINFAHRTRICHTUNGALEXANDRETTEAUSZERDEMWURDEINDERBUCHTVONXARSUSXEINGROSZESSCHIFFBEOBACHTETNACHALLDENMELDUNGENDERLETZTENTAGE
```

</details>

Continuing A2, the report describes larger transports with a cruiser and
torpedo boats southwest of Alexandretta, heading toward it, and another
large ship observed in the bay of the received place name `ARSUS`.
The raw convoy and distance labels `2`, `1`, `4` and `40 X KM` are
unchanged. The `SZ` spellings in `GROESZEREN`, `AUSZERDEM` and `GROSZES`
are kept as received. `XARSUSX` has its surrounding separators; no
geographical letter is supplied from a modern map.

## p93 A4

The source advertises and prints **328 valid coordinates**. Its
**164-position direct reading** is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
UEBERGESTEIGERTENSCHIFFVERKEHRVORDERXSYRISCHENXKUESTEUNDDERTAETIGKEITDERAUFKLAERUNGSFAHRZEUGEVORXALEXANDRETTEXMUSSMITUNMITTELBARBEVORSTEHENDENLANDUNGSVERSUCHENINDER
```

</details>

It continues the assessment that, given recent reports of increased
shipping off the Syrian coast and reconnaissance vessels near
Alexandretta, imminent landing attempts should be expected. This is a
forecast within the source. The text does not say that such a landing
had already occurred.

Parts A2–A4 together have **974 source coordinates and 487 plaintext
positions**. Earlier OCR treated them as one 977-slot stream. Their
three correctly separated readings each re-encrypt exactly to the
unchanged observed source.

## p94 A5

The source advertises **368 slots**, with one printed dash in its first
group, `GDGV-`. Its raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
BUCHTVONALEXANDRETTEXGERECHNETWERDENXROEMX2?MESOPOTAMIENX7NGLISCHERVORMARSCHAMXTIGRISXNACHENGLORIENTBERICHTGRIFFENENGLISCHETRUPPENAMX29X10XDIETUERKISCHENSTELLUNGENNOERDLXKALATXSHERGATX
```

<details>


are preserved, including the raw section and date labels. The source
forms `VXFXG` and `XDXFF` also correct earlier OCR, directly restoring
the complete words `ALEXANDRETTE` and `TRUPPEN` without source edits.

The opening completes the expectation of landing attempts in the bay
of Alexandretta. The next section is Mesopotamia: English advance on
the Tigris. According to an English Orient report, troops attacked
