## p94 A6

All **350 coordinates** are observed. The full **175-position raw text**
needs no repair:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ANUNDDRANGENNACHHEFTIGENANSCHEINENDSCHWERENKAEMPFENINDIESTELLUNGENEINTEILEDERTUERKENDIEZUENTKOMMENVERSUCHTENWURDENANGEBLICHDURCHBRITISCHEKAVALLERIEABGESCHNITTENXABTFREMDEHEERE
```

</details>

**Readable German — continuation of A5; the leading ellipsis does not mark a missing position in A6:**

> … an und drangen nach heftigen, anscheinend schweren Kämpfen in die Stellungen ein. Teile der Türken, die zu entkommen versuchten, wurden angeblich durch britische Kavallerie abgeschnitten. Abt. Fremde Heere.

`ANSCHEINEND` and `ANGEBLICH` are fully observed and retained. The report
is not presented as independent confirmation of the severity of the
fighting or the cavalry claim.

## Attribution and verification

The unchanged Nov1–3 square and ranks are previously published.
Parts one, five and six also predate this edition as readable unreviewed
repository candidates. The incorrectly merged p93 candidate was
unreadable; its exact prior output is frozen in the inputs. The new
contribution is the source transcription, separated part frames,
complete report assembly and reversible repairs.

The Lasry et al. paper and dissertation discuss Foreign Armies
intelligence generally. The bounded check did not locate an explicit
discussion of this six-part body, and the cached comment-thread check
found no such body. That does not establish decipherment priority.

The six records contain **2,020 printed slots**, **2,019 valid coordinates**
and **1,010 plaintext positions**. There are **1,009 fixed raw positions**;
the explicit candidates fix all 1,010 at a total cost of **four observed
substitutions and one printed-erasure fill**. No key, rank or source
length is changed. All dates, unit numbers, convoy figures and distance
labels are unchanged, while the separately repaired raw `7` in
`7NGLISCHER` remains visible in the audit.

```bash
python experiments/orient_intelligence/verify.py --verify
python experiments/orient_intelligence/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
```

# Parallel Orient reports on South-Slav units

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

Childs pp101–102 preserve closely related reports on South-Slav units near
Montenegro. The p102 report is an explicitly numbered three-part message.
The p101 material has a damaged first part and a matching detachment passage,
but some headers and wording differ. The edition preserves each physical
record instead of merging those differences.

## p101 C1

The [C1 source](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p101_C1_D2.png)
reads `UKS v ZON`, received at `3.15 a.m., November 2nd`, origin
`1225 (1) 3 TLE`, and `1 TL RICHI-190`. Its native 190-slot frame includes
32 printed dashes and a `C` at source 92. The fifth-row group is `GGGDA`,
with three visible `G` characters; its
[detail](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p101_C1_GGGDA.png)
prevents treating the second `G` as an additional mask.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame**

```text
NO?MEC?E?SEN?NA?H?ORI?NTB?R?CHT?OM???10X?IOD?S?EDS?AVI??HEX?INH?I?EN5?NXM??TE8?GRO?V?RGE?UEC??X
```

**Edited output — explicitly priced coordinate repairs and mask fills**

```text
NOXMACKENSENXNACHXORIENTBERICHTVOM??X10XSINDXSUEDSLAVISCHEXEINHEITENVONXMONTENEGROXVORGERUECKTX
```

</details>

**Readable German — from the edited layer**

> N.O. Mackensen. Nach Orientbericht vom ??.10. sind suedslavische Einheiten von Montenegro vorgerueckt.

The candidate has **93/95 fixed positions**, after five observed-coordinate
substitutions and 31 source-mask fills. The two date positions remain
unknown; the visible `10` is retained. Raw `5` in `5?N` and `8` in
`M??TE8?GRO` are locally priced word repairs toward `VON` and `MONTENEGRO`;
they do not assign any historical number. The beginning stays literal `NO`
(rendered `N.O.`), without changing it to a different headquarters abbreviation.
The word `EINHEITEN` fits the partially visible `?INH?I?EN` and is also
present in the related p102 B1 report.

The passage says that South-Slav units have advanced **from** Montenegro.
The corresponding p102 B1 text below says **in** Montenegro. The source
coordinates support this wording difference. The p102 date `28` is not
transferred into the two unresolved p101 positions.

## p101 B2

The [B2 source](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p101_A2_B2.png)
reads `UKS v ZON`, `3.23 a.m., November 2nd`, and `2 TL RICHI-200`.
Its own origin number is absent. A relationship with C1 is plausible from
the topic, part number and nearby reception times, but is not established
by an identical complete header. The last group is `GVXDC`; the final
[`C` at source 199](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p101_B2_C199.png)
is a mask, not a silently chosen `G`.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame**

```text
WAHRSCHEINLICHDASXAUSDERXSUEUSLAVISCHENXDIVXGEBILDETEXDETACHEMENTX2RGTRXIVFX2RGTRXKAVXMITG?BIRGSARQL
```

**Edited output — explicitly priced coordinate repairs and mask fills**

```text
WAHRSCHEINLICHDASXAUSDERXSUEDSLAVISCHENXDIVXGEBILDETEXDETACHEMENTX2RGTRXINFX2RGTRXKAVXMITGEBIRGSARTL
```

</details>

**Readable German — from the edited layer**

> Wahrscheinlich das aus der suedslavischen Div. gebildete Detachement. 2 Rgtr. Inf. 2 Rgtr. Kav. mit Gebirgsartl.

This is 99/100 fixed raw and 100/100 fixed after three observed substitutions
and one mask fill. It describes a detachment probably formed from the
South-Slav division: two `Rgtr. Inf.`, two `Rgtr. Kav.`, with mountain
artillery. The abbreviations remain in the display; their unit numbers are
literal. The related p102 copy supports the masked source coordinate and
several differing letters, with the equal-cost limitations recorded below.

## p102 B1

The [p102 B source](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p102_B.png)
prints an unavailable station pair, an unspecified reception time on
November 3, and `1227 ZON (1/11) 3 TLE`. Its first part is
`1 TL RICHI-208`, with 208 valid coordinates.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame**

```text
ABTXFRXHEEREXGDXHXQUXSXMXNACHXORIENTBESICHTXVOM28X10XSINDSUEDXLAVISCHEXEINHEITENINMONTENEGROVORGERUECKTX
```

**Edited output — explicitly priced coordinate repairs and mask fills**

```text
ABTXFRXHEEREXGDXHXQUXSXMXNACHXORIENTBERICHTXVOM28X10XSINDSUEDSLAVISCHEXEINHEITENINMONTENEGROVORGERUECKTX
```

</details>

**Readable German — from the edited layer**

> Abt. Fr. Heere. G.D.H.Qu.S.M. Nach Orientbericht vom 28.10. sind suedslavische Einheiten in Montenegro vorgerueckt.

All 104 raw labels are fixed. Two observed substitutions, source 82 `X`→`V`
and 168 `V`→`A`, repair `SUEDXLAVISCHE` and `BESICHT`. No masks or geometry
changes are needed. Its recipient and administrative abbreviations differ
from p101 C1. `GDXHXQUXSXM` is punctuated as `G.D.H.Qu.S.M.` without expanding
its letters. The source date is the literal `28.10.`.

The shared subject makes the parallel useful, but `1225`/`1227`, the recipient
strings, the date evidence and `VON`/`IN` remain separate. This is not treated
as an exact re-encryption of the whole first part.

## p102 B2

The same p102 B header identifies `2 TL RICHI-200`. All 200 source
coordinates are valid.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame**

```text
WAHRSCHEINLICHDASXAUSDERXSUEUSLAVISCHENXDIVXGEBILDETEXDETAIHEMENTXMRGTRXMNFZ2RGTRXKAVXMITGEBIRGSAR5L
```

**Edited output — explicitly priced coordinate repairs and mask fills**

```text
WAHRSCHEINLICHDASXAUSDERXSUEDSLAVISCHENXDIVXGEBILDETEXDETACHEMENTX2RGTRXINFX2RGTRXKAVXMITGEBIRGSARTL
```

</details>

**Readable German — from the edited layer**

> Wahrscheinlich das aus der suedslavischen Div. gebildete Detachement. 2 Rgtr. Inf. 2 Rgtr. Kav. mit Gebirgsartl.

The selected candidate uses six observed-coordinate substitutions and no
fills. The unchanged numeral `2` in p101 B2 supports an explicitly priced
repair of p102's raw `MRGTR` to `2RGTR`. The raw
`5` inside `AR5L` is repaired locally to `T`; no other numeral occurrence
or substitution-square entry changes.

### Copy agreement and extra shared-word repair

The two detachment records have **192 identical observed coordinates**,
**seven observed conflicts**, and **one complementary mask**. All
**128 minimum common streams** are preserved in the certificate. Their
aggregate substitution cost is seven, and they all retain the shared raw
word error `SUEUSLAVISCHEN`.

The chosen complete candidate costs three substitutions in p101 B2 and
six in p102 B2, for **nine combined substitutions**, plus the one p101 source
mask fill. The two operations above the minimum are the additional shared
source-44 change `A`→`G`, once in each copy, to obtain `SUEDSLAVISCHEN`.
Thus the fluent word is an additional priced repair; the copies do not
independently confirm it through an unchanged coordinate. The body wording,
unit labels and all individual conflicting values remain inspectable.

## p102 B3

The third part is `3 TL RICHI-192`. It has 192 valid coordinates. The
[detail of `VGDGD`](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p102_B3_VGDGD.png)
shows a `D` at source 152, not an invalid `L`; no fill is charged or claimed
at that position.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame**

```text
AUSXAGEDESXSERBISCHENOFFIZIERSDER3BATTR3FELDARTLRGTSXDONAUDIEXNXOX11NR2429VOM19X10XVODOHL11X0626
```

**Edited output — explicitly priced coordinate repairs and mask fills**

```text
AUSSAGEDESXSERBISCHENOFFIZIERSDER3BATTR3FELDARTLRGTSXDONAUDIEXNXOX11NR2429VOM19X10XVODOHL11X0626
```

</details>

**Readable German — from the edited layer**

> Aussage des serbischen Offiziers der 3 Battr. 3 Feldartl. Rgts. Donaudie. N.O. 11 Nr. 2429 vom 19.10. VODOHL 11. 0626.

All 96 raw positions are fixed. One observed substitution, source 51
`X`→`V`, supplies `AUSSAGE` in place of `AUSXAGE`. The passage attributes
the report to a Serbian officer and gives the literal designations
`3 BATTR 3 FELDARTL RGTS`, followed by `DONAUDIE` and reference strings.
`DONAUDIE` is not silently converted to a different unit abbreviation, and
`VODOHL` remains unexpanded. The numbers `3`, `11`, `2429`, `19.10.` and
`0626` keep their exact encoded forms, including the leading zero.

## Evidence and attribution

The published `Nov1-3` square and ranks retain the credit of **George Lasry,
Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**. The current source and arithmetic
review is by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Earlier unreviewed OCR
candidates are retained in the [prior-evidence snapshot](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/prior_evidence.json).
No first historical decipherment priority is claimed. The existing
[p100 challenge](../p100.md) is a separate A message and keeps Armin's earlier
body credit; its status is unchanged.

[Literal rows, key and source images](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/inputs.json),
[recomputed domains and complete ledgers](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/certificates.json)
and [verification commands](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/README.md)
make the stated frames and repairs reproducible. The verifier also checks
that each readable passage preserves every non-`X` label in its cited stream.

# p137 A6 — Conditional publicity fragment in an interference-damaged report

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and conditional reconstruction: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**
The sixth part preserves 74 coordinate slots after an explicit interference
annotation. A language-guided proposal places `DER OEFFENTLICHKEIT` and
`BLEIBEN` in a conditional 254-slot frame. Its **25 proposed letters retain
15 observed halves and supply 35 absent halves**. None of the 71 received
valid coordinates is changed. These words are conditional proposals, not
cipher-only recoveries or a completed sentence.

## p137 A6

**Readable German — conditional word fragments only; the intervening fourteen positions remain unresolved:**

> […] der Oeffentlichkeit […] bleiben […]

The central noun means “the public.” The excerpt does not establish whether
something was to remain hidden, become known, or remain available to the public.
Both the polarity and the intervening verb have materially different
zero-change alternatives. No event or policy is inferred from this fragment.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 254-slot frame with 180 added leading unknown coordinates; published Nov4–6 key; 0/127 fixed plaintext positions:**

```text
???????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????
```

</details>

Every plaintext position lacks at least one coordinate in this frame. The
received halves still constrain letter domains, but do not independently
fix even one complete letter pair.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — 25 proposed letters at positions 13–30 and 45–51; zero observed substitutions, zero printed-mask fills and 35 added-slot fills:**

```text
?????????????DEROEFFENTLICHKEIT??????????????BLEIBEN???????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????
```

</details>

**102 plaintext positions remain unassigned**, including all fourteen positions
31–44. Of the 180 inferred leading coordinates, 145 remain unknown, and all
three original printed dashes remain unfilled. The candidate is a partial
assignment within a proposed frame; the original gives no total length.

## Exact support and semantic alternatives

All indices below are zero-based. A received half is a constraint on a letter,
not an independently fixed letter.

| Proposed word | Plaintext positions, inclusive | Observed halves retained | Added-slot fills | Wholly absent letters |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `DER` | 13–15 | 2 | 4 | 1 |
| `OEFFENTLICHKEIT` | 16–30 | 9 | 21 | 6 |
| `BLEIBEN` | 45–51 | 4 | 10 | 3 |
| **Primary proposal** | **25 positions** | **15** | **35** | **10** |

The ten wholly unobserved proposed letters are **15 R, 17 E, 19 F, 22 T,
25 C, 26 H, 29 I, 46 L, 49 B and 51 N**. Their two coordinates are both
supplied. The fifteen remaining proposed letters each retain exactly one
received half.

The discovery model suggested the fuller wording
`DEROEFFENTLICHKEITNICHTVERBORGENBLEIBEN`. Its apparent fluency does not resolve
two independent ambiguities:

| Unresolved span | Equal-price examples | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| 31–35 | `NICHT`, `IMMER`, `LANGE` | “Not,” “always” and “for a long time” differ materially. |
| 36–44 | `VERBORGEN`, `VERGOENNT` | “Hidden” and “granted/allowed” support different readings. |

All six combinations have **39 assigned letters, 23 observed halves and
55 added-slot fills**, with zero observed-coordinate changes. Each has
sixteen wholly unobserved letters. They are separately priced alternatives,
not equally established historical sentences. The primary output therefore
leaves both spans unread. Other local dictionary matches also exist;
this list does not exhaust all possible wording. Even `DER` and `BLEIBEN`
remain language-guided choices within their coordinate domains.

## Conditional length and neighboring parts

| Frame | Added leading unknown coordinates | Raw fixed positions | Primary proposed positions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 254 slots | 180 | 0/127 | 25/127 |
| 256 slots | 182 | 0/128 | 25/128 |
| 258 slots | 184 | 0/129 | 25/129 |

The **entire first 127 plaintext positions have identical received-source
ownership** in these three frames. The longer two merely add one or two
wholly unobserved positions. The source cannot choose among them. The
254-slot frame is a representative of this equivalence, not a recovered
transmitted length. An independent check of the exact sparse 25-letter
pattern examined 106,953 placements across every even length 74–1000. Of
3,724 placements retaining at least fifteen observed halves, only these
three models at offset 13 fit without a change. This bounded compatibility
check excludes neither lower-support placements nor other loss patterns,
wording or longer frames.

A separately priced `VON` at 124–126 is compatible in the 254-slot model:
it retains two observed halves and supplies four missing coordinates.
Its `V` is wholly absent, and it is excluded from the primary output.
The proposed neighboring p129 A7 begins with the fully observed
`ALLGEMEINERHIERNICHTBEKANNTERPOLITISCHERLAGE`, which makes a connection through
“von” plausible. The [cross-page report assembly](transylvania_situation_report.md)
remains conditional: the 5/6 November headings and receipt times conflict.
That context supplies no missing A6 coordinate. The earlier A5 repairs and
A7 printed-dash fill retain their separate costs.

## Source and verification

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — all 74 printed slots, preserving the three dashes:**

```text
DXXAF FVAAG FAVDA VVFAX VAXVV
---FV AAXGX VGGAV GXDGF XFAFG DAAGX FXVFA
GXXAF FVXGA XGVX
```

</details>

The original labels this `6TL` and prints `RICHI` without a length. The leading
`(interference)` annotation supports a loss hypothesis but supplies no count.
The source edition retains the three dashes at source positions 25–27 and
keeps the inferred leading loss separate from them.

The [experiment and exact certificates](../../experiments/p137_publicity_fragment/README.md)
provide the source crop, source-owner maps, forward-encryption witnesses,
letter-level repair costs, frame-equivalence proof and adverse semantic
alternatives. Discovery uses the already audited exact word/bigram dynamic
program; its optimum is exact only within that declared scoring model.
Full-length-family shuffled controls are diagnostic comparisons, not a
probability that the proposed text is correct. A fresh 127-letter control
ranked its true frame first among 264 lengths but recovered only 54 true
letters, directly demonstrating that fluent model wording can be wrong.
No independent native copy
of this clause or of `OEFFENTLICHKEIT` has been found in the searched corpus.

**Verification command — independent source and candidate checks:**

```sh
python experiments/p137_publicity_fragment/verify.py --verify
```

The historical source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX
Cipher System*, printed p137 / PDF p140. The period key and prior cryptanalysis
retain their attribution to George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno
Wacker. The new conditional fragment, counterexamples and source audit are
by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

# p152 A2 — Proposed report on crossing attempts

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and partial word edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** The unchanged 128-slot frame gives 61/64 fixed native labels. Seven observed-coordinate substitutions and two printed-mask fills give a proposed 63/64-position reading about crossing attempts. The negative KEINE is part of that proposed repair, not a native source-fixed statement.

## p152 A2

**Readable German — conditional word edition; name and complete footer retained literally:**

> Bis VARC8IORO?A keine Uebergangsversuche. A O0Q 17 ROED 1Q NR V054.

The proposed wording means that no crossing attempts are reported as far as the place encoded VARC8IORO?A. Its 8 and unresolved position remain literal. The entire closing field A O0Q 17 ROED 1Q NR V054 is retained, without changing it to a familiar headquarters signature or historical numeral.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — all 128 printed slots, including E and two dashes:**

```text
GEAFD AFFVX VVGAF AADVF DADVF FAVDX DAAXD GAVGF
DFDFD VXA-- DDGVA FXAFF DAFAV FVXGG XXDGF GGGXF
AAAXV AVGGA FFVGF DFDXV AVGFD DXFVA FAVFA FGFAG
VDVVD AFD
```

**Raw output — unchanged Nov4–6 key, native order and length:**

```text
BIHVARC8IORO?AK1ILEPEVERG?NGVXERSU?HEXXAXO0QX17XROEDX1QXNRXV054X
```

**Edited output — seven observed substitutions and two printed-mask fills; native frame and opaque name retained:**

```text
BISVARC8IORO?AKEINEUEBERGANGSVERSUCHEXXAXO0QX17XROEDX1QXNRXV054X
```

</details>

The changed observed source indices are 15, 31, 39, 40, 47, 78 and 79. The two printed dashes at 48–49 are filled. Printed E at source 1 remains an unresolved coordinate; it produces one of {2,3,B,H,S,V} at name position 12. All six complete re-encryption witnesses remain in the certificate.

## Place spelling: separately priced alternatives

An independent 1896 primary source prints **VERCSIOROVA**, supplying a rare CS spelling for comparison with the opaque place label. The inspected National Széchényi Library scan is *Természettudományi Közlöny*, printed p159 / PDF p6, a report of the botanical section's January 8 meeting. Its short locality statement reads “1885-ben pedig Vercsiorova alatt szedte.” The Romanian National History Museum also catalogues a 1901–1915 postcard under Verciorova, inventory 385510.

The 1896 source supports the place-name comparison; it does not attest the exact A-vowel spelling VARCSIOROVA or the proposed telegram's negative statement. The two alternatives below therefore keep their own complete coordinate prices.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Edited output — optional VARCSIOROVA spelling; nine total observed substitutions and three total mask fills:**

```text
BISVARCSIOROVAKEINEUEBERGANGSVERSUCHEXXAXO0QX17XROEDX1QXNRXV054X
```

**Edited output — optional attested VERCSIOROVA spelling; eleven total observed substitutions and three total mask fills:**

```text
BISVERCSIOROVAKEINEUEBERGANGSVERSUCHEXXAXO0QX17XROEDX1QXNRXV054X
```

</details>

Supplying S for literal 8 and V for the masked name position adds two observed substitutions and one mask fill to the primary reading. Changing VARCSIOROVA to the independently attested VERCSIOROVA costs two further observed substitutions. The primary edition leaves both normalizations unselected.

[1896 primary scan, p6](https://epa.oszk.hu/02100/02181/00319/pdf/EPA02181_Termeszettudomanyi_kozlony_1896_154-160.pdf#page=6) · [MNIR postcard inventory 385510](https://imagoromaniae.ro/produs/gara-in-verciorova/) · [Attestation metadata](../../experiments/p152_crossing_fragment/place_attestation.json).

## Source and credit

Childs printed p152 / PDF p155, section A2, RICHI-128. Literal header: `A) UKS v ZON (--- November 7th); 2 TL; RICHI-128`. A first part is not supplied by this edition.

[Original Childs scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Source package](../../experiments/p152_crossing_fragment/README.md) · [Exact certificate](../../experiments/p152_crossing_fragment/certificates.json).

The period key retains the Lasry-team credit. Earlier source inspection and unchanged-key outputs are prior work. The present contribution is an explicitly priced partial word edition, preserving its uncertain place label, raw footer and complete source, with an independently inspected historical place-spelling comparison.

## Reproduce

```sh
python experiments/p152_crossing_fragment/verify.py --verify
python experiments/p152_crossing_fragment/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
python experiments/p152_crossing_fragment/verify.py --verify --attestation-pdf /path/to/EPA02181_Termeszettudomanyi_kozlony_1896_154-160.pdf
```

# p154 A2 — Weisskirchen halt and security fragment

[All cases](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Recovery and review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 4 November 2026.**
A newly reviewed frame recovers the phrases **Weisskirchen angehalten** and
**Sicherungen an den** from the previously unframed second part. The unchanged
published November 4–6 key fixes **36/81 raw positions**; a separately priced
word layer fixes **56/81**. The preceding passage remains incomplete.

## Reading

**Readable German — excerpts from the explicitly repaired word layer; absent passages remain omitted:**

> […] Weisskirchen angehalten. […] Sicherungen an den […]

**Meaning:** The surviving phrases mention a halt involving Weisskirchen and
security arrangements at locations whose description is incomplete. They do
not identify who was halted or establish the missing geographical endpoints.
The opening `21` is retained as an uninterpreted square-label field.

## Source and frame

Childs, printed p154 / PDF p157, gives `A) UKS v ZON (11.55 p.m., November 7th); 2 TL; RICHI-162`.
The [other message on the same page](airfield_german_troop_fragment.md) also
uses the November 4–6 key successfully. The two records have different station
directions and times; they are not joined as parts of one report.

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — all 118 observed coordinates, including the six-character group VDFDVD:**

```text
FXFXF AADVX XDDAV DFGXX DAAXV VDFDVD XXFVA
DAFXA FGVFV AFXFV XXVDV XVAXV DVVVG XXFAD
DVDXF AFXXA FAGFV VFXFF GGVFA XGXVF GAFAA
AFVGX ADGVA VF
```

</details>

The source contains 118 observed coordinates and no printed masks, against
its advertised 162. The primary frame makes two explicit assumptions:

1. Exclude the `D` at zero-based source index 28, the fourth character of
   `VDFDVD`, leaving the five-coordinate group `VDFVD` in the analysis stream.
2. Prepend 45 unknown transmitted slots to the remaining 117 observations.

The literal source is unchanged. One observed coordinate is excluded; all
other 117 observations retain their values and relative order. The source
prints no 45-coordinate gap. This frame reconciles the six-character group
and header length, but does not establish how the text was historically lost.

## Raw and edited output

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 162-slot frame and unchanged key; 36/81 fixed positions; one excluded observation, no coordinate substitutions or fills:**

```text
21??X??B?I?A??B??AR??X??R?G?R??U??ED??W??S?K?R??E??NG??A??E?X?T??HE?UN??N?ND?N?U?
```

**Edited output — the same frame; 2 observed-coordinate substitutions and 20 inserted-slot fills; 56/81 fixed positions:**

```text
21??X??B?I?A??B??AR??X??R?G?R??U??ED??WEISSKIRCHENANGEHALTENX?SICHERUNGENANDEN?U?
```

</details>

| Proposed fragment | Zero-based plaintext start | Observed substitutions | Added-slot fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| WEISSKIRCHENANGEHALTEN | 38 | source 94 `F→V` | 13 |
| SICHERUNGENANDEN | 62 | source 106 `A→G` | 7 |

The excluded source 28 `D` is separate from these two substitutions. Each of
the 20 newly fixed word positions has one observed half-coordinate; none is
wholly unobserved. Twenty-five plaintext positions remain unresolved. No
opening word, numeral value, intervening heading or final destination is
supplied from context.

An independent contemporary spelling witness appears in the U.S. War
Department's *Histories of Two Hundred and Fifty-One Divisions of the German
Army* (compiled in 1919, published in 1920), Alpine Corps history, printed p10.
It records **Weisskirchen** in a 1915 movement narrative. This supports the
name's spelling, not this telegram's unit, event or unique geographical
identification; [source metadata](../../experiments/p154_weisskirchen_fragment/historical_context.json)
keeps the distinction explicit.

## Search and review

The discovery tested each of the six characters in `VDFDVD` as the surplus
coordinate, with a single 45-coordinate loss at every shortened-stream boundary:
**708 models**. The primary ranked first in that family. Three fresh controls
gave planted-frame ranks 5, 1, 1; the first control's leader shifted the gap by one
position and produced one wrong fixed letter. The other two recovered the
correct fixed text. Exact loss placement remains conditional.

The [replay and comparison details](../../experiments/p154_weisskirchen_fragment/README.md)
retain the separate length diagnostic, shuffled controls and more complex
two-gap alternatives. A separate length diagnostic ranked the advertised 162
first. The simpler one-prefix frame remains primary; the incomplete opening
is not filled from language-model suggestions.

[Complete coordinate and edit certificate](../../experiments/p154_weisskirchen_fragment/certificates.json)
· [Search scope, controls and replay](../../experiments/p154_weisskirchen_fragment/README.md).
The source crop is authenticated against the original PDF. Independent column
arithmetic reproduces the raw domains, all repairs and complete re-encryption
witnesses; arbitrary residual witness fills are not historical text.

## Credit

Historical source: J. Rives Childs. Published November 4–6 key: George Lasry,
Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and Lasry's 2017 key list.
Source-frame discovery, word review and edition: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

# p163 A — Withdrawal instructions and headquarters movements

[All cases](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** Readable fragments of a multipart order, with all proposed repairs
recorded. Parts 13–15 and 17–18 survive; the unnumbered, jammed fragment between
parts 15 and 17 has no established complete frame; a separate conditional
clause is linked below. **Source edition and review:**
icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. **Period key:** George Lasry and colleagues.

## Most likely reading

The message concerns the withdrawal from Romania: keep Crajova and Bukarest
strongly occupied until the last moment, evacuate in one move, retain a
Bucharest garrison, and plan the movements of Scholtz's headquarters and the
army high command. The proposed reading of part 15 joins a sentence across a
part boundary and identifies the garrison's later transfer to Scholtz.

### Parts 13–15: evacuation and the Bucharest garrison

**Readable German — edited excerpts; absent text remains omitted:**

> … zu erfolgen. Hierbei ist zu beachten, dass Crajova und Bukarest bis zum
> letzten Augenblick stark besetzt — Bukarest 4 Bataillone — bleiben muessen
> und ihre endgueltige Raeumung mit einem Schlage erfolgen muss. Befehl zu
> letzterer erteilt O.K.M. I.R. 204 bleibt zur Besetzung von Bukarest,
> Generalkommando {5/6}3 unterstellt, und wird nach Ankunft in Kronstadt
> O.K. Scholtz zugefuehrt. …

**Meaning:** Crajova and Bucharest are to retain strong garrisons until the last
moment; four battalions are specified for Bucharest. Their final evacuation is
to take place in a single move. The proposed continuation leaves I.R. 204 to
garrison Bucharest, subordinate to Generalkommando {5/6}3, and transfers it to
O.K. Scholtz after reaching Kronstadt.

This passage combines two relatively complete parts with a much less complete
third. Part 13 begins with an unresolved 20-character span. Its received
268 coordinates differ from the printed `RICHI-278` header. No ten-coordinate
restoration is asserted. The reading uses the visible 268-position frame.

Part 15 has 234 printed slots, including two lines of dashes. Only **36/117**
raw plaintext positions are singletons. The proposed 91-position prefix costs
**two substitutions of known coordinates and 63 erasure fills**. Its coherent
wording and the part-14 continuation support the reconstruction; those fills
are not claimed to be uniquely forced. The final 26 positions remain
uncompleted in that earlier prefix edition. Spacing and punctuation in the
quotation are editorial.

A [linked rearguard-position supplement](../../experiments/p163_rearguard_continuation/README.md)
now proposes the complete part-15 tail `X7XAUSDER3XNACHHUTSTELLUNG`, giving
“7. Aus der 3. Nachhutstellung …” without supplying the action in the missing
continuation. It retains 33 of the tail's 34 observed coordinates and costs
**one further observed substitution and 18 mask fills**. The complete proposed
part has **116/117 fixed positions**, up from the earlier layer's 98, at totals
of **three substitutions and 81 fills**. Its sole unresolved square digit
remains the coupled `5`/`6` choice. Every newly supplied tail letter has an
observed half; the inherited prefix's wholly absent letter remains identified.

Part 13 independently supports the same `NACHHUTSTELLUNG` sequence at its
opening. The word-only extension adds **three substitutions and two fills**,
retaining raw `ALS3Q`; the separator and the contextual `AUS` preposition
cost one and two more substitutions respectively. The two remaining mask
positions become assigned under each word proposal. Requiring the two spans
to repeat one string leaves **96 joint minimum strings** at four observed
substitutions across their word spans. The military term is a contextual
selection among these, supported by independent historical vocabulary.
`ALS` versus `AUS`, and part 15's equal-price `DER` versus `NUR`, remain explicit
alternatives. The supplementary certificate and exact German displays retain
each layer; the original readings below remain the separately priced baseline.

The [unnumbered jammed continuation now has a separate conditional clause](p163_infrastructure_clause.md)
concerning the destruction of railways, roads and telephone lines. Its 121
received coordinates are unchanged. The 59-position proposal supplies 65
coordinates in an inferred missing prefix and leaves 84 plaintext positions
unread. Equivalent 284- and 286-coordinate frames, six wholly absent proposed
letters, and the optional unobserved heading `8` remain explicit. This does
not establish the fragment's transmitted length or complete the rest of point 7.

### Parts 17–18: Danube boats and headquarters

**Readable German — edited excerpts; absent text remains omitted:**

> … erfolgt noch Befehl. Ebenso betreffend Donauwachtboote und sonstiger
> Schiffsgefaesse. 9. O.K. Scholtz geht voraussichtlich am 13.11. nach
> Calimanesti, spaeter nach Hermannstadt. Generalkommando {5/6}3 am
> 1{5/6}.11. nach Kronstadt. [10.] O.K.M. verbleibt vorlaufig Bukarest,
> verlegt spaeter Hauptquartier nach Sinaia. O.K.M. Ia 11313 op. geh.

**Meaning:** Further orders will follow concerning the Danube guard boats and
other vessels. Scholtz's headquarters is expected to move to Calimanesti on
13 November and later to Hermannstadt. A corps headquarters is to move to
Kronstadt on the stated mid-November date. O.K.M. will initially remain in
Bucharest and later transfer its headquarters to Sinaia.

The two parts contain numerous isolated source garbles. The edition preserves
the unexpanded spelling `VORLAUFIG`; the readable German meaning is
*vorläufig*. The numbered heading `10` is a proposal supported by the preceding
heading `9`: raw position 66 has domain `DEQTUX`, so zero requires a recorded
known-coordinate substitution and an erasure fill. It is not a cipher-only
digit recovery. The original closing reference is garbled; `Ia 11313 op. geh.`
is also part of the explicitly repaired edition.

An [independent AOK 11 map](../../experiments/p163_headquarters_map_context/README.md),
CAMO / TsAMO 500-12519-274, places O.K. Scholtz at Calimanesti during the
13–18 November withdrawal interval. This supports the existing one-coordinate
`CA2IMANESTI` → `CALIMANESTI` repair in part 17. It adds no plaintext positions
or repairs and gives no individual date for that headquarters symbol. The
map's separate O.K. Mackensen symbol at Hermannstadt is not evidence that
Scholtz had already reached that town. Both original map details and their
pixel provenance accompany the review.

## Source and exact repair account

Childs, printed p. 163 / PDF p. 166, gives:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
INTERCEPTED BY BRITISH STATIONS.
9th NOVEMBER, 1918.
A) --- v UKS (1.21 a.m., November 9th)
```

</details>

| Source part | Header / visible slots | Raw fixed positions | Proposed known-coordinate substitutions | Proposed erasure fills |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 13 | `RICHI-278` / 268 | 126/134 | 10 | 6 |
| 14 | `RICHI-244` / 244 | 121/122 | 5 | 1 |
| 15 | `RICHI-234` / 234 | 36/117 | 2 | 63 |
| Unnumbered, `J'md` | No surviving length / 121 | No complete frame | — | — |
| 17 | `RICHI-264` / 264 | 125/132 | 16 | 6 |
| 18 | `RICHI-310` / 310 | 131/155 | 21 | 24 |

A fixed raw position can be a historical transmission or copying error. The
third column counts what the given source and key determine, including such
garbles, rather than asserting that every character is correct German.

The complete literal rows, every raw domain, every proposed edit and the
focused source images are in the
[recovery package](../../experiments/withdrawal_recovery/README.md).

## Conditional shared digits

The existing, separately justified
[historical November 7–9 square layer](../../experiments/p170_continuation/military_context.json)
assigns `VF=6`, `XA=5`, using the identification of the 6th Reserve Division.
Applying that same layer here gives:

| Field | Cipher-only evidence | Under the existing historical layer |
|---|---|---|
| Part 15 corps | Unchanged `VF` at position 26, domain `56`; next proposed character is `3` | 63 |
| Part 18 corps | Raw `K` at position 40; the edition changes one coordinate to cell `VF` | 63, after that explicit repair |
| Part 18 departure date | Unchanged `XA` at position 46, domain `56` | 15 November |

All positions above are zero-based. The original key remains unchanged.
The numeral inference and the editorial repairs can be accepted separately.
The raw part-17 unknown cell also becomes `6` under the same global assignment;
the readable edition proposes a separator there and records its substitution.

## Raw plaintexts

The question marks below retain source or square uncertainty, and the original
garbles are left untouched.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — per-part conservative source frames; missing part-15 tail remains unknown:**

```text

ALS3QIA2HHUB?TE?LUNGZUE?F??GEN?HIERBEIISTZUBEACHTENXDASSXCRAJOVAXWNAXBPKARESTBISEI?LETGTEN2UGENBLICKSTARKBE?ETZTXBUKA2EST4XBATANLLONEX

BLEIBENMUESSENUNDIHREENDGUELTIGERAEUMUNGMITEINEMS1HLAGEYFOLGENMUSSXBEFEHLZULETZTERERER9EI?TXOKMXIXRX2C4XBLEIBBZURBESETZUNG

15:
??N?U?A???T?E?E?????M?A?D?????N?T?S?E?????D???D???H?N???F???K?O???A???X?X???O???Z?G???E???X?7???S???3?N???H???B?L???G

ERFOGGTNOCHBEFEHL??BENSOBETR?FFENTDONAUWACHTBOOTJUND?ONSTIGERSCHIF2LGEFAESSEX9XWKXSCHOLT?GEHTVOR2USSICB?L9CHAM13H11XNA?OXCA2IMANESTI

18:
GP2GTERNA2?XHERMANIGTADTXGENERALKOMMANDOK3?A?1??1?HNACHKR?NWTNDTX1?XOKM??ERBLEIBTVORLA?NIGBYKARELTX?ERL?GTSPA?TE?HAUPT??AY?I?RNROHLINA?A?O?MX1II?313OPXGE?X
```

## Credit and reproduction

The source intercepts belong to Childs's collection. The period key retains the
earlier Lasry-team credit. This is a new repository source edition and review
by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**, without a first-historical-decipherment
claim. The inspected Lasry–Niebel–Kopal–Wacker author manuscript does not

# p163 A16 — Conditional infrastructure clause in a jammed continuation

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and conditional reconstruction: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**
The unnumbered fragment between parts 15 and 17 permits a partial clause about
the destruction of railways, roads and telephone lines. Its **121 received
coordinates remain unchanged**. The proposed 59-character clause depends on
an inferred missing prefix and supplies 65 absent coordinates; it is a
conditional partial reading, not a complete message or a recovered frame length.

## p163 A16

**Readable German — conditional clause in the 286-slot model; the first omission remains unread:**

> […] Wegen Zerstoerung von Eisenbahnen, Strassen und Telephonleitungen …

The following part's earlier edited opening is “erfolgt noch Befehl,” giving
the possible sense: further orders will follow concerning the destruction of
these facilities. This is an order about a future decision, not evidence that
all the listed facilities were destroyed. The continuation is separately
priced: A17 natively reads `ERFOGGTNOCHBEFEHL`, and the prior edition changes
source coordinate 172 from `G` to `D` to obtain `ERFOLGTNOCHBEFEHL`.
Its `NOCHBEFEHL` portion is entirely observed without changes. None of that
inherited repair is counted as a new A16 correction.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 286-slot frame with 165 added leading unknown coordinates; unchanged Nov7–9 partial key; 0/143 fixed positions:**

```text
???????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????
```

</details>

The received source constrains one half of many letter pairs, even though it
does not fully determine a single plaintext position in this model. The
certificate retains every half-coordinate domain and its received-source owner.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — proposed clause at positions 84–142; zero observed substitutions, zero printed-mask fills and 65 added-slot fills; 59/143 assigned positions:**

```text
????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????WEGENZERSTOERUNGVONEISENBAHNENXSTRASSENUNDTELEPHONLEITUNGEN
```

</details>

The first **84 plaintext positions** remain unresolved, including the optional
numbered heading. Of the 165 inferred missing coordinates, 100 remain
unassigned in this primary edited stream. No observed coordinate is deleted,
reordered or altered, and none of the 165 added slots is described as a printed
dash. The original only says `J'md` and gives no numerical loss count.

## Exact support and absent letters

The 59-position proposal contains **53 observed half-coordinates**, all retained,
and **65 supplied absent halves**. Fifty-three proposed positions retain one
observed half each; the remaining six have neither half observed. Their
zero-based plaintext indices and proposed letters are **92 S, 102 N, 112 E,
122 N, 132 O and 142 N**. These six letters are contextual supplies, not
independently recovered characters.

| Proposed segment | Plaintext positions, inclusive | Observed halves retained | Wholly unobserved positions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `WEGEN` | 84–88 | 5 | 0 |
| `ZERSTOERUNG` | 89–99 | 10 | 1 |
| `VON` | 100–102 | 2 | 1 |
| `EISENBAHNEN` | 103–113 | 10 | 1 |
| `X` | 114 | 1 | 0 |
| `STRASSEN` | 115–122 | 7 | 1 |
| `UND` | 123–125 | 3 | 0 |
| `TELEPHONLEITUNGEN` | 126–142 | 15 | 2 |

The separate proposal `8X` at 82–83 adds two assigned positions and three
added-slot fills, bringing the optional layer to 61/143. The `8` is wholly
unobserved. Numbered headings 7 and 9 in the neighboring parts motivate it;
they do not turn it into a cipher-only numeral recovery. It is omitted from
the primary edited output above.

## Two indistinguishable frame models

The source retains no part number or transmitted length. `A16` is the local
positional label used by the corpus census, based on its location between
printed parts 15 and 17. It is not transcribed from the fragment's header.

| Conditional frame | Added leading unknown coordinates | Ending proposal | Observed changes | Added-slot fills for the clause |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 286 slots / 143 positions | 165 | `WEGEN…TELEPHONLEITUNGEN` | 0 | 65 |
| 284 slots / 142 positions | 163 | `WEGEN…TELEPHONLEITUNGX` | 0 | 63 |

The two models give **identical native coordinate pairs and identical
received-source ownership at all first 142 plaintext positions**. The
286-slot model adds one wholly unobserved final position. Thus the received
ciphertext cannot distinguish these two lengths. Plural wording is a contextual
choice, not a proof of 286 slots. The shorter model retains the singular noun
and final proposed `X` separator as an explicit alternative.

The proposed connector `UND` also has equal-price alternatives `MIT` and `WIE`
at 123–125. The certificate prices them separately. Their arithmetic
compatibility does not establish equally suitable historical meanings.
No full text is asserted for the unknown opening or for the remainder of
point 7 from the previous part.

## Source and independent checks

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — all 121 received coordinates in printed order; no added prefix is included here:**

```text
FVVAX XAGVD VGDXV VGDVV VGDDX VXGGG XXGVG
DDVVV DGXVV DXGVX VFDDD DXGXV GDXAX VGDVD GDGVV
GDVVG GAGVV VVVVX XVVAG DADXD DDDXD DXXGA DDDDG
XXGXD A
```

</details>

The page labels this fragment `J'md` and `RICHI----`. Its first surviving row
has seven five-coordinate groups; two full rows and the final six coordinates
follow. Treating the jamming mark as missing material before this suffix is an
explicit model. Group alignment can motivate candidate lengths, but cannot
supply a vanished header or prove how many groups were lost.

![Original jammed fragment between parts 15 and 17](../../experiments/p163_infrastructure_clause/sources/p163_unlabelled.png)

The [focused package](../../experiments/p163_infrastructure_clause/README.md)
rebuilds the source map, both frame models, exact repair prices, unfilled domains,
connector alternatives and optional heading. Independent column arithmetic and
full round trips check both injective assignments of the key's unresolved
`5`/`6` cells. Witness-only fills of other missing coordinates do not enter the
published partial reading. Native messages provide separate vocabulary witnesses
for several component words; they are not copies of this clause.

[Inputs and source identity](../../experiments/p163_infrastructure_clause/inputs.json)
· [Per-position certificate](../../experiments/p163_infrastructure_clause/certificates.json)
· [Earlier parts and separately priced A17](p163_A.md)
· [Original PDF, printed p163 / PDF p166](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).

**Reproduction:**

```sh
python experiments/p163_infrastructure_clause/verify.py --verify
```

The period key and earlier cryptanalytic work retain the credit to George Lasry,
Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker. The earlier source transcription is
preserved exactly. The new conditional clause, independent audit and source
review are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

# Withdrawal from the Danube and Sereth front: p175 C3

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source analysis and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This source-defined third part becomes readable under an explicit
five-coordinate loss model. It reports a withdrawal toward the mountains
from the Danube and Sereth front, with a route via Kronstadt and
Hermannstadt. **The plaintext and source alignment remain conditional**:
six placements of one contiguous missing block fit the edited candidate
at the same observed-coordinate cost, and a broader loss family has
six lower-cost alignments.

## The source and its length

Childs printed p175 C3, PDF p178, belongs to the six-part message under
`LP v NKJ (5.40 p.m., November 10th); VON UKS KR 0915 (10/11) 6 TLE`.
The [literal part](../../experiments/romanian_ultimatum_companions/sources/p175_C3.png)
contains **217** printed slots, including four dashes. The enlarged
[header](../../experiments/romanian_ultimatum_companions/sources/p175_C3_heading_detail.png)
reads **RICHI-222**. The length difference is therefore **five**, but
the page does not mark where those missing coordinates belong.

The older source package keeps this part as frozen unread context.
This follow-up adds one newly cataloged reading of the same physical
record; the other five source parts and the existing p176a challenge
are not counted again.

## Raw and edited output

For display, insert one five-coordinate erased block before source
coordinate **95**. This is the smallest of six equally cheap placements
for the candidate, chosen as a stable representative. All indices are
zero-based. The published **Nov10–12** square and ranks are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional frame with five missing coordinates:**

```text
OK?XG?HTHE?TENACHT?ONDONAU?UND?ERETHFR?NTAUFGE?IRGQQURUECKXWIRDUEBERXKRONSTADTXHERMANNSTADTXRIWHTUNGXKLUZ?NBUR0
```

**Edited output — same conditional frame:** Four observed-coordinate
substitutions, four printed-dash fills and five unprinted-coordinate
fills give the following **111-position candidate**:

```text
OKMXGEHTHEUTENACHTVONDONAUXUNDSERETHFRONTAUFGEBIRGEZURUECKXWIRDUEBERXKRONSTADTXHERMANNSTADTXRICHTUNGXKLUZENBURG
```

</details>

**Readable German — punctuation and word spacing of the conditional candidate; the final ellipsis marks continuation into the next part:**

> O.K.M. geht heute Nacht von Donau- und Serethfront auf Gebirge zurück.
> Wird über Kronstadt, Hermannstadt Richtung Kluzenburg …

The second sentence continues into the next source part. That part is
the separately attributed [p176a challenge](../p176a.md), whose earlier
breakthrough proposal has its own missing-block and editorial assumptions.
Its wording is not imported as independent proof of this reconstruction.

The source-derived spelling **KLUZENBURG** remains visible. The raw final
`0` is repaired through one specific observed-coordinate change; this
does not assign a new value to the key's `0` label. The interpretation
of `OKM` and the report's actual historical fulfillment are not separately
established by this source edition.

## Why there is no unique recovered gap

Every possible position for one contiguous five-coordinate loss was
checked: **218** source positions. Two frozen language models both rank
position **96** first, while several neighboring positions also produce
coherent partial readings. Ranking supplied a useful interval for
inspection, not a proof of a unique historical location.

For the complete candidate, the exact minimum over this family is four
observed-coordinate substitutions at each of these six gap starts:

```text
95, 96, 98, 99, 100, 101
```

If a whole five-letter group is assumed to have disappeared between
surviving printed groups, **95 and 100** remain tied. The source provides
no fixed omission marker to choose between them.

Allowing the five missing coordinates to be distributed arbitrarily
reduces the candidate's minimum to **three substitutions**. An exact
dynamic program over all missing-position sets finds **six** optimal
alignments, all with a local 1 + 3 + 1 loss pattern. Those six are also
fully retained. This broader result changes the loss assumption; it
does not prove that three separate losses actually occurred.

## Repair costs and evidence

The displayed placement at 95 changes source coordinates
**97 G→X, 172 D→A, 174 F→D, and 209 V→F**. It fills printed dashes
**57→D, 58→D, 59→F, and 119→V**, and inserts `VVGXX`.
The resulting candidate re-encrypts exactly. Every tied alternative
has its own source mapping and equally explicit certificate.

This one record has **217 printed slots**, **213 observed coordinates**,
a **222-coordinate conditional frame**, and **111 plaintext positions**.
The displayed raw frame fixes **102** labels; the edited candidate fixes
111. Across all 218 unselected one-block frames, the common singleton
reading fixes **zero** positions. Thus the readable raw text itself
depends on choosing a frame; the complete candidate is a further
editorial layer.

Twelve newly composed synthetic controls test the screening procedure.
Both models' predeclared primary objective places a truth-compatible
layout first in all twelve. Secondary objectives fail on some controls,
and the controls have no added observed-coordinate errors. They support
this bounded method, without providing a historical confidence percentage.
The models are also correlated through their shared book component.

The [full analysis](../../experiments/p175_c3_gap_followup/README.md),
[screen results](../../experiments/p175_c3_gap_followup/screen_results.json),
and [certificate](../../experiments/p175_c3_gap_followup/certificates.json)
preserve all layouts, controls, rankings, exact minima and source indices.
No key cell is changed, no first historical decipherment claim is made,
and no exact cross-copy was accepted from the bounded corpus search.

# p176 A6 — Conditional coal-train continuation via Klausenburg

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Partial word proposal and source review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**
The sixth part permits a coherent continuation about coal trains via
Klausenburg and the phrase “gerechnet werden.” This is a **context-conditioned
partial proposal**, supported by the preceding fifth part and compatible
with every observed sixth-part coordinate. The routing field and later tail
remain unread. No complete historical message or unique wording is claimed.

A [conditional repeated-place supplement](../../experiments/p176_repeated_place/README.md)
proposes `XKLAUSENBURGX` in the first omitted field. It adds **eleven fixed
positions**, reaching **59/80**, with **zero observed substitutions and
fifteen additional printed-mask fills**. All 74 observed coordinates remain
unchanged. The two copies are both partly supplied: repeating the earlier
proposed place is a separate hypothesis, not an independently received
complete-word witness.

The native spans force only five shared letters after assuming repetition;
each of the 120 injective square completions still admits **46,656** common
strings. `XBLANKENBURGX` fits the second span at the same price. Four newly
assigned positions have neither coordinate observed. The supplement retains
these limits, the inherited `N`/`X` alternative, and the entirely uncompleted
last 24 positions. The displays below preserve the separately priced earlier
edition; the supplement contains its full conditional stream and exact ledger.

## p176 A6

**Readable German — proposed spans at positions 0–27 and 41–55; both omissions remain unread in this excerpt:**

> Kohlenzuegen ueber Klausenburg […] gerechnet werden […]

The first `[…]` omits the 13-position field at 28–40; the second omits all
24 positions at 56–79. The full positional stream below retains their raw
`A`, `G`, `X` and `1` labels and every unresolved position. The excerpt
supplies no intervening place name, signature or reference number.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 160-slot frame, unchanged Nov10–12 partial key; 14/80 fixed positions:**

```text
??H????U??E????E??L????N??R????A???????G???????N???????N???????X???????1???????X
```

**Edited output — contextual partial word proposal in the same frame; zero observed-coordinate substitutions and 44 printed-mask fills; 48/80 fixed positions:**

```text
KOHLENZUEGENUEBERKLAUSENBURG???A???????G?GERECHNETWERDEN???????X???????1???????X
```

</details>

All **74 observed coordinates remain unchanged**. The proposal fills 44 of
86 already printed dashes; the other 42 coordinate masks remain unassigned.
The resulting 32 unresolved plaintext positions remain literal question marks.
No source slot is inserted, excluded, moved or copied from another message.
The 34 additional fixed output positions are proposed labels, rather than
34 independently authenticated historical characters.

## Why propose these words?

The printed header and consecutive part labels put A5 immediately before A6
in the same six-part message. Its previously edited ending begins
`KANNMITZUFUEHRUNGVON` and ends with the literal conjunction `UND`.
That syntax motivates dative plural `KOHLENZUEGEN` at the start of A6.
The exact native half-coordinate constraints also permit
`UEBERKLAUSENBURG` at positions 12–27 and `GERECHNETWERDEN` at 41–55.
These words are contextual proposals; compatibility does not prove them.

<details>
<summary>Earlier attributed reading</summary>

**Earlier attributed reading — A5 proposal by icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, reproduced with its unresolved field; not counted as a new record here:**


# p180 A — Enemy following the withdrawal near Giurgiu

[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source and certificate](../../experiments/operational_recovery/README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

and one printed-dash fill. The source date remains uncertain.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> Bei Giurgiu folgt Feind langsam. Braila, Focsani geraeumt.
> 11. Armee keine Ereignisse. OKM.

**Meaning:** The enemy follows slowly near Giurgiu; Braila and Focsani have
been evacuated. No events are reported for the 11th Army.

The second `1` in the proposed army number is an explicit repair to the
already known `1` square cell. It does not assign a duplicate `1` to an
unresolved cell. The other parts of this report have not been supplied.

All ten coordinate decisions are enumerated in the certificate. No length,

# p191 A — Boots and clothing for Oderberg

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status: body recovered with a conditional five-coordinate group move;
unit/quantity symbols and one connective remain unresolved.** The two
parts fix **196 of 200 plaintext positions** after four explicit
known-coordinate substitutions and twelve printed-dash fills. Their
lengths remain 214 and 186 coordinates, and the published key is unchanged.

The message asks a deputy corps command at Breslau to make boots and
heavy clothing available initially for Oderberg, on call and with advance
notice. A wire/radio reply is requested. The repaired signature is
`A.O.K.11`. The exact corps symbol and number of pairs of boots are not
supplied from historical plausibility.

## Proposed fixed-length reading

Part 1:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
SELLVXGENXKOMX?XAXKXBRESLAUXXBITTEWEGENDRINGENDERNOTLAGEINBEKLEIDUNGX?0?0XPAARSTIEFELZUNAECHSTNACHXODERBERG
```

</details>

Part 2:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — conditional move of printed group 12 before group 8, followed by word repairs:**

```text
UNTERVORMELDUNGMITSTARKERBEKLEIDNGAUFABRUFBEREITSTELLENXXDRAHTX?XFUNKANTWORTERBETENXXAXOXKX11
```

</details>

The literal spellings `SELLV` and `BEKLEIDNG` remain in these strings.
Expanding them in prose adds no characters to the ciphertext edition.
Punctuation, word division and abbreviation expansion are editorial.

The three unresolved part-1 symbols occupy distinct cells `GD`, `FV`
and `XX`, each with domain `{2,3,4,7,8,9,Q,Y}`. Their assignments must
be different. The part-2 connective keeps the full domain
`{0,2,3,4,7,8,9,O,Q,U,W,Y}`. Readable `O`/`U` possibilities do not
reduce that domain or select *oder* versus *und*.

### Compatibility with the shared headquarters reading

The later [XX=Q headquarters interpretation](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md#the-intendants-address)
has an adverse consequence here: the unaltered quantity becomes **`?0Q0`**.
It cannot be read as a decimal count without a source correction. Under
both that Q assignment and the independent [FX=Y courier-name interpretation](../caucasus/tiflis_appointment.md#the-separate-historical-name-inference),
the unique one-coordinate repair making this character numerical is
**X→D at source position 102**, giving **`?000`**. These indices are zero-based.
The possible quantities are 3000, 4000, 7000, 8000 or 9000; none is selected.
Without the Y assumption, other one-coordinate numerical repairs survive.

This is a priced compatibility proposal, not an additional recovered count.
The primary edition and its four unresolved positions above remain the
baseline. [Exact neighbouring-coordinate check](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/compatibility_certificate.json).

## The displaced group

The untouched second part decrypts to:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
UFTERAORVELDUHGMFJST?R?EPPEKLE?DN6AUFA?R?IBERE?T5KELLE??A?RAHT??CNUNKA?T?URTER?E?ENXXA?OEJX1?
```

</details>

Move printed group **12**, `AXFVA`, immediately before printed group
**8**, preserving all coordinate values and every other group order:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional move of printed group 12 immediately before group 8:**

```text
UNTERVORMELDUNGMITST?R?ERBEKLE?DNGAUFA?RUFBERE?TSTELLE??XDRAHT??XFUNKA?TWORTER?ETENXXA?O5KX1?
```

</details>

Only two further observed-coordinate changes are needed in this part,
both `F → V` at original coordinates 127 and 130, plus eleven dash
fills. One source erasure remains at the connective.

The geometry check masks the entire footer and uses 77 ordinary-word
positions, with no names, unit numbers or quantities. Across the identity
and **all one-complete-group moves** among 37 complete groups—1,333
operations, 1,297 distinct streams—the displayed move is the sole
zero-disagreement candidate. The untouched source has nineteen
ordinary-word coordinate disagreements. A fresh control with the same
length, twelve erased positions and group displacement likewise recovers
its true order as the unique zero-disagreement candidate.

The word mask was developed after inspecting the damaged source, so
this is a conditional consistency check, not a blind language experiment
or a proof that no other error mechanism is possible. The certificate
retains all minimizing operations, not a chosen tie.

## Source and exact accounting

[Source crop](../../experiments/boots_request/sources/childs_p191_A.png):
Childs printed p191 / PDF p194. The heading gives **14 November 1918**.
The header is `LP v ZÖN (06.16 p.m., November ?); 2301 (11/14) 2 TLE`;
the intercept-day question mark is preserved.

| Measure | Part 1 | Part 2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Coordinate slots / printed erasures | 214 / 1 | 186 / 12 |
| Untouched raw fixed positions | 102/107 | 76/93 |
| Proposed fixed positions | 104/107 | 92/93 |
| Five-coordinate group moves | 0 | 1 |
| Observed-coordinate substitutions | 2 | 2 |
| Printed-dash fills | 1 | 11 |
| Insertions / deletions | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

Part 1 repairs `D?INGENDER` and `S1IEFEL` with counted substitutions,
and fills its dash for the separator following the quantity. Part 2
repairs the adjective and footer separator after the group move. All
edits are expressed in original printed coordinates. Every value in the
remaining connective domain has a joint, injective square witness for
both messages; arbitrary witness digits are not proposed readings.

## Credit and reproduction

The Nov13–15b key retains its prior attribution to **George Lasry, Ingo
Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**. Source transcription, the local
group-displacement identification, explicit repairs and audit are by
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment
priority is claimed.

```sh
python experiments/boots_request/geometry.py --verify
python experiments/boots_request/verify.py --verify
```

The [inputs](../../experiments/boots_request/inputs.json),
[geometry certificate](../../experiments/boots_request/geometry_certificate.json),
[source certificate](../../experiments/boots_request/certificate.json),
and [method note](../../experiments/boots_request/README.md) preserve the
literal source, proposed order, fixed-word selection limits, exact edit
costs, fresh control, and unresolved domains.

## Optional Breslau unit emendation

A [separate primary-source supplement](../../experiments/boots_request/breslau_context/README.md)
records a visually inspected VI Army Corps decree dated Breslau, 6 July 1917,
published in the *Waldenburger Wochenblatt*, 18 July 1917. A closer witness
is the decree dated **Breslau, 11 November 1918**, printed in *Der Gebirgsbote*
on **13 November 1918**, which names the same deputy command of **VI Army
Corps** alongside the soldiers' council. [Original decree crop](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/sources/breslau_vi_corps_nov11.png)
· [source and verification](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/README.md#a-separate-breslau-unit-interpretation).
This supports the recipient identification within the week of the telegram.
The optional reading still requires the already priced source change D→G at coordinate 162,
reading the existing GG=6 cell and giving 197/200 fixed positions. This is not
a fill of the received GD cell, whose domain excludes 6. The primary 196/200
edition above, the quantity and all connective alternatives remain unchanged.

# p200 A — Siedlce garrisons reach Thorn

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status: complete source-level reading with explicit repairs.** The
165-character message reports that the Siedlce and Minsk Maziowicki
garrisons have reached Thorn, while the whereabouts of Battalion Ostrowo
are unknown. It is signed General von Zedlitz, hitherto military governor
of Siedlce.

The Nov13–15b square and column order are prior published work by
**George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**. This source
edition, repair certificate and independent identity check are by
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment
priority is claimed.

## Reading

The unchanged source and key give:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ANGENERALG0UVERNEMENTWARSCHAUXGARISONXSIEDLCEXUNDMINSKMAZIOWICKIINXTHORJXEINGETROFFENVERBLEIBBWTLXOSTRVKOXNECHTBEKANNTXGENERALVZEDLIIZBI?HERMILIEAERGOUV?RNEURVIEDLCE
```

</details>

The proposed, same-length edition is:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ANGENERALGOUVERNEMENTWARSCHAUXGARISONXSIEDLCEXUNDMINSKMAZIOWICKIINXTHORNXEINGETROFFENVERBLEIBBATLXOSTROWOXNICHTBEKANNTXGENERALVZEDLITZBISHERMILITAERGOUVERNEURSIEDLCE
```

</details>

In readable English: “To General Government Warsaw. The garrisons of
Siedlce and Minsk Maziowicki have arrived in Thorn. The whereabouts of
Battalion Ostrowo are unknown. General von Zedlitz, hitherto military
governor of Siedlce.” Punctuation and expansion of `BATL` are editorial.
The literal spellings `GARISON` and `MINSKMAZIOWICKI` are retained in the
cryptographic edition, without adding normalization letters. No battalion
number or signer's forename is inferred.

## Source and validation

[Childs' source crop](../../experiments/siedlce_withdrawal/sources/childs_p200_A.png),
printed p200 / PDF p203, preserves the header
`WAU v LP (08.05 p.m., November 15th); 16.44 (15/11); RICHI-330`.
The page heading gives 15 November 1918. Both recorded times are retained.

| Measure | Result |
|---|---:|
| Printed coordinate slots | 330 |
| Observed coordinates / printed erasures | 329 / 1 |
| Insertions / deletions | 0 / 0 |
| Raw key-determined plaintext positions | 163 / 165 |
| Proposed key-determined positions | 165 / 165 |
| Known-coordinate substitutions | 11 |
| Printed-dash fills | 1 |
| Changes to the published square | 0 |

The printed `FFDF-` group has one erased slot, filled with `F`. The
eleven substitutions repair the raw spans `G0UVERNEMENT`, `THORJ`,
`BWTL`, `OSTRVKO`, `NECHT`, `ZEDLIIZ`, `BI?HER`, `MILIEAER`, and
`VIEDLCE`; the dash fill completes `GOUV?RNEUR`. Every changed observed
coordinate is listed in the certificate. Raw “key-determined” positions
include source errors and are not a count of correct German letters.

The complete proposed text re-encrypts exactly under the unchanged
published partial square and column order. This certifies its repair cost
and consistency, while the particular repairs remain editorial choices.

## Independent identity evidence

A contemporary bilingual notice in **Kreisblatt für den Kreis Grojec /
Dziennik rozporządzeń dla powiatu Grójeckiego**, no. 29, **15 October
1918**, printed p211 / PDF p4, is dated **Siedlce, 16 September 1918**
and signed by military governor **Freiherr von Zedlitz, Generalmajor**.
The [signature](../../experiments/siedlce_withdrawal/sources/grojec_1918_29_p211_signature.png)
and [issue title](../../experiments/siedlce_withdrawal/sources/grojec_1918_29_title.png)
were visually verified in the [public scan](http://mbc.cyfrowemazowsze.pl/Content/15317/15317.pdf).
This supports the proposed signer's name and office. It does not
independently attest the troop movements reported in the telegram.


The [inputs](../../experiments/siedlce_withdrawal/inputs.json),
[certificate](../../experiments/siedlce_withdrawal/certificate.json), and
[method note](../../experiments/siedlce_withdrawal/README.md) retain the
literal source, all edits, uncertain-cell domains, prior credit, and
source hashes.

# p201 B / p206 A — reporting orders linked by a shared reference

[Case guide](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** Two complete multipart messages are assembled from the source:
a two-part reporting order on p201 and a three-part request for receipt
confirmation on p206. The unchanged published `Nov16-18` partial key fixes
**660 of 702 plaintext positions** from **1,404 source coordinate slots**.
Their matching number pattern and subject support a **conditional new digit
assignment, VA = 5**. The published square remains unchanged.
**Source assembly and analysis:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. Period-key
recovery retains [the catalogued attribution](../../data/keys.json).

## Reporting order on p201

**Readable German — body excerpt; the unresolved closing reference remains in the raw output below:**

> Erreichte Ziele regelmaessig hierher melden, desgl. wo u. wann ersten
> Teile voraussichtlich die deutsche Grenze erreichen werden, ob mit
> Bahn/Fussmarsch und welche Teile des sind. Empfang bestaetigen. OHL.

**Meaning:** Report reached positions regularly, and say where and when the
first units are expected to reach the German border, whether by rail or on
foot, and which units they are. Acknowledge receipt.

The source has the awkward `ERSTEN` and `DESSIND`; both are retained in the
German reading above. No final `N` is dropped to regularize the former.
The English translation conveys the sentence's apparent meaning
without claiming that its spelling is recovered differently. `WERD?N` is
shown as `werden` using one explicitly costed source-coordinate correction.

The full raw readings are:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — two separately identified source parts:**

```text
p201 B1:
ERREICHTEZIELEREGELMAESSIGHIERHERMELDENDESGLXWOUXWANNERSTENTEILEVORAUSSICHTLICHDIEDEUTSCHEGRENZEERREICHEN

p201 B2:
WERD?NOBMITBAHNFUSSMARSCHUNDWELCHETEILEDESSINDEMPFANGBESTAETIGENXOHLXNMX1XAX11??2XGEHXOPX
```

</details>

The p201 [source crop](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/sources/childs_p201_selected.png)
shows a **16 November** heading and receipt, while the clear internal origin
stamp says **`OHL OP 15/11`**:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
NKJ, UKS, RAT v LP (3.49 p.m., November 16th)
1205 (16) SSD OHL OP 15/11 OKM HERMANNSTADT 2 TLE (16)
1 TL: RICHI-210
2 TL: RICHI-178
```

</details>

All 388 printed coordinates are valid. In part 2, `WERD?N` uses the unknown
cell `GG` at its fifth letter; the established `E` is in `AG`. Source index
**169: G→A** restores `WERDEN`. Assigning that unknown cell to `E` instead
would violate the square's existing injectivity. The raw footer `NMX` and
the reference's two unknown digits are not normalized.

## The three-part confirmation request on p206

The later message asks OKM to confirm immediately whether seven earlier
orders arrived. It identifies the subject of each: the departure order,
reporting intentions, destructions, refusal to surrender weapons,
negotiations with Romania, the armistice, and reporting reached positions.
It then demands immediate reports of the divisions' locations and
acknowledgment of the present order.

The [p206 source](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/sources/childs_p206_selected.png)
has an **18 November** heading and internal stamp but a **19 November** receipt:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
ZON v LP (06.28 a.m., November 19th)
2100 (11/18) 3 TEILE
1 TL: RICHI-368
2 TL: RICHI-400
3 TL: RICHI-248
```

</details>

The first OCR block ended after 40 coordinates, before the printed `RICHI`
label. Rejoining the two visually continuous source rows restores the
complete 368-slot first part. The third part has exactly its stated 248
slots; the earlier OCR's extra character is not part of the printed source.
These are transcription/layout corrections, not hypothetical historical
insertions or deletions.

| Part | Source slots | Directly fixed plaintext | Separately proposed body repairs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| A1 | 368 | 175/184 | Two erasure fills in `BETR` and `BEFEHL`. |
| A2 | 400 | 179/200 | Six erasure fills in words/separators; one erased coordinate in a number remains unresolved. |
| A3 | 248 | 115/124 | Four erasure fills; two known-coordinate substitutions for `DMR→DER` and `EXPFANG→EMPFANG`. |

The first part retains an overtyped, unclear coordinate as `?`; visible dashes
remain erasures. The third part's repeated `BEFEHLSBEFEHLS` is retained rather
than silently shortened. Its final reference begins with a directly decoded
`J`; this is not replaced with a guessed `1`.

## The shared reference and conditional digit 5

The p201 order ends with the number `11??2`. The seventh p206 reference also
has `11??2`, followed by the subject `BEFEHL ERREICHTE ZIELE MELDEN`.
Their number is identical at the square-cell level:

| Position in five-character reference | p201 B2 digraph | p206 A2 digraph | Published-key reading |
| ---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| 0 | VX | VX | 1 |
| 1 | VX | VX | 1 |
| 2 | FA | FA | ? |
| 3 | VV | VV | ? |
| 4 | DV | DV | 2 |

The unknown number positions are therefore shared variables, not four
independent guesses. The matching body subject further supports identifying
the seventh reference with the p201 order.

The referenced date on p206 is `1{VA}.11`. If the clear p201 origin stamp
`OHL OP 15/11` is the date of that same order, **VA must contain 5**.
This assigns zero-based square cell **24**. It changes no source coordinate
and is independent of the [p204 calendar inference](../radio/p204_A.md).

The link remains conditional on the identification of the order and the
correct copying of its date and reference. An equal partly unknown number
alone would not prove that two documents concern the same order; the matching
subject and explicit source date are why the inference is recorded here.
No unrestricted completion of the remaining square cells is claimed.

## Reference list under the two explicit inferences

The following display applies **VA = 5** from the order link and **FD = 8**
from p204's Monday date. Other unknown cells and erasures stay unknown:

| Reference | Conditional number | Conditional date | Directly readable subject |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `11212` | `?.11` | `ABMARSCHBEFEHL` — departure order |
| 2 | `1125?` | `?.11` | `BEFEHL ABSICHTEN ZU MELDEN` — report intentions |
| 3 | `11?2?` | `8.11` | `ZERSTOERUNGEN` — destructions |
| 4 | `11???` | `8.11` | `ABLEHNUNG DER WAFFENABGABE` — refusal to surrender weapons |
| 5 | `11???` | `8.11` | `VERHANDLUNGEN MIT RUMAENIEN` — negotiations with Romania |
| 6 | `11???` | `1?.11` | `WAFFENSTILLSTAND` — armistice |
| 7 | `11??2` | `15.11` | `BEFEHL ERREICHTE ZIELE MELDEN` — report reached positions |

The date order in this list is not used as an additional constraint. The
other serial numbers are not forced into an assumed numerical sequence.

Across p204 and the three p206 parts, the two assignments jointly add **seven
fixed positions** under the stated assumptions. They also fix exactly one
position in the separately audited [p205 financial message](../finance/p205_A.md):
part A4's plaintext index **86** becomes `5`, turning `NRX1???STRICH11` into
`NRX1??5STRICH11`. The p205 source package and base reading remain unchanged.
Its other unknown reference cells then share the remaining digit domain
`034679`; they are not independently chosen.

## Verify

The [input package](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/inputs.json)
contains every source row and historical assumption. The
[certificate](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/certificates.json)
checks both number patterns cell by cell, all source-to-plaintext offsets,
each editorial cost and every consequence of the conditional square.

```sh
python3 experiments/open_targets_continuation/verify.py --verify
```

This is an edition and a qualified key inference by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**,
using the published period key. No first-decipherment priority is claimed for
these supplementary messages.

# p210 D — request for the situation in Reval

[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source certificate](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/certificates.json) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Record:** p210 D, 20 November 1918. **Result:** all **58 plaintext
positions** are fixed from **116 unchanged source coordinates** under the
published Nov19–21 key. One explicitly costed spelling repair gives:

# p215 A — Breslau–Oderberg dispatch fragment

[All cases](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Recovery and review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 4 November 2026.**
A conditional relocation of five printed mask slots reveals a dispatch from
Breslau via Oderberg, mentioning wagonloads and accompanying personnel.
The unchanged published November 22–24 key fixes **176/196 raw positions**.
In that raw layer, all **372 observed coordinates remain unchanged and in their original relative order**.
A separately priced word restoration now identifies horseshoes, hoof nails,
screw nails and the closing **Traindepot Breslau**; its primary layer fixes
**192/196 positions**, including still-uninterpreted numerical labels.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German — excerpt from the conditional raw frame; omitted passages remain outside this quotation and J stays a literal square label:**

authenticate the numerical value of either `J`. The displayed raw stream still contains garbles and unknowns. The word layer
below restores the equipment terms and closing, while leaving numerical
uncertainty explicit. No source-mask fill or observed-coordinate substitution
has been made to obtain the raw output.

## Source and conditional frame

The source header is `A) ZON v BSL (04.50 a.m., November 23rd); WORGAG DORT NR C4A6688;1500(11/22);RICHI-392`.

   of the 387-slot stream remaining after their removal. The final mask block

OCR correction. The source prints the all-dash group at the start of its sixth
body row. Every source slot is retained exactly once. Choosing any contiguous

different mask-identity maps; none is treated as a new message or an additional
