model inserts them between original source 268 and 269. The comparison covers
9,700 frames: 25 possible short-group placements and 388 mask destinations.
The word-cost result is conditional on the proposed words, not an independent
plaintext discovery. A language-score optimum is not historical proof.

The three word streams agree at **192/196 positions**. Their differing quantity

|---:|---|---|
| 270 | `J??11` | `9K??11111` |

The remaining eight cells are globally injective and unassigned; the complete
witness chooses one of 40,320 possible square completions for arithmetic only.

**Conditional interpretation — full primary word stream under that partial global square; new `?` positions also retain unassigned-cell uncertainty:**

```text
2??XIDXRAUMGYULAXSIKLOXKISJENOEXERREICHTXDIVXSTABA1SOS?M?NJX?CENX?X?X12?NSTRECKERUTTKAXTESCHENXABGEFAHRENXXAO21?EINAA
```

The resulting numeral labels are not authenticated unit numbers, train counts,
dates or times. No abbreviation, preposition or footer is supplied from context.

The official [1913 Hungarian gazetteer](https://www.kshkonyvtar.hu/helysegnevtar/1913/helysegnevtar-1913.pdf),
*A Magyar Szent Korona országainak helységnévtára*, independently records
Gyula on printed p138, Sikló and the Kisjenő district heading on p171, and
Kisjenő and Alsósimánd on p172; its alphabetical Alsósimánd entry is on p343.
These entries support historical spellings and administrative context. They
do not establish this telegram's unit, deployment or itinerary.

A contemporary timetable in [*Eperjesi Lapok*, 8 July 1917, PDF p7](https://epa.oszk.hu/05600/05623/00978/pdf/EPA05623_eperjesi_lapok_1917_27.pdf)
lists Ruttka, Zsolna, Teschen and Oderberg consecutively. It supports the
railway vocabulary and place spellings, not a particular November 1918 train
movement or the continuation of that service after the armistice.

## Separately priced Alsosimand proposal

The incomplete staff-location field permits the historical name `ALSOSIMAND`,
but doing so costs **two more observed substitutions**: source 191 `F→G`
and source 171 `D→G`, plus one printed-mask fill and one inserted-slot fill.
The gazetteer attests the name; it does not select this proposed repair.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — optional Alsosimand extension of the primary word layer; totals 4 observed substitutions, 15 printed-mask fills and 11 inserted-slot fills; 111/117 fixed positions:**

```text
J?QXIDXRAUMG4ULAXSIKLOXKIS9ENOEXERREICHTXDIVXSTABALSOSIMANDX?CENX?X?XYJ?NSTRECKERUTTKAXTESCHENXABGEFAHRENXXAOJY?EINAA
```

</details>

**Readable German — excerpt from that optional edited layer; surrounding fields are omitted:**

> […] Div. Stab Alsosimand. […]

This extension is separate from the 109-position proposal. Neither the
unfinished field after the staff location nor the identifier before `STRECKE`
is normalized into a unit, number or grammatical completion.

## Credit and reproduction

Historical source: J. Rives Childs. Published period key: George Lasry,
Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and Lasry's 2017 key list.
Source-frame review, word pricing and edition: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.
The recovery package preserves both frame models and complete global witnesses.

**Reproduction command — verifies the source mapping, repair prices and witnesses:**

```sh
python experiments/p215_third_positions_fragment/verify.py --verify
```

# p217 A — Coal shortages, disarmament and transport through Czechoslovakia

[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source and certificate](../../experiments/operational_recovery/README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Record:** all five parts of message A, originated 24 November 1918 and
intercepted on 26 November.
**Result:** 1,014 source coordinates yield 507 baseline-label plaintext
positions. The first three parts need no coordinate repairs. Four
known-coordinate substitutions across the final two parts clarify the
transport and disarmament instructions. Unit numbers have a separately
documented historical interpretation; the published square is preserved.

## Most likely reading

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the historical numeral and shared place-letter assignments:**

> An OHL und KM. Von [command designation unresolved] noch [keine]
> Nachricht. O.K. Scholtz: 16. Ldw. D. und 226. I.D., Maersche im
> Versammlungsraum. Nachhut 226. I.D. suedl. Rimnic Valcea.
>
> 11. Armee: Alpenkorps unveraendert. Am 22. wegen Kohlenmangels kein
> Abtransport. 6. R.D., Raum suedoestl. Oroshaza. [21?6 D.] in gestrigem
> Raum verblieben. A.O.K. Szolnok. 1 Batl. R.I.R. 21 im Poestyen
> eingetroffen. Verbleib der [damaged phrase] anderen Btlne unbekannt.
> Anscheinend fehlgeleitet.
>
> Cechen verweigern Aufenthalt. Wollen auch Durchfahrt nur nach
> Entwaffnung gestatten. Massow Budapest ist ersucht, letztere Fragen
> zu klaeren. OKM [damaged reference].

**Meaning:** The report locates troops withdrawing across Romania and
Hungary. Coal shortages have stopped outward transport. Some battalions
appear to have been misdirected; the Czechs refuse their stay and intend
to allow transit only after disarmament. Massow in Budapest has been asked
to clarify those questions.

The displayed numbers assume baseline `Y→1`, `J→2`, and `2→6`. The
contemporary French telegram identified below supports the 11th Army,
16th Landwehr, 226th Infantry and 6th Reserve Division identifications.
The same assignments yield *am 22* and R.I.R. 21. Several fields remain
damaged: `21?6 D` has not been replaced with an expected division number,
the number of other battalions is not asserted. The place spelling uses
the already established shared-Y interpretation described below. The certificate retains raw `KEENNE`;
the bracketed *keine* above is an editorial shortening outside the
same-length coordinate edition.

## Poestyen and the contested route

The [already established DD=Y interpretation](../../experiments/p215_hungarian_y/README.md)
reads the entirely observed `POEST4EN` as **POESTYEN**, without a source
change. Its Y comes from plaintext position 57, source positions **139 and
222**. The same shared cell is supported by the separate Nagybanhegyes
field. This display applies that earlier result to the report; it adds no
new square assignment or fixed position.

A contemporary report places the town in the political circumstances of
the telegram. The [*Hamburgischer Correspondent*, 22 November 1918,
morning issue, Zweites Blatt p2 / PDF p7](https://img.sub.uni-hamburg.de/kitodo/PPN689065248_19181122/PDF/PPN689065248_19181122.pdf#page=7)
reprints a Budapest report dated 21 November, attributed to the *Pester
Lloyd*. It names **Poestyen** and describes the local Slovak council's
protest against Czech occupation, with neighboring communities already
under Czech control. The newspaper's hostile language reflects its own
political perspective.

The dispatch of 24 November then reports one battalion at Poestyen,
uncertainty about others, and demands for disarmament before transit.
The newspaper places the town in a contemporary territorial dispute; it
does not verify the battalion's arrival or the military demand.
[Source comparison and exact image provenance](../../experiments/late_place_comparison/README.md).

## Raw decipherment

The [source crop](../../experiments/operational_recovery/sources/childs_p217_A.png)
shows all five parts. The following uses the published baseline labels,
before historical number interpretation or coordinate repairs:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ANOHLUNDKMXVONGJDO28NOCHKEENNENACHRICHTXOKSCHOLTZXY2XLDWXDXUNDJJ2XIDMAERSCHEIMVERSAMMLUNGSRAUMXNACHHUTJJ2XIDSUEDLX
RIMNICXVALCEAXXYYARMEEXALPENKORPSUNVERAENDERTXAMJJXWEGENKOHLENMANGELSKEINABTRANSPORTX2RXDXRAUMSUEDOESTLXOROSHAZAXJYQ2XDX
INGESTRIGEMRAUMVERBLIEBENXAOKXSZOLNOKXYXBATLXRIRJYIMPOEST4ENEINGETROFFENXVERBLEIBDERBE6DEDENANDERENBTLNEUNBEKANNTX
ANSCHEINENDFEHLJELEITETXCEFHENVERWEIGERNAUFENTHALTXWOLLENAUCHDURCHFAHRTNURNACHENTWAFFNUNGGESTATTEN
MASSOWBUDAPESTISTERSUCHUXLETZTEREFRAGENZUKLAEHENXOKMYAYY7YMOP
```

</details>

| Part | Coordinates | Plaintext positions | Proposed repairs |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| A1 | 228 | 114 | None |
| A2 | 240 | 120 | None |
| A3 | 228 | 114 | None |
| A4 | 196 | 98 | Two coordinate substitutions: `FEHLJELEITET→FEHLGELEITET`, `CEFHEN→CECHEN` |
| A5 | 122 | 61 | Two coordinate substitutions: `ERSUCHU→ERSUCHT`, `KLAEHEN→KLAEREN` |

In A5 the source-visible `VVXFX` group and final `VA`, both omitted by OCR,
are included in the literal transcription. This restoration is supported
by the image and the printed length, not by a plaintext guess. There are
no source erasures in these five parts.

## Source, interpretation and credit

Printed p217 / PDF p220, heading **24 November 1918**:
`LP v NKJ (01.36 a.m., November 26th); VON UKS 2230 (11/24)
FUER LP (BSL) 5 TLE`. The original sender/recipient fields are retained.
The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, in the [public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).

The historical number interpretation uses document 39, printed p79 / PDF
p153, in *Documents diplomatiques français sur l'histoire du Bassin des
Carpates, 1918–1932*, vol. I (Budapest, 1993): Franchet d'Esperey's
19 November 1918 telegram reporting German formations as of 11 November.
The [provenance record](../../experiments/p170_continuation/military_context.json)
identifies its source and hash. It is contextual evidence, not a printed
key or proof of every later formation location.

The optional map clears the other potential numeral/J/Q/Y labels and
preserves one global bijection. It never assigns both baseline `Y` and
baseline `J` to 1. Baseline labels, conditional domains and all source
edits are separately recorded. Published period-key credit remains in
[data/keys.json](../../data/keys.json). This source inspection and edition
are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment
priority is claimed.

```sh
python experiments/operational_recovery/verify.py --verify
```

See the [literal input](../../experiments/operational_recovery/inputs.json)
and [certificate](../../experiments/operational_recovery/certificates.json)
for source hashes, exact edits, domains and consistent re-encryption
witnesses. The witnesses fill unassigned key cells only to demonstrate
consistency; they are not proposed historical plaintexts.

# p219 C — Kiev unrest and the soldiers' council

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Conditional recovery: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** The printed group
alternatives and marked jamming loss reveal a report of impending unrest
in Kiev and a soldiers' council decision for neutrality. The new
`BEVORSTEHENDX` completion joins the previously separated body excerpts;
the shared Y also makes the proposed `MARKOWSKY` signature compatible
with every retained observed coordinate.

## Current joint completion

**Conditional interpretation — continuous body with the PETLJURA proposal;
two observed substitutions and twenty inserted-slot fills:**

*Heeresgruppe Kiew. Unruhen zwischen Regierung Hetman und Petljura bevorstehend. Soldatenrat beschloss Neutralitaet.*

The report says that unrest between the Hetman government and the named
opponent is impending, and that the soldiers' council decided on
neutrality. Petljura remains a separately priced name proposal. Without
those two substitutions, the new clause is still source-compatible and
the received name remains `PEDFJ?RA`.

The [joint completion certificate](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/kiev_completion_certificate.json)
rechecks **all 81 declared source models**. The full word selects the
printed **`GXAFV`** alternative over `GXAGV`: its original F at source
28 and A at 131 give **B** at plaintext position 66. The next half-pair
`?D` admits **E**, and the final `X?` admits separator **X**. Filling
modeled slots **95 with F and 96 with V** completes `BEVORSTEHENDX`.
Both slots already belong to the twenty-five-coordinate jamming gap;
this layer introduces no further missing coordinates or observed changes.

Two minimum models remain, differing only in which copy of the duplicated
initial `XFXDD` supplies the first five retained coordinates. They give
**one identical completed ciphertext and body**. The printed group-choice
question and the duplicate-origin ambiguity are therefore distinct.

The original `AD` pair at plaintext 145, source **73 A and 206 D**, now
gives **`MA?KO?SKY`**. The optional spelling **`MARKOWSKY`** needs two
compatible inserted-slot fills and **zero observed substitutions**, down
from two under the published labels. This is a spelling proposal, not
an independently established personal identity.

| Current conditional scope | Observed substitutions | Total inserted-slot fills | Fixed positions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `BEVORSTEHENDX`, raw names | 0 | 19 | 137/147 |
| Clause plus `MARKOWSKY` | 0 | 21 | 139/147 |
| Clause plus `PETLJURA` | 2 | 20 | 138/147 |
| Clause plus all three proposed names | 3 | 22 | 140/147 |

The combined version retains the one-coordinate `ODELSA→ODESSA` repair.
Its three observed changes are source **10 V→X, 85 X→F and 155 A→F**.
All compact footer fields remain unresolved where their source or square
values are unknown. These counts use the shared partial square and do
not treat unresolved numeral labels as historically established digits.

## Earlier recovery layers

The earlier selected frame fixes **122/147 raw published-label positions**.
Seventeen inserted-slot fills give **139/147** with zero observed-coordinate
substitutions. Its complete streams and the separately priced original
name proposals remain below.

The later [shared-square reading](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/README.md#the-kiev-report-outside-the-original-snapshot)
reduces the optional `PETLJURA` spelling from four to **two observed-coordinate changes**.
The received name becomes `PEDFJ?RA` under the independently proposed
`VD=J` assignment. Reading its remaining damaged letters as `PETLJURA`
keeps the same 18 inserted-slot fills and all four minimum source models
at that J-only stage, before the new complete-word constraint.
The two preserved source coordinates are V at index 181 and D at 212;
the remaining substitutions are V→X at 10 and A→F at 155.

## p219 C

**Readable German — three excerpts from the zero-substitution lexical completion; intervening clause and footer omitted:**

> Heeresgruppe Kiew. Unruhen zwischen Regierung Hetman und PEDF9?RA. […] Soldatenrat beschloss Neutralitaet.

The report concerns unrest between the Hetman government and the unresolved
name `PEDF9?RA`, and says that a soldiers' council resolved on neutrality.
The incomplete modifier `VORSTEHEND?`, the intervening `7?` field and the
full footer remain visible in the complete streams below. The quotation
uses plaintext spans 0–16, 19–64 and 79–112, all zero-based.

## Printed alternatives and jamming

The source contains 284 coordinate observations and advertises `RICHI-294`.
It prints three parenthesized groups, a repeated initial `XFXDD`, and a
`(jammed)` note with no stated length. The model retains those observations
as data and tests how to use them in the cipher frame.

`{JAMMED}` in the transcription marks the original `(jammed)` annotation;
the braces are a boundary marker, not coordinate observations.

The earlier selected model excludes source 0–4 (one duplicate), 25–29 (parenthesized
`GXAFV`) and 200–204 (`VDGDD`, choosing its parenthesized `VDFDD` alternative).
The later parenthesized `FXVDD` remains in sequence. Twenty-five unknown
slots are inserted at the printed jamming boundary before original source
85. The model has 294 coordinates and uses the published Nov25–28 key.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 294-slot frame; all 25 added coordinates unassigned:**

```text
HEER?SGRU?PEXKIE?XXUN?UHENX?WISC?ENXREG?ERUN?XHETM?NXUN?XPEDF9?RAX7?VORST?HEND?SOLDAT?NRAT?BESCH?OSSX?EUTRAL?TAET?X7XVX?XODELSA?RM1?3230TMA?KO?SKQX
```

**Edited output — same conditional frame; zero observed substitutions and 17 inserted-slot fills; eight positions unresolved:**

```text
HEERESGRUPPEXKIEWXXUNRUHENXZWISCHENXREGIERUNGXHETMANXUNDXPEDF9?RAX7?VORSTEHEND?SOLDATENRATXBESCHLOSSXNEUTRALITAETXX7XVX?XODELSA?RM1?3230TMA?KO?SKQX
```

</details>

Choosing the printed `VDFDD` alternative matters: its surviving half-pair
permits E in `HEERESGRUPPE`. The other printed group would require a
separately priced coordinate change for that E. The primary edition fills
only compatible erased half-pairs and preserves the remaining labels.

## Optional name spellings

The same-length proposals `PETLJURA`, `ODESSA` and `MARKOWSKY` have separate
prices. They do not replace the primary raw names or establish historical
identities from an external document.

The following table records the earlier prices under the unchanged
published labels. The joint `J` interpretation above has its own
[certificate](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/kiev_certificate.json).

| Proposal | Baseline observed substitutions | Total added-slot fills | Fixed positions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Primary lexical completion | 0 | 17 | 139/147 |
| `PEDF9?RA → PETLJURA` | 4 | 18 | 140/147 |
| `ODELSA → ODESSA` | 1 | 17 | 139/147 |
| `MA?KO?SKQ → MARKOWSKY` | 2 | 19 | 141/147 |
| All three proposals together | 7 | 20 | 142/147 |

**Readable German — the same excerpt spans under the optional combined name proposal:**

> Heeresgruppe Kiew. Unruhen zwischen Regierung Hetman und Petljura. […] Soldatenrat beschloss Neutralitaet.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — optional combined names; seven observed substitutions and 20 inserted-slot fills; five positions unresolved:**

```text
HEERESGRUPPEXKIEWXXUNRUHENXZWISCHENXREGIERUNGXHETMANXUNDXPETLJURAX7?VORSTEHEND?SOLDATENRATXBESCHLOSSXNEUTRALITAETXX7XVX?XODESSA?RM1?3230TMARKOWSKYX
```

</details>

In this earlier layer, no extra letter is inserted to complete `VORSTEHEND?`.
Numerical and compact footer fields such as `7XVX?`, `RM1?3230T` retain
their earlier literal labels.

## Complete declared source-model check

For each parenthesized group the check retains both observations, retains
the preceding group only, or retains the parenthesized group only. It also
retains both initial duplicates or excludes either copy: **27 × 3 = 81 maps**.
Each model adds enough unknown slots at the marked jamming boundary to reach
294 coordinates.

In the earlier comparison, four maps attain the primary template's
zero-substitution minimum. The
combined optional names also have four minimum maps, at seven substitutions.
Both scopes retain two edited streams: an opaque field reads `7?` or `B?`
depending on the first printed alternative. All prices, origins and streams
are retained. The templates leave that field unconstrained rather than using
it to choose a historical label.

## Source and credit

Childs, printed p219 / PDF p222, `C) IWE v RAT (------- November 25th)`;
`1900 (KR)`; `RICHI-294`.
[Original PDF](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view)
· [Edition and verifier](../../experiments/p219_kiev_unrest/README.md)
· [Complete certificate](../../experiments/p219_kiev_unrest/certificates.json).

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — all 284 coordinate observations; parentheses and the jamming annotation retained separately:**

```text
XFXDD XFXDD VFDAD XVDFX GXAGV (GXAFV) FVFDA VDXDX
VVFFD XFDFX GFAXA XFFVV FXVGG XDXGG DAXAF VFVFD
XXGVX {JAMMED} XFAXA XAFFG DFAXD FXXGF VGVGG VGAXV
FDXGF AGVDV AGAAA AAXVX VGFFF XVGAD AXVDV DADXD
AGAFX VXGGG FFXFA DDFXV GGFVX VVVFA GVVFG XFXFX
ADFFV VDGDD (VDFDD) DDDFV GXXGF GGFDX DGVFV GVDFA
FVGFD GDADX ADAAA DDFFF GDDDX (FXVDD) XFDFV XXFGF
XVADX DFVX
```

</details>

The key retains the Lasry–Niebel–Kopal–Wacker work and Lasry's 2017 list.
The earlier unverified repository OCR block is preserved. The source-model
recognition, conditional reading and exact repair account are by
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

# p228 B2 — Demobilization district and formations

[All cases](../README.md) · [The three-part Neuhof telegram](neuhof_demobilization.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Recovery and review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 4 November 2026.**
Moving five printed mask slots exposes a substantial continuation of the
Neuhof demobilization instruction. The unchanged November 28–December 1 key
fixes **90/132 raw positions** in this conditional frame. The word proposal
fixes **121/132 positions**, comprising **95 proposed word positions** and
26 retained labels in other fields. Its five observed-coordinate substitutions
and 32 printed-mask fills are individually recorded.

Two shared-reference steps now extend that proposal to **125/132 positions**:
the first part supplies the order suffix and the first enclosure number.
Together with the later numeral interpretation, the latter passage reads
**Anlg. 1 u. 2**. Both steps use complete original donor pairs and add four
mask fills, with no additional observed-coordinate substitution.

The earlier edition proposed only the first 33 positions. This continuation
adds the phrases `DIE NACH ANLG`, `DES ERL`, `IM BEREICH DES STELLV`,
`DEMOBILMACHENDEN` and the suffix `FORMATIONEN`. The intervening command
designation and the prefix `???CK` remain unresolved.

## Readable fragments

**Conditional interpretation — readable German after the shared-reference and enclosure transfers, with the declared numeral interpretation; ellipses omit fields shown below:**

> An Strecke Hanau–Fulda demobil gemacht. Die nach Anlg. 1 u. 2 des Erl. […] im Bereich des stellv. […] demobilmachenden ???CKformationen […]

The wording concerns formations undergoing demobilization within a deputy
command's district and refers to two enclosures and an order. The incomplete
compound ending in `FORMATIONEN` does not identify a specific formation type.
The [third part](neuhof_demobilization.md#b3-routing-to-neuhof) continues with
`DESFELDHEERES` and directs the relevant items toward Neuhof. The new fragment
helps connect the instruction's two previously readable ends; it does not
supply the remaining reference values or establish that the order was executed.

## Source and frame

Childs, printed p228 / PDF p231, section B2, `2 TL RICHI-264`, under
`30th NOVEMBER, 1918.` The parent header reads
`B) ZON v BSL (01.33 a.m., December 1st); NO 152 1512 3 TLE`.
The body contains exactly **264 slots: 221 observed coordinates and 43 dashes**.

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — unchanged 264-slot body:**

```text
XFXDD VAVXV AXDVX FXVVA FGXVV VGFVG VDVDA GVFDF
AGAVX XAGDD FGFAA GAXXV ADDFG FGVFX VVGGG FDGAV
XGVXD DXXFA AXFGV XDVGD DAGGV FAAAX FDAGV VDDGV
GVGGA FFDGA -AVVG FGVFG DVXAG XFXGG GFGFG ADXFV
DDVFV G-DAF GXFXX GGVFV FVGVD -GDXG FF--- -----
----- ----- ----- ----- DFGFF VAAVX XGFFD FGFFV
XAVAA FVDXX FF--- ----- ----
```

</details>

All indices are zero based, with end-exclusive ranges. Remove the existing
five printed masks at source[195:200], then insert them at boundary246 of
the shortened 259-slot stream. They occupy model[246:251]. No source slot
is dropped or added; all 221 observed coordinates retain their values and
relative order.

This is a conditional placement of a printed mask group, not an OCR correction.
Any five contiguous masks starting at source192 through215 give the same
ciphertext: 24 different mask-identity maps are preserved. The printed page
does not independently select the new location or any one of those identities.

## Raw and edited output

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — mask relocation, unchanged published key; 90/132 fixed positions; no observed substitutions or fills:**

```text
A?ST??CKEHAN??FULDAD??OBILGED??HTDIB??CHANLG??UJDESE??Y2680Y??GEHY0Y??MBEREI??DESSTE???YYKDO???MX4AK???OBILM???ENDEN???CKF?????I4NE?
```

**Edited output — same frame; five observed substitutions and 32 printed-mask fills; 121/132 fixed positions:**

```text
ANSTRECKEHANAUFULDADEMOBILGEMACHTDIENACHANLG??UJDESERLY2680Y??GEHY0Y?IMBEREICHDESSTELLVYYKDO???MX4AKDEMOBILMACHENDEN???CKFORMATIONEN
```

</details>

| Source index | Printed | Proposed | Word position |
|---:|:---:|:---:|---|
| 148 | G | D | `O` in `FORMATIONEN` |
| 179 | V | D | `A` in `DEMOBILMACHENDEN` |
| 181 | V | F | `M` in `FORMATIONEN` |
| 240 | X | V | `E` in `DIE` |
| 251 | F | X | `M` in the opening `GEMACHT` |

The 32 fills fix 31 previously unresolved positions. **Position4, R in
STRECKE, has both coordinates missing** and consumes two printed-mask fills;
it lies inside the previously proposed opening. Every one of the **22 newly
fixed tail-word positions** has one observed half-coordinate. The other five
repairs change observed values and remain separate from the fills.

The 11 unresolved positions are **44,45,60,61,68,92,93,94,116,117,118**.
The three positions before `CKFORMATIONEN` are deliberately unfilled.
The known numeral labels, `Y` labels and `X4AK` field are not assigned
historical numbers by this edition. A complete arbitrary re-encryption
witness checks the arithmetic without claiming the remaining erased values.

## Comparison and reproducibility

| Frame and proposal | Raw fixed | Edited fixed | Observed substitutions | Printed-mask fills | Proposed word positions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Earlier native frame, opening only | 89/132 | 99/132 | 5 | 10 | 33 |
| Relocated frame, same opening only | 90/132 | 99/132 | 1 | 10 | 33 |
| Relocated frame, new word spans | 90/132 | 121/132 | 5 | 32 | 95 |

The earlier edition and its literal displays remain available. The improved
opening price is a useful check independent of the newly proposed tail words;
it does not prove unique historical geometry. Blind mask-placement searches
and fresh source-shaped controls are described in the
[recovery package](../../experiments/p228_demobilization_fragment/README.md).

[Inputs](../../experiments/p228_demobilization_fragment/inputs.json) and
[certificates](../../experiments/p228_demobilization_fragment/certificates.json)
retain every coordinate origin, word span, repair, remaining domain and
mask-ownership alias. The original PDF and the previously published source
crop have matching authenticated pixels; no new source image is duplicated.

**Reproduction command — verifies the unchanged source, frame, prices and complete witnesses:**

```sh
python experiments/p228_demobilization_fragment/verify.py --verify
```

## Shared reference and enclosure witnesses

The first part has the fully observed reference fragment `P680YX4GEH`;
B2 has `2680Y??GEH`. If these denote the same order-reference field,
B1 supplies the two missing labels `X4` at B2 positions 60–61. The
[separate certificate](../../experiments/p228_demobilization_fragment/reference_witness.json)
records the original donor pairs `GX` and `GD`, fills source255 with `G`
and source210 with `D`, and verifies both parts under the same unchanged key.
This optional layer reaches **123/132 fixed positions**, with **34 printed-mask
fills and the same five observed substitutions**. The primary layer stays at
121/132. The observed `P` versus `2` disagreement is retained; neither label
receives a numerical interpretation. These are separate parts with a proposed
shared reference, not duplicate receptions. Reproduce with
`python experiments/p228_demobilization_fragment/verify_reference.py --verify`.

The first part also has the fully observed `ANLGYX`. Its two final pairs,
`AX` and `GX`, fit B2's `ANLG??UJ` at positions 44–45. Transferring them fills
source253 with `A` and source208 with `X`, producing `ANLGYXUJ`. This
**enclosure extension fixes 125/132 positions**, with five observed
substitutions and 36 mask fills in total. Positions 68, 92–94 and 116–118
remain unresolved.

Under the [shared calendar and unit interpretation](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/README.md),
the enclosure field reads `ANLGX1U2`, and B2's order reference reads
`3067X18GEH`. B1 has `P067X18GEH`; that initial P/3 disagreement remains.

<details>
<summary>Combined conditional reading</summary>

**Edited output — mask relocation, five observed substitutions, 36 printed-mask fills and the shared numeral interpretation:**

```text
ANSTRECKEHANAUFULDADEMOBILGEMACHTDIENACHANLGX1U2DESERLX3067X18GEHX7X?IMBEREICHDESSTELLVXXKDO???M18AKDEMOBILMACHENDEN???CKFORMATIONEN
```

The verifier checks both original donor pairs, every added fill, the displayed
word spans and complete witnesses under both remaining square assignments.

</details>

Historical ciphertext: **J. Rives Childs**. Published period key:
**George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**. The earlier Neuhof
source edition and its attribution are preserved. Mask-frame recovery,
continuation and independent review: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

# p230 A — Divisions around Hermannstadt and an OKM headquarters move [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source and certificate](../../experiments/operational_recovery/README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md) **Record:** surviving third and fourth parts of message A on printed p230; the source says the first two parts are missing. **Result:** 462 source coordinates yield 231 baseline-label plaintext positions. The proposed edition makes eight known-coordinate substitutions. The further historical `303` division proposal below adds one, bringing the optional combined edition to **nine** substitutions. Historical number identifications, separator convention and lexical letter assignments are separate optional layers; the published key is unchanged. ## Divisions and headquarters movement **Conditional interpretation — readable German with the shared calendar and unit assignments:** > 226. I. D. nordwestl. Hermannstadt. 16. Ldw. Div. um Muehlbach. > 218. Div. im Raume Hatszeg, Livazeny. Drittens. Gen. Kdo. 63 Kronstadt. > 89 und 3L3 Div. um Kronstadt. 7 bayr. Kav. Brig. um Fogaras versammelt. > OKM verlegt Hauptquart. nach Muehlbach. OKM1ANRZ11U30OP. **Meaning:** The report gives the positions of withdrawing divisions, places General Command 63 at Kronstadt, and announces an OKM headquarters move to Muehlbach. The shared interpretation now identifies the **7th Bavarian cavalry brigade** around Fogaras. The received division field `3L3` admits the historically supported **303rd Division** proposal below; the closing reference remains literal. The [joint date and unit study](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/README.md) assigns `VG=7` from this brigade field and the `217` formation in p229 A1, with support from Barkóczy-Klopsch's 1923 military history. The November date in p229 separately fixes `GA=0`. These two assignments bring part 4 from **113 to 115/115 interpreted positions**, without adding source edits. ### The 303rd Division: one separately priced correction Reading the damaged division field as **`303`** gives **89 und 303 Div. um Kronstadt**. Barkóczy-Klopsch's 1923 order of battle lists the **89th Infantry Division and 303rd Landsturm Division** together under the 63rd Bavarian corps. [Printed p11](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/sources/barkoczy_p11.png) · [Institutional scan](https://real-eod.mtak.hu/8911/1/MTA_AKisAkademiaKonyvtara_043.pdf). This supports the formation identity without independently proving its 30 November location. The original middle character is `L`, pair **GG**, at part 4 plaintext position **7**, from source positions **0 and 86**. Changing source **86 from G to A** gives `GA=0` under the shared date interpretation. The source glyph is G: this is one added observed-coordinate correction, not a retranscription. Part 4 then costs **two substitutions** including the earlier `HEUPT→HAUPT` repair, with no mask fills or frame changes. The [separate division certificate](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/division_certificate.json) re-encrypts the proposal under both surviving squares. It also retains the equally cheap numerical alternatives **313, 373 and 383**; the external formation list supplies the reason for proposing 303. ### Earlier number and letter interpretations The numbers above assume a consistent interpretation of baseline labels: `X→1`, `J→2`, `8→6`, `4→8`, `5→9`, and `2→3`. Contemporary French intelligence lists the 226th Infantry, 16th Landwehr, 218th Infantry and 89th Infantry divisions. The French list itself marks the 89th as `89e D.I.?`; the later independent Hungarian account lists the 89th without that query. The reading of General Command 63 is supported by the p163 withdrawal edition under its stated historical and editorial assumptions. These are conditional identifications, not cipher-only proofs. The conventional separator `X` additionally assumes baseline `Y→X`. The `Y` in *bayr.* and *Livazeny* assumes baseline `7→Y`; the latter place also requires a counted `C→Z` repair. A fourth lexical layer keeps the unchanged `Q` in the `QUART` abbreviation as `Q`. None of these lexical or separator assumptions is silently included in the historical numeric map. ## Raw decipherment and repairs The [source crop](../../experiments/operational_recovery/sources/childs_p230_A.png) shows complete frames of 232 and 230 coordinates without erasures. The baseline-label output is:
Raw decoded text **Raw output:** ```text JJ8YIWDYNORDWESTLYHERMAN0STADTYX8YLDWYD3VYUMMUEHLBACHYJX4YDIVYIMRAUMEHATSZEGYLIVACEN7YYDRITTENSYYGENKDOY82KRONSTANTG 45YUND2L2YDIVYUMKRONSTADTY0YBA7RYKAVYBRIGYUMFOGARASVERSAMMELTYYOKMYVERLEGTHEUPTQUARTYNACHMUEHLBACHYYOKMXANRZXXU26OP ```
The same-length proposed edition, still in baseline-label space, is:
Proposed text and exact labels **Edited output:** ```text JJ8YIYDYNORDWESTLYHERMANNSTADTYX8YLDWYDIVYUMMUEHLBACHYJX4YDIVYIMRAUMEHATSZEGYLIVAZEN7YYDRITTENSYYGENKDOY82KRONSTADTY 45YUND2L2YDIVYUMKRONSTADTY0YBA7RYKAVYBRIGYUMFOGARASVERSAMMELTYYOKMYVERLEGTHAUPTQUARTYNACHMUEHLBACHYYOKMXANRZXXU26OP ```
Part 3 needs seven coordinate substitutions and part 4 one. The first part's `IYD` and final `Y` become separators only under the separator hypothesis. Baseline `0` in the brigade field becomes `7` only in the new historical layer. The exact unchanged `Q` occurs at plaintext position 80 of part 4, cell `DF`, from source coordinates 10 and 96 (one-based); reading it as ordinary `Q` is recorded as its own lexical assumption. ## Source and credit Printed p230 / PDF p233, heading **30 November 1918**: `BSL v ZON (09.26 p.m., December 1st); 2200; 1st and 2d TL missing`. The missing parts have not been reconstructed. The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, in the [public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view). Context comes from Franchet d'Esperey's 19 November 1918 telegram, document 39, printed p79 / PDF p153 in *Documents diplomatiques français sur l'histoire du Bassin des Carpates, 1918–1932*, vol. I (Budapest, 1993). The [provenance record](../../experiments/p170_continuation/military_context.json) identifies the edition and scan. This telegram reports formations as of 11 November; it does not directly establish their locations at month end. Published period-key attribution remains in [data/keys.json](../../data/keys.json). Source inspection, coordinate audit and this edition are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment priority is claimed. ```sh python experiments/operational_recovery/verify.py --verify ``` The [input records](../../experiments/operational_recovery/inputs.json) and [certificate](../../experiments/operational_recovery/certificates.json) include literal rows, source hashes, individual edits, optional partial squares, all domains and consistent re-encryption witnesses. Unassigned cells in those witnesses are arbitrary consistency completions, not accepted readings.

# p79 — medical formations lost in Palestine and their dissolution

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** A complete two-part source edition. The second part is identical in all 336 observed coordinates to the previously reviewed p83 B. Its immediately preceding first part supplies the medical-formation antecedent that was missing from the p83-only edition.

Source edition and comparison: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The unchanged **Oct28–31** key is credited to Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker. The existing [p83 dissolution reading](formation_dissolution.md) and earlier unreviewed p79 A1 candidate retain prior credit; no existing physical record is added again.

## Meaning

The telegram reports that field hospitals labelled 212,213 and 219, medical company 300 and a replacement medical company in Palestine have been lost, except for portions of their personnel. A request has been made to declare these formations dissolved, and their remaining personnel are to proceed to replacement units at home.

This identifies the antecedent of “these formations” in p83 B. The reading is evidence of what the telegram reports; it does not independently establish the circumstances of the losses or a casualty total. Unit numbers remain the literal labels supplied by the published key, without a new numerical interpretation.

## Source

Childs printed page 79 / PDF page 82 gives:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) OSM v LP (4.02 p.m., October 30th)
SS DD AN TUERK GR H QU (GEN V SEECKT)
1310 (30/10) 2 TEILE
1 TL RICHI-262
2 TL RICHI-336
```

</details>

The first and second parts contain 262 and 336 printed slots. The first includes one P-shaped glyph outside the ADFGVX alphabet; it is retained literally in the input and treated as an unknown coordinate. The second is entirely valid coordinate text.

The p83 repeat is separately headed4.09 p.m. on30 October. Both interception times remain as printed. The exact ciphertext equality connects the second parts without assuming a particular relay or retransmission chronology.

## p79 A1

Raw decryption:

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
NACHMELDUNGDESFELDSANCHEFSSINDDIEF?LDLAZX212X213X219XSANXKPX300XUNDXERSXSANXKPXINXPALAESTINABISAUFTEILEDESPERSONALSVERLORENGEGANGEN
```

**Edited output:**

```text
NACHMELDUNGDESFELDSANCHEFSSINDDIEFELDLAZX212X213X219XSANXKPX300XUNDXERSXSANXKPXINXPALAESTINABISAUFTEILEDESPERSONALSVERLORENGEGANGEN
```

</details>

The E in `FELDLAZ` fills the invalid-glyph coordinate at index 134. It costs **one source-mask fill and zero observed-coordinate substitutions**. All other 130 plaintext positions are direct readings.

## p79 A2

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
BEIMXKXMXISTBEANTRAGTSIEFUERAUFGELOESTZUERKLAERENXXNOCHVORHANDENESPERSONALDIESERFORMATIONENISTZUDENHEIMISCHENERSATZTRUPPENTEILENINMARSCHZUSETZENXOHLXRMX1XCXNRX103577XOP
```

</details>

This is a direct168-position reading with no source repairs. The verifier checks its full336-coordinate equality with the frozen p83 B transcription; the match is not limited to a selected plaintext passage. `K.M.` and the closing reference remain source abbreviations and labels.

## Counts and verification

The two new physical records contain **598 native coordinate slots and 299 plaintext positions**, with 298 raw fixed positions and 299 in the edition. There are **zero known-coordinate substitutions**, one mask fill, and no added, deleted or reordered coordinates. The published key remains unchanged.

The total includes the repeated second part; it is not299 entirely new message characters. The new contextual result is the explicit link from p83's dissolution instruction to the named medical formations in the contiguous p79 first part.

[Inputs](../../experiments/palestine_medical_dissolution/inputs.json) preserve both manual transcriptions, header information and exact crop provenance. [The certificate](../../experiments/palestine_medical_dissolution/certificates.json) verifies all repairs, source positions, round trips and the complete duplicate. [The README](../../experiments/palestine_medical_dissolution/README.md) gives reproduction commands and attribution limits.

# Oderberg transport fragment and a troop-situation query

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Two additional physical records from the upper part of Childs p211 have source-reviewed readings.** The 176-coordinate second part is readable without repairs. A separate 68-coordinate query asks about the situation and the troops' behavior, with three word repairs. The lower three-part key-schedule message on the same page is [already cataloged separately](../radio/p211_key_schedule.md).

Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The unchanged published Nov19–21 key retains the credit of George Lasry and the research of Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker. The earlier OCR screen already recovered the complete second-part body; this edition supplies manual source review and exact accounting, without a first-decipherment claim.

| Record | Literal source coordinates | Raw fixed labels | Source edits | Geometry |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| p211 A2, upper section | 176 | 88/88 | None | Native frame |
| p211 B, upper section | 68 | 34/34 | 3 coordinate substitutions | Native frame |

Both lengths agree with the printed RICHI labels. No coordinate is inserted, deleted, excluded or reordered. “Fixed” means fixed under the published square; it does not independently authenticate numeral or reference labels.

## A2: the first part is explicitly missing

The upper section is headed **INTERCEPTED BY BRITISH STATIONS**, **20 November 1918**. The A header gives unknown sender and receiver, reception on **November 21**, and the message field **2317 (11/20)**. Immediately above the ciphertext it says **“1st TL missing”**, followed by **2 TL, RICHI-176**.

The literal 88-label reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ODERBERGKEINESCHWIERIGKEITENINDENWEGLEGENWIRDXXEMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNGXXOHLXRMJAJJ9JJOPXGEH
```

</details>

The surviving clause ends with “will place no difficulties in the way,” followed by a request to acknowledge receipt. Its beginning names Oderberg. The missing first part contains the subject and preceding context, so this fragment alone does not identify who made the undertaking, what complete route was involved, or a final permission decision. The closing `OHL X RMJAJJ9JJ OP X GEH` remains exactly as deciphered; no J or 9 is normalized into a different reference format.

The final glyph in printed group 26 is D, as confirmed by the enlarged source crop. It is retained as an observed coordinate, not treated as an erasure or a conjectural fill.

### Possible relationship to the Prague fragment on p209

The [p209 A1 edition](transport_and_disarmament_orders.md) is explicitly part 1 of a two-part message. Its final words are `AUFSTRECKETESCHEN`. This p211 part begins `ODERBERGKEINESCHWIERIGKEITENINDENWEGLEGENWIRD`. The two fragments therefore make a coherent **Teschen–Oderberg** route-name continuation, and both use the published Nov19–21 key.

That textual fit is useful, but the headers do not establish that these are the two parts of the same telegram:

| Evidence | p209 A1 | p211 A2 |
|---|---|---|
| Printed part | 1 of 2 | 2; first part explicitly missing |
| Sender/receiver | `ZO'N v LP` | Not recorded |
| Message field | `22.35 (19/11)` | `2317 (11/20)` |
| Reception date | November 19 | November 21 |

The relationship is therefore recorded as a **possible companion**, with the date and time mismatch retained. Neither package's frozen source is changed, and no complete combined message or definitive transport permission is asserted.

## B, upper section: situation and conduct of troops

This is the short B immediately below the transport fragment, before the horizontal division and the separate November 19 key-schedule message. Its header reads `ZON v LP (04.49 p.m., November 20th)`, `1645 (11/20)`, `RICHI-68`.

The unchanged source yields:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
WIELAGEDORTXWIRVERHALTANDERTRUPPAN
```

</details>

The editorial proposal is:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
WIELAGEDORTXWIEVERHALTENDERTRUPPEN
```

</details>

With spacing and punctuation: **“Wie Lage dort? Wie Verhalten der Truppen?”** It asks about the situation there and the behavior of the troops. The context does not identify which troops or location.

The proposal costs exactly three observed-coordinate substitutions, using zero-based indices:

| Source index | Printed → proposed | Affected word |
|---:|---|---|
| 22 | V → F | `VERHALTAN` → `VERHALTEN` |
| 23 | V → F | `TRUPPAN` → `TRUPPEN` |
| 34 | G → D | `WIR` → `WIE` |

All three are local word repairs under the unchanged square. There are no source-mask fills or additional plaintext characters.

## Evidence and reproduction

The [inputs](../../experiments/prague_route_and_situation/inputs.json) preserve both diplomatic transcriptions, all header fields, the published key provenance and four source crops. The [certificates](../../experiments/prague_route_and_situation/certificates.json) record every plaintext pair's source coordinates and all three repairs. The [earlier candidate snapshot](../../experiments/prague_route_and_situation/prior_evidence.json) preserves the prior complete A2 reading.

```bash
python experiments/prague_route_and_situation/verify.py --verify
python experiments/prague_route_and_situation/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf
```

The default verifier uses only the Python standard library. Optional PyMuPDF verification checks the exact source PDF hash and crop pixels. The [experiment README](../../experiments/prague_route_and_situation/README.md) states the finite scope and the unresolved relationship between the two transport fragments.

# A regimental journey report with unresolved route and unit labels

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This two-part report follows a regimental journey after minor interruptions and records the assistance received. A shared reading with p227 supplies the J of JEDE from its original coordinate pair, reducing part 2’s word-repair cost from two substitutions to zero. The further shared unit interpretation fixes the arrival day as **27**; parts of the route and unit descriptions remain unresolved.

## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p225 excerpt](../../experiments/regimental_journey_report/sources/p225_reviewed.png) · [Inputs](../../experiments/regimental_journey_report/inputs.json) · [Position and change certificates](../../experiments/regimental_journey_report/certificates.json)

The published `Nov28-Dec1` key is unchanged. [Original OCR records](../../experiments/regimental_journey_report/ocr_snapshot.json) and [reproducible comparisons with that earlier evidence](../../experiments/regimental_journey_report/prior_candidates.json) are preserved separately. The present edition supplies checked source framing, exact costs and readable passages; it makes no first-public-decipherment claim.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [p225 B1](#p225-b1) | 254 | 122 / 127 | 8 | 4 |
| [p225 B2](#p225-b2) | 212 | 106 / 106 | 2; **0 with shared J** | 0 |

## p225 B1

**Source transcription — header:** `B) ZON v UKS (01.17 a.m., November 29th); 1130 (11/28) (VON BSL); 1 TL RICHI-254`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
ARMEE?KDOXXYY?EGIMENSSTABMIT2BAONJXUNDPEISENBAHLBUUCOMPYNACCFOLGENDJTRANMPYLANDWY1KXJSINDNAKHBEREITIGUNGLEI?HTERUNL?RBRECHU?GEN
```

**Edited output — 8 observed-coordinate substitutions and 4 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
ARMEE?KDOXXYYREGIMENSSTABMIT2BAONJXUNDPEISENBAHNBAUCOMPYNACHFOLGENDJTRANSPYLANDWY1KXJSINDNACHBESEITIGUNGLEICHTERUNTERBRECHUNGEN
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> ARMEE?KDOXX. REGIMENSSTAB mit 2BAONJX und P Eisenbahnbaucomp. Nachfolgend J TRANSP. LANDW 1KXJ sind nach Beseitigung leichter Unterbrechungen

**Meaning:** The first part lists a regimental staff, battalion and railway-construction company fields, and a following transport. It says minor interruptions have been overcome and continues with the journey and arrival report in part 2. The opening command designation and unit or quantity labels remain unresolved.

**Editorial limits.**

- All 254 occupied source slots are retained. The source contains one complete group of five dashes; four of its values are supplied explicitly, while the remaining command-field erasure stays unknown.
- The raw ARMEE?KDOXX unknown has domain {4, 8, A, K, O, U}. It is not filled with a separator or a presumed army designation.
- REGIMENSSTAB is retained without inserting the absent T of a familiar spelling. The labels 2BAONJX, P, J TRANSP and LANDW 1KXJ are not converted into historical unit numbers or quantities.
- EISENBAHLBUUCOMP to EISENBAHNBAUCOMP, NACCFOLGEND to NACHFOLGEND, TRANMP to TRANSP, NAKH to NACH, BEREITIGUNG to BESEITIGUNG and UNL?RBRECHU?GEN to UNTERBRECHUNGEN are explicitly priced word proposals.
- The Nov28–Dec1 key uses Y as the separator label. X remains literal within fields, including KDOXX and 1KXJ.

## p225 B2

**Source transcription — header:** `B) ZON v UKS (01.17 a.m., November 29th); 1130 (11/28) (VON BSL); 2 TL RICHI-212`

**Conditional interpretation — the shared Nov28–Dec1 letter and numeral layer:**

> Von POESTYEN I TRENCSEN ueber PUHO in SILEIN in der Nacht am 2?
> eingetroffen. Jede Unterstuetzung gefunden. R I RGT21.

At plaintext position 67, source positions 194 and 48 carry the complete pair
`FA`. The same original pair begins `JEDER` in [p227 D](avoid_fighting_instruction.md).
Assigning `FA=J` reads both ordinary words without altering their ciphertexts.
The J-only extension fixes **105/106 positions** in the interpreted second
part, leaving the arrival date `2?`. `POESTYEN` and `RGT21` follow the earlier
Y and numeral interpretation, while the spelling `SILEIN` and intervening `I`
labels remain literal. The full interpretation inherits the prior period-key
assumptions. [Joint evidence and 24 square witnesses](../../experiments/late_november_joint_completion/README.md).

The later [calendar and unit comparison](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/README.md)
assigns `VG=7` through the independently documented 217th Division and 7th
Bavarian cavalry brigade. Its unchanged occurrence here completes the date:

| Field | After the shared J | After the unit interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Arrival day | `2?` | **27** |

All **106/106 interpreted positions** are then fixed, with all 212 received
coordinates retained. This supports arrival during the night of the 27th;
it adds no inference about the route's remaining spelling problems.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
VONPOEST7ENYIYTRENCSENUEBERPUHOINSILEININDERNACHTAMJ0YEINGETROFFENY1EDEUNTERSTUETZUNGGEFUNDENYYRYIYRGTJXYY
```

**Edited output — earlier unchanged-key wording; 2 observed-coordinate substitutions:**

```text
VONPOEST7ENYIYTRENCSENUEBERPUHOINSILEININDERNACHTAMJ0YEINGETROFFENYJEDEUNTERSTUETZUNGGEFUNDENYYRYIYRGTJXYY
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Von POEST7EN I TRENCSEN ueber PUHO in SILEIN in der Nacht am J0 eingetroffen. Jede Unterstuetzung gefunden. R I RGTJX.

**Meaning:** The continuation reports arrival in SILEIN during the night represented by J0, after a journey from the literal POEST7EN I TRENCSEN route field via PUHO, and says every assistance was received. The place spellings, date-like label and closing unit field are not silently normalized or independently identified.

**Editorial limits.**

- The native 212-coordinate second part has no source erasures or length changes. Under the published square, 1EDE to JEDE costs two substitutions. The shared FA=J interpretation removes both changes and retains all 212 observed coordinates.
- POEST7EN retains its numeral-like 7, and SILEIN retains the source-length spelling. Neither is silently converted into a presumed historical place name.
- J0, I and RGTJX remain literal. The body date-like label is not chosen from the November 29 interception header or the separate 11/28 originating line.

## Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates independently reconstruct column positions and domains, compare them with the cipher implementation, replay every priced change, and check all readable nonseparator labels. Partial readings have one consistent injective square/source-mask completion witness that re-encrypts exactly; those witness choices are not historical identifications. Source images are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and pixel digest.

Reproduce the source edition with `python experiments/regimental_journey_report/verify.py --verify` and the joint extension with `python experiments/late_november_joint_completion/verify.py --verify`. The source verifier accepts `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` for the original PDF and exact crop pixels.

# Equipment disposal, Alpenkorps return, and Finland evacuation orders

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Seven source-reviewed physical records on Childs pp207–208 are now readable.** The clearest gain is the complete two-part Alpenkorps order: its first part was missing an entire row in the earlier OCR extraction, while its second part supplies a printed witness for five erased coordinates and one differing coordinate on p207. Two neighboring messages concern equipment and horses that cannot reach Germany, and the German force in Finland.

Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The published Nov16–18 key and the earlier OCR-derived candidates retain their separate prior credit. These are source editions under that published key; no claim of first historical decipherment is made.

## Evidence and costs

The page headings both say **18 November 1918**. All counts below use the manually transcribed printed rows and the conservative published square. The separate shared date and order interpretation described below fixes six further positions across A2 and C1.

| Printed record | Source slots | Raw fixed labels in the working frame | Editorial fixed labels | Explicit cost |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| p207 A1 | 318, including 12 dashes | 146/159 | 159/159 | 7 coordinate substitutions; 12 dash fills |
| p207 A2 | **221**, heading 220 | 102/110, conditional | 102/110 | Exclude the final printed X before untransposition; no substitutions |
| p207 B | 228, including 5 dashes | 105/114 | 109/114 | 1 substitution and 5 fills, supplied by the p208 A2 witness |
| p207 C1 | 208 | 101/104 | 101/104 | 1 substitution |
| p207 C2 | 140 | 67/70 | 68/70 | 2 substitutions; the doubled A remains |
| p208 A1 | 246 | 123/123 | 123/123 | None |
| p208 A2 | 228 | 109/114 | 109/114 | None |

The complete diplomatic rows, raw readings, per-position domains, coordinate origins and repair ledgers are in the [inputs](../../experiments/repatriation_orders/inputs.json) and [certificates](../../experiments/repatriation_orders/certificates.json). Every printed coordinate, including the excluded final X of p207 A2, remains in those records.

## Alpenkorps return: p208 A1–A2 and the p207 B witness

The p208 header reads `ZO'N v LP (20.59 p.m., November 18th)`, `07.10 (18/11) 2 TLE`. Part 1 gives this unaltered 123-label reading:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ANOBERKDOMACKENSENXXWENNVERHAELTNISSEESGESTATTENISTALPENKORPSSOANZUSETZENDASSPREUSSISCHEVERBAENDENACHSCHLESIENZURVERFUEGUNG
```

</details>

Part 2 continues, also without coordinate repairs:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
PREUSSXKMSXXBAYRXVERBAENDENACHBAYERNZURVERFUEGGDESBAYRXKMZUGEFUEHRTWERDENXXEMPFANGBESTAETIGENXXOHLXRM1AXX1?????OPX
```

</details>

With word spacing, the instruction is addressed to Oberkommando Mackensen. If conditions permit, the Alpenkorps is to be directed so that Prussian formations are sent to Silesia for the Prussian `K.M.`, and Bavarian formations to Bavaria for the Bavarian `K.M.`. Receipt is to be acknowledged. The abbreviation `VERFUEGG`, the office labels and the unresolved numerical reference are retained as deciphered.

The p207 B header instead reads `ZO'N v LP (20.10 p.m., November 18th)`, followed by a blank message-time field and `2 TLE`. Its single printed body has no explicit part number. It corresponds to p208 A2, rather than to the unrelated p207 A message above it.

Of p207 B's **223 observed coordinates, 222 agree** with the later printed witness. At source index 127, p207 has G and p208 has F; that distinction produces the raw `...WERDENXM...` versus `...WERDENXX...`. The five dashes at indices 165–169 are supplied as `ADAGX`. One of those fills restores a coordinate in an unresolved numeral cell: it does **not** assign that cell a digit. After these separately recorded changes, the entire 228-coordinate working witness is identical to the literal p208 A2 source. The agreement establishes a strong printed-copy relationship; it does not establish independent transmissions or intercepts.

## Equipment and horses: p207 A1–A2

The header reads `ZO'N v LP`, an unspecified reception time on November 18, and `13.00 (18/11) 2 TLE`. The first part's editorial reading is:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ANXOKMXGERAETUNDPFERDEDIEWEDERDURCHMARSCHNOCHDURCHBAHNDEUTSCHLANDERREICHENKOENNENXFREIHAENDIGVERKAUFENXMOEGLICHSTVERHINDERNXDASSEIGENETRUPPEGANZENTBLOESSTWIRDX
```

</details>

This directs `OKM` to sell equipment and horses that can reach Germany neither by marching nor by rail, while preventing the German troops from being left entirely without them. The raw wording is already substantially legible, but this complete reading requires **seven observed-coordinate changes and twelve dash fills**. It is an explicitly repaired source edition.

The seven substitutions, at zero-based source indices, are `18 V→F`, `43 V→F`, `51 V→F`, `61 G→D`, `106 D→X`, `124 X→D` and `192 X→D`. The certificate lists each affected plaintext label and each independently priced dash fill.

The printed second part contains 44 complete five-coordinate groups followed by one extra X: **221 source slots against RICHI-220**. Excluding only that final X before untransposition yields:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional exclusion of the final observed X at source index 220:**

```text
GLEICHESERGEHTANXETRAXSUEDOSTXFECHXGRXHXQUXUNDKRIWEISOKMXNRX??1?X11X1?XANCHXKMXALLGMXKRDPXNRX2???X1?XGEHXANCHX
```

</details>

The opening says that the same instruction goes to the listed addressees. `ETRA SUEDOST`, `FECH`, `KRIWEISOKM`, `KRDP`, the `ANCH` tokens and all partly known references remain literal. In particular, `FECH` has not been silently reordered into a more familiar word.

The [existing FD=8 and VA=5 constraints](../../experiments/nov16_18_reference_completion/README.md)
give `Nr. 5?18 / 11 / 18` and `Nr. 25?? / 18` in the closing references.
They fix **five further positions**, reaching **107/110** under the same
conditional 220-slot frame. No coordinate is changed or filled; the final
printed X remains the sole frame exclusion.

The verifier prices all **221 possible single-coordinate exclusions** against this retrospective known-letter template, allowing the marked numeral positions to remain in any of the eight unfilled square cells. Excluding index 220 is the sole zero-substitution placement in that bounded comparison. That is conditional template evidence, not proof that the final X was historical padding or that all other damage mechanisms are impossible. The unmodified 221-slot reading and its unpaired coordinate are preserved alongside the conditional reading.

## Finland: p207 C1–C2

The header reads `KOW v LP (04.04 p.m., November 18th)`, `17.00 (18/11) FUER - H 2 TLE`. The message and reception time fields are retained without imposing a chronology.

Part 1, after the single substitution `32 F→G`, reads:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ANDEUTSCHENGENERALINFINNLANDXXDORTIGEXNRXBXCX212XUNDXRMX1AXNRX???XBEURTEILENLAGEVERSCHIEDENXOHLXNIMMTANX
```

</details>

Part 2, after `66 V→A` and `67 G→A`, reads:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
BALDIGERABTRAANSPORTFUERNOETIGGEHALTENWIRDXOHLXRMX1AXNOX11?1?XGEHXOPXX
```

</details>

The German general in Finland is told that two cited reports assess the situation differently. OHL assumes that early removal or transport of the force is considered necessary. The body contains the literal doubled A in `ABTRAANSPORT`; it has not been deleted. The references `B.C.212`, `RM.1A`, `11?1?`, and the other partly known number remain unexpanded.

Under the same `FD=8` layer, the first message’s three-digit reference becomes **?8?**.
That part reaches **102/104** positions with its earlier one-coordinate
word repair. The two outer digits and the second part's reference remain
unresolved.

The raw beginning of part 2 is `BALDIGLRABTRAAN?PORT`. The unknown label inside the word has the numeral domain `03456789` under the published square. Producing S requires the stated observed-coordinate substitution into the existing S cell. It is a word repair, **not** a newly inferred square assignment. The two unresolved numeral labels later in the reference remain unknown.

## Reproduction and credit

Run the [standalone verifier](../../experiments/repatriation_orders/verify.py):

```bash
python experiments/repatriation_orders/verify.py --verify
python experiments/repatriation_orders/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf
```

The default check needs only the Python standard library. The optional PDF check uses PyMuPDF to verify the exact scan hash and all nine saved source-image pixel hashes. The [experiment README](../../experiments/repatriation_orders/README.md) gives the finite scope and provenance. The seven earlier OCR candidates are retained in [prior evidence](../../experiments/repatriation_orders/prior_evidence.json), including their omitted rows, damaged group lengths and partial earlier readings. George Lasry's published key, Childs's source, and the research of Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker remain credited separately from this source-edition work.

# Romanian pacification proposal and a request for consultation

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p157 A, PDF p160, is headed `LP v NKJ (--- November 8th)` and
`5 TLE`, beneath a page heading dated **7th NOVEMBER, 1918**. The
[overview](../../experiments/romanian_pacification_consultation/sources/p157_overview.png)
shows the surviving source divisions. Parts **2–5** are transcribed and
decoded below using the unchanged partial **Nov7–9** key. The incomplete
first part remains separate contextual evidence; the date difference is
not silently resolved.

The readable portions concern a proposed pacification action, a request
for a general to discuss it, and a request for early information. They do
not report that the proposed action took place. The beginning of part 2
is a continuation fragment, so the event preceding “Ministeriums
herbeigeführt” is not supplied here.

## p157 A2

The [source crop](../../experiments/romanian_pacification_consultation/sources/p157_A2.png)
contains **200 slots**, matching `2 TL RICHI-200`.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 200-coordinate frame:**

```text
MINISTERIUMLFERBEIGEFUEHRTXRUYAENISCHERLGIERUNGZIXTINERWAEGUNGXEINEMILITAEWISCHEPAZIAIZIERUNGSAKTION
```

**Edited output — 7 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 printed-mask fills:**

```text
MINISTERIUMSHERBEIGEFUEHRTXRUMAENISCHEREGIERUNGZIETINERWAEGUNGXEINEMILITAERISCHEPAZIFIZIERUNGSAKTION
```

</details>

Seven observed-coordinate substitutions repair the indicated candidate words:
**1 X→V, 32 G→F, 33 D→V, 137 X→D, 138 D→X, 141 D→X, 184 V→D**.
The literal edited spelling **ZIET** remains; `zie[h]t` below supplies H
only in the displayed German. No coordinate or plaintext slot is added.

**Readable German — spacing, punctuation, umlauts and explicitly bracketed display letters:**

> Ministeriums herbeigeführt. Rumänische Regierung zie[h]t in Erwägung eine militärische Pazifizierungsaktion

## p157 A3

The [source crop](../../experiments/romanian_pacification_consultation/sources/p157_A3.png)
contains **218 slots**, matching `3 TL RICHI-218`.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 218-coordinate frame:**

```text
NACHSIEBENBUERGENXOBKDOXHATZRSUCHTXEINENBEVOLLMXGENERALSOFORTNACHBUKARSTZURBESPRECHUNGUEBERDIESEANGELEGEN4EIT
```

**Edited output — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 printed-mask fills:**

```text
NACHSIEBENBUERGENXOBKDOXHATERSUCHTXEINENBEVOLLMXGENERALSOFORTNACHBUKARSTZURBESPRECHUNGUEBERDIESEANGELEGENHEIT
```

</details>

Two observed-coordinate substitutions, **177 F→V** and **196 A→X**,
repair ERSUCHT and ANGELEGENHEIT. The literal **BUKARST** remains;
`Bukar[e]st` supplies E only in the displayed German. The abbreviation
**bevollm.** is retained rather than silently expanded.

**Readable German — spacing, punctuation, umlauts and explicitly bracketed display letters:**

> nach Siebenbürgen. Obkdo. hat ersucht, einen bevollm. General sofort nach Bukar[e]st zur Besprechung über diese Angelegenheit

## p157 A4

The [source crop](../../experiments/romanian_pacification_consultation/sources/p157_A4.png)
contains **210 slots**, matching `4 TL RICHI-210`.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — native 210-coordinate frame:**

```text
ZUENTSENDENXDAFUERSTELLUNGDESOXKXMXDIEHINSICHTLICHWAFFENSTILLSTANDESGEPFLOGENENVEREINBARUNGENENTSCHEIDEND
```

</details>

This native frame requires no changes. “Da für” is a word-boundary reading
of the literal DAFUER; no word or article has been added. Its final
ENTSCHEIDEND continues into the following source-labeled part.

**Readable German — spacing, punctuation and umlauts:**

> zu entsenden. Da für Stellung des O. K. M. die hinsichtlich Waffenstillstandes gepflogenen Vereinbarungen entscheidend

## p157 A5

The [source crop](../../experiments/romanian_pacification_consultation/sources/p157_A5.png)
contains **128 slots**, matching `5 TL RICHI-128`.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 128-coordinate frame:**

```text
SIFDXWIRDUMMOEGLICHSTBA?DIGEORIENTIERUNGGEBETENXOKMXCHEF11291GUH
```

**Edited output — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions and 1 printed-mask fill:**

```text
SINDXWIRDUMMOEGLICHSTBALDIGEORIENTIERUNGGEBETENXOKMXCHEF11291GEH
```

</details>

Observed substitutions **6 A→D** and **64 X→G** repair SIND and GEH.
The printed dash at source **99** is filled with D for BALDIGE. Before
that fill, plaintext position **23** has the domain **02ACLR**; all six
coordinate completions remain in the certificate. **11291** stays literal.

**Readable German — spacing, punctuation and umlauts:**

> sind, wird um möglichst baldige Orientierung gebeten. O. K. M. Chef 11291 Geh.

## Truncated A1: source context, excluded from the four-record count

The [first-part crop](../../experiments/romanian_pacification_consultation/sources/p157_A1.png)
contains **83 visible slots**, including five printed dashes, under a
blank `RICHI----` length heading. Its beginning is missing, and two of the
surviving groups contain four symbols. No native full-frame decryption or
unique gap layout is asserted for this odd-length fragment.

It shares a **33-coordinate exact valid run** with the independently
transcribed [p151 A1](nov7_fragment_and_acknowledgment.md#p151-a1):
p151 source positions **143–175** correspond to p157 A1 positions **38–70**.
The certificate recomputes this comparison from frozen literal sources.
That is evidence of overlapping material, not proof that all source-labeled
parts on the two pages are identical. In particular p151 A2 has **186**
coordinates and a different body from p157 A2's **200**. The p151 opaque
STUR3FSS closing and the absent p157 A1 prefix remain unreconstructed.

## Conditional interpretation, costs and reproduction

The four cataloged native frames contain **756 slots**, **755 valid
coordinates** and **378 plaintext positions**. Raw output fixes
**377 / 378**, edited output **378 / 378**; the exact candidate cost is
**eleven observed substitutions and one printed-mask fill**. A fixed
position can be an abbreviation or numeric label, not an understood word.
The incomplete A1's 83 slots are excluded from every total above.
No numeral assignment, key change or geometry repair is adopted.

The two bracketed display letters in `zie[h]t` and `Bukar[e]st` are absent
from the edited streams. Removing them, folding umlauts and stripping
punctuation reproduces each complete edited stream with separator X
removed. This explicit mapping is checked by the verifier. It does not
claim the missing letters were transmitted or restore them to the source.

Earlier unreviewed body candidates and the published partial key retain
their credit. The new contribution is the source-defined native frames,
visible OCR corrections, reversible repairs and complete evidence
accounting. See [inputs](../../experiments/romanian_pacification_consultation/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/romanian_pacification_consultation/certificates.json),
[prior candidates](../../experiments/romanian_pacification_consultation/prior_candidates.json)
and [verification instructions](../../experiments/romanian_pacification_consultation/README.md).

# Romanian ultimatum and the crossing near Rustschuk

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Three newly source-edited parts belong to Childs's six-part message
on printed pp175–176, PDF pp178–179. The repeated header is
`LP v NKJ (5.40 p.m., November 10th); VON UKS KR 0915 (10/11) 6 TLE`.
Its fourth part is the existing [p176a challenge](../p176a.md), whose
breakthrough proposal retains prior credit to **Norbert and Max Baertl
in 2017**. This frozen three-record companion edition left two other
surviving parts unread; separate later editions now address C3 and A6.
Those parts remain excluded from its original three-record count.

The message reports that the Romanian government has presented an
ultimatum to evacuate its territory or lay down weapons. It then reports
French troops beginning to cross the Danube near Rustschuk and fighting
in progress. A later part discusses sending messages and material first
to Hermannstadt. These are statements in the intercepted report, not
independent confirmation of the events or their timing.

## Conditional shared digits

The two unknown positions in the crossing report use the same cell and both become **7**, taking the edited part to **104/104 labels**. The literal sequence remains **7 X 7 X VORM**; its exact time notation is unresolved. The earlier one-coordinate word repair is retained. The [joint reconstruction](../../experiments/nov10_joint_completion/README.md) combines the earlier Marineamt and formation interpretations with the army-number constraint and the mobilization decree; the reversed 7/9 assignment is retained there.

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the joint square:**

> … oder Waffen niederzulegen. Franzosen haben heute 7 7 vorm. mit Donauuebergang bei Rustschuk begonnen. Kampf im Gange.

<details>
<summary>Exact conditional labels</summary>

**Edited output — p175_C2, conditional shared square; 104/104 fixed positions:**

```text
ODERWAFFENNIEDERZULEGENXFRANZOSENHABENHEUTE7X7XVORMXMITDONAUUEBERGANGBEIXRUSTSCHUKBEGONNENXKAMPFIMGANGEX
```

</details>


## p175 C1

The [first-part source](../../experiments/romanian_ultimatum_companions/sources/p175_C1.png)
has 212 printed slots, including three dashes. Its direct reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ANXOHLXOPXJUDORTX1XAX11212OMXXRUM4ENISCHE?EGI2RUN?STELLTS?EBENULTIMATUMXGEBIETBINNEN24X24XSTUNDENZURAEUMEN
```

</details>

Two observed-coordinate substitutions and three printed-dash fills give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ANXOHLXOPXJUDORTX1XAX11212OMXXRUMAENISCHEREGIERUNGSTELLTSOEBENULTIMATUMXGEBIETBINNEN24X24XSTUNDENZURAEUMEN
```

</details>

The body says that the Romanian government has just issued an ultimatum
to clear the territory within the repeated literal `24X24` hours. The
prefix `JUDORTX1XAX11212OM` remains unidentified and unchanged. The
two copies of `24` are not summed or replaced by another duration.

## p175 C2

The [208-coordinate continuation](../../experiments/romanian_ultimatum_companions/sources/p175_C2.png)
directly reads:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ODERWAFFENNIEDE0ZULEGENXFRANZOSENHABENHEUTE?X?XVORMXMITDONAUUEBERGANGBEIXRUSTSCHUKBEGONNENXKAMPFIMGANGEX
```

</details>

One observed-coordinate replacement gives this candidate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ODERWAFFENNIEDERZULEGENXFRANZOSENHABENHEUTE?X?XVORMXMITDONAUUEBERGANGBEIXRUSTSCHUKBEGONNENXKAMPFIMGANGEX
```

</details>

It completes the ultimatum with the alternative of laying down weapons,
then reports that French troops began crossing near Rustschuk that
morning and that fighting is in progress. The two unknown time digits
are both the same square cell **GF**, so they must agree if the key is
unchanged. Their value remains in **56789**. All 120 injective square
completions preserve the candidate ciphertext and give five equal-digit
possibilities, each in 24 completions. No historical hour is chosen.

## p176 A5

The [fifth-part source](../../experiments/romanian_ultimatum_companions/sources/p176_A5.png)
contains 168 printed slots, including a full five-dash group. It reads:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
NAC?RICHTEN?NDMATER?ALZUN1E?HSTN4CHXHERMANNSTADTXXKANNMITZUSUEHRUNGVONVERPFLEG?ZXUND
```

</details>

Three observed-coordinate substitutions and four dash fills give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
NACHRICHTENUNDMATERIALZUNAECHSTNACHXHERMANNSTADTXXKANNMITZUFUEHRUNGVONVERPFLEG?ZXUND
```

</details>

The beginning directs messages and material first to Hermannstadt. The
following provisioning phrase is incomplete in this edition. The ending
`VERPFLEG?ZXUND`, including its anomalous `Z`, remains unchanged; the
last unknown has domain **56789JQSUZ**. Neither that letter nor an
unseen grammatical continuation is supplied from context.

## Optional VERPFLEGSZ completion

The later [A6 coal-train proposal](p176_coal_train_fragment.md) supplies
`KOHLENZUEGEN … GERECHNETWERDEN` after A5's `KANNMITZUFUEHRUNGVON…UND`.
This context motivates **S** in the provision-train abbreviation `VERPFLEGSZ`.
The optional word layer fixes **84/84 positions** by filling the remaining
printed dash, source **50**, as `D`; with source **136 G**, its pair is `DG=S`.
The price above the primary A5 proposal is **one mask fill and zero observed
substitutions**, giving totals of **three observed substitutions and five
printed-mask fills**. No square cell or historical digit is assigned.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — optional A5 completion conditioned on the A6 continuation; the primary 83/84 reading above remains unchanged:**

```text
NACHRICHTENUNDMATERIALZUNAECHSTNACHXHERMANNSTADTXXKANNMITZUFUEHRUNGVONVERPFLEGSZXUND
```

</details>

The A6 routing field and later tail remain unread. The [supplementary
certificate](../../experiments/p176_verpflegs_joint_completion/certificates.json)
checks the single-event delta and full A5 round trips under all 120 square
completions. [Reproduce the supplement](../../experiments/p176_verpflegs_joint_completion/README.md).
The optional completion is by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

## Surviving unread parts and the earlier challenge

The source sequence is C1, C2, C3 on p175, followed by A4, A5, A6 on
p176. C3 has **217** printed slots against a stated length of **222**;
the missing five coordinates have no selected location. A6 has **160**
printed slots, of which **86** are dashes. Both are retained as source
context within this frozen companion edition, with no contribution to its
three-record totals. The later [conditional C3 withdrawal edition](p175_c3_withdrawal_followup.md)
now supplies a readable candidate while preserving all tied loss layouts.

A4 is already cataloged as p176a. Its earlier reconstructed text and
missing-block assumptions remain separate from these native-frame
companions. Being part of the same source-labeled message does not
independently prove the earlier reconstructed letters.

## Exact scope of the edition

The three new records contain **588 printed slots**, **580 observed
coordinates**, and **294 plaintext positions**. Their raw readings fix
**284** positions; the separately recorded candidates fix **291** after
**six known-coordinate substitutions and seven printed-dash fills**.
One printed dash and two occurrences of an unknown key label remain.
There is no modeled gap, deletion or key change in those three records.

Earlier unreviewed screening already contained the readable C2 and A5
bodies; C1 was garbled in a shorter OCR-derived frame. The present
contribution is exact source transcription, the full arithmetic and
uncertainty record, and a transparent assembly with prior credit.
No first historical decipherment claim is made.

The [package](../../experiments/romanian_ultimatum_companions/README.md),
[inputs](../../experiments/romanian_ultimatum_companions/inputs.json) and
[certificate](../../experiments/romanian_ultimatum_companions/certificates.json)
preserve all coordinates, domains, repairs, source crops, unread context,

reads **RICHI-222**. An initial reading of 232 was rejected. With 217
