15-coordinate estimate is retained only as a transcription-error note,
not as a source model or an alternative restored body. The three readable
records and their repair counts are unchanged.

# Evening report on crossing the Sava

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

## p99 B1

The [source crop](../../experiments/nov1_contact_mail_and_sava/sources/p99_B1.png)
shows `UKS v ZON`, an unspecified reception time on November 2, origin
`2016 (1) AN LP 3 TLE`, and `1 TL RICHI-172`. The native frame has **172
valid coordinates**, including the first row of 40 coordinates omitted from
the earlier OCR-derived frame. Recovering that visible row is a source
transcription correction, not an insertion into a historical transmission.

The published `Nov1-3` square and column ranks give **86/86 fixed plaintext
positions without any coordinate changes, fills or geometry changes**.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — unchanged native frame**

```text
FUERXOXHXLXABENDMELDGXSAVEXISTVONX30XIXDXMITXHAUPTTEILENXVONXGXKX39GANZXUEBERSCHRITTEN
```

</details>

**Readable German — from the unchanged raw layer**

> Fuer O.H.L. Abendmeldg. Save ist von 30 I.D. mit Hauptteilen, von G.K. 39 ganz ueberschritten.

This is an evening report to `O.H.L.`. It says that `30 I.D.` has crossed
the Sava with its main elements and that `G.K. 39` has crossed completely.
The comma reflects the compressed telegram syntax. The text retains the
literal abbreviated unit designations and both numbers; it does not identify
particular formations from outside history. `ABENDMELDG` is not silently
expanded inside the quoted display.

## Possible relation to the p100 challenge

The [p100 A header crop](../../experiments/nov1_contact_mail_and_sava/sources/p100_A_header.png)
has the same `UKS v ZON` direction and `2016 (1)` origin. Its body is the
existing [p100 challenge](../p100.md), whose earlier reading describes no
enemy interference and two enemy divisions marching on Belgrade.

The source headings are not identical: **p99 says `3 TLE`, while p100 says
`2 TLE`**. They support a possible multipart relation, but this edition does
not silently reinterpret the latter as an unambiguous part number, identify
an absent third part, or merge the catalog entries. The earlier p100 body
remains credited to **Armin, 2017-03-01, comment 13**. The current p99 source
edition does not claim a new solution of that challenge.

## Evidence and reproduction

The [literal rows](../../experiments/nov1_contact_mail_and_sava/inputs.json),
[independent certificate](../../experiments/nov1_contact_mail_and_sava/certificates.json)
and [prior-evidence record](../../experiments/nov1_contact_mail_and_sava/prior_evidence.json)

and the earlier 132-coordinate OCR frame. The
[experiment README](../../experiments/nov1_contact_mail_and_sava/README.md)
provides reproducible checks, including exact source-image pixel binding.

The published period key retains the credit of **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel,
Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**. The source and arithmetic review is by
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment priority
is claimed. The [other p99 messages](../radio/nov1_contact_and_mail.md)
concern contact times, service mail and receipt acknowledgment.

# Return Seeflugstation Ost personnel to the second detachment

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p141 B, PDF p144, directs any personnel being returned from
Seeflugstation Ost, formerly Sewastopol, to the second Seefliegerabteilung.
It explicitly says they should not be sent to the first. Its heading is
`ASO v LP (08.19 p.m., November 6th)`, followed by
`FUER ASO 1920 (6/11)`.

## p141 B

The [source crop](../../experiments/mecklenburg_and_seaplane_personnel/sources/p141_B.png)
contains **340 valid coordinates**, exactly matching `RICHI-340`.
The unchanged published **Nov4–6** key fixes all **170 positions** before
editing, although three resulting symbols require ordinary-word repairs.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 340-coordinate frame:**

```text
SEEFLUGSTATIONXOSTXFRUEHERXSEWASTOPOLXETWAZURUECKZUUEBERWEISENDESPERSONALISTANXZWEITEXSEEFLIEGERABTEILUNGUNDNISHTANXERSTEXSXFXAVZUUEBRRWEISENXMARINEFLUGCHEFXGX4774XROEMX1
```

**Edited output — three observed-coordinate substitutions, with no mask fills:**

```text
SEEFLUGSTATIONXOSTXFRUEHERXSEWASTOPOLXETWAZURUECKZUUEBERWEISENDESPERSONALISTANXZWEITEXSEEFLIEGERABTEILUNGUNDNICHTANXERSTEXSXFXAXZUUEBERWEISENXMARINEFLUGCHEFXGX4774XROEMX1
```

</details>

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation:**

> Seeflugstation Ost, früher Sewastopol. Etwa zurückzuüberweisendes
> Personal ist an zweite Seefliegerabteilung und nicht an erste S. F. A.
> zu überweisen. Marineflugchef. G. 4774. Roem. 1.

The changes are source **133 G→D**, **135 G→D** and **175 V→F**.
They repair `NISHT` to `NICHT`, the separator after `S.F.A.`, and
`UEBRRWEISEN` to `UEBERWEISEN`. All other symbols, including the written
`ZWEITE` and `ERSTE`, remain as directly decrypted.

## Conditional interpretation and limits

The instruction concerns personnel **if returned**; it does not establish
that a transfer actually took place. `S.F.A.` is retained as the telegram's
abbreviation, and **GX4774XROEMX1** remains the literal reference. No new
formation number, administrative interpretation or numerical relabeling is
needed to read the contrast between the second and first detachments.

The complete candidate re-encrypts to the source after exactly those
three substitutions. There is no insertion, deletion, erasure fill,
frame change or key change. The prior repository screen already contained
this body with OCR-induced uncertainties; this edition resolves the
source transcription and makes the editorial changes independently checkable.

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p139 A1/A2/A3, PDF p142, form the message headed
`NKJ v LP (5.57 a.m., November 6th)` and `SSD FUER ASO 1940 3 TLE`.
The consecutive source labels give native lengths **200 / 220 / 212**.
All three parts use the unchanged published **Nov4–6** key.

The opening and distribution are readable German routing text. Part 2
contains **CUJOMAREMO** followed by twelve five-figure groups. The outer
ADFGVX cipher yields those labels, but their possible inner code or
codebook meaning remains unresolved. They are preserved exactly rather
than translated or treated as known quantities.

## p139 A1

The [first-part crop](../../experiments/sevastopol_coded_routing/sources/p139_A1.png)
contains **200 valid coordinates**, giving **100 / 100 fixed positions**.
The [enlarged heading](../../experiments/sevastopol_coded_routing/sources/p139_A1_length.png)

before publication. There is no inferred 100-coordinate gap.

```text
NATEKOXSEWASTOPOLXVONSEEKRIEGSLTGXGRXHXYUXSLX4475XINABAENDERUNGXFECHX3XGROSSXBXFRX53083XSINDGEMAESSX
```

</details>

**Readable German — spacing, punctuation and umlauts; abbreviations remain literal:**

> NATEKO, Sewastopol. Von Seekriegsltg. Gr. H. YU. SL. 4475.
> In Abänderung FECH. 3. Gross B. FR. 53083 sind gemäß

The sentence continues in part 2. **YU** is retained without converting
it to a more familiar headquarters abbreviation. The raw 3 and all
reference numbers remain unchanged.

## p139 A2

The [second-part crop](../../experiments/sevastopol_coded_routing/sources/p139_A2.png)
contains **220 visible slots**. Its first glyph is B in **BVAGD**, which
is outside the ADFGVX coordinate alphabet. That occupied source slot is
masked without deletion.

<details>



</details>

Source **0 B→X** supplies N in **NR**. The raw unknown is plaintext
position **3**, pair **X?**, domain **4CMNST**, with source indices **194**
and **0**. N is a contextual editorial selection for “Nr.”; the
certificate retains all six complete raw alternatives. The edited
candidate fixes **110 / 110 positions** and re-encrypts exactly.

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation, with the opaque groups copied literally:**

> A. Nr. 11120 Geh. Op. CUJOMAREMO
> 36117 59000 13814 39800
> 42097 85206 82520 51933
> 32342 28215 38105 04376
> zuleiten.

The marker and twelve groups are retained in their source order, including
the initial 0 of **04376**. This reading does not supply their underlying
meaning. In particular, **316 fixed plaintext positions** across the
message would not mean 316 recovered German letters or a solved inner
code.

## p139 A3

The [third-part crop](../../experiments/sevastopol_coded_routing/sources/p139_A3.png)
contains **212 valid coordinates**, giving **106 / 106 fixed positions**.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

```text
GLEICHESSXETRAXSUEDOSTXEZXKIEWXBVGXRUMXSXMXSTXDEUTSCHERSTABXNACARXRXMXAXADMIRALSTABFECH2XGROSZXBXERX53689X
```

</details>

> Stab. NACAR. R. M. A. Admiralstab. FECH2. Grosz B. ER. 53689.

The extra S after **GLEICHES** is retained as a separate S. field.
**EZ** is displayed as “Ez.”, **NACAR** is not changed into an assumed

## Conditional interpretation and source recovery

instead of the scan's 200. The
[frozen OCR snapshot](../../experiments/sevastopol_coded_routing/ocr_snapshot.json)
and [certificate](../../experiments/sevastopol_coded_routing/certificates.json)
verify that single source-visible difference. The old corpus is unchanged.
Restoring the visible X repairs the transcript; it is not an insertion
into the historical ciphertext.

Across the three records there are **632 visible slots**, **631 valid
source coordinates**, and **316 plaintext positions**. The raw layers
fix **315 / 316**; the edited layers fix **316 / 316**, with **zero known
coordinate substitutions and one invalid-glyph fill**. All source frames
and the published key remain unchanged, and every complete edited stream
re-encrypts exactly. The message is an instruction and distribution list,
not proof that a shipment or transmission actually occurred.

Earlier repository candidates and published key provenance remain
explicit, including the previously readable distribution. The edition
makes no historical first-solution claim. See the
[inputs](../../experiments/sevastopol_coded_routing/inputs.json) and

# Prague transport fragment, Ukrainian provisions priority and disarmament orders

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and exact repair accounting: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro (2026).** Published Nov19–21 key: Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker. Earlier unreviewed machine candidates for p209 are preserved and credited; this is not a universal first-decipherment claim.

Childs p209 contains five physical parts from three telegrams intercepted on 19 November 1918. Hand transcription restores rows missed by OCR in A1 and B1, making their native source frames readable. B and C each have both numbered parts; only A's first part appears here.

## Source and exact costs

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed p209, PDF p212. The source crops preserve all five parts, their shared headers and the eight printed dashes in A1. Each counted length agrees with its printed RICHI label. No received coordinate is inserted, deleted, excluded or moved.

| Record | Source slots | Raw fixed → edited fixed | Observed-coordinate substitutions | Printed-dash fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| p209 A1 | 224 | 104/112 → 112/112 | 0 | 8 |
| p209 B1 | 310 | 155/155 → 155/155 | 4 | 0 |
| p209 B2 | 230 | 115/115 → 115/115 | 3 | 0 |
| p209 C1 | 242 | 121/121 → 121/121 | 4 | 0 |
| p209 C2 | 182 | 91/91 → 91/91 | 4 | 0 |
| **Total** | **1,188** | **586/594 → 594/594** | **15** | **8** |

The 1,188 source slots comprise 1,180 valid ADFGVX coordinates and eight printed dashes.

“Fixed” describes output under the published square labels. It does not independently authenticate reference numbers, remove transmission mistakes or establish uniquely correct wording. Source-directed repairs remain proposals with their exact coordinate cost.

## A1: an incomplete statement from Prague

The header reads `ZO'N v LP`, intercept `06.30 p.m., November19th`, followed by `22.35 (19/11) 2 TLE`; the delivered text is explicitly `1 TL`. It addresses `OK MACKENSEN` and reports that the Minister-President in Prague has made a statement concerning transport of Mackensen's army group on the Teschen route. The clause stops at Teschen, so the operative continuation is unknown. No permission, refusal, destination beyond Teschen or later transport decision is supplied.

Eight printed dashes occupy source indices 97–104. Filling them supplies the missing letters in `MACKENSEN`, `MINISTERPRAESIDENT`, `HAT`, `ERKLAERT`, `STRECKE` and `TESCHEN`, without changing any observed coordinate. This is a lexical restoration from the surviving text, not an independent unseen prediction.

The conspicuous adjective `TS8HESCHICHE` stays unchanged. Its context suggests Czech, but the edition neither changes the 8 label to a letter nor normalizes the malformed spelling. The missing second part is outside this edition.

## B1/B2: food transport takes priority over raw materials

The two parts share `IWE v LP`, intercept `07.31 p.m., November19th`, and `04.00 (19/11) 2 TLE`. The message addresses `HEERESGR X KIEW`. Because of difficulties with food supply and shortage of transport, it orders the utmost acceleration of dispatching all provisions acquired or available in Ukraine, giving them priority over raw materials of every kind.

The first forty printed coordinates of B1 were omitted by the earlier OCR stream. Restoring the actual first source row gives the native 310-coordinate frame and the coherent order. This is a correction to the machine transcription, not an insertion into the received source.

B1's four single-coordinate repairs are `TRANSPORTMITTEC→TRANSPORTMITTEL`, `AHBEFOERDERUNG→ABBEFOERDERUNG`, `UKRAING→UKRAINE` and `BESCHAFFTGN→BESCHAFFTEN`. Its `ABMMD` label and final `LEBENSMITTELM` remain untouched. In B2, three observed-coordinate changes produce `AUCHDER` and `ABBEFOERDERUNG` from raw `AUCQ6ER` and `ABBE9OERDERUNG`. These local word repairs do not assign Q, 6 or 9 new global square meanings.

The ending `NO X J0192SM X BEWEGE X BERLIN` remains exactly as the baseline labels yield it. No reference number or agency expansion is inferred.

## C1/C2: arms surrendered in Warsaw

The two numbered parts share `KOW WAU v LP`, intercept `08.05 p.m., November19th`, and `22.30 (19/11) 2 TLE`. The text says that a large number of organized units in the former General Government of Warsaw had given weapons to the Poles. It continues that there must be no doubt that it is dishonourable for organized units to allow themselves to be disarmed without a fight. This is the message's statement and instruction.

C1 needs four single-coordinate repairs: `GROSSEDNZAHL→GROSSEANZAHL`, two letters in `GESCCLOJSENER→GESCHLOSSENER`, and `ESDDRF→ESDARF`. The grammatical anomaly `HABENGROSSEANZAHL` is retained. Its first-row final group is visibly `GFXAF`: the two unknown slots in an earlier OCR candidate were fictitious, and no source-mask fills are counted here.

C2 has four single-coordinate repairs: `WESN→WENN`, `GESCHLOSNENE→GESCHLOSSENE`, `SICL→SICH` and `LNSSEN→LASSEN`. Its final `OHL X RMJAJJ970 GEH X OP` remains unnormalized. No J or numeral relabel is proposed.

## Raw streams and edited proposals

### p209 A1

```text

```

**Edited output:**

```text

```

</details>

### p209 B1

<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

```text
HEERESGRXKIEWXABMMDXWEGENSCHWIERIGKEITENERNAEHRUNGSFRAGEUNDMANGELTRANSPORTMITTECISTAHBEFOERDERUNGSAEMTLICHERINXUKRAINGBESCHAFFTGNUNDGREIFBARENLEBENSMITTELM
```


</details>

### p209 B2

```text
AUFDASAEUSSERSTEZUBESCHLEUNIGENUNDAUCQ6ERABBE9OERDERUNGVONROHSTOFFENALLERARTVORANZUSTELLENXNOXJ0192SMXBEWEGEXBERLIN
```

**Edited output:**

```text
AUFDASAEUSSERSTEZUBESCHLEUNIGENUNDAUCHDERABBEFOERDERUNGVONROHSTOFFENALLERARTVORANZUSTELLENXNOXJ0192SMXBEWEGEXBERLIN
```


**Edited output:**


</details>

### p209 C2

</details>

## Evidence and reproduction

The [inputs](../../experiments/transport_and_disarmament_orders/inputs.json) preserve all literal source rows, headers, published key values and crop-rendering metadata. The [certificates](../../experiments/transport_and_disarmament_orders/certificates.json) enumerate all fifteen substitutions, eight fills and every plaintext pair's original source coordinates. The [prior candidate snapshot](../../experiments/transport_and_disarmament_orders/prior_candidates.json) retains the old OCR candidates, including readable B2/C bodies and frozen retrieval entries; the bounded publication check is not a universal priority claim.

# Surviving Transylvania situation report

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

This is a proposed cross-page assembly of an eight-part message marked 1840 / 18.40, 8 TLE, LP v NKJ. Parts 1, 7 and 8 survive on pp128–129; p137 supplies part 4 and conditional partial readings of interference-damaged parts 5 and 6. Parts 2 and 3 remain unlocated. All uses of the Nov4–6 key retain its published square and ranks.

The headings conflict: pp128–129 say 5 November with different evening receipt times; p137 has a 6 November page heading and 08.14 on 5 November in its receipt line, alongside the 18.40 origin. Matching headers, part numbers and content support the association but do not resolve those dates or prove an exact transmission history.

## Missing and unread material

The p128 copy explicitly states that parts 2–6 are missing. The separate p137 page supplies independent surviving material for 4–6. It does not restore parts 2/3, and part 6 has no stated length. A [separate conditional A6 edition](p137_publicity_fragment.md) proposes 25 letters in a 254-slot frame, preserving 102 unknown positions and the equally compatible 256/258-slot alternatives. Its polarity and intervening verb remain unread.

## p128 B1

Military situation after the collapse in Transylvania and Hungary’s armistice.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame with its printed mask retained:**

```text
OHLOPXXFEINDLAGEXVOELLIGEDEROUTEINSIEBENBUERGENUNDWAFFENSTILLSTANDUNGARNSMACHTMILITA?RISCHELAGEDER
```

**Edited output — same native frame; stated printed-mask fill:**

```text
OHLOPXXFEINDLAGEXVOELLIGEDEROUTEINSIEBENBUERGENUNDWAFFENSTILLSTANDUNGARNSMACHTMILITAERISCHELAGEDER
```

</details>

## p137 A4

Security measures at Kronstadt/Hermannstadt and intended material transport.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional single-slot and five-coordinate gaps; one representative tied layout:**

```text
OXKXM0HATMASSNAHMENZURSICHERUNGVONKRONST?D1UNDHERMANNSTADTGETROFFENUNDB?AB?ICHTIGTM?TABTRAN?PORTVONM?TE?IALI?N9ONMORGENABZUBEGINNENX
```

**Edited output — same conditional two-gap layout, with the stated substitutions and fills:**

```text
OXKXMXHATMASSNAHMENZURSICHERUNGVONKRONSTADTUNDHERMANNSTADTGETROFFENUNDBEABSICHTIGTMITABTRANSPORTVONMATERIALIENVONMORGENABZUBEGINNENX
```

</details>

Printed 258 / advertised 264: a one-coordinate gap in AAAV plus a five-coordinate gap are modeled separately. All 1,295 placements give four tied minima: single gap 5/6/7/8 and five-coordinate gap 69. The primary candidate needs three observed-coordinate changes, two invalid-glyph fills and six missing-coordinate fills. An independently retained A/X source-glyph alternative lowers the observed changes to two; primary totals use A.

## p137 A5

The conditional complete reading orders the removal of economic and
administrative staffs before military movements begin:

**Readable German — conditional complete part-5 proposal:**

> Anschliessend muessen vor Beginn militaerischer Bewegungen Personal der
> Wirtschafts- und Verwaltungsstaebe ab 6. November abgeschoben werden.

The proposal reaches **126/126 positions**, including two separately priced
`X` separators after `WIRTSCHAFTS` and `WERDEN`. Each separator supplies one
missing coordinate while retaining its observed half. The full part costs
**seven observed substitutions, four printed-mask fills and 37 missing-coordinate
fills** under the earlier conditional 0/37 interference frame. The source-68
V alternative lowers the substitution total to six. The literal `MUESSEN`
and date label `6` are retained.

The [completion account](../../experiments/p137_governing_clause/README.md#completing-the-two-separators)
shows all 36 possible residual label pairs before the punctuation choice.
This completes the proposed reading of part 5; the missing parts and the
separate part-6 fragment remain as described above.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 0/37 interference-loss allocation, selected by the stated prefix crib:**

```text
ANS?HLI?SSE?DMUE?SEN?ORB?GNN?MI?I?AER?SC??RSO?RG?N?ENP?RS??ALD?RW?R?SSH?FT??UNQ?ER?K?TUN?SS??EBE?B6?N?VEM?ER??GES?HO?E?WER?EN?
```

**Edited output — same conditional interference-loss model; four partial word completions:**

```text
ANSCHLIESSENDMUESSEN?ORB?GNN?MILITAERISCHERSO?RG?N?ENPERSONALDERW?R?SSH?FT??UNQ?ER?K?TUN?SS??EBE?B6?NOVEMBERABGESCHOBENWERDEN?
```

</details>

Printed 215 / advertised 252 means 37 missing coordinates in addition to four printed dashes. All 38 allocations between the two explicit INTERFERENCE locations are retained. The 0/37 model is the unique zero-observed-error fit for the explicit 20-character prefix ANSCHLIESSENDMUESSEN; this remains conditional on that crib. Four compatible word spans fill 21 erased coordinates without changing any observed coordinate. Twenty plaintext positions and the awkward observed middle wording remain unresolved. This is a partial reading, not a completed sentence.

A [separate staff-vocabulary proposal](../../experiments/p137_optional_staff_vocabulary/README.md)
reads `WIRTSCHAFTS?UNDVERWALTUNGSSTAEBE` under the same conditional 0/37 frame.
It adds three observed-coordinate substitutions and ten missing-coordinate
fills; the alternative reading of one overtyped source glyph is retained
separately. Ten plaintext positions remain unresolved, including the literal
`?B6?` field. The primary partial edition above and its zero-substitution
price remain unchanged. Independent witnesses attest the two staff compounds,
not this complete clause or its historical execution.

The [governing-clause supplement](../../experiments/p137_governing_clause/README.md)
first extends the optional reading to **124/126 positions**: `VORBEGINN
MILITAERISCHER BEWEGUNGEN` and `AB6XNOVEMBER`. Relative to the staff layer,
it adds four observed substitutions, one printed-mask fill and seven
missing-coordinate fills. The separate `AB6X` proposal needs only two fills
and preserves the observed 6. The two final separator fills give the complete
optional reading displayed above; the governing clause remains a contextual
reconstruction.

## p129 A7

Request concerning the unknown general political situation and a possible armistice.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame with its printed dash retained:**

```text
ALLGEMEINERHIERNICHTBEKANNTERPOLITISCHERLAGEXXEVTLXEINTRITTEINESWAFFENS?ILLSTANDESVXABHAENGIGZUMACHENWAEREXDRINGENDERBETENXX
```

**Edited output — same native frame; printed-dash fill only:**

```text
ALLGEMEINERHIERNICHTBEKANNTERPOLITISCHERLAGEXXEVTLXEINTRITTEINESWAFFENSTILLSTANDESVXABHAENGIGZUMACHENWAEREXDRINGENDERBETENXX
```

</details>

Only its printed dash is filled. Raw VX and the absent governing context remain unresolved.

## p129 A8

Request for acknowledgment; raw secret reference retained.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame; baseline reference labels retained:**

```text
GLENCHESDURCHFER4SPRUCHVEMPFANGBESTAETIGENXXOXKXMX1ANOX11226O6XGEHEIMX
```

**Edited output — same native frame; three stated coordinate substitutions:**

```text
GLEICHESDURCHFERNSPRUCHXEMPFANGBESTAETIGENXXOXKXMX1ANOX11226O6XGEHEIMX
```

</details>

Three coordinate substitutions repair two words and the separator before EMPFANG. The reference 1ANOX11226O6 retains its original 1 and letter O.

## Evidence and totals

The five readable physical sources provide 550 modeled plaintext positions: 499 fixed under their declared raw geometries and 530 after the stated candidates. Costs are six observed-coordinate substitutions, seven fills of printed dashes/invalid glyphs, and 24 missing-coordinate fills. The 74-slot part 6 now has its own [25-letter conditional catalogue entry](p137_publicity_fragment.md); it remains excluded from these five-source totals. That separate model has zero raw fixed positions and does not establish the missing sentence.

The earlier corpus screen already recognized parts 1/7/8. Lasry et al. describe a different thirteen-part report of 3 November in their Table 3; this edition makes no first historical decipherment claim. A complete 788-block exact-window search found only one short 12-coordinate incidental lead and no missing part 2/3.

[Source transcripts and attribution](../../experiments/transylvania_situation_report/inputs.json), [full source/geometry/interference certificates](../../experiments/transylvania_situation_report/certificates.json), and [method, limits and reproduction](../../experiments/transylvania_situation_report/README.md).

# Turkish armistice report: stop supply shipments and send evacuation ships

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p90 B1 and p91 A2/A3, PDF pp93–94, form one source-labeled
three-part message. Both pages repeat the receiving header
`OSM v LP (12.52 p.m., November 1st)` and the line
`SSD SSD BVG KOSPOLI (1.11) 01.55 3 TEILE`. The consecutive 1, 2, 3
labels support the assembly. All parts use the unchanged **Nov1–3** key.

The message reports news from an intercepted radio transmission, then
gives shipping instructions. It should be read as a historical report
and order, rather than independent confirmation of the reported armistice
conditions or of ships actually sailing.

## p90 B1

The [first-part crop](../../experiments/turkish_armistice_shipping_order/sources/p90_B1.png)
has **338 valid coordinates**, matching `1 TL RICHI-338`.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 338-coordinate frame:**

```text
BVGXKOSPOLIXXNACHAUFGEFANG7NEMFUNKSPRUCHWAFFENSTILLSTANDTUERHEIMITENTE8TAABGESCHLOSZENXBEDINGUNGENDOPPELTUNKTFREIEDURCHFAHRTXDARDANELLENXUNDXBOSPORUSXINSCHWARZESMEERSTOP
```

**Edited output — six observed-coordinate substitutions, with no fills:**

```text
BVGXKOSPOLIXXNACHAUFGEFANGENEMFUNKSPRUCHWAFFENSTILLSTANDTUERKEIMITENTENTEABGESCHLOSSENXBEDINGUNGENDOPPELPUNKTFREIEDURCHFAHRTXDARDANELLENXUNDXBOSPORUSXINSCHWARZESMEERSTOP
```

</details>

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation:**

> BVG, Kospoli. Nach aufgefangenem Funkspruch Waffenstillstand Türkei
> mit Entente abgeschlossen. Bedingungen, Doppelpunkt: freie Durchfahrt
> Dardanellen und Bosporus in schwarzes Meer. Stop.

The wording `in schwarzes Meer` follows literal `INSCHWARZESMEER`; no grammatical normalization is applied.

The raw labels **7** in `AUFGEFANG7NEM` and **8** in `ENTE8TA` are
repaired through the listed local source substitutions. This does not
relabel those symbols elsewhere or change the key. **BVGXKOSPOLI** is
already fully present in the raw output.

## p91 A2

The [second-part crop](../../experiments/turkish_armistice_shipping_order/sources/p91_A2.png)
has **344 valid coordinates**, matching `2 TL RICHI-344`.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 344-coordinate frame:**

```text
KEINERLEIMATEVIALTRANSPORPEEINSCHLXKOHLEXUNDXOELXMEHRNACHXTUERKEIXABSENDENXLEDIGLICHLEERDAMPFERFUERRAEUMUNGSZWECKEIMEINVERNEHMENMITMITTELMEERDIVISIONNACHXKOSPOLIXSENDENSTOP
```

**Edited output — two observed-coordinate substitutions, with no fills:**

```text
KEINERLEIMATERIALTRANSPORTEEINSCHLXKOHLEXUNDXOELXMEHRNACHXTUERKEIXABSENDENXLEDIGLICHLEERDAMPFERFUERRAEUMUNGSZWECKEIMEINVERNEHMENMITMITTELMEERDIVISIONNACHXKOSPOLIXSENDENSTOP
```

</details>

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation:**

> Keinerlei Materialtransporte einschl. Kohle und Oel mehr nach Türkei
> absenden. Lediglich Leerdampfer für Räumungszwecke im Einvernehmen mit
> Mittelmeerdivision nach Kospoli senden. Stop.

The two changes are source **219 V→F** and **291 G→A**, repairing
`MATEVIAL` and `TRANSPORPE`. The destination and the order's distinction
between material shipments and empty evacuation ships remain as directly
decrypted in the source.

## p91 A3

The [third-part crop](../../experiments/turkish_armistice_shipping_order/sources/p91_A3.png)
contains **236 valid coordinates**, matching `3 TL RICHI-236`.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 236-coordinate frame:**

```text
GLXSXMXSTXDTSCHXSGABXZUGLXFUERXSCHIFFSAUSQL7ICHXXETRASOXBVGXRUMXKOSPOLIXSXAXBERLINXXFECHXRMX2XGROSSXBXRMX5XBXFRX52758X
```

**Edited output — three observed-coordinate substitutions, with no fills:**

```text
GLXSXMXSTXDTSCHXSTABXZUGLXFUERXSCHIFFSAUSGLEICHXXETRASOXBVGXRUMXKOSPOLIXSXAXBERLINXXFECHXRMX2XGROSSXBXRMX5XBXFRX52758X
```

</details>

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation of the abbreviated distribution:**

> Gl. S. M. St. Dtsch. Stab, zugl. für Schiffsausgleich. Etra SO.
> BVG. Rum. Kospoli. S. A. Berlin. FECH. RM. 2. Gross B. RM. 5. B.
> FR. 52758.

The abbreviations, including **GL**, remain unexpanded. The candidate
repairs `SGAB` and `AUSQL7ICH`; it does not infer an organization from
the reference or change any surviving numerical field.

## Conditional interpretation, source qualifications and related traffic

The three primary records contain **459 / 459 algebraically fixed
positions**, before and after the eleven disclosed substitutions. Fixed
positions may still carry received errors. There are no erasure fills,
insertions, deletions, frame changes or key changes in the primary edition,
and all three complete edited candidates re-encrypt exactly.

Two faded D glyphs have separate masked sensitivity variants. A2 source
**39** gives plaintext position **28**, the I in `EINSCHL`; masking it
leaves domain **9FILOU**. A3 source **79** gives position **40**, the S
in `AUSGLEICH`; masking it leaves domain **3BFKQS**. The variants leave
these positions unknown and retain all six possible re-encryption
witnesses. They do not silently fill the glyphs from the desired words.

The separate [p112 D source edition](../../experiments/nov3_evening_and_nov4_radio/inputs.json)
also reports an armistice and access through the Straits, under the later
Nov4–6 key. A [frozen comparison](../../experiments/turkish_armistice_shipping_order/related_traffic.json)
retains its original source and records every raw **BVG** and **KOSPOLI**
occurrence in the present three-part message. These are useful contextual
parallels, but the messages differ in wording, length and headers. They
are not established as retransmissions of the same plaintext. In
particular, this edition leaves p112 D's **BVNXBEIBVGX7OSPOLIX?**
unchanged.

The bodies already appeared in earlier unreviewed repository screens,
and the published period key retains its credit. No historical
first-solution claim is made. The
[inputs](../../experiments/turkish_armistice_shipping_order/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/turkish_armistice_shipping_order/certificates.json)
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/turkish_armistice_shipping_order/README.md)
preserve the complete source, edited coordinates and limits.

# Recall of contract-bound military-mission members from Turkey

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source:** J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
printed p130 A1–A2 and p131 A3–A4, PDF pp133–134.
**Edition:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The four parts share `OSM v OUI (8.25 p.m., November 5th)` and
`#12 2015 4 TEILE`. The order recalls contract-bound members of the
military mission, including those already under notice of termination,
and directs arrangements for return and reporting after arrival in
Germany. One received office abbreviation remains unresolved; the
edition preserves it visibly alongside the readable instructions.

The unchanged Nov4–6 square and ranks produce all 645 plaintext labels.
The [experiment](../../experiments/turkish_mission_recall/README.md)
retains exact source crops, coordinates, domains and repair costs.

## p130 A1

The source advertises and prints **394 valid coordinates**. The second
group, `VGVVF`, is complete in the source but was omitted by earlier OCR.
The raw 197-position reading needs no coordinate change:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
MILITAERMISZIONKONSTANTINOPELXZURM2NR46873XSEMAJDERKAISERUKOENIGHABENBEFOHLENXSAEMTLICHEVERTRAGLICHVERPFLICHTETENMITGLIEDERDERMILMISZIONEINSCHLISZLICHDERJENIGENWELCHENDERVERTRAGBEREITSGEKUENDIGTIST
```

</details>

The text addresses the military mission at Constantinople, retains the
raw reference `ZURM2NR46873`, and states an order of the Emperor and King
concerning all members bound by contract, including those whose
contracts had already been given notice. The transmitted `SZ` forms and
`EINSCHLISZLICH` remain exactly as received.

## p130 A2

The source advertises and prints **330 valid coordinates**. The raw text is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
WERDENAUFGRUNDMESIRTIKELS10DESMITGENERALDERKAVLIMANVONSANDERSABESCHLOSZENENVERTRAGSMITDEMTAGEDERVEROEFFENTLICHUNGDESWAFFENSTILLSTANDESDERTUERKEIZUMHEEREZURUCKBERUFEN
```

</details>

The conservative candidate makes only two ordinary-letter changes:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
WERDENAUFGRUNDDESARTIKELS10DESMITGENERALDERKAVLIMANVONSANDERSABESCHLOSZENENVERTRAGSMITDEMTAGEDERVEROEFFENTLICHUNGDESWAFFENSTILLSTANDESDERTUERKEIZUMHEEREZURUCKBERUFEN
```

</details>

These require source-coordinate **156 X→D** and **176 X→F**, both
zero-based. They repair `MESIRTIKELS` to `DESARTIKELS`. The article label
`10`, the name `LIMANVONSANDERS`, and all other pairs remain unchanged.

The text says the members are recalled to the army, under the cited
article of the contract with General der Kav. Liman von Sanders,
effective upon publication of Turkey's armistice. The received
`ABESCHLOSZENEN` and `ZURUCKBERUFEN` are not lengthened by supplying
an unseen `G` or `E`. The underlying contract is not independently
authenticated by this edition.

## p131 A3

The source advertises and prints **396 valid coordinates**, separately
from the following fourth part. Earlier OCR merged the two frames.
The 198-position raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DIEMILMISZIONVERANLASZTZUGEGEBENENENZEITPUNKTDIEHEIMSENDUNGUWEISTDIEHEIMKEHRENDENANIHRENAUFENTHALTSORTSOGLEICHNACHEINTREFFENINDEUTSCHLANDDEMMILIGRHYUBEZWDENKRIEGSMINISTERIENDERBUNDESSTAATENZUDRAHTEN
```

</details>

No coordinate change is proposed. The mission is to arrange the return
at the relevant time and instruct those returning to telegraph their
whereabouts immediately after arriving in Germany. The recipients are
the unresolved received **`MILIGRHYU`** and, in the following `BEZW`
clause, the war ministries of the federal states.

The nine letters at plaintext indices **140–148** all have complete
observed pairs, but the office word is not resolved. It is not silently
replaced with a plausible Military Cabinet abbreviation. The apparent
duplication in `ZUGEGEBENENEN` also remains. Thus 198 fixed square labels
do not mean that every word has been editorially identified.

## p131 A4

The source advertises and prints **170 valid coordinates**. The raw text is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
LETZTERESINDBENACHRICHTIGTXWUFALLERHOECHSTENBEFEHLCHEFMILITAERKABINETTSFRHRMARSCHALLX
```

</details>

The candidate changes only **source index 133 A→V**, giving `AUF`
instead of `WUF`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
LETZTERESINDBENACHRICHTIGTXAUFALLERHOECHSTENBEFEHLCHEFMILITAERKABINETTSFRHRMARSCHALLX
```

</details>

It reports that the latter recipients have been notified and closes
with the received title and signature. With editorial spacing:

**Readable German:**

> Letztere sind benachrichtigt. Auf allerhöchsten Befehl, Chef Militärkabinetts, Frhr. Marschall.

The complete 58-character closing beginning `AUF` is independently
observed in the raw reading of already-reviewed
[p149 A2](../people/osthoff.md). The verifier compares all 58 coordinate
pairs and keeps the earlier source hash and crop. This is support for
the repaired closing; the other message concerns Osthoff and is not
treated as an exact retransmission of this entire order. The earlier
record is not counted again, and no independent identity is assigned
to the received `FRHR MARSCHALL` signature.

## Attribution, costs and limits

The four records contain **1,290 valid source coordinates** and **645
fixed raw labels**. The candidate costs **three observed-coordinate
substitutions**, with no erasure fills, source insertions, deletions,
key changes or rank changes. All numeric labels remain unchanged.
The nine-letter office field remains unresolved despite its complete
coordinates.

The key is previously published. Part two was already readable in the
earlier unreviewed repository screen; defective OCR and merged frames
obscured the other parts. Frozen earlier outputs distinguish source
correction from prior body availability. Bounded paper, dissertation
and comment-thread checks did not locate an explicit treatment of this
body, without establishing historical priority.

The text records a recall order and reporting instructions. It does not
establish that each person returned, that each report was sent or that
the cited contract has been independently verified.

```bash
python experiments/turkish_mission_recall/verify.py --verify
python experiments/turkish_mission_recall/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
```

cases/military/wallachia_withdrawal_prep.text:
# Wallachia withdrawal preparations: p150 B1–B5

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** Five readable parts in their unchanged native source frames. The edition resolves ordinary text while leaving one wholly erased date symbol open.

Source edition and exact verification: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The unchanged **Nov4–6** period key is credited to Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker. Earlier unreviewed candidates already exposed the first and final parts; their texts and any appearances in the frozen p73 retrieval corpus are retained in the package. The newly complete source edition does not claim first decipherment of every included sentence.

## Meaning and source

The message reports to OHL that OKM has prepared to depart on the raw date `12.11` if ordered. Further delay is considered highly undesirable because of the enemy situation along the Danube, particularly near Rustschuk. If the enemy crosses earlier, the Wallachian plain would have to be evacuated. Advance parties have been sent to Kronstadt and Hermannstadt; railway lines are to come under German operation. Constanta and Medgidia have been evacuated, and the former Dobrudscha administration has moved to Kronstadt as an army rear-area administration.

These are claims in the telegram, not independent verification of the movements. The source's `KONSTANTA` spelling is retained, as are its abbreviations and reference labels.

Childs printed page 150 / PDF page 153 has the page heading 6 November 1918 and intercept header `B) LP v NKJ (--- November 7th)`, `2100 (6) VON UKS 5 TLE`. Those two dates are preserved separately. Parts 1/2/3/5 carry lengths 194/198/204/214. Part 4's length heading is partly cancelled or overwritten; its **202 actual source slots are counted independently**, without reading that number back into the damaged annotation.

Part 3's `WALACHEI??E?E` is completed lexically as `WALACHEIEBENE`. # Supply cargo at Nikolaev and the sale of Corcovado

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and recovery: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

**Prior identification of the p199 A body: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils
Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), §6.5.**

Five source records recover two distinct messages intercepted on November 15,
1918. The first reports on steamers and goods at Nikolaev and asks what the
recipient intends to do as circumstances change. The second orders that a
ship sale to Turkey, or the transfer of ownership following a sale, should
be stopped unless the stated payment condition is met.

Both messages use the published `Nov13-15b` partial square. They are separate
traffic, not overlapping copies of one plaintext. Literal source crops and
headers are in the [source edition](../../experiments/black_sea_shipping/inputs.json),
and each geometric choice and coordinate repair is in the
[exact certificate](../../experiments/black_sea_shipping/certificates.json).
The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, printed pp. 199–200, PDF pp. 202–203.

Lasry and colleagues already describe the p199 supply message in
[their paper](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461), §6.5, *A Code
within a Code* (author PDF p. 25, printed p. 24). The work added here for p199
is the exact source edition, the full set of frame alternatives and
coordinate-level repair certificates. Its body identification is credited
to that prior publication. Their approximate ten-ton paraphrase differs from
the `120`-ton field obtained below under the conditional shared digit reading.

## The three-part supply message, p199 A

The common source header reads `XYZ v LP (06.01 p.m., November 15th)`,
`16.50 (15/11)`, `3 TLE`. It belongs to the correspondence using
`FEIGENHAUS`, `HERKULES` and `REICHSVERSORGUNG`, also seen in the earlier
[p120/p123 messages](p120_p123.md). The new reference is written out as
`SECHSHUNDERTACHTZEHN` (618); the earlier message has 617. This is further
correspondence, not a retransmission of the previously published text.

### A1: incoming steamers and a garbled cargo description

**Readable German — existing source frame and word repairs, with conditional VG=2:**

> An Feigenhaus sechshundertachtzehn. Herkules meldet zwoelften November, dass Nikolajew mehrere Dampfer LEBER Kakaopulver aus OPERETTE, zirka 120 Tonnen, eingelaufen.

The [shared award-class interpretation](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md#the-award-class)
assigns **VG=2**, completing the quantity `1?0` as **120** and fixing
**146/146** labels in this edition. The quantity's pair is formed by observed
source coordinates **52 and 235**; no new repair is required.

The source advertises `RICHI-292`, but prints **293 valid coordinates**.
Its tenth group is the six-letter `XAXADV`. Removing its final `V`, source
index 50, gives this 146-position raw decryption:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional removal of the final V in six-coordinate group XAXADV:**

```text
ANFEIGENHAUSSECHSHUNDERTACHTZEHNXHERKULESMELDETZWOEZFTENNOVEMBERDASSNIKOLAJEWMEHREREDAMPFERLEBERKAKAUPULSERAUSXOPERETTEXZIRKA1?0TONNENEINGELAUFENX
```

</details>

It addresses Feigenhaus and reports Herkules's news of November 12 about
several steamers entering Nikolaev. The cargo wording is damaged. Three
observed-coordinate substitutions support the same-length ordinary-word
repairs `ZWOELFTEN` and `KAKAOPULVER`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional single-coordinate deletion, followed by word repairs:**

```text
ANFEIGENHAUSSECHSHUNDERTACHTZEHNXHERKULESMELDETZWOELFTENNOVEMBERDASSNIKOLAJEWMEHREREDAMPFERLEBERKAKAOPULVERAUSXOPERETTEXZIRKA1?0TONNENEINGELAUFENX
```

</details>

`LEBER` remains unexplained, and `OPERETTE` remains an unidentified code word.
The displayed baseline streams retain `1?0`; the readable text above applies
the shared conditional digit assignment.

The deletion is not called globally unique. When names, the `LEBER` segment
and the quantity are masked, deleting source index 50, 51 or 52 gives the same
minimum of three ordinary-word coordinate changes. Only index 50 lies inside
the visibly six-letter source group. The certificate retains all three
broader models, including the alternatives' changed code-name/quantity text.
With VG=2, the source-50 and source-51 exclusions both yield `120`; the
source-52 exclusion still gives `1G0`. The new digit does not establish a
unique source geometry.

### A2: goods remain aboard under military guard

All 344 source coordinates are valid. The raw 172-position reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DASCHWALBENSCHWANZUNDABTRANVPORTABNIKO?AJEWELSEVORLAEUFIGUNMOEGLICHXWAREBLEIBTDAHERUNTERMILITAERISCHERBEWACHUNGANBORDXVERSUCHETDURCHVORZUGSKARTENDARUEBERNAEHERESZUERFAHRENX
```

</details>

Two observed-coordinate changes restore `ABTRANSPORT` and `NIKOLAJEW`,
giving a complete, exactly reencryptable candidate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
DASCHWALBENSCHWANZUNDABTRANSPORTABNIKOLAJEWELSEVORLAEUFIGUNMOEGLICHXWAREBLEIBTDAHERUNTERMILITAERISCHERBEWACHUNGANBORDXVERSUCHETDURCHVORZUGSKARTENDARUEBERNAEHERESZUERFAHRENX
```

</details>

The plain passage says that the goods therefore remain aboard under military
guard, and asks the recipient to obtain more information through
`VORZUGSKARTEN`. The opening retains `SCHWALBENSCHWANZ` and `ELSE`, alongside
the statement that onward transport is temporarily impossible. These terms
may belong to the correspondence's additional vocabulary code. Recovering
their letters does not identify their operational meaning.

### A3: uncertainty about the recipient's plans

There are 205 printed slots under `RICHI-206`. The malformed group is
`VAYA`, and the next group has an overstruck first glyph recorded as `?`.
The certificate tests all 206 possible single-coordinate insertion boundaries
with the whole footer excluded from the stencil.

Five positions, **164–168**, tie at **zero changes to observed coordinates**
for the ordinary-word body. Gap 165 is a representative, not an established
unique location. Its raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional missing-slot placement at gap 165; equivalent alternatives retained:**

```text
SINDBEUNR?HIGTDANICHTWISS?NWASIHRINANBETRACHTLAGEBEGINNENWERDETXREICHSVERSORGUNGXADMIRALSTAB15?16DZWCIX
```

</details>

Filling two source erasures gives:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional gap model, with the two stated fills:**

```text
SINDBEUNRUHIGTDANICHTWISSENWASIHRINANBETRACHTLAGEBEGINNENWERDETXREICHSVERSORGUNGXADMIRALSTAB15?16DZWCIX
```

</details>

The sender is concerned because it does not know what the recipient will do
in view of the situation. The message ends with `REICHSVERSORGUNG` and
`ADMIRALSTAB`. All five tied models can be filled to this same **92-character
prefix**, without changing an observed coordinate. Their footer readings
differ and are all retained in the certificate.

A separate footer proposal reads `15X16DZWEIX`, filling the separator and
changing one observed coordinate to turn `ZWCI` into `ZWEI`. It is explicitly
editorial; the footer does not select the ordinary-body gap model and does
not establish a new digit assignment.

## The two-part ship-sale order, p200 B

The common source header is `NKJ v LP (08.19 p.m., November 15th)`,
`16.00 (15/11) FUER COS`, `2 TLE`. The received ship name is `CORCOWADO`.
The association with Corcovado is kept separate from that literal spelling.

### B1: stop the sale or ownership transfer

The first part has 394 source slots. The last glyph in group 7, `AAXFY`,
is an invalid coordinate `Y` and remains an erasure in the raw reading:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
MXMXDXNICOLAJEFFXWENNVERKAUFXCORCOWADOXANTUERKEINOCINICHTINORDNUNGSOLLVERKAUFNI?HTSTA?TFINDENXFALLSAUFGRUNDBEREITSGETAETIGTENVERKAUFSEIGENTUMSUEBERTRAGUNGNOCHWICHTERFOLGTISTHATSOLCHEZUUNTERBLEIBENX
```

</details>

Three observed-coordinate substitutions and one invalid-glyph fill give
this complete 197-position candidate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
MXMXDXNICOLAJEFFXWENNVERKAUFXCORCOWADOXANTUERKEINOCHNICHTINORDNUNGSOLLVERKAUFNICHTSTATTFINDENXFALLSAUFGRUNDBEREITSGETAETIGTENVERKAUFSEIGENTUMSUEBERTRAGUNGNOCHNICHTERFOLGTISTHATSOLCHEZUUNTERBLEIBENX
```

</details>

Addressed to `M. M. D., Nicolajeff`, it says that if the sale to Turkey has
not yet been settled, it should not take place. If a sale has already been
made but ownership has not yet been transferred, that transfer must not
proceed. This is the message's historical instruction, not an inference
about what ultimately happened to the ship.

### B2: payment in Germany before ownership transfer

All 360 printed slots are retained. One glyph is unreadable and another is
an `E`-like overstrike, both preserved as source erasures. The raw text is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
TUERKEIGEGENUEBERKNNGELTENDGEMCHTWERDENXREED?REIWILLDAMPFERANTUEKEINICHTVERKAUFENESSEIDENNDASSKAUFPREISINDEUTSCHLANDVOREIGENTUMSUEBERTRAGUNGBARBEZAHLTWERDEXMARIN?AMTXAXSECHSXS????0
```

</details>

Filling those two erased coordinates recovers `REEDEREI` and `MARINEAMT`,
without changing any observed valid coordinate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
TUERKEIGEGENUEBERKNNGELTENDGEMCHTWERDENXREEDEREIWILLDAMPFERANTUEKEINICHTVERKAUFENESSEIDENNDASSKAUFPREISINDEUTSCHLANDVOREIGENTUMSUEBERTRAGUNGBARBEZAHLTWERDEXMARINEAMTXAXSECHSXS????0
```

</details>

The message supplies the position to present to Turkey: the shipowner will
not sell the steamer unless the purchase price is paid in cash in Germany
before ownership transfers. The source omits letters in `KNN`, `GEMCHT` and
`TUEKEI`; those strings are not silently length-corrected in the candidate.
The footer's four baseline unknowns use cells `VG`, `VG`, `GD`, `AD`.
The shared conditional VG=2 reading gives **`S22??0`**, taking this edition
from **176 to 178/180** fixed labels. The two remaining cells are unassigned;
the two earlier erasure fills and the source's omitted letters are unchanged.

## Exact scope and reproducibility

The five records have 1,596 printed slots, 1,591 valid coordinates and 798
modeled plaintext positions. The declared source models fix 785 positions
before repairs. Conservative candidates fix 792; the shared conditional
VG=2 reading adds **three** labels, reaching **795/798**. Fixed counts include
received garbles and therefore do not mean that every word is restored.

The [shared-traffic certificate](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/traffic_certificates.json)
checks these three digits against the original coordinates and retains all
three equally priced A1 exclusion models.

The [verifier](../../experiments/black_sea_shipping/verify.py) recomputes every
plaintext domain and source mapping, the broad and source-local deletion
results, all five gap ties, and each exact repair. It checks the separate
conditional `FX=Y` hypothesis against 21 variants, retaining all effects:
there are no newly fixed raw letters, only listed domain reductions. No
published key file is changed.

# Corcovado: sale terms, Turkish crew and a conditional office number

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and recovery: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Six source records recover a detailed November 9, 1918 proposal for selling
Corcovado to Turkey, followed by a November 10 report that the vessel was
already operating with a Turkish crew and captain. The sale terms include
a directly decrypted price of **10 million**, with the currency unstated,
a separate valuation for inventory and materials, payment and risk
provisions, and restrictions on resale and use. These messages precede
the [November 15 order](black_sea_shipping.md) to stop the sale or
ownership transfer unless the payment condition was met.

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX
Cipher System*, printed pp. 165 and 173, PDF pp. 168 and 176. The
[literal transcription and source crops](../../experiments/corcovado_sale_terms/inputs.json)
retain every coordinate and invalid glyph. The
[exact certificate](../../experiments/corcovado_sale_terms/certificates.json)
separates unchanged-key raw readings, individual coordinate repairs, and
the conditional office-number inference described below.

The square cells and transposition orders are prior published work.
Their provenance, including Lasry and colleagues' final key table and
the 2017 discussion, is preserved in the inputs. A bounded check found
no explicit discussion of these Corcovado bodies in the checked paper,
the corresponding dissertation chapter or the cached 55 comments. That
check does not establish universal historical priority. Lasry, Niebel,
Kopal and Wacker's prior identification of the separate p199 cargo
message is credited in its own edition.

## Conditional shared digits

The sale correspondence now carries the conditional reference **A6S824**. This supplies its last unknown position; the six previously priced word repairs remain part of the edition. The [joint reconstruction](../../experiments/nov10_joint_completion/README.md) combines the earlier Marineamt and formation interpretations with the army-number constraint and the mobilization decree; the reversed 7/9 assignment is retained there.

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the joint square:**

> Zu dort A6S824 G. G. Mittelmeerdivision oder Vertreter nicht mehr in Nikolajew. Corcovado faehrt bereits mit tuerkischer Besatzung unter …

<details>
<summary>Exact conditional labels</summary>

**Edited output — p173_A1, conditional shared square; 121/121 fixed positions:**

```text
ZUDORTXA6S824GXGXXMITTELMEERDIVISIONODERVERTRETERNICHTMEHRINNIKOLAJEWXXCORCOVADOFAEHRTBEREITSMITTUERKISCHERBESATZUNGUNTER
```

</details>


## November 9: proposed sale conditions, p165 A

The source header reads `NKJ v LP (04.00 p.m., November 9th)`,
`1420 (9/11)`, `4 TEILE`. Its four physical blocks are labelled **1, 2, 3,
5 TL**, so the final block is called **A5** here. No absent fourth part is
invented. All four blocks use the published `Nov7-9` partial square.

### A1: price and the seller

All 380 printed coordinates are valid. The raw 190-position reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
MITTELMEERDIVISIONXNICOLAJEFFXBEIVERKAUFXCORCOVAUOXMOEGLICHSTFOLGENDEBEDINGUNGENDURCHZUSETZENXXVERKAUFERFOLGTFUERHFMBURGAMERIKALINIEXKAUFPREISFESTX10XMILLXFUERSCHIFFOHNEINVENTARUNDMATERIALXX
```

</details>

Two observed-coordinate substitutions give this complete, exactly
reencryptable candidate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
MITTELMEERDIVISIONXNICOLAJEFFXBEIVERKAUFXCORCOVADOXMOEGLICHSTFOLGENDEBEDINGUNGENDURCHZUSETZENXXVERKAUFERFOLGTFUERHAMBURGAMERIKALINIEXKAUFPREISFESTX10XMILLXFUERSCHIFFOHNEINVENTARUNDMATERIALXX
```

</details>

Addressed to the Mediterranean Division at Nicolajeff, it asks that the
following conditions be obtained if possible in the sale. The sale is for
the Hamburg-Amerika Line; the fixed purchase price for the ship without
inventory or materials is `10XMILL`. Both digits and every letter of that
price field come from complete observed coordinate pairs, with no repair
or unknown key label. The text does not name a currency.

The received name is `CORCOVAUO`. The following day's message independently
contains all nine letters of `CORCOVADO` under a different key. Conditional
on the two sale reports referring to the same vessel, this supplies a
source witness for the single `U` to `D` change at plaintext position 48.
It does not make the entire messages duplicate copies.

### A2: inventory, present condition and seizure risk

The printed length is 458. Source coordinate 239 is `C` in `GVGVC`, and
417 is `L` in `FALXX`; both are invalid ADFGVX coordinates. They remain
erasures in the raw 229-position reading:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
MATERIALUNDINVENTARZUMSELBSTKOSTENPAEISMINUFABNUT?UNGXXSCHIFFWIRDVERKAUFTINAUGENBLICKLICHEMZUSTANDXAUS?ESCHLOSSENPERGOENLICHESEIGENTPMKAPITAENSUNDBESATZUNGXAUSSCHLIESSLICHKOHLENXXUEBERNAHMERISIKOVONSEITENTUERKEIGEGENBESCHLAGNAHME
```

</details>

Four observed-coordinate substitutions and the two erased-coordinate
fills produce this complete candidate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
MATERIALUNDINVENTARZUMSELBSTKOSTENPREISMINUSABNUTZUNGXXSCHIFFWIRDVERKAUFTINAUGENBLICKLICHEMZUSTANDXAUSGESCHLOSSENPERSOENLICHESEIGENTUMKAPITAENSUNDBESATZUNGXAUSSCHLIESSLICHKOHLENXXUEBERNAHMERISIKOVONSEITENTUERKEIGEGENBESCHLAGNAHME
```

</details>

Materials and inventory are to be valued at cost less wear. The ship is
sold in its current condition; the captain's and crew's personal property
and coal are excluded. Turkey is to assume the risk of seizure. The next
part states by whom and from what date.

The full source transcription also restores two five-letter groups and
the final `VDD` omitted by the earlier OCR extraction. Those coordinates
are visible source material, not a conjectural ciphertext insertion.

### A3: risk, interest and recovery for nonpayment

All 380 source coordinates are valid. The raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DURCHFEINDEDEUTSCHENREICHESVOMZEITPUNKTKAUFABSCHLUSSESABXXVERZINSUNGKAUFPREISESBEGINNTSPAETESTENSXSIEBENXUONATENACHKAUFABSCHLUSSXXBEINICHTZAHLUNGRUECKFORDERUNGSRECHTANDEMDAMPFERVORBEHALTENXX
```

</details>

One observed-coordinate change, `UONATE` to `MONATE`, gives:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
DURCHFEINDEDEUTSCHENREICHESVOMZEITPUNKTKAUFABSCHLUSSESABXXVERZINSUNGKAUFPREISESBEGINNTSPAETESTENSXSIEBENXMONATENACHKAUFABSCHLUSSXXBEINICHTZAHLUNGRUECKFORDERUNGSRECHTANDEMDAMPFERVORBEHALTENXX
```

</details>

The seizure risk is from enemies of the German Empire and begins at the
conclusion of the sale. Interest on the purchase price is to begin no later
than seven months after the sale. The right to recover the steamer in the
event of nonpayment is reserved.

### A5: resale, evacuation and encrypted forwarding

The printed `5 TL` has exactly 500 slots. The invalid glyphs are `J`, `L`
and `C`, at source positions 90, 147 and 199. The raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
VORKAUFSRECHTDEUTSCHLANDSBEIETWAIGENWIEDERVERKAUFXVERBOTVERKAUFSANNICHTDEUTSCHEREEDEREIXVERWENDUNGDAMPFEASAUSSCHLIESSLICHODERINERSTERLINIEFUDRABTRANSPORTDERDEU?SCHENXWEITERGABEDIESESTELEGRAMMSNACHKONSTANTIYOPELNURGESCHLU?SSELTXMARINEAMTXAX?XSX8?3XGXG
```

</details>

Three observed-coordinate substitutions and two erased-coordinate fills
restore the ordinary words, leaving both numerical uncertainties intact:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
VORKAUFSRECHTDEUTSCHLANDSBEIETWAIGENWIEDERVERKAUFXVERBOTVERKAUFSANNICHTDEUTSCHEREEDEREIXVERWENDUNGDAMPFERSAUSSCHLIESSLICHODERINERSTERLINIEFUERABTRANSPORTDERDEUTSCHENXWEITERGABEDIESESTELEGRAMMSNACHKONSTANTINOPELNURGESCHLUESSELTXMARINEAMTXAX?XSX8?3XGXG
```

</details>

Germany is to retain a right of first refusal on resale. Sale to a
non-German shipping company is prohibited. The ship is to be used
exclusively or primarily to transport Germans away. The telegram is to
be forwarded to Constantinople only in enciphered form.

The signature is `MARINEAMT`; the office/reference ending is
`AX?XSX8?3XGXG`. Its first question mark is a complete observed pair at an
unfilled key cell, while the second includes an invalid printed source
glyph. Their uncertainty has different causes and is retained separately.

## November 10: Turkish crew and no radio contact, p173 A

The header reads `LP v NKJ (7.07 p.m., November 10th)`,
`VON NKJ AN LP MARINE AMT BERLIN 1710 (10)`, `2 TLE`.
Both blocks use the published `Nov10-12` partial square.

### A1: the division has left; Corcovado already has Turkish personnel

All 242 coordinates are valid. The raw 121-position reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ZUDORDXA?S?24GXGXX2ITTELMEXRDIVISIONODERVERTRETERNICHTMEHRINNIKOLAJEWXXCORCOVADOFAEHRTBEREITSMI2TUERKISOHERBESATZUNGUNTER
```

</details>

Six observed-coordinate substitutions restore ordinary words while
leaving both unknown reference digits unresolved:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ZUDORTXA?S?24GXGXXMITTELMEERDIVISIONODERVERTRETERNICHTMEHRINNIKOLAJEWXXCORCOVADOFAEHRTBEREITSMITTUERKISCHERBESATZUNGUNTER
```

</details>

Referring to the recipient's `A?S?24 G G`, the report states that the
Mediterranean Division or its representative is no longer in Nikolaev.
Corcovado is already sailing with a Turkish crew under a captain whose
nationality appears in the next part. The ship name itself is completely
observed and needs no repair.

### A2: Turkish captain and failed contact with Constantinople

The 160-slot source begins with `AGAD-`. Its final dash is an erased
coordinate. The raw text is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
TUERKXKAPITAENXMITKONSTANTINOPEOXKEINFU?KVERKEHRMEHRMOEGLXXGOUVERNEMENTXNKJX1XAX
```

</details>

One observed-coordinate change and the erased-coordinate fill give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
TUERKXKAPITAENXMITKONSTANTINOPELXKEINFUNKVERKEHRMEHRMOEGLXXGOUVERNEMENTXNKJX1XAX
```

</details>

The captain is Turkish. Radio communication with Constantinople is no
longer possible. The ending reads `GOUVERNEMENT NKJ 1 A`.

## A separate conditional inference: the Marineamt A6S prefix

The November 15 p200 B2 order independently spells out `SECHS` in the raw
ending `MARIN?AMTXAXSECHSXS????0`. Its letters have complete observed
coordinate pairs under `Nov13-15b`; none requires a source repair or an
unknown square cell. The nearby erasure in `MARIN?AMT` does not affect the
word `SECHS`.

| Word letter | p200 B2 plaintext index | Pair | Original source indices |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| S | 168 | `GF` | 88, 246 |
| E | 169 | `XF` | 111, 313 |
| C | 170 | `XV` | 201, 156 |
| H | 171 | `AA` | 358, 21 |
| S | 172 | `GF` | 269, 336 |

The hypothesis is that these three same-vessel reports use the same
stable Marineamt **A6S office/file prefix**, and that the earlier two
unknown prefix pairs are correctly copied. Under that explicit condition:

| Earlier key | Assignment | Earlier direct witness | Additional consequence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nov7–9 | `VF=6` | p165 A5 plaintext 239, source pair 473/98 | `XA=5`, since 5 and 6 are the only unused symbols |
| Nov10–12 | `XX=6` | p173 A1 plaintext 8, source pair 121/167 | The four other unknown cells retain the symbols 5, 7, 8, 9 |

The pair in each earlier message is fully observed and unchanged by all
ordinary-word repairs. There is no direct local `XA` occurrence, so the
`XA=5` complement adds no local plaintext character. `VF=6` adds one
physical character, and `XX=6` adds one more. Each is displayed twice in
the certificate because both the source model and repaired candidate are
checked; those variant checks are not counted as distinct recoveries.

The **reference tails are not the same**: p165 ends `A?S8?3GG`, while p173
cites `A?S?24GG`. Neither equality nor consecutive numbering is assumed.
In particular, the source erasure in the first tail is not silently read
as `2`, and the later unknown hundreds digit is not silently read as `8`.

All effects of the two conditional key layers are retained:

| Record / variant | Position | Pair | Domain before | Domain after |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| p165 A2 raw only | 49 | `?F` | `5679JMZ` | `679JMZ` |
| p165 A5 raw and candidate | 239 | `VF` | `56` | `6` |
| p173 A1 raw and candidate | 8 | `XX` | `56789` | `6` |
| p173 A1 raw and candidate | 10 | `XG` | `56789` | `5789` |
| p173 A2 raw only | 39 | `?X` | `156789ENVX` | `16ENVX` |

No other marginal domain or raw character changes in the twelve checked
variants. After the conditional assignments, the raw models still retain
p165 A2 positions 49 (`679JMZ`) and 102 (`3EGLSZ`); p165 A5 positions 159
(`29BITV`), 220 (`DEQTUX`) and 244 (`02ACLR`); p173 A1 position 10 (`5789`);
and p173 A2 position 39 (`16ENVX`). Ordinary-word repairs resolve all but
the two reference positions, p165 A5 position 244 and p173 A1 position 10.

These conditional values disagree with the earlier published
complete-square hypotheses `VF=5`, `XA=6` and `XX=9`. The conservative
partial squares remain unchanged. The certificate enumerates both
possible Nov7 digit permutations and all five Nov10 values for `XX`:
all are compatible with the observed coordinates. The office-prefix
association supplies the distinguishing assumption, not reencryption.

The Nov7 result has an earlier independent line of support. The preserved
[military-context certificate](../../experiments/p170_continuation/military_context.json)
identifies the 6th Reserve Division from historical unit evidence and
therefore supports `VF=6`, with `XA=5` as its remaining-symbol consequence.
That layer has already been propagated to the corps, date and time fields
in [the withdrawal edition](../../experiments/withdrawal_recovery/README.md).
The Corcovado office prefix independently corroborates the same conditional
Nov7 assignment; it is not counted as discovery of a new Nov7 key cell.
The two evidence routes retain different assumptions and are not collapsed
into an unconditional key. The Nov10 `XX=6` inference remains a separate
conditional constraint.

## Exact scope and verification

The six records contain **2,120 printed slots**, of which **2,114** are
valid coordinates, and **1,060 plaintext positions**. The unchanged partial
keys fix **1,051** raw positions. Seventeen observed-coordinate
substitutions and five erased-coordinate fills produce readable candidates
with **1,056** fixed positions. The separate conditional office layer adds
two physical characters, giving **1,058/1,060** positions locally.

No source coordinate is inserted, deleted or reordered. Full candidates
without unknowns are checked by exact reencryption; partial candidates
are checked against their complete coordinate stencil and explicit
residual domains. Every source/model/plaintext coordinate is reversible.

```bash
python experiments/corcovado_sale_terms/verify.py --verify
python experiments/corcovado_sale_terms/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
```

The second command checks the full primary PDF hash and rerenders each
crop pixel-for-pixel. The conditional layer also binds and rederives the
later `SECHS` witness from the independently preserved p200 source
transcription. It does not assume that the sale was completed or settle
the vessel's eventual history.

## Independent office context

The Bundesarchiv's institutional description of the Reichsmarineamt lists
A VI S as the maritime transport division in 1914 and describes its 1917
organization. This independently supports the office interpretation used
above. The [source note](../../experiments/corcovado_sale_terms/office_context.json) distinguishes the
retrieved institutional catalogue from the underlying uninspected business
plans. Identifying particular telegram fields with that office and assuming
they were copied correctly remain conditional; no source certificate or
published square is changed.

# Gerlach oil-release inquiry: the overprinted parallel

[Case index](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

## p83 A

**Status:** 122/122 native raw positions fixed; 0 coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills. No frame or key change.

**Source and dates:** Page heading: 30th OCTOBER, 1918; A) POT v NKJ (4.17 a.m., November 1st); FUER BEAUFTRAGT PREUSS K M HAUPTM GERLACH BATUM; 1830 (30); RICHI-244.

![Source p83 A](../../experiments/oct30_oil_and_supply_records/sources/p83_A.png)

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — declared visual readings of the five overprints:**

```text
DRAHTETOBERNEUTERBEFEHLIZZETPASCHAXIZZETPASCHAZURFREIGABEDEROELEERFOLGGEHABTHATXXKRIEGSAMTKRIEGSROHSTOFFABTLGXNRX0ROEMX1XX
```

</details>

**Readable German — the same candidate labels with spacing and punctuation:**

> Drahtet, ob erneuter Befehl Izzet Pascha, Izzet Pascha, zur Freigabe der Oele Erfolg gehabt hat. Kriegsamt, Kriegsrohstoffabtlg. Nr. 0, roem. 1.

**Meaning:** Telegraph whether Izzet Pasha's renewed order to release the oil has been successful. The text asks for a result; it does not establish that the oil was released. The clear routing is for Hauptm. Gerlach at Batum, with the Prussian War Ministry designation. Both occurrences of Izzet Pascha and the unexplained footer 0 ROEM 1 remain literal.

**Conditional interpretation and source details:** Five positions carry visible overprinting: source 99, 136, 146, 176 and 177. Their declared surviving glyph readings are X, X, G, A and F. With these readings the 244-coordinate stream is identical to the independently reviewed p84 A source, and all 122 plaintext positions decode without a cryptographic edit. The certificate also retains a conservative five-mask sensitivity branch: 117/122 raw positions, then five explicitly counted fills supplied by the independent p84 witness. The zero-edit result is tied to the stated visual transcription; it does not describe the overprints as pristine. The clear p83 header gives 1830 (30), where the corresponding p84 time is partly illegible.

### Conservative overprint sensitivity

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — mask all five overprinted positions instead of reading the surviving glyphs:**

```text
DRA?TETOBERN?U?ERBEFEHLIZZETPASCHAXIZZET?ASCHAZURFREIGABEDEROELEERFOLGGEHABTHATXXKRIEGSAMTKRIEGSROHSTOFF?BTLGXNRX0ROEMX1XX
```

</details>

That stricter branch fixes 117 of 122 positions. Filling source 99→X, 136→X, 146→G, 176→A and 177→F restores the same full reading with five counted fills and no observed-coordinate substitution. Each value is independently present in the clear [p84 witness](../../experiments/oct30_oil_and_supply_records/sources/p84_A_witness.png).

![Five overprinted positions](../../experiments/oct30_oil_and_supply_records/sources/p83_A_overprints.png)

The [earlier p84 case](p84_AB.md) remains the previously documented body reading. The new contribution is the additional p83 physical witness, its clear 1830 header, and the explicit sensitivity accounting.

### Reproducibility and attribution

The [input](../../experiments/oct30_oil_and_supply_records/inputs.json) binds the complete literal rows to exact PDF crops. The [certificate](../../experiments/oct30_oil_and_supply_records/certificates.json) records every coordinate pair and the sensitivity branch. The [verifier](../../experiments/oct30_oil_and_supply_records/verify.py) checks the published Oct28–31 key, live German quotations, source-image hashes and optional PDF pixel regeneration.

Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro (2026). Childs supplies the historical collection; the published reconstruction and key provenance credit Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker. The [attribution record](../../experiments/oct30_oil_and_supply_records/prior_candidates.json) retains earlier OCR and the already reviewed p84 source.

# An enquiry about an MMD command or representative

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

A complete native short message asks whether a command or representative is present. MMD and the final reference remain literal. The proposed A in KOMMANDO costs an observed-coordinate change; the separate Y-like source glyph stays masked and unresolved.

## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p190 excerpt](../../experiments/mmd_command_whereabouts/sources/p190_reviewed.png) · [Inputs](../../experiments/mmd_command_whereabouts/inputs.json) · [Position and change certificates](../../experiments/mmd_command_whereabouts/certificates.json)

The published `Nov13-15b` key is unchanged. [Original OCR records](../../experiments/mmd_command_whereabouts/ocr_snapshot.json) and [reproducible comparisons with that earlier evidence](../../experiments/mmd_command_whereabouts/prior_candidates.json) are preserved separately. The present edition supplies checked source framing, exact costs and readable passages; it makes no first-public-decipherment claim.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [p190 C](#p190-c) | 126 | 59 / 63 | 1 | 0 |

## p190 C

**Source transcription — header:** `C) --- v --- (06.05 p.m., November 14th); FUER ASO RAT 13.41; RICHI-126`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
BEFINDETSICHDORTKOMM?NDOXXMMDXXODERVERTRETERXADMIRALSTAB15?6?D?
```

**Edited output — 1 observed-coordinate substitution and 0 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
BEFINDETSICHDORTKOMMANDOXXMMDXXODERVERTRETERXADMIRALSTAB15?6?D?
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Befindet sich dort Kommando MMD oder Vertreter. Admiralstab 15?6?D?.

**Meaning:** The message asks whether the command labeled MMD, or a representative, is present at the destination. It closes with Admiralstab and the unresolved reference 15?6?D?. The source does not expand MMD or identify the destination.

**Editorial limits.**

- The native source contains126 slots, including the final AAGFF G. The first-row fifth group has a Y-like or Y/V-uncertain third glyph, conservatively retained as FVYAG and masked at source 22.
- The raw KOMM?NDO unknown comes from the fully observed VG square cell, not from the Y-like source glyph. Its domain is {2,3,4,7,8,9,Q,Y}; proposing A therefore costs an observed G→V substitution at source 112. No unknown key cell is silently assigned A.
- The final reference has two fully observed unknown square cells GD and AD, and a final source-mask pair ?G. Their domains remain explicit; they are not forced into a numerical date or serial number.
- The single source mask remains unresolved. The final character domain is {2,3,4,6,7,8,9,B,G,P,Q,R,Y}, while the earlier two unknown cells range over {2,3,4,7,8,9,Q,Y}.
- The question is punctuated with a period in the exact reading so that ? continues to denote an unresolved plaintext position.

The final three unresolved labels also obey a joint constraint. GD and AD are distinct square cells. The source-mask pair ?G can select known B, P, R, 6 or G, or an unused label through VG; it cannot select GD or AD. Thus the three final labels must be mutually different, even though their marginal domains overlap.

## Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates independently reconstruct column positions and domains, compare them with the cipher implementation, replay every priced change, and check all readable nonseparator labels. Partial readings have one consistent injective square/source-mask completion witness that re-encrypts exactly; those witness choices are not historical identifications. Source images are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/mmd_command_whereabouts/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to check the original PDF and exact source-crop pixels.
