# Constantinople: instruction to attempt a motorboat sale

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

## p147 A

Childs p147, PDF p150; [source crop](../../experiments/nov4_radio_and_departure_queries/sources/p147_A.png). Key: unchanged published **Nov4–6**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — literal received header:**

```text
6th NOVEMBER, 1918.
A) YZ v LP (08.10 a.m., November 7th)
1637 (6/11)
RICHI-254
```

**Raw output — native 254-slot frame; 127/127 fixed positions:**

```text
BEVOLLMAECHTIGTERSCHIFFAHRTSBEBUFTRAGTERXKONSTANTINOPELXXBOOTXROEMXQ5XUNTERALLENUMSTAENDENZUVERKAUFENSUCHENXMOTORBOOTVORPSX6235
```

**Edited output — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills; 127/127 fixed positions:**

```text
BEVOLLMAECHTIGTERSCHIFFAHRTSBEAUFTRAGTERXKONSTANTINOPELXXBOOTXROEMXQ5XUNTERALLENUMSTAENDENZUVERKAUFENSUCHENXMOTORBOOTKORPSX6235
```

</details>

Observed source changes, with zero-based indices: **47 G→F**, **177 G→F**.

The full edited stream re-encrypts under its stated frame and listed changes.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Bevollmaechtigter Schiffahrtsbeauftragter Konstantinopel. Boot ROEM Q5 unter allen Umstaenden zu verkaufen suchen. Motorbootkorps 6235.

**Meaning:** The instruction asks the shipping representative in Constantinople to try to sell the boat designated by the literal ROEM Q5 under all circumstances. The Motorbootkorps reference is 6235. A sale is requested, not reported as completed.

## Source-specific boat identifier

The native source has **254 valid coordinates**, matching `RICHI-254`. Two local word repairs supply `BEAUFTRAGTER` and `MOTORBOOTKORPS`. The label following `ROEM` is **Q5**, not the earlier OCR candidate 35. This edition does not replace Q with 3, identify a specific vessel, or infer that the requested sale took place. The separate reference 6235 also remains literal.

## Attribution and evidence

Earlier unreviewed repository candidates already suggested these bodies. This edition checks the primary images, preserves conflicting source labels and publishes every frame operation, coordinate substitution and fill. Prior published key recovery keeps its original credit; no first-solution priority is claimed.

[Inputs](../../experiments/nov4_radio_and_departure_queries/inputs.json), [certificates](../../experiments/nov4_radio_and_departure_queries/certificates.json), [earlier candidates](../../experiments/nov4_radio_and_departure_queries/prior_candidates.json) and [reproduction](../../experiments/nov4_radio_and_departure_queries/README.md) provide complete source and positional evidence.

# p178 — The naval armistice order of 11 November

[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source and certificate](../../experiments/naval_armistice_order/README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Prior reading and interpretation:** George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal
and Arno Wacker, [*Deciphering ADFGVX messages from the Eastern Front of
World War I*](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461), 2016/2017.
Their author manuscript, printed p23, discusses these p178 A/B parts and
the cease-fire, U-boat and neutral-water instructions.

**Current source edition:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. This adds the
complete German reconstruction, two explicit short-group insertions,
fourteen known-coordinate repairs, and re-encryption certificates. It
does not claim a new body discovery.

## Conditional shared digits

The final part gains **OP1A944** and **Admiralstab 18340**, fixing **161/161 labels** with its two existing coordinate repairs. The literal spelling WASZER is retained. The [joint reconstruction](../../experiments/nov10_joint_completion/README.md) combines the earlier Marineamt and formation interpretations with the army-number constraint and the mobilization decree; the reversed 7/9 assignment is retained there.

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the joint square:**

> Genehmigung zum Befahren neutraler Hoheitsgewaesser ueber Waszer ist bei neutralen Regierungen erbeten. 3. Empfangsbestaetigungen. Admiral G G. OP1A944. Admiralstab 18340 zwei.

<details>
<summary>Exact conditional labels</summary>

**Edited output — p178_A5, conditional shared square; 161/161 fixed positions:**

```text
XGENEHMIGUNGZUMBEFAHRENNEUTRALERHOHEITSGEWAESSERUEBERWASZERISTBEINEUTRALENREGIERUNGENERBETENXX3XXEMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNGENXADMIRALXGGXXOP1A944XXADMIRALSTAB18340ZWEI
```

</details>


## Most likely reading

**Readable German — under the stated per-part reconstruction:**

> Zwei Adressen: 1. MMD; 2. Sdo-Kommando. Von SKL SKL.
>
> 1. Sofort an alle Streitkraefte mit allen verfuegbaren Verkehrsmitteln
> uebermitteln: Am 11.11., 12 Uhr mittags, tritt an allen Fronten der
> Waffenstillstand in Kraft. Mit diesem Zeitpunkt sind alle
> Kriegshandlungen einzustellen. Alle Seestreitkraefte beschleunigt in
> Stuetzpunkten sammeln nach Anweisung der Immediatbefehlshaber.
>
> 2. An alle U-Boote ist bis auf Weiteres geschluesselt zu geben:
> Waffenstillstand abgeschlossen. Da nicht damit zu rechnen ist, dass
> alle feindlichen Seestreitkraefte hiervon Kenntnis haben, weiter mit
> feindlichen Angriffen rechnen. Waffengebrauch nur zur Notwehr.
> Genehmigung zum Befahren neutraler Hoheitsgewaesser ueber Wasser ist
> bei neutralen Regierungen erbeten.
>
> 3. Empfangsbestaetigungen.
>
> [Closing labels: `ADMIRAL GG. OP1A?44. ADMIRALSTAB1?340ZWEI`.]

**Meaning:** Forward the armistice order immediately to all forces. War
actions cease at noon on 11 November, and naval forces are to assemble at
their bases. U-boats must receive an enciphered notice, continue to expect
enemy attacks from ships that may not yet know of the armistice, and use
weapons only in self-defense. Permission for surfaced passage through
neutral territorial waters has been requested. Receipt is to be
acknowledged.

The raw labels `MMD`, `SDOKOMMANDO` and `VONSKLSKL` are preserved in the
certificate. The ordinary reading adds spacing and punctuation and
normalizes the source spellings `ADRESZEN`, `DASZ` and `WASZER`; the
same-length coordinate edition retains those three strings unchanged.
The two reference digits are not supplied.

## Source frames and exact repairs

The [full source page](../../experiments/naval_armistice_order/sources/childs_p178_page.png)
contains 1,436 ADFGVX letters. Two visibly short four-letter groups
account for a one-coordinate shortfall in each of parts 2 and 3. The
proposed frames total 1,438 coordinates and 719 plaintext positions.

| Part | Visible coordinates | Frame | Raw fixed positions | Candidate changes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| [1](../../experiments/naval_armistice_order/sources/childs_p178_A1.png) | 238 | 238 | 119 / 119 | One known-coordinate substitution |
| [2](../../experiments/naval_armistice_order/sources/childs_p178_A2.png) | 309 | 310 | 154 / 155 | Three substitutions and one insertion |
| [3](../../experiments/naval_armistice_order/sources/childs_p178_A3.png) | 279 | 280 | 137 / 140 | Three substitutions and one insertion |
| [4](../../experiments/naval_armistice_order/sources/childs_p178_A4.png) | 288 | 288 | 144 / 144 | Five substitutions |
| [5](../../experiments/naval_armistice_order/sources/childs_p178_A5.png) | 322 | 322 | 158 / 161 | Two substitutions |

Part 2's thirteenth group is literally `VXDX`; the edition supplies a
final `D`. Part 3's fourteenth group is `AFGA`; the edition supplies an
initial `D` and separately changes the final source `A` to `F`.
The inserted symbols are not observed in the scan. Each chosen position
uniquely minimizes known-coordinate changes among the five possible
one-loss positions within its short group for this proposed plaintext.

The raw readings below use those explicit frames but leave the inserted
symbols unknown and make no known-coordinate repairs:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional per-part frames listed above; added coordinates remain unknown:**

```text
2XADRESZENX1XXMMDX2XXSDOKOMMANDOXVONSKLSKLXX1XSOFORTANALLESTREITKRAWFTEMITALLENVERFUEGBARENVERKEHRSMITTELNUEBERMITTELNX
AM11X1EX12UHRMITTAGSTRITTANALLENFROOTENDERWAFFENSTILLST?NDINKRAFTXMITDIESEMZEITPUNKTSINDALLEKRIEGSHANDLUNGENEINZUSTELLEIXALLESEESTREITKRAEFTEBESCHLEUNIGTIN
STUETZTUNKTENSAMMEL?NACHANWEISUNGDERIMMEDIATBEFEHLSHABERX2XXANALLEUBOOTEISTBISAUFWEITERESGESCHLUESSELTZUG?BENXW?FFENSTILLSTANDABGESCHLOSSENX
DANICHTDAMITZURECHNENISTDASZALLEFEINDLICHENSEESTREITKRAEFTFHIERVONKENNTNIS2ABENXWEITERMITFEINDLICHENANGRIFFENRECHNENXWAFFENGEBRAUGHNURZURNOTWEHR
XGENEHMIGUNGZUMBEFAHRENNEUT1ALERHOHEITSGEWAESSERUEBERWASZERISTBEINEUTRALENREGIERUNGENERBETENXX3XXE?PFANGSBESTAETIGUNGENXADMIRALXGGXXOP1A?44XXADMIRALSTAB1?340ZWEI
```

</details>

Fourteen substitutions and the two inserted values produce 717 fixed
positions. Only part 5's reference digits remain unknown: position 137,
cell `XA`, in `OP1A?44`, and position 154, cell `XG`, in
`ADMIRALSTAB1?340`. Both have domain `56789`, but they must be different
digits because they occupy different square cells. Twenty ordered pairs
remain consistent; none is selected. The published Nov10–12 square and
column order are unchanged.

## Dates, layout and credit

Printed p178 / PDF p181. The page heading says **11 November 1916**, but
the intercept header explicitly says **11 November 1918**:
`A) NKJ v VLP (07.06 p.m. November 11, 1918); 1430 (11) 5 TLE`.
The conflicting source years are retained; no silent date correction or
time-zone conversion is applied. A printed `B)` appears beside `2 TL`
without a new route or timestamp. The sequential part labels and text
joins are preserved. The uncertain length labels are retained as
`RICHI-2[6/8]0` for part 3 and `RICHI-2[6/8][6/8]` for part 4. Those header
glyphs are not resolved from the body. Independently, the literal part 3
contains 279 coordinates and one four-letter group, motivating the
conditional 280-coordinate frame; part 4 contains 288 visible coordinates
and is used at that literal length without an insertion or deletion.

J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
[public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The period key and the prior body interpretation retain their Lasry-team

# November 27: Helsingfors shipping and a vehicle-sale instruction

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Two source records on Childs p223 describe ships secured for Helsingfors
and an instruction addressed through General von Kress to sell trucks and
surplus material. The first uses its native printed frame. The second has
five surplus source slots relative to its questioned length label and is
read under an explicitly priced exclusion model. Both use the unchanged
published **Nov25–28** key, credited to George Lasry and collaborators.

| Record | Printed slots | Analysis-frame slots | Fixed raw positions | Additional reading proposal |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| p223 B | 246 | 246, native | 123/123 | 7 observed-coordinate substitutions |
| p223 C | 235 | 230, conditional exclusion | 113/115 | 2 source-mask fills; no substitution of a retained observed coordinate |

For C, the **five excluded observed coordinates** remain part of the repair
price. They are not counted as a free transcription correction or a visibly
cancelled group. The [reviewed source image — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov27_ships_and_vehicle_sale/inputs.json)
retains both messages and their distinct headers.


**Reviewed source crops:** [p223_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov27_ships_and_vehicle_sale/sources/p223_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).
## p223 B

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — literal header:**

```text
B) KOW v RVA (09.25 p.m., November 27th)
1835 (11/27) AN LP v FHR
RICHI-246
```

**Raw output — native 246-slot frame; 123/123 fixed positions:**

```text
ZENIRALFUNKLEITUNGXXELLEXVORBEREIT0GGENXGETRIFFENXSCHIFFEXNACZXMITTEILUNGXREICHSMARINEAMTSXSICHERGESTELLTXXFUSTAHBLSINGFORS
```

**Edited output — seven observed-coordinate substitutions; no fills; 123/123 fixed positions:**

```text
ZENTRALFUNKLEITUNGXXALLEXVORBEREITUNGENXGETROFFENXSCHIFFEXNACHXMITTEILUNGXREICHSMARINEAMTSXSICHERGESTELLTXXFUSTAHELSINGFORS
```

</details>

The changes, at zero-based source indices, are **12 F→D**, **56 D→A**,
**78 F→D**, **130 A→X**, **160 F→V**, **165 D→A** and **202 A→D**.
They repair `ZENIRAL`, `ELLE`, `VORBEREIT0GGEN`, `GETRIFFEN`, `NACZ` and
`HBLSINGFORS`. No published square cell changes.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Zentralfunkleitung. Alle Vorbereitungen getroffen. Schiffe nach Mitteilung Reichsmarineamts sichergestellt. Fusta Helsingfors.

The message reports that preparations have been made and ships secured,
according to the Reichsmarineamt. It does not report that troops have
embarked or arrived. The earlier
[Helsingfors transport inquiry](p210_A.md)
belongs to the wider radio record; no absent reference number is supplied to
identify this as a particular reply.

The source has all **246** coordinates. Earlier OCR retained only **239**:
it omitted the final visible `GVGVF D` and malformed another group. Restoring
the actually printed groups repairs the machine transcript without adding
historical coordinates or altering the native frame.

## p223 C

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — literal header:**

```text
C) COS v NKJ (------- November 28th)
POT FUER COS GENERAL VON KRESS 1555 (11/27)
RICHI-230?
```

</details>

The header retains both the November 28 reception date and the internal
November 27 date. Its question mark after **230** is part of the length
annotation. The source actually prints **235 body slots**, including two
dashes in `DXX--` and these adjacent final-row groups:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — final four groups, excerpt:**

```text
DDFDD GAFDG GDFDG XGGAV
```

</details>

The primary analysis excludes the five observed coordinates **`GAFDG` at
source indices 220–224**. The source does not clearly mark that group as
cancelled. This is therefore an explicit conditional source exclusion, with
the original sequence retained in full.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 230-slot frame after the five-coordinate exclusion; 113/115 fixed positions:**

```text
AUFBEFEHLHEERESGRUPPEALLELASTAUTOSS?WIEALLESUE?ERFLUESSIGEMATERIALWEGENUNMOEGLICHKEITABTRANSPORTSVERKAUFENXXBXMXKXX
```

**Edited output — same conditional exclusion; two source-mask fills and no observed-coordinate substitution; 115/115 fixed positions:**

```text
AUFBEFEHLHEERESGRUPPEALLELASTAUTOSSOWIEALLESUEBERFLUESSIGEMATERIALWEGENUNMOEGLICHKEITABTRANSPORTSVERKAUFENXXBXMXKXX
```

</details>

Filling the printed dashes at **source indices 83 and 84** with **D** and
**A** supplies the O in `SOWIE` and the B in `UEBERFLUESSIGE`. All retained
observed coordinates are unchanged. The five excluded valid coordinates
remain separately charged.

**Readable German — complete edited stream under the conditional exclusion model:**

> Auf Befehl Heeresgruppe alle Lastautos sowie alles ueberfluessige Material wegen Unmoeglichkeit Abtransports verkaufen. B M K.

The source header addresses General von Kress; the decoded body orders a
sale because transport is impossible. It does not identify the army group
more precisely or report that a sale occurred. The signature-like **`B M K`**
comes from literal **`BXMXKXX`**, with separators spaced and no expansion.

### The two equivalent source alignments

Against this exact 115-position candidate, the verifier checks every one of
the **231 consecutive five-slot exclusions** from the 235-slot source.
There are exactly two windows with no substitution of a retained observed
coordinate:

| Exclusion start, zero based | Excluded source letters | Result |
|---:|---|---|
| 220 | `GAFDG` | Retains the displayed 230-slot stream |
| 221 | `AFDGG` | Retains exactly the same 230-slot stream |

The overlap is possible because the G at either end of that six-coordinate
region can survive. Both alignments give the same raw output and the same
complete repaired ciphertext, but their retained source-coordinate maps
are different. Both maps and all 231 prices are stored in the
[certificate](../../experiments/nov27_ships_and_vehicle_sale/certificates.json).
This is a comparison conditioned on the stated plaintext and one exclusion
family, not proof of a unique historical error mechanism. The untouched
235-slot decode and its unpaired final coordinate remain in the certificate.

## Evidence and verification

[Source inputs](../../experiments/nov27_ships_and_vehicle_sale/inputs.json) ·
[Certificates](../../experiments/nov27_ships_and_vehicle_sale/certificates.json) ·
[Reproduction notes](../../experiments/nov27_ships_and_vehicle_sale/README.md).

```sh
python experiments/nov27_ships_and_vehicle_sale/verify.py --verify
python experiments/nov27_ships_and_vehicle_sale/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
```

The optional PDF check compares the inspected crop with the identified
original's RGB pixels. The verifier checks independent transposition
offsets, every raw domain and repair, both source alignments, exact
re-encryption and the complete readable-label mappings. Earlier OCR,
recomputed comparison outputs and published period-key credits remain
separate from this source review. No universal first-decipherment priority
is asserted.

# Tobacco ready for loading at Poti: a November 3 inquiry

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p113 section C reports tobacco at Poti ready for loading and asks
when loading will be possible. Its native **212-slot frame** gives **106/106
fixed output positions** under the unchanged published **Nov1–3** key. The
edited reading makes **one observed-coordinate substitution**, supported by
an unedited repetition of the same abbreviation at the end of the message.
There are no source-mask fills, insertions, deletions or source reorderings.


**Reviewed source crops:** [p113_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov3_poti_tobacco_loading/sources/p113_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).
## p113 C

[Reviewed source image — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov3_poti_tobacco_loading/inputs.json).

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — header:**

```text
Page heading: 3rd NOVEMBER, 1918.
C) POT v NKJ (8.42 a.m., November 4th)
SS FÜR POT V OSM (3) 1430
RICHI-212
```

</details>

The embedded `28X10` is retained as a separate date-like label. Its readable
rendering as `28/10` does not replace the November 3 page heading or
November 4 intercept date. The literal header and complete grouped
ciphertext are preserved in the
[inputs](../../experiments/nov3_poti_tobacco_loading/inputs.json).

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 212-slot frame; 106/106 fixed positions:**

```text
28X10XSCHUTZOFFZRSCHIFFZAUSGLXPOTIXKXAXSAGTPOTI2400TONSTABAKVERLADEBEREITXWANVERLADGMOEGLICHXSCHIFFSAUSGLX
```

**Edited output — 1 observed-coordinate substitution; no fills; 106/106 fixed positions:**

```text
28X10XSCHUTZOFFZRSCHIFFSAUSGLXPOTIXKXAXSAGTPOTI2400TONSTABAKVERLADEBEREITXWANVERLADGMOEGLICHXSCHIFFSAUSGLX
```

</details>

The proposed change is **source index 81 F→V**, changing the first
`SCHIFFZAUSGL` to `SCHIFFSAUSGL`. The closing raw `SCHIFFSAUSGL` already
supplies this spelling without any repair. The exact internal match and
complete re-encryption are checked in the certificate; this is a local
editorial proposal, not a change to the key or the literal transcription.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> 28/10. Schutzoffz. R. Schiffsausgl. Poti. K. A. sagt Poti 2400 Tons Tabak verladebereit. Wan Verladg moeglich. Schiffsausgl.

The isolated **R**, the abbreviation **K. A.**, the single-N spelling **Wan**
and the shortened **Verladg** remain visible. The text does not silently
supply a second N, turn R into a separator, or expand an abbreviation into
an identified office. `2400` is the literal numerical field returned by
the published square; its historical numeral assignment is not independently
proved by this reading.

**Meaning:** A report that tobacco is ready to load at Poti is followed by
an inquiry about when loading will be possible. The message reports
readiness and asks a question; it does not establish that a shipment left,
identify a vessel, or authenticate the quantity independently of the
cipher's numerical labels.

## Source restoration and prior credit

The source's final row visibly prints **ADVXD**. Earlier repository OCR had
**ADV?D**. Restoring that observed X gives the complete native raw reading;
it is an OCR correction, not a supplied historical coordinate. The old OCR
block is frozen with its recomputed unchanged-key output in
[prior candidates](../../experiments/nov3_poti_tobacco_loading/prior_candidates.json).

J. Rives Childs's historical scan remains the source. Published period-key
recovery by George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker, and Lasry's
2017 key list, retain their credit. This is a source-reviewed edition and
explicitly priced word repair; no first-decipherment priority is asserted.

[Inputs](../../experiments/nov3_poti_tobacco_loading/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/nov3_poti_tobacco_loading/certificates.json)
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/nov3_poti_tobacco_loading/README.md)
preserve the key, all source and plaintext positions, the one changed
coordinate, the internal word witness and a complete re-encryption.

# p120 / p123 - Three-part instruction to Feigenhaus

[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source records](../../experiments/corpus_readings/selected_sources.json) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Records:** p120 B1, the repeated suffix p122 D, and p123 A2-A3.
**Result:** an assembled three-part message under the published Nov4-6 key.
The 461-position reading below is conditional on the repairs in the table:
five valid-coordinate substitutions, nineteen erasure fills and one deletion.
The names and unusual expressions remain literal; their intended referents
have not been established.

**Prior body reading:** George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker
already describe the three-part Feigenhaus/Herkules message in §6.5 of
[*Deciphering ADFGVX messages from the Eastern Front of World War I*](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
printed p24 / author-PDF p25. The present contribution by **icekylinx and
GPT-6 Astra Pro** is the source-level edition, exact repair accounting and
identification of the p122 D repeated suffix. This includes the inherited
prior body of that suffix; it is not a first decipherment of the message.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> Feigenhaus, Konstantinopel. Sechshundertsiebzehn. Beichtvater
> zweihundertdreiundneunzig. Nachdem Diktator Anweisung gegeben,
> Notschreie in Andreas nicht vorzunehmen, haben wir uns nochmals mit
> Herkules in Verbindung gesetzt.
>
> Herkules ablehnt Verantwortung fuer neue Notschreie. Infolgedessen
> koennen wir auf keinen Fall neue Notschreie in Andreas vornehmen.
>
> Sie wollen deshalb unseren Anweisungen entsprechend sich verhalten.
> Drahtet, was ihr in Anbetracht veraenderter politischer Lage nunmehr
> zu tun gedenkt. Reichsversorgung.

**Meaning:** The sender reports renewed contact with Herkules after Diktator
instructed that no further *Notschreie* be undertaken in Andreas. Herkules
declines responsibility, so the prohibition stands. The recipient is to follow
these instructions and telegraph the action now intended in view of the
changed political situation. The opening names Feigenhaus in Constantinople
and the references 617 and 293, written out as words in the ciphertext.

*Notschreie* literally means cries for help. Together with Feigenhaus,
Beichtvater, Diktator, Andreas, Herkules and Reichsversorgung, it may belong
to a special vocabulary. This edition does not substitute guessed people,
places, institutions or operations for these terms. The irregular telegram
word order and the shift from *Sie* to *ihr* are retained. Word spacing,
punctuation and capitalization are editorial.

## Source support

| Part | Source slots and raw reading | Exact cost of the displayed candidate |
|---|---|---|
| [p120 B1](../../sources/excerpts/other_p120_B1.png) | 394 slots; all 197 raw positions fixed | One coordinate substitution: raw `ANWEISYNG` becomes `ANWEISUNG`. |
| [p123 A2](../../sources/excerpts/other_p123_A2.png) | 232 slots; 97/116 raw positions fixed | Fill 18 printed dashes and one unreadable glyph; change two valid coordinates. |
| [p123 A3](../../sources/excerpts/other_p123_A3.png) | 297 printed slots against the declared 296 | Delete one of two adjacent `A` coordinates, then make two substitutions for `ANBETRACHT` and `LAGE`. |

The [p122 D intercept](../../sources/excerpts/other_p122_D_suffix.png) is an
**exact 164-coordinate suffix** of p120 B1, starting at zero-based source
index 230. It independently confirms that part of the transmitted stream.
It is not decrypted as a separate short message: changing the transposition
frame to 164 would change the column boundaries.

For part 3, the source visibly prints the eleven-coordinate sequence
`VAAXX VXXAVA`. Deleting source index **211 or 212** gives the same repaired
stream. Among all 297 one-coordinate deletions, these are the only two
minimizers for the **stated candidate**, each requiring two further
valid-coordinate substitutions. This candidate-specific check does not
prove that every possible German reading has been considered.

The direct raw strings, with the declared deletion applied only to part 3,
are:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — stated per-part frames; the declared deletion applies only to part 3:**

```text
FEIGENHAUSKONSTANTINOPELXSECHSHUNDERTSIEBZEHNBEICHTVATERZWEIHUNDERTDREIUNDNEUNZIGNACHDEMDIKTATORANWEISYNGGEGEBENNOTSCHREIEINANDREASNICHTVORZUNEHMENHABENWIRUNSNOCHMALSMITHERKULESINVERBINDUNGGESETZTX
HERKU?ESABLEH?TVERANTW?RTUNGFU?RNEUENOT?CHREIEX?NFOLGED??SENKOEN?ENWIRAU1?EINENFA?LNEUE?OJ?CHRE?EI?ANDRE?SV?RNEH?EN?
SIEWOLLENDESHALBUNSERENANWEISUNGENENTSPRECHENDSICHVERHALTENXDRAHTETWASIHRINANIETRACHTVERAENDERTERPOLITISCHERLARENUNMEHRZUTUNGEDENKTXREICHSVERSORGUNG
```

</details>

## Assembly, dates and credit

The source labels the parts `1 TL`, `2 TL`, `3 TL` and `3 TEILE`.
The p120 header is `OSM v OUI (8.32 p.m., November 4th); 1956`;
p122 repeats its suffix at 8.33 p.m. with `1056`, and p123 supplies parts 2
and 3 at 8.40 p.m., also with `1056`. The differing four-digit fields are
retained. The route, part labels and exact repeated suffix support the
assembly. No date is changed to fit the period key.

The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, printed pp. 120, 122-123 / PDF pp. 123, 125-126 in the
[public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The complete Nov4-6 key retains its attribution to George Lasry and the
historical/research sources in [the key register](../../data/keys.json).
Source assembly, inspection, repair accounting and this edition:
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment priority
is claimed.

```sh
python3 experiments/corpus_readings/verify.py --verify
```

The [certificate](../../experiments/corpus_readings/certificates.json)
preserves the unchanged source, every plaintext-to-coordinate map, the exact
suffix match and all deletion trials. Every complete candidate re-encrypts
to its explicitly repaired source.

# p198 A — Prices and freight for wheat delivered to Poti

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Conditional recovery: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** Source-defined group
repairs and the registered **Nov7–9 key** recover a shipping-price query from
the irregular transmission on printed p198. The 244-slot model fixes
**111/122 raw positions**; five observed-coordinate substitutions and seven
fills give **118/122**.

## Conditional shared digits

**Readable German — conditional shared digits, with the existing source edition retained:**

> Drahtet Kaufpreis, Schiffsfracht, Transporversicherung fuer Ende Sept. mit Dampfer ??PASIA und IBALIA Poti gelieferte 116?0K Pud Weizen.

The [shared-reference assignment](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) gives **116?0K** from the unchanged VF pair at original source 109/158, raising this edition from **118 to 119/122** fixed labels. The opposite assignment gives 115?0K. All four minimum source maps and both C/G glyph alternatives retain this consequence; no ship name, full quantity or unit value is selected.

In the primary frame, the original 12 jointly attainable quantity strings reduce to **six** under the selected square, with **216** complete arithmetic witnesses rather than 432 across both squares. These are compatibility alternatives, not historical quantities. The two unresolved ship-name positions and one quantity mask remain.


## p198 A

**Readable German — conditional word edition; received spelling, names and quantity retained:**

> Drahtet Kaufpreis, Schiffsfracht, Transporversicherung fuer Ende Sept. mit Dampfer ??PASIA und IBALIA Poti gelieferte 11??0K Pud Weizen.

The query asks for the purchase price, ship freight and transport insurance
for wheat delivered to Poti at the end of September. `TRANSPOR` lacks the T
of ordinary German *Transport*; the readable text preserves that spelling.
The steamer labels and `11??0K` quantity are retained exactly. No vessel
identity or numerical tonnage is supplied.

This is section **A**. The original p198 challenge is section **D** and has
its own separate status.

## Source-defined frame

The source advertises `RICHI-244` but prints **247 glyph slots**. Its first
two groups have six glyphs (`XADTAF`, `AATAGV`), `XGAX` has four, and the
ending contains six coordinates. The annotation says **Very irregular spark**.
All eight noncoordinate letters and both dashes remain in the literal source.

The selected conditional model excludes source indices **4, 8, 245 and 246**,
then inserts one unknown coordinate before original source index **92**.
Thus it excludes three observed coordinates and one invalid T, adds one
unknown slot, and retains all other source slots in order. The frame has
244 slots and uses the unchanged registered Nov7–9 square and ranks.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 244-slot frame; every printed mask and inserted slot unassigned:**

```text
DRAHT?TKAUFPREISS?HIFFSFRAC0TTRA?SP?RVERSICH?RUNGFUEYENDESEPTX?GTDAMPFER??PASIAUNDIBALIAPOTIXIELIEFERTEX11??0KXPUDWEIZE?XX
```

**Edited output — same frame; five observed substitutions, six printed-mask fills and one inserted-slot fill:**

```text
DRAHTETKAUFPREISSCHIFFSFRACHTTRANSPORVERSICHERUNGFUERENDESEPTXMITDAMPFER??PASIAUNDIBALIAPOTIXGELIEFERTEX11??0KXPUDWEIZENXX
```

</details>

The word corrections repair `FRAC0T`, `FUEY`, `?GT` and `IELIEFERTE`.
The numeral label `0` is changed only within the explicitly repaired word;
the separate `0` in the quantity remains unchanged.

Two source glyphs at indices 49 and 192 are C-like rather than clearly barred
G. The primary transcription preserves both as literal C and treats them as
masks. The ordinary word `WEIZEN` supplies one fill; the corresponding vessel
letter remains unknown. All four C/G combinations are checked separately.
Reading source 192 as G would give `?TPASIA`, but that alternative is not
silently selected in the primary edition.

## Four tied source maps

Every choice of one exclusion in each initial six-glyph group, one insertion
boundary in `XGAX`, and two exclusions in the final six coordinates is
checked: **2,700 maps**. The word template has four minima at five observed
substitutions. All exclude source 4 and the final 245–246, insert before 92,
and exclude one source position from `{6, 7, 8, 9}`.

All four give the same displayed raw and edited labels. The selected map
excludes only three observed coordinates; the others exclude four. Their
uncertainty differs: the initial `?` of `??PASIA` lies in `MPRUWY` for the
selected map, but one tied map permits any square label. These alternatives
are retained rather than choosing a vessel name. The enumeration prices this
declared template and does not prove a unique historical error mechanism.

The two quantity positions are also linked. One is an unassigned VF square
cell with labels `{5, 6}`; the other depends on a surviving printed mask and
the same globally injective square. There are **12 joint quantity strings**,
not 14 independent marginal combinations. With the selected first-two-label
name domains they produce **432 complete roundtrip witnesses**, all retained in the
certificate. None is selected as the historical quantity.

## Original source and attribution

Childs, printed p198 / PDF p201; `A) IWE v KI (17.21 p.m., November 15th)`;
`VON POT AN IWE SS 18.06 WIR GEN TRA`; `RICHI-244`.
The page heading and reception date remain **15 November**. Nov7–9 is the
registered key identifier that decrypts this body, not a replacement date.

[Original PDF](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view)
· [Edition and verification](../../experiments/p198_shipping_query/README.md)
· [Complete certificate](../../experiments/p198_shipping_query/certificates.json).

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — all 247 glyph slots, including invalid letters and masks:**

```text
XADTAF AATAGV DAVUV GXDAG XDUDN DXUAX XXDDF DVGVD
XAXVX VGCXV XXXVG VXGVV XXXAD AGDXG AVVAA XXGDV
AXGGA VGGAA XGAX DFAGD FAADX DGGVG DXVVG VADAX
DVDDX GDG-- GVVVV XXDXV VVGVD VVVXD DVVDX GGFGV
GDAVG VADVG XDAXD GVVDV GVAVV DXDVD DCGGV XGXDA
GXFGD VAFVX DXDVV DDDGV AGGAX AXAFD VXXVG DDDAX
AXVDX X
```

</details>

The key retains the published Lasry–Niebel–Kopal–Wacker work and Lasry's
2017 list. The earlier repository OCR block remains preserved as provenance;
the source transcription, conditional frame and readable recovery here are
by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

# Naval reporting after dissolution of the Seekriegsleitung

[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source and verification](../../experiments/corpus_joint/README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Record:** p205 B, two parts, intercepted on 17 November 1918 with the internal date `16/11`. **Result:** the unchanged Nov16–18 partial key fixes **269 of 271 plaintext positions** from all **542 printed coordinates**. The order ends submission of the daily reports and war diaries to the dissolved command, while requiring offices to continue keeping their diaries.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> Mit Auflösung der Seekriegsleitung fallen die bisher dahin erstatteten Tagesmeldungen fort. Das gleiche gilt für Vorlage der Kriegstagebücher. Kriegstagebücher [s]ind von allen Dienststellen vorläufig weiterzuführen. Gleichlautend Ost-, Nordflotte, BMK. Admiralstab `1?` Op. Eins.

**Display notes:** The readable German uses the explicitly repaired output. The bracketed `[s]` is the one priced source-coordinate repair, not an abbreviation expansion or a completion of the unknown square. The closing `1?` retains exactly one unresolved numeral position; it is not an unspecified-length omission.

**English meaning:** With dissolution of the Naval Warfare Command, the daily reports previously sent there are discontinued. The same applies to submission of the war diaries. Every office is to continue maintaining its war diary for the time being. The closing names further addressees and gives an Admiral Staff reference whose second digit remains unknown.

Punctuation, word spacing and the separation of the compact addressee string are editorial. The repeated `KRIEGSTAGEBUECHER` is meaningful: one sentence concerns submitting the diaries, and the next concerns continuing to maintain them. It is therefore retained. `BMK` is not expanded to a specific office on the strength of this ciphertext alone.

## Direct reading and one explicit emendation

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
MITXAUFLOESUNGXDERXSEEKRIEGSLEITUNGXFALLENXDIEXBISHERXDAHINXERSTATTETENXTAGESMELDUNGENXFORTXDASGLEICHEXGILTXFUERXVORLAGEXDERXKRIEGSTAGEBUECHERXKRIEGSTAGEBUECHER
?INDXVONXALLENXDIENSTSTELLENXVORLAEUFIGXWEITERZUFUEHRENXGLEICHLAUTENDXOSTNORDFLOTTEXBMKXADMIRALSTABX1?XOPXEINSX
```

</details>

Part B1's **160/160 positions** are fixed. Part B2 fixes **109/111**. Its initial unknown is the square cell `GD`, whose possible values under the published partial square are `03456789`. Consequently, `SIND` cannot be obtained by completing an unassigned square cell: `S` is already established at `GA`. The proposed initial `S` requires the single source-coordinate change **B2 index 128 `D → A`**. All other 221 B2 coordinates remain unchanged, and the final unknown digit is left unresolved.

This is a readable editorial reconstruction with an exact one-coordinate cost, not a complete unchanged-source decipherment. The [certificate](../../experiments/corpus_joint/p205_readings.json) supplies the two raw texts, all plaintext domains and the edit map.

## Source and credit

The [p205 B image](../../experiments/corpus_joint/sources/p205_B.png) contains 320 coordinates in B1 and 222 in B2. The extra internal space in B1's printed `V AAFX` does not remove a coordinate. The B2 groups `GXXAV`, `FGAXA` and `DDXDV` were checked at higher magnification; their letters are preserved in the source transcription even where the result suggests a copying error.

The historical source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed p. 205, PDF p. 208 in the [complete scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view). The header reads `ASO v LP (6.38 a.m., November 17th)`, `FUER ASO 1655 (16/11) 2 TEILE B M K SEBASTOPOL`.

The **Nov16–18** period key retains the attribution in [data/keys.json](../../data/keys.json) to **George Lasry** and the historical/research work of **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**. Source assembly, review, exact edit costs and this edition are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment priority is claimed.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 experiments/corpus_joint/build_readings.py \
  experiments/corpus_joint/p205_inputs.json \
  experiments/corpus_joint/p205_readings.json --verify
python3 experiments/corpus_joint/verify_p205.py
```

# p210 A — Helsinki and return transport for the Ostsee Division

[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source certificate](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/certificates.json) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Record:** the two parts of p210 A, intercepted on 20 November 1918.
**Result:** all **208 plaintext positions** are fixed from **416 source
coordinates** under the published Nov19–21 key. Four explicit coordinate
substitutions give the following readable reconstruction.

## Reading

**Readable German:**

> Fustation Helsingfors mitteilet hierher, ob Ruecktransportmoeglichkeit
> fuer Ostseedivision gesichert.
>
> Andernfalls wird versucht, Schiffe dorthin zu entsenden. Welcher
> Verladehafen kaeme in Frage? Zentralfunkleitung, Vollzugsrat Berlin.

**Meaning:** The radio station at Helsingfors is asked to report whether
return transport for the Ostsee Division is secured. If it is not, the
sender will try to send ships there and asks which embarkation port would
be suitable. The closing names the Central Radio Direction and the
Executive Council in Berlin.

The unusual **MITTEILET** is retained as a same-length reading; it is not
silently shortened or replaced with a longer modern expression. The names
Helsingfors, Ostseedivision and Berlin are directly deciphered. The source
does not establish whether the proposed shipping was subsequently arranged.
Word spacing, punctuation and capitalization are editorial.

## Two source frames and exact costs

The [source image](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/sources/p210_A.png)
explicitly labels `1 TL RICHI-186` and `2 TL RICHI-230` below one header:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
KOW v LP (19.42 p.m., November 20th)
```

</details>

The odd combination `19.42 p.m.` is retained as printed. Both bodies contain
exactly their stated lengths. The seventeenth group in part 1 is visibly
`VFGVV`; the OCR uncertainty there is not a source erasure.

| Part | Raw positions fixed | Editorial changes |
|---|---:|---|
| A1, 186 coordinates | 93/93 | Exchange adjacent source coordinates 112 and 113, `DG→GD`, for `YITTEILET HXERHER → MITTEILET HIERHER`. |
| A2, 230 coordinates | 115/115 | Source 113 `G→D` gives `KAEME`; source 225 `X→V` gives `VOLLZUGSRAT`. |

The raw strings remain separately visible:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FUSTATIONHELSINGFORSYITTEILETHXERHEROBRUECKTRANSPORTMOEGLICHKEITFUEROSTSEEDIVISIONGESICHERTXX
ANDERNFALLSWIRDVERSUCHTSCHIFFEDORTHINZUENTSENDENWELCHERVERLADEHAFENKAETEINFRAGEXZENTRALFUNKLEITUNGVOLLZUGSRPTBERLIN
```

</details>

The four substitutions preserve **412** source coordinates. No square,
column order or frame length changes. Each complete candidate independently
re-encrypts to its stated repaired frame.

## Source and credit

Printed p210 / PDF p213 in J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX
Cipher System*, [public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [source package](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/README.md) provides
the literal rows, image coordinates, unchanged key snapshot and every
plaintext/source-coordinate map. The existing period key retains its
attribution in [data/keys.json](../../data/keys.json).

Source inspection, two-part assembly and this edition:
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment priority
is claimed.

```sh
python3 experiments/corpus_recovery/verify.py --verify
```

# p84 A/B — Release of oil and Black Sea shipping safety

[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Coordinate certificate](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/certificates.json) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Two complete, unchanged-source readings.** The published October 28–31 key
deciphers all **223 plaintext positions** from **446 received coordinates**.
Neither record needs a source correction, missing-coordinate fill or new key
assignment. The page is headed **30 October 1918**, while both reception
headers explicitly say **1 November**; these date layers remain distinct.

## A: Has the order to release the oil succeeded?

**Readable German:**

> Drahtet, ob erneuter Befehl Izzet Pascha — Izzet Pascha — zur Freigabe
> der Oele Erfolg gehabt hat. Kriegsamt, Kriegsrohstoffabtlg.
> Nr. 0, roem. 1.

**Meaning:** Telegraph whether Izzet Pasha's renewed order to release the
oil has been successful. The signature names the War Office's raw-materials
department. The clear routing names Captain Gerlach at Batum as the
representative of the Prussian War Ministry.

The name **IZZETPASCHA** occurs twice in the decrypted text, separated by
`X`; both occurrences are preserved. Its repetition is not repaired by
deleting ciphertext. The footer is literally **0ROEM1**. Its intended
administrative notation is not independently established.

The [source](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/sources/p84_A.png) gives
`FUER POT v NKJ (4.17 a.m., November 1st)` and `RICHI-244`. A time before
`(30)` is partly illegible. All 244 ciphertext coordinates are legible.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DRAHTETOBERNEUTERBEFEHLIZZETPASCHAXIZZETPASCHAZURFREIGABEDEROELEERFOLGGEHABTHATXXKRIEGSAMTKRIEGSROHSTOFFABTLGXNRX0ROEMX1XX
```

</details>

All **122/122** positions follow directly from the stated source and key.
The displayed prose adds spacing and punctuation only.

The [p83 A source edition](gerlach_oil_release_query.md) preserves the same
244-coordinate body. Its clearer internal heading reads `1830 (30)`; the
partly illegible p84 time remains transcribed as such. The p83 edition also
retains a conservative five-overprint mask branch, for which the clear p84
coordinates supply the five fills.

## B: Request daily reports on Black Sea shipping

**Readable German:**

> Erbitten fuer Truppenkdo. Kaukasus, wenn moeglich taeglich, kurze
> Mitteilung, ob Schwarze-Meerschiffahrt gefaehrdet.

**Meaning:** The Caucasus troop command requests a short daily report,
if possible, on whether shipping in the Black Sea is at risk. The message
asks for the assessment; it does not itself report that shipping is unsafe.

The [source](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/sources/p84_B.png) gives
`OSM v NKJ (3.30 a.m., November 1st)`, the clear routing
`316 15/10 V POT 1021 FUER OSM UND COS (30) VON POT`, and `RICHI-202`.
The body has exactly 202 valid coordinates.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ERBITTENFUERTRUPPENKDOXKAUKASUSWENNMOEGLICHTAEGLICHKURZEMITTEILUNGOBSCHWARZEMEERSCHIFFAHRTGEFAEHRDETX
```

</details>

All **101/101** positions are fixed with no source edit.

## Source, verification and credit

J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed
p84 / PDF p87 in the [public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [source package](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/README.md) retains
every literal coordinate, source-image hash and plaintext-coordinate pair.
Both plaintexts independently re-encrypt to the complete, unchanged source.

```sh
python3 experiments/corpus_recovery/verify.py --verify
```

The published period key keeps the historical and modern researchers'
attribution in [the key register](../../data/keys.json). Source inspection,
exact verification and this edition: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.
No first historical decipherment priority is claimed.

# Reval: expected steamers and further transport capacity

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** Childs p213 A1–A3 (PDF p216), **23 November 1918**; published `Nov22-24` key, unchanged. [Inputs](../../experiments/reval_steamer_notice/inputs.json), [exact certificates](../../experiments/reval_steamer_notice/certificates.json), [method](../../experiments/reval_steamer_notice/README.md).

The header reads `KOW v LP (06.20 p.m., November 23rd); FUER RVA 20.00 (23/11) 3 TLE`. Its stated receipt precedes the origin time on the same printed date; the discrepancy is preserved. These parts belong to the lower, 23 November section, separately from the 22 November medical continuation above them.

The message reports arrangements for two steamers to serve troops and provisions at Reval by the end of November, with more tonnage and raw-material transport to follow. Contemporary shipping records now support three separately priced name readings in the second part: **Peter Benoit, Björn and Babylon**. The tonnage remains unresolved. The source reports intended movements; their completion and the port of departure are not established here.

## p213 A1

[Source crop](../../experiments/reval_steamer_notice/sources/p213_A1.png); [overprinted glyph enlargement](../../experiments/reval_steamer_notice/sources/p213_A1_g13.png). All 200 slots are retained. The primary source reading gives 100 fixed raw labels without repair:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
RPHAXREVALXBISENDENOVEMBERWERDENZWEIDAMPFERFUERTRUPPENUNDPROVIANTVONZUSAMMENXY5111XTONNENINREVALSEIN
```

</details>

Reading: by the end of November two steamers for troops and provisions, of a combined unresolved tonnage, are expected in Reval. `RPHAX` and `Y5111` remain raw labels.

Source index 62 is an overprinted glyph, read primarily as D in `GDDVF`. The retained V alternative changes the quantity to `YP111` and nothing else in the plaintext. Neither variant is normalized to a historical capacity.

## p213 A2

**Readable German — existing word repairs and shared J/Y interpretation, with three historical ship-name proposals:**

> Weitere Tonnage folgt baldigst. Ferner Rohstofftransport abging heute Peter Benoit. Folgt morgen Bjoern und Babylon.

The names can be compared with contemporary shipping sources. *Lloyd's
Register*, **1917–18**, lists **Peter Benoit** at PES–PET, entry P471, and
three vessels named **Björn** at BJE–BLA, entries B733–735. A shipping notice
in the *Hamburger Fremdenblatt*, **28 December 1915**, evening edition,
printed p3, names the steamer **Babylon**.

| Received field | Name proposal | Extra observed-coordinate changes under the existing J/Y layer |
|---|---|---:|
| `PETERXBENVIT` | **Peter Benoit** | 2 |
| `B9VERN` → conditional `BJVERN` | **Bjoern** | 2 |
| `BAC4LON` → conditional `BACYLON` | **Babylon** | 2 |

These sources establish the spellings, not the November transport identities.
The three Björn entries make a unique vessel identification especially
uncertain. No same-movement witness has been found. Accepting all three
proposals gives the quotation above at **nine observed substitutions and
one source-mask fill**, six substitutions beyond the earlier word edition.
It uses the existing **GD=J** and **DD=Y** hypotheses without another key
assignment. No previously unknown plaintext position is added to the count.

[Register and newspaper crops, exact name costs and source provenance](../../experiments/reval_ship_name_comparison/README.md).

[Source crop](../../experiments/reval_steamer_notice/sources/p213_A2.png). There are 208 printed slots, including C at index 181. Raw:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
WEITERETANNAGEFOL?TBALDIGSTFERNERROHSTOFFTRANSPHRTABGINGHE8TEXPETERXBENVITXFOLGTMORGENXB9VERNUNDBAC4LONX
```

</details>

Three observed-coordinate substitutions and one printed-glyph fill produce:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
WEITERETONNAGEFOLGTBALDIGSTFERNERROHSTOFFTRANSPORTABGINGHEUTEXPETERXBENVITXFOLGTMORGENXB9VERNUNDBAC4LONX
```

</details>

The earlier edition reports more tonnage and raw-material transport, with
`PETERXBENVIT` leaving today and `B9VERN` and `BAC4LON` following tomorrow.
Its literal fields remain in the streams above; the historical spelling
proposals are separately priced in the current reading.

## p213 A3

[Source crop](../../experiments/reval_steamer_notice/sources/p213_A3.png). There are 162 slots with three printed dashes. Raw:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FUEREUCHWIRDMITALLENKRAEFTENGESORGTXROHAVALXXKMXALLGX?RIEFSDEPXN?YLY1XYYXYN?ANCHX
```

</details>

Filling source index 137 as F and changing index 159 F to X gives:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
FUEREUCHWIRDMITALLENKRAEFTENGESORGTXROHAVALXXKMXALLGXKRIEGSDEPXN?YLY1XYYXYN?ANCHX
```

</details>

Reading: “Für euch wird mit allen Kräften gesorgt.” The received `ROHAVAL` and the closing reference remain unexpanded. Two erased coordinates in that reference are still unresolved; no date or serial is guessed.

## Attribution

Earlier unreviewed repository screens already recognized the first two bodies. The present edition adds the source audit, exact repair costs, the separately retained glyph alternative and the closing source frame. It makes no first historical decipherment claim and changes no baseline key.

# German tonnage and proposed ship sales to Turkey

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and recovery: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

A three-part Marineamt instruction says that selling German ships to
Turkey is advisable only in the most extreme emergency. It warns that the
Turkish interest appears to be acquiring German tonnage more than
transporting Germans away, requires immediate payment and authorization,
and gives price terms for `GENERAL` and a second vessel whose received
name varies between `KERKIJRA` and `KEHKYRA`.

This is distinct from the [Corcovado sale correspondence](corcovado_sale_terms.md).
The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX
Cipher System*, printed p177, PDF p180, record B. Its page heading says
November 11, 1918; the receipt line says `NKJ v LP (2.55 a.m., November 12th)`;
the origin line reads `1410 (11/11)`, `3 TLE`. These dates are retained as
printed.

The [literal source edition](../../experiments/turkish_tonnage/inputs.json)
uses the published `Nov10-12` partial square and transposition order.
The [exact certificate](../../experiments/turkish_tonnage/certificates.json)
contains every source coordinate, raw plaintext domain, proposed repair
and the two tied models of the second part. Published key authorship is
preserved in the inputs. A bounded check found no explicit body discussion
of this ship-sale instruction in the checked Lasry and colleagues paper,
its corresponding dissertation chapter or the cached 55 comments on the
2017 ScienceBlogs post. No universal historical-priority claim is made.

## Conditional shared digits

The third part gains the final reference digit, **A6S22647**, reaching **187/187 labels** with its four earlier word repairs. The price proposals and their attribution remain as recorded below. The [joint reconstruction](../../experiments/nov10_joint_completion/README.md) combines the earlier Marineamt and formation interpretations with the army-number constraint and the mobilization decree; the reversed 7/9 assignment is retained there.

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the joint square:**

> Falls dort Verkauf fuer unaufschiebbar angesehen wird, ist drahtlich zu berichten. Verkauft nicht ohne Genehmigung. Forderung General 1200 Mark, Kerkyra tausend Mark fuer Bruttoregistertonne. Marineamt A6S22647.

<details>
<summary>Exact conditional labels</summary>

**Edited output — p177_B3, conditional shared square; 187/187 fixed positions:**

```text
FALLSDORTVERKAUFFUERUNAUFSCHIEBBARANGESEHENWIRDXISTDRAHTLICHZUBERICHTENXVERKAUFTNICHTOHNEGENEHMIGUNGXFORDERUNGGENERAL1200MARKKERKYRATAUSENDMARKFUERBRUTTOREGISTERTONNEXXMARINEAMTXXA6S22647
```

</details>


## B1: sale only in an extreme emergency

The first part contains all 330 advertised slots. The first 40 coordinates,
which were split into a separate block by the OCR extraction, are simply
the first printed grid row. They are retained in their original order.
Source index 280 is the invalid `C` at the beginning of `CGVAD`.
The raw 165-position reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
MMDXXAUFTELEGRAMMVOM?X11XVERKAUFGENERALKERKIJRANURIMAEUSSERSTENNOTFALLRATSAMX?ONHIERWIRDERSUCHTA3SWA?FENSTILLSTANDSBEDINGUNGABTRANSPORT?ITDEUTSCHERTONNAGEZUERWIRKENX
```

</details>

Three observed-coordinate substitutions and the invalid-coordinate fill
produce this 164/165-position candidate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
MMDXXAUFTELEGRAMMVOM?X11XVERKAUFGENERALKERKIJRANURIMAEUSSERSTENNOTFALLRATSAMXVONHIERWIRDERSUCHTALSWAFFENSTILLSTANDSBEDINGUNGABTRANSPORTMITDEUTSCHERTONNAGEZUERWIRKENX
```

</details>

Addressed to the M.M.D., it refers to a telegram of an unresolved November
date. Sale of `GENERAL` and `KERKIJRA` is advisable only in the most extreme
emergency. The sender is trying to obtain transport using German tonnage
as an armistice condition.

The source's eight-character `KERKIJRA` is preserved. It is not silently
shortened to the seven-character spelling proposed in the third part.
The unknowns in `?ON` and `?IT` come from unfilled numerical cells, so their
ordinary-word repairs to `VON` and `MIT` explicitly change received
coordinates; they are not consequences of filling those key cells.

## B2: Turkish motives and immediate payment

The second part advertises 296 coordinates but prints **295 valid
coordinates**. Row 6, group 7 is `GDXV`, with only four letters.
The representative model inserts a single erased coordinate at boundary
232, inside that deficient group. Its raw 148-position reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional insertion at boundary 232 in the short printed group:**

```text
WUNSCHDERTUERKENRICHTETSICHWOHLMEHRAUFERWERBDEUTSCHERTONNAGEALSAUFABTRANSPORTD?UTSCHERXVORSICHTGEBOTENXXREEDERWOLLENNURGEGENSOFORTIIEKASSEV?RKAUFENX
```

</details>

All **296** possible single-loss boundaries are screened against the same
ordinary-word candidate. **Boundaries 232 and 233 tie** for the minimum of
two changes to observed coordinates. The second tied model has the raw
fragment `ABTRANSPORTDEUTSCHER?VORSICHT`, instead of the first model's
`ABTRANSPORTD?UTSCHERXVORSICHT`. Both fill the inserted coordinate with `X`,
restoring the same five-letter group `GDXXV`, and both give the identical
complete corrected ciphertext.

Two observed-coordinate changes, plus that one missing-coordinate fill,
yield this exactly reencryptable candidate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional missing-slot frame, with the stated repairs and fill:**

```text
WUNSCHDERTUERKENRICHTETSICHWOHLMEHRAUFERWERBDEUTSCHERTONNAGEALSAUFABTRANSPORTDEUTSCHERXVORSICHTGEBOTENXXREEDERWOLLENNURGEGENSOFORTIGEKASSEVERKAUFENX
```

</details>

The sender suspects that the Turkish aim is more to acquire German tonnage
than to transport Germans away. Caution is required. The shipowners wish
to sell only for immediate cash payment. The source does not distinguish
which of the adjacent identical `X` coordinates was lost, and the edition
does not force a unique loss boundary.

## B3: prior authorization and prices

All 374 coordinates are valid. The raw 187-position reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FALLSDORTVERKAUFFUERUNAUFSCHIEBBARANGESEHENWIRDXISTDRAHTLICHZUBERICHTENXVERKAUFTNICHTOHNEGVNEHMIGUNGXFORDERUNGGENERAL1200MARKKEHKYRATAUSEN?MARKFUERZRUTTOREGISTERTONNEXXMARINEAMTXXA?S22?4?
```

</details>

Four observed-coordinate substitutions support this candidate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
FALLSDORTVERKAUFFUERUNAUFSCHIEBBARANGESEHENWIRDXISTDRAHTLICHZUBERICHTENXVERKAUFTNICHTOHNEGENEHMIGUNGXFORDERUNGGENERAL1200MARKKERKYRATAUSENDMARKFUERBRUTTOREGISTERTONNEXXMARINEAMTXXA?S22?4?
```

</details>

If the recipient regards sale as impossible to postpone, it must report
by telegraph. It must not sell without authorization. The price clause
reads `GENERAL1200MARKKERKYRATAUSENDMARKFUERBRUTTOREGISTERTONNE`: 1,200 marks
for General and 1,000 marks for the second vessel, per gross register ton.
The first `1200MARK` field is directly observed in full. The second amount
is raw `TAUSEN?`; the final `D` is an explicit one-coordinate ordinary-word
repair. The `Z` to `B` in `BRUTTO` and the `H` to `R` in the candidate
`KERKYRA` are also priced repairs.

No external ship identification is needed to decode these words, and this
edition does not claim to settle the vessels' later histories. The whole
reference ending remains `A?S22?4?` under the unchanged partial key.

## Applying the separate XX=6 hypothesis

The Corcovado package separately argues that the Marineamt office/file
prefix is `A6S`, using a later independently observed `SECHS`. It keeps that
association conditional. This edition applies its **Nov10–12 `XX=6`**
hypothesis uniformly to every source and repaired variant; the p177
reference is not used to derive the hypothesis anew.

| Physical occurrence | Plaintext index | Source indices | Conditional effect |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| B1 referred date | 20 | 270, 22 | `VOM?X11` becomes `VOM6X11` |
| B2 received ordinary word | 139 | 293, 108 | `V?RKAUFEN` becomes **`V6RKAUFEN`** |
| B3 office prefix | 180 | 327, 45 | `A?S` becomes `A6S` |
| B3 reference tail | 184 | 210, 281 | `22?4?` becomes `2264?` |

All indices are zero-based. The B2 occurrence is a received garble under
the condition; it is retained, not suppressed. The independent
ordinary-word repair changes that received `XX` pair to the known pair
for `E`, so this conditional `6` is absent from the repaired candidate.
Only the other three fixed positions persist after ordinary-word repairs.
Both B2 frame alternatives include the same physical `V6RKAUFEN` effect.

Every marginal-domain change is retained as well. In B1, the raw domains
at positions 77 (`FD`) and 135 (`GF`) shrink from `56789` to `5789`, while
position 100 (`?F`) shrinks from `056789BFHR` to `05789BFHR`. In the alternate
B2 gap-233 model, position 86 (`G?`) shrinks from `56789DJLMX` to
`5789DJLMX`; the representative gap-232 model instead retains a different
raw erasure at position 78, domain `2CEHQW`. In B3, both raw `GF` positions,
138 and 186, shrink from `56789` to `5789`. Position 138 is separately
repaired to the `D` of `TAUSEND`; position 186 remains unresolved.

The conditional date `6/11` has not been independently tied to an earlier
same-vessel telegram. It must not be used to select a presumed original
message and then cited as proof of its own key assignment. No reference
tail is equated to a Corcovado reference.

## Scope and verification

The three records have **999 printed slots**, **998 valid coordinates**,
and **1,000 modeled coordinates**, yielding **500 plaintext positions**.
The raw source models fix **490** positions. Nine observed-coordinate
substitutions, one invalid-`C` fill and one missing-coordinate fill give
**496/500** fixed candidate positions. The separate conditional `XX=6`
layer fixes three additional candidate positions, giving **499/500**.
The final reference cell `GF` retains the domain `5789`.

The [verifier](../../experiments/turkish_tonnage/verify.py) recomputes the
independent transposition and raw domains, every exact repair, all 296 gap
candidates, both tied models and all eight conditional source/candidate
variants. Full readings reencrypt exactly; partial readings retain their
explicit unresolved coordinates and domains.

```bash
python experiments/turkish_tonnage/verify.py --verify
python experiments/turkish_tonnage/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
```

The PDF option verifies the complete primary source hash and rerenders all
three crops pixel-for-pixel. The conditional dependency is bound by its

# Urgent shipping capacity and probable reliance on sea transport

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The surviving second and third parts request urgent shipping capacity and say that all troops will probably need sea transport. The source explicitly marks the first part missing. Repeated capacity labels, differing command fields and the unresolved source-mask position remain literal.

## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p218 excerpt](../../experiments/urgent_shipping_space/sources/p218_reviewed.png) · [Inputs](../../experiments/urgent_shipping_space/inputs.json) · [Position and change certificates](../../experiments/urgent_shipping_space/certificates.json)

The published `Nov25-28` key is unchanged. [Original OCR records](../../experiments/urgent_shipping_space/ocr_snapshot.json) and [reproducible comparisons with that earlier evidence](../../experiments/urgent_shipping_space/prior_candidates.json) are preserved separately. The present edition supplies checked source framing, exact costs and readable passages; it makes no first-public-decipherment claim.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [p218 B2](#p218-b2) | 188 | 94 / 94 | 1 | 0 |
| [p218 B3](#p218-b3) | 200 | 99 / 100 | 0 | 0 |

## p218 B2

**Source transcription — header:** `B) KOW v RVA (01.36 a.m., November 26th); KR AN LP 2100 (11/25) 3 TLE; (1 TL missing); 2 TL RICHI-188`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
SOFORTIGESEGDUNGVONSCHIFFSRAUMFUERJ3YYYMANN3YYYPFERDEXJ3YYYMANN3YYYPFERDEXRTVLDRINGENDGEBOTENX
```

**Edited output — 1 observed-coordinate substitution and 0 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
SOFORTIGESENDUNGVONSCHIFFSRAUMFUERJ3YYYMANN3YYYPFERDEXJ3YYYMANN3YYYPFERDEXRTVLDRINGENDGEBOTENX
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Sofortige Sendung von Schiffsraum fuer J3YYY Mann 3YYY Pferde. J3YYY Mann 3YYY Pferde. RTVL dringend geboten.

**Meaning:** The surviving second part urgently requests shipping capacity for personnel and horses. The paired capacity labels are repeated in the source. J3YYY, 3YYY and RTVL remain literal; no numerical total or port identification is imposed.

**Editorial limits.**

- The source explicitly says “1 TL missing.” This edition starts with the complete native 188-coordinate second part and supplies no missing first body.
- SEGDUNG to SENDUNG is one observed-coordinate substitution. All source coordinates remain in native order.
- Both repetitions of J3YYY MANN 3YYY PFERDE remain in the exact stream and readable passage. They are not silently converted to familiar decimal numbers or counted as separate telegrams.
- RTVL is not expanded into a named port or headquarters. The printed interception date November 26 and originating line 11/25 remain separate.

## p218 B3

**Source transcription — header:** `B) KOW v RVA (01.36 a.m., November 26th); KR AN LP 2100 (11/25) 3 TLE; 3 TL RICHI-200`

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
DAWAHRSCHEINLICHALLETRUPPENAUFSEETRANSPORTANGEWIESENXGENXKDOX?XBXVX72XGENXKDOXZXBXNX72XJAXNR42XJ2GEH
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the unchanged raw output:**

> Da wahrscheinlich alle Truppen auf Seetransport angewiesen. Gen. Kdo. ? B V 72. Gen. Kdo. Z B N 72. JAXNR42XJ2GEH.

**Meaning:** The third part explains that all troops will probably depend on sea transport. Its command and reference fields remain literal. This is a stated expectation and an urgent request for capacity, not proof that ships were supplied or the troops transported.

**Editorial limits.**

- The native 200-coordinate body contains one printed dash in -AGXG. It remains masked and unfilled; no observed coordinate changes.
- The remaining source-mask position has domain {3, D, F, M, T, X}. A familiar abbreviation is not forced into that field.
- The two command fields retain their different V and N labels, the repeated 72, and the complete footer JAXNR42XJ2GEH. No historical unit identity or numbered reference is inferred.

## Meaning without converting the labels

The request concerns transport capacity for men and horses, and the following explanation expects general reliance on sea transport. It does not establish that transport was supplied. Both repetitions of `J3YYY MANN 3YYY PFERDE` are retained. A familiar-looking decimal conversion is not silently applied to the J/Y labels, and RTVL is not expanded to a particular port.

The third-part unknown is a printed source erasure under an otherwise fixed square, with domain `{3, D, F, M, T, X}`. The second command field retains N where the first has V. Both details remain visible rather than being normalized to a standard command abbreviation.

## Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates independently reconstruct column positions and domains, compare them with the cipher implementation, replay every priced change, and check all readable nonseparator labels. Partial readings have one consistent injective square/source-mask completion witness that re-encrypts exactly; those witness choices are not historical identifications. Source images are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/urgent_shipping_space/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to check the original PDF and exact source-crop pixels.

**State: OPEN.** Source transcription and review: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

The second part remains unread. All 152 printed slots are transcribed, but 48 are erasures, leaving only 104 observed coordinates. Its preceding first part is separately catalogued; its reading does not by itself restore the missing coordinates here.

## Source

```text
2 TL
```

```text

XXXX- ----- XFFGG AADAX AXVX- ----- DA-FA XADXA
AVGXX ----- FXFDX GXVAG GVDDD VGFVA X-XFV GAVXV

```

</details>

|---|---:|

| Observed ADFGVX coordinates | 104 |

## Boundaries and uncertainty

The page heading says `4th NOVEMBER, 1918`, while the reception header says
November 5th. Both dates are preserved. `2 TL` identifies this physical body
as part two of the printed two-part transmission.

The repeated group `XFFGG` occurs twice, at zero-based source indices 35–39
and 50–54. Both occurrences remain in place. Repetition alone does not
establish a copying error or justify deleting one. The final row ends with
22 consecutive printed dashes, including a final two-dash group.

The [first part, p127 B1](../radio/nov4_personnel_transmission_notice.md#p127-b1),
contains personnel and radio-transmission wording. That context is a
research lead, not a plaintext crib licensed by the second part’s source.

## Research leads

- Compare the confirmed first-part key and header with the second part while keeping the conflicting printed dates visible.
- Seek an independently received copy that can constrain the 48 erased coordinates, especially the long final gap.
- Examine the two `XFFGG` groups and the surrounding observed coordinates before proposing duplication or a relocated erasure run. Score competing geometries against controls; sparse-coordinate fluency alone is weak evidence.

These are research directions, not accepted decipherments. A failed search
under one key or loss model does not exclude other source-supported models.

# p100 — Enemy divisions approaching Belgrade

[Case index](README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** Earlier body verified after explicit erasure resolution and two-coordinate insertion. **Key:** `Nov1-3`.

**Earliest credited record:** [Armin, 2017-03-01, comment 13](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-852373). **Current source and arithmetic review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German — earlier credited reconstruction:**

> Keine Stoerung durch Feind. Mittags 2 feindl. Div. im Marsch auf Belgrad.

**Meaning:** No interference by the enemy. At midday, two enemy divisions are marching toward Belgrade.

**Notes:** `feindl. Div.` means enemy divisions. Spaces and punctuation expand the telegram's `X` separators; the wording follows Armin's repaired reading. Its treatment of the invalid printed `T` and the two inserted coordinates remains conditional, as recorded below.

## Recomputed reading


</details>

## Review

- The scan prints T at source 20 in TAFGV; it is outside ADFGVX and remains unknown in the analysis layer.
- The A interpretation at source 20 is required by the published STOERUNG. A legacy V transcription yields STOERFNG instead.

## Earlier published readings

**Raw decryption — [Armin, 2017-03-01, comment 13](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-852373).**

| `armin_body_exact` | 62 / 62 | — | Yes |

**Notes:** Brackets mark editorial interpretations of garbled words. The reference numbers are retained without attempting to reconstruct their administrative meaning. Baertl's longer completion is printed below for attribution; its extra wording is not recovered by the 143-position model. The final unpaired coordinate and its optional deletion are separately certified.

<details>


## Verified variants

## Explicit repair of the orphan coordinate

The unpaired final intermediate `D` comes from original source index **244** (the 245th received character, final `D` of group 49 `XAXGD`). Deleting it in addition to the three published deletions produces 286 coordinates and exactly the same 143-position body, now with a complete ordinary re-encryption. This equivalent reconstruction is a contribution of the present arithmetic review; it does not establish the historical error mechanism.

A separate [optional two-deletion model](../experiments/p105_optional_two_deletions/README.md) retains 288 of the 290 printed coordinates and gives a fully paired 144-label raw stream, with three explicitly priced ordinary-word substitutions. It preserves the earlier reading above and documents all twelve equal-cost word-only deletion descriptions, retrospective held-out comparisons and independent native vocabulary witnesses. Its changed reference/date labels remain geometry-dependent alternatives, and the visibly printed excluded coordinates remain in its full source ledger.
