# p109 — Evening report and the Sava crossing

[Case index](README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** Earlier damaged body reviewed against a newly transcribed same-page near-parallel. **Key:** `Nov1-3`.

**Earliest credited record:** [Norbert, 2017-03-01, comment 18](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-852658). **Current source and arithmetic review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German — earlier credited reconstruction and later source comparison:**

> O.K.M. [Abendmeldung]. [Save/Sava]: [Uebergang letzter Teile beendet].
> [1 weitere fdl. Div.] im Marsch [auf Belgrad erkannt]. Sonst keine
> [Ereignisse]. `ASOXK511`.

**Meaning:** An evening report: the last elements have completed the Sava crossing; one further enemy division has been observed marching toward Belgrade. No other events are reported. The closing reference remains damaged. This is the most likely interpretation of two imperfect witnesses, not an unedited decipherment of either one.

**Notes:** The neighboring [p109 B source](../sources/excerpts/childs_p109_B.png) independently supplies `SAV?`, a damaged `UEBERGANG`, and the exact ending `ERKANNT`. It supports reading `BELGRAD ERKANNT`, rather than the earlier segmentation `BELGRADER KAVV`. The compact proposal has the same 124 positions as the target's earlier repair, retaining the source-like spelling `ABENDMELUNG` and the uninterpreted closing characters. Baertl's `UNTERBRINGUNG` version is six letters longer.

The literal closing `ASOXK511` is retained from the target's recomputed
earlier reading and its compact proposal. Its labels, including `511`,
remain uninterpreted. The different closing of the neighboring B witness
is shown separately below and does not resolve this reference.

## The neighboring witness

Section B has 248 slots, six of them erased. It decrypts directly under `Nov1-3` to:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
OX?XMXABENDM?LUNGXSAV?5UEB0RG4V?LA5ZTERXALLEBEENDETXHNEITAREFDLXD?VXIMEARSCHAUFBML7RADERKANNTXSONSTKEIVMEREIGNIXSE?XAXOXKX16
```

</details>

It agrees with the earlier reconstructed target D at **200 known coordinates** and disagrees at **42**. The two printed timestamps and different endings remain unresolved. The [source-parallel certificate](../data/certificates/p109_parallel.json) preserves both witnesses and their independent transcription review.

The retained compact proposal using `SAVA` needs 23 further coordinate changes relative to each witness. Under the explicitly conditional common-plaintext model, 42 total disagreements are unavoidable; that proposal has 46, with its four extra disagreements confined to three plaintext positions. This quantifies the remaining editorial choice instead of treating fluent German as source evidence. The [editorial certificate](../data/certificates/editorial_readings.json) maps every change through the earlier target repair.

The source comparison and revised interpretation are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**; Norbert retains the original target-reading credit.

## Exact search over the competing readings

The [multi-witness decoder](../experiments/parallel_decoder/README.md) jointly
scores German language and the exact coordinate disagreement with B and the
explicitly repaired D. It uses no proposed phrase as a crib. Dynamic
programming finds the exact ten best strings under each stated objective and
edit budget; the full minimum-cost model alone contains **2^42** possible
plaintexts.

All 28 first-ranked results, spanning two language objectives, seven budgets
and full-message/body-only scopes, share:

<details>
<summary>Search diagnostic</summary>

**Search diagnostic — shared segment of ranked candidates; not an accepted recovery:**

```text
XIMMARSCHAUFBELGRADERKANNTXSONSTKEINEEREIGNISSE
```

</details>

Within those 47 positions, 33 are already unique in the minimum-cost source
domains and 14 are selected among competing letters. This agreement supports
the reading but does not turn the 14 choices into received evidence. The two
language objectives share a corpus, so their agreement is a sensitivity check.

| Unresolved editorial choice | Exact source constraint |
|---|---|
| `SAVE` or `SAVA` | Equal combined cost. `SAVE` preserves every known B coordinate in the word; `SAVA` spends one change in B and one fewer in D. The final vowel remains unsettled. |
| `UEBERGANG` | Requires two changes above the local minimum; selected by mixed four-/six-gram scoring once that budget is available. |
| `TEILE` | Requires one change above the local minimum. It is a grammatical interpretation, but no reported top-ten language result selects it. |
| Numeral, unit and closing reference | Remain editorial or unresolved. Language scores do not establish their identities. |

The historical spelling *Save* also occurs in the Austrian State Archives'
[catalogue of a 26 October 1918 crossing order](https://www.archivinformationssystem.at/detail.aspx?ID=7182872).
The order's image was not inspected; this is nomenclature context only. The
decoder retains its garbled optima and all coordinate changes, including cases
where a larger budget damages an otherwise plausible abbreviation.

## Recomputed reading

Variant `norbert18`; the reading is conditional on its recorded repairs.

<details>
<summary>Recomputed earlier reading</summary>

**Recomputed prior reading — under the recorded variant and repairs:**

```text
OXKXMXABECDPELUNGXS4V4XUMBJRGA8GLETZTEVTVILEBEEVUETX1WEITEDEFDUXNIV5IMMARSCH4UFBELGRADERKAVV2XSONSTKEINEEDMILNISSEXXASOXK511
```

</details>

## Review

The published raw decipherment is reproduced after its explicitly recorded edits. Residual garbles remain in the text; editorial normalization is listed separately.

## Earlier published readings

**Raw decryption — [Norbert, 2017-03-01, comment 18](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-852658).**

Same text as the recomputed reading above.

**Editorial completion — [Max Baertl, 2017-03-11, comment 39](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-858010).**

<details>
<summary>Earlier attributed reading</summary>

**Earlier attributed reading:**

```text
OXKXMXABENDMELDUNGXS4V4XUNTERBRINGUNGLETZTERTEILEBEENDETX1WEITERERDUXDIV5IMMARSCHAUFBELGRADERKAVVX2XSONSTKEINEEREIGNISSEXXASOXK511
```

</details>

Published length 130; model length 124.

## Verified variants

| Variant | Fixed / total positions | Unpaired suffix | Ordinary re-encryption |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `norbert18` | 124 / 124 | — | Yes |

Source strings, edit positions, plaintext domains and attribution are retained in [the prior-reading certificate](../data/prior_readings.json). Re-encryption checks the stated reconstruction, including any conjectural repairs.

A separate [literal duplicate-pair alternative](../experiments/p109_optional_duplicate_pair/README.md) removes one printed `XXAXA DDVVV` copy from D, retains all other coordinates unchanged, and compares every ten-exclusion source description with B. It records 204 known agreements and 38 disagreements, both complete-copy maps, all tied full/body minima, a geometry-conditioned `SAVE` preference supported by the native p99 spelling, and a separately priced complete reading. The older edition above, its `SAVA` alternative and the different literal closings remain preserved.

# p132 — Repeat-transmission instructions for Eilvese

[Case index](README.md) · [Reading conventions](../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Childs p132 B, received on 5 November 1918, instructs Eilvese to repeat a telegram and precede it with a signal. The conditional reading uses the published **Nov4–6** key and a model in which one extra `V` entered the intermediate coordinate stream.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German — conditional extra-coordinate model, with three substitutions and two erasure fills:**

> Für Eilvese. Wiederholet Telegr[amm] von vierter Periode in fünfter.
> Gebet vorher 5 Min. VVV.

**Meaning:** For Eilvese: repeat the telegram from the fourth period during
the fifth. Send `VVV` for five minutes beforehand. The older imperatives
`WIEDERHOLET` and `GEBET` and the numerical `5` remain literal. `[amm]` only
expands the telegram abbreviation.

The [p134 repeat instruction](context/radio_instructions.md#p134-b--repeat-a-fourth-period-telegram-in-the-fifth) independently uses the fourth/fifth-period formula. The preceding `VORHER` signal clause is a p132 reconstruction, first proposed by Norbert in 2017.

## Source and current conditional model

The [B source](../experiments/november_radio_service/sources/childs_p132_B.png)
is marked with explicit urgency:

<details>
<summary>Source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
B) LP v NKJ (6.13 p.m., November 5th)
SSD EILT SOFORT LOESEN 1410 (5)
RIZI-155
```

</details>

The printed length and manual transcription both give **155 slots**. There
are two printed dashes in group `XFF--`; all other coordinates are retained.
The direct odd-frame reading has 77 paired positions and one unpaired coordinate:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — original odd frame; paired prefix and orphan coordinate reported separately:**

```text
FFEREILVESEXWIEDERHOLETT?LEGGWD3?MYMFLWF7MFFS7KFNT8RLTIWFWUAFQLL3F1QF7PZNMDQQ
```

</details>

The latter portion becomes readable in the opposite pairing phase. Under the extra-coordinate model, undoing the original transposition exposes four consecutive `V` coordinates at interim indices **54–57**. Removing any one gives the same 154-coordinate stream:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional deletion of one V at interim indices 54–57 after untransposition:**

```text
FFEREILVESEXWIEDERHOLETT?LEGRXVO?VIERTERPERIODEINFU1NFTERXGEBETSORHER5MINXVVV
```

</details>

Three observed-coordinate substitutions and two printed-dash fills give:

<details>
<summary>Exact edited proposal</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional interim-deletion model, with the stated repairs and fills:**

```text
FUEREILVESEXWIEDERHOLETTELEGRXVONVIERTERPERIODEINFUENFTERXGEBETVORHER5MINXVVV
```

</details>

### Exact costs and the four equivalent positions

| Received source index, zero-based | Printed group / position, one-based | Change | Effect |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 52 | 11 / 3 | `X` → `F` | `SORHER` → `VORHER` |
| 64 | 13 / 5 | `A` → `D` | `FFER` → `FUER` |
| 88 | 18 / 4 | `A` → `F` | `FU1NFTER` → `FUENFTER` |
| 103 | 21 / 4 | printed dash → `F` | Missing `E` in `TELEGR` |
| 104 | 21 / 5 | printed dash → `X` | Missing `N` in `VON` |

The repair of `FU1NFTER` changes the affected coordinate within the word; the square's digit `1` and the numeral in `5MIN` retain their assignments.

Re-encryption of the 77-character proposal reintroduces the extra intermediate `V` before applying the original column order. All four positions produce the same 155-slot witness with **three observed substitutions, two dash fills and one extra intermediate coordinate**. Their differing source origins remain in the certificate.

The [geometry audit](../experiments/november_radio_service/geometry_audit.json) compares all 156 one-insertion and 155 one-removal positions. For the stated wording, the four equivalent `V` removals form the unique minimum-cost set. Earlier insertion candidates and the full comparison remain in that audit; the result is conditional on the plaintext template.

<details>
<summary>Earlier readings and exact comparison</summary>

## Earlier source model and credited variants

Variant `norbert37_displayed_rectangle`: Exact reconstruction of the 2017 displayed rectangle, including its previously implicit correction at source index 88.

<details>
<summary>Earlier reconstructed stream</summary>

**Recomputed prior reading — under the recorded variant and repairs:**

```text
FFEREILVESEXWIEDERHOLETTELEGRXVONVIERTERPERIODEINFUTNFTERXGEBETSORHER5MINXVVV
```

</details>

## Review

Norbert's marked extra `V` is intermediate 56; adjacent identical coordinates make its position within the run indistinguishable. His displayed rectangle also changes source 88 from A to X. That additional change produces `FUTNFTER`; the unaltered source reads `FU1NFTER`. The current wording instead uses the A→F repair in the table above.

## Earlier published readings

**Early fragment — [Thomas, 2017-03-02, comment 27](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-853089).**

<details>
<summary>Earlier attributed reading</summary>

**Earlier attributed reading:**

```text
WIEDERHOLETELEG??
```

</details>

**Raw decryption — [Norbert, 2017-03-11, comment 37](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-857907).**

Same text as the recomputed reading above.

**Editorial completion — [Max Baertl, 2017-03-11, comment 39](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-858010).**

<details>
<summary>Earlier attributed reading</summary>

**Earlier attributed reading:**

```text
FUEREILVESEXWIEDERHOLETTELEGRXVONVIERTERPERIODEINFUENFTERXGEBETSORDER5MINXVVV
```

</details>

Conflicts at 3 plaintext positions under the compared variant.

**Alternative wording — [Norbert, 2017-03-12, comment 40](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-858211).**

`GEBET VORHER` is an explicitly published alternative to `GEBETSORDER`. Norbert compared the substitution pairs for `S` and `V`, noting the one-coordinate change. The present edition prefers this interpretation of the instruction while retaining both earlier proposals.

## Verified variants

| Variant | Fixed / total positions | Unpaired suffix | Ordinary re-encryption |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `norbert37_source_preserving` | 75 / 77 | — | Partial |
| `norbert37_displayed_rectangle` | 77 / 77 | — | Partial |

The [prior-reading certificate](../data/prior_readings.json) retains both variants, their source edits and plaintext domains.

The [explicit editorial certificate](../data/certificates/editorial_readings.json) maps the three readable normalizations to three additional coordinate changes, including the previously emended source position 88. Run `python3 -m adfgvx.editorial` to reproduce them.

The [p189 C instruction](context/p189_C.md) concerns difficult messages and a December key. Its different wording and key distinguish it from the p132 transmission.

</details>

## Source evidence and reproduction

The [current source inputs](../experiments/november_radio_service/inputs.json),
[cipher certificate](../experiments/november_radio_service/certificates.json)
and [geometry audit](../experiments/november_radio_service/geometry_audit.json)
retain the native source, exact origins, all compared positions and forward witnesses. The package identifier `p132_B` is an evidence alias for this source. Source comparison and the current repair audit are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**; Thomas, Norbert and Max Baertl's earlier readings are reproduced above.

The period key is prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**, [2016, DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461).
Their Eilvese discussion supplies the station context. The [source image](../experiments/november_radio_service/sources/childs_p132_B.png)
is from J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
printed p132, PDF p135 in the [scanned volume](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).

```sh
python experiments/november_radio_service/verify.py --verify
python experiments/november_radio_service/geometry_audit.py --verify
python -m adfgvx.editorial
```

# p146 — Kerch radio call-sign instruction

[Case index](README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../docs/reading-conventions.md)

The Kerch radio station is assigned the call sign Richard–Emil–Karl. Our duplicate-group reconstruction of the Nov4–6-key message fixes **117 of 122 positions** while retaining all 239 coordinates outside the duplicated group unchanged.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German — reconstructed frame and word repairs stated below:**

> Funkstelle Kertsch erhaelt ab 12.[11] Rufnamen Richard Emil Karl. Funkstellen dortigen Bereichs benachrichtigen. Nachrichtenchef 4BG7834.

**Meaning:** The Kerch radio station is to use the call sign spelled out as Richard–Emil–Karl from the stated date, most plausibly 12 November. Notify the radio stations in that area. The closing administrative reference remains literal.

The conditional model removes one of two identical `XAAXV` groups and restores a missing five-coordinate group. The proposed fill `AAXAA` supplies `L, 1, N, E, F` in the reading. Its month digit is `1` under the ordinary day.month interpretation of `12.1?`.

The five unresolved domains permit 7,776 strings. The proposed completion follows the words and date convention; the final administrative reference remains literal.

The [new certificate](../data/certificates/p146_duplicate_group.json) retains all eighteen insertion/deletion alignments compatible with the chosen full reading. Only two alignments use printed five-letter group boundaries, corresponding to deletion of either duplicate. # p152 — Silk purchases and transport from the Caucasus

[Case index](README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../docs/reading-conventions.md)

This order concerns silk bought in the Caucasus and its resale where transport cannot be assured. We identified the truncated p152 challenge with the fuller p136 B transmission and compared its continuation with the independent p144 reception. All use the published **Nov4–6** key.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German — associated witnesses; editorial wording and names remain qualified:**

> Fuer kaiserliche deutsche Delegation, fuer MAIER HALLER, Tiflis. Nummer sechszehn. [Veranlassen, dass] im [Kaukasus] gekaufte Seide, Seidengarne, [Abfaelle], Strusen, [deren] Abtransport nicht unbedingt sichergestellt ist, nach Moeglichkeit dort wieder verkauft werden. Mercator. Kriegsamt, Kriegsrohstoffabteilung. R. 138, Strich, elf. KRA.

**Meaning:** To the Imperial German delegation in Tiflis, for the person or designation written `MAIER HALLER`: arrange for silk, silk yarn, waste and coarse cocoon filaments bought in the Caucasus to be resold locally where their transport cannot be guaranteed. The message is signed Mercator and the War Office's raw materials department.

The reading combines the fuller p136 first part with the continuation witnesses. Brackets mark word repairs; `MAIER HALLER` remains unidentified. The transmitted forms `SECHSZEHN` and `STRICH` are retained. *Strusen* is a historical silk-trade term, described in an [1853 technical account](https://dingler.bbaw.de/articles/ar128114.html).

| Record | Received slots | Header | Review |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| p152 E, part 1 | 104, including 2 erasures | No length | Damaged tail of the fuller record. |
| p136 B, part 1 | 314 | 304 | Directly decrypts without edits. |
| p136 B, part 2 | 269 | 270 | One missing `F` supplied by p152's parallel group. |
| p152 E, part 2 | 270 | 280 | Directly decrypts with residual garbles. |
| p144 A2 | 270 | 270 | Native continuation; one explicitly supported coordinate substitution. |

## Raw p136 B1 parallel plaintext

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FUERKAISERLICHEDEUTSCHEDELEGATIONFUERMAIERHALLERXTIFLISXNUMMERSECHSZEHNVERANLASSELXDGSSIMKAPKKSUSGEKAUFTEXSEIDEXSEIDENGARNEXABFAEHLEXSTRUSENXDETENABTRANSPORT
```

</details>

This direct p136 reading supplies the first-part text absent from the 104-slot p152 fragment. Its word repairs are marked in the readable edition above.

## Raw continuation witnesses

The [p144 A2 continuation](finance/nov6_silk_resale_continuation.md) supplies 270 observed coordinates. Its sole proposed change, source index 146 `D` → `A`, repairs `GESTELPT` to the `GESTELLT` already present in p152. Together these receptions give all **135 positions** of the continuation direct paired-coordinate support.

The p144 group `XAFFF` also confirms the `F` supplied in p136's short `XAFF`. The adjacent identical `F`s leave the exact loss position indistinguishable. The p144 edition links its complete source and cipher certificate.

**p136_B2**

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — cross-copy-supported frame including the separately supplied missing F:**

```text
NICHTUNBEDINGTSICHERGESTELLTXISTNACHMOXG9ICHKEITDORTWIEDERVERKAUFTWERDENXMERCATORKRIEGSAMTKRNEGSROHS4OFFQBTEILUNGXRX138XSTRICHXELFXKRAX
```

</details>

**p152_E_part2**

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
NICHTPNBEDINGTSICHERGESTELLTXISTNACHMOEGLICHKEITDORTWIODERVERKAUFTWERDENXMERCATORKRIEGMAMTKRIEGSROHSTOFFABTEILUNGXRX138VSTRICHXELF8KRAX
```

</details>

## Evidence

At group alignment 210, the fragment and the full record share 88 known symbols, differ at 14, and have 2 erased positions. Restoring the 210-symbol prefix comes from the historical parallel. An exhaustive suffix edit comparison instead has cost 11 and four tied offsets, 211–214, each with 92 known-symbol matches. Neither model establishes a unique historic error sequence.

Three source versions pass exact re-encryption. The complete raw continuation texts, all edits, and both alignment models are in [the certificate](../data/certificates/p152.json). Inspect [p136 B](../sources/excerpts/childs_p136_B.png) and [p152 E](../sources/excerpts/childs_p152_E.png).

The fragment identification and source comparison are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026**. This is the first documented identification of that relationship found in our review of the 2017 discussion and 2026 public work. The published period key retains its [original attribution](../data/keys.json).

# p153a — Earlier orders and unresolved date fields

[All cases](README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Our newly recovered eighteen-column key reads **60 of 66 positions** without changing a source coordinate. This fifth part refers to earlier orders; its date and serial fields remain partly unknown and share unresolved square cells with [part 6](p153b.md).

## Most likely reading

**Readable German — linked unresolved-cell variables; exact variable definitions remain below:**

```text
ANORDNUNGEN VOM <alpha>TEN <beta><beta>TEN NR <gamma><delta><gamma>
BEZIEHEN LASSEN SOWEIT NOCH NICHT GESCHEHEN
```

| Field in the displayed text | Exact unresolved structure | Display rule |
|---|---|---|
| Day-like field | `<alpha>` followed by the known `TEN` | No day value is supplied. |
| Month-like field | `<beta><beta>` followed by the known `TEN` | Both unknown positions are the same cell. |
| Serial-like field | `<gamma><delta><gamma>` | The outer positions are equal; the middle cell is distinct. |

The closing phrase approximately instructs that something be taken up or occupied insofar as this has not already been done. Its object lies in the missing preceding context.

The four variables denote distinct square cells. A date interpretation of the repeated month as `11` would make `<gamma>` different from `1`; the search output's arbitrary `NR121` is not a recovered serial.

### Date and serial: what can be narrowed

Under an ordinary decimal day/month/serial interpretation, the repeated month is **11**. Requiring the order to predate reception on 8 November restricts the day to **2–8**. These assumptions leave **392** assignments if the serial may start with zero, or **343** otherwise.

The `<gamma>` character also occurs in the trailing text of [part 6](p153b.md).
That equality is fixed by the shared square even without a decimal
interpretation. The [linked-field analysis](../experiments/p153_extension/README.md)
records the exact domains and assumptions. A separate
[key-construction investigation](../experiments/p153_key_structure/README.md)
finds that the tested historical conventions and keyword searches cannot
justify filling the missing digits.

## Source

Printed page 153 / PDF page 156, section C5; November 8, 1918.
`FKR v CGH (11.55 p.m.); 2250; 5 TL; CHI-132`. The header means CGH to FKR.
This is part 5 of multipart traffic; [part 6](p153b.md) is also preserved.
No total part count is printed, and parts 1–4 were not located in the inspected
book. The [primary crop](../sources/excerpts/p153_CHI_parts5_6.png) and
[source review](../data/reviews/p153_source_review.json) preserve these limits.

The [header review](../experiments/p153_headers/README.md) covers all 175 printed log pages, 56–230, and finds no further verified FKR/CGH part. Misread or differently headed companions remain possible.

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription:**

```text
VFVAX FXDAD ADVGX FAVGD VDDDA DXGAA AXVGV FVDAD DXADA DVVAV
GFXDA GDDDG DXGGG VVXDX FVVAV VVFAX FXDXA FAVVG GXAVX VFVXV
FGFVA XGAAV XXGDX XFVXF XGGVA DAVAF DG
```

</details>

## Key and verification

The [recovery report](../experiments/p153_recovery/README.md) gives the column
ranks, conservative nineteen-cell square, blind-search lineage and exact
source-coordinate maps. The [certificate](../data/certificates/p153.json)
retains both the raw fitted output and the conservative reading.

Independent [C and Python exhaustive checks](../experiments/p153_crib/README.md) find two equivalent partial-key representations at width 18 for the sixty known letters, leaving the six unresolved positions uncribbed. The [even-width](../experiments/p153_even_widths/README.md) and [odd-width](../experiments/p153_odd_widths/README.md) extensions cover widths 14–26 and 3,492,604 length-class layouts. Only width 18 fits this crib; the uniqueness result is scoped to that model.

## Attribution

[Norbert, September 17, 2017, comment 56](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-918886)
suggested joint and separate attacks on these two CHI fragments without giving
a key or plaintext. The shared key and partial reading were recovered by
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro on 2 November 2026**. This is the **first
documented reconstruction identified in our review** of the literature and
public discussion. The [prior-work audit](../docs/historical-studies/README.md#what-this-edition-contributes)
sets out the reviewed record and the evidence for this attribution.

# p153b — Rearguard artillery ammunition report

[All cases](README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../docs/reading-conventions.md)

The shared key recovered with [part 5](p153a.md) supports an instruction to report the rearguard artillery's ammunition stock. Its nineteen established letter cells fix **33 of 54 raw positions**; the readable reconstruction below requires twelve erased-coordinate fills and two source corrections.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German — conditional on the source repairs and separator interpretation below:**

> Munitionsbestand der Nachhutartillerie melden.

The twelve-position closing remains unidentified. The full template preserves its known labels and linked unknown cells:

**Conditional interpretation — readable reconstruction with AF = X and linked unresolved footer variables:**

```text
MUNITIONSBESTAND DER NACHHUTARTILLERIE MELDEN
X <gamma> X G X R <u><v><w> B X A
```

**Meaning:** Report the ammunition inventory of the rearguard artillery. With the stated body repairs and square cell `AF` interpreted as the separator `X`, the full template fixes **50 of 54 positions**.

The `<gamma>` is the same unresolved character as both outer characters of
the serial in [part 5](p153a.md). The three erased footer positions are coupled:
`u=v` or `v=w` can occur only when both are `G`; `u=w` is otherwise possible.
Even after a date/serial assignment, **2,537** footer triples remain possible. The [linked-field analysis](../experiments/p153_extension/README.md) gives their exact constraints.

## Untouched source and explicit repairs

The conservative raw decode is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
M?N?T?ONSB?S?A?DDERNA?H?UTARTI?G?RIEMEL??????G?R???B?A
```

</details>

The proposed first 42 positions are a **conditional reconstruction**, requiring twelve erased-coordinate fills and
two explicit changes to observed coordinates:

| Source index, zero based | Printed | Proposed | Effect |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 3 | A | X | Raw `G` becomes `L` in `ARTILLERIE` |
| 4 | A | X | Unassigned `AA` cell becomes `E` in `MELDEN` |

Both source glyphs are clearly printed A. Of the coordinates constrained by the proposed body, seventy agree, two require the changes above, and twelve are erased. The remaining three erasures lie in the closing text. The [certificate](../data/certificates/p153.json) records every origin and fill; the separate `AF=X` interpretation supplies four separator positions.

## Source

Printed page 153 / PDF page 156, section C6; November 8, 1918.
`FKR v CGH (11.55 p.m.); 2250; 6 TL; CHI-108`. The header means CGH to FKR.
Parts 5 and 6 survive; the source does not state a total number of parts.

```text
GXFAV VAADA GXXXA XDDGV AVAXV AXAAV VXVAV GXAXX FGXXF AAAFX
VADFD XVF
```

# p158 — Composite routing and key instructions

[Case index](README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../docs/reading-conventions.md)

The historical p158 D record combines portions of two routing instructions under the published **Nov7–9** key. We identified its prefix with p159 B and its suffix with p159 C; repeated transmissions on p168 C/D support the component readings and several source repairs.

## Most likely component readings

**Component B, from the p159/p168 witnesses:**

**Readable German — excerpt of the component reconstruction; bracketed expansions remain editorial:**

> Ueber 2. bayr. Gen.-[Kdo.], [Muenchen], an 7. [unit unclear] Div., [Landsberg an/am Lech]. Nicht durch Kabel. Armeeschluessel [doppelt]. Empfang [bestaetigen]. O.H.L. […] 11338 geh. […]

**Component C, from the p159/p168 witnesses:**

**Readable German — excerpt of the component reconstruction; bracketed expansions remain editorial:**

> Ueber 2. bair. Gen.-Kmd., Muenchen, an 4. bair. Div., [Innsbruck]. Nicht durch [Kabel]. [Armee-CHI] doppelt. Empfang [bestaetigen]. An O.H.L. […]

In both displays, `[…]` omits damaged or unexpanded administrative fields.
The exact component witnesses below retain their labels and positions.

**Meaning:** Route messages through the Bavarian command in Munich, onward to the indicated formations or destinations. Do not use cable transmission; apply the specified army-key treatment and acknowledge receipt.

The place-name expansions, unit labels and administrative fields remain partly conjectural. `Doppelt` concerns the army-key instruction discussed in the historical report below.

| Source layer | Slots | Optimal split | Edit cost |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Typed text | 232 | 130 | 19 |
| Typed text plus handwritten groups | 242 | 130 | 24 |

The 242-slot alignment has 222 exact known-symbol matches. Exhaustive comparison gives a unique split at 130 in the prefix/suffix model, across all eight combinations of source layers and ambiguous glyphs. Treating both glyphs as unknown retains that split, at costs 17 and 22 for the typed and augmented layers. The resulting correspondence identifies the components; the cause of their combination remains unknown.

## Component readings

The p159 B frame has a duplicated five-coordinate group, a missing group, two erased coordinates and a source disagreement. In p159 C, comparison with the repeat reduces a six-coordinate group to five. Three edited component versions re-encrypt exactly using the established square cells, with the digit pair 5/6 unresolved. The [certificate](../data/certificates/p158.json) records the repairs and raw readings.

Sources: [p158 D](../sources/excerpts/childs_p158_D.png), [p159 B/C](../sources/excerpts/childs_p159_BC.png), [p168 C/D](../sources/excerpts/childs_p168_CD.png).

## Raw component witnesses

**p159B_supported_V**

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional component reconstruction with the supported V source reading:**

```text
UEBER2XBAYRXGENXHDOXMUENCXENXXAN7XRSSXDIVXXLA3DSBERGXAN0LECHXXNICHTDURCHKABELXARMEESCHLUESSELDOWPELTXEMPFANGBESTXXOXHXLXRMX1ANRX11338GEHXORX
```

</details>

**p159B_supported_F**

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional component reconstruction with the supported F source reading:**

```text
UEBER2XBAYRXGENXHDOXMUENCXENXXAN7XRSSXDIVXXLA3DSBERGXAN0LECHXXNICHTDURCH1ABELXARMEESCHLUESSELDOWPELTXEMPFANGBESTXXOXHXLXRMX1ANRX11338GEHXORX
```

</details>

**p159C_one_deletion**

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional component frame after its recorded single-coordinate deletion:**

```text
UEBER2XBAIRXGENKMDXMUENCHENAN4XBAIRXDIVXJNSBRUCKXNICHTDURCHKAHELXARMEE0HIDOPPELTXEMPFANGSBESTAETGXANOXHXLXX1A113V7GEHXOPX
```

</details>

## Earlier historical reading of a component

Childs's report dated **20 November 1918**, printed on p42 of *German Military Ciphers from February to November 1918* (1935), deciphers order **11338**. Its SY→RVV via N4 header, 9 November date and 21:03 time agree with the p168 retransmission. [Primary report, p42](https://www.nsa.gov/Portals/75/documents/news-features/declassified-documents/friedman-documents/publications/FOLDER_268/41784789082381.pdf).

The report expands the garbled destination as `LANDWEHR REGIMENT; AN FECH`. The coordinate-derived `LA3DSBERGXAN0LECH` more closely suggests Landsberg an/am Lech; the exact expansion remains editorial. The surrounding report describes a separate **double-transposition army cipher**. It does not establish two complete ADFGVX encipherments.

The component bodies on **p168 C and D** are also discussed by **George Lasry,
Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker** in §6.4 of
[*Deciphering ADFGVX messages from the Eastern Front of World War I*](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
printed p23 / author-PDF p24. That credit also applies to the parallel p159 B/C bodies. Their gloss describes doubled confirmation; the raw text distinguishes the doubled army-key instruction from receipt acknowledgment.

The p158 composite identification and repair audit are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026**. The [historical comparison](../data/reviews/historical_component_prior.json) records the earlier readings.

The [full p168 C witness](radio/p168_munich_routing_witness.md) resolves the six-coordinate/four-coordinate group alignment. Its conditional frame fixes 139/140 raw positions, and an observed `V` from p159 B supplies the last coordinate. Twelve ownership aliases yield the same completed stream. The observed p168 pair `VG = K` also supports `GEN KDO`: adopting its G at p159 source 169 costs one `X→G` substitution, changing the H in `GEN HDO` above.

# p170 — Open short intercept

[All cases](README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** No accepted plaintext. **Current source and attack review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. Original challenge: [Lasry–Schmeh](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/unsolved-adfxvx-messages-from-world-war-i/).

## Most likely reading

No defensible plaintext has yet been identified. The source and the best tested hypotheses are recorded below; no language-ranked diagnostic is promoted to a historical reading.

| Source fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Printed page / PDF page | 170 / 173 |
| Section | A |
| Received slots | 106 |
| Valid coordinates / uncertain slots | 106 / 0 |
| Header | `--- v --- (11.24 p.m., November 9th); RICHI [handwritten 106]` |

## Literal ciphertext

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription:**

```text
AAGVG VVDAG GAGAV AGGAA VAXGV AAAXF AAXAF AGVGV VVVVG DADAF
GDVGV GVGAD XAGAA GXGGA GVFVG XGXAG GGAFA XGFXX AGXVG VFDVX
VDFGX V
```

</details>

The [catalog](../data/messages.json) retains the literal source, conservative analysis layer, and earlier online transcription separately. Headers follow `recipient v sender`.

## Length qualification

All 106 received coordinates are valid and legible. The number **106 is handwritten** beside typed `RICHI`; no transmitted numeric length, part number, or call signs survive. Treating these coordinates as a complete cryptogram is a hypothesis. A longer original with missing beginning or ending remains possible.

## Coordinate-count constraint for a complete body

The source contains only **seven `D` coordinates**. If these 106 coordinates
are a complete 53-character body, the two adjacent dated squares impose the
following necessary bounds, where $n_c$ counts plaintext character $c$:

| Assumed square | Ordinary-letter count bound |
| --- | --- |
| Nov7–9 | $n_A+n_C+n_E+n_G+n_R+n_S+n_Z+2n_L\leq7$ |
| Nov10–12 | $n_A+n_D+n_F+n_G+n_K+n_N+n_O+n_S+n_W+2n_I\leq7$ |

Each character contributes one `D` for row D, one for column D, or two at
DD. Transposition preserves that total, so these bounds allow every column
width, rank and readout direction. The remaining relevant cells are digits:
for Nov7–9, adding $n_0+n_2+n_3$ gives equality; for Nov10–12, the
unassigned digit at FD consumes any remainder. No unresolved digit assignment
can weaken either bound.

The [source-bound evidence record](../experiments/open_targets/p170_coordinate_budget.json)
also compares every 53-character window from the two pinned German books used
in the [p73 count study](../experiments/open_targets/P73_HISTOGRAM.md).
None meets either bound under joined or sentence-X normalization. For actual
operational references, the known ordinary letters in unrestored p155 A1 cost
17–23 Ds per such window under Nov7–9; p179 B costs 21–29 under Nov10–12.
Unknown characters are charged zero. These comparisons are descriptive, not
p-values.

Actual telegrams also show why this is only a necessary condition. The first
53 raw characters of [p121 A1](radio/nov4_repetition_and_connections.md),
which include eleven date and reference digits, cost exactly seven ordinary-letter
Ds under the Nov10–12 square. Seventy-two of that square's 120 digit
completions also give exactly seven Ds in total. This example was actually
received under Nov4–6; it is not a p170 candidate. Its full six-coordinate
histogram would still require at least eighteen substitutions to match p170,
under every completed square and coordinate permutation. Passing one count
bound does not establish ciphertext compatibility.

The book comparison supports lowering the research priority of a complete
body of ordinary German prose under those squares. It **does not exclude either key, prove truncation, or recover
plaintext**. Other squares, unusual vocabulary, numerals, code traffic or
another language remain possible.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the count constraint and reference comparison</summary>

The [verifier](../experiments/open_targets/p170_coordinate_budget.py) binds the
literal source and recorded squares, checks all 122 digit completions, and
independently decrypts the two operational references without coordinate
substitutions. It also checks the numerical p121 example under all 120
Nov10–12 completions. Its default check needs only Python's standard library:

```sh
python experiments/open_targets/p170_coordinate_budget.py
```

To recompute every book window as well, supply the pinned texts in a cache
directory. This uses the existing p73 normalization and requires NumPy:

```sh
python experiments/open_targets/p170_coordinate_budget.py \
  --cache /path/to/heldout-books --download
```

</details>

## Attack status

The [known-key truncation experiment](../experiments/known_key/P170_TRUNCATION_NOTE.md) checked **1,291,584 contiguous placements** across 21 keys and fixed total-length bounds. No plaintext was accepted. Its long-suffix control ranks the planted geometry highly while determining zero plaintext letters, so the search cannot exclude truncation. Upstream training overlap with a control body is disclosed.

Other bounded component searches are described in [the experiment index](../experiments/README.md). A high-scoring German-looking fragment is not treated as a recovered message.

The [completed open-target campaign](../experiments/open_targets/README.md)
adds 35 arbitrary-column-order cases under five anchored squares at widths
16–22, plus independent row/column relabeling under 24 fixed key hypotheses.
No accepted reading emerged. Its fresh relabeling control recovers all 53
plaintext positions, while separate unknown-square component controls fail;
both outcomes remain available. These experiments do not resolve the missing
length and provenance information in the header.

A [direct source-similarity search](../experiments/source_similarity/README.md)
finds only a 20-coordinate local resemblance to p110 C. Image review does not
extend it: fitting the entire 106-coordinate target still costs 58 unit edits.
The search retrieves a deliberately shortened and damaged source control, but
establishes no new p170 parallel in the 788-block OCR corpus.

> An O.H.L. 11. Armee: Alpenkorps, Raum Peterreve–Verbasz. [219.], [217.], [6.] R.D.D., Linie Nagybesskerek–Versecz. Versecz von Serben besetzt.

# p189 — Vehicle request and orders to wait

[Case index](README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** conditional partial source-linked reading of **p189 section A**. **Key:** Nov13–15b. **Contribution:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026, located the clearer p185 C near-parallel and audited all source-preserving alignments.

## Most likely associated message

**Readable German — body excerpt from the associated message; no full p189 recovery asserted:**

> Gestellung [Auto] unmoeglich. Befehl abwarten. […]

**Meaning:** Providing a motor vehicle is impossible; await orders. The final signature or reference is garbled.

**Notes:** This is the most plausible interpretation of the clearer **p185 C near-parallel**, with `AUTU` normalized to `AUTO`. Its application to p189 is conditional on the source relationship. p189 itself does not fix this whole sentence: its exact shared plaintext constraints are retained below. The separate transport conversation strengthens the subject-matter context without filling the challenge's missing coordinates.

The p185 record directly decrypts, without edits, to:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
GESTELLUNGAUTUUNMOEGLICHXBEFEHLABWARTENXIXVRENTE
```

</details>

This approximately says provision of `[AUTU]` is impossible and orders should be awaited. `AUTO` is a plausible interpretation, not a certified substitution. The ending remains garbled.

## What p189 itself supports

The original has 90 slots: 78 valid ADFGVX coordinates, six literal `U` glyphs, one `R`, and five dashes. The online normalization U→V is unsupported. Treating all twelve invalid/erased positions as unknown preserves the actual evidence.

Aligning all 90 source positions monotonically to p185's 96 slots, without deleting or changing any received symbol, gives ten optimal alignments. Each inserts six erased slots and retains fifteen valid-symbol disagreements. Their invariant singleton plaintext is:

**Conditional interpretation — invariant singleton template across the ten stated alignments:**

```text
G??T????N???TOUNUO?GLI?H0B?FEH?ABA??WC?XIX??TN??
```

The shared clear `1835` header and ciphertext similarity support a relationship. Reversed callsign direction and inconsistent reception times prevent treating complete message identity as established. The full p185 reading must not be relabeled as an exact p189 decipherment.

[Certificate](../data/certificates/p189.json) · [p185 C](../sources/excerpts/childs_p185_C.png) · [p189 A](../sources/excerpts/childs_p189_A.png). The verifier recomputes every optimal alignment and all plaintext domains while preserving every received valid coordinate.


## Transport context

[Seven adjacent intercepts and two near-parallel pairs](context/transport.md) now have source transcriptions and direct known-key checks. The p194/p196 transport order can be combined to retain 86 of 87 positions, including `HANAU`, with every chosen source variant recorded. The p185 D missing-group model yields a conditional 91/99-position reading, but its gap location is not cipher-forced. # p198 — Open CHI intercept with a length shortfall

[All cases](README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** No accepted plaintext. **Current source and attack review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. Original challenge: [Lasry–Schmeh](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/unsolved-adfxvx-messages-from-world-war-i/).

## Most likely reading

No defensible plaintext has yet been identified. The source and the best tested hypotheses are recorded below; no language-ranked diagnostic is promoted to a historical reading.

| Source fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Printed page / PDF page | 198 / 201 |
| Section | D |
| Received slots | 165 |
| Valid coordinates / uncertain slots | 165 / 0 |
| Header | `PZU v CM (18.27 p.m., November 15th); 18.45; CHI-170` |

## Literal ciphertext

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription:**

```text
DFVXV XGAXD GXVXD VGVGD VADXF FADVX XXVFV AAXGF DGFFA VXAVV
VXVFV GFVFG DGVFG FFFGV VVGGG XVFXF XXFVD VDFDD FXAAX VVXAA
FXXXV GXFVD VVXXF FGXGV FGXFG GFAAA FGXVV FXXXF FADXD AFXFV
VDGVX FGAGF ADDFX
```

</details>

The [catalog](../data/messages.json) retains the literal source, conservative analysis layer, and earlier online transcription separately. Headers follow `recipient v sender`.

## Length qualification

The header advertises **CHI-170**, while the body contains **165 valid coordinates**. No erased group is explicitly printed. A single five-coordinate loss is a plausible model, but the source does not establish its location or contiguity. Ordinary complete ADFGVX requires an even coordinate count; silent truncation is not accepted.

This challenge target is **section D**. The separately readable
[p198 C transport message](context/transport.md) and the newly linked
[p198 B/E equipment and lorry orders](context/transport_197_198.md) use the
`RIZI` identifier and do not solve this `CHI` entry. Section E contains one
extra five-coordinate group, but moving that group into D is only a tested
corruption hypothesis, not an established source repair.

## Attack status

No accepted plaintext. Bounded missing-group and component-reuse searches preserve the 165 valid coordinates under their declared length hypotheses. [The experiment index](../experiments/README.md) records completed scopes and controls. Unknown keys, noncontiguous losses, other corruption models, and header errors remain unexcluded.

### Exact scattered-loss experiments

The [marginal decoder](../experiments/p198_exact_sparse/README.md) covers all
**1,115,034,284** possible positions of five scattered losses for each supplied
complete key. The [joint decoder](../experiments/p198_joint_exact/README.md)
also chooses their six-valued coordinates consistently, covering
**8,670,506,592,384 loss-and-fill witnesses**. The latter count includes aliases;
it does not count distinct plaintexts.

The recorded historical runs fix one transposition and one heuristic
completion of each of two partial squares. Neither gives a readable result.
The joint four-gram objective also selects wrong plaintexts in both synthetic
controls even when supplied with the true complete keys. The source witnesses,
exact scores and failures are retained. These experiments resolve the search
optimum under their stated assumptions; they do not establish a historical key,
validate the damage model, or solve p198.

The [six-gram calibration](../experiments/p198_joint_six/README.md) does recover
one complete 85-position control, including its exact loss mask and fills, under
both pure-six and mixed objectives. A feasible wrong competitor still beats
the other control's truth under both objectives. This improves the demonstrated
capability of the method while preserving its remaining scoring limitation.

The subsequent [historical pure-six run](../experiments/p198_six_historical/README.md)
under the frozen CHI13 completion changes the best geometry and improves its
six-gram objective, but the full result remains unreadable. At that selected
geometry, the conservative partial square has 48 singleton positions; this is
a conditional diagnostic, not 48 newly recovered plaintext positions. The report keeps
the entire model output and its disagreements with four-gram ranking.

### Exact constraints without a language model

An independent [letter-count bound](../experiments/p198_letter_bounds/README.md)
covers **all 40,320 completions** of the partial Nov13–15b square, with its
recorded transposition and every five-loss placement/fill. The attainable
ordinary-letter counts range from 44 to 82, so this family requires at least
three digits among the 85 plaintext positions. This is a modest exact
constraint without a language model; the actual message's digit count is
unknown, so it does not reject the key.

A stronger [category audit](../experiments/p198_letter_bounds/CATEGORY_BOUNDS.md)
gives `digits + Q + Y ≥ 10` throughout the same partial-key family. If a proposed
plaintext contains no Q or Y, it must therefore contain at least ten digits;
a witness attains that bound. A separate Python algorithm factors the problem
into adjacent-column pairs and fully recomputes the optimum, independently of
the original C++ decoder. Neither inequality assumes that the historical text
had a particular digit or Q/Y count.

The complete [digit/Q/Y frontier](../experiments/p198_category_frontier/README.md)
sharpens those separate inequalities. The following count pairs are attainable,
and every other attainable pair has at least as many digits and Q/Y positions
as one of these:

| Digit positions | Minimum Q/Y positions at that digit count |
|---:|---:|
| 3 | 13 |
| 4 | 6 |
| 5 | 5 |
| 6 | 4 |
| 7 | 3 |
| 8 | 2 |
| 9 | 1 |
| 10 | 0 |

Thus **three digits force at least thirteen Q/Y occurrences**, rather than
the seven allowed by the separate inequalities alone. Every frontier point
has a complete source-preserving witness. Two separate algorithms exhaust
all 28 letter/digit membership classes and their 15,504 loss allocations;
285,264 short exhaustive witnesses include an explicit control with two
incomparable count pairs. Different points may require different square
completions. These exact counts constrain future proposals within this
family; they do not supply a readable historical message or reject the key.

### Conditional restriction from an independently attested name

The [Tiflis appointment](other/tiflis_appointment.md) supplies a separate
historical-name argument for **Nov13–15b FX = Y**. If that inference and the
Nov13b/five-loss hypothesis for p198 are both accepted, the exact family
shrinks to 5,040 complete squares. Its digit/QY frontier is
`(4,6), (5,5), (6,4), (7,3), (8,2), (10,1), (13,0)`.
Thus at least four digits are required, or at least thirteen if the reading
contains no Q or Y. The [conditional certificate](../experiments/contextual_key_constraints/README.md)
preserves all received coordinates, supplies witnesses for every frontier
point, and independently recomputes all seven retained membership classes.
Neither the historical counts nor this key's applicability to p198 are
established. No plaintext position becomes fixed from this count result.

### Why individual positions remain open

For either frozen complete-key hypothesis, **each of the 85 positions can
contain any of the 36 alphabet symbols in some compatible five-loss witness**.
The construction marks that position's two ciphertext coordinates as lost,
puts the remaining three losses elsewhere, and fills the selected pair with
the desired character. Every received coordinate still appears unchanged and
in order.

The [constructive domain audit](../experiments/p198_letter_bounds/domain_witnesses.json)
checks all **6,120** key/position/symbol witnesses and exact re-encryption.
Each choice can use a different witness; arbitrary choices at all positions
need not coexist in one plaintext. That is why full individual domains can
coexist with the joint requirement of at least three digits. Additional source
evidence about the missing positions could narrow those domains.

```sh
python3 experiments/p198_letter_bounds/domain_witnesses.py --verify
```

The [direct source-similarity search](../experiments/source_similarity/README.md)
also checks all 788 extracted OCR blocks. Its leading p198 candidate is p154 A2;
independent page inspection confirms only a short local resemblance and does
not establish a parallel transmission.

# p215 — Entente fleet report and Corps Kosch interpretation

[Case index](README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** Earlier partial reading verified exactly; the conditional closing interpretation identifies Corps Kosch. Shared numeral and letter hypotheses narrow the `?1?6` ending to **56 globally consistent values**, including 42 all-numerical values. The opening remains unresolved. **Key:** `Nov22-24`.

**Earliest credited record:** [Norbert, 2017-03-03, comment 32](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-853562). **Current source and arithmetic review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026.

## Most likely partial interpretation

**Readable German — earlier partial interpretation under the stated geometry:**

> […] [Kertsch]. Bringt [Ententeflotte] zwo [Divisionen] — [Neuseelaender],
> Engl. u. [Franzo] — mit. [Nur] OHL, [Korps Kosch]. 3Y52.

**Meaning:** The damaged report connects Kerch with an Entente fleet bringing two divisions, described as New Zealanders, English and French. The closing words may restrict circulation to the Supreme Army Command and Corps Kosch. This translates the proposed report; it does not establish that those troops actually arrived or that its nationalities and numbers were accurate. The opening remains unresolved. The closing field has baseline labels `3Y52`; the separate historical numeral hypothesis below gives `?1?6`, without identifying a particular reference number.

**Notes:** Brackets mark interpretations requiring fills or changed known coordinates; all punctuation is editorial. `Franzo` remains an abbreviation. The proposed 92-character segment from `KERTSCH` through the separator after `KOSCH` needs **nine known-coordinate changes and fifteen fills** under Norbert's two-gap geometry. Eight fills concern printed erasures and seven concern the inserted gaps. This is a narrower, explicitly costed proposal, not a repair of the whole message.

### Why Corps Kosch is the preferred closing interpretation

| Reading of raw `KOR1S??OSCH` | Known-coordinate changes | Erasure fills |
|---|---:|---:|
| `KORPSXKOSCH` | 2 | 2 |
| Earlier `KORPSFRISCH` | 5 | 2 |

The Kosch reading changes original coordinate 22 from `X` to `V` and 193 from
`D` to `X`, then fills two inserted gaps. The proposed separator is outside
the raw letter domain; it is not supplied merely by choosing an erased symbol.
A 29 April 1918 naval directive identifies Kosch as German commander in Crimea,
and Hopman's November diary places him in the same operational setting.
The [coordinate and historical review](../experiments/p215_context/README.md)
gives the exact maps, primary-document references and remaining limits.

Baertl's earlier full proposal still requires at least **27** changes to known
coordinates, even after optimizing its extra-position deletion and insertion
geometry. The separately retained language-ranked completions are compatible
with the source under their stated model; they do not recover new historical
letters.

## Separate late-key numeral interpretation

The [source-reviewed p217 operational report](other/p217_A.md) and contemporary formation evidence support a consistent optional Nov22–24 map: baseline `Y→1`, `J→2`, `2→6`. Applying exactly that map here gives **`?1?6`** at the end, with no change to a received coordinate or to Norbert’s gap geometry. The other unproved digit and rare-letter labels are cleared before this map is applied, preserving a single injective square.

More precisely, the ending is `a1b6`, with different `a` and `b` from `0345789JQY`. All **90** combinations have source-preserving global witnesses. An additional all-numerical-reference assumption leaves **42** candidates, allowing a leading zero. This does not select a serial number or fill any of the 21 unknown coordinates. The [propagation certificate](../experiments/late_key_interpretation/README.md) retains the original baseline output, the conditional domains and the exact source indices.

**Shared-letter refinement:** The later [J inference](../experiments/nov22_nikolajew_constraint/README.md) reduces those 90 values to 72. A new [Hungarian place-spelling constraint](../experiments/p215_hungarian_y/README.md) assigns DD, baseline `4`, to Y: operational p217 A3 has observed `POEST4EN`, and p215 B2 has two observed DD pairs in its inherited `NAG4BANHEG4ES` word proposal. Contemporary directories attest Pöstyén and Nagybánhegyes. The spellings support this shared-cell hypothesis without establishing the reports' historical content.

Combining both letter hypotheses with the numeral layer leaves distinct `a,b` from **`0345789Q`**, hence **56** endings. The all-numerical subset remains **42**; Y alone would give 72. Every ending has a full injective-square witness shared across 26 physical bodies and 61 source/word variants. No observed coordinate changes. The opening's resulting `SYN` and `SY?` fields remain unidentified, and all 21 unknown coordinates remain unfilled. This refinement is by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

## Recomputed reading

Variant `norbert32`: Exact published partial geometry; no inserted coordinate is guessed.

<details>
<summary>Recomputed earlier reading</summary>

**Recomputed prior reading — under the recorded variant and repairs:**

```text
ABSXMI?I5XNA6M?LD?XS4NXS4?XN?R?DAKER?SC?XBRINGTENT?N?EFLHTTEZWO?IVI?IONENX?EUSRELAEND?RXENGLXUXF?ATZ?XMITXN??OHLXKOR1S??OSCHX3Y52
```

</details>

## Review

- The primary 248-slot transcript has 237 known coordinates and 11 erasures. Two inserted unknown groups increase the geometry to 258 slots.
- The model fixes 109 of 129 plaintext positions and leaves 6^21 compatible completions under the fixed complete square.
- Baertl's 130-position editorial text has the wrong length for this geometry. Even its best single-position deletion contradicts 27 known coordinates at 20 plaintext positions.

## Earlier published readings

**Partial raw decryption — [Norbert, 2017-03-03, comment 32](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-853562).**

Same text as the recomputed reading above.

**Editorial completion — [Max Baertl, 2017-03-11, comment 39](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-858010).**

<details>
<summary>Earlier attributed reading</summary>

**Earlier attributed reading:**

```text
ABSXMIDIV5XEILMELDGX24NX24NXARMADAKERTSCHXBRINGTENTENTEFLOTTEZWODIVISIONENXNEUSEELAENDERXENGLXUXFRANZOXMITXNUROHLXKORPSFRISCHX3Y52
```

</details>

Published length 130; model length 129.

## Verified variants

| Variant | Fixed / total positions | Unpaired suffix | Ordinary re-encryption |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `norbert32` | 109 / 129 | — | Partial |

Source strings, edit positions, plaintext domains and attribution are retained in [the prior-reading certificate](../data/prior_readings.json). Re-encryption checks the stated reconstruction, including any conjectural repairs.

## Full uncertainty audit

The [p215 constraint certificate](../data/certificates/p215.json) verifies all 21 unresolved coordinates under the two-group insertion model. It yields exactly **21,936,950,640,377,856** compatible plaintexts. Exhaustively deleting each possible single plaintext position from Baertl's longer wording still requires at least **27 changes to received coordinates**, affecting **20 plaintext positions**. Run `python3 -m adfgvx.constraints215` to reproduce the comparison.

Source: [Childs p215 C](../sources/excerpts/childs_p215_C.png).

## Source-compatible model completions

The [exact completion experiment](../experiments/p215_completion/README.md) retains the ten highest-ranked strings under each of three language objectives. All thirty preserve every one of the 237 known source coordinates under Norbert's two-gap geometry. These are conditional completions, not recovered historical letters; the source still permits 6^21 strings.

The [broader insertion-geometry audit](../experiments/p215_completion/README.md#broader-audit-of-the-earlier-editorial-text)
shows that the best one-position deletion of Baertl's completion still needs at
least 27 known-coordinate changes even when all ten inserted coordinates may
be placed anywhere. This strengthens the earlier fixed-gap comparison without
accepting a different plaintext or corruption model.

# p217 — Allied naval arrivals at Sevastopol

[Case index](README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** Earlier 2026 body reproduced exactly; later one-symbol 24STEN correction independently verified. **Key:** `TRUPPENVERSCHIEBUNG`.

**Earliest credited record:** [Prinz and GPT-6 Astra, 2026-09-17](https://www.prinzai.com/p/gpt-6-astra-solves-a-wwi-german-radio). **Current source and arithmetic review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026.

The raw body and keyword were published by Prinz with GPT-6 Astra on 17 September 2026. The version below includes Christian Horvat's 21 September correction.

## Most likely reading

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the recorded prior repair and digit hypothesis:**

> Ein englischer Kreuzer [einlief] Sewastopol [24.]sten. Ein Geschwader der Alliierten folgt 26.sten.

**Meaning:** A British cruiser arrived at Sevastopol on the 24th; an Allied squadron follows on the 26th.

**Notes:** `EINLIEG` is read editorially as `EINLIEF`. The date 24 combines Horvat's one-coordinate correction with the reported square assignment `AX=4`; the more conservative square leaves that digit as 4 or 8. Contemporary naval records support the 24/26 November interpretation independently. This historical corroboration does not authenticate the separately reported key manuscript.

## Recomputed reading

Variant `horvat2026_24sten`: One known-symbol correction suggested in prior published commentary.

<details>

- This conservative layer reads `S?STEN`, or `2?STEN` after Horvat's coordinate repair. The repair does not independently resolve the second digit.
- The claimed 1919 manuscript and December 9 key attribution were reported by the 2026 author. This audit verifies arithmetic and attested cells, not the unexamined manuscript provenance.
- Christian Horvat suggested the AVXFF→AVXVF correction in a 2026-09-21 comment on the September 19 follow-up article. Under the reported `AX=4` assignment, it changes `S4STEN` to `24STEN`.

**Raw decryption — [Prinz and GPT-6 Astra, 2026-09-17](https://www.prinzai.com/p/gpt-6-astra-solves-a-wwi-german-radio).**


</details>

| Variant | Fixed / total positions | Unpaired suffix | Ordinary re-encryption |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Source-crop-conservative square | 84 / 85 | — | Partial |
| `prinz2026_source_exact` (`AX=4`) | 85 / 85 | — | Yes |

## Independent historical context

[Hopman's contemporary diary](../data/reviews/hopman_context.json), published in an edited primary-source volume, records Canterbury at Sevastopol on November 24 and the Allied squadron on November 26. This independently corroborates the existing Prinz/Horvat interpretation alongside the British ship logs. It does not authenticate the separately reported key manuscript.

The Australian War Memorial also preserves a [24 November fleet memorandum](https://transcribe.awm.gov.au/transcription/item/rcdig0000179-4)
recording the advance ships' departure on 23 November and the main fleet's

[source review](../experiments/p215_context/README.md#what-the-documents-support)

cases/p73.md.text:
# p73 — Open message for General von Kress

[All cases](README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** No accepted plaintext. **Current source and attack review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. Original challenge: [Lasry–Schmeh](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/unsolved-adfxvx-messages-from-world-war-i/).

## Most likely reading

No defensible plaintext has yet been identified. The source and the best tested hypotheses are recorded below; no language-ranked diagnostic is promoted to a historical reading.

| Source fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Printed page / PDF page | 73 / 76 |
| Section | A |
| Received slots | 178 |
| Valid coordinates / uncertain slots | 176 / 2 |
| Header | `POT v NKJ (2.33 a.m., November 8th); FUR COS GENERAL VON KRESS 0911 (26); RICHI-178` |

## Literal ciphertext

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription:**

```text
D--FX GDVDX DGGAA AGFFD DVDXF XFGGD DAVGD DDADG DGFGG DDVVD
XDGDA FDDXG XXDGX AVDXX DDGAD DFGFA GVDXV FDXFD DFDDD FXDFG
XFXVF DDDXX DXGDA GXFDG DDVFX GAXDF VFDVD XVXDF XDDXF DFVDG
FDGDA DGDGX XFGXF AAAXX XDXAG VXD
```

</details>

The [catalog](../data/messages.json) retains the literal source, conservative analysis layer, and earlier online transcription separately. Headers follow `recipient v sender`.

## Source context

The page heading says **October 26**, the clear header contains `0911 (26)`, and the interception line says **November 8 at 02:33**. Norbert raised the conflict in 2017; Lasry left it unresolved. Neither date is silently corrected.

The [p155 companion](context/p155.md) has the same `POT v NKJ` route onward to General von Kress, was intercepted five minutes earlier, and explicitly carries origin day 7. Its readable shipping message is independently corroborated in Hopman's diary. Reception proximity does not prove a shared encryption date or key.

The bounded original-book search found no additional clearly dated October 25–27 ciphertext or period key. The [source-context record](../data/reviews/p73_source_context.json) documents the inspected pages, earlier observations, delayed-telegram context, and unretrieved archive leads.

A further [primary-source check](../experiments/p73_primary_followup/README.md)
inspected the accessible late-period Kress memoir, the October/November tail of
Lepsius's 1919 diplomatic edition, and the institutional Kress-name retrieval
in the Hopman edition. No matching incoming radiogram was found in those
bounded scopes. The superficially matching October 26 / November 8 dates in
the memoir's editorial introduction refer to **1917**, so they add no evidence
for p73's 1918 calendar or encryption date.

The [archival access follow-up](../experiments/p73_primary_followup/ARCHIVE_ACCESS.md)
confirms that the official inventory lists RZ 201 as digitized and gives
concrete catalogue searches for the older file-number leads. No individual
record or telegram image was retrieved; those leads remain uninspected.

## A clue independent of column order

![p73 coordinate counts and held-out German reference means](../experiments/open_targets/p73_coordinate_profile.svg)

The [coordinate-count analysis](../experiments/open_targets/P73_HISTOGRAM.md)
tests a property that every column transposition preserves. Under the published
Nov7–9 square, all **26 observed F coordinates** must belong to `CJMOQZ` or
digits. Even the most favorable fill of the two erasures is farther from the
reference mean than every tested 89-character window in two independent war
books, under joined-text and sentence-separator conventions. The readable
p155 A1 companion lies within the observed range for those conventions.

The opposite side of the histogram gives another exact constraint. The 15
observed `V` coordinates plus two erasures imply

\[
n_D+n_E+n_H+n_K+n_Q+n_T+n_U+2n_X\leq17,
\]

where `n` counts plaintext characters. Thus at most eight `X` characters can
occur. A candidate containing five `X` separators could contain at most seven
of `DEHKQTU` combined. This provides a direct check on future proposed cribs,
independent of column order and the unresolved 5/6 assignment.

This supports lowering the priority of Nov7–9 square reuse under ordinary
German prose assumptions. It does **not** exclude the key or choose between
the conflicting dates. The report preserves both possible 5/6 assignments,
all count completions, and a word-separator convention that fails the historical
control. Atypical digits, names, abbreviations or code groups remain possible.

## Attack status

No accepted plaintext. Known-key, transcription-geometry, and component searches remain bounded hypotheses. The [experiment index](../experiments/README.md) separates completed coverage and calibration failures from exclusion claims. A longer companion under the original key remains the most useful missing evidence.

A [direct source-similarity search](../experiments/source_similarity/README.md)
over 788 OCR blocks retrieves established parallels as controls. The leading
p73 candidate, p105 C1, was checked against the page image and supplies only
a short local resemblance, not another transmission of this message.
