# A staff officer's assignment to Breslau [Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md) **Source edition and recovery: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** A two-part personnel order assigns a staff officer to special employment with a corps command at Breslau, says that he has already been ordered directly, and requests notification to another corps command. Its name, rank and formation fields contain raw published-square labels whose historical interpretation is kept separate from the ordinary-word reading. The later [Article XII numeral interpretation](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/README.md) reads the addressee as `AOK11`, using the two received `FX` pairs without source changes. Together with the earlier `VD=J` letter interpretation, the opening addresses the 11th Army command and identifies the officer's rank as Major. A further shared **`AD=Y`** assignment now supports the surname **Strzemieczny**, also completing the place name **Nagymágocs** in a different telegram. The previous corps numbers remain unresolved. ## Conditional reading **Readable German — shared letter and numeral interpretation, with the same nine observed-coordinate word repairs:** > AOK 11. Major beauftragt mit Wahrnehmung der Geschaefts des Chef des Generalst. ?? Res. K. Strzemieczny ist unter Versetzung zu den Offizieren V. D. A. dem Generalkdo. 6 A. K. Breslau zu bes. Verwendung zugeteilt, ist unmittelbar beordert. Mitteilung an Generalkdo. ?? AK erbeten. Chef des Generalstabs d. Feldheeres. ???2?. The order concerns Major Strzemieczny's assignment to special employment with the VI Army Corps command at Breslau. The reserve-corps and second command numbers, as well as most of the closing reference, stay unknown. The [joint surname and place check](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/README.md#the-shared-y-in-strzemieczny-and-nagymagocs) adds no coordinate repair. It identifies the spelling of the surname, without establishing the officer's given name or service record. ## Source and earlier edition The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed p224 C, PDF p227. The header reads `UKS v BSL (00.13 a.m., November 28th)`, followed by the undated origin time `2230`. A preceding page subheading says November 26. The edition preserves those printed dates without inferring an original sending date. All 558 coordinates are valid and the lengths match `RICHI-260` and `RICHI-298` exactly. The [literal source edition](../../experiments/breslau_staff_transfer/inputs.json) includes enlarged crops for ambiguous-looking `G` glyphs. The [certificate](../../experiments/breslau_staff_transfer/certificates.json) uses the unchanged published `Nov25-28` square and records every repair and every numeral or `J/Q/Y` occurrence. Both bodies had already appeared as unreviewed OCR-derived entries in [`p73_new_methods/retrieval_inputs.json`](../../experiments/p73_new_methods/retrieval_inputs.json). The contribution here is their visually checked transcription, exact source mapping, priced ordinary-word edition and separated historical context, rather than first computation of those candidates. ## C1: the officer and his previous function The raw 130-position reading is:
Raw decoded text **Raw output:** ```text AOKJJXXMA9ORBEAUFTRAGTMITWAHRNEHMUNG0ERGESCHAEFT9DESCHEFDESGENERALSTX40XRESXKXXSTRZEMIECZNQISTUNTERVERSETZUNGZUDENOFFIZIERENVXDXAX ```
Three observed-coordinate substitutions repair the ordinary words `0ER` to `DER` and `GESCHAEFT9` to `GESCHAEFTS`:
Proposed text and exact labels **Edited output:** ```text AOKJJXXMA9ORBEAUFTRAGTMITWAHRNEHMUNGDERGESCHAEFTSDESCHEFDESGENERALSTX40XRESXKXXSTRZEMIECZNQISTUNTERVERSETZUNGZUDENOFFIZIERENVXDXAX ```
The text addresses `AOKJJ` and describes the officer as acting in the capacity of chief of the general staff of the reserve corps labelled `40 RES K`. His received surname is `STRZEMIECZNQ`. He is being transferred to the category of officers designated `V. D. A.`; the destination and special employment follow in C2. The token `MA9OR` is consistent with an intended military rank, but the edition does not select a global interpretation of raw `9`. In particular, the same unchanged square cell also appears in the garbled `GESCHAEFT9`. That second occurrence receives its own explicit coordinate repair; a rank-based relabelling must not conceal its different ordinary-word role. The surname's final `Q`, the two `J` army labels and the `40` formation labels are all retained. ## C2: special employment with the Breslau command The raw 149-position reading is:
Raw decoded text **Raw output:** ```text DEMGENERALKDOX7XAXKXBRESLAUZUBESXVERWENDUNGZUGETEILTISTUNMITTELBARBEORDERTXMITTEOLUNGANGENREALKDOX40AKEGBETENXXXCHEFDESGENERALSTABSDXFELDHEERES04013X ```
Six observed-coordinate changes restore `MITTEILUNG`, `GENERAL` in the second command reference, and `ERBETEN`:
Proposed text and exact labels **Edited output:** ```text DEMGENERALKDOX7XAXKXBRESLAUZUBESXVERWENDUNGZUGETEILTISTUNMITTELBARBEORDERTXMITTEILUNGANGENERALKDOX40AKERBETENXXXCHEFDESGENERALSTABSDXFELDHEERES04013X ```
The officer is assigned to special employment with the command labelled `7 A K`, Breslau. He has already been ordered directly, and notification to the command labelled `40 A K` is requested. The signature reads `CHEF DES GENERALSTABS D. FELDHEERES`, followed by raw `04013`. The source's `40AK` is not silently changed to match the earlier `40 RES K` designation. Immediately after the final three-letter ciphertext group `XDV`, the page carries a cleartext fragment beginning `VON LP AN CO`. It is outside this part's 298-coordinate length and is excluded from the ciphertext transcription and from the count of recovered encrypted records. ## Three untouched fields useful for separate interpretation | Field | Plaintext index | Pair | Original source indices | | --- | ---: | --- | --- | | C1, the `9` of `MA9OR` | 9 | `VD` | 125, 79 | | C1, final `Q` of `STRZEMIECZNQ` | 90 | `AD` | 86, 210 | | C2, `7` before `A K BRESLAU` | 14 | `GA` | 247, 1 | These zero-based source positions are complete observed pairs and are unchanged by every ordinary-word repair. The certificate lists all other numeral and `J/Q/Y` positions as well: **16 physical source occurrences**, with **14** remaining in the ordinary-word candidates. The two removed occurrences are the separately repaired `0ER` and `GESCHAEFT9`. ### The VI Army Corps command in November 1918 *Der Gebirgsbote*, no. 129, **13 November 1918**, p1, publishes joint orders of the Breslau soldiers council and the deputy general command of **VI Army Corps**, dated Breslau, **11 November 1918**. The [original scan](https://bibliotekacyfrowa.pl/Content/60534/PDF/directory.pdf), [masthead](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/sources/gebirgsbote_1918_129_title.png) and [decree crop](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/sources/breslau_vi_corps_nov11.png) place that command in Breslau during the month of the intercept. The command signs through Freiherr von Egloffstein; Voigt and Berg sign for the soldiers council. Identifying the telegram's Breslau recipient with this command gives `6XAXKXBRESLAU` from the received pairs. The [optional `GA=6` layer](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/breslau_certificate.json) propagates that identification through the same 23-record set without source changes. It also gives `6?` for the first German-bank mark amount in the [lei-redemption proposal](../finance/lei_note_exchange.md). The earlier [July 1917 decree](../../experiments/boots_request/breslau_context/source.json) provided the initial institutional lead. The November source supplies the closer dated witness; neither decree identifies the officer named in p224. ### The surname and the shared Y cell The original `AD` pair at C1 position 90, source positions **86 and 210**, gives `STRZEMIECZNQ` under the published labels. The optional assignment `AD=Y` gives **`STRZEMIECZNY`** without changing either observed coordinate. The spelling is visible in *Schlesische Zeitung*, 172nd year, no. 337, morning edition, **17 May 1913**, PDF page 6: an officer-awards notice names a captain von Strzemieczny of Infantry Regiment 143. [Institutional scan](https://bibliotekacyfrowa.pl/Content/139045/GSL_P_31292_IV_1913_26511_337.pdf) · [Masthead](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/sources/schlesische_1913_title.png) · [Printed name](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/sources/strzemieczny_1913_military.png). This supplies image evidence beyond the earlier [*Reichsanzeiger* OCR lead](https://digi.bib.uni-mannheim.de/reichsanzeiger/ocr/film/tesseract-4.0.0-20181201/126-9532/0243.hocr) recorded in the original [historical-context file](../../experiments/breslau_staff_transfer/historical_context.json). The 1913 captain is not identified here with the 1918 major. The same unchanged pair completes `NAGYMAGOCS` in the [p220 evening report](../military/nov25_provisions_and_evening_report.md#p220-b). Across **33 reviewed records**, four native `AD` occurrences include these two names and the earlier damaged `VORQELEGT` and `EINQIGES`; their separate word repairs are retained. With the earlier conditional assignments, the shared Y reduces **362,880 to 40,320** possible complete squares. The [certificate](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/names_certificate.json) keeps both supporting pairs, both inconvenient occurrences and all earlier source costs. ## Scope, credit and reproduction The published period square fixes all **279 raw-label positions** in the two parts. The candidates make **nine** observed-coordinate substitutions and reencrypt exactly. There are no missing-coordinate fills, source erasure fills, deletions or reordered blocks. These counts are not a claim that 279 previously unknown key symbols have been solved or that every raw numerical label has its intended historical value. Published key provenance is preserved. Lasry and colleagues explicitly cite the neighboring p224 A message; no explicit discussion of C was located in the bounded paper/dissertation/comment check. The prior repository OCR candidates are separately credited, and no universal historical-priority claim is made. ```bash python experiments/breslau_staff_transfer/verify.py --verify python experiments/breslau_staff_transfer/verify.py --verify \ --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf --historical-pdf /path/to/waldenburg_1917.pdf ``` The verifier reconstructs the column mapping independently, checks every plaintext position and exact repair, audits the complete label inventory, and confirms that the three interpretation fields remain untouched. The PDF options verify both full source hashes and all retained crop pixels.

# German civilians in Constantinople: an enquiry and a diplomatic appeal

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and recovery: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

A four-part enquiry asks whether German civilians, principally women and
children, have departed from Constantinople, where they have gone and what
is known of them. It asks for verification through the Swedish legation
and for reports on troop transports. It then says that the request to
permit German civilians to remain in Turkey has been put before the
Allies and the Supreme War Council in Paris, and that transport through
Ukraine is currently impossible.

The headcount is preserved as the published square's literal labels
**`0YY`**. No conventional numerical value is assigned. The source treats
the departure as a report requiring confirmation; its occurrence is not
established by this enquiry.

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX
Cipher System*, printed p221 B, PDF p224. The page heading is November 25,
1918; the message header reads `XYZ v LP (06.14 a.m., November 26th)`,
`1300 (25/11)`, `4 TLE`. The
[literal edition](../../experiments/constantinople_civilians/inputs.json)
and [exact certificates](../../experiments/constantinople_civilians/certificates.json)
retain all glyphs, source mappings, frame alternatives and coordinate
repairs. The published `Nov25-28` square and transposition are unchanged.

## B1: reports of civilians leaving Constantinople

The first part advertises 298 coordinates but prints **297**. The source
has a four-letter `ADDG` group at positions 225–228. Inserting an erased
coordinate at boundary 227 gives this 149-position raw reading:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional insertion at source boundary 227 in the short group:**

```text
ANDEUTSCHENGESCHAEFTSTRAEGERKONSTANTINOPELXHIERVORLIEGENMELDUNGENWONACH0YYDEUTSCHEZI?ILPERSONENHAUPTSAECHLICHXRAUENKINDERVONDORTHIERHERABGEREISTSINDX
```

</details>

One observed-coordinate change, `XRAUEN` to `FRAUEN`, and filling the
missing coordinate for `ZIVILPERSONEN` give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional insertion model, with the stated repair and fill:**

```text
ANDEUTSCHENGESCHAEFTSTRAEGERKONSTANTINOPELXHIERVORLIEGENMELDUNGENWONACH0YYDEUTSCHEZIVILPERSONENHAUPTSAECHLICHFRAUENKINDERVONDORTHIERHERABGEREISTSINDX
```

</details>

Addressed to the German chargé d'affaires at Constantinople, the text
says that reports received at the sender's end describe German civilians,
mainly women and children, departing from there toward the sender. The
reported number has the raw labels `0YY`.

The geometry is not selected to obtain that quantity. The certificate
checks all **298 insertion boundaries**, masking all three headcount
positions. Boundary **227** uniquely minimizes ordinary-word changes at
one observed substitution; the next-best boundaries require two. All
three headcount characters then come from complete, unchanged observed
coordinate pairs:

| Plaintext position | Pair | Original source indices | Raw label |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 71 | `AF` | 123, 251 | `0` |
| 72 | `DG` | 6, 200 | `Y` |
| 73 | `DG` | 226, 84 | `Y` |

The earlier OCR-based fit `0Y5` depended on a different missing-coordinate
placement. The source-supported ordinary-word optimum gives `0YY`, with
its repeated final pair made explicit. The source edition supplies those
pairs, not their conventional numerical interpretation.

## B2: verification through the Swedish legation

This part advertises 344 coordinates and prints **345 slots**. Its
six-letter group `AXDGXF` occupies source positions 130–135. Removing
source index 134, the second `X`, gives:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional deletion of the second X at source index 134:**

```text
BITTEDURCHVERMITTELUNGSCHWEDISCHERGESANDTSCHAFTDRAHTENOBMELDUNGZUTREFFENDWANNUNDWOHINABREISEERFOLGTXW6SUEBERVERBLEIBBEKANNTISTUNDUMWELCHEKA?EGORIENNUNPERSONENESSICHHANDELTX
```

</details>

The question mark comes from the printed dash in `A-FGA`, source index
207. Four observed-coordinate substitutions and one erased-coordinate
fill produce:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional deletion model, with the stated substitutions and dash fill:**

```text
BITTEDURCHVERMITTELUNGSCHWEDISCHERGESANDTSCHAFTDRAHTENOBMELDUNGZUTREFFENDWANNUNDWOHINABREISEERFOLGTXWASUEBERVERBLEIBBEKANNTISTUNDUMWELCHEKATEGORIENVONPERSONENESSICHHANDELTX
```

</details>

The sender asks for a telegraphic report through the Swedish legation:
is the report correct, when and to where did the departure occur, what is
known of the people's whereabouts, and which categories of people are
involved?

All **345 possible single-coordinate deletions** are checked against the
same declared ordinary-word stencil. Source index **134** is the unique
minimum at four observed substitutions. The source erasure is priced
separately, and its removal is not used to conceal an extra coordinate.
The received `W6S` and `NUNPERSONEN` remain visible in the raw layer.

## B3: troop transports and the request to remain in Turkey

The third part has exactly **348 slots**. Its invalid `Y` in `DGADY`,
source index 319, remains an erasure. The raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
BITTEFERNERDRAHTEN?EBERSTANDDERTRUPPENTRANSPORTEUNDALLGEMEINELZGEDERDEUTSCHENI8DERTUERKEIX0NSERERSUCHENUMBELASSUNGDERDEUTSCHENZIVILPERSONENINDERTUERKEIISTVONPRAESIDENTWILSONX
```

</details>

Three observed-coordinate changes and the erased-coordinate fill give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
BITTEFERNERDRAHTENUEBERSTANDDERTRUPPENTRANSPORTEUNDALLGEMEINELAGEDERDEUTSCHENINDERTUERKEIXUNSERERSUCHENUMBELASSUNGDERDEUTSCHENZIVILPERSONENINDERTUERKEIISTVONPRAESIDENTWILSONX
```

</details>

The sender also requests the status of troop transports and the general
situation of Germans in Turkey. Its request for German civilians to be
allowed to remain there has, it says, been acted on by President Wilson;
the sentence continues in the next part. The raw `LZGE`, `I8` and `0NSER`
are repaired at explicit source coordinates. They are not silently
relabelled as global square values.

## B4: referral to the Allies and the route through Ukraine

The last part advertises 266 coordinates but prints **265 valid
coordinates**. The visibly deficient group is `XDXG`, source positions
190–193. Constraining the missing coordinate to that group gives its best
fit at boundary **190**. This primary, source-local model reads:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional missing-slot placement at source boundary 190:**

```text
DENALLWEERTENUNDDEMOBERKRWEGSR6TINPARISVORQELEGTWORDE?XBEFOERDERUNGDERZIVILPERSONENDURCHXUKRAINEXZURZELTUNMYEGLICHXXYUSWAERTIGBERLINX
```

</details>

Nine observed-coordinate changes and one missing-coordinate fill support:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional missing-slot frame, with the stated repairs and fill:**

```text
DENALLIIERTENUNDDEMOBERKRIEGSRATINPARISVORGELEGTWORDENXBEFOERDERUNGDERZIVILPERSONENDURCHXUKRAINEXZURZEITUNMOEGLICHXXAUSWAERTIGBERLINX
```

</details>

The request has been submitted to the Allies and the Supreme War Council
in Paris. Transport of civilians through Ukraine is currently impossible.
The signature is the Foreign Office in Berlin.

This source-local frame is not presented as the only possible original.
A broader screen masks **PARIS**, **UKRAINE** and the whole signature
before comparing all 266 insertion boundaries. It gives **six tied
body-only minima at 181–186**, just before the visibly short group. These
all need five observed-coordinate changes in the unmasked body. Their
full-text repair costs are:

| Inserted-coordinate boundary | Body-only cost | Full proposed-text cost |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 181 | 5 | 8 |
| 182 | 5 | 7 |
| 183 | 5 | 7 |
| 184 | 5 | 6 |
| 185 | 5 | 6 |
| 186 | 5 | 6 |
| 190, primary source-local fit | 8 | 9 |

The fully specified target therefore has three cheaper broad minima at
184–186. The edition retains **all six** masked-body ties, their raw
readings and separate source maps, as well as the primary source-local
frame. Every retained frame can be repaired to the same proposed
plaintext and exactly the same corrected ciphertext; the required source
changes differ. The cheaper word fit does not erase the competing
physical-group evidence, and the historical context below is not used to
choose a boundary.

## Independent contemporary corroboration

After transcribing the source and running the geometry screens, two
contemporary diplomatic texts were located in the official U.S.
*Foreign Relations* edition. They corroborate the subject and routing of
B3–B4 independently of the ciphertext:

- [Lansing to the Swiss Minister, November 15, 1918](https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1919Parisv02/d4),
  no. 290, archival reference `763.72119/2800a`, printed pp. 17–18,
  acknowledges German radio appeals concerning the armistices and states
  that they will be communicated to the associated governments and the
  Supreme War Council in Paris.
- [Lansing to House, November 16, 1918, noon](https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1919Parisv02/d5),
  telegram 38, archival reference `763.72119/9126a`, printed pp. 18–20,
  transmits Solf's November 15 wireless request that German civilians be
  permitted to remain in Turkey for consideration by that council.

These official editions reproduce contemporary documents; the underlying
manuscripts were not inspected. The German intercept credits President
Wilson, while the corroborating texts record Lansing's official actions.
They do not establish a separate personal act by Wilson, the `0YY`
headcount, the claimed departure, or any source-coordinate geometry.
The precise source note is retained in
[`historical_context.json`](../../experiments/constantinople_civilians/historical_context.json).

## Attribution and exact scope

Lasry and colleagues explicitly discuss the neighboring **p221 A**
Mackensen message. This source edition covers **B1–B4** only. Its bounded
prior-work check located no explicit discussion of this B body in the
checked paper, dissertation chapter or cached 55 ScienceBlogs comments;
that is not a universal historical-priority claim. The period key's prior
authorship remains credited in the inputs.

The four parts contain **1,255 printed slots**, **1,253 valid coordinates**
and **1,256 modeled coordinates**, producing **628 plaintext positions**.
The primary raw models fix **624** positions. Seventeen observed-coordinate
substitutions, two source-erasure fills and two missing-coordinate fills,
along with B2's one explicitly identified surplus-coordinate removal,
give a full **628-position candidate under the published raw labels**.
Its numerical headcount is still semantically unresolved.

```bash
python experiments/constantinople_civilians/verify.py --verify
python experiments/constantinople_civilians/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
```

The verifier reconstructs each transposition independently, checks every
raw domain and repair, reruns the exhaustive frame comparisons, and
exactly reencrypts all full candidates. The PDF option checks the complete
primary scan hash and every crop pixel. No substitution-square label is
changed by this edition.

This short message in Childs printed p161 (PDF p164) contains an urgent embassy address and the signature STUMM. All **98 native source coordinates** are visible. Their **49 / 49 raw plaintext positions** are fixed without a historical coordinate edit, mask fill or geometry change.

```text

YZ v LP 0022 (9/11) 2 TLE
1 TL RICHI-98
```

</details>

The receipt's **November 8th**, the subsection heading's **9th November**, and the internal **(9/11)** are retained separately. The edition does not force them into one date. The label says part 1 of two; an absent second part is not reconstructed.

```text
DEUTSCHEBOTSCHAFTCONSTANTINOPELDRINGENDXGEZXSTUMM
```

# Major Dunst — cancellation of the Turkey and military-mission assignment

[All cases](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** This two-part
message cancels the assignment of Major `DUNST` to Turkey and his allocation
to the military mission. The stated earlier posting date, the order reference
and the final number are literal labels under the published November 1–3 key;
no historical biography or numerical reassignment is used to obtain them.

Childs p. 95 is headed 1 November 1918. The shared source header is
`A) OSM v LP (5.22 p.m., November 1st)`, `SSD GRHQU (1/11)0400 2 TEILE`.
The numbered parts advertise 282 and 464 coordinates. All **746 valid source
coordinates** are retained in those working frames, fixing **373 raw
plaintext positions**. Four observed-coordinate word repairs are proposed.
A separate prefixed dash before the first complete group is preserved and
explicitly excluded from the working first-part frame.

## p95 A1

[Source crop](../../experiments/dunst_assignment/sources/p95_A1.png).
`1 TL RICHI-282`.

### The prefixed dash

The [enlarged beginning](../../experiments/dunst_assignment/sources/p95_A1_prefix.png)
prints `-DGDGX`. The five coordinate letters `DGDGX` begin at the same first-
character alignment as the following rows; the dash lies just to their left.
There are **282 valid coordinate letters**, matching the advertised length,
and **283 displayed slots if the prefixed dash is counted**.

The working reading excludes that one noncoordinate mark. It excludes no
observed ADFGVX coordinate. The certificate preserves the complete 283-slot
literal source, its paired-prefix diagnostic and its unpaired coordinate.
The source does not explain the mark, so the boundary interpretation remains
explicit rather than being silently treated as an absent ciphertext symbol.

A retrospective consistency check evaluated all **283 single-slot exclusions**
against the displayed raw reading. Excluding slot 0, the dash, requires no
other change. Excluding slot 1, the first observed `D`, also gives no known-
coordinate mismatch, but additionally deletes that observed `D` and fills the
retained dash with `D`. All other placements disagree with the fixed target.
The selected slot-0 model preserves every observed coordinate and needs no
fill. This check prices alternatives to that fixed reading; it does not
establish a unique historical copying mechanism.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — 282-coordinate frame, with the prefixed dash excluded.**


</details>

`[aer]` expands the abbreviation `MILIT` in the readable layer only. The dash
at the end of this quotation is display punctuation indicating continuation
into the next numbered part; it is unrelated to the source's prefixed dash.

The source-supported repairs change `KONST1NTINOPEL` to `KONSTANTINOPEL`
and `R7S` to `DES` before `MAJORS`. Raw numeral labels `1` and `7` change

## p95 A2

[Source crop](../../experiments/dunst_assignment/sources/p95_A2.png).
`2 TL RICHI-464`. The complete native frame contains 464 valid coordinates.

<details>

# An enquiry about Glatz's whereabouts

[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source audit](../../experiments/corpus_attack/SOURCE_FAMILIES.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Records:** p140 B and p149 C. **Result:** 167 of 168 proposed positions have complete coordinate-pair support in a printed witness under the published Nov4–6 key. One damaged glyph needs an explicit reading to complete `KONSTANTINOPEL`.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> Militär-Mission Konstantinopel. Drahtnachricht über Verbleib Reg. Bmstr. Glatz vom Straßenbau-Sonderkommando 1 erbeteten [wohl: erbeten]. Milverkehr, röm. 2 A 100166 Ko, durch Admiralstab, Kz. 95537.

**Display notes:** The bracketed `[wohl: erbeten]` is a proposed ordinary-German normalization of the literal `ERBETETEN`. It is a gloss, not a deletion in either exact output. Abbreviation expansions in the meaning below remain interpretations; the following notes distinguish the uncertain institutional terms.

The literal numeral label after `ROEM` remains `2` in the readable version;
it is not replaced by a Roman-numeral rendering.

**English meaning:** To the Military Mission in Constantinople. A telegram is requested reporting the whereabouts of Government Master Builder Glatz of Road Construction Special Detachment 1. The closing contains routing and reference information, including transmission through the Admiral Staff and reference 95537.

*Reg. Bmstr.* is probably *Regierungsbaumeister*. The precise institutional meanings of `MILVERKEHR`, `ROEM 2 A 100166 KO` and `KZ 95537` are not established here. The source-supported wording is **ERBETETEN**, with an extra `TE` compared with ordinary **ERBETEN**. The readable edition marks this irregularity; the fixed-length candidate retains all its letters.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
MILITAERXMISSIONKONSTANTINOPELXDRAHTNACHRICHTUEBERVERBLEIBREGXBMSTRXGLATZVOMSTRASSENBAUSONDERKOMMANDO1ERBETETENXMILVERKEHRXROEMX2XAX100166XKOXDURCHADMIRALSTABXKZX95537X
```

</details>

## Source support and remaining repair

Both printed copies contain 336 coordinate slots. In [p140 B](../../experiments/corpus_attack/sources/childs_p140_B.png), the last character of group 64, `VDAF?`, is visibly damaged. All other **335 legible coordinates** directly yield the candidate above. Supplying `X` at this source slot (index 319) gives pair `VX` = `I` at plaintext position 24, completing `KONSTANTINOPEL`. This is the explicit editorial fill; the damaged glyph remains masked in the source transcription.

The [p149 C](../../experiments/corpus_attack/sources/childs_p149_C.png) copy has a clear final `G` in that group. It gives `VG` = `B`, hence `KONSTANTBNOPEL`; it does not independently supply the proposed `I`. Three other coordinate disagreements produce `STRKSSENBAU`, `ERBETETRN` and `4ILVERKEHR`. The proposed candidate costs zero known-coordinate substitutions in p140 and four in p149, plus the one p140 damaged-glyph fill. It is not the absolute minimum-disagreement candidate: retaining `KONSTANTBNOPEL` would lower the combined cost from four to three. The preference for the normal place-name is therefore explicit editorial reasoning.

The [certificate](../../experiments/corpus_attack/source_pair_results.json) records both raw texts, the four substitutions and the source coordinates supporting every proposed letter. The [source inputs](../../experiments/corpus_attack/source_pairs.json) preserve the literal transcriptions and complete headers.

## Dates and provenance

Both headers give **6 November 1918**: 4.00 p.m. in p140 and 7.54 p.m. in p149. The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed pp. 140 and 149 in the [complete scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).

The unchanged **Nov4–6** period key retains the credit recorded in [data/keys.json](../../data/keys.json): **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**, with the public key also supplied by George Lasry in the [2017 discussion](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1). Source comparison, reconstruction, repair analysis and this edition are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment priority is claimed.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 experiments/corpus_attack/build_source_pairs.py --verify
python3 experiments/corpus_attack/verify_source_pairs.py
```

```text
KEING?LDUEBERMITTELNXHEERESGRXKIEWX1CXHRW8536X
```

**Edited output — counted proposal:**

```text
KEINGELDUEBERMITTELNXHEERESGRXKIEWX1CXHRW8536X
```

</details>

**Readable German — the same candidate labels with spacing and punctuation:**

> Kein Geld uebermitteln. Heeresgr. Kiew. 1C. HRW8536.

**Meaning:** The second part instructs that no money be transmitted. The closing reads Heeresgr. Kiew, with the literal labels 1C and HRW8536. Those labels are not changed to a presumed staff branch or number prefix.

**Conditional interpretation and source details:** The printed GAGEV contains a clear out-of-alphabet E at source 43. One counted mask fill supplies E in GELD. The result uses the native 92-coordinate frame and no observed-coordinate substitution.

### Explicit source changes

All indices are zero-based.

| Source index | Printed | Proposed | Cost |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 43 | `E` | `A` | Source-mask fill |

### Reproducibility and attribution

The [input](../../experiments/gokieloff_return_payment_stop/inputs.json) binds each literal source to exact PDF crops. The [certificate](../../experiments/gokieloff_return_payment_stop/certificates.json) contains the raw paired-coordinate domains, each source change and the forward checks. The [verifier](../../experiments/gokieloff_return_payment_stop/verify.py) checks the unchanged published keys and the live German quotations, retaining all numerical and letter labels.

Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro (2026). Childs supplies the historical collection; published reconstruction and key provenance credit Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker. Earlier repository OCR and body readings are retained in the [attribution record](../../experiments/gokieloff_return_payment_stop/prior_candidates.json).

# Kremp's request for a departure date — p131, p149 and p159

[Case guide](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Kremp reports his recovery and asks the military mission's transport section to set his departure date. The unlettered final message on p159 reads completely under the published **Nov7–9** key: **98 positions, with no source correction**. Its different-key reception also repairs the earlier p131 B / p149 B version.

## Reading

**Readable German:**

> Coeln 11. Ab. 1. S. Milmiss., Transp.-Abt. 1b, Constantinopel.
> Bin wiederhergestellt. Bitte Abfahrtstag bestimmen. Kremp.

**Meaning:** Kremp reports that he has recovered and asks the transport section
of the military mission in Constantinople to specify his departure date.
The opening `COELN11XAB1XSX` is directly decoded; its administrative meaning remains unknown. The displayed spacing and abbreviation breaks are editorial.

The complete p159 plaintext is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
COELN11XAB1XSXMILMISSTRANSPABT1BCONSTANTINOPELXBINWIEDERHERGESTELLTBITTEABFAHRTSTAGBESTIMMENXKREMP
```

</details>

All 196 source coordinates re-encrypt exactly using established square cells.

## Three source witnesses

| Witness | Source heading and receipt | Key | Directly fixed positions |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| [p131 B](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/sources/childs_p131_selected.png) | 5 November, continued; received 6 November at 02:36 | `Nov4-6` | 82/84 |
| [p149 B](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/sources/childs_p149_selected.png) | 6 November, continued; received 7 November at 08:59; internal `0110 (6/11)` | `Nov4-6` | 84/84 |
| [p159, final unlettered item](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/sources/childs_p159_selected.png) | 9 November; received at 06:12; internal `NR 17 (9/11)` | `Nov7-9` | 98/98 |

The last item follows a fresh **9 November** heading below the three messages
under 8 November. The machine-readable identifier `p159_D` is a local label
for the fourth item; the source itself does not print a `D` beside it.

The p131 and p149 ciphertexts differ at three slots: two p131 dashes correspond to p149 `A`s, and one `D` corresponds to `V`. The p159 reception uses a different transposition, square and address prefix. Its 51-character body matches **48 of 51** directly decoded characters in p149 and **45 of 51** in p131.

## Exact repairs to the earlier version

The p149 source decodes literally as:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
MILMISTRANSPABT1BKONSTANTINOPELXBINWIEDERHER4ESTELLTBITTEABFA7ETSTAGBESTIMMENXKREMPX
```

</details>

The independently readable p159 body supports `WIEDERHERGESTELLT` and
`ABFAHRTSTAG`. The resulting p149 reconstruction requires precisely three
changes to valid source coordinates, with no insertions or erasure fills:

| Source index, zero based | Printed | Proposed | Plaintext effect |
| ---: | :---: | :---: | --- |
| 134 | X | V | `4` becomes `G` in `WIEDERHERGESTELLT`. |
| 26 | D | G | `7` becomes `H` in `ABFAHRTSTAG`. |
| 106 | F | V | The following `E` becomes `R`. |

The remaining **165 printed coordinates** and the earlier address forms `MILMIS` and `KONSTANTINOPEL` are retained. The 84-position reconstruction re-encrypts to this three-change witness.

For p131, the same body additionally fills its two dashes and changes source
index 145 from `D` to `V`, yielding `BITTE` followed by `ABFAHRTSTAG`.
Its complete repair cost is **four known-coordinate substitutions and two erasure fills**.

## Verification and credit

The [source inputs](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/inputs.json)
retain all three transcripts, exact headers and image hashes. The
[certificates](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/certificates.json)
record every plaintext-to-source pair, the independent inverse, all edits and
the two cross-key body alignments.

```sh
python3 experiments/open_targets_continuation/verify.py --verify
```

The source identification, comparison and edition are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Period-key recovery retains [George Lasry's published attribution](../../data/keys.json).

# Mecklenburg inquiry about a letter to Herzog Karl Michael

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p141 A, PDF p144, contains two parts received under
`ASO v LP (08.12 p.m., November 6th)`, with `FUER ASO (6/11) 2 TLE`.
The Mecklenburg legation requests quick answers through
Kapitänleutnant Wagner and the Tiflis consulate. The second part asks about a
July letter to Herzog Karl Michael and his opportunity to respond. The
wording is awkward in one place and is preserved below.

## p141 A1

The [first-part crop](../../experiments/mecklenburg_and_seaplane_personnel/sources/p141_A1.png)
has **304 slots**, matching `1 TL RICHI-304`. There is one printed dash
and one unreadable visible glyph. The unchanged published **Nov4–6** key
fixes **150 / 152 positions** before editing.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 304-coordinate frame:**

```text
BXMXKXSEWASTOPOLX?ECKLENBURGISCHEGESZNDTSCHAFTBITTETDRINZENDBEIKAPITAENLEUTNANTXWAGNERXUNDKONSULATXTIFLISXSCHNELLEBEANTWORTUNGFOLGEN?ERFRAGENZUERWIRKENX
```

**Edited output — three observed-coordinate substitutions, one printed-dash fill and one unreadable-glyph fill:**

```text
BXMXKXSEWASTOPOLXMECKLENBURGISCHEGESANDTSCHAFTBITTETDRINGENDBEIKAPITAENLEUTNANTXWAGNERXUNDKONSULATXTIFLISXSCHNELLEBEANTWORTUNGFOLGENDERFRAGENZUERWIRKENX
```

</details>

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation:**

> B. M. K., Sewastopol. Mecklenburgische Gesandtschaft bittet dringend,
> bei Kapitänleutnant Wagner und Konsulat Tiflis schnelle Beantwortung
> folgender Fragen zu erwirken.

The `?` inside the ciphertext transcription's group `XAX?F` is a
placeholder for an indeterminate visible mark at source **68**, not a
printed question mark or an omitted source slot. The candidate supplies F,
yielding the D in `FOLGENDER`. The printed dash at source **109** is filled
with X, yielding the M in `MECKLENBURGISCHE`.

## p141 A2

The [second-part crop](../../experiments/mecklenburg_and_seaplane_personnel/sources/p141_A2.png)
contains **422 slots**, including six printed dashes, exactly matching
`2 TL RICHI-422`. Its raw reading fixes **205 / 211 positions**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 422-coordinate frame:**

```text
1XST?PXISTBEKANNTXOBDASIMJULIANXHERZOGXKARLXMICHAELXABGESANDTHANDSCHREIBENDESGROSSHERZOGSABGESANDTWOODENISTX2XSTOPXISTBEKANNTXOBHERZOGGE?EGENHWIT?UEINERR?ECKAEUSS?RUNGGEH?BTHATXBESTAETIGUNGXAUMIRALSTABX32982XBX2
```

**Edited output — five observed-coordinate substitutions and six printed-dash fills:**

```text
1XSTOPXISTBEKANNTXOBDASIMJULIANXHERZOGXKARLXMICHAELXABGESANDTHANDSCHREIBENDESGROSSHERZOGSABGESANDTWORDENISTX2XSTOPXISTBEKANNTXOBHERZOGGELEGENHEITZUEINERRUECKAEUSSERUNGGEHABTHATXBESTAETIGUNGXADMIRALSTABX32982XBX2
```

</details>

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation; one grammatical spelling expansion is bracketed:**

> 1. Stop. Ist bekannt, ob das im Juli an Herzog Karl Michael
> abgesandt[e] Handschreiben des Grossherzogs abgesandt worden ist?
> 2. Stop. Ist bekannt, ob Herzog Gelegenheit zu einer Rückäusserung
> gehabt hat? Bestätigung. Admiralstab. 32982. B. 2.

The first **ABGESANDT** is directly adjacent to **HANDSCHREIBEN** in the
edited stream. The bracketed E makes that adjective readable in normal
German but is **not** an encoded plaintext position. The later repeated
**ABGESANDT** is also literal. This edition does not silently replace
either occurrence with “delivered,” “received,” or another smoother verb.

## Conditional interpretation and source limits

The primary editions accept a faded G at A1 source **161** and a faint A
at A2 source **279**. The
[detail crop](../../experiments/mecklenburg_and_seaplane_personnel/sources/p141_A1_glyphs.png)
shows the first glyph, and the
[faint group ending](../../experiments/mecklenburg_and_seaplane_personnel/sources/p141_A2_faint_end.png)
shows the second. Their masked alternatives remain in the certificate:

- Masking A1 source 161 changes the initial **B** of `BXMXK` to domain
  **8ABGIR**. The variant leaves that code character unresolved.
- Masking A2 source 279 changes the **E** of the first `ABGESANDT` to
  domain **9EKVXZ**. That variant also leaves its position unresolved.

Each alternative retains all six exact re-encryption witnesses. No newly
masked glyph is filled simply to preserve the primary reading. The
variants do not add physical records or enter the primary counts.

The names, titles and questions are what the telegram says. This source
edition does not independently identify the grand duke, confirm a letter's
dispatch or reply, or expand the `B.M.K.` address and `32982 B2` reference.
The two primary candidates together contain **363 positions**, use **eight
observed substitutions and eight source fills**, and re-encrypt exactly.
There is no frame or key change.

Both bodies were already partly readable in earlier repository screens.
Their prior credit and the published key are retained. The
[inputs](../../experiments/mecklenburg_and_seaplane_personnel/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/mecklenburg_and_seaplane_personnel/certificates.json)
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/mecklenburg_and_seaplane_personnel/README.md)
provide the complete source and editing ledger.

# Medical-company report and a request for clarification

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

## p117 A

The source is addressed to the leading medical officer of the German
Caucasus delegation. The page heading is November 3, the origin says
`1807 (3)`, and the receipt line says **November 5**. The published key remains
labelled Nov1–3; this delayed/conflicting receipt does not extend its date
range. The middle letter of the printed `POT` call sign may be Q.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame**

```text
IMDORTXBERICHTNR1314E16VOM29X9XISTEINESANITXKOMPXNR30ERWAEHNTXSOVIELHIERBEKANNTISTNUREIN9ELDLAZARETTDORTXSOFORTDRAHTAUFK?AERUNGX?TSCHXFELDSANITXCHE?XGHQ38302X18
```

**Edited output**

```text
IMDORTXBERICHTNR1314E16VOM29X9XISTEINESANITXKOMPXNR30ERWAEHNTXSOVIELHIERBEKANNTISTNUREINFELDLAZARETTDORTXSOFORTDRAHTAUFKLAERUNGXDTSCHXFELDSANITXCHEFXGHQ38302X18
```

</details>

Price: 1 observed-coordinate substitution, 3 source-mask fills.

**Readable German — based on the edited output**

> Im dort. Bericht Nr. `1314E16` vom `29X9` ist eine Sanit.Komp. Nr.30 erwaehnt. Soviel hier bekannt, ist nur ein Feldlazarett dort. Sofort Drahtaufklaerung. Dtsch. Feldsanit. Chef. `GHQ38302X18`.

The message asks for urgent clarification of a reported medical company
because the sender knows only of a field hospital. `9ELD`→`FELD` is one
priced observed-coordinate repair. The three printed dashes supply L in
`AUFKLAERUNG`, D in `DTSCH`, and F in `CHEF`. The shorthand, unit label 30
and references are retained; no further digit or institutional identification
is inferred. Spacing and punctuation in the readable paragraph are editorial.

## Evidence and reproduction

The published Nov1–3 square and ranks retain the credit of George Lasry,
Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker. The earlier unreviewed OCR candidates
are preserved separately. These are source editions and conditional frame
analyses, without a first historical decipherment claim.

[Literal rows and source images](../../experiments/nov3_medical_radio_withdrawal/inputs.json),
[domains, origins and exact repair certificate](../../experiments/nov3_medical_radio_withdrawal/certificates.json),
and [full method and verification commands](../../experiments/nov3_medical_radio_withdrawal/README.md).

# Return to a replacement unit on medical grounds

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The two p104 C parts report being sent to a replacement unit for specialist
medical treatment and recovery. The literal closing contains both
`RETTERL` and `KETTERL`, followed by `LTN`; neither spelling is silently
replaced by the other. The office-like field `DTSCHXSTAAT` remains unresolved.

Part 1 has a visibly short cipher group and remains conditional on one
missing transmitted coordinate. Part 2 has an ordinary complete frame.
Together the edition requires four known-coordinate substitutions and the
one separately charged insertion. No square label changes.

## Source and header

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [printed p104, PDF p107](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [full page](../../experiments/inventory_and_medical_return/sources/childs_p104_full.png)
places these parts under a November 2 heading. Their reception line says
November 4:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
C) POT v NKJ (9.10 a.m., November 4th)
FÜR POT FÜR HAFENKDTR 1135 (2) 2 TLE
1 TL RICHI-228
2 TL RICHI-140
```

</details>

The unchanged published `Nov1-3` key applies. The heading, internal day `(2)`
and later reception date are preserved without renaming the key period.

## C1: one coordinate missing from the source frame

The [first-part crop](../../experiments/inventory_and_medical_return/sources/childs_p104_C1.png)
contains **227 valid coordinates**, although its label says 228. Group 34,
row 5/group 2, is visibly only **`GAGA`**, beginning at zero-based source
index 165. This is not merely an odd OCR extraction: the four-character
group is present in the image.

The unmodified 227-slot frame gives an unreadable 113-position string plus
an unpaired coordinate; that result is preserved in the certificate. Under
the conditional 228-slot model, inserting an unknown coordinate at index
168 gives 113 fixed labels out of 114:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional insertion at source index 168:**

```text
W?RDEHEUTEAUFGRUNDAERZTLXGUTACHTJDSEITENSSCHWARZMEERSTELLEDTSCHXSTAATZUSPEZIALAERZTLXBEHADDLUNGUXWIEDERHERSTELLUNG
```

</details>

Inserting `A` and applying three source-coordinate substitutions gives:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional missing-slot frame, with A supplied and three substitutions:**

```text
WURDEHEUTEAUFGRUNDAERZTLXGUTACHTENSEITENSSCHWARZMEERSTELLEDTSCHXSTAATZUSPEZIALAERZTLXBEHANDLUNGUXWIEDERHERSTELLUNG
```

</details>

The phrase continues directly into part 2. It says that action was taken
today on the basis of a medical opinion from the `SCHWARZMEERSTELLE`
followed by the literal `DTSCHXSTAAT` field, for specialist medical treatment
and restoration of health. This edition does not turn `STAAT` into `STAB`
or assign a specific institutional identity.

### Equal-A insertion ambiguity

All **228** possible insertion positions were priced against the later
114-character template. The minimum is three observed-coordinate
substitutions, reached at positions **168, 169 and 170**, always with a
missing `A`. The three choices produce **one identical completed cipher
stream and one identical repaired received witness**.

Positions 168 and 169 lie within or at the end of the visibly short `GAGA`
group. Position 170 is just beyond it, after the first `A` of the next
printed group. It remains an arithmetic equivalent because the completed
stream contains three consecutive A coordinates there; it is not an
independently witnessed location of the source gap.

| Proposed insertion index | Where the unknown label appears before filling | Relationship to the short group |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 168 | `W?RDE` | Within `GAGA` |
| 169 | `A?FGRUND` | At the end of `GAGA` |
| 170 | `AE?ZTL` | Just beyond the printed short group |

The certificate preserves all three mappings from observed coordinates to
plaintext. The template was chosen after reading the message; this pricing
is not an independently supplied crib or proof of a uniquely placed loss.

## C2: completion of the sentence and the literal closing

The [second-part crop](../../experiments/inventory_and_medical_return/sources/childs_p104_C2.png)
has exactly 140 valid coordinates and 70 fixed raw labels:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DERGESUNDHEITZUMERSATZTRUPPJNTEILINMARSHGESETZTXXRETTERLXKETTERLXLTNXX
```

</details>

One known-coordinate substitution gives:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
DERGESUNDHEITZUMERSATZTRUPPENTEILINMARSHGESETZTXXRETTERLXKETTERLXLTNXX
```

</details>

Together the parts report being sent to the replacement unit for specialist
treatment and recovery. The source spells the phrase `IN MARSH GESETZT`;
no extra plaintext `C` is inserted to make modern `MARSCH`. Both name tokens
in `RETTERL KETTERL LTN` remain literal. The text supports a lieutenant's
medical-return report, not a unique historical identification from a repaired
surname.

## Costs and reproduction

All indices below refer to the **original received source**, before the
missing C1 coordinate is reconstructed. Printed group numbers and positions
are counted separately within each part.

| Part | Source index | Printed group / position | Change | Effect |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | 194 | 40 / 1 | `A` → `G` | `J` → `E` in `GUTACHTEN` |
| C1 | 200 | 41 / 2 | `A` → `G` | `BEHADDLUNG` → `BEHANDLUNG` |
| C1 | 218 | 44 / 5 | `A` → `G` | Final `D` → `N` in `GUTACHTEN` |
| C2 | 61 | 13 / 2 | `A` → `G` | `TRUPPJNTEIL` → `TRUPPENTEIL` |

The extra reconstructed `A` in C1 is charged as one **missing transmitted
coordinate**, not as a source-glyph fill. There are no unreadable coordinates
in either observed body. The [inputs](../../experiments/inventory_and_medical_return/inputs.json)
and [certificates](../../experiments/inventory_and_medical_return/certificates.json)
preserve every original group, raw domain, insertion alternative, edit and
full/received forward witness.

```sh
python experiments/inventory_and_medical_return/verify.py --verify
```

The period key is prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**, [DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
also reproduced in Lasry's 2017 key comment. Earlier unreviewed OCR candidates
existed. No universal first-decipherment claim is made from the bounded
author-paper review. The conditional reconstruction certifies its arithmetic
and repair cost, while the source gap and unresolved words remain explicit.

# Batum: Lieutenant Meier ordered to Berlin

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The source advertises **RICHI-150** but contains **149 typed coordinates**. The fifth group in row 3 is visibly `ADAG`, containing four symbols. Supplying one **A** produces `ADAAG` and a complete **75-position** reading without changing any observed coordinate. The recovery is conditional on that local missing-coordinate model.

## p104 D

Childs p104, PDF p107; [reviewed source crop](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/sources/p104_D.png). Key: unchanged published **Nov1–3**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — literal received header:**

```text
D) POT v NKJ (8.36 a.m., November 4th)
POT ZUR UBERMITTLUNG NACH BATUM (2) 1650
RICHI-150
```

**Raw output — conditional 150-slot frame, inserting one unknown coordinate at source boundary 103; 74/75 fixed positions:**

```text
LTXMEIERXBATUMXSO?ORTBERLINABREISENXBEIMERSXBATLX2XGARDEREGTXMELDENXMILMISS
```

**Edited output — 0 observed-coordinate substitutions; 0 source-mask fills; 1 fill in the hypothesized added slot; same conditional frame; 75/75 fixed positions:**

```text
LTXMEIERXBATUMXSOFORTBERLINABREISENXBEIMERSXBATLX2XGARDEREGTXMELDENXMILMISS
```

</details>

The full edited stream re-encrypts exactly under the declared frame and listed changes.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Lt. Meier. Batum. Sofort Berlin abreisen. Beim Ers. Batl. 2. Garderegt. melden. Milmiss.

**Meaning:** The conditional reading orders Lieutenant Meier at Batum to leave immediately for Berlin and report to the replacement battalion designated 2. Garderegt. It does not prove that the journey occurred or establish a biographical identity.

## Two compatible locations for the same missing A

All five insertion boundaries within the short group are checked against the complete proposed text:

| Source boundary | Added value | Observed-coordinate substitutions |
|---|---|---:|
| 100 | A | 2 |
| 101 | D | 1 |
| 102 | A | 0 |
| 103 | A | 0 |
| 104 | G | 1 |

The two zero-substitution alignments produce **the same complete ciphertext and the same plaintext**. Their raw uncertainty differs: boundary 102 leaves the last letter of `MEIER` unresolved; boundary 103 leaves a letter of `SOFORT` unresolved. Neither alignment is preferred as the exact historical loss location. The displayed raw stream uses boundary 103, with the alternative retained in the certificate. The finite comparison concerns this local short-group model and proposed wording, not every imaginable corruption mechanism.

The unit number 2 remains the published-square label, and `ERS`, `BATL`, `GARDEREGT` and `MILMISS` are not silently expanded in the complete German display. No specific biography of Meier is asserted.

## Attribution and reproducibility

Earlier unreviewed repository candidates already identified these bodies. This edition reviews the source images, retains their literal observations and publishes the exact repair or frame account; it makes no first-decipherment claim. The key keeps its earlier published provenance.

[Inputs](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/inputs.json), [full certificates](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/certificates.json), [earlier candidates](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/prior_candidates.json), and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/README.md) preserve the evidence.

cases/people/military_mission_recalls.md.text:
# Siegfried and Osthoff: later military-mission recall messages

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** Four newly source-reviewed physical parts on Childs p161. The Osthoff body was already identified from p138/p148/p149; this edition adds a later differently keyed witness and directly supports three previously editorial letters.

Source edition and verification: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Published period keys: Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker, unchanged. Earlier unreviewed p161 second-part readings and the existing [Osthoff source-family edition](osthoff.md) retain their prior credit. No existing p138/p148/p149 record is counted again.

## Conditional digit reading

An earlier Siegfried cancellation, [p135 A](siegfried_assignment_cancellation.md), directly supplies **45610** under the Nov4–6 key. If both orders cite the same reference, p161 C1’s observed XA/VF pairs fix **XA=5, VF=6**, so its reference reads **ZU2NR45610**. The two orders differ in wording and reception; [the complete comparison](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) retains the alternative 46510. The erased date digit has the separately priced
completion below.

## Conditional complete Siegfried order

A separately priced date completion reads **MK 2.11**. The erased position has native domain **1GIKNY**, so 1 is its only numerical value if this is a day/month date. The distinct Osthoff recall on p161 D1 directly preserves `MKX2X11` in observed pairs. This supports the format and month, rather than treating the two orders as copies.

The completion supplies **F at printed dash 185**, changing `?G` to `FG`.
It adds one source-mask fill and no observed-coordinate substitution.
Together with the 45610 reference interpretation, C1 reaches **102/102
fixed labels** at **four observed substitutions and five printed-erasure
fills**. C2 is already an unchanged 77-label source reading.

**Readable German — complete conditional C1–C2 order; source abbreviations and spellings retained:**

> SS Doppel GR. HQ. MK. 2.11. Militaermiszion Konstantinopel. Zu 2 Nr. 45610. Komdo Oberlts Siegfried nach Tuerkei u deszen Zuteilung zur Milmiszion ist aufgehoben. AKO folgt. Allerh. Bef. Chef Milkab Frhr Marschall.

The two parts therefore have **179/179 conditional fixed labels**. The
spelling `DESZEN`, the abbreviation `u` and the received `MISZION` spellings
remain literal. The calendar reading does not force the reference
assignment: under the opposite 5/6 square the same date reads 2.11 while
the reference becomes 46510.

## Meaning and exact scope

C is an order cancelling Oberleutnant Siegfried's posting to Turkey and assignment to the Military Mission. D concerns Captain of the Reserve Osthoff: his Turkey posting and mission assignment are cancelled, and he is to be transferred to the replacement battalion of a railway regiment. The cabinet order will follow; the closing is from the Chief of the Military Cabinet, Frhr. Marschall.

These are readings of the telegrams. The edition does not establish a further biographical identity for either officer. The original abbreviations and the recurring spellings `MISZION` and `DESZEN` remain in the literal and edited strings.

Childs printed page 161 / PDF page 164 gives C at 05.57 a.m. on 9 November, `NR16 (9/11) 2 TLE`, and D at 06.05 a.m., `FUER YZ NR17 (9/11) 2 TEILE`. All four parts decrypt under the unchanged Nov7–9 key. Their printed lengths 204/154/254/190 exactly match the counted source slots.

## Counts and source readings

The table retains the baseline editions. With the separate reference and date
completion above, all four parts have **401/401 conditional fixed labels**,
at six observed substitutions and five printed-erasure fills in total.

| Record | Source slots | Raw fixed positions | Edited fixed positions | Observed-coordinate substitutions | Source fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|p161_C1|204|95/102|99/102|4|4|
|p161_C2|154|77/77|77/77|0|0|
|p161_D1|254|127/127|127/127|2|0|
|p161_D2|190|95/95|95/95|0|0|

The physical-record total is **802 coordinate slots / 401 plaintext positions**. Raw fixed positions total 394; the edited layer fixes 398.

## p161 C1 — Siegfried posting cancellation, first part





## p161 D2 — Osthoff railway battalion reassignment and cabinet-order closing

<details>

```text

```

</details>

## Cross-period evidence for the earlier Osthoff edition

The earlier p149 A2 literal source had `UEM`, `ERSBKTL`, and `REGM1S`. Its already published editorial reading proposed `DEM`, `ERSBATL`, and `REGMTS`. The new p161 D2 source directly gives all three proposed letters under the other period key, without an edit to D2:

| Earlier p149 A2 position | Earlier raw → proposed | New p161 D2 observed pair | New original coordinate indices | Result |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
|11|U→D|XV|58,135|Direct D in DEM|
|20|K→A|XD|49,107|Direct A in BATL|
|36|1→T|GV|80,118|Direct T in REGMTS|

Indices are zero-based. The certificate independently decrypts the selected older source, verifies that these were exactly its three preexisting editorial changes, and checks the new complete coordinate pairs. The older source's original repair costs remain unchanged.

The later wording is abbreviated and includes an additional raw `1` after `REGMTS`. It is not an identical ciphertext stream or a proof of a common original at every character. Its value is direct corroboration of the three specific earlier readings.

## Remaining uncertainty

In the unchanged baseline edition, C1's date-like field remains `2X?1`: its erased position 19 has domain **1GIKNY**. The two question marks in `ZU2NR4??10` are different: they arise from the observed XA and VF cells of the published partial square, at plaintext positions 58 and 59. Their joint assignments are **56 or 65**, not independent choices that could both be 5 or both be 6. The conservative streams retain both assignments; the optional cross-period interpretation is given above.

The baseline C1 layer has four known-coordinate changes and four printed-erasure fills; the conditional date completion adds the fifth fill. The local `0→U` proposal before `DESZEN` alone costs two observed-coordinate substitutions; it is not a global reassignment of the digit0 key label. D1 has two word repairs, `KOMMRNDO→KOMMANDO` and `END→UND`. C2 and D2 are entirely unchanged source readings.

## Evidence and reproduction

[The input record](../../experiments/military_mission_recalls/inputs.json) preserves all manual rows, literal irregular glyphs, source headers and crop-rendering metadata. [The certificate](../../experiments/military_mission_recalls/certificates.json) retains all coordinate changes, masks, symbol domains, digit/J/Q/Y labels and round trips. Global witnesses demonstrate consistency only; they do not recover a unique original.

[The README](../../experiments/military_mission_recalls/README.md) provides portable verifier commands, including exact source-crop pixel regeneration from the pinned full scan. Prior candidates and specific earlier source editions are distinguished; the bounded literature check is not a universal priority claim.

# The Namur order: two witnesses for Staedt and Weiher

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source reconciliation and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Two closely related transmissions instruct **Hauptmann Staedt in Namur**
to contact `HPT V. WEIHER` at an Etappen inspection. The latter is to receive
a detailed order by `11 VORM`; the message is signed `MJR KROEGER`.
The witnesses together support this 126-position reading:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — joint witness reconstruction under the stated same-message model:**

```text
HPTMANNSTAEDTNAMURXXBITTESICHMITHPTVXXWEIHERETAPPENINSP1INVERBINDUNGSETZENDERBIS11VORMAUSFUEHRLICHENBEFEHLBEKOMMTXXMJRKROEGERX
```

</details>

The anomalous **`INSP1IN`** and literal **`HPTVXX`** are retained. The
edition does not silently replace the `1` with a separator or insert letters
into the title abbreviation. The source spelling `STAEDT` is retained
without a new biographical identification.

## The two physical sources

Both are in Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
[complete scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view),
and use the unchanged published **Nov10–12** square and ranks.

| Witness | Source | Header | Received slots |
|---|---|---|---:|
| p171 C | [Printed p171, PDF p174](../../experiments/namur_order_witnesses/sources/p171_C.png) | `--- v SY (7.26 p.m., November 10th); 1800; RICHI-252` | 252, including four printed dashes |
| p172 E | [Printed p172, PDF p175](../../experiments/namur_order_witnesses/sources/p172_E.png) | `SY v MAX (7.21 p.m., November 10th); RICHI----; (J'md)` before the received groups | 242, all valid coordinates |

The receiving time on E is five minutes earlier than C's. The edition
preserves both timestamps and does not infer an actual relay sequence.
The p171 page heading is November 9, while C's own receiving timestamp
explicitly says November 10.

C's direct reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
HPTMDNNSTAEDTNAMQRXXBITTESICHMITHPTVXXWEGHERE?AB?ENINSP1?NVERBINDUNGSETZENDE4BIS11VORMAUSFUEHRLICHENBQFE?LBEKOMMTXXMJRKROEGERX
```

</details>

E's earlier OCR stream had only 235 positions and did not yield this
coherent body. Visual retranscription supplies its actual **242 received
coordinates**. Under the same-message model, E is missing ten leading
coordinates, giving this direct reading in a 252-coordinate frame:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional same-message 252-slot frame with ten absent leading coordinates:**

```text
HPTMANN?1AEDTNA?URXXBIT?ESICHJI?HPTVXXW?IHERETA?PENINSP?I?VERBI?DUNGSET?ENDERBI?11VORMAUSFUEHRLICHENBEFEHLBEKOMMRXXPJRKROEGERX
```

</details>

The ten-coordinate leading loss is inferred from the relationship between
the witnesses; E does not display a legible total length or explicitly
count a ten-coordinate gap. It remains a stated model assumption.

## Why the alignment is useful

Aligning E's first received coordinate with C source index **10** compares
**238 jointly observed coordinates**: **227 agree** and **11 conflict**.
E supplies observed values for all four printed dashes in C, while C
supplies E's ten modeled missing leading values:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — ten leading coordinates supplied by the other witness:**

```text
DGAAV FADFD
```

</details>

This offset is the unique highest agreement fraction among the **87 relative
offsets with at least 200 jointly observed coordinate pairs**. The comparison
uses ciphertext values, without a language score. It is a finite alignment
check, not a statistical significance claim or a global exclusion of every
possible original length.

The name correction **`WEGHER→WEIHER`** is supported by an observed coordinate
in E, rather than merely by the familiarity of a surname. Conversely, C
supplies correct-looking word and name values where E has other errors.
Lasry et al.'s separate discussion of the neighboring p172 C/p175 A family
also mentions von Weiher; that is retained as prior context, not used to
claim a new identification of the officer in these two witnesses.

## Exact reconciliation cost, with the alternatives retained

For two aligned streams to represent one common ciphertext, at least one
observed coordinate must change at each of the **11 conflicts**. The
selected readable body needs exactly **six substitutions in C and five in
E**, meeting that lower bound. Four printed-dash fills in C and ten modeled
prefix fills in E are separately accounted for.

Every coordinate value in the selected common ciphertext is **observed in
at least one witness**. No new coordinate value is supplied solely from a
word guess. The evidence for its plaintext pairs is:

| Complete coordinate pair supporting a selected character | Positions |
|---|---:|
| Observed in both witnesses | 102 |
| Observed only in C | 14 |
| Observed only in E | 9 |
| One coordinate supplied by each witness | 1 |
| **Total** | **126** |

The mixed pair is the first `P` in `ETAPPEN`, plaintext position **47**:
C supplies working coordinate 5 and E supplies working coordinate 52.
Thus **125 of 126 whole pairs** are directly observed in one of the two
sources, and the remaining pair is covered coordinate by coordinate.

Minimum cost does not establish a unique original reading. Each conflicting
coordinate has two source-supported choices, yielding **2¹¹ = 2,048**
minimum-cost common coordinate streams under this fixed alignment. The
verifier enumerates all of them, checks the same total cost, and records
their ordered digest. The complete conflict table and selected choice bits
make every alternative reproducible. The readable body is an editorial
choice within that set, with `INSP1IN` left unrepaired.

| Witness | Literal source slots | Analysis-frame slots | Raw fixed labels | Edition labels | Known-coordinate substitutions | Printed fills | Modeled-prefix fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| p171 C | 252 | 252 | 122 / 126 | 126 / 126 | 6 | 4 | 0 |
| p172 E | 242 | 252 | 115 / 126 | 126 / 126 | 5 | 0 | 10 |
| **Total** | **494** | **504** | **237 / 252** | **252 / 252** | **11** | **4** | **10** |

These are two physical witnesses of **one 126-position body**, not two
independent bodies totaling 252 distinct characters. There is no deletion,
source reordering or baseline-key change.

## Attribution and reproduction

The period key is credited to **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**. C already appeared as an unreviewed OCR-derived candidate.
The new contribution is the exact source review of both witnesses, the
recovery of E's actual received stream, the joint reconstruction and its
complete repair accounting. The bounded publication check is documented;
no universal decipherment-priority claim is made.

The [inputs](../../experiments/namur_order_witnesses/inputs.json) preserve
all source rows and headers. The
[certificate](../../experiments/namur_order_witnesses/certificates.json)
contains all 87 alignment comparisons, all 11 coordinate conflicts,
character-by-character support, repairs, raw domains and global round-trip
witnesses. Arbitrary key/erasure witnesses certify consistency only.

```sh
python experiments/namur_order_witnesses/verify.py --verify
```

The optional `--pdf` argument verifies the pinned scan and independently
regenerates both source-crop images for pixel comparison.

# An award notification and a congratulation

[Case index](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)


**Reviewed source crops:** [p193_F.png](../../experiments/nov13_congratulation_conditional_frame/sources/p193_F.png) · [p193_date_heading.png](../../experiments/nov13_congratulation_conditional_frame/sources/p193_date_heading.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).
## p193 F

**Status:** The source and its header both have **75 coordinates**. The conditional 74-coordinate edition excludes one observed terminal X and changes one observed D to G. Its baseline fixes **36/37** positions; the separate class interpretation below completes the remaining label.

**Source and dates:** Page heading 14 November 1918; F) CM v CZ (1.24 a.m., November 13th); separate label `2.10`; RIZI-75. The date layers and the label 2.10 are retained without reconciliation.

[Source p193 F — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov13_congratulation_conditional_frame/inputs.json)

### Conditional award-class reading

**Readable German — EK interpreted as an Iron Cross class and numerical DD=1 retained; existing terminal-X frame and word repair retained:**

> JTN. KR. EK2 verliehen. Glueckwunsch. S. R.

The message reports an award and offers congratulations. If `EK` denotes
the Iron Cross and the following character its class, **and the separate
DD cell retains numerical value 1**, the remaining square domain admits
only **2**. Numerical DD=1 is a contextual interpretation, not a fact
established by the published label alone. The independent native
`10X11` in [p186 B1](../military/oberost_troop_movement_obliterations.md#p186-b1)
supports it if that field is a day/month date: its repeated month can only
be 11. The [joint source account](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md#the-award-class)
replays all ten untouched coordinates and states the date condition.

The resulting representative text has **37/37** fixed labels, with the
earlier **one observed-coordinate exclusion and one substitution**, and no
new source edit. `JTN`, `KR` and `S R` remain opaque. Without retaining DD's
numerical value, the distinct square cells alone do not exclude class 1.

The royal decree of 5 August 1914 specifies two classes and a Grand Cross.
Its contemporary reprint in *Die Presse*, 8 August 1914, p1, supplies the
[class-system evidence](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/sources/die_presse_1914_decree.png)
and [continuation](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/sources/die_presse_1914_classes.png).
It does not identify this recipient. The resulting **VG=2** assignment
also gives `ALLE 2 TAGE` in the [p188 supply request](../military/armistice_provisions_requests.md#c1-flour-and-oats-to-szolnok).

All four endpoint alternatives below retain the same received `VG` pair
at source positions 19 and 60. The class interpretation leaves those
geometries unresolved. [Joint certificate](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/certificates.json).

### Native odd frame retained

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — paired portion of the unmodified 75-coordinate frame:**

```text
JGXVER5EZNEAXRLHEMKNUIL?ICS0RK1AM1OCK
```

</details>

The unmodified inverse transposition leaves one orphan **A at inverse-stage index 74, originating at source index 27**. The 37 paired labels above are not the displayed congratulation. Excluding the last received X is therefore a different model from dropping the native orphan.

### Conditional terminal-X model

Exclude the **observed X at source index 74 before inverse transposition**. This is an explicitly priced exclusion, not a source-mask fill, a claim that the source printed 74, or a correction to the header. All other 74 observed positions remain in order.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 74-coordinate model:**

```text
JTNXKRXEK?XVERLIEHENXGLUECKWUN5CHXSXR
```

**Edited output — one additional observed-coordinate substitution:**

```text
JTNXKRXEK?XVERLIEHENXGLUECKWUNSCHXSXR
```

**Readable German — the same candidate labels with spacing and punctuation:**

> JTN. KR. EK? verliehen. Glueckwunsch. S. R.

</details>

**Explicit source changes:**

| Source index | Printed | Treatment | Cost |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 74 | X | Exclude before inverse transposition | One observed-coordinate exclusion |
| 12 | D | Propose G | One observed-coordinate substitution; GLUECKWUN5CH → GLUECKWUNSCH |

The baseline label after EK is **plaintext index 9, pair VG, source indices 19 and 60**. Both source coordinates are observed; the published square leaves VG unassigned, with domain `234789QY`. The separate class interpretation above assigns 2; it is not a source erasure fill.

### Endpoint alternatives remain open

The same congratulation core survives four source-exclusion choices, yielding three distinct streams. Each excludes one observed coordinate and changes the **same source index 12 from D to G**. The first two V exclusions are exact ciphertext aliases. These alternatives prevent a claim that the terminal-X error is historically unique.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — alternative excluding source 0 or 1 (V):**

```text
K?XVERLIEHENXGLUECKWUN5CHXSXR?JKCJOEK
```

**Edited output — the same one-coordinate word repair:**

```text
K?XVERLIEHENXGLUECKWUNSCHXSXR?JKCJOEK
```

**Raw output — alternative excluding source 73 (D):**

```text
JTNXKRXEK?XVERLIEHENXGLUECKWUN5CHXSCR
```

**Edited output — the same one-coordinate word repair:**

```text
JTNXKRXEK?XVERLIEHENXGLUECKWUNSCHXSCR
```

</details>

The V-exclusion alternative retains opaque opening K? and closing ?JKCJOEK. Excluding source 73 retains SCR at the end. None of these endpoints is expanded into a person, rank, unit or signature. The source-74 version above provides one convenient full-message presentation; the stable finding is the shared VERLIEHEN / GLUECKWUNSCH core.

### Exact prices and their limits

The certificate prices **all 75 received-source exclusions and all 75 inverse-stage exclusions** against the stated 37-position primary candidate. Two conventions are recorded: one prices only its 36 fixed labels, and the stricter one also requires EK? to occupy an unassigned cell of the unchanged published square. Under either convention, the full primary layout uniquely costs one substitution at source exclusion 74. This is conditional on that full layout, including the chosen opaque endpoints.

For inverse-stage exclusions, the minimum is **37 substitutions when EK? is an unconstrained wildcard**, or **38 when its unfilled-key-cell domain is enforced**. These are fixed-target prices, not a proof that no other plaintext is possible. The other endpoint alternatives above have their own one-substitution readings and are not hidden by the primary-target comparison.

The verifier preserves all paired coordinates, including the unresolved VG pair, and reproduces the conditional 74-coordinate ciphertext. Reattaching the explicitly excluded terminal X restores the full 75-position received shape with only the charged D→G substitution. This coordinate-level forward check is distinct from a complete plaintext re-encryption: the EK? symbol remains unassigned.

[Page date heading — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov13_congratulation_conditional_frame/inputs.json)

### Reproducibility and attribution

The [input](../../experiments/nov13_congratulation_conditional_frame/inputs.json) binds literal rows and date layers to exact source crops. The [certificate](../../experiments/nov13_congratulation_conditional_frame/certificates.json) retains the native odd frame, conditional models, full coordinate ledgers, all 150 exclusion prices and forward checks. The [verifier](../../experiments/nov13_congratulation_conditional_frame/verify.py) checks these values, the live German quotation and the unchanged published partial key.

Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro (2026). Historical source: J. Rives Childs. Published partial-key credit remains with Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker. The [attribution record](../../experiments/nov13_congratulation_conditional_frame/prior_candidates.json) preserves earlier OCR and the bounded discovery diagnostic. Search scores are not used as historical evidence.
