# Osthoff's posting to Turkey is cancelled

[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source audit](../../experiments/corpus_attack/SOURCE_FAMILIES.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Four receptions, p138 A1–A2 and p148 C1 / p149 A2, reconstruct the cancellation of Osthoff's posting to Turkey. Under the published **Nov4–6** key, they jointly support all **121 positions** of the first part and **115 of 118** in the second; three word repairs complete the proposed reading.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> Militärmission Konstantinopel. Kommando des Hptms. der Res. Osthoff nach der Türkei und seine Zuteilung zur Militärmission ist aufgehoben. Derselbe ist dem 1. Ers. Batl. Eisenbahn-Regmts. zu überweisen. AKO folgt. Auf Allerhöchsten Befehl: Chef Militärkabinetts, Frhr. Marschall.

**English meaning:** To the Military Mission in Constantinople. Captain of the Reserve Osthoff's posting to Turkey and assignment to the Military Mission have been cancelled. He is to be transferred to the first replacement battalion of the railway regiment. The cabinet order will follow. By supreme command: the Chief of the Military Cabinet, Baron Marschall.

The English expands the military abbreviations *Ers. Batl.* and *AKO*. The cancellation concerns Osthoff's assignment. His full identity and the regiment number remain unestablished.

## What the witnesses establish

| Part | Printed witnesses | Direct source evidence | Remaining editorial work |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [p138 A1](../../experiments/corpus_attack/sources/childs_p138_A.png), [p148 C1](../../experiments/corpus_attack/sources/childs_p148_C1.png) | p148 fixes 120/121 positions. The other witness supplies the missing `R` in `DERRES`. All 121 candidate positions have complete coordinate-pair support in a witness. | The earlier p138 copy is five coordinates short. A unique best alignment among all 238 insertion positions supplies `XVAXX` before received index 140. Three other known-coordinate disagreements remain. |
| 2 | [p138 A2](../../experiments/corpus_attack/sources/childs_p138_A.png), [p149 A2](../../experiments/corpus_attack/sources/childs_p149_A2.png) | The two copies jointly support 115/118 proposed positions. p149 independently supplies the `N` in `KABINETTS` and the `C` in `HOECHSTEN`. | Both copies contain `UEM`, `ERSBKTL` and `REGM1S`. Reading `DEM`, `ERSBATL` and `REGMTS` requires three changes in p149 and four in the more damaged p138 copy. |

The literal p149 second part is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DERSELBEISTUEM1XERSBKTLEISENBAHNREGM1SZUUEBERWEISENAKOFOLGTXAUFALLERHOECHSTENBEFEHLCHEFMILITAERKABINETTSFRHRMARSCHALLX
```

</details>

Two repairs form the adjacent coordinate exchange `VF → FV` at transmitted indices 210–211; the third changes index 31 from `A` to `X`. The [certificate](../../experiments/corpus_attack/source_pair_results.json) records the raw readings, source differences, coordinate maps and repair costs.

## Dates and provenance

The p138 header gives 5 November; the clearer p148–149 transmission was intercepted on 7 November and includes `0015 (6/11)`. Both parts use the unchanged published **Nov4–6** key. The later interception time therefore does not by itself require a new period key.

The historical records are from J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed pp. 138, 148–149 in the [source scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view). The period-key work is credited to **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**, with the public key also given by George Lasry in the [2017 discussion](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1).

Source comparison, reconstruction and edition: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 experiments/corpus_attack/build_source_pairs.py --verify
python3 experiments/corpus_attack/verify_source_pairs.py
```

The second implementation independently reconstructs the columns, checks all 238 missing-group positions and re-encrypts the candidate readings. The [full source audit](../../experiments/corpus_attack/SOURCE_FAMILIES.md) retains the exact raw texts and unresolved source disagreements.

# p167 D — Captain and replacement-detachment dispatch fragment

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Partial word proposal and source review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**
The fragment concerns a captain's dispatch to a replacement detachment.
The established word layer reads `HPTM`, the title ending `CHEF`, `WIRD`,
and `ERSATZABTLG ABBEFOERDERT`, followed by `NACHCHEF`. An additional name
proposal reads **Zimmermann**, supported by another telegram that names a
captain in the radio service. The full title, destination and footer remain
unread.

## Conditional digit reading

The [shared Nov7–9 reference interpretation](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) fixes positions **41, 49 and 91 as 6, 5 and 6**, giving **92/95 conditional edited labels**. The opposite assignment gives 5, 6 and 5. This adds no source change or fill and applies equally to the separately priced Zimmermann proposal. The resulting destination field remains garbled; only three numerical labels are selected. Positions 52, 89 and 94 remain source-mask uncertainty.

## Conditional name proposal

**Readable German — optional Zimmermann reading; unread fields remain omitted:**

> Hptm. Zimmermann […] Chef wird […] Ersatzabtlg abbefoerdert. Nachchef […]

The raw ten-letter field `LIMMER2ANG` can be read as **ZIMMERMANN** at four
additional observed-coordinate substitutions. A separate radio-service
telegram, [p121 B1](../radio/nov4_repetition_and_connections.md#p121-b1),
directly reads `HPTM ZIMMERMANN` while asking about the Bucharest–Constanza
connection. Its complete observed pairs support the proposed name and
rank; they do not establish that both messages concern the same officer.

The new name layer extends the interpreted spans from 45 to 55 positions.
It retains all six unknown positions, the opaque `KODESEL` and title fields,
and the uncompleted destination and footer. The omitted intervals are
15–30, 39–53 and 86–94; no given name or biographical identity is supplied.

<details>
<summary>Name proposal and exact source cost</summary>

**Edited output — optional ZIMMERMANN proposal; 14 observed substitutions, 2 source-mask fills and 2 added-slot fills; 89/95 fixed labels:**

```text

```

| Original source index | Additional observed change | Name repair |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 160 | `D`→`F` | Initial `L`→`Z` |
| 57, 132 | `G`→`A`, `D`→`F` | `2`→`M` |
| 66 | `D`→`X` | Final `G`→`N` |

The four changes have the same positions and cost in all six retained
frames. Repricing all 125 permitted short-group layouts with the added name
span leaves the same six minima, now at 14 substitutions. The new name
does not favor a particular missing-coordinate placement.

</details>

## p167 D

**Readable German — three proposed spans; each omission retains an unread field:**

> Hptm. […] Chef wird […] Ersatzabtlg abbefoerdert. Nachchef […]

The omissions cover positions **5–30**, **39–53** and **86–94** respectively.
`Chef` is the ending of the unidentified title-like `FESDEILO…` field.
The fragment mentions a captain and dispatch in connection with a replacement
detachment; the full destination and the person's identity remain unread.
`NACHCHEF` is retained as the proposed closing designation.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 190-slot frame with three added unknowns, unchanged Nov7–9 key; 84/95 fixed positions:**

```text
H?TMXLIMMER2ANGKODESELXFESDEILO?HEFWIRDN0?HRA2T11?RK?RZRLATZRBTLGJBBEAFE?DERF??ACHCHEFT1B?7?17?
```

**Edited output — partial word proposal in the same frame; ten observed substitutions, two source-mask fills and two added-slot fills; 89/95 fixed labels:**

```text
HPTMXLIMMER2ANGKODESELXFESDEILOCHEFWIRDN0?HRA2T11?RK?RERSATZABTLGABBEFOERDERTXNACHCHEFT1B?7?17?
```

</details>

All output outside the proposed spans stays exactly raw. In particular,
`LIMMER2ANG`, `KODESEL`, `FESDEILO` and the garbled destination/reference
fields are preserved. The 89 fixed labels include those opaque fields;
they are not 89 independently read historical characters.

## Source frame and exact price

The body has **187 native slots**, including the invalid printed `C` and `W`
and two dashes; **183** slots are valid coordinates. The header advertises
**190**. Three groups contain four glyphs: `DFGX`, `VVGD` and `WVDG`.
Inserting one unknown at each group's five possible boundaries gives
**125** source-retaining models.

For the stated word spans, all 125 models are priced exactly. **Six** tie
at ten observed substitutions. Their insertion boundaries are
`[35,59,100]`, `[35,59,101]`, `[36,59,100]`, `[36,59,101]`,
`[37,59,100]` and `[37,59,101]`, measured before original source slots.
Two require four supplied unknown values rather than five. The displayed
primary is the first of those two, **[36,59,100]**. This selection is
conditioned on the word proposal, not proof of historical gap locations.
No source slot is deleted, moved or copied.

| Change class | Exact primary events, zero-based |
|---|---|
| Observed substitutions | Source 34 D→X, 52 A→X, 53 X→F, 56 D→A, 82 X→G, 117 D→X, 119 X→V, 126 F→V, 158 F→V, 166 F→D |
| Existing source-mask fills | Invalid `C` at source 91→G; dash at source 131→A |
| Added-slot fills | Model 60→F and 102→D |
| Remaining unknown coordinates | Added model 36; invalid `W` at source 98; dash at source 130 |

The six unresolved plaintext positions are **41, 49, 52, 89, 91 and 94**.
Positions 41 and 91 share square cell `VF`; position 49 uses `XA`, the
opposite digit in `{5,6}`. The three remaining coordinate masks impose
additional coupled domains. All **432** complete square/mask assignments
for the primary are enumerated and exactly re-encrypted; no one completion
is selected. The certificate retains the alternative maps and their full
compatibility witnesses too.

## Source and credit

Childs, printed p167 / PDF p170, section D. The header reads
`NKJ v LP (03.23 a.m., November 10th)` and
`(RAT) SSD BLITZBLUECHER (9/11) 2245; RICHI-190`.

# p210 B — Consul Burkhardt's oil-company assignment

[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source certificate](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/certificates.json) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Record:** p210 B, 20 November 1918, to Consul Burkhardt in Tiflis.
**Result:** **158/158 raw plaintext positions** are fixed by the unchanged
published Nov19–21 key. Five explicit coordinate substitutions restore
body words; the date-like **J** and the administrative references remain
literal and historically unresolved.

## Readable body

**Readable German:**

> An Konsul Burkhardt, Tiflis. Ihr Auftrag fuer
> Kriegsschmieroelgesellschaft am J Dezember beendet.
> K.R.A. Nr. 455, JJ, J4, A. Nch.
> Kriegsministerium, Allgem. Kriegsdepartement.

**Meaning:** A War Ministry telegram informs Consul Burkhardt in Tiflis
that his assignment for the lubricating oil company is ended on a December
date. Its day is transmitted as **J** under the published key. This edition
does not silently turn that letter into a numeral or establish a specific
historical completion date.

The addressee and place are directly read. `KRA`, `A NCH`, **455**, **JJ**
and **J4** remain source strings without a forced administrative expansion
or date interpretation. The prose supplies only spacing, capitalization
and punctuation. It does not identify the consul beyond the printed surname.

## Raw text and reconstruction cost

The [source](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/sources/p210_B.png) reads:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
COS v LP (02.58 p.m., November 20th)
17.30 (20/11)
RICHI-316
```

</details>

All **316** printed coordinates are valid. The direct decipherment is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ANKONSULXBURKHARDTXTIFLISXIHREUFTRAGFUE3KRIEGSSCH1IEROELGESE8LJCHAFTAMXJXDEZEMBERBEENDETXKXRXAXXNRX455XJJXJ4XAXNCHXKRIEGSMINISTERIUMALLGEMXKRIEGSDEPARTEMENTXX
```

</details>

The same-length candidate changes only the body sequences
`IHREUFTRAG → IHRAUFTRAG`, `FUE3 → FUER`, and
`KRIEGSSCH1IEROELGESE8LJCHAFT → KRIEGSSCHMIEROELGESELLSCHAFT`.
The exact coordinate substitutions are:

| Source index, zero-based | Source | Proposed |
|---:|:---:|:---:|
| 2 | F | V |
| 3 | G | F |
| 4 | V | G |
| 211 | F | V |
| 306 | G | A |

The candidate preserves **311** source coordinates and re-encrypts exactly
after those five changes. No source erasure, length change, column-order
change or square relabelling is involved. The known raw `J` in the date
and the `J` strings in the footer are untouched.

## Source and credit

J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed
p210 / PDF p213, [public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
Literal rows, source image metadata and every source pair are in the
[source package](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/README.md).
The published period key retains its external attribution in
[data/keys.json](../../data/keys.json).

Source inspection and this annotated edition: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.
No first historical decipherment priority is claimed.


# p92 A — Dutch courier Vreede's passage to Constantinople

[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source certificate](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/certificates.json) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Record:** p92 A, 1 November 1918, addressed in clear to the Political
Section at Bucharest. **Result:** all **214 plaintext positions** are fixed
from **428 unchanged source coordinates** with the published Nov1–3 key.
One explicit coordinate substitution gives the readable text below.

## Reading

**Readable German:**

> Nr. 607. Bitte dafuer zu sorgen, dass niederlaendischer Kurier,
> Rittmeister Vreede, der mit unserem COSPOLI-Kurier zusammen am 3.11.
> hier abfaehrt, in Braila mit dem Schiff nach Konstantinopel
> mitgenommen wird. Auswaertiges Amt. 1. 41362.

**Meaning:** The Foreign Office asks the Political Section to arrange for
the Dutch courier, Rittmeister Vreede, to be taken aboard the ship from
Braila to Constantinople. He is to leave the sender's location on
3 November together with its `COSPOLI` courier.

The surname **VREEDE**, rank, nationality, **607**, **3.11**, Braila,
Constantinople and closing **1 / 41362** all come directly from unchanged
source coordinates. The text does not identify Vreede by first name.
`COSPOLI` is retained as transmitted, and the source does not itself name
the location meant by “here.” Spacing, punctuation and capitalization are
editorial.

## Source and one repair

The [source image](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/sources/p92_A.png) reads:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
UKS v LP (8.25 p.m., November 1st)
1730 (1/11) POLITISCHE ABTEILUNG BUKAREST
RICHI-428?
```

</details>

The question mark after the advertised length is literally printed; the
body contains exactly **428 valid coordinates**. Its fifteenth group is
clearly `VVVFG`. The earlier OCR's shorter `V?FG` is not used as a source
transcription or repaired by inventing a historical coordinate.

The direct raw decipherment is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
NRX607XBITTEDAFUERZUSORGENXDASSNIEDERLAENDISCHERKURIERXRITTMEISTERXVREEDEXDERMITUNSEREMXCOSPOLIXKURIERZUSAMM7NAMX3X11XHIERABFAEHRTXINXBRAILAXMITDEMSCHIFFNACHXKONSTANTINOPELXMITGENOMMENWIRDXAUSWAERTIGESAMTX1X41362XX
```

</details>

Only **`ZUSAMM7N → ZUSAMMEN`** is proposed. It costs one source-coordinate
change, zero-based index **123: F→V**. The candidate preserves the other
**427** coordinates, changes no length or key, and re-encrypts exactly to
that explicitly repaired source.

## Reproduction and credit

The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher

# p96 B — Entry permission for Filittis and family

[Case guide](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Source image](../../sources/excerpts/other_p96_B.png) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** A source-reviewed supplementary message. The unchanged published
`Nov1-3` key fixes **180 of 181 raw plaintext positions**. One invalid printed
coordinate remains an erasure. The most likely place-name requires that fill
and one further change to a valid coordinate.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> Nr. 605. Auf Telegramm Nr. 536. Rheinbaben an Horstmann:
> Nach Mitteilung Passzentrale stellvertretenden Generalstabes ist nunmehr
> Einreise Filittis mit Familie aus [Kopenhagen] genehmigt. Auswaertig.

**Meaning:** Message 605, replying to telegram 536: Rheinbaben informs Horstmann
that, according to the passport office of the deputy General Staff, entry for
Filittis and his family from Copenhagen has now been approved. The closing
`AUSWAERTIG` identifies the message with foreign-affairs business; the decoded
text does not spell out a longer institutional title.

The personal names and the numbers **605** and **536** are directly decoded.
This case does not identify which individuals the surnames designate or add a
destination that is absent from the body. The cleartext address is the
political section in Bucharest. The German wording retains the telegram's
omitted articles; spacing and punctuation are editorial.

## The place-name and its exact uncertainty

The unchanged source yields:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
NRX605XAUFTELEGRAMMNRX536XRHEINBABENXANXHORSTMANNXNACHMITTEILUNGPASSZENTRALESTELLVERTRETENDENGENERALSTABESISTNUNMEHREINREISEXFILITTISXMITFAMILIEAUSXKOPENH?HENXGENEHMIGTXAUSWAERTIGXX
```

</details>

The group **`ACVGD`** visibly contains `C`, which is outside the ADFGVX
coordinate alphabet. The literal source retains that `C`; the analytical
transcript represents it as `?`. The likely `KOPENHAGEN` is therefore an
editorial reading of `KOPENH?HEN`, with the following exact cost:

| Source index, zero based | Printed | Proposed | Type |
| ---: | :---: | :---: | --- |
| 226 | C | G | Supply one invalid-coordinate erasure. |
| 340 | V | F | Replace one valid printed coordinate. |

The candidate re-encrypts exactly to this reconstruction, with **360 valid
source coordinates unchanged**. No coordinate is inserted or deleted and no
key cell is reassigned. Copenhagen is strongly suggested by the word shape
and the resulting sentence, but the two repaired letters are not reported as
unchanged-source recoveries.

## Source and verification

Printed p96 / PDF p99, section B, headed **1 November 1918**:
`UKS v LP (8.11 p.m., November 1st); 1800 (1/11) POLITISCHE ABTL BUKAREST;
RICHI-362`.

The [literal source record](../../experiments/corpus_readings/selected_sources.json)
and [coordinate certificate](../../experiments/corpus_readings/certificates.json)
preserve the invalid glyph, all 181 position maps, the complete published key
and the proposed place-name's substitutions.

```sh
python3 experiments/corpus_readings/verify.py --verify
```

**Credit:** George Lasry's published period key and its historical sources are
retained in [the key register](../../data/keys.json). Source inspection,
verification and this annotated reading are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.
No first-decipherment priority is claimed for this supplementary message.

# p203 C / p210 C — inquiries about Richter in Aleppo

[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source certificate](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/certificates.json) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Records:** two related personnel inquiries, on 18 and 20 November 1918,
under different published period keys. **Result:** the earlier message
fixes **93 of 96 raw positions** without any source edit. The later fixes
**201 of 204**, and its readable body requires six coordinate substitutions
and three source-erasure fills. Their postal-number fields differ; they
are not forced into one recovered number.

## The earlier inquiry, p203 C

**Readable German:**

> K.M., Abt. Nachrichtenmittel, erbittet Nachricht Verbleib Untffz.
> Richter, Funkerpark Aleppo, Feldpost ???.

**Meaning:** The War Ministry's communications-equipment section asks
for news of the whereabouts of an NCO named Richter at the radio park
in Aleppo. Its field-post number remains unresolved.

The source abbreviation **UNTFFZ** is retained. Its interpretation as an
NCO is supported by the later message's directly read **UNTEROFFZ**.
The earlier message itself does not supply the first name Kurt.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
KMXABTXNACHRICHTENMITTELXERBITTETNACHRICHTVERBLEIBUNTFFZXRICHTERXFUNKERPARKXALEPPOXFELDPOSTX???X
```

</details>

All **192** coordinates in [p203 C](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/sources/p203_C.png)
are valid and unchanged. The three question marks are unknown square-cell
values, not damaged source glyphs. The source section belongs to the
**18 November** heading, below an earlier 16 November section:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
XYZ v LP (03.51 p.m., November 18th)
IWE KOW AS FUER XYZ 14.50 (18/11)
RICHI-192
```

</details>

## The later inquiry, p210 C

The same-length editorial reconstruction reads:

**Readable German:**

> Ist ueber den Unteroffz. Kurt Richter, Aleppo, Armeenachrichtenpark
> J527, Deutsche Feldpost 227, Auskunft ueber jetzigen Standort oder
> Verbleib zu erfahren? [Raw following character: J.]
> Nr. Q90 strich JJ, J4, A. Nch. Kriegsminist., Allgem.
> Kriegsdepartement.

**Meaning:** The later message asks whether information can be obtained
about the current location or whereabouts of NCO Kurt Richter in Aleppo,
giving an Army Signals Park designation and field-post number. The name
**KURT RICHTER**, Aleppo, and **FELDPOST227** are directly read.
The designation **J527**, references **Q90 / JJ / J4**, and the isolated
`J` following `ERFAHREN` remain literal. They are not silently converted to
numerals or a reconstructed reference.

The [p210 C source](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/sources/p210_C.png)
has **408** coordinate slots and this header:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
XYZ v LP (02.55 p.m., November 20th)
17.40 (20/11)
RICHI-408
```

</details>

Its raw decipherment under the unchanged Nov19–21 key is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
IS0XEBERDENUNTEROFFZXKURTXRICHTERXALEPPOXARMEENACHRICHTENPARKXJ527XDEUTSCLEFELDPOSTX227XAUSKUNFTUEBER3ETZIGENSTANDORTOWERVERBLEIBZUERFAHRENJXNRXQ90STRICHJJXJ4XAXNCHX?RIEGSMINISTXALLGEMXK?I?GSDEPARTEMENTXX
```

</details>

The invalid source glyphs in **AFEVF**, **CXVVA** and **EGFDF** retain
their positions in the literal transcript. For analysis, they are masked
as erasures at source indices **302, 365 and 385**. The candidate fills
those slots with **F, G and F**, respectively. The remaining body repairs
change six valid coordinates:

| Source index, zero-based | Source | Proposed |
|---:|:---:|:---:|
| 50 | G | X |
| 61 | G | F |
| 230 | A | X |
| 265 | A | X |
| 316 | G | F |
| 378 | X | V |

These give the readable opening `IST UEBER`, `DEUTSCHE`, `JETZIGEN`,
`ODER` and the War Ministry closing. The candidate preserves **399 valid
source coordinates** and re-encrypts exactly after the six changes and
three fills. It adds no plaintext letters and does not change the key.
The question mark in the spaced German is editorial punctuation; the
following literal `J` is explicitly acknowledged above.

## Why the postal number is not transferred across keys

The shared surname, rank and Aleppo location support reading these as
related inquiries. They do not establish that the address fields were
identical or copied without error.

| Message and positions | Printed-key result | Observed pairs |
|---|---|---|
| p203 C, 92–94 | `???` | `VA VA VV` under Nov16–18 |
| p210 C, 84–86 | `227` | `DG DG DA` under Nov19–21 |

The earlier first two digits are one shared unknown, and the last digit
must be different under an injective square. The base domain for each
cell is `{0,3,4,5,6,7,8,9}`. The later **227** cannot simply be copied back:
that would put `2` at **VA**, while the unchanged Nov16–18 square already
puts `2` at **DV**. The coordinate certificate checks this conflict.

The separate [p201/p206 order-date inference](../military/p201_p206_orders.md)
conditionally assigns **VA=5**. If accepted, it would make this earlier
field `55?`; it would not settle the mismatch with `227`. This edition
preserves the evidence without selecting a changed address, a copying
error, or a different digit labelling as the explanation.

## Source, reproduction and credit

The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, printed pp. 203 and 210 / PDF pp. 206 and 213 in the
[public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [source package](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/README.md) preserves
literal rows, source images, complete published key snapshots and every
plaintext-to-coordinate map. The existing keys retain their external
attribution in [data/keys.json](../../data/keys.json).

Source inspection, related-message comparison and this edition:
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment priority
is claimed.

```sh
python3 experiments/corpus_recovery/verify.py --verify
```

# Roesler: leave and departure on the next ship

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

The native p102 D frame concerns leave, the arrival of Rittm. Roesler, and departure on the next ship. It ends with **HOENIGSCHMID** and the abbreviation **S.M.St.Pers.** The complete body already appears in the earlier OCR screen; this edition adds source verification and a reproducible certificate without changing any coordinate.

Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Source: J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed p102 (PDF page105). The Nov1–3 square and column ranks are the published key credited to George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker. Earlier OCR bodies are retained in [prior evidence](../../experiments/nov1_ammunition_and_leave/prior_evidence.json); this is not a claim of first historical body recovery.

## p102 D

### Source and frame

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — literal cleartext header:**

```text
D) FÜR COS, ÖST v NKJ (0.24 a.m., November 3rd)
UNG MISSION BARON FRANKENSTEIN FÜR HPTM BENEDIKT 0730 (1)
RICHI-258
```

</details>

The [full page](../../experiments/nov1_ammunition_and_leave/sources/p102_full.png) and [native C/D detail](../../experiments/nov1_ammunition_and_leave/sources/p102_C_D_detail.png) show all 258 coordinates, matching the advertised length. The source frame contains no masks, added slots or excluded coordinates.

| Layer | Fixed plaintext positions | Observed substitutions | Source fills | Added / excluded coordinates |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Raw output, native 258-coordinate frame | 129 / 129 | 0 | 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Edited output | Same as raw | 0 | 0 | 0 / 0 |

### Raw output

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — published Nov1–3 key, native source frame:**

```text
AUFEXHXNR109XXURLAUBNACHEINTREFFENRITTMXROESLERXROESLERBEWILLIGTXGEHTMITNAECHSTEMSCHIFFDORTHINABXXOBSTXHOENIGSCHMIDXSXMXSTXPERSXX
```

</details>

### Readable German

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation only; umlauts display their literal two-letter equivalents:**

> Auf E. H. Nr. 109. Urlaub nach Eintreffen Rittm. Roesler. Roesler bewilligt. Geht mit nächstem Schiff dorthin ab. Obst. Hoenigschmid. S. M. St. Pers.

`ROESLER` occurs twice, separated by `X`; both occurrences remain in the display. The punctuation around “Roesler bewilligt” is editorial and does not settle the repeated name’s grammatical attachment. `HOENIGSCHMID`, `109`, and `SXMXSTXPERS` are unchanged. The displayed name Roesler is not normalized to another spelling.

The source header names `BARON FRANKENSTEIN` and `HPTM BENEDIKT`; they are cleartext addressing evidence, not additional recovered ciphertext names. `UNG` and the station label `ÖST` remain as printed. The old OCR ciphertext and plaintext agree exactly with the native reading in this edition.

### Evidence and limits

The [input transcription](../../experiments/nov1_ammunition_and_leave/inputs.json) preserves every source row, the published key and the exact readable display. The [certificate](../../experiments/nov1_ammunition_and_leave/certificates.json) maps each plaintext position to its two source coordinates, preserves all numeral labels, and checks every non-`X` label in the displayed German. # Two-part discharge instruction naming Rudolf twice

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p108 B1/B2, PDF p111, are headed
`OSM v LP (9.25 p.m., November 2nd)` and `1710 (2/11) 2 TEILE`.
The consecutive part labels and the split **AUS / MILITAERDIENST**
connect the two parts. Both use the unchanged published **Nov1–3** key.
The separate p108 A naval inquiry is not part of this assembly.

## p108 B1

The [first part](../../experiments/p108_naval_and_personnel/sources/p108_B1.png)
contains **130 valid coordinates**, matching `1 TL RICHI-130`.
It fixes **65 / 65 plaintext positions** without repairs.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — native 130-coordinate frame:**

```text
MILITAERMISSXBITTEGEFRXRUDOLFRUDOLFZUGETDERDEUTSCHBOTSCHSOFORTAUS
```

</details>

**Readable German — spacing, punctuation and umlaut:**

> Militärmiss. Bitte Gefr. Rudolf Rudolf, zuget. der deutsch. Botsch.,
> sofort aus

The sentence continues with **MILITAERDIENST** in part 2. The two
occurrences of **RUDOLF** remain as transmitted; they are not silently
collapsed or assigned to independently identified first and family names.
The abbreviations **GEFR**, **ZUGET**, **DEUTSCH BOTSCH** remain abbreviated
in the readable layer.

## p108 B2

The [second part](../../experiments/p108_naval_and_personnel/sources/p108_B2.png)
has **135 visible coordinates**, although its heading says
`2 TL RICHI-136`. The first row's fifth group is **DAGD**, with four
symbols. The following raw and edited layers use the explicitly
conditional model of one missing coordinate after its initial D:
**D?AGD**. The scan identifies the short group, but does not specify that
exact internal loss position.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 136-coordinate frame with one missing coordinate inside DAGD:**

```text
MILITAERDIENSTENTLASSENDEUTSCHEBOTSCHBENACHRNACHRICHXNACHCHEF2BO52?X
```

</details>

**Readable German — spacing, punctuation and umlaut, with the unresolved reference retained:**

> Militärdienst entlassen. Deutsche Botsch. benachr. Nachrich.
> Nach Chef 2 BO 52?.

The two parts request immediate discharge from military service and
embassy notification. They do not certify that those actions happened.
The consecutive **BENACHR / NACHRICH / NACHCHEF** fields remain separate;
no missing word or expansion is supplied to make the closing smoother.

## Conditional interpretation and every short-group placement

All five insertion positions inside **DAGD** are retained. The following
costs refer to a separately disclosed diagnostic constraint: preserve the
selected readable prefix through `NACHCHEF2BO52`, while leaving each
alternative's final reference label as found. This is a lexical constraint,
not independent ciphertext proof of the loss geometry.

| Group model | Observed substitutions for the stated prefix | Missing-coordinate fills | Resulting reference |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `?DAGD` | 0 | 1 | `2BO522X` |
| `D?AGD` | 0 | 0 | `2BO52?X` |
| `DA?GD` | 0 | 1 | `2BO520X` |
| `DAG?D` | 1 | 1 | `2BO520X` |
| `DAGD?` | 2 | 1 | `2BO520X` |

The diagnostic fills and substitutions in this table are **not adopted
or included in the primary repair count**. The primary frame retains
**67 / 68 fixed positions**. Its unknown plaintext position **66** has
pair **F?** and domain **027GQT**, supplied by source index **35** and the
missing coordinate. Even a decimal-only assumption leaves **0, 2 or 7**;
no digit is chosen.

The verifier enumerates all **30 geometry-labeled completions** of the
five group models and six coordinate values. They produce **26 distinct
complete ciphertexts and plaintexts**. Applying the stated readable-prefix
constraint leaves six distinct completions, precisely the six completions
of **D?AGD**. The filled `?DAGD` and `DA?GD` alternatives duplicate two of
those complete ciphertexts, with reference endings **522** and **520**.
This finite audit preserves the ambiguity instead of presenting one
reference number as solved. Every complete witness re-encrypts exactly.

B1/B2 together contain **265 visible coordinates**, **266 modeled
coordinates** and **132 / 133 fixed plaintext positions under the stated
frames**. The primary layers use no observed substitutions and no fills.
The two bodies already appeared in earlier unreviewed repository
candidates; this edition supplies source layout, complete geometry
accounting and exact reproduction, with published key credit retained.
It makes no historical first-solution claim. See
[inputs](../../experiments/p108_naval_and_personnel/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/p108_naval_and_personnel/certificates.json)
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/p108_naval_and_personnel/README.md).

# Braila inquiry about dragoman Schaefer's return from leave

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

## p107 C

Childs p107 C, PDF p110, is a separate message headed
`UKS v LP (3.04 a.m., November 3rd)` and `SS 2025 (2/11)`.
The [source crop](../../experiments/p107_railway_and_dragoman/sources/p107_C.png)
contains **348 source slots**, matching `RICHI-348`: **347 unambiguous
coordinates and one damaged or overstruck glyph** at source index 45.
It uses the unchanged published **Nov1–3** key.
Source and plaintext indices below are zero-based; printed rows and groups
are counted from one.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 348-coordinate frame:**

```text
GEHEIMRATENDERHEIDENBRAILAXXISTRUECKKEHRDRAGOMANSXSCHAEFERXDESSENURLAUBBALDABLAEUFTSO?ERNUEBERHAUPTAUSFUEHRBARJETZTERWUENSCHTUNDZWECKMAESSIGDRAHTBERIC1TXXAUSWAERTCGESXA2TX1XB
```

**Edited output — three observed-coordinate substitutions and one damaged-glyph fill:**

```text
GEHEIMRATENDERHEIDENBRAILAXXISTRUECKKEHRDRAGOMANSXSCHAEFERXDESSENURLAUBBALDABLAEUFTSOFERNUEBERHAUPTAUSFUEHRBARJETZTERWUENSCHTUNDZWECKMAESSIGDRAHTBERICHTXXAUSWAERTIGESXAMTX1XB
```

</details>

The observed-coordinate changes are source **182 F→V**, **253 X→V** and
**292 D→A**, repairing `DRAHTBERIC1T` and `AUSWAERTCGES A2T`.
The separate fill **45 ?→V** supplies F in `SO?ERN`. The conservative raw
layer fixes **173/174 positions**; the unchanged edited candidate fixes
**174/174** and re-encrypts exactly. There are still **four coordinate
operations**. Reclassifying the damaged glyph does not reduce the total
repair count or add a newly observed plaintext letter.

**Readable German — spacing, punctuation and umlauts; the opaque address remains unexpanded:**

> GEHEIMRATENDERHEIDEN, Braila. Ist Rückkehr Dragomans Schaefer, dessen
> Urlaub bald abläuft, sofern überhaupt ausführbar, jetzt erwünscht und
> zweckmäßig? Drahtbericht. Auswärtiges Amt. 1. B.

The question explicitly retains both conditions: whether return is
feasible at all, and whether it is now desired and expedient. It requests
a telegraphic report; it does not establish a completed return or replace
the question with a return order.

## Conditional interpretation and source qualifications

### Source 45: preserve the damaged glyph

The first glyph of the second row's second group is conservatively recorded
as **`?XGFF`**. The [detail crop](../../experiments/p107_railway_and_dragoman/sources/p107_C_source45.png)
comes directly from PDF page 110, rectangle `[188,551,227,568]`, rendered
at scale 16. Its upper strokes look V-like, while lower feet suggest an
overprint or damage; it differs from the adjacent clear X and nearby clear
V. Visual review does not establish an unconditional X or V. The `?`
records this uncertainty in one existing source slot, without adding a gap.

That slot supplies the second coordinate of plaintext position **85**.
The conservative pair **`A?`** permits **`9FILOU`**. The main reading selects
F by filling the glyph with V; the source does not independently fix F.
The certificate retains two explicit, separately identified glyph assumptions:

| Source handling | Fixed raw positions | Plaintext 85 | Changes from that stated branch to the unchanged main candidate |
|---|---:|:---:|---|
| Conservative `?` | 173/174 | `?` | 3 observed substitutions and 1 damaged-glyph fill |
| Assume X | 174/174 | `9` | 3 observed substitutions and 1 replacement of the assumed X |
| Assume V | 174/174 | `F` | 3 observed substitutions; V has already been assumed |

The two fully assigned branches are **hypotheses about the same glyph**,
not independent observations, parallel copies or additional records. Their
branch-relative costs do not replace the primary three-substitution,
one-fill account. The former definite-X transcription is retained through
the X branch, including its `SO9ERN` output.

The frozen earlier OCR already marked this slot `?` and produced `SO?ERN`.
It is an earlier transcription of this same source, not independent evidence
for a different transmission. The new image review restores the conservative
uncertainty instead of claiming a new decipherment.

### Preserved labels and a separate clear glyph

The continuous address **GEHEIMRATENDERHEIDENBRAILA** and surname string
**SCHAEFER** remain as decoded. The displayed boundary before Braila does
not establish a particular person's identity, nor does it normalize the
opaque address into an assumed historical name. The final **1 B** labels
remain literal.

The [detail crop](../../experiments/p107_railway_and_dragoman/sources/p107_C_VDVGV.png)
shows G at source **133** in **VDVGV**. A preliminary C reading from the
small full-page image was rejected before publication; no extra erasure
or fill is introduced at that position. This clear-G check is separate from
the damaged source 45 and the three observed-coordinate substitutions above.

The earlier unreviewed repository candidate already contained this body.
The source edition adds exact transcription, repair accounting and
re-encryption, with published key credit retained. It makes no historical
first-solution claim. See the [inputs](../../experiments/p107_railway_and_dragoman/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/p107_railway_and_dragoman/certificates.json)
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/p107_railway_and_dragoman/README.md).

# Von Schorlemer: demobilization work inquiry and reply

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

A clear-address request on p122 and an encrypted reply on p155 form a source-linked exchange about von Schorlemer's availability for demobilization work. The earlier request asks whether he can be released to the Trade Ministry; the later administrative-staff reply says he cannot currently be spared. Both native frames and every repair remain explicit. The later reply supports the name and topic; the 33 supplied mask values in the first request remain editorial proposals.

## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed page excerpt](../../experiments/schorlemer_demobilization_inquiry/sources/p122_reviewed.png) · [Second source excerpt](../../experiments/schorlemer_demobilization_inquiry/sources/p155_reviewed.png) · [Exact inputs](../../experiments/schorlemer_demobilization_inquiry/inputs.json) · [Position-by-position certificates](../../experiments/schorlemer_demobilization_inquiry/certificates.json)

The unchanged published keys are `Nov4-6`, `Nov7-9`. The [earlier unreviewed candidates](../../experiments/schorlemer_demobilization_inquiry/prior_candidates.json) and [original OCR records](../../experiments/schorlemer_demobilization_inquiry/ocr_snapshot.json) are preserved. The present work supplies an image-reviewed source edition and a reproducible repair account; it does not claim that every body is a first public decipherment.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Coordinate substitutions | Source-mask fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [p122 B](#p122-b) | 252 | 93 / 126 | 5 | 33 |
| [p155 B](#p155-b) | 160 | 76 / 80 | 3 | 4 |

## p122 B

**Source transcription — header:** `B) NKJ v LP (08.40 p.m., November 4th); FUER UKS 1400 (4). OBERLEUTNANT VON SCHORLEMER OBERKOMMANDO M VERWALTUNGSSTAB; RICHI-252`

**Readable German** — based on the explicitly repaired output below.

> Erbitte Rueckantwort durch Funkspruch, ob Sie zur Beschaeftigung im Handelsministerium, Demobilmachungsgruppe, abkoemmlich. Handelsminister.

**Meaning:** The Trade Minister asks for a radio reply on whether the addressee can be released for work in the ministry demobilization group. The clear header names First Lieutenant von Schorlemer at the Oberkommando M administrative staff.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
E?BI?TERUE?KA?TFOT?DU?CHFUN?SP?UCHO?SI?ZU?BE?CH?E?TI?UN?IM?ANDEL?M?NISTE?GU?XDEMO?I?MACHU??S?RPPPE?A?KOESM?IC?XHAND?L?MINIS?ER
```

**Edited output** — 5 observed-coordinate substitutions and 33 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
ERBITTERUECKANTWORTDURCHFUNKSPRUCHOBSIEZURBESCHAEFTIGUNGIMHANDELSMINISTERIUMXDEMOBILMACHUNGSGRUPPEXABKOEMMLICHXHANDELSMINISTER
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The source contains 33 printed dashes, including six complete masked groups. They are part of the native 252-slot frame. Their supplied values are editorial source-mask fills, not recovered visible coordinates.
- The five observed-coordinate substitutions are separately priced. They repair word-level corruptions; there is no source insertion or change of key.
- The clear address is an independent source witness for the surname in the later p155 B response. The two bodies were enciphered under different published period keys.

## p155 B

**Source transcription — header:** `B) LP v NKJ (7.09 p.m., November 7th); 0800 VON UKS (7/11); RICHI-160`

**Readable German** — based on the explicitly repaired output below.

> Handelsminister Berlin. Oblt. v. Schorlemer z. Zeit hier nicht abkoemmlich. OKM Verw. Stab.

**Meaning:** The administrative staff informs the Trade Minister in Berlin that First Lieutenant von Schorlemer cannot currently be released.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
KANDELSMINISTERBERLINXOBLTXVXSCKORLEMERXZXZEIT?IERNI?HTABKOEM?LICKXOKMX?ERWXSTAB
```

**Edited output** — 3 observed-coordinate substitutions and 4 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
HANDELSMINISTERBERLINXOBLTXVXSCHORLEMERXZXZEITHIERNICHTABKOEMMLICHXOKMXVERWXSTAB
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The source visibly prints four dashes. The 160-slot native frame is unchanged.
- The name repair SCKORLEMER to SCHORLEMER is supported by the independent clear p122 B address, not by a guessed biography. No first name or unique historical person is supplied.
- The exchange concerns availability for duty; it does not itself establish that a reassignment or recall actually occurred.

## Evidence and credit

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates replay every coordinate alteration, compare the independent column/domain reconstruction with the cipher implementation, and re-encrypt every complete edited output. For a partial output, an injective global completion of the square and residual source masks supplies an explicitly nonhistorical roundtrip witness. Each readable passage preserves every nonseparator output label; literal protected fields are also checked without removing their internal separators. Source crops are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and RGB-pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/schorlemer_demobilization_inquiry/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to regenerate and compare the delivered source pixels.

A roundtrip proves compatibility with a stated reading. Editorial spelling repairs remain proposals, and literal number labels are not automatically historical dates, quantities or reference numbers.

# Sevastopol: consent to a personnel transfer

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

## p104 E3

Childs p104, PDF p107; [reviewed source crop](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/sources/p104_E3.png). Key: unchanged published **Nov1–3**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — literal received header:**

```text
E) POT v NKJ (9.06 a.m., November 4th)
0810 (2)
3 TL RICHI-140
```

**Raw output — native 140-slot frame; 68/70 fixed positions:**

```text
KOMDEURXRESXJ?EGXBATLX?ISTMITVERSETZGXEINRERSTANDEDXXGOUVXSEWASTOPOLXX
```

**Edited output — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions; 1 source-mask fill; 69/70 fixed positions:**

```text
KOMDEURXRESXJAEGXBATLX?ISTMITVERSETZGXEINVERSTANDENXXGOUVXSEWASTOPOLXX
```

</details>

Observed source changes, with zero-based indices: **41 A→G**, **130 A→G**.

Source-mask fills: **119 C→G**.

The coordinate-pair certificate verifies every fixed candidate position and retains the unresolved source mask. A complete plaintext re-encryption is not claimed for the remaining unknown position.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Komdeur. Res. Jaeg. Batl. ? ist mit Versetzg. einverstanden. Gouv. Sewastopol.

**Meaning:** A surviving third part says that the commander of a reserve Jaeger battalion agrees to a transfer. The battalion field remains unknown. The signature gives the Sevastopol governor abbreviation; no officer identity is supplied.

## Unresolved unit and source glyphs

The source prints C-like noncoordinate glyphs in `GAAXC` and `GXAVC`, at source indices **39** and **119**. The latter is supplied as G to read `JAEG`; the former remains masked. Its resulting one-position battalion field is the literal `?` in both the edited stream and readable display. There is no assignment of an assumed battalion number.

The two observed-coordinate changes repair `EINRERSTANDED` to `EINVERSTANDEN`. The remaining abbreviations, including `KOMDEUR`, remain as transmitted. This source is explicitly part 3; the absent first two parts are not reconstructed.

## Attribution and reproducibility

Earlier unreviewed repository candidates already identified these bodies. This edition reviews the source images, retains their literal observations and publishes the exact repair or frame account; it makes no first-decipherment claim. The key keeps its earlier published provenance.

[Inputs](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/inputs.json), [full certificates](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/certificates.json), [earlier candidates](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/prior_candidates.json), and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/README.md) preserve the evidence.

# Siegfried's assignment to the Military Mission is cancelled

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The source's 401-coordinate frame yields a clear first portion followed by a
pairing-phase failure. A conditional surplus-X model recovers the rest of the
order, with an exact source-shaped forward witness. Its complete closing has
independent, unedited coordinate-pair support from the previously reviewed
Osthoff order. Neither the error model nor the shared formula assigns a
biographical identity to Siegfried or Marschall.

## p135 A

Childs p135, PDF p138; [source crop](../../experiments/siegfried_assignment_cancellation/sources/p135_A.png).
The page heading and internal date are 5 November, while reception is 7 November.
The key remains the published **Nov4–6** key.

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — literal header:**

```text
5th NOVEMBER, 1918.
A) YZ v LP (8.59 a.m., November 7th)
FUER YZ 2400 (5/11)
RICHI-401
```

</details>

The scan contains **401 source slots**, exactly its printed `RICHI-401`:
397 valid coordinates and four printed dash slots. The original inverse
transposition leaves one final coordinate unpaired.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — unaltered 401-coordinate frame, with its final orphan retained separately in the certificate:**

```text
DTSCHEMILITAERMISS?ONINKONSTANTINOPELXZUNR45610XKOMDODESOBERLTSSIEGFRIEDNACHDERTUERKEIDESZENZUTEILUNGZURMILITAEEMRSNYSL4N6FXRGA13FQLMUKV1B14IWUXRGETMF13WLJ66WL4Q?A1ONJQ1?ZT4NFKFW?EYNMLLLOGR6LZZL6JYETM
```

</details>

## A conditional surplus coordinate before transposition

The proposed error stage is precise: an extra observed **X** entered the
fractionated coordinate stream **before transposition**. After applying the
original 401-slot inverse transposition, excluding that X restores an even
400-coordinate paired stream. The received ciphertext is not shortened to
400 before inverse transposition.

Two adjacent interim X coordinates are indistinguishable under this model:

| Excluded interim position | Original received source position | Observed value |
|---:|---:|:---:|
|230|296|X|
|231|84|X|

Either exclusion gives the same 400-coordinate interim stream and the same
candidate source-shaped ciphertext. Both source-origin alternatives remain
in the certificate; no unique physical origin is asserted. The excluded X
is an observed coordinate with an explicit one-coordinate model cost, not a
free mask or an invisible omission from the source transcription.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional surplus-X exclusion at interim 230 or 231; 196/200 fixed positions:**

```text
DTSCHEMILITAERMISS?ONINKONSTANTINOPELXZUNR45610XKOMDODESOBERLTSSIEGFRIEDNACHDERTUERKEIDESZENZUTEILUNGZURMILITAEEMRSSIONISTAUFGEHOBENXAKOFOLGTXAUFALLERHOECHSTENB?FEHLCHEF?ILITAER?AHINETTSFGHTMARSCHALLX
```

**Edited output — same declared model, seven observed-coordinate substitutions and four printed-mask fills; 200/200 fixed positions:**

```text
DTSCHEMILITAERMISSIONINKONSTANTINOPELXZUNR45610XKOMDODESOBERLTSSIEGFRIEDNACHDERTUERKEIDESSENZUTEILUNGZURMILITAERMISSIONISTAUFGEHOBENXAKOFOLGTXAUFALLERHOECHSTENBEFEHLCHEFMILITAERKABINETTSFRHRMARSCHALLX
```

</details>

Observed substitutions, with zero-based received source indices: **127 F→X**, **186 A→V**, **187 V→A**, **225 F→V**, **258 X→V**, **293 V→G**, **367 A→X**.

Printed-mask fills: **42→A**, **43→X**, **44→F**, **167→V**.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Dtsche Militaermission in Konstantinopel. Zu Nr 45610. Komdo des Oberlts Siegfried nach der Tuerkei, dessen Zuteilung zur Militaermission ist aufgehoben. AKO folgt. Auf allerhoechsten Befehl Chef Militaerkabinetts Frhr Marschall.

**Meaning:** Regarding 45610 and the posting of Oberleutnant Siegfried to Turkey, the message cancels his assignment to the Military Mission. AKO follows. It closes with the Chief of the Military Cabinet formula and FRHR MARSCHALL. The message does not report a completed return journey or establish a separate biographical identity.

The original reference **45610** and the abbreviations **DTSCHE**, **KOMDO**,
**OBERLTS**, **AKO** and **FRHR** remain literal in the reading. No digit is
relabelled, and no abbreviation is expanded into an independently asserted
person or document.

## Exact forward witness and bounded stage comparison

To reconstruct the actual source shape:

1. Fractionate the proposed 200-character plaintext with the unchanged square.
2. Reinsert the observed surplus X at interim 230 or 231, restoring 401 coordinates.
3. Transpose those 401 coordinates with the unchanged column ranks.
4. Compare with the literal source: exactly seven observed substitutions and
   four dash fills remain, and no received source position has been deleted.

This replay succeeds for both aliases. Ordinary encryption of the 200-position
proposal into a 400-coordinate ciphertext is not presented as the source
witness; the declared surplus stage is part of the verified reconstruction.

All single-coordinate exclusions at both relevant stages were priced against
the same complete proposed text:

| Model stage | Candidates examined | Minimum observed substitutions | Minimum positions | Mask fills at minima | Observed surplus/excluded coordinates |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
|After inverse transposition of the 401-slot source|401|7|Interim 230 or 231|4|1|
|From the received ciphertext before inverse transposition|401|144|Source 297, 298 or 299|4|1|

The comparison favors the declared stage within this fixed-template,
single-coordinate family. It does not prove what happened historically,
exclude multi-error explanations, or turn the whole tail into a direct
ordinary-frame decoding.

## Independent support for the complete closing

The last **58 plaintext positions**, beginning `AUFALLERHOECHSTENBEFEHL`,
match the direct raw closing of [p149 A2](osthoff.md). That older physical
record has its own [source crop](../../experiments/corpus_attack/sources/childs_p149_A2.png),
which was reviewed again for this comparison. The new certificate checks
all 58 coordinate pairs, their letters and both sets of source positions.

This supports the repairs in `BEFEHL`, `MILITAERKABINETTS` and `FRHR` without
inventing a smoother signature from general historical expectations. The
parallel concerns Osthoff, so its other body words and identity are not
transferred to Siegfried's order. It is not counted as another newly recovered
record.

## Attribution and evidence

The published key and previously reviewed Osthoff source retain their
original attribution. Earlier unreviewed OCR screens for p135 are frozen
separately; their garbled output is not treated as a primary transcription.
This edition supplies source review, the explicit surplus-coordinate model,
both aliases, finite stage prices and the complete qualified reading. It
makes no historical first-decipherment claim.

[Inputs](../../experiments/siegfried_assignment_cancellation/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/siegfried_assignment_cancellation/certificates.json),
[prior screens](../../experiments/siegfried_assignment_cancellation/prior_candidates.json)
and [reproduction](../../experiments/siegfried_assignment_cancellation/README.md)
provide the complete evidence.

# Delegates directed through Spa toward Berlin

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

**Prior body and historical discussion:** George Lasry, Ingo Niebel,
Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker, *Deciphering ADFGVX messages from the Eastern
Front of World War I* (2016), §6.4, author PDF p24,
[DOI](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461). That discussion
explicitly cites p175 A together with p172 C. This edition adds a
source-exact transcript and quantified repairs; it does not claim the
travel message as a new historical decipherment.

Childs printed p175 A, PDF p178, contains two parts under
`ZM v SY (10.57 p.m., November 10th); VE (10) 2 TLE`.
The text directs delegates by train or car to Spa, with onward travel
toward Berlin on the following date-like field. Its time remains
partly unknown. The two parts have native lengths **192** and **104**
coordinates and use the unchanged published **Nov10–12** key.

## Conditional shared digits

The Berlin journey continuation gains **5.03 p.m.** and reaches **52/52 labels**, retaining its earlier one-coordinate word repair. The [joint reconstruction](../../experiments/nov10_joint_completion/README.md) combines the earlier Marineamt and formation interpretations with the army-number constraint and the mobilization decree; the reversed 7/9 assignment is retained there.

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the joint square:**

> … dass Weiterfahrt nach Berlin am 11.11., 5.03 nachm. OHL RM4B.

<details>
<summary>Exact conditional labels</summary>

**Edited output — p175_A2, conditional shared square; 52/52 fixed positions:**

```text
DASSWEITERFAHRTNACHBERLINAM11X11X5X03XNACHMXOHLRM4BX
```

</details>


## p175 A1

The [source crop](../../experiments/nov10_delegates_and_field_report/sources/p175_A1.png)
directly decrypts to:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
HPTMXMANNITAED1XNAMUTXZUGLEICHFUERHPTMXVXWEIHERXEXIX2XXABGEORDNETEMITZUGODETAUTOSONACHSPALEITENX
```

</details>

Four observed-coordinate repairs give this readable candidate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
HPTMXMANNSTAEDTXNAMURXZUGLEICHFUERHPTMXVXWEIHERXEXIX2XXABGEORDNETEMITZUGODERAUTOSONACHSPALEITENX
```

</details>

It addresses the officer named by the candidate `MANNSTAEDT` at Namur,
also for Captain von Weiher, and directs delegates by train or car to
Spa. The exact address field `EXIX2` is retained. This edition does not
independently identify either officer, expand the unit field or identify
the delegates as particular historical people.

The separate [Namur order witnesses](namur_order_witnesses.md) have
`HPTMANNSTAEDT` without this part's separator after `HPTM`. That string
can instead be segmented as a title followed by `STAEDT`. Their related
wording supports comparison, but does not establish a shared person
or make these messages exact retransmissions. The earlier source
reconciliation remains unchanged.

## p175 A2

The [second-part crop](../../experiments/nov10_delegates_and_field_report/sources/p175_A2.png)
directly reads:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DASSWEITERFAHRTNACHBERLINAM11X11X?X03XNACWMXOHLRM4BX
```

</details>

One observed-coordinate repair changes `NACWM` to `NACHM`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
DASSWEITERFAHRTNACHBERLINAM11X11X?X03XNACHMXOHLRM4BX
```

</details>

The continuation gives onward travel to Berlin on `11X11` at
`?X03 NACHM`, followed by `OHLRM4B`. All these labels remain literal.
The unknown time digit has domain **56789** under the published partial
square. It is not a missing coordinate. Enumerating all **120** full
square completions gives five compatible literal time digits, each in
24 completions, with the exact same candidate ciphertext.

The earlier paper describes a Berlin arrival at 15:00. That historical
narrative is credited separately; the present source edition does not
borrow its time or change `03`, and the wording here concerns onward
travel rather than an independently verified arrival.

## Exact cost and evidence

The two parts contain **296 observed coordinates**, **148 plaintext
positions**, **147 fixed raw labels**, and the same 147 fixed labels
after repairs. They require **five observed-coordinate substitutions**,
with no fill, gap, deletion or key change. The unknown time remains
unknown; no increase in the fixed-label count is claimed for this pair.

[Inputs](../../experiments/nov10_delegates_and_field_report/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/nov10_delegates_and_field_report/certificates.json)
and the [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/nov10_delegates_and_field_report/README.md)
retain every literal row, source position, plaintext domain and edit.
Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are frozen separately.

# Sale of communication apparatus: p157 B1–B2

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** Two readable source parts, with one final source-erased symbol still unresolved.

Source edition and repair accounting: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Published **Nov7–9** square and ranks: Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker, unchanged. Earlier unreviewed OCR-derived candidates already identified much of this apparatus-sale message. They, and their frozen p73 retrieval uses where present, are explicitly preserved; the present work provides the source edition and full repair ledger rather than a universal first-decipherment claim.

## Meaning and source

The telegram tells the Nachrichtenchef that selling apparatus is advisable because of transport difficulties. It says the Romanians want to buy Siemens teleprinters and telephone apparatus, and requests permission and a sale price by radio. This is a request in the text; the edition supplies no evidence that the sale was approved or completed.

Childs printed page 157 / PDF page 160 gives `B) LP v NKJ (7.26 p.m., November 7th)`, `1400 (7) VON UKS 2 TLE`, with lengths 170 and 272. The source heading is 7 November 1918. Both native coordinate frames are preserved exactly.

## Source and repair totals

| Part | Source slots | Printed erasures | Raw fixed positions | Edition fixed positions | Known-coordinate substitutions | Erasure fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| p157_B1 |170|4|81/85|85/85|1|4|
| p157_B2 |272|15|121/136|135/136|5|14|
| **Total** |**442**|**19**|**202/221**|**220/221**|**6**|**18**|

A fixed position means a single symbol under the stated source frame and published key. It does not mean every damaged source letter is historically certain.

## p157 B1 — Apparatus sale recommended because of transport difficulties

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
NA?HRICHTENCHEFGRXHX?XWEGENTRANSPORTSC0WIERIGKE?TENVERKAUFVONAPPARATENEMPFEHLE?SWERTX
```

**Edited output:**

```text
NACHRICHTENCHEFGRXHXQXWEGENTRANSPORTSCHWIERIGKEITENVERKAUFVONAPPARATENEMPFEHLENSWERTX
```

</details>

## p157 B2 — Romanian purchase request and request for permission and price

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
RUMA?NENW?LLEN?IEME?SFERNSCHR?IBERUNDFE?NSPRECHAP?AR?TEKAU?ENX?ENEHMIGUNGUNGVERKAUFSP?EISDURCHFUNKSPRUCH?RB?TENNKONAC?18ROEMX3ANRX11023?
```

**Edited output:**

```text
RUMAENENWOLLENSIEMENSFERNSCHREIBERUNDFERNSPRECHAPPARATEKAUFENXGENEHMIGUNGUNDVERKAUFSPREISDURCHFUNKSPRUCHERBETENXKONACH18ROEMX3ANRX11023?
```

</details>

## Repairs and remaining reference

`SIEMENS`, `FERNSCHREIBER` and `FERNSPRECHAPPARATE` are explicitly editorial lexical completions. Most lost letters can be filled without changing an observed coordinate. The A in `APPARATE`, however, requires **one observed-coordinate substitution in addition to its erased-coordinate fill**; the ledger does not count this as a pure erasure restoration.

Part 1 repairs raw `SC0WIERIGKE?TEN` to `SCHWIERIGKEITEN`, changing one observed coordinate and filling the missing I. This repairs a local word and does not assign H to the baseline key's digit0 elsewhere.

Part 2 also repairs raw `GENEHMIGUNGUNG` to `GENEHMIGUNGUND` at a cost of two observed coordinates. Proposed closing punctuation `ERBETENX` replaces raw `ERBETENN`, also at a cost of two observed coordinates. The source reference after it remains `KONACH18ROEMX3ANRX11023?`; its abbreviations and number labels are not expanded or reinterpreted.

The final unknown symbol has source pair `?V` at indices 40 and 245 and exact domain **DEQTUX**. It might be a separator, but this edition does not choose one. Its one printed erasure remains unfilled. No key assignment is made.

## Reproduction and attribution limits

There are **zero added or deleted coordinates, block reorders, baseline key changes or new numeral assignments**. Every printed erasure, observed substitution and remaining plaintext domain is recorded in [the certificate](../../experiments/apparatus_sale_request/certificates.json), alongside raw and edited round trips. Global completion witnesses are consistency examples, not recovered originals.

The [input record](../../experiments/apparatus_sale_request/inputs.json) contains the literal manual rows, original headers and full crop-rendering provenance. The [experiment README](../../experiments/apparatus_sale_request/README.md) gives the default verification and optional exact PDF-pixel comparison commands.

A bounded check of the author paper and the cached complete2017 discussion found no explicit prior body identification for these particular records. Earlier machine-derived body leads remain credited, and this check is not a universal priority search.

# A parallel car enquiry with an explicit extra-coordinate model

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The p183 D source is almost identical to the independently readable car enquiry in p183 E, but it has an extra observed coordinate and one other disagreement. This edition preserves D's native odd-length diagnostic and separately prices a parallel-copy proposal. The wording was already obtained directly from E; D adds another physical witness with explicit limitations.

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed D/E image](../../experiments/car_query_parallel_frame/sources/p183_D_E.png) · [Inputs](../../experiments/car_query_parallel_frame/inputs.json) · [All position and exclusion certificates](../../experiments/car_query_parallel_frame/certificates.json) · [Native E edition](nov12_arrival_departure_and_car.md#p183-e)

## The three lengths remain distinct

| Evidence layer | Coordinate slots | Treatment |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| D's printed RIZI header | 27 | Retained literally as printed |
| D's actually occupied source body | 37 | Every observed coordinate retained in the native diagnostic |
| E's native body | 36 | Directly decodes the complete car enquiry |
| Conditional D comparison model | 36 | Excludes one observed final X; not a free erasure fill |

D's literal header is `D) CZ v CM (17.20 p.m., November 12th); 12.40; RIZI-27`.

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — the complete 37-coordinate printed body:**

```text
AAXDF AVDFA AADAG FVVAG DDAGV DDVFF VGDVG DX
```

</details>

The following `CM UM` is printed transmission control outside that body. D and E retain their different routing directions and time expressions. No unrecorded historical retransmission or cancellation is asserted.

## Raw output — all 37 observed coordinates retained

Undoing the published Nov10–12 transposition gives 18 complete pairs and one unpaired coordinate. The complete-pair diagnostic is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — complete pairs of the unchanged 37-coordinate source; the unpaired coordinate is recorded separately:**

```text
AUPOXKRAMMTGIUTRF?
```

</details>

The unpaired coordinate is **V at native source index 6**, occupying intermediate index 36. It is retained explicitly in the certificate. It is not the final printed X later excluded in the comparison model. The final question mark in this diagnostic comes from an unassigned square cell, not from a missing printed glyph.

## Raw output — conditional 36-coordinate comparison frame

The native E source supplies the independently fixed target `WOBLEIBTAUTOXKRAMM`. Against that target, excluding each of D's 37 observed positions in turn gives a unique lowest substitution cost when excluding **final source index 36, X**. In that frame, before any coordinate substitution, D reads:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 36-coordinate frame excluding observed source 36 (X):**

```text
WOBLEIBTAUTODKRAMM
```

</details>

The exclusion is a hypothesis based on the parallel source. The printed X is not visually canceled, and its exclusion is not justified merely by the existence of an odd count or by the printed 27 header.

## Edited output — one observed-coordinate exclusion and one substitution

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — conditional exclusion of observed source 36 (X) and substitution at retained source 3 (D→X):**

```text
WOBLEIBTAUTOXKRAMM
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the conditional edited output:**

> Wo bleibt Auto. KRAMM.

**Meaning:** The conditional reading asks where the car is or why it has not arrived. KRAMM remains a literal closing label. The text is an enquiry, not proof that a car was dispatched. The question uses a period in the exact reading so that `?` remains reserved for an unresolved plaintext position.

| Model | Observed-coordinate exclusions | Further observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Native E source | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| D: exclude final source 36 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| D: exclude source 35 | 1 | 2 | 0 |
| D: exclude source 34 | 1 | 3 | 0 |

All **37** exclusion positions, their retained-source maps, raw results and exact substitution vectors are in the certificate. The unique minimum is relative to this fixed E target and the single-exclusion model; it does not prove the historical cause of D's discrepancy. The fully observed E witness is evidence and is not counted again as a new record in this package.

## Evidence, credit and reproduction

The unchanged period key retains the credit to George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry's 2017 key list. The directly readable E witness is frozen separately in [native_witness.json](../../experiments/car_query_parallel_frame/native_witness.json), with its earlier artifact hash and edition credit. This package adds a literal D transcription, the unpaired-coordinate provenance, and a completely priced parallel-source model. No first historical decipherment is claimed.

The verifier independently reconstructs the native odd-length column map, checks the project decoder, exhausts every one-coordinate exclusion, replays all proposed changes and verifies a globally injective full-square completion. It binds the D/E crop to the original PDF by file hash, page, rectangle, scale and exact pixels.

```sh
python experiments/car_query_parallel_frame/verify.py --verify
python experiments/car_query_parallel_frame/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf
```

# Constantinople addresses, signatures and receipt instructions

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** Three visible first parts, containing addresses, signatures and receipt instructions. Their headings announce two or three parts, but no missing continuation payload is claimed recovered here.

Source edition and verification: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The published Nov4–6 and Nov7–9 keys are credited to Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker and remain unchanged. Earlier unreviewed p147 C/p156 C address-and-signature readings are retained in the prior-work record; those fragments are not presented as newly discovered full message bodies.

## What the visible parts say

- **p147 C1:** To the German Embassy at Pera, with signature `STUMM`. The heading gives `YZ v LP`,08.19 a.m. on 7 November, `FUER YZ1450 (6/11) 2 TEILE`, and `1 TL RICHI-96`.
- **p148 B1:** To the Military Mission at `COSPOLI`, with reference labels, a signature for both parts `I.A. GROENER`, and an instruction for receipt to be acknowledged by an officer. The heading gives 08.40 a.m. on 7 November, `FUER YZ1135 (6/11) 3 TEILE`, and `1 TL RICHI-328`.
- **p156 C1:** German charge d'affaires at Constantinople, with raw signature `BUSSCHS`. The heading gives 06.03 a.m. on 8 November, `FUER YZ2030 (7/11) 2 TLE`, and `1 TL RICHI-102`.

`BUSSCHS` is not silently respelled or expanded to a named historical person. All numerical references remain the published-key labels. The source scan supplies only the first parts represented in this edition.

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|p147_C1|96|48/48|48/48|0|0|
|p148_B1|328|163/164|163/164|2|0|
|p156_C1|102|51/51|51/51|0|0|

The physical-record total is **526 coordinate slots / 263 plaintext positions**. Raw fixed positions total 262; the edited layer fixes 262.

```text
ANXMILXMISSIONCOSPOLIXZUXRMX2XDXNRX755XXUNTERSCHRIFTFUERBEIUETLEXXIXAXGROENERXBXRM811193XGEHXPX?ZUSXOPXFUERXKOSPOLIXDOPPELPUNKTXEMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNGDURCHOFFZERBEEEN
```

## The p148 source annotation and invalid glyph

The source visibly places an X above the F at coordinate 37. Applying that annotation produces the T in `ERBETEN`. The edition counts it as **one observed-coordinate substitution**, not zero-cost transcription. A separate ordinary-word repair changes `BEIUETLE` to `BEIDETLE` at coordinate 122; that also costs one observed substitution.

Coordinate 49 is printed as an L-shaped glyph outside the ADFGVX alphabet. It remains a source mask. The affected plaintext position 95 has exact domain **9EKVXZ**, so the reference is retained as `GEHXPX?ZUSXOP`. The edition does not infer a desired coordinate from that unclear field.

p147 C1 and p156 C1 need no source edits. None of these records has a coordinate insertion, deletion, reordering or key change, and none establishes the substance of its unlinked continuation parts.

[The input record](../../experiments/constantinople_address_parts/inputs.json) preserves all manual rows, literal irregular glyphs, source headers and crop-rendering metadata. [The certificate](../../experiments/constantinople_address_parts/certificates.json) retains all coordinate changes, masks, symbol domains, digit/J/Q/Y labels and round trips. # Conditional Constantza station-shutdown notice

**Status:** a readable conditional edition of p112 C. The enlarged
[source](../../experiments/nov3_evening_and_nov4_radio/sources/p112_C_detail.png) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)
clearly advertises 122 coordinates but contains only 110. Its two short
groups are `DVAX` and `AGFF`. A source-preserving 122-slot model adds twelve
unprinted coordinates; their values are not an observed continuation.

The selected frame adds ten coordinates before the visible stream, one
after DVAX and one inside AGFF. No printed marker independently proves
the missing prefix. All **161,025 parameter configurations** in the declared short-group
and two-five-block family are evaluated. They represent **155,400 distinct
source-origin layouts**, with 5,625 duplicate configurations where inserted
positions coalesce. Against the displayed candidate,
this is the only one-cost layout in that family. Allowing twelve arbitrary
missing coordinates gives **eight** equally cheap layouts, all retained.
A minimum for one chosen text does not prove unique wording or loss history.

## p112 C

The header is OUI v OSM, received at 5.59 p.m. on November 4, origin (4) 1700. The readable passage follows the priced edited stream, including its loss assumptions. The literal spelling CONSTANTZA and abbreviation NACHRCHEF are retained in the readable display.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 122-slot loss frame:**

```text
NAC?RCWE?XCO?STA?TZA?EITH?UTE?400AUSS?RB?TRI?B?ESETZTX?ILMISS
```

**Edited output — priced editorial candidate under the same stated frame:**

```text
NACHRCHEFXCONSTANTZASEITHEUTE?400AUSSERBETRIEBGESETZTXMILMISS
```

</details>

**Readable German — based on the edited candidate above; the local qualifications remain in force:**

> Nachrchef. Constantza seit heute ?400 außer Betrieb gesetzt. Milmiss.

The candidate uses **1 observed-coordinate substitution**, **0 source-mask fills** and **11 unprinted-coordinate fills**. Its remaining zero-based plaintext-position domains are `29: 0578CX`. These are literal square labels, without an additional historical numeral assignment.

The unknown position in `?400` has exact domain **0578CX**. Even under a
separate decimal-only assumption, it permits four values; no specific hour
is selected. The quoted time-like field keeps one question mark.

The [complete optional language screen](../../experiments/nov3_evening_and_nov4_radio/language_screen.json)
ranks every declared parameter configuration without a known plaintext. Its fresh synthetic
controls and failed 112-slot diagnostic frames remain separate from the
fixed-candidate cost proof. A high language rank is a lead, not an independent
source witness.


## Evidence and reproduction

The [source package](../../experiments/nov3_evening_and_nov4_radio/README.md),

# Constanza naval radio: telegram routing and exchange connections

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** Childs p80 B1/B2 and p82 A1–A4, 30 October 1918; published `Oct28-31` key, unchanged. [Source inputs](../../experiments/constanza_radio_connections/inputs.json), [exact certificates](../../experiments/constanza_radio_connections/certificates.json), [method and limits](../../experiments/constanza_radio_connections/README.md).

The four-part message quotes the naval department at Constanza on telegram routing and telephone-exchange connections. Telegrams for foreign stations are said to travel over German lines to Bucharest or Braila. The naval radio station is described as directly connected to the local main exchange and also to the naval department's exchange, allowing communication with the main exchange and other telephone points.

The source describes these arrangements. It does not independently demonstrate that each link was operational. All original reference and date labels remain unchanged.

## p80 B1

The independent p80 B1 copy advertises 242 and agrees at 241 coordinates.
