# Munich couriers carrying radio operating documents

[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source and certificate](../../experiments/courier_recovery/README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Five records intercepted on 9 November concern couriers carrying radio operating documents to Munich: first parts p153 E1 / p162 A1 and continuations p151 D2 / p153 D2 / p158 C2. The best continuation fixes **67 of 68 positions** under the published Nov7–9 key; the damaged first part has a conditional 134-position reconstruction. The unit numeral remains **{5,6}** in the key, with a historical argument for **6** below.

## Most likely reading

The first part is an editorial reconstruction with the source costs below:

**Readable German:**

> An Ingenieurinspektion Muenchen. Gefr. Geraus und Feldgr. Mahrer als
> Kurier mit Funkbetriebsunterlagen fuer Grukonach{5,6}02 7 Uhr abds.
> nach dort abgefahren.

The best-preserved second-part witness, p158 C2, reads directly without any
source-coordinate change:

**Readable German:**

> Grukonach{5,6}02 benachrichtigen. Eintreffen hierher drahten.
> Nachrchef 4 B 49909.

**Meaning:** The proposed first part tells the Engineer Inspectorate in
Munich that the two named men left at 7 p.m. as couriers carrying radio
operating documents for `GRUKONACH?02`. The continuation instructs the
recipient to notify that unit and telegraph the arrival back to the sender.

The names `GERAUS` and `MAHRER` remain unidentified; their U and H are not supported across every fit of both alignment models. The reading retains the unexpanded `FELDGR` and singular `ALS KURIER`.

## What is directly supported

All three second-part records contain exactly 136 coordinates. Under the
known partial square, each fixes 67 of 68 plaintext positions. The p158 C2
text is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
GRUKONACH?02BENACHRICHTIGENEINTREFFENHIERHERDRAHTENXNACHRCHEF4B49909
```

</details>

The p151 D2 repeat has `GRU1ONACH` at the beginning, and p153 D2 has
`BENACHWICHTIGEN`; the source edition preserves both. The unaltered p158
witness independently supplies the readable forms of both words.

The question mark denotes the observed pair **VF**, whose unassigned square value is **5 or 6**.

### A separately linked conditional reading: GRUKONACH602

The [November 9 operational reports](../military/nov9_operational_reports.md#historical-identification-most-likely-the-6th-reserve-division) use the same **VF** cell for a reserve-division numeral. A contemporary French telegram identifies the matching formation as the **6th Reserve Division**. Under that historical identification, **VF=6**, and both courier fields read **GRUKONACH602** with no additional source-coordinate changes.

This is one historical inference applied through a shared key cell. The base domain remains 5/6; the first-part reconstruction and its association with the continuation retain the assumptions below. The [context certificate](../../experiments/p170_continuation/military_context.json) records the external source, its date limits and the earlier p176b application.

## First-part damage and explicit reconstruction cost

The first parts both advertise 268 coordinates but actually preserve 259
and 264 slots. Both visibly contain the six-letter group `VXDVDD`, which
the transcription retains. One overstruck glyph in p162 A1 is masked as a
source erasure; its displayed reading is kept separately.

Comparing the two sources without the key finds a five-slot relative gap:
all 260 possible gap starts were tested, and seven tied starts, 151–157,
leave only two known-coordinate disagreements. This does not locate the
other four slots missing from the longer witness.

For the **stated 134-position candidate**, exact alignment gives:

| Alignment model | p153 E1 | p162 A1 |
|---|---|---|
| Retain every source coordinate | Insert 9 slots; change 6 known coordinates; 32 tied minimum fits | Insert 4 slots; change 8 known coordinates; 2 tied minimum fits |
| Delete one received coordinate | Delete 1, insert 10; change 4 known coordinates; 192 tied minimum fits | Delete 1, insert 5; change 6 known coordinates; 14 tied minimum fits |

Every deletion position and tied optimum is retained. A fill of the overstruck p162 glyph is charged separately from observed-coordinate changes.

Within the first model, **123/134 proposed positions** have an unchanged coordinate pair in at least one witness for every combination of minimum fits. Requiring that support under both models gives **118/134**. These counts are conditional on the proposed wording and alignment families. The [certificate](../../experiments/courier_recovery/certificate.json) includes all raw masked-frame readings and exact costs.

## Association, source and credit

The two first-part records explicitly say first part of two, and all three
continuations say second part. The p153 D/E headers both read `RVV v N4` on
the same morning; the first-part `2120 (SY)` field also fits the p151 D
`SY v N4` continuation. Both bodies use the same unresolved `GRUKONACH?02`
field, and the instruction to report arrival follows naturally from the
departure notice. These facts support the association, but the typed log
does not explicitly cross-reference the parts as one original transmission.
The direct continuation remains readable independently of that association.

The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, printed pp. 151, 153, 158 and 162 / PDF pp. 154, 156, 161 and 165,
in the [public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [source inputs](../../experiments/courier_recovery/inputs.json) give
literal rows, headers and reproducible image rectangles. The Nov7–9 key
retains its historical and George Lasry / coauthor attribution in
[the key register](../../data/keys.json).

Source inspection, repeated-copy recovery, reconstruction and edition: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

```sh
python3 experiments/courier_recovery/build.py --verify
python3 experiments/courier_recovery/verify.py
```

# Damascus radio station and a smaller transmitter at Aleppo

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs printed p64 B, PDF p67, preserves a short report addressed to
the communications chief. It says that the Damascus radio station
was blown up and mentions a smaller transmitter at Aleppo. The
receiving header is `LP v OSM (12.49 a.m., October 4th)`, followed by
`(4) 1130`. Those two header times remain unchanged; this fragment
does not establish a consistent sending and receiving chronology.

## p64 B

The [source crop](../../experiments/p64_oil_and_radio/sources/p64_B.png)
has **176 slots**, including one printed dash, matching `RICHI-176`.
It uses the unchanged published **Oct4–6** key.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 176-coordinate frame:**

```text
NACHRCHEFXRADIODAMASKUSAM1X10X?600UHRGESPRENBTXKLEINERSENDERINALEPPOXAKONACH70XNRX30056X
```

**Edited output — one observed-coordinate substitution, with the printed
dash still unfilled:**

```text
NACHRCHEFXRADIODAMASKUSAM1X10X?600UHRGESPRENGTXKLEINERSENDERINALEPPOXAKONACH70XNRX30056X
```

</details>

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation of that candidate:**

> Nachr. Chef: Radio Damaskus am 1.10. ?600 Uhr gesprengt. Kleiner Sender
> in Aleppo. Ako Nach 70. Nr. 30056.

The single word repair changes source coordinate **28 G→X**, producing
`GESPRENGT`. The code-like `AKONACH70` and reference `30056` are retained,
without a new office or unit identification. The events are statements
in this historical report, not independently verified findings.

## Conditional interpretation of the hour

The unknown in **`?600UHR`** is plaintext position **30**. It is pair
**F?**, using observed source coordinate **82** and the printed dash
at source **162**. Under the published square, its full domain is
**1EKLOS**. All six coordinate completions are preserved and re-encrypt
exactly with the one stated word repair.

**If the unknown is required to be a decimal digit**, the domain contains
only **1**, producing **1600UHR**. This is an explicit field-type
interpretation and requires one additional source-mask fill. It is
kept separate from the raw and edited streams above and from their
counts. The baseline still fixes **87 / 88** plaintext positions.

## Source and attribution limits

This one physical record has **176 source slots**, **175 valid
coordinates**, and **88 plaintext positions**. Its price is one
observed-coordinate substitution, with no source-mask fill, insertion,
deletion or key change in the main edition.

The body already appeared in an earlier unreviewed repository screen.
A bounded search found no explicit separate Damascus/Aleppo discussion
in the paper, thesis or cached 2017 comments; that absence does not
establish historical priority. The published period key remains credited
to the earlier key recoverers, and the adjacent oil inquiry has its
own explicit prior publication.

[Inputs](../../experiments/p64_oil_and_radio/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/p64_oil_and_radio/certificates.json)
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/p64_oil_and_radio/README.md)
retain the source rows, exact inverse, domains and all six hour witnesses.

# Destroy written material and report by telephone

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p177 A orders destruction of written material, while retaining the
necessary cipher-key material, and asks for a telephone report of completion.
The source has an ordinary **186-coordinate** frame. Two observed-coordinate
substitutions give a readable 93-character body under the unchanged partial
`Nov10-12` key. No erased coordinate or unknown square cell is filled.

## Source and literal reading

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [printed p177, PDF p180](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [source crop](../../experiments/november_radio_service/sources/childs_p177_A.png)
retains both the page heading and reception line:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
11th NOVEMBER, 1918.
A) MSX v MUA (11.50 a.m., November 10th)
1220
RIZI-186
```

</details>

The heading's November 11 and reception line's November 10 are preserved
without resolving the chronology. No historical identities are assigned to
MSX or MUA from the document-destruction wording alone.

All 186 source coordinates are valid. The conservative published square fixes
92 of 93 raw positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ALLESCHRIFTSTUECKEBISAUFNOTWENDIGESSCHLUESSELMATERIALVERNICHTENXME?DUNGGESLHEHENENTELEFONISCH
```

</details>

The `?` comes from an **unassigned square cell**, not an unreadable source
coordinate. Its available labels are `56789` under the conservative partial
key. Assigning that cell the letter `L` would violate the existing published
anchors; this edition does not do so.

## Proposed reading and exact repairs

Two received-coordinate substitutions instead move the affected pairs to
already known letter cells:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ALLESCHRIFTSTUECKEBISAUFNOTWENDIGESSCHLUESSELMATERIALVERNICHTENXMELDUNGGESCHEHENENTELEFONISCH
```

</details>

Readable German, with an unencoded grammatical word explicitly bracketed:

**Readable German:**

> Alle Schriftstücke bis auf notwendiges Schlüsselmaterial vernichten.
> Meldung [des] Geschehenen telefonisch.

The instruction is to destroy written material except the necessary key
material, and report by telephone that it has been done. The bracketed
`des` only smooths the telegram's grammar; it is not claimed as recovered
ciphertext. No reason for the order is supplied in the body.

| Source index, zero-based | Printed group / position, one-based | Change |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 31 | 7 / 2 | `X` → `G` |
| 32 | 7 / 3 | `G` → `V` |

The [certificate](../../experiments/november_radio_service/certificates.json)
maps each change to its plaintext position and includes the full re-encrypted
witness. The source still has 186 slots; no coordinate is inserted, removed
or reordered, and the partial square remains unchanged.

## Why the initial odd-length lead was rejected

An earlier OCR extraction contained 185 slots and nominated this record
during a screen for before-transposition phase errors. Manual inspection
finds **186 slots, exactly matching `RIZI-186`**. The odd length was an OCR
transcription problem. This source edition therefore uses the ordinary
frame and does not count p177 A as evidence for the conditional mechanism
seen in [p126 A5](../military/armistice_transit_planning.md#a5-conditional-recovery-of-the-odd-frame)
or [p132 B](p132_radio_service.md#b-repeat-the-fourth-period-telegram-in-the-fifth).

The [inputs](../../experiments/november_radio_service/inputs.json) preserve
the manual rows, exact header, source crops and both published key records
used by the combined source package. The period key is credited to
**George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**,
[DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
and George Lasry's [2017-02-24 key comment](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1).
Earlier unreviewed OCR candidates existed. No explicit p177 A body example
was located in the bounded author-paper check; that absence does not establish
first-decipherment priority.

```sh
python experiments/november_radio_service/verify.py --verify
```

# Hermannstadt radio station and armistice instructions

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

Childs p216 A is explicitly a four-part report. Its origin is 2245 on 24 November 1918; the receiving header is 06.38 p.m. on 25 November. The published Nov22–24 key is unchanged.

It reports construction of a radio station near Hermannstadt, railway difficulties, unsuccessful or intermittent communications, and eventual reception through Breslau. The final part requests repeated messages, a situation assessment, and an interpretation of the armistice. Lasry and coauthors already describe the broad Nikolajev/Breslau communication problem in section 6.3; this page adds the source-specific transcript, exact repairs and uncertainty record.

## p216 A1

Radio station construction near Hermannstadt.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ANOHLXXFUNK6NSTATXUNMITTELBARBEIHERMANNSTADTAUFGEBAUTXNACHDEMAUFBAUXDERDURCHSCHWIERIGKEITENDERBAHNBEHOERDENSEHRVERLANGSAMTX
```

**Edited output:**

```text
ANOHLXXFUNKENSTATXUNMITTELBARBEIHERMANNSTADTAUFGEBAUTXNACHDEMAUFBAUXDERDURCHSCHWIERIGKEITENDERBAHNBEHOERDENSEHRVERLANGSAMTX
```

</details>

One observed-coordinate substitution; no length change.

## p216 A2

Reception difficulties and raw NIKOLA3EW.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
AMYQXBEENDETXWARVERSTAENTIGUN6NICHTMOEGLICHXDANIKOLA3EWGARTICHTUNDWUSTERHAUSENNURREITWEISEAUZNAHMENXVERSUCHEUEBERBUDAPEST
```

**Edited output:**

```text
AMYQXBEENDETXWARVERSTAENDIGUNGNICHTMOEGLICHXDANIKOLA3EWGARNICHTUNDWUSTERHAUSENNURZEITWEISEAUFNAHMENXVERSUCHEUEBERBUDAPEST
```

</details>

Six observed-coordinate substitutions. **NIKOLA3EW and AMYQ are unchanged.** Raw 3 is FD at source positions 26 and 180. Assigning J to GD elsewhere does not fix this occurrence; a same-spelling reading would require an additional copying/source assumption, which is not applied.

## p216 A3

Breslau reception and missing message references.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional deletion of source 56 F from the six-coordinate group:**

```text
WIENMUENCHEQKRFOLGLOSXERSTSEITBRESLAUAUFNIMMTXJ7XYYXVERBINDUNGGESICHERTXDORTXOUNKSPRUECUERMYANRYY837XYY3J7NJCHTEINGEGANGEN
```

**Edited output — same conditional deletion model, followed by five word repairs:**

```text
WIENMUENCHENERFOLGLOSXERSTSEITBRESLAUAUFNIMMTXJ7XYYXVERBINDUNGGESICHERTXDORTXFUNKSPRUECHERMYANRYY837XYY3J7NICHTEINGEGANGEN
```

</details>

The source prints 245 coordinates against 244 advertised, with six-letter VFAFDV. Deleting source 56 F is the unique minimum among all 245 single-coordinate deletions, followed by five ordinary-word coordinate repairs. Every date/reference label is retained. The minimum is conditional on the explicit candidate.

## p216 A4

Request to repeat situation and armistice instructions.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional deletion of one source X at 34, 35 or 36; aliases retained:**

```text
ERBITTENWIEDERHOLUNGBEURTEILUNGDERLAGEBESONDERSAUSLEGUNGDESWAFFENSTILLSTANDESFU?ROKMXXOKMYAYY7Y1OPX
```

**Edited output — same conditional deletion model, with one printed-dash fill:**

```text
ERBITTENWIEDERHOLUNGBEURTEILUNGDERLAGEBESONDERSAUSLEGUNGDESWAFFENSTILLSTANDESFUEROKMXXOKMYAYY7Y1OPX
```

</details>

The source prints 199 slots against 198 advertised. Deleting any one of three adjacent Xs at source 34, 35 or 36 produces the same ciphertext. All three source maps are retained. One printed dash is filled for FUER; no observed coordinate is substituted.

## Evidence

The edition contains 465 plaintext positions, 12 observed-coordinate substitutions, one printed-dash fill and two conditional source-coordinate deletions. The source-defined four-part assembly does not include the adjacent cash request. Fixed raw labels do not certify historical numbers or names.

[Source inputs and attribution](../../experiments/hermannstadt_radio_report/inputs.json), [exact certificates](../../experiments/hermannstadt_radio_report/certificates.json), and [complete method and verification instructions](../../experiments/hermannstadt_radio_report/README.md).

# Communication through Hungary — wireless routing, repetition and supplies

[All cases](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** Three separate
messages on Childs p. 97 concern retransmission, disrupted communication
through Hungary, and a reference to tubes and oil. Their typed source frames
contain 638 valid coordinates and match all three advertised lengths. The
unchanged November 1–3 key fixes all 319 raw plaintext positions.

The first two records need no coordinate repair. The proposed edition of the
third changes three plaintext labels through six observed-coordinate
substitutions. There are no erased slots, inserted or excluded source
coordinates, changed key cells, or changed numeral fields. The shared sender
and date do not make these three separate headings one multipart telegram.

## p97 A

[Source crop](../../experiments/hungary_connection_and_supplies/sources/p97_A.png). `A) OSM v LP (8.50 p.m., November 1st)` | `RICHI-196`.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — all 196 observed coordinates; unchanged key.**

```text
SOFORTIGEWIEDERHOLUNGDORTIGENTELEGRXKOFCHIX56XX30STRICH10XXROEMX2XDX8XONHXVOMX30STRICH10XXKXMXANCH
```

</details>

**Readable German — the request, with unexplained reference fields kept literal:**

> Sofortige Wiederholung dortigen Telegr. `KOFCHIX56XX30STRICH10XXROEMX2XDX8XONHXVOMX30STRICH10XXKXMXANCH`.

The message requests immediate repetition of the indicated telegram. The
reference contains `CHI`, the number `56`, two `30STRICH10` strings, and an
unexpanded `ROEMX2XDX8XONH` field. This edition does not silently turn those
codes into a new message header or choose a grammatical expansion for them.
The physical source is marked `RICHI-196`; mentioning `CHI` in its body does
not establish use of a different key for this record.

All 98 raw labels are fixed. No edited stream is needed.

## p97 B

[Source crop](../../experiments/hungary_connection_and_supplies/sources/p97_B.png). `B) UKS v LP (8.29 p.m., November 1st)` | `1710 (1/11) POLITISCHE ABTEILUNG BUKAREST` | `RICHI-246`.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — all 246 observed coordinates; unchanged key.**

```text
NRX608XDAVERBINDUNGDURCHXUNGARNXGESTOERTXGEHENTELEGRAMMEBISAUFWEITERESFUNKENTELEGRAPHISCHXEMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNGXAUSWAERTIGXX
```

</details>

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation only:**

> Nr. 608. Da Verbindung durch Ungarn gestoert, gehen Telegramme bis auf Weiteres funkentelegraphisch. Empfangsbestaetigung. Auswaertig.

The clear header addresses the political department in Bukarest. The body
says that communication through Hungary is disrupted and telegrams will be
sent by wireless until further notice; it asks for acknowledgment. The closing
`AUSWAERTIG` remains literal, without an invented personal signature.

All 123 raw labels are fixed. The earlier OCR frame had 241 slots and did not
produce this reading. Manual source transcription restores the visible
246-slot frame; that is an OCR correction, not a five-coordinate historical
insertion. No edited stream is needed.

## p97 C

[Source crop](../../experiments/hungary_connection_and_supplies/sources/p97_C.png). `C) UKS v LP (8.15 p.m., November 1st)` | `1330 (1/11)` | `RICHI-196`.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — all 196 observed coordinates; unchanged key.**

```text
AKONACH18XBZGDRTRM3CNRX25089XXGEHZUZIFF1XUEBEWSGROEHRENDUNMOELZU2XFOLGTWEITERESXNACHCHEFRM4B49240X
```

**Edited output — the six observed-coordinate substitutions below.**

```text
AKONACH18XBZGDRTRM3CNRX25089XXGEHZUZIFF1XUEBERSGROEHRENXUNDOELZU2XFOLGTWEITERESXNACHCHEFRM4B49240X
```

</details>

**Readable German — the proposed word repair; abbreviations retained:**

> `AKONACH18`. Bzg. drt. RM 3 C Nr. 25089, geh. Zu Ziff. 1: Uebersg. Roehren und Oel. Zu 2 folgt Weiteres. Nach[richten]chef RM 4 B 49240.

The message cites an earlier reference, mentions `ROEHREN` and `OEL` in
connection with its first numbered point, and says further information will
follow on the second. `[richten]` expands the displayed abbreviation only;
it is not additional decoded text. `AKONACH18` and all reference numerals
remain literal.

The raw `UEBEWSG` becomes `UEBERSG`; `D` immediately after `ROEHREN`
becomes separator `X`; and `M` in the raw sequence `UNM` becomes `D`.
Each proposed plaintext change needs two coordinate substitutions. These are
language-supported repairs, not corrections to uncertain source glyphs:
all six printed coordinate symbols are legible in the crop.

| Source index, zero based | Printed | Proposed | Plaintext effect |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 14 | `G` | `D` | Position 45: `W` → `R` |
| 37 | `V` | `G` | Position 58: `M` → `D` |
| 108 | `A` | `X` | Position 55: `D` → `X` |
| 138 | `F` | `A` | Position 45: `W` → `R` |
| 139 | `G` | `D` | Position 55: `D` → `X` |
| 150 | `D` | `A` | Position 58: `M` → `D` |

The key determines 98 labels before and after the proposal. A fixed-position
count is therefore not a correctness score for these three word repairs.
The raw text remains available beside the proposed edited stream.

## Evidence, verification and credit

The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
printed p. 97 / PDF p. 100, headed 1 November 1918. The
[full page](../../experiments/hungary_connection_and_supplies/sources/p97_full.png),
[literal inputs](../../experiments/hungary_connection_and_supplies/inputs.json),
[coordinate certificates](../../experiments/hungary_connection_and_supplies/certificates.json)
and [reproduction notes](../../experiments/hungary_connection_and_supplies/README.md)
preserve the three headers, source rows, exact key, raw outputs and repair
ledger.

The published November 1–3 key is prior work credited to George Lasry and
colleagues. The [prior-evidence snapshot](../../experiments/hungary_connection_and_supplies/prior_evidence.json)
retains the earlier unreviewed p97 OCR candidates: C already had the same raw
body, while the A/B frames had incorrect 197/241 lengths. The complete native
A/B readings, source review and explicit C repair ledger are the present
contributions by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No universal first-
decipherment priority is claimed.

```sh
python3 experiments/hungary_connection_and_supplies/verify.py --verify
python3 experiments/hungary_connection_and_supplies/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
```

# Kiel radio-control order — p140 A and p146 A

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Prior interpretation: J. Rives Childs; George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker. Source comparison and exact repair audit: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The four-part order instructs radio stations to come under an officer's immediate control, prevent the reception and distribution of messages from Kiel, and confiscate and destroy texts already received. Its historical interpretation and the p146 repeat were already described in [section 6.4 of Lasry et al.](https://www.apprendre-en-ligne.net/crypto/bibliotheque/PDF/adfgvx.pdf), printed p. 23. The present edition adds literal source transcriptions, independently checked coordinate arithmetic, and an explicit repair of the repeated first part.

## Readable text

**Readable German:**

> Sämtliche Funkstellen sofort durch Offizier fest in Hand nehmen. Verhindern, dass Funksprüche aus Kiel, Kiel aufgenommen und verbreitet werden. Bereits aufgenommene Texte beschlagnahmen und vernichten. Größte Eile geboten. Nachrchef, röm. vier, V, 47?00, geh.

The wording is an editorial reading. The repeated **Kiel, Kiel** is retained. The reference `47?00` remains incomplete; the displayed uncertainty is not permission to choose any digit independently of its coordinate domain.

p140 A is headed `YZ NKJ v LP (3.52 p.m., November 6th)`, `1331 (6/11) 4 TEILE`. The first part reappears in p146 A, headed `ASO v NKJ (04.19 a.m., November 7th)` and `WH BIS 0025 30 GR 1331 (KR)`. Both use the published **Nov4–6** key. The later interception date does not imply that the repeat was re-encrypted under the next key.

| Record | Source slots / advertised | Fixed raw positions, including garbles | Changes for the displayed reading |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| p140 A1 | 112 / 112 | 56/56 | 2 known-coordinate substitutions |
| p140 A2 | 134 / 134 | 65/67 | 3 substitutions and 2 erasure fills |
| p140 A3 | 102 / 102 | 47/51 | 2 substitutions and 4 erasure fills |
| p140 A4 | 98 / 98 | 45/49 | 3 substitutions and 3 fills; number remains unresolved |
| p146 A | 117 / 112 | 51/56 after the declared five-slot deletion | 1 substitution and 5 fills |

p146 A is a separate record from the challenge's **p146 B**, whose duplicated `XAAXV` group has its [own case](../p146.md).

## Repeated first part: an extra group and a witnessed letter

p146 prints **117 slots** despite its `RICHI-112` label. Its twelfth group, `VAADX`, is absent from p140. Removing that group yields a 112-slot stream with only two disagreements at known coordinates against p140. Screening every contiguous five-slot deletion gives the same minimum at zero-based starts **54 and 55**; the two deletions produce an identical stream because of a repeated boundary `X`. Both aliases are preserved in the certificate.

The resulting literal decryptions are:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — p146 uses the stated duplicate-group deletion; p140 is separate:**

```text
p140 A1
SAEMTLICHEFUNKSTELLENSOFORTDURCHO1FIGIERFESTINHANDNEHMEN

p146 A after the declared deletion
SAEMTL?CHEFUNKS?ELLE?SOFORTDURCHOFFIFIERFEST?NHANDNE?MEN
```

</details>

Across the two copies, **55 of the 56 positions** in the readable first part are witnessed directly. The later copy supplies the first `F` in `OFFIZIER`, where p140 gives `1`. The letter `Z` remains an editorial correction: p140 gives `G` and p146 gives `F` at that position. Thus the repeat improves the text without turning every proposed letter into observed evidence.

## Other raw parts

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — separate literal p140 parts:**

```text
p140 A2
VERHIND1RNDASSF?NKSPRUEC?EAUSKIELKIELAUFGENOMMENUNDVEABREITETWRRDEN

p140 A3
BEREITSA?FGENOMM?NETEXTEB?SCHLAGN?WMENUNDVERNICHTEN

p140 A4
GROESSTEKILEGEBOTONNACHRC?EFXR?EMB?ERXVX47?00XGEH
```

</details>

The literal transcripts retain the dashes, the invalid `C` in p140's `FDCGF`, and the invalid `O` in p146's `VOVVX`. Neither invalid glyph is silently replaced by a valid coordinate.

## Evidence

- [p140 source](../../experiments/corpus_extension/sources/p140_A.png) and [p146 repeat](../../experiments/corpus_extension/sources/p146_A.png).
- [Literal inputs, key snapshots and proposed readings](../../experiments/corpus_extension/inputs.json).
- [Coordinate maps, domains, edit lists and alignment certificate](../../experiments/corpus_extension/certificates.json).

```sh
python experiments/corpus_extension/verify.py --verify
```

A close alignment supports the declared extra-group model; it cannot establish how the historical copying error happened. The original sources remain intact.

# Late-November cipher and routing instructions — p225–228

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source reading and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. Published period keys: George Lasry and collaborators.**

Five ciphertext records and one cleartext notice describe missing December key tables, proposed sharing of keys, a fragment of a numerical-code instruction, and direct routing to an army station. All ciphertext below is read with the unchanged published **Nov28–Dec1** key. These messages give evidence about specific communications arrangements; they do not assign a key to an unresolved challenge.

| Record | Received slots | Fixed raw positions, including garbles | Content |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| p225 A | 232 | 110/116; completed 116/116 | UKS to use a November key from 1 December because December tables have not arrived |
| p226 B2 | 208 | 104/104 | Surviving continuation about reading numerical sequences backwards |
| p227 B | 152 | 76/76 | Send messages for the army and subordinate formations directly to ZOEN |
| p228 C1 | 176 | 88/88 | Agreement involving UKS, ZOEN and BSL about the December key |
| p228 C2 | 144 | 72/72 | BSL and UKS should use the same key; UKS agrees |
| p227 C | Cleartext | Not a decipherment | ITOCHI parts cannot be deciphered; request RICHI or plaintext |

## November key reused because December tables are missing

**Readable German — six compatible fills and two word repairs:**

> Station UKS chiffr. ab ersten Dez. mit NSL Nov., da Dez.-Tafeln noch nicht
> eingegangen. Bitte Telegr. an uns ebenfalls mit NSL Nov. schluesseln.

UKS reports that December tables have not arrived and requests reciprocal
use of the material labelled `NSL NOV` from 1 December. The two occurrences
of `NSL` are retained. The abbreviation does not identify a particular
November day's key.

The notice is headed `BSL v UKS (09.24 p.m., November 28th)`,
`2200 (28/11)`, `RIZI-232`. Its native frame has **232 slots**, including
five printed dashes and the invalid `R` in `DFGVR`. Six compatible word fills
complete **116/116 positions** while retaining all **226 valid coordinates**.
Reading `NICGT` as `NICHT` and `TELEGD` as `TELEGR` costs two additional
observed-coordinate substitutions. The quotation uses that edited layer,
with editorial spacing and punctuation.

<details>
<summary>Original decryption and completed text</summary>

**Raw output — unchanged published key; 110/116 fixed positions:**

```text
STATI?NUKSCHIFFRABERSTENDEZMITNSLNOVYD?DEZTAFELNNOCHNICGTEINGEGANG?NYBITTE?EL?GDANUNSEBENFALLSMITNSLNOVSCHLUES?ELNYY
```

**Edited output — six source-mask fills; zero observed-coordinate substitutions:**

```text
STATIONUKSCHIFFRABERSTENDEZMITNSLNOVYDADEZTAFELNNOCHNICGTEINGEGANGENYBITTETELEGDANUNSEBENFALLSMITNSLNOVSCHLUESSELNYY
```

**Edited output — the same six fills and two observed-coordinate substitutions:**

```text
STATIONUKSCHIFFRABERSTENDEZMITNSLNOVYDADEZTAFELNNOCHNICHTEINGEGANGENYBITTETELEGRANUNSEBENFALLSMITNSLNOVSCHLUESSELNYY
```

| Treatment | Source indices and values |
|---|---|
| Printed dashes filled | 68→V, 110→F, 164→D, 173→V, 174→D |
| Invalid glyph filled | 109: R→A |
| Observed coordinates changed | 6: A→D; 9: F→V |

Indices are zero based. Each completed letter retains one observed half-pair.
The unenciphered annotation after the body remains separate.

</details>

[Source image](../../experiments/corpus_extension/sources/p225_A.png) ·
[Completion and exact re-encryption](../../experiments/late_november_joint_completion/README.md)

## An explicit agreement to use the same key

p228 C is headed `BSL v ZON` (the O has two marks), `04.47 a.m., December 1st`, `0420 (11/30) 2 TLE`. Both parts are directly readable without any coordinate repair:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — two separate source parts under the unchanged key:**

```text
p228 C1
MITYUKSYVEREINBARTEYZOENYDEZEMBERSCHLUESSELWIEYBSLYZWISCHENYBSLYUNDYZOENYVORGESCHLAGENYY

p228 C2
IMVERKEHRYBSLYUNDYUKSYGLEICHENSCHLUESSELVERWENDENYYUKSYISTEINVERSTANDENY
```

</details>

The first part reports an arrangement with UKS concerning the December key as proposed between BSL and ZOEN. The second is explicit: use the same key in BSL–UKS traffic, and UKS agrees. Together, the two source streams retain **320/320 coordinates** and directly fix **160/160 plaintext positions**. This does not establish which particular November day's key the parties subsequently used. [Source image](../../experiments/corpus_extension/sources/p228_C.png).

## Numerical-code fragment and army routing

p226 B2 says that its first part is missing. The surviving continuation directly gives:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ZAHLENREIHENVONRUECKWAERTSGELESENYSODASSXYXSZ8HLEN3Y5Y9YX5YX0YUYSYWYYBENUTZENSIEGLEICHESMITUNFYANTWORTYY
```

</details>

The beginning says that numerical sequences are read backwards; the end asks the recipient to use the same procedure in communication with the sender and to answer. `Z8HLEN → ZAHLEN` and `MITUNF → MITUNS` cost two coordinate substitutions. The central examples, including `XYXS` and `3Y5Y9YX5YX0`, remain literal. The missing first part and those garbles prevent reconstruction of a complete numerical-code rule. [Source image](../../experiments/corpus_extension/sources/p226_B2.png).

p227 B directly reads:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
BITTEFUNKSPRUECHEANXXYARMEEUNDUNTERSTEL6TEFORMATIONENUNMITTELBARANZOENGEBENY
```

</details>

Restoring `UNTERSTELLTE` costs one coordinate substitution. The raw army field **`XX`** is retained, without silently treating it as an Arabic number or Roman numeral. [Source image](../../experiments/corpus_extension/sources/p227_B.png).

## Separate historical interpretation of the army field

The later [unit-based key-label review](../../experiments/late_key_interpretation/README.md) applies the optional p230 map to p227 B. Baseline `X→1` and the separate `Y→X` separator convention give **11th Army**; with the already counted one-coordinate repair of `UNTERSTELLTE`, the instruction asks for telegrams to the 11th Army and subordinate formations to be sent directly to ZOEN. The baseline text above remains the unchanged-key result. Applying the same declared layers to p226 B2 leaves its numerical examples damaged and does not recover the missing code rule.

## A cleartext request to avoid an unreadable cipher

p227 C, headed `BSL v UKS`, `2316 (11/28) K. M. BERLIN`, says that parts 3 and 4 of a referenced War Department message in **ITOCHI** cannot be deciphered. It requests **RICHI or plaintext**, then asks that ciphering be avoided if possible in future. This is a directly visible unencrypted source notice, not a new cryptanalytic result. The literal misspellings and the trailing forwarding annotation are retained in the input record. [Source image](../../experiments/corpus_extension/sources/p227_C.png).

## Evidence

[Literal inputs](../../experiments/corpus_extension/inputs.json) preserve every coordinate, invalid glyph and header. The [certificate](../../experiments/corpus_extension/certificates.json) checks the independent inverse, each raw domain and every stated word repair.

```sh
python experiments/corpus_extension/verify.py --verify
```

# Late October radio service — calls, garbled traffic and network routing

[All cases](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** Five physical
records on pp. 74–75 describe daily calls, a garbled CHI telegram, and questions
about message routing between radio stations and the German wire network.
The five typed frames contain 756 slots. Their unchanged-key outputs fix
348 of 378 plaintext positions. The proposed readings use five observed-
coordinate substitutions and 30 printed-dash fills; all 30 fills belong to
p74 C1 and remain an explicitly conditional reconstruction.

The three routing parts are printed as p74 C1/C2 and p75 A3. The change of
section letter is retained. The repeated recipient line, `1900 (28.10)`,
`3 TEILE`, numbered parts and page continuation support treating them as one
three-part source sequence.

## p74 A

**Daily calls from Deutsch-Altenburg.**

[Source crop](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/sources/p74_A.png). `A) OSM, NKJ, COS v LP (3.50 p.m., October 28th)` | `1630` | `RIZI-154`.

The typed frame has **154 slots** and fixes **77 of 77 raw plaintext positions** under the unchanged published key.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — typed source frame; no word repairs.**

```text
DEUTSIHALTENBURGXOHDXWIRDSIEVOMX29XABTAEGLICHUMX1120XMXEXZXWELLEX5200XANRUFEN
```

**Edited output — only the coordinate changes recorded below.**

```text
DEUTSCHALTENBURGXOHDXWIRDSIEVOMX29XABTAEGLICHUMX1120XMXEXZXWELLEX5200XANRUFEN
```

</details>

**Readable German — with the one recorded word repair:**

> Deutsch-Altenburg, OHD, wird Sie vom 29. ab taeglich um 11:20 M. E. Z., Welle 5200, anrufen.

The printed source has `RIZI-154`. The repair changes `DEUTSIH` to
`DEUTSCH`; it does not assign the station code or any numeral. The time colon,
hyphen and punctuation are display formatting. `OHD`, `29`, `1120` and `5200`
are unchanged literal labels under the published full square. The ciphertext
does not print a wavelength unit, so this edition does not add one.

| Typed source index, zero based | Printed | Proposed | Plaintext effect |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 85 | `A` | `G` | Position 5: `I` → `C` |

The total is **1 observed-coordinate substitution and 0 printed-dash fills**. No key cell or rank changes.

## p74 B

**Repeat the garbled parts of a CHI telegram.**

[Source crop](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/sources/p74_B.png). `B) NKJ v LP (6.10 a.m., October 29th)` | `FUER COS 2200 (28.10)` | `RICHI-170`.

The typed frame has **170 slots** and fixes **85 of 85 raw plaintext positions** under the unchanged published key.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — typed source frame; no word repairs.**

```text
KAUKASUSDELEGAXSPRUCHTLGRLEITSTX639XOSKACHIX212GR3TLVERSTX2U3TLWHXNACHCHEFRM5X15031UX
```

</details>

**Readable German — abbreviations retained or explicitly expanded:**

> Kaukasus-Delega[tion]: Spruch Tlgr.-Leitst. 639, OSKA, CHI, 212 Gr., 3 Tl., verst[ümmelt]. 2 u[nd] 3 Tl. w[ieder]h[olen]. Nach[richten]chef RM 5, 15031 U.

The brackets are proposed expansions of telegram shorthand, not supplied
ciphertext. The message refers to a three-part CHI telegram as garbled and
requests repetition of its second and third parts. `OSKA` and the reference
fields remain unexpanded. The word `CHI` belongs to the decoded report;
this physical record is headed `RICHI-170` and uses the ordinary period key.

No observed-coordinate substitutions or erased-coordinate fills are needed.

## p74 C1

**First routing part with six erased groups.**

[Source crop](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/sources/p74_C1.png). `C) FUER CVS, TAGANROG, POT (ASO) v LP (6.15 a.m., October 29th)` | `1900 (28.10) 3 TEILE` | `1 TL RICHI-148`.

The typed frame has **148 slots** and fixes **44 of 74 raw plaintext positions** under the unchanged published key.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — typed source frame; no word repairs.**

```text
ZUR?G???FTVE?K???SHAN?E???CHIF?E???EIST?T???LLEA?D???SCHESD???NETZAG???HLX
```

**Edited output — conditional supplied reading of the printed erasures.**

```text
ZUREGELNFTVERKEHRSHANDELSSCHIFFEXWIEISTFTSTELLEANDEUTSCHESDRHTNETZAGESCHLX
```

</details>

**Conditional interpretation:** The source begins with six printed
five-dash groups, exactly 30 erased coordinate slots. The full edited string
is one ordinary-language fill candidate consistent with every observed
coordinate. The 44 fixed raw labels and all partial-cell domains are preserved
in the certificate. This is not a uniqueness result for the missing wording.

The candidate opening `ZUREGELNFTVERKEHRSHANDELSSCHIFFE` is retained literally.
This edition does not choose a grammatical expansion for its `S` or silently
rewrite the phrase. The following readable excerpt begins at the next
sentence; only that already displayed opening is omitted from the excerpt.

**Readable German — excerpt of the conditional fill candidate:**

> Wie ist FT-Stelle an deutsches Dr[a]htnetz a[n]geschl[ossen]?

The bracketed letters are prose expansions of the edited abbreviations
`DRHTNETZ` and `AGESCHL`; they do not add decoded positions. The question asks
how the FT station is connected to the German wire network. Its appearance
inside the three-part routing sequence supports this reading, but does not
turn the 30 missing source coordinates into observations.

There are **30 printed-dash fills**, listed individually with their original row, group, source index and plaintext effect in the certificate. The total is **0 observed-coordinate substitutions and 30 printed-dash fills**. No key cell or rank changes.

## p74 C2

**Lines used to exchange foreign-station telegrams.**

[Source crop](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/sources/p74_C2.png). `Continuation of p74 C, 1900 (28.10) 3 TEILE` | `2 TL RICHI-130`.

The typed frame has **130 slots** and fixes **65 of 65 raw plaintext positions** under the unchanged published key.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — typed source frame; no word repairs.**

```text
AUFWELCHENLTGNERFLGTAUSTAUSCH5ERTELGRMHTFREMDLAENDSCHENSTATIONENX
```

**Edited output — only the coordinate changes recorded below.**

```text
AUFWELCHENLTGNERFLGTAUSTAUSCHDERTELGRMITFREMDLAENDSCHENSTATIONENX
```

</details>

**Readable German — with the two priced repairs and marked expansions:**

> Auf welchen Ltgn [Leitungen] erf[o]lgt Austausch der Telgr. [Telegramme] mit fremdlaend[i]schen Stationen?

The bracketed full words expand the literal abbreviations `LTGN` and
`TELGR`; `[o]` and `[i]` are prose spelling completions of `ERFLGT` and
`FREMDLAENDSCHEN`. They are not extra decoded letters. The two coordinate
repairs instead change raw `5ER` to `DER` and raw `MHT` to `MIT`.
The raw numeral label `5` is retained in the raw block and is priced as a
word repair; no numerical field or key-square digit is reassigned.

| Typed source index, zero based | Printed | Proposed | Plaintext effect |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 46 | `D` | `V` | Position 29: `5` → `D` |
| 47 | `A` | `D` | Position 38: `H` → `I` |

The total is **2 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 printed-dash fills**. No key cell or rank changes.

## p75 A3

**Via the German station or a separate line.**

[Source crop](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/sources/p75_A3.png). `A) FUER CVS, TAGANROG, POT (ASO) v LP (6.15 a.m., October 29th)` | `1900 (28.10) 3 TEILE` | `3 TL RICHI-154`.

The typed frame has **154 slots** and fixes **77 of 77 raw plaintext positions** under the unchanged published key.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — typed source frame; no word repairs.**

```text
DURCHVERMITTLGDERDEUTSSCHENSTATIONOZUEAERRBESONDLTGNUWOHINXNACHCHEF3AX110701X
```

**Edited output — only the coordinate changes recorded below.**

```text
DURCHVERMITTLGDERDEUTSSCHENSTATIONODUEBERRBESONDLTGNUWOHINXNACHCHEF3AX110701X
```

</details>

**Readable German — spelling peculiarities retained:**

> Durch Vermittlg [Vermittlung] der deutsschen Station od[er] ueberr besond[ere] Ltgn [Leitungen], u[nd] wohin? Nach[richten]chef 3 A, 110701.

The doubled `S` in `DEUTSSCHEN` and doubled `R` in `UEBERR` are present in
both raw and edited streams and are deliberately retained here. The brackets
expand abbreviations only. The message asks whether routing is through the
German station or separate lines, and where those lines lead. The two priced
repairs are `OZ` → `OD` and `UEAERR` → `UEBERR`; the `3A` and `110701` fields
remain unchanged.

| Typed source index, zero based | Printed | Proposed | Plaintext effect |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 55 | `V` | `F` | Position 38: `A` → `B` |
| 72 | `X` | `V` | Position 35: `Z` → `D` |

The total is **2 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 printed-dash fills**. No key cell or rank changes.

## Evidence, verification and credit

The [literal inputs](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/inputs.json),
[coordinate certificates](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/certificates.json)
and [source images](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/README.md)
preserve the complete source, unchanged published key, raw outputs and every
proposed repair. The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX
Cipher System*, printed pp. 74–76 / PDF pp. 77–79. Its page heading is
28 October 1918; the printed reception times include 29 October and are not
silently reconciled.

The October 28–31 key is prior work credited to George Lasry and colleagues.
The [prior-evidence snapshot](../../experiments/late_october_radio_and_materials/prior_evidence.json)
retains the earlier unreviewed repository OCR candidates, including mostly
readable p74 A/B and p75 A3. The present contribution is the source edition,
additional complete bodies, explicit source-layer separation and reproducible

# Berlin General Staff map-sheet request

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Source edition and verification: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.
The published Nov7–9 period key retains its original attribution.

## Conditional digit reading

Under the [shared Nov7–9 digit interpretation](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md), this requests **50 copies of each listed sheet at 1:75,000**. The alternative square gives 60 copies at 1:76,000. The reference comparison selects the first reading conditionally, with no additional source edit or fill.

## p162 B1

Childs printed p162 (PDF p165) has header `UKS v ZON`, reception
`03.40 a.m., November 9th`, and `1109 2 TLE`. The printed part label is
`1 TL`; its length field is literally `RICHI-182?`. That final question
mark belongs to the header, not to the encrypted body.

The [source image](../../experiments/nov8_map_and_boundary/sources/p162_B_detail.png)
contains **181 visible slots**. Its initial group is the four-character
`DGDD`. The primary **182-slot conditional frame** inserts one unknown
coordinate at source boundary 1, giving `D?GDD`; no observed glyph is
removed. The source identifies a short group but does not determine an
exact internal missing position. The other part of this physical
transmission is not identified here.

The [faded-glyph crop](../../experiments/nov8_map_and_boundary/sources/p162_B_faint.png)
needs a separate source qualification: source 110 is provisionally read F
in `VFGGD`, but an E-like reading remains possible. The primary arithmetic
uses the stated F and explicitly pays for changing it. The E/masked
sensitivity below retains the alternative; plaintext fluency is not used
to make the source glyph certain.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 182-slot frame, with the explicitly provisional F transcription:**

```text
STELLVERTRXG?NERJLSTABBERLINXZUSENDUNG?ONJE?0BL??TTERNKAR2E1ZU7?000XB1B2B3C1C2C3D1D2D3E2E3X
```

**Edited output — same frame; two observed substitutions, three printed-mask fills and one missing-coordinate fill:**

```text
STELLVERTRXGENERALSTABBERLINXZUSENDUNGVONJE?0BLAETTERNKARTE1ZU7?000XB1B2B3C1C2C3D1D2D3E2E3X
```

</details>

The substitutions are **source 110 F→D** (`J`→`A` in `GENERAL`) and
**source 150 D→V** (`2`→`T` in `KARTE`). The first cost depends on the
provisional F source reading; it is not hidden as an ordinary erasure fill.
Printed source 84 `Z` is filled with A, source 85 dash with V, and source 149
dash with D. The extra model coordinate is filled with D. These are three
different operation classes, and all source offsets are zero-based.

Under that frame and transcription the raw reading fixes **85 / 91
positions**, and the edited layer fixes **89 / 91**.

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited layer, with spacing, punctuation and conventional umlaut rendering:**

> Stellvertr. Generalstab Berlin. Zusendung von je ?0 Blättern Karte 1 zu 7?000. B1 B2 B3 C1 C2 C3 D1 D2 D3 E2 E3.

The letter-number sheet list remains literal, and `STELLVERTR` remains
abbreviated. No requested quantity or map scale is silently completed.

## Conditional interpretation: linked numbers and source sensitivity

Both unresolved numerical positions, plaintext 43 and 63, use the **same
missing square cell XA**. The two unused key labels are 5 and 6, so the
complete coupled alternatives are:

| XA label | Other missing cell VF | Quantity field | Scale field |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 5 | 6 | 50 | 1:75000 |
| 6 | 5 | 60 | 1:76000 |

Both assignments decrypt and re-encrypt the complete edited witness.
Mixed quantity/scale pairings are unsupported by this key. No external map
history is used to select one of the two alternatives.

The independent fixed-target audit checks **all 182 insertion boundaries**
under the primary F transcription, retaining the two XA identities rather
than treating the numerical question marks as free independent characters.
Boundaries 0 and 1 tie at two observed substitutions and yield the same
completed ciphertext but different source-origin maps. The first five
boundary costs are **2,2,3,4,4**. Boundary 1 is the displayed convention,
not a unique historical loss location.

A second complete 182-boundary audit treats the doubtful source 110 glyph
as noncoordinate E, hence as a source mask. It has the same two optimum
origins and the same completed reading, with **one observed substitution,
four source-mask fills and one missing-coordinate fill**. The primary
summary retains the more explicit F-based substitution cost; it does not
silently switch to this cheaper interpretation.

The unaltered 181-slot diagnostic, its unpaired coordinate, all five
source-local group placements and both complete global key witnesses are
preserved in the [inputs](../../experiments/nov8_map_and_boundary/inputs.json)
and [certificates](../../experiments/nov8_map_and_boundary/certificates.json).
The [reproduction guide](../../experiments/nov8_map_and_boundary/README.md)
also records prior OCR and key credit. The bounded comparison prices a
supplied template; it is not a claim of blind or historical uniqueness.

# Naval inquiry: has the referenced SKL item arrived?

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

## p108 A

Childs p108 A, PDF p111, is headed
`OSM v LP (1.00 p.m., November 3rd)` and
`1900 (2/11) SONDERKOMMANDO IN DER TUERKEI`.
The [source crop](../../experiments/p108_naval_and_personnel/sources/p108_A.png)
contains **282 valid coordinates**, matching `RICHI-282`.
The unchanged published **Nov1–3** key gives a complete reading without
source-coordinate repairs.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — native 282-coordinate frame:**

```text
SLX4314XAUFXGGX2890XEINSXFRAGEDOPPELPUNKTXISTXSKLXBNRXGGX546XROEMX3XNUNMEHRDORTHINGELANGTFRAGEZEICHENXADMIRALSTABSEEKRIEGSLTGXGX1121XROEMX3XX
```

</details>

**Readable German — complete decoded stream; the transmitted punctuation words remain visible:**

> SL. 4314. Auf GG. 2890. Eins. Frage Doppelpunkt. Ist SKL, BNr. GG. 546, Röm. 3,
> nunmehr dorthin gelangt Fragezeichen. Admiralstab, Seekriegsltg. G. 1121. Röm. 3.

The encoded words `DOPPELPUNKT` and `FRAGEZEICHEN` remain words in this complete readable layer. The previous display explicitly rendered them as punctuation; this change makes all decoded labels visible without adding a repair.

The message asks whether the item identified by **SKL BNR GG 546 ROEM 3**
has arrived. It does not report an arrival. Routing and reference
abbreviations remain unexpanded, and no numerical label is reassigned.

## Conditional interpretation and the OCR correction

The earlier corpus OCR retained only 280 coordinates, omitting the final
standalone **FX** row that is plainly visible at the bottom of the body.
It also masked source index **11**, the F in **GFGXV**. Recovering those
three visible glyphs from the scan restores the printed 282-coordinate
frame and all **141 / 141 fixed plaintext positions**. This is a correction
to the OCR transcript, not a conjectural insertion into the historical
source. The unchanged complete plaintext re-encrypts to the visible
ciphertext exactly.

The [frozen OCR snapshot](../../experiments/p108_naval_and_personnel/ocr_snapshot.json)
and [certificate](../../experiments/p108_naval_and_personnel/certificates.json)
retain the old 280-coordinate input, its output under the same key and
the exact source-visible difference. The old shared corpus is unchanged.
The neighboring personnel message has a different header and is treated
separately; adjacency alone is not used to join it to this inquiry.

The edition retains published key credit and the earlier unread OCR
candidate. Bounded prior-publication checks do not establish historical
priority, and no first-solution claim is made. See the
[inputs](../../experiments/p108_naval_and_personnel/inputs.json) and
[reproduction instructions](../../experiments/p108_naval_and_personnel/README.md).

# Newspaper sacks arriving via Orsova

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This two-part telegram tells the **Oberpostdirektion in Breslau** that sacks
of Berlin newspapers arrived yesterday and today via **Orsova**, and asks
for immediate postal dispatch by the same route. It gives priority to two
references, `7?3` and `308`, without spelling out their exact administrative
meaning.

The source is Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
[printed p171 B, PDF p174](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [two parts](../../experiments/newspaper_dispatch/sources/p171_B.png)
have this header:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
B) NKJ v LP (1.01 a.m., November 10th)
1858 (9/11) 2 TLE
```

</details>

The page heading says `9th NOVEMBER, 1918.`; the receiving timestamp is
November 10. Both are retained. The source lengths are exactly 200 and
186 coordinates, using the unchanged published Nov7–9 square and ranks.

## Exact readings and separately priced repairs

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
OBERPOSTDIREKTIOKBRESLAUXGESTERNUNDHEUTEBERLINERZEITUNGSSAECKEUEBERO?SOVAHIERE?NGEGANGENXVERANLASSET
```

</details>

One observed-coordinate substitution repairs `DIREKTIOK→DIREKTION`, and
two fills of printed dashes give:

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
OBERPOSTDIREKTIONBRESLAUXGESTERNUNDHEUTEBERLINERZEITUNGSSAECKEUEBERORSOVAHIEREINGEGANGENXVERANLASSET
```

**Raw output:**

```text
S8FORT3OSTBEFOERDERUNGAUFSELTEMWEGEXVOUZUGSWEISE7?3UND308XXXEUTSCHEFELDPOSTDIREKTIONRUMAENIEN
```

</details>

Five observed-coordinate substitutions repair ordinary words:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
SOFORTPOSTBEFOERDERUNGAUFSELBEMWEGEXVORZUGSWEISE7?3UND308XXDEUTSCHEFELDPOSTDIREKTIONRUMAENIEN
```

</details>

The signatory is the German field-post directorate in Romania. The doubled
`XX` before `DEUTSCHE` is retained, as are both reference fields.

| Part | Actual slots | Raw fixed labels | Edition fixed labels | Known-coordinate changes | Printed-erasure fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| B1 | 200 | 98 / 100 | 100 / 100 | 1 | 2 |
| B2 | 186 | 92 / 93 | 92 / 93 | 5 | 0 |
| **Total** | **386** | **190 / 193** | **192 / 193** | **6** | **2** |

There are no inserted, deleted or reordered source coordinates. Both bodies
were already recognizable in earlier unreviewed OCR-derived computations;
the present contribution is the source edition and exact repair accounting.

## What remains unknown, and what an earlier hypothesis would imply

The unknown in `7?3` is **not a printed erasure**. Its two coordinates are
fully observed: source positions **172 and 32** form **`XA`**, one of the two
unassigned cells in the published Nov7–9 square. Its baseline domain is
**`56`**. Both the original and edited ciphertext retain that exact pair.

The earlier [military-context certificate](../../experiments/p170_continuation/military_context.json)
separately proposes `VF→6` and consequently `XA→5`, under its independent
French-telegram unit identification. If that existing conditional layer is
adopted, this field becomes **`753`**. The new postal message supplies no
independent confirmation of that digit assignment; `7?3` remains the baseline
reading. No specific field-post office or unit is identified here.

## Attribution and verification

The period key is credited to **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**. This B telegram is physically separate from the p171 A1
challenge, whose body was read by **Norbert in 2017** and is retained in
[its canonical case](../p171.md). Nothing here changes that priority.

The [inputs](../../experiments/newspaper_dispatch/inputs.json) and
[certificate](../../experiments/newspaper_dispatch/certificates.json)
retain all source rows, raw and edited strings, global witness completions,
exact source changes and the separately marked conditional numeric field.
The bounded discussion/paper check is recorded; no universal priority claim
is made.

```sh
python experiments/newspaper_dispatch/verify.py --verify
```

The optional `--pdf` argument verifies the pinned source digest and compares
the regenerated source-crop pixels. Re-encryption certifies consistency and
cost, not uniquely original wording.

# p166 — a second witness of the newspaper-dispatch request

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** Two newly source-reviewed physical parts, compared with the already published p171 B1/B2 edition. The first part is fully supported by observed coordinate pairs across the copies. In the second, three letter choices remain editorial and one numeral cell remains unassigned.

Source edition and comparison: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The unchanged **Nov7–9** key is credited to Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker. The earlier [newspaper-dispatch edition](newspaper_dispatch.md), its underlying unreviewed body candidates and its repair accounting remain prior work. The p171 records are not added again or altered.

## Source and message

The message tells the Oberpostdirektion Breslau that Berlin newspaper sacks have arrived via Orsova and requests immediate dispatch along the same route, with priority references left as raw `7?3` and `308`.

Childs printed page 166 / PDF page 169 labels the two parts `B) NKJ v UKS (9.27 p.m., November 9th)`, `AN LP1858 2 TLE`, `RICHI-200` and `RICHI-186`. The page identifies the intercepts as British-station traffic. The p171 witness has a later interception heading; no particular relay chronology is inferred.

Both p166 native frame lengths are preserved. B1 contains a Q-shaped noncoordinate glyph at index 174. B2 contains 49 printed dashes at indices 137–185. Those slots are in the source; filling them is not an insertion of missing coordinates.

## p166 B1

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
OBERPOBTDIREKTIONBRESLAUXGESTERNUNDHEUTEBERLI?ERZEITUNGSSAECKEUEBERORSOVAHIEREINGEGANGENXVERANLASSET
```

</details>

Common proposed body:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
OBERPOSTDIREKTIONBRESLAUXGESTERNUNDHEUTEBERLINERZEITUNGSSAECKEUEBERORSOVAHIEREINGEGANGENXVERANLASSET
```

</details>

p166 needs one observed-coordinate substitution and one mask fill. The p171 copy directly supports both proposed letters. Conversely, p166 supplies complete source pairs for p171's previously repaired N in `DIREKTION` and the two previously erased letters in `ORSOVA` and `EINGEGANGEN`.

All 100 common candidate pairs are complete in at least one received copy. The two copies disagree at two observed coordinates; the common candidate costs two substitutions in total and reaches the fixed-frame coordinate-only minimum. This does not prove that their historical common source had no earlier error.

## p166 B2

Literal decryption, with its printed erasures retained:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
SQF?Y?3???BEF?E?D???NGA?F?E???MWE?S?V???UES?E?S???3UN?3?8???E?T?C?E???D?O?T?I???T?O?R?J???I?N
```

</details>

The previously published p171 edition is the declared comparison target:

<details>
<summary>Earlier attributed reading</summary>

**Earlier attributed reading — p171 edited comparison target; no new coordinate claim for p166:**

```text
SOFORTPOSTBEFOERDERUNGAUFSELBEMWEGEXVORZUGSWEISE7?3UND308XXDEUTSCHEFELDPOSTDIREKTIONRUMAENIEN
```

</details>

Applying that target to p166 costs **seven observed-coordinate substitutions and 49 fills**. Of the 49 filled coordinates,48 are directly present in the raw p171 copy. The remaining fill at 173 follows the prior editorial D in `DEUTSCHE`; it is not independently observed in either copy.

| Support for a common pair in part 2 | Positions | What it establishes |
|---|---:|---|
|Complete pair in at least one received copy|88|Direct pair evidence, including the still-unassigned XA numeral cell|
|Observed halves from different copies|2|B in `SELBEM` and R in `VORZUGSWEISE`|
|Still editorial pair choices|3|O in `SOFORT`, P in `POST`, D in `DEUTSCHE`|

The mixed B and R pairs are `GX` and `AD`, respectively. For B, p166 observes `?X` and p171 observes `GV`; for R, p166 observes `?D` and p171 observes `AV`. This strengthens those two earlier letter proposals using received coordinates, while retaining the actual contrary coordinates and their costs.

The three unsupported choices are explicit:

| Plaintext position, zero-based | Proposed letter/pair | p166 raw pair | p171 raw pair |
|---:|---|---|---|
|1|O / FX|FV|FA|
|6|P / AA|DA|DA|
|59|D / XV|?V|VV|

For part 2, the coordinate-only minimum under the fixed common-frame assumption is eight substitutions across the two copies; this readable target costs twelve. The difference is retained as evidence that language interpretation is doing work. No minimum-cost or unique-original claim is made.

## Numeral and count limits

The priority field remains **`7?3`**, with the XA cell constrained to 5 or 6 by the unchanged published square. A missing p166 coordinate is supplied from the directly observed p171 XA pair; this recovers a coordinate, not its numerical label. The earlier optional 753 historical interpretation remains a separate conditional layer and gains no independent digit evidence from this copy.

The two new p166 records total **386 source slots /193 plaintext positions**:143 raw fixed positions and 192 after the declared edition, with eight observed substitutions and 50 mask fills. The 193-position common body is counted once in the support analysis, while both physical copies contribute evidence. Across the common body,188 pairs occur completely in a received copy, two are supported by mixed observed halves, and three remain editorial.

The existing p171 costs are unchanged. Combining both old and new witnesses gives 14 substitutions for the selected common stream, compared with the coordinate-only minimum 10. There are no added or deleted coordinates, reordered blocks, key changes or new numerical assignments.

The earlier p171 edition selected the comparison target, so this is **not a blind prediction test**. [The certificate](../../experiments/newspaper_dispatch_witnesses/certificates.json) records every candidate pair, both raw pairs, all source indices, each fill's source support and the conditional minimum. [Inputs](../../experiments/newspaper_dispatch_witnesses/inputs.json) retain the literal glyphs and source images; [the README](../../experiments/newspaper_dispatch_witnesses/README.md) provides reproduction commands.

# Short arrival, departure and car enquiries on November 12

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Four short native records report arrival and departure, request an arrival notification, and enquire about a car. The arrival enquiry and departure text have earlier p174 parallels already published in this repository; the new witnesses add source support to those readings. In particular, the two complementary arrival-enquiry witnesses now supply every coordinate and every plaintext pair without changing an observed coordinate under the conservative glyph masks. The previously catalogued witnesses are not counted again.

## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p183 excerpt](../../experiments/nov12_arrival_departure_and_car/sources/p183_reviewed.png) · [Reviewed p174 excerpt](../../experiments/nov12_arrival_departure_and_car/sources/p174_parallel.png) · [Inputs](../../experiments/nov12_arrival_departure_and_car/inputs.json) · [Position and change certificates](../../experiments/nov12_arrival_departure_and_car/certificates.json)

The published `Nov10-12` key is unchanged. [Original OCR records](../../experiments/nov12_arrival_departure_and_car/ocr_snapshot.json) and [reproducible comparisons with that earlier evidence](../../experiments/nov12_arrival_departure_and_car/prior_candidates.json) are preserved separately. The present edition supplies checked source framing, exact costs and readable passages; it makes no first-public-decipherment claim.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [p183 A](#p183-a) | 64 | 32 / 32 | 0 | 0 |
| [p183 B](#p183-b) | 74 | 30 / 37 | 0 | 8 |
| [p183 C](#p183-c) | 46 | 23 / 23 | 1 | 0 |
| [p183 E](#p183-e) | 36 | 18 / 18 | 0 | 0 |

## p183 A

**Source transcription — header:** `A) CZ v CM (20.00 p.m., November 12th); 20.00; RIZI-64`

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
GUTANGEKOMMENXISTDORTWASLOSXSEIF
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the unchanged raw output:**

> Gut angekommen. Ist dort was los. SEIF.

**Meaning:** The sender reports having arrived safely and asks whether anything is happening at the other end. The closing SEIF is retained as an abbreviated label; this short message does not itself give a location or establish a full personal identity.

**Editorial limits.**

- All 64 native coordinates decode directly under the unchanged key, with no changes or source-mask fills. The following NF CM UM transmission-control text is outside the 64-coordinate body.
- The wording IST DORT WAS LOS is a question. The readable quotation uses a period so that a question mark remains reserved for an unresolved plaintext position in this edition.
- SEIF is not expanded to a full name in the exact readable quotation.

## p183 B

**Source transcription — header:** `B) CM v CZ (18.54 p.m., November 12th); 19.10; RIZI-74`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
WENN??IFERTE?NGETROF?ENBITTE?ACHR?TO?
```

**Edited output — 0 observed-coordinate substitutions and 8 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
WENNSEIFERTEINGETROFFENBITTENACHRXTOF
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Wenn Seifert eingetroffen, bitte NACHR. TOF.

**Meaning:** The message asks for notification when Seifert has arrived. NACHR is read as an abbreviated request for news or a message. TOF remains a closing label with no claimed personal or station identity.

**Editorial limits.**

- The native body contains 74 occupied slots, including literal Z at source indices 4 and 31, W at 42, and five B glyphs at 60–64. These eight invalid coordinate glyphs remain in the transcription and become eight separately priced analysis-mask fills.
- The proposal changes no observed ADFGVX coordinate. The five B-shaped slots are filled with D coordinates; this is an explicit source-mask completion, not a silent claim that five clearly printed Ds were present.
- The source ending CZ UM is transmission control after the 74-slot ciphertext and is excluded from the body on that printed framing.
- NACHR and TOF remain abbreviated or literal; no sender biography is supplied.
- The earlier p174 B witness supplies all eight invalid-glyph values here, while this source supplies D at p174 source 20, supporting its previously unresolved N in EINGETROFFEN. Under conservative masks all 74 source coordinates and all 37 target pairs have an observed witness, with zero observed-coordinate conflicts.
- If the earlier C/G-like glyph is instead treated as an observed G, the complete-word proposal costs one observed substitution in that alternative. The new D witness does not change the appearance of the old glyph.

## p183 C

**Source transcription — header:** `C) CM v CZ (17.26 p.m., November 12th); 18.20; RIZI-46`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
SQIFERTABGEFAHRENXRENTE
```

**Edited output — 1 observed-coordinate substitution and 0 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
SEIFERTABGEFAHRENXRENTE
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Seifert abgefahren. RENTE.

**Meaning:** The proposed reading reports that Seifert has departed. RENTE is the literal closing field; the record alone does not identify it as a particular person or station.

**Editorial limits.**

- All 46 printed coordinates are retained, including the final six FFVDD V omitted from the earlier OCR body. The following CZ is outside the ciphertext.
- The source produces SQIFERT directly. The proposal SEIFERT changes one observed coordinate; the neighboring arrival enquiry supports the name but does not make this change free.
- The full 46-slot ciphertext is preserved; no historical prefix or suffix is invented.
- Compared with existing p174 E, this source supports E at plaintext 4 through observed source 2 X instead of G. Both witnesses still have Q at plaintext 1, so SEIFERT requires one additional word correction in each witness there. The combined edited cost is 3 substitutions versus 1 unavoidable observed-source conflict; the extra 2 are contextual name repairs.

## p183 E

**Source transcription — header:** `E) CM v CZ (17.12 p.m., November 12th); 17.40; RIZI-36`

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
WOBLEIBTAUTOXKRAMM
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the unchanged raw output:**

> Wo bleibt Auto. KRAMM.

**Meaning:** The message asks where the car is or why it has not arrived. The closing KRAMM is preserved without assigning a biography or a vehicle. The text is an enquiry, not proof that a car was sent.

**Editorial limits.**

- The source supplies all 36 coordinates and decrypts directly, with no coordinate changes or mask fills.
- The nearby D record is a similar but differently framed printed witness. It is not silently substituted for this complete E body.
- The interrogative sentence is displayed with a period to reserve ? for unresolved plaintext positions.

## Parallel source evidence and its limits

The [earlier p174 B/E edition](seifert.md) already presents the arrival-enquiry and departure wording. The [frozen parallel-witness snapshot](../../experiments/nov12_arrival_departure_and_car/parallel_witnesses.json) and the new certificate preserve those earlier transcriptions, while the [reviewed p174 image](../../experiments/nov12_arrival_departure_and_car/sources/p174_parallel.png) is independently bound to the original PDF.

| Comparison | Complete observed pairs supporting the edited target | Minimum combined observed-coordinate conflict cost | Combined edited substitutions | Combined printed-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| p174 B / p183 B arrival enquiry | 37 / 37 | 0 | 0 | 9 |
| p174 E / p183 C departure report | 22 / 23 | 1 | 3 | 0 |

In the first pair, p174 B supplies every one of the eight invalid-glyph values in p183 B. Conversely, p183 B supplies an observed **D at source 20**, which gives **N at plaintext 22** in `EINGETROFFEN`, formerly unresolved in the conservative p174 transcription. Every complete target pair occurs in at least one witness. This is positive source evidence for that letter, beyond a plausible German completion. It does not make the nine individual printed masks disappear from the two diplomatic transcriptions.

The old p174 glyph remains C-like or a defective G. Under its explicitly retained G reading, selecting the D supplied by p183 costs one observed-coordinate substitution in that branch. The source comparison does not claim to change what the older glyph looks like.

In the departure pair, p183 C supports the second E of SEIFERT through **source 2 X**, where p174 E has G. The first E still corresponds to the same **source 28 G** in both witnesses and therefore needs one contextual G→X proposal in each. Thus the complete name costs three substitutions jointly, two more than the unavoidable single observed-source conflict. The joint source support does not turn this shared spelling repair into a direct reading.

The literal interception and originating times differ between the parallel records and remain in their headers. These are additional physical witnesses, not four newly discovered message contents or a claim of first historical decipherment.

## Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. The arrival-enquiry and departure wording was already presented for p174 B/E in cases/radio/seifert.md. The new p183 witnesses add coordinate support and a separately priced comparison, not a new claim to that wording or extra message groups.

The certificates independently reconstruct column positions and domains, compare them with the cipher implementation, replay every priced change, and check all readable nonseparator labels. Partial readings have one consistent injective square/source-mask completion witness that re-encrypts exactly; those witness choices are not historical identifications. Source images are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/nov12_arrival_departure_and_car/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to check the original PDF and exact source-crop pixels.
