# November 12: additional arrival and return enquiry witnesses

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Printed p182 A and C are additional physical witnesses to two service enquiries already read on p174. They join the reviewed p183 arrival-enquiry copy. Direct comparison of their printed coordinates supplies a bounded recovery without selecting a German language score. The earlier body readings and the previously established p174/p183 complementary evidence retain their credit; these are **two newly reviewed source records, not two newly discovered message contents**.

The **55-slot A source** has a conditional 74-slot comparison model. It adds twenty coordinates from the independent witnesses and excludes one printed slot; all **eleven minimum source maps** remain in the certificate. The **49-slot C source** has a conditional 48-slot comparison model that excludes its final observed X. Each proposal also changes one observed coordinate. The native streams, printed length discrepancies and every cost class remain separate below.

Research, source review and editorial work: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The unchanged Nov10–12 key retains the publication credit of George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker. Existing body evidence is in [the Seifert service edition](seifert.md) and [the p183 arrival/departure edition](nov12_arrival_departure_and_car.md).


**Reviewed source crops:** [p182_AC_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov12_seifert_additional_witnesses/sources/p182_AC_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).
## Source and independent witnesses

[Printed p182 A, B and C; B was already catalogued separately — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov12_seifert_additional_witnesses/inputs.json)

The B body between the new records is the already reviewed [expected-return message](return_time_and_vehicle_attempt.md#p182-b), with its literal RUECKUNFT and 0100 labels. It is not counted again or used to identify the closing S as a particular person.

The independent [p174 B/C source](../../experiments/nov12_arrival_departure_and_car/sources/p174_parallel.png) and [p183 B source](../../experiments/nov12_arrival_departure_and_car/sources/p183_reviewed.png) are bound to their existing image bytes and original-PDF pixels. Their exact transcriptions are frozen in [parallel_witnesses.json](../../experiments/nov12_seifert_additional_witnesses/parallel_witnesses.json).

| Record | Native slots | Valid source coordinates | Conditional model | Primary raw fixed | Edited fixed | Observed substitutions | Printed-mask fills | Added-slot fills | Printed exclusions |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| p182 A | 55 | 48 | 74 | 11/37 | 37/37 | 1 | 6 | 20 | 1 masked glyph |
| p182 C | 49 | 49 | 48 | 24/24 | 24/24 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 observed X |
| **Primary total** | **104** | **97** | **122** | **35/61** | **61/61** | **2** | **6** | **20** | **1 mask + 1 observed coordinate** |

The A row uses source 48 as a representative masked-slot exclusion. It is not singled out as the historical error location. The other ten minimum maps, including seven that exclude an observed D and require a seventh printed-mask fill, remain separate.

## p182 A

Literal header: `A) CM v CZ (19.35 p.m., November 12th); 19.30; RIZI-74`.

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — all 55 occupied slots, including invalid glyphs and dashes:**

```text
VVFVG XAVTA AGXVA VVVVA DAVDV AXFFI XD-VD FDDXA
DDDDD --NTD DVDVD
```

</details>

The following CZ UM transmission-control text lies outside the body. The source’s seven non-coordinate slots are **8 T, 29 I, 32 dash, 45 dash, 46 dash, 47 N and 48 T**. They remain literal in the transcription and become analysis masks. They are not silently read as ADFGVX letters.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — native 55-slot diagnostic, with the unpaired coordinate retained separately:**

```text
VAA2??WC3F2K??AQ?A?2?WWVGW1
```

</details>

This native frame has 27 complete pairs. Its intermediate orphan is **D at source 54**; the verifier does not drop a terminal source slot to hide it.

### Source-only comparison model

The p174 B and p183 B sources contain 74 slots each. They agree wherever both supply valid coordinates. Each invalid-glyph position in one has an observed value in the other. Their conservative union therefore gives **74 observed coordinates**, and every one of the 37 complete target pairs occurs in at least one unedited witness. The earlier p174 C/G-like glyph and its alternate G interpretation remain in the original edition; the union uses its conservative mask and p183’s observed D at that location.

The new p182 A source shares its CM v CZ station pair and originating 19.30 label with p174 B. Interception times differ and are retained literally. The matching source body establishes an additional printed witness; a specific retransmission or typesetting mechanism is not inferred.

The bounded comparison permits **one excluded printed slot and one contiguous twenty-coordinate gap**. All **55 × 55 = 3,025** combinations are checked against the independent raw consensus before any plaintext comparison. The objective is the number of conflicting observed coordinates; the kinds of exclusions and fills are counted separately.

All eleven minima put the twenty-slot gap **after the first five source coordinates** and exclude one source slot from **40 through 50**. Every minimum has one observed disagreement: **p182 source 0 V versus the independently observed D**. Among them, **four exclude a masked glyph** and **seven exclude an observed D**.

| Excluded source indices | Maps | Excluded class | Observed substitutions | Printed-mask fills | Added-slot fills | Raw fixed positions |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 40–44 | 5 | Observed D | 1 | 7 | 20 | 11/37 |
| 45–48 | 4 | Printed non-coordinate mask | 1 | 6 | 20 | 11/37 |
| 49–50 | 2 | Observed D | 1 | 7 | 20 | 10/37 |

The equality concerns **observed substitution count**, not a single combined edit score. Excluding a source mask and excluding a valid D remain different operations. The four mask-exclusion aliases have the same unfilled coordinate string but different source maps. Their seven D-exclusion alternatives remain inspectable in full.

For the primary source-48 mask exclusion, the frame arithmetic is **55 − 1 + 20 = 74**. The printed shortfall of nineteen is therefore not represented as nineteen unexplained additions. The twenty inserted coordinates are model slots 5–24 and are all supplied by the independent source consensus.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 74-slot frame, before any source or added-slot fills:**

```text
WE??S???????????TR??????I??E?A??RX?O?
```

**Edited output — 1 observed substitution, 6 printed-mask fills, 20 source-supported added fills, and 1 separately counted masked-slot exclusion:**

```text
WENNSEIFERTEINGETROFFENBITTENACHRXTOF
```

</details>

**Readable German — the complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Wenn Seifert eingetroffen, bitte NACHR. TOF.

**Conditional interpretation — additional arrival-enquiry witness:**

The message asks to be notified when Seifert has arrived. NACHR and TOF remain literal; the abbreviation is not expanded in the exact quotation, and no full identity or destination is supplied. The wording was already recoverable from p174 B/p183 B. This record adds a damaged physical witness and its explicitly bounded alignment, rather than new wording selected from context.

Every filled coordinate in the primary model has an observed counterpart in p174 B or p183 B. The V→D disagreement still costs one substitution in p182 A. Independent evidence does not turn that printed V into a free source-mask fill.

The final two minimum maps, excluding source 49 or 50, have the following distinct unfilled diagnostic. Their final edited target is the same, but they require seven source-mask fills rather than six.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — alternate source-49/source-50 exclusions, before source-supported fills:**

```text
WE??S???????????TR??????I??E????RX?O?
```

</details>

## p182 C

Literal header: `C) CM v CZ (21.25 p.m., November 12th); 21.00; RIZI-56`.

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — all 49 observed coordinates, including final X:**

```text
VVVFF VDAFA XXVDA XXFAD DXGXV DDAAG DVFDV DXGFA
DAGVX DDAX
```

</details>

The following CZ is transmission control outside the body. The source explicitly advertises **56**, contains **49**, and is compared with an independently printed **48-coordinate** p174 C body. None of those counts is silently substituted for another.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — native 49-slot diagnostic, with the unpaired coordinate retained separately:**

```text
2TNNFTQCIFU1RXFENIV0MI4E
```

</details>

The native intermediate orphan is **A at source 27**. The conditional model is a separate layer.

All **49 possible single-coordinate exclusions** are compared directly with the p174 C source. The unique minimum within that class excludes **source 48 X** and leaves **one observed mismatch** at source 8: p182 prints F while p174 prints V. The other 47 coordinates agree exactly. This is source evidence for the same short enquiry; the uniqueness claim does not extend to other framing classes or establish why the final X was printed.

Both sources print CM v CZ and the originating 21.00 field. The p174 interception header says 08.11 p.m.; the p182 header says 21.25 p.m. Those literal time expressions are not harmonized.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 48-slot frame after the explicit final-X exclusion:**

```text
WANNRUECKKUNFTSEIFVRTXRE
```

**Edited output — 1 observed F→V substitution at source 8, plus the separately counted source-48 X exclusion:**

```text
WANNRUECKKUNFTSEIFERTXRE
```

</details>

**Readable German — the complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Wann Rueckkunft Seifert. RE.

**Conditional interpretation — additional return-enquiry witness:**

The enquiry asks when Seifert will return. The exact RUECKKUNFT and closing RE are retained. A period is used in the quotation so that a question-mark glyph remains reserved for unresolved plaintext. The existing p174 C body already gives this complete text without edits; the new p182 source requires the priced alignment and correction above.

## Reproduction and limits

[inputs.json](../../experiments/nov12_seifert_additional_witnesses/inputs.json) retains the native transcriptions, original headers, image bounds, unchanged key and prior body credit. [certificates.json](../../experiments/nov12_seifert_additional_witnesses/certificates.json) includes all 3,025 A alignment prices, all eleven A minimum maps and position domains, all 49 C prices, native orphan coordinates and exact fill/substitution ledgers. The [frozen OCR snapshot](../../experiments/nov12_seifert_additional_witnesses/ocr_snapshot.json) preserves the earlier incomplete A OCR and C block.

The [portable verifier](../../experiments/nov12_seifert_additional_witnesses/verify.py) reconstructs the source-only consensus, confirms a complete raw-pair witness at every target position, checks the live case’s full displays, and checks exact re-encryption under all 120 global completions of the unchanged partial square. Its missing digit cells never enter these all-letter bodies. Original-PDF checking additionally compares every source crop pixel.

```sh
python experiments/nov12_seifert_additional_witnesses/verify.py --verify
python experiments/nov12_seifert_additional_witnesses/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
```

The alignment minima are conditional on the specified operation classes. They do not establish a unique historical channel error, authorize removal of source glyphs from the diplomatic transcription, or identify a person beyond the observed surname. Previously catalogued p174 and p183 records are not counted again.

[p211](p211_key_schedule.md). Its header and long literal coordinate
matches establish the copy-family link; the reconstruction below uses their
independently received source coordinates.

## p187 B1

**Readable German — source-linked 214-slot reconstruction; ten duplicate-source exclusions, 84 copied slots, five observed substitutions and one printed-mask fill:**

> November-Ringbahnschluessel nicht vernichten. Nachrchef G B848727. Dezember-Ringbahnschluessel tritt vorlaeufig

Four choices of which identical group occurrence to exclude yield the same

Filling only the 84 missing slots from the other receptions raises the fixed

```text
AAGFA AVFXA AVXVD AVXVD DAGVD FXFAF XDXAV XDXV-
DXDGA DXDGA XXXXF GVGFA AGVAX AXDFA XXAXV GAAXV
```

# Postponed departure, a supper query and a farewell

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Three separate service messages retain their complete native source frames: a postponed departure with reassurance, a proposed warm supper and headcount enquiry, and a short farewell. Source-transcription corrections recover the positions omitted by earlier OCR; ordinary-word repairs, printed-dash fills and literal abbreviations remain explicit.

## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p193 excerpt](../../experiments/nov14_15_departure_and_supper/sources/p193_reviewed.png) · [Reviewed p196 excerpt](../../experiments/nov14_15_departure_and_supper/sources/p196_reviewed.png) · [Inputs](../../experiments/nov14_15_departure_and_supper/inputs.json) · [Position and change certificates](../../experiments/nov14_15_departure_and_supper/certificates.json)

The published `Nov13-15b` key is unchanged. [Original OCR records](../../experiments/nov14_15_departure_and_supper/ocr_snapshot.json) and [reproducible comparisons with that earlier evidence](../../experiments/nov14_15_departure_and_supper/prior_candidates.json) are preserved separately. The present edition supplies checked source framing, exact costs and readable passages; it makes no first-public-decipherment claim.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [p193 C](#p193-c) | 212 | 104 / 106 | 3 | 2 |
| [p193 D](#p193-d) | 82 | 40 / 41 | 4 | 0 |
| [p196 A](#p196-a) | 74 | 37 / 37 | 0 | 0 |

## p193 C

**Source transcription — header:** `C) --- v CM (1.15 p.m., November 14th); RIZI-212`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
ABMARSCHVERSCHOBENKEIN6RUNDZURBEUNRUHIGUNGABMERFOLGTSPA5TERINVEREINBARTERWCISEDHFNBLEIBTBET?BEREITX?EIFERT
```

**Edited output — 3 observed-coordinate substitutions and 2 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
ABMARSCHVERSCHOBENKEINGRUNDZURBEUNRUHIGUNGABMERFOLGTSPAETERINVEREINBARTERWEISEDHFNBLEIBTBETRBEREITXSEIFERT
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Abmarsch verschoben. Kein Grund zur Beunruhigung. Abm. erfolgt spaeter in vereinbarter Weise. DHFN bleibt BETR bereit. Seifert.

**Meaning:** The message reports that departure has been postponed, says there is no cause for alarm, and states that departure will occur later as agreed. The closing readiness phrase is retained as DHFN bleibt BETR bereit; the edition does not identify DHFN as a particular place or silently expand BETR.

**Editorial limits.**

- The source prints 210 valid coordinates followed by two distinct dashes. Together these are 212 occupied slots, exactly matching the header. The older OCR omitted the two dashes; restoring their positions is a source-transcription correction, not insertion of hypothetical missing ciphertext.
- 6RUND → GRUND, SPA5TER → SPAETER and WCISE → WEISE require three observed-coordinate substitutions. The printed dashes at indices 210 and 211 are explicitly filled with F and G. They supply the R of BETR and the initial S of SEIFERT under the fixed frame.
- ABM is retained as an abbreviation. DHFN and BETR are literal labels, without geographical identification or a hidden expansion in the readable stream.
- The source reports a postponement and a future intention; it does not establish that the later departure occurred.

## p193 D

**Source transcription — header:** `D) CZ v CM (1.10 p.m., November 14th); RIZI-82`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
WOLLGNWALMESA?ENDBRXBEREITENVWIEVXKOEPFEX
```

**Edited output — 4 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
WOLLENWARMESABENDBRXBEREITENXWIEVXKOEPFEX
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Wollen warmes Abendbr. bereiten. Wiev. Koepfe.

**Meaning:** The proposed wording says the sender intends to prepare a warm evening meal and asks how many people there are. Abendbr. and Wiev. remain abbreviated in the quoted stream. The message does not record a supplied headcount or confirm that the meal was prepared.

**Editorial limits.**

- All 82 source coordinates are printed and retained. The earlier OCR block had only 76 coordinates; the corrected native transcription contains the complete second row and final VG.
- WOLLGN → WOLLEN, WALMES → WARMES, A?ENDBR → ABENDBR and the V following BEREITEN → separator X cost four observed-coordinate substitutions in total. No source glyph is erased or filled.
- The raw question mark comes from an unassigned square cell even though its two source coordinates are known. The proposed B therefore requires an observed-coordinate change to a known B pair; it is not a free square completion or erasure fill.
- ABENDBR and WIEV are retained literally. The natural evening-meal and headcount interpretation is attached to the explicitly repaired candidate, not presented as an unchanged raw sentence.
- This is a separate source record five minutes before the neighbouring C reception. No response relationship or combined message is assumed.

## p196 A

**Source transcription — header:** `A) CZ v CM (15.22 p.m., November 15th); 16.15; RIZI-74`

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
ABFAHRXWIEDERSEHENXGRUESSEKRAMMXOPITZ
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the unchanged raw output:**

> ABFAHR. Wiedersehen. Gruesse, Kramm. Opitz.

**Meaning:** The short unedited reading contains a departure-related opening, farewell, greetings and the names or signature labels Kramm and Opitz. It does not establish either person’s identity or assign their exact sender/addressee roles.

**Editorial limits.**

- All 74 valid source coordinates decrypt directly to 37 fixed raw labels. No observed-coordinate substitution, source fill, missing slot or frame change is used.
- The source gives ABFAHR without a final T. That shortened form is preserved in both raw and readable output; no letter is silently inserted to produce ABFAHRT.
- The header retains its anomalous 15.22 p.m. expression and separate 16.15 line. They are not normalized into a reconstructed chronology.
- KRAMM and OPITZ remain literal labels; neighbouring service traffic does not by itself identify their full names or this message’s exact historical itinerary.

## Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates independently reconstruct column positions and domains, compare them with the cipher implementation, replay every priced change, and check all readable nonseparator labels. Partial readings have one consistent injective square/source-mask completion witness that re-encrypts exactly; those witness choices are not historical identifications. Source images are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/nov14_15_departure_and_supper/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to check the original PDF and exact source-crop pixels.

# November 14 cross-key notices: an arriving pilot and a backup radio station

[Case index](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and cross-key comparison: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Seven intercepts on Childs's printed pages 190, 193 and 194 preserve three
message families. Two radio-service requests were sent under different
keys. Two notices about a pilot's arrival in Berlin describe the same
apparent event, with changed wording. A third interrupted arrival notice
matches a complete source exactly: that witness restores **85 missing
coordinates and 85 additional raw plaintext positions** without changing any
of the fragment's 195 received coordinates.

## Which station can replace NKJ?

The p190 B and p190 E messages read, with the separately certified repairs:

**Readable German:**

> Welche Station kann NKJ bei Betriebsstoerung vertreten? Vielleicht
> [Sewastopol]. Dring[end] Bescheid an LP.

**Display notes:** `[Sewastopol]` marks a coordinate-priced word proposal; `Dring[end]` expands the literal abbreviation and supplies prose letters only. Neither bracket form by itself asserts direct source support.

**Meaning:** Which station can replace NKJ during an interruption of service?
Perhaps Sevastopol; send an urgent reply to LP. The full city spelling
`SEWASTOPOL` is the candidate reading, and its S is an editorial repair.
The source abbreviation `DRING` is retained in the exact template; the
expanded word above is explanatory.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
WELCHESTATIONKANNNKJBEIBETRIEBSSTOERUNGVERTRETENXXVIELLEICHTSEWASTOPOLXDRINGBESCHEIDANLP
```

</details>

Both ciphertexts have 176 source slots, giving 88 plaintext positions. Their
published keys have different transposition widths: 16 columns for p190 B
and 20 for p190 E. This is an aligned re-encryption comparison, not simply
another message about the same subject.

The literal source decryptions are:

| Source | Unmodified published-key decryption |
|---|---|
| p190 B | `WELC?ESTATIO?KANNNKJ?EIBETRI?BSSTOERUNGVERTRETENXXVIELLEICHTSEWAVTOP?LXDRINPBESE?IIDANLP` |
| p190 E | `WELCHE?TATION?ANNNKJBEIBETRIEBSTTOERUNG?ERTRETENXXVIELLEICHTSEWA?TOPOLXDRINGB?SCHEI?ANLP` |

**87/88 preferred positions have a complete pair in at least one source.**
The exception is the S at plaintext index 64 in `SEWASTOPOL`. The earlier
copy has raw V; the other copy has a damaged half-pair whose domain includes
S. The city reading remains a separately priced editorial choice.

The p190 B candidate costs five observed-coordinate substitutions and five
fills for a printed `-----` group. The p190 E candidate costs one
observed-coordinate substitution and six uncertain-slot fills. One of those
six slots is a visible A/X overstrike: the certificate preserves and decrypts
both readings, and the candidate's X is among them. The invalid printed
letters Q and T are also retained in the literal transcription.

## Does NKJ relay messages for Mackensen?

The p190 D and p193 A notices have the following source-supported reading:

**Readable German:**

> Vermittelt NKJ Funksprueche fuer Mackensen? Habt ihr Verbindung, und wie?
> Dring[end] Bescheid an FUGROSTA. LP.

**Display notes:** `Dring[end]` is the same prose-only abbreviation expansion here. The two witnesses retain their distinct `FUR` and `FUER` spellings in the exact outputs below.

**Meaning:** Is NKJ relaying radio messages for Mackensen? Do you have
contact, and how? Send an urgent reply to FUGROSTA; signed LP. `FUGROSTA`
is retained as transmitted. The transmitted abbreviation is `DRING`.

The longer exact candidate is:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
VERMITTELTXXNKJXXFUNKSPRUECHEFUERMACKENSENHABTIHRVERBINDUNGUNDWIEXXDRINGBESCHEIDANFUGROSTAXXLP
```

</details>

The p190 D text uses `FUR`, giving 93 characters and 186 ciphertext
coordinates. The p193 A text uses `FUER`, giving 94 characters and 188
coordinates. After this one explicitly identified wording difference is
aligned, **every letter of the 94-character candidate has a complete pair
in at least one original source**. Neither ciphertext is padded or trimmed
to make their lengths agree.

The literal decryptions are:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — separate literal witnesses under their stated period keys:**

```text
p190 D:
VERMITTELTXXNKJXXFUNKSPRUECHEFURMACKENSENHABTIHRV?RBINDUNOUNDWIEXXDRINGBESCHEIDANFUGROSTAXXLP

p193 A:
LERMITTE?T0XDKRX5FUNKS0RUECHZF?ERMACTENSENHA?TIHRVERBINDUNGUNDWIEXXDRINGBE5CIE?DANFU?R0STA?XLP
```

</details>

The p190 D candidate requires two observed-coordinate substitutions. The
p193 A candidate requires 15 substitutions and three fills for printed
dashes. Their full candidate reencryption checks are separate. The large
number of garbles in p193 A does not obscure the independent support from
the cleaner p190 D copy, while p193 A supplies the latter's damaged E and G
in `VERBINDUNG` and the extra E in `FUER`.

## A Warsaw soldiers' council representative reaches Berlin

The p190 A and p194 B notices say, with their certified ordinary-word repairs:

**Readable German:**

> Zitadelle [Warschau], fuer Soldatenrat. Flieger / Flugzeugfuehrer
> FR?E, Bevollmaechtigter [des] Soldatenrats, in Berlin wohlbehalten
> eingetroffen. Auswaertiges Amt.

**Display notes:** This is a composite readable presentation, not a third recovered source. `[Warschau]` is present in the fuller p194 B witness; `[des]` is supplied grammar absent from both exact wordings. The slash in `Flieger / Flugzeugfuehrer` displays the two witnesses' different words. `FR?E` retains one unresolved name position and is not a proposed surname.

**Meaning:** To the citadel's soldiers' council: the pilot FR?E, a council
representative, has arrived safely in Berlin. The fuller p194 B wording
explicitly includes Warsaw. The raw texts omit the grammatical article
inserted in brackets above. No personal identity is assigned.

The literal decryptions are:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — separate literal witnesses under their stated period keys:**

```text
p190 A:
ZITADELLEXFUERSOLDATENRXTXXFLIEGERMFR?EXBEVOLLMAECHTIGTERSOLDATENRATSINBERLINWOHLBEHALTENEINGETROFFENXXAUSWAERTCGESAMT

p194 B:
ZITADELLEXWARSCHAUXFUERXSOLDATENRATXFLUGZEUGFUEHRERXFR?EXBEVOLLMAECHTIGTERXSOLDLTENRATSXINXBERLINXWOHLBEHALTENXEINGETROFFENXAUSWAERTIGESAMTX
```

</details>

The p190 A readable template changes three source coordinates to obtain
`RAT`, the separator after `FLIEGER`, and `AUSWAERTIGES`. The p194 B template
changes one coordinate to obtain `SOLDATENRATS`. Both name fields remain
`FR?E`. These notices share a long message body but differ in their opening
words, separators and length; no whole-message ciphertext alignment is used.

### The interrupted p193 B copy

The p193 B record is headed `WAU v LP (4.15 p.m., November 14th)` and
`RICHI---`, with 195 printed coordinates. All 195 are identical to the suffix
of p194 B beginning at ciphertext index 85. The complete p194 B record has
the same call signs, a `4.14 p.m.` interception time and a `RICHI-280` length.

The certificate first retains the fragment as a 280-position source model
with **85 unknown prefix slots**, which fixes only **54/140 raw positions**.
It then fills those 85 positions from the independently printed beginning
of p194 B. No received coordinate of p193 B is changed. The restored stream
equals p194 B exactly and fixes **139/140 raw positions**: **85 additional
positions** are recovered from the overlapping source, with an exact witness
index for every supplied coordinate.

This restoration preserves the complete copy's literal `SOLDLTENRATS`
garble and its unresolved name cell. The separate A-for-L word repair is
not passed off as part of the observed missing prefix. The 195-coordinate
fragment, its odd length and its unknown printed length label are all
retained in the input record.

### What the shared surname does and does not constrain

| Witness | Key | Unknown name position | Square cell | Original symbol domain |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| p190 A | Nov13–15b | 37 | FX | 234789QY |
| p194 B | Nov13–15a | 54 | DG | 0123456789QY |

Indices are zero-based. If both fields contain the same correctly copied
name, the two cells must represent the same symbol, with intersection
**234789QY**. This eliminates four possible assignments from the second
field, but does not identify the symbol. A further letter-only assumption
leaves **Q or Y**.

`FRYE` is a plausible surname proposal. It is not uniquely established by
the domain intersection, and no independent historical identification has
been found. The certificate checks all eight common symbols: each one
reencrypts the edited templates exactly under the corresponding conditional
cell assignments. Accordingly neither published square is filled.

<details>
<summary>An archival lead for the unresolved pilot name</summary>

The council's own *Mitteilungsblatt des Deutschen Soldatenrates Warschau*
is a concrete source to inspect. The [official ZDB record](https://zdb-katalog.de/title.xhtml?idn=989924653)
catalogues issues 1–5, dated 12–17 November 1918, with an explicit uncertainty
marker. It locates holdings at the Bayerische Staatsbibliothek in Munich
(**Rar. 1323**) and the Wuerttembergische Landesbibliothek in Stuttgart
(**ZCa 82170**). The latter records issues 1, 2, 4 and 5. The
[catalogue review](../../data/reviews/warsaw_pilot_bulletin_lead.json)
preserves the exact date strings and identifiers. No bulletin text or page
image has been inspected, so this locator supplies no evidence identifying
`FR?E` and does not settle either unknown square cell.

</details>

## Evidence and exact reproduction

- [Source inputs, headers and published keys](../../experiments/nov14_retransmissions/inputs.json)
- [Per-letter coordinate domains and repair certificates](../../experiments/nov14_retransmissions/certificates.json)
- [p190 A source](../../experiments/nov14_retransmissions/sources/p190_A.png)
- [p190 B source](../../experiments/nov14_retransmissions/sources/p190_B.png)
- [p190 D source](../../experiments/nov14_retransmissions/sources/p190_D.png)
- [p190 E source](../../experiments/nov14_retransmissions/sources/p190_E.png)
- [p193 A source](../../experiments/nov14_retransmissions/sources/p193_A.png)
- [p193 B source](../../experiments/nov14_retransmissions/sources/p193_B.png)
- [p194 B source](../../experiments/nov14_retransmissions/sources/p194_B.png)
- [Experiment and verification instructions](../../experiments/nov14_retransmissions/README.md)

The seven records contain **1,437 printed source slots**. Their declared
frames fix **654/761 raw positions** before filling the interrupted prefix,
or **739/761** after the independent witness supplies it. The denominator
includes p193 B's explicitly restored 280-coordinate frame. Fixed positions
include literal garbles; they are not all claimed as correct historical
letters. Published keys are credited in the input provenance. This edition
provides source review and exact comparison, without a claim to first
decipherment of every underlying text.

# November 15: Warsaw radio personnel and a repeated key notice

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p197 preserves a two-part order concerning radio personnel in Warsaw
and a second physical witness of the [p189 C December-key notice](../context/p189_C.md).
All three records use the unchanged published **Nov13–15b** key. The first
part of the personnel order has a five-slot source deficit; its proposed
reconstruction is explicitly conditional. The complete second part directly
names **Posen** and reads **`IN MARSCH ZU SETZEN`**.

| Record | Printed source slots | Analysis-frame slots | Fixed raw positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills | Inserted-slot fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| p197 A1 | 193 | 198, conditional gap | 93/99 | 1 | 1 | 5 |
| p197 A2 | 144 | 144, native | 68/72 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| p197 B | 124 | 124, native | 60/62 | 3 | 0 | 0 |

The counts describe the stated frames and proposals, including unresolved
numerical labels. They do not count every displayed label as an independently
authenticated historical character. Period-key credit remains with George
Lasry and collaborators as recorded in [data/keys.json](../../data/keys.json).


**Reviewed source crops:** [p197_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov15_radio_personnel_and_key_notice/sources/p197_reviewed.png) · [p189_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov15_radio_personnel_and_key_notice/sources/p189_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).
## p197 A1

[Reviewed source image — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov15_radio_personnel_and_key_notice/inputs.json).

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — shared header and first-part length:**

```text
A) WAU v LP (03.55 p.m., November 15th)
14.50 2 TLE
1 TL RICHI-198
```

</details>

The five printed rows contain **193 slots**, including one dash in `VDVG-`,
against the advertised **198**. This edition keeps those 193 source slots
unchanged in the literal record. Its proposed analysis frame inserts **five
unknown slots at source boundary 165**, between the final row's `AFXFF` and
`GFVAX`. That location is an editorial hypothesis, not a printed gap mark.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 198-slot frame with five added unknown slots; 93/99 fixed positions:**

```text
FESTUNGSFUNKAXWARSCHAUXDASGESAMTE?MBEREIC?DESGOUV?RNEMENT?WARSCHA?VERFUEGBAREFUN?ERPERSONALISTNMCHX
```

**Edited output — same conditional frame; one observed-coordinate substitution, one source-mask fill and five inserted-slot fills; 99/99 fixed positions:**

```text
FESTUNGSFUNKAXWARSCHAUXDASGESAMTEIMBEREICHDESGOUVERNEMENTSWARSCHAUVERFUEGBAREFUNKERPERSONALISTNACHX
```

</details>

The complete price, with zero-based source indices, is:

| Operation | Location | Proposed value |
|---|---|---|
| Observed-coordinate substitution | Source index 98 | `A → V`, giving `NACH` in place of raw `NMCH` |
| Source-mask fill | Printed dash at source index 134 | `D` |
| Five-slot insertion and fills | Source boundary 165 | `AAFFX` |

**Readable German — complete edited stream under the conditional gap model:**

> Festungsfunka Warschau. Das gesamte im Bereich des Gouvernements Warschau verfuegbare Funkerpersonal ist nach

`FESTUNGSFUNKA` is retained as transmitted. The sentence continues in the
native second part. That continuation independently gives the destination
and action, but does not supply every missing first-part letter.

### Comparison of the possible gap locations

For this exact 99-position candidate and the unchanged key, the verifier
compares **all 194 source boundaries** at which one five-coordinate gap
could be inserted. It prices only changes to observed coordinates in the
following column; the one printed-mask fill and five added-slot fills remain
separate in every comparison.

| Source boundary | Observed-coordinate substitutions |
|---:|---:|
| 163 | 2 |
| 164 | 2 |
| **165** | **1** |
| 166 | 2 |
| Every other boundary | At least 3 |

Boundary 165 is the unique minimum **for this candidate and this single-gap
family**. The [certificate](../../experiments/nov15_radio_personnel_and_key_notice/certificates.json)
retains all prices and the raw domains and edits for every frame within one
substitution of the minimum. The comparison does not prove unique historical
wording or exclude other damage mechanisms. The untouched 193-slot decode
and its unpaired final coordinate are retained separately in the certificate.

## p197 A2

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — second-part label:**

```text
2 TL RICHI-144
```

**Raw output — native 144-slot frame; 68/72 fixed positions:**

```text
XFESTUNGSFUNKAXPOSENXINMARSCHZUSETZENXXINACHXFUNKLEITUNGHEIMATXNRX???6?5
```

</details>

**Readable German — complete raw stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Festungsfunka Posen in Marsch zu setzen. I Nach Funkleitung Heimat Nr ???6?5.

No coordinate or key change is used. The literal sequence **`INACH`** is
shown as **`I Nach`**, without expanding it into an office or correcting it
into a different signature. The source's `VD AVD` is five printed
coordinates despite its internal space.

The final **`???6?5`** remains six output positions. The first, second and
fifth labels arise from three different unknown square cells; the second
and third positions use the **same** cell and must have the same value.
Each unknown cell has domain `{2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9, Q, Y}` under the published
partial square, and different cells must remain distinct. This coupled
uncertainty is retained in the certificate; no historical reference number
is assigned.

Under the separate [p193 award-class interpretation](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md),
the first reference digit becomes **2**, giving `2??6?5` and **69/72**
fixed positions. The repeated middle cell and the fifth label remain
unresolved; no coordinate change is needed.

## p197 B

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — literal header:**

```text
B) NKJ v LP (04.24 p.m., November 15th)
10.00 (15/11)
RIZI-124-
```

</details>

The dash after the length label is outside the ciphertext. The visible
final group `XFXX` belongs to the 124-slot body; the earlier OCR omitted it.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 124-slot frame; 60/62 fixed positions:**

```text
UNLOES?A?EHUNKSPRUECHENACHDEZEMBERSCHLUESSELENTZIFFERNXXIRRTUM
```

**Edited output — three observed-coordinate substitutions; no fills; 62/62 fixed positions:**

```text
UNLOESBAREFUNKSPRUECHENACHDEZEMBERSCHLUESSELENTZIFFERNXXIRRTUM
```

</details>

The changes are **source index 23 V→F**, **62 A→D**, and **93 F→G**. Unknown
square cells are not filled to make these words: the letters B and R already
occupy other cells, so the corresponding word proposals require coordinate
changes.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Unloesbare Funksprueche nach Dezemberschluessel entziffern. Irrtum.

### What the second copy supports

The independently inspected [p189 C source — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov15_radio_personnel_and_key_notice/inputs.json)
has the same 124-coordinate body except **source index 93**, where p189
prints **G** and p197 prints **F**. Their reception times differ; the common
internal `10.00` and November 15 date are preserved.

That single difference accounts for **B** versus an unknown at plaintext
index **6**. Thus p189's raw reading directly supports the proposed B in
p197. Both copies still have the unknown at plaintext index **8** and raw H
at index **10**. Neither copy independently supplies the proposed R or F at
those two positions. Their shared repairs are not promoted into independent
corroboration.

**`DEZEMBER`** and **`IRRTUM`** are directly decoded in both copies. The final
word is retained without deciding whether it corrects, cancels or otherwise
qualifies the preceding instruction.

# Armistice acknowledgments, personnel and Warsaw radio inquiries

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Seven native source records cover an armistice-receipt query, nightly radio listening, an inquiry for Captain von Borries, the location of the Warsaw general government, and radio equipment and personnel. Two previously OCR-damaged short messages become clear when their actually printed final groups are restored. All unresolved fields and missing-letter spellings remain explicit.

## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [p202 source](../../experiments/nov16_18_command_inquiries/sources/p202_reviewed.png) · [p203 source](../../experiments/nov16_18_command_inquiries/sources/p203_reviewed.png) · [p204 source](../../experiments/nov16_18_command_inquiries/sources/p204_reviewed.png) · [Exact inputs](../../experiments/nov16_18_command_inquiries/inputs.json) · [Position-by-position certificates](../../experiments/nov16_18_command_inquiries/certificates.json)

The present work supplies an image-reviewed source edition and a reproducible repair account; it does not claim that every body is a first public decipherment.

## p202 A2

**Source transcription — header:** `A) same two-part telegram; 2 TL RICHI-142`

> und Befehl zur Fortsetzung des Abmarsches dort angekommen. OHL 1XAXNRX1???12XOP.

## p204 B

**Source transcription — header:** `B) WAU, IWE v LP (6 p.m., November 17th); ZWEI AR FUER WAU 1300 (17); RICHI-92`

**Readable German** — based on the unchanged raw output.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>


</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

## p204 C1

**Source transcription — header:** `C) KOW v WAU (1.50 a.m., November 18th); 0115 (17), 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-244`

**Readable German** — based on the explicitly repaired output below.

> GE?NACH2O2. Leichte in Lomza und Czenstochau, Verbleib unbekannt. Vermutl. mit ihren Gouvs. aberueckt. Besatzg beiden anderen Stat. ohne Geraet.

**Meaning:** The whereabouts of the light units or equipment in Lomza and Czenstochau are unknown; they are presumed to have departed with their governors. The crews of the other two stations have no equipment. The opening is opaque and several transmitted abbreviations and the missing-letter spelling ABERUECKT remain visible.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
GE?NACH2O2LE?CHTEINLOMZAUNDCZENSTOCHAUXV?RBLEIBUNBEKANNTXVERMUTLMITI?RENGOUVSABERUECKTXBESATZGBEIDENANDERE?STATOHNEGERA?TX
```

**Edited output** — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions and 3 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.


</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The source prints four dash slots: XD--- and GG-AX. The opening GE?NACH2O2 remains unresolved.
- The source-length output ABERUECKT is not silently expanded to [abgerueckt]. VERMUTL, GOUVS, BESATZG and STAT remain their transmitted abbreviated forms.
- Part 2 advertises 282 slots but the reviewed page prints 242. A 40-slot tail-loss hypothesis yields related fragments, but is not accepted as a complete source-length decipherment or counted as another reviewed reading here.

## p204 D

**Source transcription — header:** `D) --- v --- (8.43 a.m., November 18th); RICHI-84`

**Readable German** — based on the unchanged raw output.

> Zu 2??F vom 1?X: 1. Nein. 2. PSO BSL. Fusta WAU.

**Meaning:** A short numbered reply answers no to item 1 and gives the literal call-sign-like pair PSO BSL for item 2. The inquiry number, date and expansion of PSO remain unresolved.

With the [existing shared-order assignment VA=5](../../experiments/nov16_18_reference_completion/README.md),
the date-like field becomes **15X**. The record then fixes **40/42** positions;
the inquiry number stays `2??F`. This is a consequence of the p201/p206
order-date comparison, with no additional source edit.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.


</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The source visibly prints VAXAX and the final AXGF, both omitted from the earlier OCR candidate. The native count is 84.
- The baseline quotation keeps `1?X` before the sentence separator; the shared-order layer gives `15X`.

## Evidence and credit

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are preserved separately. This is a source edition and explicit repair review, not a claim of universal first-decipherment priority.

The certificates replay every coordinate alteration, compare the independent column/domain reconstruction with the cipher implementation, and re-encrypt every complete edited output. For partial outputs, each certificate also constructs one injective global completion of the square and residual masks and verifies its full roundtrip; the witness is explicitly nonhistorical. # November 1 contact times, service mail and receipt acknowledgment

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. These four physical records
appear on Childs printed p99, under the November 1 heading. They use the
published `Nov1-3` square and column ranks. The accompanying
[Sava-crossing report](../military/sava_crossing_evening_report.md) is a
separate message on the same page.

The [full page](../../experiments/nov1_contact_mail_and_sava/sources/p99_full.png),
[literal source rows](../../experiments/nov1_contact_mail_and_sava/inputs.json)
and [coordinate certificate](../../experiments/nov1_contact_mail_and_sava/certificates.json)
retain the distinction between printed masks, observed coordinates, and
conditional missing coordinates.

## p99 A: requested contact times and a damaged Ringbahn phrase

The header reads `UKS v ZON`, reception `0.48 a.m., November 2nd`, origin
`1825 (1)`, and `RIZI-133`. The
[A crop](../../experiments/nov1_contact_mail_and_sava/sources/p99_A.png)
contains exactly **133 source slots**: 109 valid coordinates, 22 printed
dashes, and two printed `E` glyphs at source indices 38 and 40. The final
printed group is the three-letter `GAD`. The odd count is not silently
changed in the transcription.

A bounded diagnostic examined one-coordinate insertion and deletion in
either the transmitted stream or the fractionated stream. Its 534 completed
configurations are retained in the [search log](../../experiments/nov1_contact_mail_and_sava/search/one_coordinate_screen.json).
Adding one coordinate at the end of the transmitted stream gives a coherent
partial body. This is an explicit **134-slot conditional frame**, retaining
all 133 source slots. The literal 133-slot output and its unpaired coordinate
remain in the certificate.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 134-slot frame, with one appended unknown coordinate**

```text
??BITTE?V??SCHLA?FU??V?RKE?R??EITEN?WI??E?RIN?B?HNZEI??NX?KONA?H?L?
```

**Edited output — same conditional frame; 24 printed-mask fills and one missing-coordinate fill, with no observed-coordinate substitutions**

```text
ERBITTENVORSCHLAGFUERVERKEHRSZEITENZWISCENRINGBAHNZEITENXAKONACHELF
```

</details>

The conditional candidate has **67/67 fixed positions** after filling all
24 printed masks—22 dashes and both `E` glyphs—and the one missing model
coordinate. All **109 valid received coordinates remain unchanged**. The
raw count remains **43/67** under the same conditional frame; the extra
completed letters are editorial choices, not newly observed source text.

**Readable German — conditional candidate; the bracketed h is a display-only spelling completion**

> Erbitten Vorschlag fuer Verkehrszeiten zwisc[h]en Ringbahnzeiten. Akonach Elf.

This proposes a request for communication times **between the Ringbahn
periods**. The encrypted candidate contains the seven literal labels
**`ZWISCEN`**, with no `H` in that word. The bracketed letter explains the
German interpretation and adds no plaintext position or ciphertext coordinate.
`AKONACHELF` remains unexpanded. The
[November 3 notice](nov3_ringbahn_notice.md) and
[radio schedule](../../experiments/nov3_radio_and_pioneer/inputs.json)
independently contain the literal term `RINGBAHN`; this supports reading it
as a radio-service term here. They do not independently establish the whole
new phrase or the location of the proposed loss.

### The earlier X was a supplied separator

The raw seven-position span is **`?WI??E?`**, at plaintext positions 35–41.
The earlier partial edition supplied its first unknown as `X`, displaying
`XWI??E?`. That `X` came from filling **source dash 10**; it was not an
observed plaintext separator. Changing that completion from coordinate `X`
to `F` gives plaintext `Z`. Filling the other three masks gives `S`, `C`
and `N`. Each of these four letters retains an observed half-coordinate:

| Plaintext position | Source pair, zero-based indices | Raw pair and domain | Conditional completion |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 35 | 67=`D`, 10=printed dash | `D?`: `RCZVSX` | 10→`F`; `DF` gives `Z` |
| 38 | 18=printed dash, 110=`V` | `?V`: `FSQBK3` | 18→`D`; `DV` gives `S` |
| 39 | 26=printed dash, 103=`D` | `?D`: `IC28M4` | 26→`D`; `DD` gives `C` |
| 41 | 124=`G`, 40=printed `E` | `G?`: `D8WNB5` | 40→`G`; `GG` gives `N` |

The intervening `W`, `I` and `E` are fixed by complete observed pairs.
The four half-observed positions permit **1,296 local completions** before
language is considered. `ZWISCEN` is therefore a contextual, zero-substitution
candidate, not a uniqueness result. The full fill ledger and both
source-origin maps are retained in the certificate.

<details>
<summary>Earlier partial edition and the more costly WIEDER alternative</summary>

**Edited output — earlier partial edition, with 64/67 fixed positions after 21 printed-mask fills and one missing-coordinate fill; no observed substitutions:**

```text
ERBITTENVORSCHLAGFUERVERKEHRSZEITENXWI??E?RINGBAHNZEITENXAKONACHELF
```

The current proposal revises the assumed separator fill and supplies the
three masks this earlier edition left open. The earlier template, readable
display and complete ledger are preserved separately in the certificate.

**Conditional interpretation — earlier WIEDER proposal, outside the primary counts:**

```text
ERBITTENVORSCHLAGFUERVERKEHRSZEITENXWIEDERRINGBAHNZEITENXAKONACHELF
```

`WIEDER` would make the phrase “Wieder Ringbahnzeiten.” It requires three
observed-coordinate substitutions, at source 103 `D`→`A`,
110 `V`→`G`, and 124 `G`→`D`, plus three additional source-mask fills.
The additional fills are measured against the earlier partial edition. Its
total cost remains **3 substitutions, 24 source-mask fills and 1 missing-coordinate
fill**. The current `ZWISCEN` proposal gives a coherent interpretation at
zero observed substitutions. The older alternative and its original cost
remain reproducible; neither whole phrase has an independent copy here.

</details>

The complete current template was compared with every one of the **134**
possible transmitted-coordinate insertion boundaries. **132 and 133 are
equally minimum at zero observed substitutions**. Both supply coordinate
`D` and produce the same completed ciphertext, with different source-origin
maps and independent fill ledgers. Before the fills, boundary 132 fixes
42/67 raw positions and the displayed boundary 133 fixes 43/67. Appending remains the displayed convention,
not a uniquely established historical loss position. The template was chosen
after inspection, so this is a consistency check rather than a blind recovery
or an independently calibrated language-model result.

## p99 C1: service mail routed through Gleiwitz

C has header `UKS v ZON`, reception `11.35 p.m., November 1st`, origin
`2000 (1) AN LP 2 TLE`. Its first part is `1 TL RICHI-136`. The
[C crop](../../experiments/nov1_contact_mail_and_sava/sources/p99_C.png)
shows 136 slots, including 14 dashes. Its last line contains the visible
three-coordinate group `AAA` after two dashes. Those three `A` characters
are retained as observed coordinates.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 136-slot frame**

```text
OXH9L?OPXDIEDS?POSTXFUOR?AXOXKX?L?XNACHGA???SONKOM???DOXGLEI???ZXOXS
```

**Edited output — 3 observed substitutions and 14 source-mask fills**

```text
OXHXLXOPXDIENSTPOSTXFUERXAXOXKXELFXNACHGARNISONKOMMANDOXGLEIWITZXOXS
```

</details>

**Readable German — from the edited layer**

> O.H.L. Op. Dienstpost fuer A.O.K. Elf nach Garnisonkommando Gleiwitz O.S.

The candidate sends service mail for `A.O.K. ELF` to the garrison command
at Gleiwitz `O.S.`. It becomes 68/68 fixed after explicitly changing source
122–124 from `AAA` to `DGV` and filling the 14 dashes. Those substitutions
change raw label 3 `9`→`X`, label 12 `D`→`N`, and label 22 `O`→`E`.
The `9` lies inside the damaged `O.H.L.` sequence; this local repair does
not relabel the key or any historical numeric field. The completion of the
place and office names remains an editorial hypothesis constrained by the
observed coordinates, not a uniqueness claim.

## p99 C2: collection by aircraft

The same C header identifies the second part, `2 TL RICHI-102`. Its 102
source slots begin with five printed dashes. The 97 valid coordinates are
unchanged in both layers.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 102-slot frame**

```text
DORTA?HOLUNGDUR?HFLUGZEU?XAXOXKXEL?XRMXLXDX?RX7011X
```

**Edited output — 5 source-mask fills, no observed substitutions**

```text
DORTABHOLUNGDURCHFLUGZEUGXAXOXKXELFXRMXLXDXNRX7011X
```

</details>

**Readable German — from the edited layer**

> Dort Abholung durch Flugzeug. A.O.K. Elf. RM L D Nr. 7011.

The continuation requests collection there by aircraft. Reference `7011`
is literal and unchanged. `RM L D` remains an unexplained abbreviated
sequence. The five source-mask fills are at source 0–4, with values `VDFAG`.
The native source and shared header support the two-part association; no
missing third part is invented from the earlier OCR header error.

## p99 D: acknowledgment of an OHL message

D has header `UKS v ZON`, an unspecified reception time on November 1,
origin `2015 (1) AN LP`, and `RICHI-100`. The
[D crop](../../experiments/nov1_contact_mail_and_sava/sources/p99_D.png)
contains 100 valid coordinates. The final group is `VXFGD`.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — unchanged native 100-slot frame**

```text
ANXOXHXLXXEINSXAXNRX11127XGAHXOPXERHALTENXEXOXKX11
```

</details>

**Readable German — from the unchanged raw layer**

> An O.H.L. Eins A Nr. 11127 GAH Op. erhalten. E.O.K. 11.

This acknowledges receipt of the cited message. All 50 plaintext positions
are fixed without edits. `11127`, `11`, `GAH`, and the unusual closing
`E.O.K.` remain literal; no cleaner headquarters abbreviation is substituted.
The earlier OCR-derived candidate already had this body with one unresolved
label. The source check fixes that reading without a historical transmission
repair and retains the earlier candidate in the provenance record.

## Evidence, limits and reproduction

The published key retains the credit of **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel,
Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**. The current source and arithmetic review is by
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. This package makes no first historical
body-reading claim. Its [prior-evidence record](../../experiments/nov1_contact_mail_and_sava/prior_evidence.json)
retains the earlier unreviewed OCR outputs and explains their missing rows.
The separate [p100 challenge](../p100.md) keeps Armin's earlier body credit.

The [experiment README](../../experiments/nov1_contact_mail_and_sava/README.md)
gives the standard-library verifier, optional source-pixel verification,
exact model-binding check and the distinction between the primary edition
and the retained earlier `WIEDER` hypothesis. Every readable passage is checked
character by character against all non-`X` labels in its cited stream.
For A, the verifier removes only the explicitly declared bracketed `h`
before that comparison and checks the literal seven-label `ZWISCEN` span.

# November 22: reverse key use and an Aufbau date correction

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Two records on Childs p214 preserve instructions about retaining keys and
correcting date-like labels. The unchanged published **Nov22–24** key gives
**133/134 fixed raw positions** from **268 native source slots**. The proposed
complete reading fills **one invalid source glyph**, with **no change to an
observed coordinate** and no inserted, deleted or reordered source slot.
Published period-key recovery retains the credit to George Lasry and
collaborators recorded in the [key inventory](../../data/keys.json).


**Reviewed source crops:** [p214_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov22_reverse_keys_and_date_correction/sources/p214_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).
## p214 A1

[Reviewed source image — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov22_reverse_keys_and_date_correction/inputs.json).

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — literal headers:**

```text
22nd NOVEMBER, 1918.
A) ZOEN v BSL (04.25 a.m., November 23d)
1600 (11/22) 2 TLE
1 TL RIZI-180
```

</details>

`ZOEN` represents the O with two marks in the call sign. The November 22
heading and internal date are kept separately from the November 23 receipt.
The header advertises two parts, but this section prints only the first.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — native 180-slot frame; 90/90 fixed positions:**

```text
BISAUFWEITERESSAEMTLICHESSCHLUESSELABJJXAUFBEWAHRENXFUERDEZEMBERDANNXRUECKWAERTSVERWENDENX
```

</details>

**Readable German — complete raw stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Bis auf weiteres saemtliches Schluessel ab JJ aufbewahren. Fuer Dezember dann rueckwaerts verwenden.

The grammatical form **`SAEMTLICHES SCHLUESSEL`** is deliberately retained.
Changing it to a smoother form would alter the decoded stream. **`JJ`** is
kept as two literal square labels rather than converted into a date.

The message says to retain the keys from the stated label and then use them
backwards for December. **`RUECKWAERTS` is directly decoded.** This part does
not supply a complete schedule or explain every detail of the reversal, and
a transmitted instruction alone does not establish actual subsequent use.
The [p145/p211 Ringbahn schedule](nov6_ringbahn_key_witnesses.md) and the
[later BSL–UKS arrangement](late_november_cipher_instructions.md) remain
separate source statements; their rules are not silently substituted here.

The earlier OCR omitted the printed final group **`AAVXA`** and transcribed
the five-slot **`VVXAF`** as six characters. Restoring those visible groups
produces the printed 180-slot stream. These corrections repair the machine
transcript; they do not add or remove coordinates from the source.

## p214 C

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — literal header:**

```text
C) BSL v ZOEN (06.09 p.m., November 22d)
RIZI-88
```

</details>

The printed date is **November 22d**, unlike the earlier OCR's November 23d.
The ciphertext contains the Y-like invalid initial glyph in **`YXAFF`**;
that literal observation remains in the transcription and is masked for the
raw decryption.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 88-slot frame; 43/44 fixed positions:**

```text
A?FBAUNICHTJ8XODERJ7XSONDERNJ7XODERJ3XNOVXXX
```

**Edited output — one source-mask fill; no observed-coordinate substitution; 44/44 fixed positions:**

```text
AUFBAUNICHTJ8XODERJ7XSONDERNJ7XODERJ3XNOVXXX
```

</details>

Supplying **V** at **source index 60** gives the U in `AUFBAU`. The index is
zero-based. This is a fill of an already present invalid source slot, not an
inserted coordinate or a change to an accepted coordinate.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Aufbau nicht J8 oder J7, sondern J7 oder J3 Nov.

The two occurrences of **`J7`** remain, as do **`J8`** and **`J3`**. The message
corrects date-like alternatives associated with `Aufbau`; it does not itself
identify a unit or an installation. Adjacency alone does not establish that
this is the missing second part of A or a correction of a particular other
telegram.

## Evidence and verification

The [source inputs](../../experiments/nov22_reverse_keys_and_date_correction/inputs.json)
retain the complete literal groups, headers, published key and reading
proposals. The [certificates](../../experiments/nov22_reverse_keys_and_date_correction/certificates.json)
check each output position, the single mask fill, exact re-encryption and
the complete readable-label mapping. The original OCR and its unchanged-key
outputs remain available as separately labelled comparisons.

```sh
python experiments/nov22_reverse_keys_and_date_correction/verify.py --verify
python experiments/nov22_reverse_keys_and_date_correction/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
```

The optional PDF check compares the saved crop with the original source
pixels. These source editions preserve earlier key and repository credits;
no universal first-decipherment priority is asserted.

# Radio reception instructions and a brief no-events report

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The two-part p224 A telegram asks for experienced listeners, clear transmission and a suitable reception wavelength. The separate p224 B report states that nothing special has happened. This edition preserves the source-length spellings SICERES and MORENMELDUNG and the date-like field 17XJJ.

The present work supplies an image-reviewed source edition and a reproducible repair account; it does not claim that every body is a first public decipherment.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Coordinate substitutions | Source-mask fills |

**Readable German** — based on the explicitly repaired output below.

> Bitte Station mit besonders guten Hoerern zu besetzen. Maessig schnell, deutliche Zeichen in Gruppenabstaenden zu senden. Da Funkstation

**Meaning:** Staff the station with especially good listeners; transmit at a moderate speed with clear signs and spaces between groups. The sentence continues in part 2.

# Receipt request through Nikolajew: the other p105 telegram

[Case index](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This is the 300-slot **section A** on Childs p105, a request to confirm receipt of two communications to Mackensen command through Nikolajew. It is separate from the original [p105 challenge](../p105.md), which is the 290-slot section B. The complete native source yields 150 fixed output labels without changing any coordinate or square cell.


**Reviewed source crops:** [p105_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov2_nikolajew_acknowledgment/sources/p105_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).
## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed source excerpt — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov2_nikolajew_acknowledgment/inputs.json) · [Literal inputs](../../experiments/nov2_nikolajew_acknowledgment/inputs.json) · [Position and repair certificates](../../experiments/nov2_nikolajew_acknowledgment/certificates.json)

The published `Nov1-3` key is unchanged. [Earlier OCR evidence](../../experiments/nov2_nikolajew_acknowledgment/ocr_snapshot.json) and its [recomputed decode](../../experiments/nov2_nikolajew_acknowledgment/prior_candidates.json) are retained. This edition adds checked framing, explicit reading limits and a readable display; it makes no first-public-decipherment claim.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [p105 A](#p105-a) | 300 | 150 / 150 | 0 | 0 |

## p105 A

**Source transcription — header:** `A) FUER UKS v LP (5.10 p.m., November 2nd); 1530 (2/11); RICHI-300`

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order:**

```text
ANXOBERKDOXMACKENSENXEMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNGXVONXRMX1XAXA1118XGEHXOPXUNDXRMX1XAX111M7XGEHXOPXUEBERXNIKOLAJEWXDURCHXFTXERBETENXOHLXRMX1XAXNOX104716XGEWXOP
```

</details>

**Readable German — the same nonseparator labels as the unchanged raw output:**

> An Oberkdo. Mackensen. Empfangsbestaetigung von RM. 1. A. A1118 GEH. OP. und RM. 1. A. 111M7 GEH. OP. ueber Nikolajew durch F. T. erbeten. OHL. RM. 1. A. No. 104716 GEW. OP.

**Meaning:** The message requests radio confirmation through Nikolajew that Mackensen command received the two referenced communications. The raw reference strings A1118 and 111M7, and the final GEW designation, are preserved.

### Editorial limits

- This physical record is section A; the original p105 challenge concerns the different 290-slot section B and retains its identifier and earlier attribution.
- All 300 source slots are retained in the printed order. The earlier 308-slot OCR block included seven characters from the next header and expanded printed DXXXX to six characters; correcting the machine transcription is not an alteration of the historical ciphertext.
- The primary readable display changes spacing and punctuation only. A1118, 111M7 and GEW are not silently converted to more familiar references.
- A separately priced interpretation compares the two references with independent p105 C1 and p106 A2; agreement of subject matter supports a reference-identification hypothesis, not an assertion that the telegrams are identical copies.

## Conditional interpretation of the reference fields

The different telegram on [p105 C1](nov2_telegram_acknowledgments.md#p105-c1) addresses A. O. K. Mackensen and prints `11118` and `11127` together in a request to acknowledge receipt. Its continuation [p106 A2](nov2_telegram_acknowledgments.md#p106-a2) again uses `11127`. Those native readings supply a concrete comparison for this section A’s `A1118` and `111M7`.

Identifying the communications mentioned here with that independently received reference pair is an **additional assumption**. The texts have different wording and their own outgoing references. Topic, addressee and date proximity do not prove that their serials must be identical. The native p105 A fields stay unchanged above.

| Proposed change | Extra observed-coordinate substitution | Source index, zero-based |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `A1118` → `11118` | 1 | 194: `G` → `F` |
| `111M7` → `11127` | 1 | 260: `V` → `F` |
| Final `GEW` → `GEH` | 1 | 94: `G` → `V` |

The first two changes together cost **two substitutions**. The final abbreviation normalization is a separate, third substitution; the reference comparison does not authenticate that footer correction.

**Conditional interpretation — both reference identifications, two substitutions in total:**

```text
ANXOBERKDOXMACKENSENXEMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNGXVONXRMX1XAX11118XGEHXOPXUNDXRMX1XAX11127XGEHXOPXUEBERXNIKOLAJEWXDURCHXFTXERBETENXOHLXRMX1XAXNOX104716XGEWXOP
```

**Conditional interpretation — both references plus the separate footer normalization, three substitutions in total:**

```text
ANXOBERKDOXMACKENSENXEMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNGXVONXRMX1XAX11118XGEHXOPXUNDXRMX1XAX11127XGEHXOPXUEBERXNIKOLAJEWXDURCHXFTXERBETENXOHLXRMX1XAXNOX104716XGEHXOP
```

The verifier independently decodes the cited native records, checks their unchanged key and exact reference positions, and re-encrypts both optional p105 A streams. These alternatives count as no additional physical record and do not enter the primary zero-repair totals.

## Reproduction and credit

Run `python experiments/nov2_nikolajew_acknowledgment/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to check the original PDF and the exact rendered pixels of the preserved source excerpt.

The verifier reconstructs source-coordinate pairs, checks raw domains, replays all priced changes, verifies the readable display without dropping unresolved labels, and checks a global completion witness where required. Such a completion is mechanical evidence, not a historical guess.

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

# November 2: acknowledgment instructions and a conflicting copy

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The matching `FUER UKS 2/11 1300 3 TEILE` headers on pp105–106 identify three numbered parts. Their **636 native coordinates** give **318/318 fixed raw positions** without any repair. The page-local C/A section labels remain in the physical record identifiers.

## p105 C1

Childs p105, PDF p108; [reviewed source crop](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/sources/p105_C1.png). Key: unchanged published **Nov1–3**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — literal received header:**

```text
C) NKJ v LP (4.55 p.m., November 2nd)
FUER UKS 2/11 1300 3 TEILE
1 TL RICHI-238
```

**Raw output — native 238-slot frame; 119/119 fixed positions:**

```text
ERSTENSXANXAXOXKXMACKENSENXXBITTEDRAHTUNGXROEMX1XAX11118XGEHXOPXUNDFUNKSPRUCHXRMX1XAX11127XGEHXOPXINZUKUNFTEMPFANGALLER
```

</details>

**Readable German — complete raw stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Erstens an A. O. K. Mackensen. Bitte Drahtung ROEM. 1. A. 11118. GEH. OP. und Funkspruch RM. 1. A. 11127. GEH. OP. in Zukunft Empfang aller

**Meaning:** The first instruction addresses AOK Mackensen and cites a wire and a radio telegram. The request continues in the next printed part; no words are silently supplied to improve its telegraphic syntax.

## p106 A2

Childs p106, PDF p109; [reviewed source crop](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/sources/p106_A.png). Key: unchanged published **Nov1–3**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — literal received header:**

```text
A) NKJ v LP (4.55 p.m., November 2nd)
FUER UKS 2/11 1300 3 TEILE
2 TL RICHI-250
```

**Raw output — native 250-slot frame; 125/125 fixed positions:**

```text
TELEGRAMMEDURCHXFXTXZUBESTAETIGENXXOXHXLXRMX1XAX104660XOPXXZWEITENXANXAXOXKX11XXBITTEEMPFANGFUNKSPRUCHXRMX1XAX11127XGEHXOPXIN
```

</details>

**Readable German — complete raw stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Telegramme durch F. T. zu bestaetigen. O. H. L. RM. 1. A. 104660. OP. Zweiten an A. O. K. 11. Bitte Empfang Funkspruch RM. 1. A. 11127. GEH. OP. in

**Meaning:** This completes the instruction to acknowledge telegrams by radio, then begins the second instruction addressed to AOK 11. The encoded ZWEITEN and all references remain unchanged.

## p106 A3

Childs p106, PDF p109; [reviewed source crop](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/sources/p106_A.png). Key: unchanged published **Nov1–3**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — literal received header:**

```text
A) NKJ v LP (4.55 p.m., November 2nd)
FUER UKS 2/11 1300 3 TEILE
3 TL RICHI-148
```

**Raw output — native 148-slot frame; 74/74 fixed positions:**

```text
ZUKUNFTEMPFANGALLERTELEGRAMMEDURCHXFXTXBESTAETIGENXXOXHXLXRMX1XAX104659XOP
```

</details>

**Readable German — complete raw stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Zukunft Empfang aller Telegramme durch F. T. bestaetigen. O. H. L. RM. 1. A. 104659. OP.

**Meaning:** The third part completes the instruction for future radio acknowledgment. Its reference is 104659, differing by one literal digit from the p104 copy.

### Earlier-page third-part witness

The p104 source says that parts 1 and 2 are missing and dates its message `1/11`; the three-part copy is dated `2/11`. The p104 body differs from p106 A3 in exactly **source coordinate 54**, V versus X. That changes **plaintext position 68** from 3 to 6: `104359` versus `104659`. Both sources are kept unchanged. The shared wording supports a near-copy relationship, not permission to overwrite either date or reference.

## p104 A3

Childs p104, PDF p107; [reviewed source crop](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/sources/p104_A3.png). Key: unchanged published **Nov1–3**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — literal received header:**

```text
Page heading: 1st NOVEMBER, 1918.
A) NKJ (COS) v LP (8.03 p.m., November 3rd)
WH UKS (1/11) 1300 3 TEILE
(1st and 2nd Teile missing)
3 TL RICHI-148
```

**Raw output — native 148-slot frame; 74/74 fixed positions:**

```text
ZUKUNFTEMPFANGALLERTELEGRAMMEDURCHXFXTXBESTAETIGENXXOXHXLXRMX1XAX104359XOP
```

</details>

**Readable German — complete raw stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Zukunft Empfang aller Telegramme durch F. T. bestaetigen. O. H. L. RM. 1. A. 104359. OP.

**Meaning:** A surviving third part requests future radio acknowledgment of every telegram. Its reference is literally 104359, and its date conflicts with the near-copy elsewhere in this edition.

## Attribution and reproducibility

Earlier unreviewed repository candidates already identified these bodies. This edition reviews the source images, retains their literal observations and publishes the exact repair or frame account; it makes no first-decipherment claim. The key keeps its earlier published provenance.

[Inputs](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/inputs.json), [full certificates](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/certificates.json), [earlier candidates](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/prior_candidates.json), and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/README.md) preserve the evidence.

# UKS connection and an unnecessary relay

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

## p104 B

Childs p104, PDF p107; [reviewed source crop](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/sources/p104_B.png). Key: unchanged published **Nov1–3**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — literal received header:**

```text
Page heading: 2nd NOVEMBER, 1918.
B) LP v NKJ (9.34 p.m., November 3rd)
FUR COS SS BERLIN W20 1240 SS BERLIN W43 1241 SS BERLIN W14 1350 VE 1537 (2/11)
RIZI-102
```

**Raw output — native 102-slot frame; 50/51 fixed positions:**

```text
VERBDGXMIT5UKSXGUTXRERMITTLGXNSMXNICHT?OETIGX6NKJXX
```

**Edited output — 1 observed-coordinate substitution; 1 source-mask fill; 51/51 fixed positions:**

```text
VERBDGXMIT5UKSXGUTXVERMITTLGXNSMXNICHTNOETIGX6NKJXX
```

</details>

Observed source changes, with zero-based indices: **82 A→G**.

Source-mask fills: **84 -→G**.

The full edited stream re-encrypts exactly under the declared frame and listed changes.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Verbdg. mit 5UKS gut. Vermittlg. NSM nicht noetig. 6NKJ.

**Meaning:** The link to 5UKS is reported good and mediation through NSM unnecessary. The 5, 6 and NSM remain literal output labels; they are not replaced by presumed spaces or OSM.

## Interpretation limits

The damaged source slot belongs to the adjective `NOETIG`; the local fill does not solve a numerical key assignment. The exact output `5UKS`, `NSM` and `6NKJ` is preserved in every layer. In particular, the readily guessed station spelling OSM is not imposed on the received `NSM`. The report establishes only what the sender stated about the connection.

## Attribution and reproducibility

Earlier unreviewed repository candidates already identified these bodies. This edition reviews the source images, retains their literal observations and publishes the exact repair or frame account; it makes no first-decipherment claim. The key keeps its earlier published provenance.

[Inputs](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/inputs.json), [full certificates](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/certificates.json), [earlier candidates](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/prior_candidates.json), and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/README.md) preserve the evidence.
