# Radio notices, Tiflis personnel and internment on p230

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Four source-length telegrams on Childs p230 become complete literal readings under the published Nov28–Dec1 square. All 490 coordinates are preserved: no coordinate substitution, source-mask fill or frame change is needed. The source itself gives two first-group readings for C; both are retained.

## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed page excerpt](../../experiments/nov30_radio_personnel/sources/p230_reviewed.png) · [Exact inputs](../../experiments/nov30_radio_personnel/inputs.json) · [Position-by-position certificates](../../experiments/nov30_radio_personnel/certificates.json)

The unchanged published key is `Nov28-Dec1`. The [earlier unreviewed candidates](../../experiments/nov30_radio_personnel/prior_candidates.json) and [original OCR records](../../experiments/nov30_radio_personnel/ocr_snapshot.json) are preserved. The present work supplies an image-reviewed source edition and a reproducible repair account; it does not claim that every body is a first public decipherment.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Coordinate substitutions | Source-mask fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [p230 B](#p230-b) | 136 | 68 / 68 | 0 | 0 |
| [p230 C](#p230-c) | 78 | 39 / 39 | 0 | 0 |
| [p230 D](#p230-d) | 188 | 94 / 94 | 0 | 0 |
| [p230 E](#p230-e) | 88 | 44 / 44 | 0 | 0 |

## p230 B

**Source transcription — header:** `B) ZON v CV (06.33 p.m., December 3d); 2130 (30/11); RICHI-136`

**Readable German** — based on the unchanged raw output.

> Inspektion und Kriegsministerium verstaendigt. Antwort steht noch aus. Papp.

**Meaning:** The inspection and the War Ministry have been notified; a reply is still outstanding. Signed Papp.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
INSPEKTIONUNDKRIEGSMINISTERIUMVERSTAENDIGTYYANTWORTSTEHTNOCHAUSYPAPP
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The page is headed 30 November; the intercept annotation says December 3 and the service line says 2130 (30/11). These are separate source dates.
- A small mark after the last V of VVGFV is not counted as a sixth coordinate. The source count is exactly 136.

## p230 C

**Source transcription — header:** `C) CV v ZON (11.15 p.m., December 6th); 1900 (30/11); RIZI-78; XAFFV (or XVFFV)`

**Readable German** — based on the unchanged raw output.

> Station baut 0ZXJ frueh 9 Uhr ab. Burkard.

**Meaning:** A station announces when it will dismantle. The printed key labels do not establish the historical day or hour; Burkard is the literal signature.

The [shared late-November square](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/README.md)
narrows the hour to **4 or 5**. Its `DX` pair is also the final digit of
`SCHWERE1?` on [p226 A2](radio_traffic_transfer_fragment.md#a-date-and-station-field-that-must-be-read-together).
The earlier date-like field becomes `7Z12`, still garbled. Both printed
first-group variants remain in the
[additional-traffic certificate](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/traffic_certificate.json).

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
STATIONBAUT0ZXJYFRUEH9YUHRABYYBURKARDYY
```

**Raw output — second printed source variant**, independently re-encrypted without repair.

```text
STATIONBAUT0ZXJZFRUEH9YUHRABYYBURKARDYY
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The source explicitly prints XAFFV (or XVFFV). Both complete 78-slot frames are decrypted and re-encrypted. Their only output difference is position 15: Y versus Z. Neither version is silently selected as historically authentic.
- The readable text uses the first printed variant. Its literal field 0ZXJ and its hour label 9 stay unassigned. Under the alternative, the token immediately before FRUEH is 0ZXJZ rather than 0ZXJ followed by Y.
- The intercept annotation says December 6; the service line says 1900 (30/11).

## p230 D

**Source transcription — header:** `D) NKJ v LP (05.47 p.m., December 4th); Fuer COS 1225 (30/11); RICHI-188`

**Readable German** — based on the unchanged raw output.

> Zentralfunkleitg erbitten Nachricht ueber Verbleib Funker und Baupersonal der Funkenstation Tiflis. 54X05.

**Meaning:** The central radio command asks where the radio operators and construction personnel of the Tiflis station have gone. The final 54X05 remains a literal reference.

The closing reference reads **98179** under the
[shared late-November square](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/README.md).
All five coordinate pairs are fully observed. The fourth digit uses the
newly supported `VG=7` assignment, at source positions 187 and 128; this
extends the earlier seven-record comparison by one numeral position.
No source repair is added. The number's documentary referent is unknown.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
ZENTRALFUNKLEITGERBITTENNACHRICHTUEBERVERBLEIBFUNKERUNDBAUPERSONALDERFUNKENSTATIONTIFLISY54X05
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- ZENTRALFUNKLEITG is kept as the transmitted abbreviation; the readable display does not insert its omitted letters.
- The source header says December 4; the service line says Fuer COS 1225 (30/11).

## p230 E

**Source transcription — header:** `E) ZON v CV (04.43 p.m., December 6th); 0930 (30/11); RICHI-88`

**Readable German** — based on the unchanged raw output.

> Internierung rechtzeitig hierher mitteilen. Papp.

**Meaning:** Give timely notification here of the internment. Signed Papp. The short message does not name the persons or formation to be interned.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
INTERNIERUNGRECHTZEITIGHIERHERMITTEILENYPAPP
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The intercept annotation says December 6; the service line reads 0930 (30/11). The earlier OCR gave 0830, which is not retained as the primary source transcription.

## Evidence and credit

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are preserved separately. This is a source edition and explicit repair review, not a claim of universal first-decipherment priority.

The certificates replay every coordinate alteration, compare the independent column/domain reconstruction with the cipher implementation, and re-encrypt every complete edited output. Each readable passage preserves every nonseparator output label; literal protected fields are also checked without removing their internal separators. Source crops are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and RGB-pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/nov30_radio_personnel/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to regenerate and compare the delivered source pixels.

A roundtrip proves compatibility with a stated reading. Editorial spelling repairs remain proposals, and literal number labels are not automatically historical dates, quantities or reference numbers.

# Bucharest dispatch enquiry and power-source specifications

[Case index](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)


**Reviewed source crops:** [p109_A2.png](../../experiments/nov3_bucharest_power_source/sources/p109_A2.png) · [p109_A3.png](../../experiments/nov3_bucharest_power_source/sources/p109_A3.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).
## p109 A2

**Status:** 81/81 native raw positions fixed; 4 coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills. No frame change.

**Source and dates:** Page heading: 3rd NOVEMBER, 1918; A) UKS v OSM (2.09 a.m., November 3rd); VE; 2 TL RICHI-162.

[Source p109 A2 — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov3_bucharest_power_source/inputs.json)

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
GLEICSTVOMOHNEKRAFTQELLEVEDSANDBERBITXBEINACHRCEFANGEFRAGTOBBUKARESTSENDENSOLLENX
```

**Edited output — counted proposal:**

```text
GLEICSTROMOHNEKRAFTQELLEVERSANDBEREITXBEINACHRCEFANGEFRAGTOBBUKARESTSENDENSOLLENX
```

</details>

**Readable German — the same candidate labels with spacing and punctuation:**

> Gleicstrom ohne Kraftqelle versandbereit. Bei Nachrcef angefragt, ob Bukarest senden sollen.

**Meaning:** The fragment reports readiness for dispatch without a power source and says that the office represented by NACHRCEF was asked whether the item should be sent to Bucharest. It does not confirm that dispatch took place. The exact item is not identified by this surviving part alone.

**Conditional interpretation and source details:** All 162 original coordinates are present, including the final VA omitted by the earlier OCR block. Four observed-coordinate substitutions propose GLEICSTROM, VERSAND and BEREIT for GLEICSTVOM, VEDSAND and BERBIT. The residual forms GLEICSTROM, KRAFTQELLE and NACHRCEF are retained exactly: no missing H or U is added to produce fluent modern spellings. This is the source-defined second part; the first part is outside this edition. The following third part supplies a direct power-source query but does not establish that equipment was obtained or transported.

### Explicit source changes

All indices are zero-based.

| Source index | Printed | Proposed | Cost |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 3 | `G` | `V` | Observed-coordinate substitution |
| 10 | `G` | `D` | Observed-coordinate substitution |
| 105 | `V` | `G` | Observed-coordinate substitution |
| 110 | `G` | `A` | Observed-coordinate substitution |

## p109 A3

**Status:** 114/114 native raw positions fixed; 0 coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills. No frame change.

**Source and dates:** Same A heading and reception as p109 A2; 3 TL RICHI-228.

[Source p109 A3 — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov3_bucharest_power_source/inputs.json)

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ISTKRAFTQELLEMOTORETWA50PSMIT220VOLTGLEICHSTRDYNAMO25KWDORTBESCHAFFBARODERTRIEBWXKRAFTANLAGEVERWENDBARXFUNKANTWORT
```

</details>

**Readable German — the same candidate labels with spacing and punctuation:**

> Ist Kraftqelle, Motor etwa 50 PS mit 220 Volt Gleichstr. Dynamo 25 KW, dort beschaffbar oder Triebw. Kraftanlage verwendbar; Funkantwort.

**Meaning:** Asks whether a power source—a motor of about 50 PS with a 220-volt direct-current dynamo rated 25 kW—can be procured there, or whether the power installation denoted TRIEBW can be used. Requests a radio reply. The message asks about availability and does not establish that the equipment exists there or was sent.

**Conditional interpretation and source details:** All 228 observed coordinates yield 114 fixed plaintext positions without any substitution, fill, deletion or insertion. The quantities 50PS, 220VOLT and 25KW are direct raw labels. The source final group is FXX, whereas earlier OCR had FAX. KRAFTQELLE remains the literal spelling; GLEICHSTR and TRIEBW remain abbreviations, and TRIEBW is not expanded into a particular vehicle or plant type. The semicolon before FUNKANTWORT is editorial punctuation only.

### Explicit source changes

No source-coordinate substitution or source-mask fill is used.

### Reproducibility and attribution

The [input](../../experiments/nov3_bucharest_power_source/inputs.json) binds each literal source to exact PDF crops. The [certificate](../../experiments/nov3_bucharest_power_source/certificates.json) contains the raw paired-coordinate domains, each source change and the forward checks. The [verifier](../../experiments/nov3_bucharest_power_source/verify.py) checks the unchanged published keys and the live German quotations, retaining all numerical and letter labels.

Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro (2026). Childs supplies the historical collection; published reconstruction and key provenance credit Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker. Earlier repository OCR and body readings are retained in the [attribution record](../../experiments/nov3_bucharest_power_source/prior_candidates.json).

# Eilvese/OUI: transmission arrangements and provisional traffic times

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p113 section D, part 1, gives transmission and reception arrangements
for **Eilvese/OUI**, followed by provisional transmitting windows. A repeated
source group and its adjacent damaged group create a length conflict:
**362 printed slots** appear under **RIZI-352**. An explicitly conditional
exclusion of ten slots produces a complete **176-position raw reading**
under the unchanged published **Nov1–3** key.

Two ordinary-word repairs, **UNGEDAENPFT→UNGEDAEMPFT** and **BIX→BIS**, cost
**3 observed-coordinate substitutions**. The primary frame needs **no
coordinate fills**. It excludes **7 observed coordinates and 3 printed
dashes**, counted separately from those three word-repair substitutions.
All equally priced frame alternatives are retained. Numerical labels,
including the unusual **3X13**, remain literal.


**Reviewed source crops:** [p113_D1_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov3_eilvese_traffic_schedule/sources/p113_D1_reviewed.png) · [p113_D1_repetition_detail.png](../../experiments/nov3_eilvese_traffic_schedule/sources/p113_D1_repetition_detail.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).
## p113 D1

[Complete reviewed source — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov3_eilvese_traffic_schedule/inputs.json)
and [repeated-group detail — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov3_eilvese_traffic_schedule/inputs.json).

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — header:**

```text
Page heading: 3rd NOVEMBER, 1918.
D) NKJ (UKS) v LP (3 p.m., November 3rd)
0605 (3/11) 2 TLE
1 TL RIZI-352
```

</details>

The page announces two parts. This edition recovers only the printed first
part and does not attach an unrelated nearby telegram as its continuation.
The cipher field is literally **RIZI**, retained as printed.

### Native source, before any exclusion

The [literal transcription](../../experiments/nov3_eilvese_traffic_schedule/inputs.json)
has **362 slots**, of which **359 are valid coordinates** and three are
printed dashes. In row 5, the source prints **FAGVD DG--- FAGVD**, at indices
175–189. All three groups remain in the source record, along with the final
`AV` that the earlier OCR omitted.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — native 362-slot frame; 178/181 fixed positions:**

```text
5DDVOQH855BS4KMW9LP08MP5BF6ENJA2P9S070OXIVGAU1O028PQVI8987C8X5RKBG57QU7H3RDPJFRS1EC57E3PBOFG8WNP1Q1IA?WLNBBCC2R?EZDJARQN?JK65TI83R2VX240D9VD9OM9N9LNYWJE2ODX6I3MPJOH1ARTS7XVC0OAM2UPM
```

</details>

The native output is retained as evidence of the frame conflict; it is not
the readable message below. The printed length difference motivates a
bounded ten-slot comparison, but does not by itself prove a deletion.

### Declared 352-slot frame

The primary frame excludes **source indices 175–184 inclusive**: the first
`FAGVD` and the adjacent `DG---`. It retains the second `FAGVD`, all other
source positions and their order. The scan has no cancellation mark through
the excluded groups, so this remains an editorial frame hypothesis.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional ten-slot exclusion; 176/176 fixed positions:**

```text
EILVESEXOUIXSENDETABX3X13X12XNACHTSXUNGEDAENPFTANSIEMITWELLE9500XOUIEMPFAENGTSIEWELLEX4250XTOENENDXXVORLAUFIGEVERKEHRSZEITENXXOUIXSENDET12NACHTSBIX0100X0330BIS0345X0530BIS0600X
```

**Edited output — the same conditional frame; 3 observed-coordinate substitutions and no fills; 176/176 fixed positions:**

```text
EILVESEXOUIXSENDETABX3X13X12XNACHTSXUNGEDAEMPFTANSIEMITWELLE9500XOUIEMPFAENGTSIEWELLEX4250XTOENENDXXVORLAUFIGEVERKEHRSZEITENXXOUIXSENDET12NACHTSBIS0100X0330BIS0345X0530BIS0600X
```

</details>

**Readable German — complete conditional edited stream, with literal labels and spelling retained:**

> Eilvese. OUI sendet ab 3X13, 12 nachts, ungedaempft an Sie mit Welle 9500. OUI empfaengt Sie Welle 4250, toenend. Vorlaufige Verkehrszeiten: OUI sendet 12 nachts bis 0100, 0330 bis 0345, 0530 bis 0600.

**Meaning:** The telegram sets out sending and receiving arrangements for
Eilvese/OUI and provisional transmitting windows. It uses the technical
terms *ungedaempft* and *toenend*. The stated numerical fields and windows
are reported as transmitted labels; the edition does not independently
authenticate their numerical assignments, add a wavelength unit or a time
zone, or establish that the schedule was implemented.

The field **3X13** is not converted into a plausible date. **Vorlaufige**
keeps the source's encoded spelling without silently adding E or changing
it into an umlauted form. All values **9500**, **4250**, **12**, **0100**,
**0330**, **0345**, **0530** and **0600** remain unchanged.

## Coordinate costs and complete frame alternatives

The word repairs affect two plaintext positions but three observed
coordinates:

| Original source index | Model index after exclusion | Observed-coordinate change |
| ---: | ---: | --- |
| 4 | 4 | G→D |
| 321 | 311 | X→V |
| 348 | 338 | G→V |

The certificate maps each changed pair to its raw and proposed plaintext
letter. It fully re-encrypts the complete 176-position candidate. This
checks the explicit proposal and its source price; it does not turn the
exclusion hypothesis into a visible historical correction.

### Every consecutive ten-slot exclusion

All **353** possible consecutive ten-slot exclusions are compared against
the fixed complete candidate. The minimum is **3 observed-coordinate
substitutions**, attained by starts **172–185 inclusive**. These frames
have different additional source-mask-fill and exclusion costs:

| Exclusion start | Retained source masks that must be filled | Observed coordinates excluded |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 172 or 185 | 3 | 10 |
| 173 or 184 | 2 | 9 |
| 174 or 183 | 1 | 8 |
| Any start from 175 through 182 | 0 | 7 |

All rows exclude ten source slots and require the same minimum observed
substitution count. The **eight no-fill starts 175–182** produce exactly
the same retained ciphertext and raw plaintext. Their source-to-model
mappings differ, so every alias remains in the certificate. The displayed
start 175 is the natural whole-group choice, not a uniquely determined
historical location.

### Every pair of complete five-slot groups

The verifier also compares all **2,556** ways to exclude two of the 72
complete five-slot groups, retaining the final two-character `AV` group.
Three pairs attain the same three-substitution minimum:

| Group starts in original source | Source-mask fills | Observed coordinates excluded |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 175 and 180 | 0 | 7 |
| 180 and 185 | 0 | 7 |
| 185 and 190 | 3 | 10 |

The first two remove `DG---` and one of the two copies of `FAGVD`; they
produce the same complete raw stream. The third remains a recorded minimum
of the observed-substitution objective, but retains all three dashes and
requires their values to be supplied. It is not silently discarded from
the comparison.

These are **fixed-candidate comparisons** within two stated families.
Arbitrary ten-position subsets and all other possible plaintexts have not
been exhausted. The repeated group, advertised length and strong body
reading support this reconstruction, while the absence of an explicit
cancellation keeps the frame conditional.

## Source restoration, attribution and reproduction

Earlier repository OCR supplied **355 slots**, omitting the visible
`DG---` group and final `AV` and masking several printed coordinates.
The reviewed 362-slot transcription restores those marks first; the later
ten-slot exclusion is a separate operation. The frozen old input and its
recomputed unchanged-key output remain available in
[prior candidates](../../experiments/nov3_eilvese_traffic_schedule/prior_candidates.json).

J. Rives Childs's scan is the historical source. Published period-key
recovery by George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker, Lasry's
2017 key list, and earlier repository work retain their credit. The current
work supplies a source edition, bounded frame comparisons and explicitly
priced word repairs. It asserts **no first-decipherment priority**.

[Inputs](../../experiments/nov3_eilvese_traffic_schedule/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/nov3_eilvese_traffic_schedule/certificates.json),
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/nov3_eilvese_traffic_schedule/README.md)
preserve the native reading, exact crops, every retained and excluded source
position, all minimum-frame aliases and full candidate re-encryption.

# Additional listening times on the Ringbahn radio circuit

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

## p117 B

The header is `OUI v OSM`, received at 1.20 a.m. on November 4, with origin
`1900 (3) SSD`. Its unenciphered reception note says that only the first
item was found, that Nr2 could not be copied, and that the characters ran
together. It requests another transmission. No missing second item is supplied.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame**

```text
NACHRCEFXAUSSERVONFALKENHAUSENGENANNTENZEITENW8RDXYSZUDENALTENRINGBAHNZEITENAUFLPHOERENXIMMERINNAECHSTERPERIODEWDHXNURNOCHITOCHI
```

**Edited output**

```text
NACHRCEFXAUSSERVONFALKENHAUSENGENANNTENZEITENWIRDXYSZUDENALTENRINGBAHNZEITENAUFLPHOERENXIMMERINNAECHSTERPERIODEWDHXNURNOCHITOCHI
```

</details>

Price: 1 observed-coordinate substitution, 0 source-mask fills.

**Readable German — based on the edited output**

> Nachrcef. Ausser von Falkenhausen genannten Zeiten wird `YS` zu den alten Ringbahnzeiten auf LP hoeren. Immer in naechster Periode wdh. `NURNOCHITOCHI`.

Only `W8RD`→`WIRD` is repaired. This is a local spelling change, without
relabeling that square cell in other occurrences. The received shortened
`NACHRCEF`, literal `YS`, abbreviation `WDH` and unexplained closing
`NURNOCHITOCHI` remain visible. The paragraph does not identify YS as a
particular station or manufacture a cleaner ending. All 256 source slots
are valid coordinates; the cipher frame itself is unchanged.

## Evidence and reproduction

The published Nov1–3 square and ranks retain the credit of George Lasry,
Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker. The earlier unreviewed OCR candidates
are preserved separately. These are source editions and conditional frame
analyses, without a first historical decipherment claim.

[Literal rows and source images](../../experiments/nov3_medical_radio_withdrawal/inputs.json),
[domains, origins and exact repair certificate](../../experiments/nov3_medical_radio_withdrawal/certificates.json),
and [full method and verification commands](../../experiments/nov3_medical_radio_withdrawal/README.md).

# November 3 radio transmission schedule: surviving second part

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

Childs p110 A explicitly labels this as part 2 of a two-part message:
OSM v LP, received at 3.52 p.m. on November 3, origin `1605 (3/11)`.
Only this second part is identified here. The first part is not supplied.
The published Nov1–3 square and column order are unchanged.

## Source reading

### p110 A2

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
1000BIS1200X1545BIS1645X2100BIS2230XXOSMXSENDET0200BIS0330X0430BCS0530X0900BIS0X45X1900BIS0025X2230BIS2300XXRINGBAHNVERKERAENDERTSICHNICHPXX
```

**Edited output:**

```text
1000BIS1200X1545BIS1645X2100BIS2230XXOSMXSENDET0200BIS0330X0430BIS0530X0900BIS0X45X1900BIS0025X2230BIS2300XXRINGBAHNVERKERAENDERTSICHNICHTXX
```

</details>

Cost: **2 observed-coordinate substitutions** and **0 source-mask fills**. Source length and transposition are unchanged.

The fragment lists transmission intervals, then says that the Ringbahn
traffic does not change. Only `BCS`→`BIS` and `NICHP`→`NICHT` are repaired.
The awkward raw `VERKER` is retained; the missing letters needed for the
modern spelling `VERKEHR` are not inserted.

All time-like fields remain as received, including `0900BIS0X45` and
`1900BIS0025`. The X in the first field is a decoded symbol, not an unknown
placeholder. No replacement hour, date rollover or time zone is inferred.
The earlier OCR screen already gave a largely readable schedule; this is
an exact source edition and repair ledger, not a first-decipherment claim.

## Notation and evidence

The fixed-width strings preserve every plaintext position. `?` means one
unresolved position, `X` is a literal decoded symbol that may serve as a
separator, and digits retain the published square's labels. Word spacing,
calendar values and numerical identities are not silently inferred. A source
mask fill is separate from a change to an observed ADFGVX coordinate.

[Source rows and image metadata](../../experiments/nov3_radio_and_pioneer/inputs.json),
[coordinate and domain certificate](../../experiments/nov3_radio_and_pioneer/certificates.json),
and [method, prior credit and reproduction](../../experiments/nov3_radio_and_pioneer/README.md).

# November 4: Eilvese reception and a setup notice

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The embassy reception query contains an ambiguous overprint; its declared frame makes that uncertainty explicit. The separate short setup notice is a native 56-coordinate record. Both preserve all reference and location labels.

## p120 A

Childs p120, PDF p123; [source crop](../../experiments/nov4_radio_and_departure_queries/sources/p120_A.png). Key: unchanged published **Nov4–6**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — literal received header:**

```text
4th NOVEMBER, 1918.
A) OSM v OUI (11.16 p.m., November 4th)
1950 (4)
RICHI-236
```

**Raw output — conditional 236-slot frame, excluding the overprinted source slot 188; 117/118 fixed positions:**

```text
DEU?SCHMILIATTACHEXXKJDORTX8303X18XISTHELTERTSVERANLASSTXKANN8ORSCHAFTAUCHUNGEDAEMPFTXEILVESEEMPFANGENNACHCHEF4B47883X
```

**Edited output — 7 observed-coordinate substitutions and 1 source-mask fill; same conditional exclusion; 118/118 fixed positions:**

```text
DEUTSCHMILIATTACHEXXZUDORTX8303X18XISTWEITERESVERANLASSTXKANNBOTSCHAFTAUCHUNGEDAEMPFTXEILVESEEMPFANGENNACHCHEF4B47883X
```

</details>

Observed source changes, with zero-based indices: **2 F→V**, **7 V→X**, **34 D→G**, **169 A→V**, **171 G→F**, **186 X→F**, **200 A→V**.

Source-mask fills: **0→A**.

The full edited stream re-encrypts under its stated frame and listed changes.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Deutsch Miliattache. Zu dort 8303.18 ist Weiteres veranlasst. Kann Botschaft auch ungedaempft Eilvese empfangen? Nachchef 4 B 47883.

**Meaning:** The proposed reading addresses the German military attache, refers to 8303.18 and asks whether the embassy can also receive undamped Eilvese transmissions. It does not establish the reception equipment or the outcome of that request.

### Six printed slots and a conditional exclusion

The sixth group of ciphertext row 5 has six spatial glyph positions:
`XXF[T-like overprint]VA`. The literal transcription uses `XXFTVA`, with T
masked as outside the coordinate alphabet. The [detail crop](../../experiments/nov4_radio_and_departure_queries/sources/p120_A_overprint.png)
shows the overstrike. There are **237 source slots**, against `RICHI-236`.
The displayed frame excludes source slot **188**, the masked overprint,
retaining every one of the source's **235 valid coordinates**. A cancellation
is possible, but its intention is not proved; this is a conditional one-slot
exclusion, not a claim of a native five-letter group.

Every local single-slot exclusion is priced against the same proposed text:

| Excluded source slot | Literal | Observed coordinates excluded | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
|185|X|1|6|2|
|186|X|1|6|2|
|187|F|1|7|2|
|188|T-like overprint|0|7|1|
|189|V|1|7|2|
|190|A|1|8|2|

The fewer substitutions in two alternatives are accompanied by deletion of
an observed coordinate and an extra fill. The table is a cost vector, not an
invented single numerical ranking. No other historical damage geometry is
excluded by this local comparison.

The restoration `HELTERTS→WEITERES` is an editorial lexical proposal. It is
not authenticated by a second source. The complete reading preserves the
abbreviations `DEUTSCH MILIATTACHE`, `NACHCHEF` and reference `8303.18`.
The question mark after *empfangen* is editorial question punctuation,
not an extra unresolved decoded position.

## p120 C

Childs p120, PDF p123; [source crop](../../experiments/nov4_radio_and_departure_queries/sources/p120_C.png). Key: unchanged published **Nov4–6**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — literal received header:**

```text
C) UKS v ZON (2.10 a.m., November 5th)
2332 (4)
RIZI-56
```

**Raw output — native 56-slot frame; 28/28 fixed positions:**

```text
0500ABBAUXAPFBAUNAGQBESCEREK
```

**Edited output — 1 observed-coordinate substitution and 0 source-mask fills; 28/28 fixed positions:**

```text
0500ABBAUXAUFBAUNAGQBESCEREK
```

</details>

Observed source changes, with zero-based indices: **51 X→V**.

The full edited stream re-encrypts under its stated frame and listed changes.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> 0500 Abbau. Aufbau NAGQBESCEREK.

**Meaning:** A short notice gives 0500, dismantling and setup, followed by the literal location-like token NAGQBESCEREK. That spelling is not replaced with a modern place-name identity.

### Literal locality and time labels

The source-visible second group on the last row is `VFVFX`; an early low-resolution transcription of its third glyph as T is rejected by the crop. No historical mask or fill is introduced there. Only `APFBAU→AUFBAU` is proposed. `0500` and `NAGQBESCEREK` stay literal; the latter is not silently changed to a familiar locality spelling.

## Attribution and evidence

Earlier unreviewed repository candidates already suggested these bodies. This edition checks the primary images, preserves conflicting source labels and publishes every frame operation, coordinate substitution and fill. Prior published key recovery keeps its original credit; no first-solution priority is claimed.

[Inputs](../../experiments/nov4_radio_and_departure_queries/inputs.json), [certificates](../../experiments/nov4_radio_and_departure_queries/certificates.json), [earlier candidates](../../experiments/nov4_radio_and_departure_queries/prior_candidates.json) and [reproduction](../../experiments/nov4_radio_and_departure_queries/README.md) provide complete source and positional evidence.

# Existing personnel and agreed radio transmissions

[Case index](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

## p127 B1

**Status:** 76/80 native raw positions fixed; 1 observed-coordinate substitution and 3 source-mask fills in the proposal. No frame change. Key: Nov4-6.

**Source and dates:** Page heading: 4th NOVEMBER, 1918; B) LP v NKJ (9.45 p.m., November 5th); 2200 2 TLE; 1 TL RIZI-160.

![Source p127 B1](../../experiments/early_radio_and_leave_records/sources/p127_B1.png)

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
?I?RNOCHALTESPERSONAFXWIRSENDENWIEVERABREDETXWENNNICTMEHRDANNISTOS?AUSGESCHIE?EN
```

**Edited output — counted proposal:**

```text
HIERNOCHALTESPERSONALXWIRSENDENWIEVERABREDETXWENNNICTMEHRDANNISTOS?AUSGESCHIEDEN
```

</details>

**Readable German — the same candidate labels with spacing and punctuation:**

> Hier noch altes Personal. Wir senden wie verabredet. Wenn NICT mehr, dann ist OS? ausgeschieden.

**Meaning:** The sender says the previous personnel are still present and transmissions continue as agreed. The final sentence contains the literal defect NICT and an unresolved OS? label. If NICT is intended as NICHT, it conditionally links ceased transmissions with the departure of OS?; that missing H is not inserted into the cryptographic reading.

**Conditional interpretation and source details:** The first source group is AXVFF; ALTES is already present in the complete raw reading. The later group VFFGF contains a clear F, not an out-of-alphabet T; neither visual correction is a historical ciphertext edit. The proposal changes one observed coordinate and fills three printed masks. The fourth mask leaves OS? unresolved. NICT is retained without adding H. Only the first of two announced parts is included.

### Explicit source changes

All indices are zero-based. Printed masks retain their original slots.

| Source index | Printed | Proposed | Cost |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 2 | `V` | `X` | Observed-coordinate substitution |
| 55 | `-` | `A` | Source-mask fill |
| 93 | `-` | `D` | Source-mask fill |
| 94 | `-` | `A` | Source-mask fill |

### Optional OSM field completion

The unresolved position 66 has domain `4CMNST`, from `X?` at source 44 and
111. Reading the station call sign **OSM** fills the remaining printed mask
111 with **F**, giving `XF=M`. This adds one source-mask fill, with no new
observed-coordinate change: the optional total is **one substitution and
four printed-mask fills**, fixing 80/80 positions under the same native frame.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — optional OSM identification, one mask fill beyond the preceding proposal:**

```text
HIERNOCHALTESPERSONALXWIRSENDENWIEVERABREDETXWENNNICTMEHRDANNISTOSMAUSGESCHIEDEN
```

</details>

**Readable German — same optional labels, retaining NICT:**

> Hier noch altes Personal. Wir senden wie verabredet. Wenn NICT mehr, dann ist OSM ausgeschieden.

This is a conditional identification, supported by the separate
[OSM/OUI staff query](p137_station_staff_query.md) and an independent diary
notice. The [published 2016 study, section 6.5](https://www.apprendre-en-ligne.net/crypto/bibliotheque/PDF/adfgvx.pdf)
identifies OSM with Osmanie. In his entry headed **5 November**, Albert Hopman records at
`11h 30m N` the notice “FT-Station Osmanie von uns aufgegeben”.
[Original diary image, Baumgart edition (1971), p636 / scan646](https://api.digitale-sammlungen.de/iiif/image/v2/bsb00042051_00646/full/1800,/0/default.jpg).
The notice does not quote this telegram. The source's 4 November page heading,
5 November receipt and undated `2200` field remain distinct; no reply relation
or clock reconciliation is asserted. The second announced part remains unread.

[Exact optional-field witness and documentary metadata](../../experiments/early_radio_and_leave_records/osmanie_field_certificate.json)
· [Optional-field verifier](../../experiments/early_radio_and_leave_records/verify_osmanie.py).

### Reproducibility and attribution

The [input](../../experiments/early_radio_and_leave_records/inputs.json) binds each literal source to exact PDF crops. The [certificate](../../experiments/early_radio_and_leave_records/certificates.json) records each raw paired-coordinate domain and every proposed source change. The [verifier](../../experiments/early_radio_and_leave_records/verify.py) checks the live German quotation against the same candidate labels, preserving every digit and unknown position.

This source edition is by icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro (2026). Childs supplies the historical collection. The published reconstruction and unchanged key provenance credit Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker, with Lasry's published period-key list. Earlier repository OCR input is frozen in the [attribution record](../../experiments/early_radio_and_leave_records/prior_candidates.json).

# November 4: repeated-part request and communications inquiry

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The four records preserve two messages with different source frames. All use the unchanged published Nov4–6 key. No group is added, dropped, moved or reordered; all numerical and reference labels remain literal.

The two p121 A parts have the header `FUER COS 1955 (4.11) 2 TL`, explicitly address `GENERAL VON KRESS KAUKASUS`, and are recorded at `03.13 a.m., November 5th` under the November 4 page heading. The discrepancy is retained.

## p121 A1

<details>


> Zu Telegramm vom 30.10. Nr. 8538.18. Z. A. 1. K. C.: hatte um Wiederholung des ersten Teils gebeten. Der 2 und 3 Teil ist bereits

## p121 A2

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — 117/118 fixed positions:**

```text
DECHIFFRIERTXWEI?ERGEGEBENXERNEUTEXBITTEXUMXWIKDERHOLUNGXDESXERSTENXTEILSXKRIEGSMINISTERIUMXNRX8538X18XGXAX1XRMX2XANGX

```

The printed Z-like noncoordinate glyph at source index **224** is masked in the raw analysis and supplied as **X** in this proposal. Its one fill is separate from the known-coordinate changes.

**Meaning:** The second part says that parts 2 and 3 were deciphered and forwarded, and again asks for the first part. The clear header addresses General von Kress in the Caucasus.

### Two parts on different pages

p121 B1 and p122 A2 both print `FUER UKS (4.11) 0035 2 TLE` with parts `1 TL` and `2 TL`. Their recorded reception times are `06.55 a.m.` and `05.25 p.m., November 4th`. > AKONACH 18. Zum Telegr. von Hptm. Zimmermann wegen Konstanza: drahtet, ob Verbindung Bukarest-Konstanza noch im Betrieb, u. was wegen Konstanza

**Meaning:** The query refers to Captain Zimmermann and asks whether the Bucharest–Constanza link is still operating. Its final clause continues on p122.

## p122 A2

Childs p122, PDF p125; [reviewed source crop](../../experiments/nov4_repetition_and_connections/sources/p122_A2.png). The unchanged published **Nov4–6** key uses the native **182-slot** frame.

**Meaning:** The continuation asks what has been arranged concerning Constanza and the cable, and asks about communications with Army High Command 11. It does not answer either operational question.

## Interpretation, attribution and evidence

The first message asks for the **first part** again; it does not identify that missing part in this collection or establish that the request was fulfilled. `Z A 1 K C`, `G A 1 RM 2 ANG`, `8538.18`, `AKONACH 18`, `111511` and `95086` are retained without a new numeral or office interpretation. `U` and `NACHRICHEF` remain the encoded abbreviations.

# German embassy address and abbreviated signature label, reference RM3D8956

[Case index](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

## p148 A1

**Status:** 65/65 native raw positions fixed; 5 coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills. No frame change.

**Source and dates:** Page heading: 6th NOVEMBER, 1918; A) YZ v LP (08.31 a.m., November 7th); FUER YZ 1645 (6/11) 2 TEILE; 1 TL RICHI-130.

![Source p148 A1](../../experiments/nov6_embassy_8956_annotation/sources/p148_A1.png)

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DEUTSCHEBETSCHAFTXKONSTANTINOPEFXD4TERSC1RXAUSWAERTIGXRMX3XDX8956
```

**Edited output — counted proposal:**

```text
DEUTSCHEBOTSCHAFTXKONSTANTINOPELXUNTERSCHRXAUSWAERTIGXRMX3XDX8956
```

</details>

**Readable German — the same candidate labels with spacing and punctuation:**

> Deutsche Botschaft, Konstantinopel. Unterschr. Auswaertig. RM. 3. D. 8956.

**Meaning:** The first part addresses the German embassy in Constantinople and includes the abbreviated signature label UNTERSCHR followed by AUSWAERTIG. The closing retains RM, 3, D and 8956. This address and signature fragment does not establish the content of the second part, which is outside this edition.

**Conditional interpretation and source details:** The source has 130 coordinate slots and all 65 raw plaintext positions are fixed. The earlier OCR input has only 120 positions because it omits two complete five-coordinate groups, VDDVA and FDVVV. The baseline transcribes the printed F at source index 70; a G annotation stands directly above it. Adopting that annotated correction is explicitly charged as one of the five substitutions, and its isolated effect is shown below. The other four substitutions are linguistic proposals; no extra coordinate, source-mask fill or key change is used. The raw word-internal digits in D4TERSC1R are changed only by the explicit coordinate ledger. RM3D8956 is retained exactly. UNTERSCHR is not expanded by adding IFT, and AUSWAERTIG is not expanded by adding AMT.

### Explicit source changes

All indices are zero-based.

| Source index | Printed | Proposed | Cost |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 11 | `F` | `V` | Observed-coordinate substitution |
| 35 | `A` | `G` | Observed-coordinate substitution |
| 70 | `F` | `G` | Observed-coordinate substitution |
| 73 | `V` | `X` | Observed-coordinate substitution |
| 111 | `V` | `X` | Observed-coordinate substitution |

### Source annotation considered on its own

The above-line **G** at source index 70 is retained separately from the printed baseline **F**. Applying only this visible annotation costs one observed-coordinate substitution. It changes **BETSCHAFT** to **BOTSCHAFT**, while the other garbles remain:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — annotation-only branch, applying just source 70 F→G:**

```text
DEUTSCHEBOTSCHAFTXKONSTANTINOPEFXD4TERSC1RXAUSWAERTIGXRMX3XDX8956
```

</details>

The complete reading above costs five substitutions in total: this annotated F→G correction plus four further linguistic proposals. The 130-slot source frame is already present in the scan; restoring the two groups omitted by OCR does not insert anything into the original ciphertext.

### Reproducibility and attribution

The [input](../../experiments/nov6_embassy_8956_annotation/inputs.json) binds each literal source to exact PDF crops. # Osmanie unavailable: the November 6 marine-service notice

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

The telegram reports **Osmanie unavailable** and asks that all stations be
notified. Two source-mask fills complete the names **KIEW** and **OSMANIE**:
earlier telegrams independently supply both spellings from fully observed
coordinate pairs. Heeresgruppe Kiew appears among the recipients; the
literal address label **HZYU** has a separately priced **H. Qu.** proposal below.

## Completed reading

**Readable German — complete conditional reading with the two name fills:**

> Seekriegsleitung. Grosses HZYU. Admiral Berlin. Nachchef. Deutsche Marinevertr und Heeresgruppe Kiew. Osmanie ausgefallen. Alle Stellen benachrichtigen.

The reading has **143/143 fixed labels** in the existing conditional frame.
It requires **3 observed-coordinate substitutions, 6 source-mask fills and
1 added-slot fill**. The new name readings account for two of the source
fills and require no further change to an observed coordinate.

The frame treats a narrow stroke before `VAADA` as an extra mark and supplies
one coordinate at the end. These two assumptions remain necessary: the
native transcription and its different decoding are preserved below.

<details>
<summary>Completed stream and the two new mask values</summary>

**Edited output — completed conditional stream; 3 observed substitutions, 6 source-mask fills and 1 added-slot fill:**

```text
SEEKRIEGSLEITUNGGROSSESXHZYUXXADMIRALBERLINXXNACHCHEFXXDEUTSCHEXMARINEVERTRXUNDHEERESGRUPPEXKIEWXXOSMANIEAUSGEFALLENXALLESTELLENBENACHRICHTIGEN
```

All indices are zero-based and refer to the original 286-slot transcription.

| Field | Plaintext position | Native pair and domain | Added source fill | Independent name witness |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| `KIE?` → `KIEW` | 95 | `A?`: `17FHLW` | 44: printed `C` → `F` | [p110 B](../military/kiew_morning_and_pioneer_reports.md#p110-b), raw `HRG KIEW` |
| `O?MANIE` → `OSMANIE` | 99 | `?G`: `23BHSV` | 146: printed `O` → `X` | [p77 B](../context/radio_instructions.md#p77-b--call-sign-instruction-for-konia), raw `FUNKERABTLG OSMANIE` |

The witnesses use different period keys. Their complete name pairs are
recomputed in the [certificate](../../experiments/nov6_marine_service_notice/certificates.json);
they support these contextual selections from the native domains. Neither
source is a repeated copy of this notice.

</details>

The abbreviations `Nachchef` and `Marinevertr` are retained. The notice gives
no cause or duration for Osmanie's reported unavailability.

## Optional headquarters address

The address may read **Grosses H. Qu.** (Grosses Hauptquartier). Independent raw telegrams use `HXQU`; applying that abbreviation here changes `GROSSESXHZYUXX` to `GROSSESXHXQUXX`.

The [p102 B1 Orient report](../military/orient_south_slav_reports.md#p102-b1)
contains raw `GD X H X QU`; the [p86 A machine-gun enquiry](../military/mg08_inventory.md)
contains raw `GR X H X QU`. Both abbreviation spans are entirely observed
under earlier period keys. They show usage of the abbreviation, not another
copy of this notice.

| Proposed label change | Pair change | Additional observed substitution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Position 25: `Z` → separator `X` | `FV` → `FD` | Source 104: `V` → `D` |
| Position 26: `Y` → `Q` | `GV` → `GF` | Source 121: `V` → `F` |

Both printed `V` values are clear observations. This interpretation therefore
costs **two further substitutions**, bringing the complete conditional reading
to **5 observed substitutions, 6 source-mask fills and 1 added-slot fill**.
It supplies a plausible recipient without adding fixed positions: the cheaper
143-label layer above still reads `HZYU`. The original frame alternatives and
all numeric labels are unchanged.

## p138 C

Childs's page is headed 6 November 1918. The reception and origin lines also
give 6 November; the cleartext ending follows the ciphertext.

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — headers and cleartext ending:**

```text
6th November 1918.
C) UKS RAT v NKJ (10.32 p.m., November 6th, 1918.)
10.15 6/11 VON ASO KR
RICHI-286
Cleartext ending: B M K - UKS RAT v NKJ UM
```

</details>

**Reviewed source crops:** [p138_C_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov6_marine_service_notice/sources/p138_C_reviewed.png) · [p138_stroke_detail.png](../../experiments/nov6_marine_service_notice/sources/p138_stroke_detail.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).

The [source transcription and crop recipes](../../experiments/nov6_marine_service_notice/inputs.json)
retain the three invalid `W` glyphs, one `C`, two `O` glyphs and the additional
narrow stroke. The cleartext ending is outside the coordinate stream.

### Native frame including the stroke

The narrow stroke is transcribed as `|` at source index 225, between `FADFF`
and `VAADA`. This records a visible mark without identifying it as a cipher
coordinate. Including it gives 286 slots: 279 valid coordinates and 7 masks,
matching the advertised `RICHI-286`.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — native 286-slot frame including the stroke; 136/143 fixed positions:**

```text
SEEM??OGSLEATUMG?ROSSESCFZYU9XADM6RAL2ER9GNXXUAC1CSE?XCDEYTSCBKXM8RLNEV1RTEZ?NWWEEGE2G8U6PE79IE?XXO?MKNREDUSYZFANF1NZALLESTRLPENB1NAC1RLCWTNGE6
```

</details>

### Conditional frame and word repairs

The conditional model omits the masked stroke at original source 225 and
adds an unknown at original source boundary 286. The added coordinate has
model index 285, so the model retains 286 slots. The earlier word-repair layer
is preserved here with its two name masks still open.

<details>
<summary>Earlier conditional stream and word-repair layer</summary>

**Raw output — conditional stroke exclusion plus final-slot insertion; 136/143 fixed positions:**

```text
SEEK??EGSLEITUNG?ROSSESXHZYUXXADMIRALBERLINXXPACHCHEFXXDEUTSCHEXMARINEVERTRX?NDHEERESGRUPPEXKIE?XXO?MANIEAUSGEFALL1NXALLESTRLLENBENACHR?CHTIGEN
```

**Edited output — the same conditional frame; 3 observed-coordinate substitutions, 4 source-mask fills and 1 inserted-slot fill; 141/143 fixed positions:**

```text
SEEKRIEGSLEITUNGGROSSESXHZYUXXADMIRALBERLINXXNACHCHEFXXDEUTSCHEXMARINEVERTRXUNDHEERESGRUPPEXKIE?XXO?MANIEAUSGEFALLENXALLESTELLENBENACHRICHTIGEN
```

**Readable German — complete conditional edited stream, with unresolved labels retained:**

> Seekriegsleitung. Grosses HZYU. Admiral Berlin. Nachchef. Deutsche Marinevertr und Heeresgruppe KIE?. O?MANIE ausgefallen. Alle Stellen benachrichtigen.

</details>

## Separate frame and coordinate costs

The two new name fills extend the earlier word layer; all other costs are
unchanged. No observed coordinate is excluded or reordered.

| Operation | Source position | Result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Exclude ambiguous masked mark | 225 | Omitted only in the conditional model |
| Add unknown slot | Boundary 286 | Added model slot 285, filled with `V` |
| Observed-coordinate substitution | 13 `A`→`F` | `E` in `AUSGEFALLEN` |
| Observed-coordinate substitution | 98 `V`→`F` | `E` in `STELLEN` |
| Observed-coordinate substitution | 174 `D`→`X` | `N` in `NACHCHEF` |
| Invalid `W` fill | 18 `W`→`V` | `G` in `GROSSES` |
| Invalid `W` fill | 84 `W`→`V` | `R` in `SEEKRIEGSLEITUNG` |
| Invalid `W` fill | 110 `W`→`V` | `U` in `UND` |
| Invalid `O` fill | 135 `O`→`X` | `I` in `SEEKRIEGSLEITUNG` |
| Invalid `C` fill, new | 44 `C`→`F` | `W` in `KIEW` |
| Invalid `O` fill, new | 146 `O`→`X` | `S` in `OSMANIE` |
| Added-slot fill | Model 285 →`V` | `I` in `BENACHRICHTIGEN` |

The raw `1` in `AUSGEFALL1N` becomes `E` through the explicit source 13
substitution. The published square is unchanged.

## What the gap comparison establishes

After the stroke exclusion, the retained stream has 285 slots. The original
comparison prices all 286 single-gap alignments against the earlier partial
candidate, with its two unresolved names unconstrained. Adding the slot at
the end is the unique minimum in that family, at 3 observed substitutions.
The [certificate](../../experiments/nov6_marine_service_notice/certificates.json)
retains every price.

| Gap boundary in retained 285-slot stream | Observed substitutions |
| ---: | ---: |
| 280 | 6 |
| 281 | 5 |
| 282 | 4 |
| 283 | 4 |
| 284 | 4 |
| 285, at the end | 3 |

This comparison holds the stroke exclusion and selected body fixed. The
scan shows neither a cancellation through the stroke nor a blank proving a
final omission; other error models and plaintexts remain outside the test.

## Source restoration, attribution and reproduction

Earlier OCR had 279 slots: it omitted the final `FVAAA`, the invalid `W`
after `VXVX`, and the narrow stroke. The [prior-work record](../../experiments/nov6_marine_service_notice/prior_candidates.json)
preserves that input and its unchanged-key output.

Source edition and verification: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Childs
supplies the historical collection. The Nov4–6 period key retains the credit
of George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker, with its published
provenance recorded in the inputs.

[Inputs](../../experiments/nov6_marine_service_notice/inputs.json),
[name-completion evidence](../../experiments/nov6_marine_service_notice/label_completion.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/nov6_marine_service_notice/certificates.json),
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/nov6_marine_service_notice/README.md)
preserve the native frame, source mapping, earlier word repairs, independent
name witnesses and complete re-encryption of the conditional reading.

# November 6 Ringbahn-key instruction: a second three-part witness

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Third reception restored.** The [p187 B1 fragment](nov13_ringbahn_retransmission.md) adds a separately received witness with an exact origin map for every restored coordinate.

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p145 supplies three additional physical witnesses of the instruction
already read in the [p211 lower-B edition](p211_key_schedule.md). They say to
keep the November Ringbahn keys, postpone the December keys, and use the
10 November key for 1 December through the 30 November key for 21 December.
These are the stated instructions; implementation by every station is not
inferred.

The source has **531 typed coordinates**, with a visibly four-symbol group
in part 2 against its advertised length. The declared 532-slot frames give
**266 positions**, **265 fixed raw**. The complete candidates use **5 observed
coordinate substitutions** and **1 fill in the hypothesized added slot**.
Every proposed changed plaintext position is directly supported by a fixed
raw position in the independently inspected p211 source. Conversely, the
p145 raw text directly supports all four earlier p211 word repairs.

## Dates and source identity

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — literal p145 headers:**

```text
6th NOVEMBER, 1918.
B) WAU (KOW RVA) NKJ (IWE RTS) ASO v LP (02.53 a.m., November 7th)
SS DD 2230 (6/11) 3 TEILE
1 TL RICHI-214
2 TL RICHI-184
3 TL RICHI-134
```

</details>

The [p211 source crop](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/sources/childs_p211_selected.png)
instead has a **19 November** heading and **22 November** receipt, with
`FUER POT COS VON LP SS DD 2230 3 TLE`. Both copies decode under the unchanged
published **Nov4–6** key. The date layers remain as printed. No date is
rewritten to fit the cipher period or the December instruction.

## p145 B1

[Reviewed source crop](../../experiments/nov6_ringbahn_key_witnesses/sources/p145_B1.png).

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 214-slot frame; 107/107 fixed positions:**

```text
NOVEMBERXRINGBAHNSCHLUESSELNICHTVERNICHTENXNACHRCHEFXGXB848727XXDEZEMBERX1INGBAHNSCHLUESSELTRITTVORLAEUFIGX
```

**Edited output — 1 observed-coordinate substitution; no fills; 107/107 fixed positions:**

```text
NOVEMBERXRINGBAHNSCHLUESSELNICHTVERNICHTENXNACHRCHEFXGXB848727XXDEZEMBERXRINGBAHNSCHLUESSELTRITTVORLAEUFIGX
```

</details>

Observed source changes, using zero-based indices: **46 A→V**.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> November-Ringbahnschluessel nicht vernichten. Nachrchef G B848727. Dezember-Ringbahnschluessel tritt vorlaeufig

## p145 B2

[Reviewed source crop](../../experiments/nov6_ringbahn_key_witnesses/sources/p145_B2.png).

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 184-slot frame: one unknown slot inserted at source boundary 33; 91/92 fixed positions:**

```text
NICHTINKRAFTX?MFUERSCHLDESSELERSTERDEZEMBERWIEZEHNTERNOVEMBERUSWBISEINUNDZWKNZIGSTERDEZEMBER
```

**Edited output — 3 observed-coordinate substitutions and 1 inserted-slot fill, under the same conditional frame; 92/92 fixed positions:**

```text
NICHTINKRAFTXDAFUERSCHLUESSELERSTERDEZEMBERWIEZEHNTERNOVEMBERUSWBISEINUNDZWANZIGSTERDEZEMBER
```

</details>

Observed source changes, using zero-based indices: **44 F→V**, **87 X→V**, **127 F→V**.

The visibly short `XFVA` at source positions 30–33 becomes `XFVFA` by adding **F at source boundary 33**. This added value is not counted as a fill of a printed dash. The resulting complete ciphertext is **identical to the unedited p211 lower-B part 2**.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> nicht in Kraft. Dafuer Schluessel erster Dezember wie zehnter November usw. bis einundzwanzigster Dezember

## p145 B3

[Reviewed source crop](../../experiments/nov6_ringbahn_key_witnesses/sources/p145_B3.png).

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 134-slot frame; 67/67 fixed positions:**

```text
WIEDREISSIGSTERNOVEMBERXXEMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNGXXNKCHRCHEFX4XBX47857X
```

**Edited output — 1 observed-coordinate substitution; no fills; 67/67 fixed positions:**

```text
WIEDREISSIGSTERNOVEMBERXXEMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNGXXNACHRCHEFX4XBX47857X
```

</details>

Observed source changes, using zero-based indices: **68 F→V**.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> wie dreissigster November. Empfangsbestaetigung. Nachrchef 4 B47857.

## Cross-copy repair support and preserved disagreements

All five possible insertions within the short `XFVA` group are priced against
the independently read p211 part 2:

| Source boundary | Observed-coordinate substitutions | Added value |
|---|---:|---|
| 30 | 6 | X |
| 31 | 5 | F |
| 32 | 4 | V |
| 33 | 3 | F |
| 34 | 4 | A |

The boundary-33 frame has the least observed-coordinate cost within this
explicit five-alignment family. The three substitutions concern source
indices **44, 87 and 127**. This comparison uses an actual copy, not a text
selected solely for a higher language score; it still does not identify the
historical stage at which the coordinate was lost.

The reverse support is also exact. In p145 part 1, the unedited letters at
plaintext indices **9, 19 and 67** support the p211 proposals `RINGBAHN`,
`SCHLUESSEL` and `DEZEMBER`. In p145 part 3, unedited position **10** supports
the p211 `DREISSIGSTER` fill. Both source transcriptions remain available;
these observations do not merge the physical records.

The reference labels remain different. p145 has literal `NACHRCHEFXG` in
part 1 and `NACHRCHEFX4` in part 3; the p211 outputs have `NACHRCHEFX4` and
`NACHRCHEFZ4`. Those labels are **not regularized**, even though the schedule
words agree. The numerical fields `B848727` and `47857` likewise stay literal.

**Meaning:** The schedule itself is the already established instruction to
reuse November key dates for the beginning of December. These p145 witnesses
provide independent character-level support for the text, recover a short
source group, and expose the differing date and reference layers. They add
no claim about the behavior of any station or the key of a particular
December ciphertext.

## Attribution and verification

The previously published p211 edition and prior published period-key recovery
retain their separate credit. An earlier unreviewed repository candidate
already read the p145 ending; the new source edition reconstructs all three
printed parts and prices their correspondence to p211. No first-decipherment
priority is claimed.

[Inputs](../../experiments/nov6_ringbahn_key_witnesses/inputs.json),
[certificates and mutual source support](../../experiments/nov6_ringbahn_key_witnesses/certificates.json),
[prior attribution](../../experiments/nov6_ringbahn_key_witnesses/prior_candidates.json),
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/nov6_ringbahn_key_witnesses/README.md)
preserve exact source and frame indices, every raw domain, all five local
alignments and full re-encryptions.

# November 6 Ringbahn-key instruction to Tiflis

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The two-part **section C on Childs p146** tells the Caucasus delegation at
Tiflis to retain November Ringbahn keys and use them for the beginning of
December. Its schedule agrees with independently readable spans in the
[p145 instruction](nov6_ringbahn_key_witnesses.md) and
[p211 lower-B instruction](p211_key_schedule.md), but this dispatch has its
own wording, address and part boundaries. The original
[p146 challenge](../p146.md) is section B; these are two different physical
records.

The literal source contains **365 slots**, including six masked coordinates,
against **368 advertised**. The conditional frames insert three unknown
coordinate slots and produce **184 plaintext positions, 175 fixed before
word repairs**. The complete proposed reading uses **1 observed-coordinate
substitution, 6 source-mask fills and 3 inserted-slot fills**. No printed
slot is deleted or reordered and the published **Nov4–6** key is unchanged.
The insertion positions and complete wording remain stated hypotheses.


**Reviewed source crops:** [p146_C_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov6_tiflis_ringbahn_instruction/sources/p146_C_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).
## Source and date layers

[Reviewed source image — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/nov6_tiflis_ringbahn_instruction/inputs.json).

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — headers and cleartext annotation:**

```text
Page heading: 6th NOVEMBER, 1918.
C) COS v LP (06.46 a.m., November 7th)
FUER COS 2040 (6/11) AN NACHRICHTENKOMMDR KAUKASUS DELEGATION
TIFLIS 2 TLE
1 TL RICHI-176
2 TL RICHI-192
Cleartext ending after part 2: NKJ v LP UM
```

</details>

The dispatch date in the heading and address line is November 6; the
intercept line says November 7. These layers are retained. The separately
printed `NKJ v LP UM` follows the second ciphertext and is not an extra
coordinate group. Exact grouped ciphertext, including every dash and the
invalid printed `W`, is preserved in the
[inputs](../../experiments/nov6_tiflis_ringbahn_instruction/inputs.json).

## p146 C1

Part 1 prints **174 valid coordinates** and advertises **176**. Its `XAAF`
group at source indices 65–68 is visibly short. The displayed frame inserts
one unknown at **source boundary 66** and another at **source boundary 173**.
A boundary is before the original source index of that number. Consequently,
the inserted slots have **model indices 66 and 174**; original source indices
do not shift in the transcription.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 176-slot frame; 86/88 fixed positions:**

```text
RINGBAHNNOVEMBERSCHLUESSELNICHTVERNICHTENX?CHLUESSELERSTERDEZEMBERWIEZEHNTE?NOVEMBERUSWX
```

**Edited output — the same conditional frame; 0 observed-coordinate substitutions, 0 source-mask fills and 2 inserted-slot fills; 88/88 fixed positions:**

```text
RINGBAHNNOVEMBERSCHLUESSELNICHTVERNICHTENXSCHLUESSELERSTERDEZEMBERWIEZEHNTERNOVEMBERUSWX
```

</details>

| Added source boundary | Model index | Supplied coordinate | Plaintext position supplied |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| 66 | 66 | G | 42, S in SCHLUESSEL |
| 173 | 174 | A | 75, R in ZEHNTER |

The first fill changes the short group from `XAAF` to `XGAAF` in the model.
The second adds a coordinate before the final printed `D`; that location is
inferred from the cipher comparison, not a visible blank. Neither fill is
counted as a change to an observed coordinate.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Ringbahn-Novemberschluessel nicht vernichten. Schluessel erster Dezember wie zehnter November usw.

**Meaning:** Keep the November Ringbahn keys; use the November 10 key for
December 1, and continue in the stated sequence.

The exact complete candidate is encrypted and compared against the literal
174-slot source under **all 15,400 ways of inserting two slots**. There is
exactly **one zero-substitution alignment** for that fixed candidate: source
boundaries 66 and 173. The certificate records the cost histogram and the
minimum. This establishes a precise compatibility result within the declared
family. It does not prove that every possible plaintext has been excluded,
or identify when the historical omissions occurred.

## p146 C2

Part 2 prints **191 source slots**, of which **185 are valid coordinates**,
and advertises **192**. The first-line group `VF--` at source indices 35–38
is visibly four slots long. For the displayed raw output, one unknown slot
is inserted at **source boundary 37**. The literal two dashes, the two dashes
in the following `VF--X`, the `W` in `FXXDW`, and the dash in `-DGVD` all
remain source observations.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 192-slot frame; 89/96 fixed positions:**

```text
BISEINUNDZWANZIGSTERDEZEMBERWI?DREISSIG?TERNO?E?BERXEMPFANGS?ESTAETIGUNGX?A8HRICH?ENCHEF4B47857X
```

**Edited output — the same conditional frame; 1 observed-coordinate substitution, 6 source-mask fills and 1 inserted-slot fill; 96/96 fixed positions:**

```text
BISEINUNDZWANZIGSTERDEZEMBERWIEDREISSIGSTERNOVEMBERXEMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNGXNACHRICHTENCHEF4B47857X
```

</details>

The sole observed-coordinate substitution is **source 132 V→X**, supplying
`C` in the proposed word `NACHRICHTENCHEF` where the raw output has `8`.
No numeral elsewhere is relabeled. The complete repair account for the
boundary-37 display frame is:

| Kind | Source index or boundary | Model index | Value supplied |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Added-slot fill | Boundary 37 | 37 | A |
| Printed dash fill | 37 | 38 | X |
| Printed dash fill | 38 | 39 | F |
| Printed dash fill | 41 | 42 | X |
| Printed dash fill | 42 | 43 | A |
| Invalid printed W fill | 108 | 109 | V |
| Observed-coordinate substitution | 132 | 133 | V→X |
| Printed dash fill | 174 | 175 | G |

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Bis einundzwanzigster Dezember wie dreissigster November. Empfangsbestaetigung. Nachrichtenchef 4B47857.

**Meaning:** Continue through December 21 using the November 30 key, and
acknowledge receipt. The trailing reference **4B47857** is literal under the
published square; its historical numerical assignment is not independently
established here.

### Equal-cost gap alternatives

The verifier tests **all 192 single-gap positions** against the same complete
candidate. Three positions tie at the minimum cost of one observed-coordinate
substitution:

| Source boundary | Added coordinate | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills | Inserted-slot fills |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 37 | A | 1 | 6 | 1 |
| 38 | X | 1 | 6 | 1 |
| 39 | F | 1 | 6 | 1 |

All three produce the same displayed raw and edited plaintext. They differ
in which part of the restored `VFAXF` group is attributed to the missing slot
and which to the two printed masks. The certificate preserves each mapping
and its complete repair events. **Boundary 37 is the presentation choice;
the evidence does not distinguish these three gap positions.**

## Independent support and limits

The verifier independently decodes pinned source rows from the earlier
editions, rather than treating their edited prose as direct evidence:

| New proposed span | Independently fixed raw source |
| --- | --- |
| SCHLUESSELERSTERDEZEMBERWIEZEHNTERNOVEMBERUSW | p211 lower B2 |
| BISEINUNDZWANZIGSTERDEZEMBER | p211 lower B2 |
| WIEDREISSIGSTERNOVEMBER | p145 B3 |
| EMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNG | p145 B3 |

These matches directly support the missing schedule letters in C1 and the
schedule/acknowledgment fills in C2. The final `NACHRICHTENCHEF` is a separately
priced lexical restoration from `?A8HRICH?ENCHEF`; the other dispatches print
the shorter `NACHRCHEF` and do not by themselves supply this expanded word.
All three repairs in that word remain editorial.

The new instruction begins `RINGBAHNNOVEMBER` and does not reproduce the
other dispatch's separate sentence postponing the December key. These
records are not merged into one purported identical copy. The agreement
supports the transmitted schedule, without demonstrating that every
station followed it or assigning a key to any particular December message.

## Attribution and reproduction

The source is J. Rives Childs's *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*. Published period-key recovery by George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils
Kopal and Arno Wacker, Lasry's 2017 key list, and the already published p145
and p211 editions retain their original credit. Earlier repository OCR is
frozen with recomputed unchanged-key outputs: it separated the first row
of C1 and then merged the remainder of C1 with C2. The current work restores
the physical source frames and makes the word repairs reviewable. It makes
**no first-decipherment claim**.

[Inputs and literal source](../../experiments/nov6_tiflis_ringbahn_instruction/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/nov6_tiflis_ringbahn_instruction/certificates.json),
[prior OCR comparison](../../experiments/nov6_tiflis_ringbahn_instruction/prior_candidates.json),
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/nov6_tiflis_ringbahn_instruction/README.md)
provide every position domain, source/model map, exact re-encryption,
independent supporting span and gap-search boundary.
