# November 7–8: embassy, legation and Etappe address parts

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

Source review and editorial work: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Published Nov7–9 key: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker; unchanged here. The earlier repository OCR and explicitly recomputed unchanged-key outputs are retained.


**Reviewed source crops:** [p156_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov7_8_embassy_address_parts/sources/p156_reviewed.png) · [p158_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov7_8_embassy_address_parts/sources/p158_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).
## Scope and evidence

Seven physical first/address parts on printed pp156 and 158 contain embassy,
legation or Etappe addresses and signatures. They are not seven recovered
substantive message bodies. Most headings announce additional parts that are
absent from the relevant section; the two printed p158 A parts themselves
both contain address/signature language.

The source edition has **568 native coordinate slots and 284 plaintext
positions**. Under the primary p156 A1 overstrike reading, all 284 positions
are fixed directly by the published key. Eleven observed-coordinate
substitutions produce the displayed ordinary-word proposals. There are no
insertions, exclusions, reorderings, source-mask fills or key changes. The
retained alternative p156 A1 glyph changes one raw letter and raises that
record's proposal cost from two substitutions to three.

| Record | Native slots | Raw fixed positions | Observed substitutions | Source fills |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| p156_A1 | 84 | 42/42 | 2 | 0 |
| p156_B1 | 80 | 40/40 | 0 | 0 |
| p156_D1 | 44 | 22/22 | 1 | 0 |
| p156_E1 | 78 | 39/39 | 0 | 0 |
| p158_A1 | 100 | 50/50 | 4 | 0 |
| p158_A2 | 106 | 53/53 | 2 | 0 |
| p158_B1 | 76 | 38/38 | 2 | 0 |

The three p162 D1 source masks receive independent character support from
these address witnesses; conversely, p162 D1's raw output supports all four
p158 A1 and both p158 A2 ordinary-word repairs. This is evidence for the
shared address formula, with different headers retained. It does not
establish identical missing payloads or a historical copying mechanism.

## p156 A1

**German embassy address with Bussche signature.**

**Literal header:** `A) YZ v LP (6.11 a.m., November 8th); FUER YZ 2200 (7/11) [2/3] TLE; 1 TL RICHI-84`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DERTSCHEXBOTSCHAFTXKSNSTANTIOPELXXBUSSCHEX
```

**Edited output — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions:**

```text
DEUTSCHEXBOTSCHAFTXKONSTANTIOPELXXBUSSCHEX
```

</details>

**Readable German:**

> Deutsche Botschaft Konstantiopel. Bussche.

**Conditional interpretation:** An address to the German embassy and a Bussche signature. The transmitted place-name lacks the second N of Konstantinopel and is preserved as Konstantiopel.

The two proposed ordinary-word repairs change DERTSCHE to DEUTSCHE and KSNSTANTIOPEL to KONSTANTIOPEL. The missing N is not inserted into the plaintext or the source.

The overstruck second character in the third group of source row 2 is transcribed X in the primary VXXVX reading. A V alternative, VVXVX, is retained independently; the alternative changes the raw H in DERTSCHE to X and does not establish a different historical message.

The faint part-count digit admits 2/3 readings. The header display uses editorial brackets to retain both alternatives; only the first part is printed in this section. The advertised 84-coordinate body length is clear and does not depend on that header digit. The Bussche signature is not expanded to a named historical person.

All indices below are zero-based. The exact source remains unchanged in the raw layer.

| Source index | Printed | Edited |
|---:|:---:|:---:|
| 22 | D | F |
| 42 | D | V |

**Retained overstrike alternative:** `VVXVX` instead of primary `VXXVX`, changing source index 51 from X to V, gives:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — retained V overstrike alternative:**

```text
DERTSCXEXBOTSCHAFTXKSNSTANTIOPELXXBUSSCHEX
```

</details>

The same readable proposal then costs **three observed substitutions**, including V→X at source index 51. The stronger German produced by the primary X reading is not treated as independent proof of that glyph. Both variants and their repair ledgers are verified.

## p156 B1

**German embassy at Constantinople and Stumm signature.**

**Literal header:** `B) YZ v LP (5.52 a.m., November 8th); 1835 (7/11) 2TLE; 1 TL RICHI-80`

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DEUTSCHEBOTSCHAFTKONSTANTINOPELXXSTUMMXX
```

</details>

**Edited output:** identical to raw; zero repairs.

**Readable German:**

> Deutsche Botschaft Konstantinopel. Stumm.

**Conditional interpretation:** A directly readable embassy address and Stumm signature, with its advertised second part absent from this section.

All 80 source coordinates directly decrypt. The source time is 1835, not the earlier OCR 1838.

The first printed part is a complete address and signature field, not a recovered substantive telegram body.

## p156 D1

**Etappe address at Constantinople.**

**Literal header:** `D) YZ v LP (6.21 a.m., November 8th); FUER YZ 0127 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-44`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ETAPPEXKHNSTANTINOPELX
```

**Edited output — 1 observed-coordinate substitution:**

```text
ETAPPEXKONSTANTINOPELX
```

</details>

**Readable German:**

> Etappe Konstantinopel.

**Conditional interpretation:** A short Etappe address at Constantinople. The missing continuation is not supplied.

The native final XDVA is visible below the first source row and restores the advertised 44-coordinate frame without inserting anything into the source.

One observed-coordinate substitution changes raw KHNSTANTINOPEL to KONSTANTINOPEL. ETAPPE remains the literal transmitted designation.

All indices below are zero-based. The exact source remains unchanged in the raw layer.

| Source index | Printed | Edited |
|---:|:---:|:---:|
| 42 | V | F |

## p156 E1

**French-language German legation address at Constantinople.**

**Literal header:** `E) YZ v LP (6.15 a.m., November 8th); FUER YZ 2330 (8/11) 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-78`

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FUERXLEGATIONXALLEMANDEXKONSTANTINOPELX
```

</details>

**Edited output:** identical to raw; zero repairs.

**Readable German:**

> Fuer Legation Allemande Konstantinopel.

**Conditional interpretation:** An address for the German legation at Constantinople; the transmitted designation Legation Allemande is French and is retained as printed in the decoded text.

All 78 source coordinates directly decrypt, including the final three-coordinate AGV.

The heading literally combines a 6.15 a.m. reception on November 8 with 2330 (8/11); the edition does not silently reconcile that chronology.

Only the first of two advertised parts is visible in this section.

## p158 A1

**German embassy address and Stumm signature, first printed part.**

**Literal header:** `A) YZ v LP (05.05 p.m., November 8th); 1331 (7/11) 2 TTLE; 1 TL RICHI-100`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DEUTSCHEBOTSAHAFTKONSTCNTINOPELXDNTERSCHRIOTSTUMMX
```

**Edited output — 4 observed-coordinate substitutions:**

```text
DEUTSCHEBOTSCHAFTKONSTANTINOPELXUNTERSCHRIFTSTUMMX
```

</details>

**Readable German:**

> Deutsche Botschaft Konstantinopel. Unterschrift Stumm.

**Conditional interpretation:** An embassy address with an explicit Stumm signature label. Four raw letter errors are repaired at their full coordinate cost.

The source supplies 100 native coordinates; the earlier OCR lost one, so its odd-length output is not used as the physical frame.

The raw BOTSAHAFT, KONSTCNTINOPEL, DNTERSCHRIOT letter errors are not source-transcription changes: the literal source remains fixed and all proposed replacements are priced in the edited layer.

The two printed A parts both contain address/signature language. Their headings are retained without inventing a distinct substantive payload.

All indices below are zero-based. The exact source remains unchanged in the raw layer.

| Source index | Printed | Edited |
|---:|:---:|:---:|
| 1 | X | F |
| 2 | F | X |
| 3 | X | A |
| 4 | F | X |

## p158 A2

**Repeated embassy address with literal UPK3 prefix.**

**Literal header:** `2 TL RICHI-106; following control: LP`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
UPK3DEWTSCHEBOTSCHAATKONSTANTINOPELXUNTERSCHRIFTSTUMM
```

**Edited output — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions:**

```text
UPK3DEUTSCHEBOTSCHAFTKONSTANTINOPELXUNTERSCHRIFTSTUMM
```

</details>

**Readable German:**

> UPK3. Deutsche Botschaft Konstantinopel. Unterschrift Stumm.

**Conditional interpretation:** The second printed part repeats the embassy address and Stumm signature, preceded by the unresolved literal field UPK3. Its purpose is not inferred.

The first row repeats GDDGV in adjacent five-coordinate groups. Both are retained in the full native 106-slot frame; visible repetition is not a license to remove a group.

The raw DEWTSCHE and BOTSCHAAT are ordinary-word repair proposals with explicit coordinate costs. UPK3 is retained unchanged and is not expanded as a unit, station or reference.

The final D is part of the encrypted body; the following LP is a source control.

All indices below are zero-based. The exact source remains unchanged in the raw layer.

| Source index | Printed | Edited |
|---:|:---:|:---:|
| 17 | D | X |
| 65 | X | V |

## p158 B1

**German embassy address with an explicit Stumm signature.**

**Literal header:** `B) YZ v LP (05.15 p.m., November 8th); FUER YZ 1325 (7/11) 2 TEILE; 1 TL RICHI-76; following control: LP`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DNDEUTSCHEBOTSCHAFVUNTERSCHRIFTXSTUMMX
```

**Edited output — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions:**

```text
ANDEUTSCHEBOTSCHAFTUNTERSCHRIFTXSTUMMX
```

</details>

**Readable German:**

> An deutsche Botschaft. Unterschrift Stumm.

**Conditional interpretation:** A separate embassy address and signature part; it does not itself name the embassy city.

The visible final G completes the native 76-coordinate frame; the following LP is excluded as source control.

The raw DN and BOTSCHAFV become AN and BOTSCHAFT through two explicitly priced observed-coordinate substitutions.

The second of two advertised parts is absent from this section. The adjacent Constantinople addresses do not license inserting that city into this record.

All indices below are zero-based. The exact source remains unchanged in the raw layer.

| Source index | Printed | Edited |
|---:|:---:|:---:|
| 36 | A | V |
| 42 | V | D |

## Independent address witness on p162

The earlier [p162 D1 edition](../people/constantinople_embassy_signature.md)
preserves three C-like source glyphs as masks. Its independently recomputed
raw output is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — independently recomputed p162 D1 witness:**

```text
DEUTSCHEBOTSCHAFTKONSTA??INOPELXUNTERSCHRIF?STUMMX
```

</details>

Its literal header is `D) XYZ v LP (06.12 a.m., November 10th); 1330 (8/13)
2 TEILE; 1 TL RICHI-100`. The unusual `8/13` field remains literal. This
differs from p158 A's `1331 (7/11)` header.

| Comparison | Aligned plaintext positions | Agreeing known labels | Disagreeing known labels | p162 unknowns supported by new raw labels | New repairs supported by p162 raw labels |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| p158 A1 from position 0 / p162 D1 from position 0 | 50 | 43 | 4 | 3 | 4 |
| p158 A2 from position 4 / p162 D1 from position 0 | 49 | 44 | 2 | 3 | 2 |

The p158 A2 offset skips only its literal `UPK3` prefix. The comparison
neither deletes that prefix nor changes its numerical label. The final
separator that is present in p162 D1 and absent from p158 A2 is outside the
49-position comparison. Every agreeing, disagreeing and mask-supporting
position is listed with its coordinate pair in the certificate. The p162
record is a previously reviewed witness and is not added to this package's
physical-record count.

## Reproduction and credit

[Inputs](../../experiments/nov7_8_embassy_address_parts/inputs.json) preserve
all literal rows, headers, competing overstrike readings, proposals,
published-key provenance and source-image bindings. The
[certificate](../../experiments/nov7_8_embassy_address_parts/certificates.json)
recomputes raw domains, every repair cost, complete readable-label
preservation, exact re-encryption and the independent p162 comparisons.
The existing p162 source record and crop are bound by hashes. A complete
square witness demonstrates consistency only; it is not a recovered
historical digit assignment.

The [package README](../../experiments/nov7_8_embassy_address_parts/README.md)

# Request to repeat an unreadable eighth part

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and conditional edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p155 C is a two-part request to check and repeat an earlier eighth part that could not be deciphered. The second part reads directly under the published Nov7–9 key. The first part prints a six-coordinate group where its advertised length requires five; its body is shown under explicitly priced one-coordinate exclusions. The original earlier eighth part is not supplied or solved by this request.

[Reviewed source](../../experiments/nov7_eighth_part_repetition/sources/p155_C.png) · [Exact inputs](../../experiments/nov7_eighth_part_repetition/inputs.json) · [All alternatives and joint witnesses](../../experiments/nov7_eighth_part_repetition/certificates.json)

**Source transcription — header:** `C) NKJ v LP (6.42 a.m., November 8th); FUER COS 2240 (7/11), 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-186; 2 TL RICHI-136`.

## Conditional digit reading

The [shared Nov7–9 digit interpretation](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) reads **25.10** in part 1 and **RM 5 Nr. 153303** in part 2. The opposite square gives 26.10 and RM 6 Nr. 163303. The first part’s `AL?CHIS` field remains unresolved, and the retained source-frame alternatives are unchanged.

## p155 C1

**Conditional frame.** The literal source has 187 slots, including the six-slot group `VGVXAA`, three noncoordinate glyphs (`H`, `S`, `H`), and no printed dash. The advertised length is 186. The displayed example excludes the observed `G` at source index 61, then masks the three invalid glyphs. Excluding an observed coordinate is a separate frame operation; it is not a zero-cost OCR correction. Other exclusions are retained below.

**Readable German — conditional interpretation**, after that one exclusion and two explicitly recorded source-mask fills:

> Da achter Teil des AL?CHIS 2?X10, Leitstelle 707 POT Nr. 1002 an Sektion Politik Berlin nicht zu entziffern,

**Meaning:** The eighth part of a message identified by the literal token AL?CHIS and the date-like field 2?X10 cannot be deciphered. The routing names Sektion Politik Berlin. The sentence continues in C2.

`AL?CHIS`, the date-like field `2?X10`, and the station/reference labels remain literal. The primary pair `707 / 1002` is one example, not a uniquely recovered identification.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 186-slot frame**, before either word fill:

```text
DAACHTERTEILDESAL?CHISX2?X10XXLEIT?TELLE707POTNRX1002?NSEKTIONPOLITIKBERLINNICHTZUENTZIFFERNX
```

**Edited output — conditional 186-slot frame:** one observed-coordinate exclusion, no observed-coordinate substitution, and two source-mask fills. Two output positions remain unresolved.

```text
DAACHTERTEILDESAL?CHISX2?X10XXLEITSTELLE707POTNRX1002ANSEKTIONPOLITIKBERLINNICHTZUENTZIFFERNX
```

</details>

## p155 C2

**Readable German**, directly from the native 136-slot source frame:

> Pruefung und Wiederholung 8. Teiles erbeten. Nachrichtenchef RMX?NRX1?3303.

**Meaning:** Checking and repetition of the eighth part are requested. The two unknowns in the final reference are the same globally unassigned square cell as the unknown in the first part date.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — native 136-slot frame:** no source-coordinate edit, fill or change of frame.

```text
PRUEFUNGUNDWIEDERHOLUNG8XTEILESERBETENXNACHRICHTENCHEFRMX?NRX1?3303X
```

</details>

## The overlong group does not determine unique reference labels

All six choices of one excluded coordinate inside the literal `VGVXAA` group are preserved. Each costs one observed-coordinate exclusion. The table records the further word substitutions and source-mask fills needed for the common readable body.

| Excluded source index | Printed coordinate | Station / reference labels | Additional observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
|---:|---|---|---:|---:|
| 60 | V | `727 / 1002` | 0 | 2 |
| 61 | G | `707 / 1002` | 0 | 2 |
| 62 | V | `707 / 1022` | 0 | 2 |
| 63 | X | `707 / 1022` | 1 | 2 |
| 64 | A | `707 / 1022` | 2 | 2 |
| 65 | A | `707 / 1022` | 2 | 2 |

The first three choices produce different correlated numerical fields with the same repair price. The final two choices delete one of the adjacent As and produce the same frame, but their source indices remain distinct. A plausible duplicated A is not silently treated as the historically correct deletion. Conversely, the cheaper language repair does not prove that the excluded G was a transmitted error.

## One shared unresolved cell, three fields

The unknown in `2?X10` and both unknowns in `RMX?NRX1?3303` all decode from **the same square cell `XA`**. They cannot be chosen independently. Under the published pair of unused labels `{5, 6}`, the two complete shared assignments are:

| XA label | First-part date-like field | Second-part reference |
|---|---|---|
| `5` | `25X10` | `RMX5NRX153303` |
| `6` | `26X10` | `RMX6NRX163303` |

The other unknown cell receives the remaining label, preserving injectivity. Both assignments have joint full roundtrip witnesses for both message parts under every recorded exclusion. These demonstrate compatibility; neither assignment is selected as an authenticated historical date or reference. The separate `AL?CHIS` character remains source-mask uncertainty and is not resolved by this equality alone.

## Evidence and credit

Published Nov7–9 key: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed OCR candidates are retained. Source review and conditional geometry/word edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The machine record also preserves the native odd 187-slot diagnostic, including its final unpaired coordinate and the corresponding original source position. It never silently drops that orphan. Each conditional frame maps every retained coordinate back to the original source; all word fills and substitutions are separately listed.

The verifiers independently reconstruct the transposition, check all marginal domains, protect the globally shared cell, verify twelve joint two-part global witnesses and compare every nonseparator label in both readable passages. Optional PDF verification compares every delivered crop pixel with the pinned primary source.

```sh
python experiments/nov7_eighth_part_repetition/verify.py --verify
python experiments/nov7_eighth_part_repetition/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf
```

# Operations-map sheets for the Gleiwitz garrison

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source restoration and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

## Conditional digit reading

The [shared Nov7–9 digit interpretation](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) supplies the closing **AOK 11, 1d 7065**, completing the two remaining labels at no additional source edit or fill. The opposite square gives 7056. The map scale, sheet names and quantities are already read independently of this choice.

## p151 E2

This surviving second part lists operations-map sheets at the directly
read scale **1 zu 100000**, with named sheet areas and quantities, followed
by a Gleiwitz garrison-office address. The complete printed body has
**224 slots** and decrypts under the unchanged published **Nov7–9** key.
Two explicitly priced word substitutions and two printed-erasure fills
produce 110 fixed labels out of 112. The conservative layer retains the final two labels as globally
coupled unknown digits; the optional reference reading is given above.

The [Childs source, printed p151, section E](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view)
prints `LP v NKJ`, `7.09 a.m., November 9th`, `2 TL` and `RICHI-224`.
Its full page and enlarged E crop were directly inspected. The source PDF,
page, crop rectangle, dimensions and decoded-pixel digest are pinned in
[the inputs](../../experiments/nov9_operations_map_sheets/inputs.json).
The [verifier](../../experiments/nov9_operations_map_sheets/verify.py)
recreates those pixels when given the PDF; the source is not represented
by an unavailable image link.

The manuscript has 44 five-slot groups and the four-character final group
`XDVV`. Group 16 is **GGVVX**. Earlier repository OCR gave **GGVVXX**, an
extra unprinted `X`, which changed the length to 225. Restoring the actual
five-coordinate group repairs the digital transcription; it excludes no
coordinate from the manuscript. The OCR snapshot and its odd-length
arithmetic remain in the experiment for comparison.

## Raw and optional edited readings

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — all 224 printed source slots in order, with the two dashes and unknown key cells retained:**

```text
OPERATIONSKA0TE1ZU100000SALZ?URGWIENLE?BERGBRESLAUJE40BLATTXWARSCHAU10BLATTANGARNISONKDOGLEIWVTZFSXAOK11X1D70??X
```

**Edited output — two observed-coordinate substitutions and two printed-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or changed key:**

```text
OPERATIONSKARTE1ZU100000SALZBURGWIENLEMBERGBRESLAUJE40BLATTXWARSCHAU10BLATTANGARNISONKDOGLEIWITZFSXAOK11X1D70??X
```

</details>

**Readable German — complete optional stream, retaining the literal separators, quantities and closing labels:**

> Operationskarte 1 zu 100000 Salzburg Wien Lemberg Breslau je 40 Blatt X Warschau 10 Blatt an Garnisonkdo Gleiwitz FS X AOK 11 X 1D70?? X.

**Conditional interpretation:** The fragment lists operations maps at
1:100,000, forty sheets each for the areas labeled Salzburg, Wien, Lemberg
and Breslau, and ten sheets for Warschau. It gives the garrison command at
Gleiwitz as the delivery address. The `FS`, `AOK11` and `1D70??` fields are
retained without reconstructing their administrative meaning. The absent
first part and any evidence of actual dispatch or receipt are not supplied.

The named-place spellings in this reading are source-language labels. Two
of their letters are fills and one is a substitution, as shown below;
identifying a familiar name does not make the supplied letter an observation.

## Exact word costs

All indices are zero-based. Every received coordinate stays in its original
slot; the two dashes in printed group `XGG--` are source slots 103 and 104.

| Plaintext position | Raw → proposed label | Raw pair → edited pair | Source operation | Word |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 12 | `0` → `R` | `VD` → `AD` | Source 1, `V` → `A` | `KA0TE` → `KARTE` |
| 28 | `?` → `B` | `G?` → `GX` | Fill printed dash 103 with `X` | `SALZ?URG` → `SALZBURG` |
| 38 | `?` → `M` | `A?` → `AF` | Fill printed dash 104 with `F` | `LE?BERG` → `LEMBERG` |
| 93 | `V` → `I` | `GA` → `GG` | Source 53, `A` → `G` | `GLEIWVTZ` → `GLEIWITZ` |

Before the fills, the two name positions have domains **29BITV** and
**MPRUWY**, respectively. The proposed `B` and `M` belong to those domains,
but the surviving half-pairs do not uniquely select them. The scale
`1ZU100000`, quantities `40` and `10`, and `AOK11` are already raw labels;
none is introduced by the word repairs.

## The two unresolved digits are coupled

The remaining unknown positions use **different unassigned square cells**.
All source coordinates in these two pairs are observed.

| Plaintext position | Observed pair | Original source indices | Literal domain |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 109 | `VF` | 212, 43 | `5` or `6` |
| 110 | `XA` | 66, 134 | `5` or `6` |

A single injective square must govern both cells. The only complete
assignments and corresponding closing strings are:

| VF label | XA label | Literal closing field |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 5 | 6 | `1D7056` |
| 6 | 5 | `1D7065` |

Both full-key witnesses re-encrypt the complete edited stream exactly.
They are mathematical alternatives, not historical numeral assignments;
`1D7055` and `1D7066` would violate the unchanged square's injectivity.
The main reading therefore retains **1D70??**.

## Evidence and reproduction

The [certificate](../../experiments/nov9_operations_map_sheets/certificates.json)
contains all 112 raw and edited pair maps, the four changes, both unresolved
domains, both complete global-key witnesses and the retained earlier OCR
comparison. The experiment's [reproduction guide](../../experiments/nov9_operations_map_sheets/README.md)
gives the source metadata and optional original-PDF pixel check.

**Reviewed source crops:** [p151_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov9_operations_map_sheets/sources/p151_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).

```sh
python experiments/nov9_operations_map_sheets/verify.py --verify
python experiments/nov9_operations_map_sheets/verify.py --verify --pdf /tmp/adfgvx-childs.pdf
```

The source is **J. Rives Childs**. The published period keys retain the
credit of **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker** (2016)
and George Lasry's 2017 key disclosure, as recorded in the unchanged key
metadata. This edition is a source restoration and explicit editorial
review by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**, with earlier repository OCR
preserved and no claim to universal first-decipherment priority.

# Wire communications, return instructions and the Tiraspol continuation

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source collation and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The two surviving copies supply complementary evidence. The short first
part on printed p162 overlaps the end of the longer first part on p166,
and their second parts differ at only two source positions. This edition
adds three physical records: **p162 C1, p166 C1 and p166 C2**. The earlier
[p162 C2 edition](../military/tiraspol_border_report.md) remains a supporting
witness, with its original displays unchanged.

The primary unfilled frames fix **205 of 362 plaintext positions** across
the three records. Copying the independently observed p166 prefix to the
p162 model supplies 156 further labels; supplying one missing p166 `X`
from p162 supplies one more. Those **157 source-linked completions are
counted separately**, because p162 by itself fixes no complete plaintext
pair in the restored 312-coordinate frame. Six distinct observed-source
substitutions produce the optional complete edition: three supported by
the other copies and three lexical choices in the shared p166 prefix.

The [Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view)
prints p162 C at `09.45 a.m., November 9th`, with an unread recipient
identifier and `v NKJ`, followed by `missed first part of this message`.
The p166 C header reads `UKS v NKJ`, `9.47 a.m., November 9th`,
`0920 (9) 2 TLE`. These receipt times remain distinct. Both full pages and
the enlarged C crops were directly inspected. The exact PDF, pages,
rectangles, dimensions and RGB digests are preserved in
[the source inputs](../../experiments/nov9_wire_return_source_family/inputs.json);
no unpublished image asset is needed to reproduce the evidence.

## p162 C1

The printed body contains **117 coordinates**, and its first-part header
gives no recoverable total length. In the source-linked 312-coordinate
frame, all **195 absent prefix coordinates remain unknown in the primary
layer**. There are 117 half-pairs with one observed p162 coordinate and 39
pairs with neither coordinate present. No complete pair is fixed by this
fragment alone. Its literal odd-length 117-coordinate inverse, including
the unpaired final coordinate, is retained as a diagnostic in the
certificate; it is not used as a readable message or included in the
fixed-position total.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — 195 unassigned prefix slots followed by all 117 observed p162 coordinates; zero fixed labels out of 156:**

```text
????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????
```

</details>

The next layer copies only p166's **original source coordinates 0:195**.
Every complete pair retains both source origins. Of the resulting 156
pairs, 117 combine a p162 coordinate with a p166 prefix coordinate; 39
come entirely from the p166 prefix. None is independently observed as a
complete p162 pair.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — source-linked comparison, with the 195-coordinate prefix copied from p166 and no alteration to the 117 p162 coordinates:**

```text
AKONACH18XMITTEILTOBDRAHTVERKEHRODESSAXODELSAMITDORTBGERHGRXMOGGLICHXSTOERUNGSPOSTENACKERMANNSOLLVONBRAILAZURRUECKKEHRANGEWIESENSEINXSTOERUNGSPOSTENTIRASPOL
```

**Edited output — three lexical substitutions at borrowed p166 prefix origins; zero substitutions to the observed p162 fragment:**

```text
AKONACH18XMITTEILTOBDRAHTVERKEHRODESSAXODESSAMITDORTIGERHGRXMOEGLICHXSTOERUNGSPOSTENACKERMANNSOLLVONBRAILAZURRUECKKEHRANGEWIESENSEINXSTOERUNGSPOSTENTIRASPOL
```

</details>

**Readable German — complete conditional source-linked edition, preserving the literal wording, separators and labels:**

> Akonach 18 X mitteilt ob Drahtverkehr Odessa X Odessa mit dortiger Hgr X moeglich X Stoerungsposten Ackermann soll von Braila zur Rueckkehr angewiesen sein X Stoerungsposten Tiraspol.

**Conditional interpretation:** The collated text concerns whether wire
communication involving Odessa and the local `Hgr` is possible. It says
that the post labeled Ackermann should have been instructed to return
from Braila, and then names a Tiraspol post. The awkward `MITTEILT`, repeated
`ODESSA`, and `AKONACH18` are retained. This reading does not determine a
person's identity, a precise organizational expansion of `Hgr`, or the
technical duties of a `Stoerungsposten`.

## p166 C1

The header advertises **RICHI-312**, but the reviewed body contains
**311 valid coordinates**. The four-character group **XVGD** is visibly
short. Its comparison with p162 supports one inserted `X`, with two exact
aliases: insertion before original source 225 or 226 produces the same
`XXVGD` sequence. The location of the missing copy within the adjacent
`XX` cannot be distinguished. Before the fill, the two aliases place the
unknown at different plaintext positions; both raw streams are retained.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — all 311 original coordinates plus one unassigned slot before source 225; 155 of 156 labels fixed:**

```text
AKONACH18XMITTEILTOBDRAHTVERKEHRODESSAXODELSAMITDORTBGERHGRXM?GGLICHXSTOERUNGSPOSTENACKERMANNSOLLVONBRAILAZURRUECKKEHRANGEWGESENSEINXOTOERUNGSPOSTENTIRASPOL
```

**Raw output — equally valid unfilled alias before source 226; 155 of 156 labels fixed:**

```text
AKONACH18XMITTEILTOBDRAHTVERKEHRODESSAXODELSAMITDORTBGERHGRXMOGGLICHXST?ERUNGSPOSTENACKERMANNSOLLVONBRAILAZURRUECKKEHRANGEWGESENSEINXOTOERUNGSPOSTENTIRASPOL
```

</details>

In the first alias the unresolved label is plaintext 61; in the second
it is plaintext 71. Both have pair `F?` and domain **178COQ**. The p162
copy provides `X` at source 30 or 31, respectively, fixing `O`. This fill
is independently supported by a received coordinate, not chosen solely
to spell a German word.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — source-linked missing-X fill only; both observed-copy disagreements and the three lexical defects remain visible:**

```text
AKONACH18XMITTEILTOBDRAHTVERKEHRODESSAXODELSAMITDORTBGERHGRXMOGGLICHXSTOERUNGSPOSTENACKERMANNSOLLVONBRAILAZURRUECKKEHRANGEWGESENSEINXOTOERUNGSPOSTENTIRASPOL
```

**Edited output — the source-supported missing-X fill, two copy-supported observed substitutions and three optional lexical substitutions:**

```text
AKONACH18XMITTEILTOBDRAHTVERKEHRODESSAXODESSAMITDORTIGERHGRXMOEGLICHXSTOERUNGSPOSTENACKERMANNSOLLVONBRAILAZURRUECKKEHRANGEWIESENSEINXSTOERUNGSPOSTENTIRASPOL
```

</details>

**Readable German — complete optional p166 C1 edition, preserving every literal label:**

> Akonach 18 X mitteilt ob Drahtverkehr Odessa X Odessa mit dortiger Hgr X moeglich X Stoerungsposten Ackermann soll von Braila zur Rueckkehr angewiesen sein X Stoerungsposten Tiraspol.

**Conditional interpretation:** This longer copy supports the same reading
as the source-linked p162 first part. The full result depends on the stated
one-coordinate loss model and six operations on p166 C1: one insertion/fill
and five observed substitutions. The 195-coordinate prefix supplies the
p162 restoration; that shared evidence is counted once at its source origins.
The labels `18` here and `17` in the continuation remain different.

## p166 C2

The second part is independently labeled **2 TL RICHI-100** and contains
exactly 100 observed coordinates. Its native frame gives all 50 plaintext
labels under the unchanged published **Nov7–9** key.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — all 100 printed source coordinates, with no fill or changed key:**

```text
TIRASPOLERHIELTMXGXFEUERANDERGRENZEXAKONACH17ROZM4
```

**Edited output — one observed substitution at source 84, supported by the p162 C2 copy:**

```text
TIRASPOLERHIELTMXGXFEUERANDERGRENZEXAKONACH17ROEM4
```

</details>

**Readable German — complete optional second part, with every separator and closing label retained:**

> Tiraspol erhielt M X G X Feuer an der Grenze X Akonach 17 Roem 4.

**Conditional interpretation:** The continuation reports `M G FEUER` at a
border for the place or post labeled Tiraspol. It ends with the literal
`AKONACH17ROEM4`. No exact border, incident, unit, administrative number
or outside historical referent is supplied.

The p162 and p166 second parts differ only at two positions: p162 source
36 is a printed dash where p166 prints `G`; p162 source 84 is `V` where
p166 prints `F`. Thus p166 independently supports the earlier p162 fill
in `ERHIELT`, while p162 independently supports the optional p166 change
from `ROZM` to `ROEM`. Both coordinates of each relevant pair are recorded
in the certificate. The previously accepted p162 C2 record is not added
to the new-record or new-position counts.

## Source-only alignment and exact costs

All indices are zero-based. The geometry is selected from source
coordinates, before introducing a German word target. In each unfilled
p166 gap alias, all **196 contiguous 117-position windows** are compared
with the p162 fragment. Offset **195** is uniquely best at two observed
coordinate disagreements. At that suffix, all **117 possible locations**
for a single absent coordinate are compared: only local gaps **30 and 31**
attain the same two-disagreement minimum.

The overlap contains **114 independently agreeing observed coordinates,
two disagreements and one absent p166 coordinate**. Once the absent
coordinate is copied from p162, the filled strings agree at 115 positions;
one of those matches is supplied from the other copy and is not a 115th
independent agreement. These exact comparisons establish the best match
within the declared single-loss model, without excluding every possible
alternative error history.

| Origin of operation | Original source position | Operation | Plaintext effect | Evidential role |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| p166 C1 | Gap before 225 or 226 | Insert `X` from p162 C1 source 30 or 31 | Completes one raw `O` | Independent source-linked fill; aliases preserved |
| p166 C1 | 246 | `D` → `G` | `ANGEWGESEN` → `ANGEWIESEN` | Supported by p162 C1 source 52; other half of the pair still comes from p166 |
| p166 C1 | 247 | `F` → `D` | `OTOERUNGSPOSTEN` → `STOERUNGSPOSTEN` | Supported by p162 C1 source 53; other half of the pair still comes from p166 |
| p166 C1 | 160 | `D` → `X` | `ODELSA` → `ODESSA` | Optional lexical correction; the earlier `ODESSA` is already raw |
| p166 C1 | 161 | `X` → `G` | `DORTBGER` → `DORTIGER` | Optional lexical correction in borrowed prefix |
| p166 C1 | 162 | `G` → `V` | `MOGGLICH` → `MOEGLICH` | Optional lexical correction in borrowed prefix |
| p166 C2 | 84 | `F` → `V` | `ROZM` → `ROEM` | Supported by the complete raw p162 C2 pair |

The three prefix corrections appear in both readable first parts, but
there are only **three distinct corrected received coordinates**, all
from p166. Counting them a second time as p162 edits would confuse a
copied reading with independent evidence. The entire 117-coordinate p162
fragment remains unchanged throughout.

| New physical record | Printed coordinates | Modeled coordinates | Primary fixed labels | Source-linked labels added | Optional fixed labels |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| p162 C1 | 117 | 312 | 0 / 156 | 156 | 156 / 156 |
| p166 C1 | 311 | 312 | 155 / 156 | 1 | 156 / 156 |
| p166 C2 | 100 | 100 | 50 / 50 | 0 | 50 / 50 |
| Total | 528 | 724 | **205 / 362** | **157** | **362 / 362** |

## Reproduction and credit

The [certificate](../../experiments/nov9_wire_return_source_family/certificates.json)
contains the primary unfilled records, both gap aliases, every complete
pair's two coordinate origins, all source-only costs, the six unique
observed substitutions, the independent gap witness, native odd-frame
diagnostics and preserved OCR comparisons. Earlier OCR counted 307
coordinates for p166 C1; the actual printed source has 311. Restoring
misread digital transcription is kept separate from the one still absent
manuscript coordinate. Neither the published key nor the core challenge
messages are changed.

```sh
python experiments/nov9_wire_return_source_family/verify.py --verify
python experiments/nov9_wire_return_source_family/verify.py --verify --pdf /tmp/adfgvx-childs.pdf
```

Without the PDF argument, the verifier explicitly reports that source
pixel reproduction is skipped; all source, alignment, origin, cipher,
round-trip and display assertions still run. With the PDF argument, both
reviewed crop RGB digests are reproduced from the pinned source.

The manuscript source is **J. Rives Childs**. Published period-key credit
remains with **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker** (2016)
and George Lasry's 2017 disclosure, as recorded in the unchanged key
metadata. This is source restoration and explicit editorial collation by
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**, with prior OCR and the earlier p162 C2
edition preserved.

# Odessa courier report: a conditional loss before transposition

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

The conditional reconstruction of p201 C reports courier Elsner’s arrival via Wilna and asks whether further couriers should leave for Odessa. The clear header dates the Berlin telegram to **15 November 1918**. The recovered body now fixes **161/163 positions**; two reference labels remain unresolved.

Research and edition: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The published Nov16–18 key retains the credit of George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker; the [same-page address witness](../finance/odessa_wagon_sale.md#p201-a1) retains its earlier body credit.

## Current conditional reading

**Readable German — both retained loss models, the existing word repairs and shared FD=8 / VA=5 conditions:**

> Deutschen Bevollmaechtigten Odessa. Kurier Elsner heute ueber Wilna hier eingetroffen. Sollen Kuriere nach dort noch abfahren. Verbind. Offz. O Roem 2 der O. H. L. Berlin. ZT? Nr. 1?1118.

**Meaning:** Elsner has arrived via Wilna. The sender asks whether further couriers are still to depart for Odessa. The liaison-officer closing and Berlin remain literal; the report does not establish Elsner’s full identity.

The reading uses the existing two-coordinate loss model before transposition, two added fractionation fills and four observed-coordinate word repairs. The **324 received coordinates** remain in their printed order. The existing [FD=8 / VA=5 interpretation](../../experiments/nov16_18_reference_completion/README.md) supplies the final **8** without another source edit: the pair is **FD**, at received positions **187** and **289**. It survives both loss descriptions, **[36, 74]** and **[37, 74]**, and the conservative **G??DV** branch, which fixes **159/163 positions**.

The remaining reference cells **AF** and **GG** take distinct values from **034679**. The [propagation certificate](../../experiments/nov16_18_reference_completion/courier_certificate.json) retains all **30** reference tuples and **720** complete square assignments, with the original **324-coordinate transposition** and **326-coordinate fractionation**.

## p201 C

Literal header: `C) NKJ (RAT) v LP (4.15 p.m., November 16th); FUER RAT 1720 (16) SSS BERLIN 15/11 (16); RICHI-324`.

The source and two enlarged crops were visually reviewed locally. Their PDF page, rectangles, scales, dimensions and RGB hashes are pinned in [inputs.json](../../experiments/odessa_courier_pretransposition/inputs.json). **Reviewed source crops:** [p201_C_reviewed.png](../../experiments/odessa_courier_pretransposition/sources/p201_C_reviewed.png) · [p201_C_overstrike.png](../../experiments/odessa_courier_pretransposition/sources/p201_C_overstrike.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify). The optional `--pdf` check reproduces the reviewed pixels from the original Childs scan; ordinary verification explicitly reports that source-pixel checking was not requested.

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — all 324 native slots, with the two overstruck X-like glyphs retained:**

```text
AGXGA XDDXG ADDFD GDGAX XDAGA FFGDV XGAXA VAFAD
VXGXX XAXFD GXXDV GAGFA XDVFX DXXDD GGDVD AAAXG
XGDFX ADFDD XAFDD DGFVV VVFGD ADFVA GVDDA AAGDF
DDVGV GXGVX DXFXX XXXVA DAADD GDADF AAAXD GADDG
DFXXX DFFXF VDGAV AAAGD GFXXF XXFGA AGXAG AAAXD
VXGAA AADXG GDXVG XGXAX GVGVA AGDAA ADXDA DXDXX
GGXAG AADDD FFGDA VFXAA GDDAG AAGGX FVFAX FAGAV
DXXFD FFXAD DXXFX DXFVD DAFDF FXGGX XDGAX AAXAX
GXVG
```

</details>

Group 11, source 50–54, appears as **GXXDV**. Both X skeletons at **51 and 52** are visible beneath the heavy overstrike, but the image does not establish ink order or make either reading unambiguous. The primary transcription uses the visible X readings. A conservative **G??DV** analysis is separately retained below; the deciphered words do not select the glyphs. Thus 324 slots have primary ADFGVX readings, of which 322 are not affected by this overstrike qualification.

An independent source audit corrected the initial draft’s row 1 group 4 from DDGAX to the clearly printed **GDGAX**. The [transcription audit](../../experiments/odessa_courier_pretransposition/source_transcription_audit.json) preserves both literal streams and the earlier artifact hashes. Source 15 is therefore already G, and BERLIN is present in the raw reading. This source-reading correction is not charged as a historical ciphertext substitution.

The earlier OCR retained only 315 slots in its p201 block 6. Reading the complete printed rows restores the native 324-slot body. That OCR correction is separate from the two missing fractionation coordinates hypothesized later.

## The direct native layer

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — unchanged Nov16–18 key, all 324 printed coordinates in the native transposition:**

```text
DEUTSCHENBEVOLLMAEANO?NO?TJ?S?ETRJV?KERELSNERHEUTBBEBERWILNAHIEREINGETROFFENSOLLENKURIERENACHDORTNOCHABFAHR?NXVERBINDXOFFZXOXROEMX2XDERXOXHXLCBERLINXZT?NRX1?111?X
```

</details>

This layer fixes **153/162 positions**. ELSNER, WILNA, HIER EINGETROFFEN, SOLLEN KURIERE NACH DORT NOCH and much of the closing are already present. The opening BEVOLLMAEANO… is retained here exactly. The conservative G??DV source analysis fixes 151/162 positions; it does not erase any printed slot from the record.

## What the two-loss model means

All indices below are zero-based. The inverse column permutation always has length **324**. Its output is a 324-coordinate intermediate stream. The proposed original fractionated stream has length **326**, with missing positions **36 and 74**. Inserting **X** and **A** there makes complete plaintext pairs.

The forward check is equally explicit:

1. Fractionate the proposed 163-label plaintext into 326 coordinates.
2. Remove the coordinates at the stated two fractionation positions.
3. Apply the published column permutation to the remaining **324** coordinates.

Before the later word repairs, this process reproduces the entire native received source exactly. After those repairs it reproduces a 324-slot received stream differing from the source at precisely the four disclosed indices. Applying a 326-coordinate column permutation would be a different model and is not used here.

The first missing X can be described at position **36 or 37**, next to the same observed X. Both descriptions produce the same filled fractionated stream. They retain different origin maps and different unfilled pair domains; neither alias is selected as the historical location.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 326-coordinate fractionation frame, with both added coordinates still unknown:**

```text
DEUTSCHENBEVOLLMAE?HTIGTENXODESSAXKUR?ERELSNERHEUTBBEBERWILNAHIEREINGETROFFENSOLLENKURIERENACHDORTNOCHABFAHR?NXVERBINDXOFFZXOXROEMX2XDERXOXHXLCBERLINXZT?NRX1?111?X
```

</details>

This unfilled model fixes **157/163 positions**. The restored pair boundaries already expose most of the address and courier wording. Its two question marks at the inserted coordinates remain source absences rather than observed values.

**Conditional interpretation — same fractionation frame after the two explicit X/A fills, before the four ordinary-word repairs:**

```text
DEUTSCHENBEVOLLMAECHTIGTENXODESSAXKURIERELSNERHEUTBBEBERWILNAHIEREINGETROFFENSOLLENKURIERENACHDORTNOCHABFAHR?NXVERBINDXOFFZXOXROEMX2XDERXOXHXLCBERLINXZT?NRX1?111?X
```

The X/A fills fix **159/163 positions**. They are not two additions to the received ciphertext. The received length and the transposition remain 324.

## Bounded placement evidence

The search uses five retrospective prefix spans at fixed offsets: DEUTSCHEN, BEVOLLMAECHTIGTEN, ODESSA, KURIER and ELSNER. It compares every pair of missing positions in a 326-coordinate fractionated stream with the **unchanged 324-coordinate intermediate source**. All **52,975** pairs are priced in each scope. The objective counts conflicts with observed coordinates; inserted values are separately supplied from the chosen word stencil.

| Retrospective word scope | Minimum observed changes | All tied missing-position pairs |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| All five prefix spans | 0 | 2 |
| ODESSA omitted | 0 | 2 |
| Address words only | 0 | 522 |
| KURIER omitted | 0 | 32 |

The first two scopes retain exactly **[36,74] and [37,74]**. ODESSA therefore appears without being forced by that second stencil. The broader address-only and courier-omitted minima remain in full; they show what depends on the selected courier vocabulary. These are sensitivity checks after the reading was seen, not blind predictions.

Repeating the same scans with both overstruck source glyphs masked leaves the same minimum sets. That protects the geometry comparison from choosing the X readings through the prefix words. Completing the two glyph masks as X would nevertheless be two additional mask fills in that conservative branch.

The existing p201 A1 body directly reads **BEVOLLMAECHTIGTEN** followed by **ODESSA**, with complete observed pairs. Its exact source indices are rechecked in the certificate. This independently attests the recipient vocabulary. It is not an identical courier report and supplies no name, travel route, date or reference number to this body.

## Four separately priced word repairs

The opening recovery and the following spelling proposals have different costs. The latter change four already observed source coordinates, after the fractionation-loss model has been fixed.

| Received source index | Printed coordinate | Proposed coordinate | Role in the word proposal |
| ---: | :---: | :---: | --- |
| 210 | G | F | HEUTBBEBER → HEUTEUEBER |
| 227 | D | A | HEUTBBEBER → HEUTEUEBER |
| 267 | G | A | ABFAHR?N → ABFAHREN |
| 287 | X | F | O H L C → O H L X separator |

The unknown character in ABFAHR?N comes from an unassigned square cell in the unedited frame. Replacing its observed GG pair by the known E pair is a source-coordinate substitution; it does not assign that unknown square cell or alter the reference fields that also use it.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — 2 added fractionation fills and 4 observed received-coordinate substitutions:**

```text
DEUTSCHENBEVOLLMAECHTIGTENXODESSAXKURIERELSNERHEUTEUEBERWILNAHIEREINGETROFFENSOLLENKURIERENACHDORTNOCHABFAHRENXVERBINDXOFFZXOXROEMX2XDERXOXHXLXBERLINXZT?NRX1?111?X
```

**Readable German — earlier word edition under the published partial square:**

> Deutschen Bevollmaechtigten Odessa. Kurier Elsner heute ueber Wilna hier eingetroffen. Sollen Kuriere nach dort noch abfahren. Verbind. Offz. O Roem 2 der O. H. L. Berlin. ZT? Nr. 1?111?.

VERBIND, OFFZ, O, ROEM 2 and the final ZT? NR field remain as decoded.

</details>

## Conservative overstrike sensitivity

Under the earlier baseline square, keeping source 51 and 52 masked and applying the same two fractionation fills and four observed substitutions gives the following **158/163-position** edition. It does not add source-glyph fills.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — conservative G??DV branch, with the two source glyph masks still unresolved:**

```text
DEUTS?HENBEVOLL?AECHTIGTENXODESSAXKURIERELSNERHEUTEUEBERWILNAHIEREINGETROFFENSOLLENKURIERENACHDORTNOCHABFAHRENXVERBINDXOFFZXOXROEMX2XDERXOXHXLXBERLINXZT?NRX1?111?X
```

</details>

Completing those two masks as X reproduces the primary visible-X reading, but it would cost **two additional source-mask fills** in this branch. The source image supports the X skeletons; the mathematical completion does not make the overstrike unambiguous.

## Reference labels and exact reproduction

Under the earlier baseline square, the three remaining primary unknowns occur at plaintext positions **152, 157 and 161**, from the distinct square cells **AF, GG and FD**. Each has the individual domain **0,3,4,5,6,7,8,9**. Because the square is one-to-one, their three labels must be distinct. The literal known 1s and ROEM 2 do not select the missing labels.

The earlier baseline check retains all **40,320** assignments to the eight unknown square cells with the forward loss-before-transposition process. They yield **336 distinct ordered reference triples**. One full-square witness for every triple is retained. These are proofs of alternatives, not historical choices of a date, serial or telegram number.

| Quantity | Earlier baseline edition |
| --- | ---: |
| Native received slots / advertised slots | 324 / 324 |
| Received transposition length | 324 |
| Reconstructed fractionation length | 326 |
| Plaintext positions | 163 |
| Native fixed positions | 153/162 |
| Unfilled loss-model fixed positions | 157/163 |
| After X/A fills / after four word changes | 159/163 / 160/163 |
| Added fractionation slots / fills | 2 / 2 |
| Received source insertions / exclusions | 0 / 0 |
| Observed substitutions / primary source-mask fills | 4 / 0 |

[The portable verifier](../../experiments/odessa_courier_pretransposition/verify.py) binds the native source, both origin maps, all placement minima and cost-distribution hashes, every word repair, the conservative glyph branch, the live complete displays, the independent address-word pairs and all global reference alternatives. [The certificate](../../experiments/odessa_courier_pretransposition/certificates.json) contains the complete evidence. [The frozen OCR record](../../experiments/odessa_courier_pretransposition/ocr_snapshot.json) preserves the earlier incomplete transcription.

```sh
python experiments/odessa_courier_pretransposition/verify.py --verify
python experiments/odessa_courier_pretransposition/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
python experiments/nov16_18_reference_completion/verify_courier.py --verify
```

The exact forward reproduction establishes the arithmetic of the proposed model. It does not authenticate a historical omission mechanism, replace the native reading, or prove global optimality over other keys and error models.

# OKM availability through an incompletely identified radio route

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This short native body reports a communication route to OKM. Its readable wording is an explicitly priced proposal, while AOK1? and FXT remain literal. The unresolved address character is a source erasure with both numerical and alphabetic possibilities.

## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p180 excerpt](../../experiments/okm_radio_route/sources/p180_reviewed.png) · [Inputs](../../experiments/okm_radio_route/inputs.json) · [Position and change certificates](../../experiments/okm_radio_route/certificates.json)

The published `Nov10-12` key is unchanged. [Original OCR records](../../experiments/okm_radio_route/ocr_snapshot.json) and [reproducible comparisons with that earlier evidence](../../experiments/okm_radio_route/prior_candidates.json) are preserved separately. The present edition supplies checked source framing, exact costs and readable passages; it makes no first-public-decipherment claim.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [p180 C](#p180-c) | 86 | 42 / 43 | 6 | 0 |

## p180 C

**Source transcription — header:** `C) LP-vZON (----- November 11th); 24.00; RIZI-86`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
ANOHLXOKMXOKMUEBERAOK1?XSUBCHFXTXEHREACHHAR
```

**Edited output — 6 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
ANOHLXOKMXOKMUEBERAOK1?XDURCHFXTXERREICHBAR
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> An OHL. OKM. OKM ueber AOK1? durch FXT erreichbar.

**Meaning:** The proposed reading addresses OHL and OKM and reports that OKM can be reached via the literal address AOK1? through FXT. The last address character and FXT are not expanded into a unit identity or named station.

**Editorial limits.**

- All 86 occupied source slots are retained in native order. The O-like glyph in FAXOX is masked and remains unfilled.
- SUBCH to DURCH and EHREACHHAR to ERREICHBAR cost six observed-coordinate substitutions in total. The exact raw layer remains available; the familiar wording is not represented as an unedited source reading.
- The unresolved source position in AOK1? has domain {1, 4, A, R, T, U}. It is not necessarily a numerical digit, and the edition does not choose a standard army designation.
- FXT remains a literal routing label. The missing interception-time field and separate printed 24.00 line are retained without chronological normalization.

## Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates independently reconstruct column positions and domains, compare them with the cipher implementation, replay every priced change, and check all readable nonseparator labels. Partial readings have one consistent injective square/source-mask completion witness that re-encrypts exactly; those witness choices are not historical identifications. Source images are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/okm_radio_route/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to check the original PDF and exact source-crop pixels.

# “First half from the front, second half from the back”

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p138 B gives a short operational instruction:

**Readable German — under the conditional final-X exclusion and stated word repairs:**

> Erste Hälfte von vorne, zweite Hälfte von hinten lösen. NKJ.

Its meaning is to solve or decipher the first half from the front and the
second half from the back. **The instructional body is shared by two equally
priced source variants.** The internal closing is `NKJ` in the preferred
variant and `NMJ` in the retained alternative. The separately printed
`NKJ 472` footer favors the former, without proving a unique geometry.

The edition is conditional: the source really contains **105 slots**, but
its readable body uses a 104-coordinate transposition with one extraneous
received coordinate separately retained. Two known-coordinate substitutions
and one invalid-glyph fill are also required. This is not an unchanged
ordinary-frame decryption.

## Exact source and dates

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [printed p138, PDF p141](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [full page](../../experiments/bidirectional_deciphering/sources/childs_p138_full.png)
is headed **November 6**, but the [B reception line](../../experiments/bidirectional_deciphering/sources/childs_p138_B.png)
reads **00.15 November 5**:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
B) LP v NKJ (00.15 November 5th)
SSD ZU 14.10 (5)
RICHI-105
NKJ 472
```

</details>

The `TEILE`/`RICHI` labels are overprinted, and the original image is retained.
The date contradiction is not silently repaired. There are 21 complete
five-character cipher groups; the fourth glyph of group 2, `FAARG`, is a
printed `R` outside the ADFGVX alphabet. It remains an erasure in analysis.
The external `NKJ 472` footer is outside the 105-slot ciphertext.

## Raw readings and two surviving variants

Using all 105 slots in the unchanged published `Nov4-6` transposition gives
52 paired labels plus an unpaired `G`, and no readable body:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — original odd frame; paired prefix is unreadable and an orphan coordinate remains:**

```text
EIM1VLM3LFT1VRF91R4KF19LW?HMYL4W9S3ML6NMJML1REELLTM2
```

</details>

Under the preferred conditional model, the **final received `X`, source
index 104**, is extraneous to a 104-coordinate cipher. Removing it for
transposition, while preserving it in the source witness, gives 51 fixed
labels out of 52:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional exclusion of final source 104 X:**

```text
ERSTEHAELFTEVONVORNEFFEIT?HAELFTEVONHINTENLOESENXNKJ
```

</details>

The proposal is:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional final-X exclusion, with the stated repairs:**

```text
ERSTEHAELFTEVONVORNEZWEITEHAELFTEVONHINTENLOESENXNKJ
```

</details>

Removing the preceding received **`F`, source index 103**, instead gives:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — alternate conditional exclusion of source 103 F:**

```text
ERSTEHAELFTEVONVORNEFFEIT?HAELFTEVONHINTENLOESENXNMJ
```

</details>

After the same repairs, its complete alternative is:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same alternate exclusion, with the stated repairs:**

```text
ERSTEHAELFTEVONVORNEZWEITEHAELFTEVONHINTENLOESENXNMJ
```

</details>

Both variants require exactly the same source edits:

| Source index, zero-based | Printed group / position, one-based | Change | Cost category |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | 2 / 4 | printed `R` → `F` | One invalid-glyph fill |
| 76 | 16 / 2 | `V` → `F` | One known-coordinate substitution |
| 94 | 19 / 5 | `A` → `F` | One known-coordinate substitution |

The two substitutions restore `ZWEITE`; the fill supplies the missing `E`.
In addition, each variant separately charges **one extraneous transmitted
coordinate**, either the final `X` or the preceding `F`. Encoding either
52-character proposal, transposing at length 104, and reinserting its
unchanged extra coordinate produces **the same repaired 105-slot witness**.
Neither coordinate is silently deleted from the historical source.

The independently printed `NKJ 472` is evidence favoring the `NKJ` closing.
It is not part of the ciphertext or an additional coordinate repair. Calling
the final `X` intentional padding is a possible explanation, not an established
historical fact.

## What the bounded search actually found

The archived comparison evaluated every single-coordinate insertion or
removal at two stages: before untransposition in the received stream, or
after untransposition in the intermediate stream. It supplied the one
published key, tried all six values of the printed `R` erasure and every
inserted coordinate, and used two unchanged frozen language objectives.

This completed **8,892 candidate records and 17,784 model-score evaluations**
over 422 geometric locations. The count includes repeated fill-value
witnesses; it is not a count of unique plaintexts. Both objectives tied the
two raw endings `NMJ` and `NKJ` at their highest score. The source footer,
rather than the scorer, favors the latter.

For the retrospective fixed `NKJ`-ending template, index 104 uniquely
minimizes substitutions among the 105 received-coordinate removal positions.
That statement is **conditional on the chosen closing**. Index 103 remains
equally cheap under its own `NMJ`-ending proposal. All original candidates,
ties and earlier unsuccessful stage interpretations remain in the
[phase archive](../../experiments/bidirectional_deciphering/search/original_phase_screen.json).

## Relation to p132 B's 1410 (5) telegram

The [p132 B source edition](p132_radio_service.md#b-repeat-the-fourth-period-telegram-in-the-fifth)
contains this header:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
B) LP v NKJ (6.13 p.m., November 5th)
SSD EILT SOFORT LOESEN 1410 (5)
RIZI-155
```

</details>

The two records share the route **LP v NKJ**, the urgency label `SSD` and
the internal reference **1410 (5)**, with punctuation added in p138's
`ZU 14.10 (5)`. `ZU` explicitly introduces a reference to that time-stamped
message. These are concrete grounds for treating p138 as a likely related
instruction. They do not establish a reply in the reverse direction: the
printed route is the same in both. Nor is their chronological order fully
resolved, because p138's reception line and page heading conflict.

The preserved 622-block OCR-header inventory finds this time/day combination
only at p132 B and p138 B; another `1410` belongs to p177 with day `11/11`.
That is a bounded inventory of available OCR headers, not a universal
uniqueness claim about the original traffic.

### A precisely limited opposite-end interpretation

The p132 source has 155 intermediate coordinates after its original
transposition is undone. With an odd length, pairing from the front and
pairing from the back use opposite pair phases. A finite comparison tried
all **78** ways to join an initial run of forward labels to a final run of
backward labels, leaving exactly one intermediate coordinate unpaired.

| Leading labels read from front | Trailing labels read from back | Unpaired intermediate index | Known-coordinate substitutions for the prior p132 proposal |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 27 | 50 | 54 | 3 |
| 28 | 49 | 56 | 3 |
| 38 | 39 | 76 | 20 |
| 39 | 38 | 78 | 22 |

The first two reproduce the earlier low-cost conditional p132 reading.
Their unpaired `V` belongs to the same run of four identical V coordinates
at indices **54–57** already retained in that edition. The literal balanced
halves, 38/39 or 39/38 labels, do **not** reproduce it at the same cost.

Thus the newly read instruction supports the general relevance of working
from opposite ends. A flexible split is algebraically the existing one-extra-
intermediate-coordinate model; it does not reduce that model's assumptions
or repair cost. The instruction does not explicitly identify intermediate
coordinates, a split point, or a mathematical procedure. **The p132 extra-V
interpretation remains conditional**, and none of these observations changes
the status of an unrelated challenge.

The two source models also act at different stages:

| Record | Conditional operation | Source-shaped forward witness |
| --- | --- | --- |
| p138 B | Exclude one received coordinate before 104-slot untransposition | Reinsert that same coordinate after transposition, preserving all 105 slots |
| p132 B | Exclude one intermediate V after 155-slot untransposition | Reinsert that V before transposition, preserving all 155 slots |

## Reproduce and attribution

The [inputs](../../experiments/bidirectional_deciphering/inputs.json),
[certificate](../../experiments/bidirectional_deciphering/certificates.json)
and [method package](../../experiments/bidirectional_deciphering/README.md)
preserve all source bytes, image hashes, both full variants and the 78 finite
comparisons. The p132 inputs and certificate are frozen snapshots; its older
record is not modified by this comparison.

```sh
python experiments/bidirectional_deciphering/verify.py --verify
python experiments/bidirectional_deciphering/phase_audit.py --verify
```

The unchanged period key is prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils
Kopal and Arno Wacker**, [DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
also published in George Lasry's [2017-02-24 comment 4](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1).
Earlier unreviewed OCR and insertion-only candidates existed. No explicit
p138 B body example was found in the bounded author-paper review; no universal
first-decipherment priority is claimed.

# p111 B — Use radio for important messages

[Case guide](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Source image](../../sources/excerpts/other_p111_B.png) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** A complete direct reading of a supplementary message. The unchanged
published `Nov1-3` key fixes **all 154 plaintext positions** and reproduces all
**308 source coordinates**. No source coordinate, key cell or message length
is changed.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> Fuer Chef Mittelmeerdivision, B. M. K., Nateko:
> Wegen Unsicherheit der Kabelverbindungen fuer wichtige Mel[d]ungen
> Funkspruch benutzen. Admiralstab 18266 D, roem. 2.

**Meaning:** Addressed to the chief of the Mediterranean Division, B.M.K. and
Nateko: because cable connections are unreliable, use radio for important
messages. The message closes with an Admiralty Staff reference, `18266 D`,
followed by the instruction to read `2` as a Roman numeral.

The body provides a direct reason for using radio: uncertainty about the
cable connections. It does not specify whether this was caused by physical
damage, interception, censorship or some other problem. `B. M. K.` and
`NATEKO` are retained as decoded abbreviations, without an unverified expansion.

The only supplied letter in the displayed reading is the bracketed `d` in
*Meldungen*. The raw text spells the word **`MELUNGEN`**. That spelling omission
is kept in the cryptographic transcript and is not counted as an extra
recovered position. Spacing, capitalization and punctuation are editorial.

## Exact direct reading

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FUERXCHEFXMITTELMEERDIVISIONXBXMXKXNATEKOXWEGENXUNSICHERHEITXDERXKABELVERBINDUNGENXFUERXWICHTIGEXMELUNGENXFUNKSPRUCHXBENUTZENXADMIRALSTABX18266XDXROEMX2XX
```

</details>

Every letter and digit in this string is fixed by the source and the complete
published key. Re-encryption reproduces the literal source exactly, including
the spelling `MELUNGEN`. The `X` characters act as separators here; `ROEMX2`
is the direct text behind the rendered “roem. 2.”

## Source and dates

Printed p111 / PDF p114, section B. The page heading is **3 November 1918**,
and the internal stamp is `2315 (3.11)`. The reception header actually prints
`FUER NKJ, ASO, RAT v LP (2.54 a.m., November 5th); RICHI-308`.
The differing dates are visible in the source and are retained without
inferring a cause or silently changing either date.

The [literal source record](../../experiments/corpus_readings/selected_sources.json)
contains all grouped coordinates. The
[certificate](../../experiments/corpus_readings/certificates.json) gives every
plaintext position's source pair, the key provenance, an independent
column-offset inverse and the exact re-encryption check.

```sh
python3 experiments/corpus_readings/verify.py --verify
```

**Credit:** George Lasry's published period key and its historical sources are
retained in [the key register](../../data/keys.json). Source inspection,
verification and this annotated reading are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.
No first-decipherment priority is claimed for this supplementary message.

# p132 A and C — An officer-register request and a garbled-message repeat

[Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p132 contains three separate records: a partly garbled request for
an officer-register extract, a conditional recovery of a repeat-transmission
instruction for Eilvese, and an exact request to repeat a garbled incoming
Caucasus message. The unchanged published `Nov4-6` key applies throughout.
The middle record has its own [canonical p132 case](../p132.md); A and C
have ordinary exact frames and remain separately catalogued physical sources.

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [printed p132, PDF p135](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [full page](../../experiments/november_radio_service/sources/childs_p132_full.png)
is headed `5th NOVEMBER, 1918.`

## A: an officer-register request, with the name unresolved

The [A source](../../experiments/november_radio_service/sources/childs_p132_A.png)
has this header and exactly 242 slots, including one printed dash:

<details>
<summary>Source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) OSM v OUI (9.29 p.m., November 5th)
HIER 13 2207
RICHI-242
```

</details>

The raw 121-position reading fixes 120 positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
MILLTAEGMISZIONKOSJOIIXUEBERTENDUNGEILESKRIEGSRANGLI?TRNAUSZUGESDESGENERALMAJRHYDEWALDERBETENXFELDEISENBAHNNHEFPAFR53540X
```

</details>

Six observed-coordinate substitutions and one dash fill repair ordinary
words, giving:

<details>
<summary>Exact edited proposal</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
MILITAERMISZIONKOSJOIIXUEBERSENDUNGEINESKRIEGSRANGLISTENAUSZUGESDESGENERALMAJRHYDEWALDERBETENXFELDEISENBAHNCHEFPAFR53540X
```

</details>

The readable clause is:

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with the literal addressee and name fields:**

> Militärmiszion `KOSJOII`. Übersendung eines Kriegsranglistenauszuges des `GENERALMAJRHYDEWALD`
> erbeten. Feldeisenbahnchef `PAFR53540`.

The readable quotation includes the entire opening `MILITAERMISZIONKOSJOII`. Its Z spelling and unresolved field remain literal; the six substitutions and one dash fill above are unchanged.

It requests an extract from a wartime officer register. **The addressee/place
field `KOSJOII` and the general-name field `GENERALMAJRHYDEWALD` remain
unresolved.** Neither is expanded into an identified person or place. The
raw `MISZION` spelling and `PAFR53540` footer also remain literal. This is a
partial source edition, not a securely identified personnel record.

A [separate surname proposal](../../experiments/p132_rohdewald_name/README.md)
reads `GENERALMAJ ROHDEWALD` at four additional observed-coordinate
substitutions, for ten substitutions and one dash fill in total. A 1913
*Deutscher Reichsanzeiger* personnel notice attests the surname Rohdewald
in a railway-general-staff context. This supports the proposed spelling;
it does not establish the officer's identity. The primary displays above
and the separate address proposal remain unchanged.

## B: repeat the fourth-period telegram in the fifth

The complete source/model edition is consolidated in [canonical challenge
p132](../p132.md). That page combines Thomas’s initial fragment, Norbert’s
fuller sender-error reading and `VORHER` proposal, the later three-substitution
and two-erasure-fill account, and all four equivalent intermediate-`V`
positions. `p132_B` survives only as an identifier inside the frozen evidence
package; it is not a second catalogue entry.

## C: request to repeat a garbled incoming message

The [C source](../../experiments/november_radio_service/sources/childs_p132_C.png)
has this header:

<details>
<summary>Source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
C) NKJ v LP (7.45 p.m., November 6th)
FUER COS 2150 (5/11)
RICHI-198
```

</details>

The November 5 origin line and November 6 reception line are retained.
All 198 coordinates and all 99 plaintext labels are fixed without repair:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
KAUKASUSDELEGAXWIEDERHLGVERSTUEMMELTEINGEGXOSKACHIX54GRXSSX1912XANXNACHCHEFERBETENXNACHCHE5X150527X
```

</details>

The message addresses the Caucasus delegation and asks for repetition of a
garbled incoming message to `NACHCHEF`. Its literal reference is
`OSKACHI 54GR SS 1912`; the footer is `NACHCHE5 150527`. Those abbreviations
and numerical labels, including the final `5` in `NACHCHE5`, remain as read.
No new numbering interpretation or silent spelling change is introduced.

## Source status and reproducibility

The [inputs](../../experiments/november_radio_service/inputs.json) preserve
manual rows, literal headers, key provenance and source-image hashes. The
[certificate](../../experiments/november_radio_service/certificates.json)
records the raw and conditional readings, all possible label domains,
coordinate origins and exact forward witnesses. A remains partly garbled
at its names; B remains conditional on the extra-coordinate model; C is an
unchanged direct reading.

The period key is prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**, [2016, DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
also reproduced in George Lasry's [2017-02-24 comment 4](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1).
Earlier unreviewed OCR-derived candidates existed. The bounded paper check
found no explicit p132 body example; no universal first-decipherment claim
is made.

```sh
python experiments/november_radio_service/verify.py --verify
python experiments/november_radio_service/geometry_audit.py --verify
```

A [separate address-spelling supplement](../../experiments/p132_optional_address/README.md) prices `KOSJOII` → `KOSPOLI` at two additional observed-coordinate substitutions and binds independent raw occurrences in p90, p98 and p148. This optional proposal leaves the primary streams and unresolved name above unchanged.
