# p137 B — Query about the station's former staff

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Recovery and source review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** A conditional
group-movement and three-loss reconstruction exposes a query about whether
the station is still staffed by its former personnel, followed by a request
to answer and the closing name Eilvese.

## p137 B

**Readable German — conditional 138-slot frame; three observed substitutions, two printed-mask fills and two inserted-slot fills; time unresolved:**

> Ist dortige Station noch vom alten Personal besetzt? Antwortet um `17?0`. Eilvese.

The question mark after *besetzt* is editorial punctuation. The question mark
inside `17?0` is one unresolved plaintext position, retained literally.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — primary conditional 138-slot frame, before substitutions and fills; 64/69 fixed positions:**

```text
ICTDORTIGEVTATIONN?CHVOMALT?NPERSONALBESETZTXANTWO?TETUM17?0XEILBES?X
```

</details>

The source prints **135 slots**, including two dashes, against `RIZI-138`.
The primary model moves the last printed group `VDF--` (source 130–134) to
retained-stream boundary 105, the beginning of the final printed row. It
then appends three unknown coordinates to reach the advertised length.
All 135 source slots remain represented once; none is excluded. The movement is part of the stated reconstruction.

For the fixed 69-position proposal, exact integer pricing compares **481,032
maps**: each of 27 printed groups, each of 131 destinations after removal,
and each of 136 boundaries for the three missing coordinates. The minimum
is three observed substitutions. Exactly **five maps** attain it: source
group 130 moves to boundary 103, 104, 105, 106 or 107, and all three missing
slots follow the resulting 135-slot stream. Every minimum gives 64/69 fixed
raw positions and the same 68/69-position edited proposal. The certificate
retains all five alternatives; boundary 105 is the primary display because
it coincides with a printed group and row boundary.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same primary frame; three observed substitutions, two printed-mask fills and two inserted-slot fills; 68/69 fixed positions:**

```text
ISTDORTIGESTATIONNOCHVOMALTENPERSONALBESETZTXANTWORTETUM17?0XEILVESEX
```

</details>

| Primary repair or frame operation | Exact account, zero-based indices |
|---|---|
| Source group movement | Source 130–134 to retained-stream boundary 105 |
| Missing coordinates | Three unknown slots appended at model 135–137 |
| Observed substitutions | Source 130 `V→F`, 131 `D→G`, 132 `F→X` |
| Existing printed-mask fills | Source 133 `-→A`, 134 `-→F` |
| Inserted-slot fills | Model 135 `?→V`, 137 `?→F` |
| Retained uncertainty | Model 136 unassigned; plaintext 58 has domain `036OQY` |

The three changes include all three observed coordinates of the moved group
in this primary layout; the movement does not conceal their price. The
other 130 observed coordinates remain unchanged. Each of the six possible
labels at plaintext 58 has a complete exact re-encryption witness under the
same unchanged global key. The primary edition retains `17?0`.

The independent [p127 personnel notice](nov4_personnel_transmission_notice.md)
contains `HIER NOCH ALTES PERSONAL` and says transmission continues as
agreed. Its subject is compatible with this query. Its LP/NKJ route differs
from OSM/OUI here, and neither source explicitly identifies the other: this
is topical context, with no copied coordinates or proved reply relationship.

## Source and reproduction

Childs, printed p137 / PDF p140, section B. The page heading is
`6th NOVEMBER,1918`; the receipt line instead says November 5. The clear
continuation, advertised length and footer below are contextual annotations,
outside the 135 ciphertext slots.

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — full header, all 135 cipher slots and clear footer:**

```text
B) OSM v OUI (14.58 November 5th)
CONTD HIER SS NR 10 - 11.00
RIZI-138
FVGDG XVAVX AAFAG AXGXA ADXAV AGAXA AGAGF
XAGDX GFFXF XXXVV XXXVX DFXAG AVAFD AVAVG
AAFXF XXXXA FDAXD XXVAV VAVGX AGGAX GFAXF
FFAFX XXAFF AADAA XVFDX XXFGA VDF--
OSM
V OUI
```

</details>

[Original source PDF, p140](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view)
· [Reproduction and source recipe](../../experiments/p137_station_staff_query/README.md)
· [All minimum maps, domains and repair ledgers](../../experiments/p137_station_staff_query/certificates.json).

The **Nov4–6** square and column ranks remain exactly as published by George
Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and Lasry's 2017 key

source review, new query reading, frame reconstruction and independent
verification are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

# p164 B — Dismantling the station and marching to Temesvar

[All cases](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** 69/70 raw positions fixed; two explicit coordinate substitutions
in the readable edition; one time digit remains conditional. **Source edition
and review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. **Period key:** George Lasry and
colleagues.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German — both unresolved time-cell alternatives retained:**

> Wir abbauen 9.11., [05:00 oder 06:00], Weitermarsch Temesvar. Wenn dort aufgebaut,
> rufen wir.

**Display notes:** This readable German includes the two recorded repairs below and keeps both time alternatives. The bracketed whole field is an alternative display of the single unassigned digit in `0?00`; the colon is editorial punctuation. It does not select the later historical `05:00` interpretation.

**Meaning:** The station will be dismantled, followed by an onward march to
Temesvar; it will call again once set up there. The literal cipher-only time is
05:00 or 06:00. Under the already documented historical completion of the
November 7–9 square, it is **05:00 on 9 November**.

The telegram style is retained; *wir bauen ab* is the ordinary German wording.
The proposed month `11` repairs the raw `18`. The proposed `RUFEN` repairs raw
`RUDEN`. Both changes are individually costed below.

## Source

Childs, printed p. 164 / PDF p. 167, section B:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
LP v ZON (3.34 a.m., November 9th)
1133
RIZI-140

AVGVA XXXXX DFAGG VAAXG VVDXD VVVVG VVVGV AXAFA
XAGGD VVAAX FDDXD XGVAD XXAVD DADVD DVGVX XVXGX
DDDDX DFVVD XDAVV GVGGF VXVVV VFGGD DDDAD XXVGX
VDFGX VDVDX GVVAV AGAGA
```

</details>

All 140 coordinates are legible; the received length agrees with the header.
The source marker is printed `RIZI`, not silently normalized to `RICHI`.

## Unchanged-key raw reading

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
WIRXABBAUEN9X18X0?00WEITERMARSCHXTEMESVARXWENNDORTAUFGEBAUTXRUDENXWIRX
```

</details>

The unknown plaintext position 17 is the square cell `XA`, whose baseline
domain is exactly `56`. It is not a lost source coordinate. Every other
position is fixed by the published key and literal transcript.

| Proposed correction | Plaintext position | Received-coordinate change |
|---|---:|---|
| Month `18` → `11` | 14 | Source position 92: `A` → `G` |
| `RUDEN` → `RUFEN` | 62 | Source position 76: `V` → `X` |

All indices are zero-based. The source header supports the November reading;
the verb is a language-based repair. There are **two known-coordinate
substitutions, no erasure fills**, and 138 coordinates remain unchanged.

## Conditional time digit

The existing
[historical square layer](../../experiments/p170_continuation/military_context.json)
gives `VF=6`, `XA=5`, from the independently identified 6th Reserve Division.
Using that same global square assigns `XA=5` here and gives `0500` without any
additional ciphertext change. The baseline square and its `{5,6}` alternative
remain intact. Accepting the date and verb repairs does not require accepting
this separate historical inference.

The proposed edition under that layer is:

**Conditional interpretation — two coordinate repairs plus the separate historical XA = 5 hypothesis:**

```text
WIRXABBAUEN9X11X0500WEITERMARSCHXTEMESVARXWENNDORTAUFGEBAUTXRUFENXWIRX
```

It re-encrypts exactly to the two-substitution ciphertext.

## Evidence and credit

The [source crop](../../experiments/withdrawal_recovery/sources/childs_p164_B.png),
[literal inputs](../../experiments/withdrawal_recovery/inputs.json) and
[exact certificate](../../experiments/withdrawal_recovery/certificates.json)
retain the full evidence. The period key is prior Lasry-team work; the present
source edition and arithmetic review are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.
No first-historical-decipherment priority is claimed.

```sh
python3 experiments/withdrawal_recovery/verify.py --verify
```

# p167 C1 — Mission and Nachrichtenchef service address

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Partial recovery and source review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Nachrichtenchef routing/signature field. The opaque labels `MILB`, `0RM`
and `RELA` remain literal; no particular institution or location is identified.

The [shared Nov7–9 reference interpretation](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) reads **Roem 5; KR 130615**, completing **66/66 conditional edited labels**. The opposite assignment gives Roem 6; KR 130516. All three affected pairs are originally observed. The six word substitutions and two printed-mask fills are unchanged, and the labels MILB, 0RM and RELA remain literal.

> An MILB Mission. Abtlg 0RM. 10. RELA. Nachrichtenchef. Roem ?. KR 130?1?.

The readable content is an address/service fragment, with `MISSION`, `ABTLG`
and `NACHRICHTENCHEF` as explicitly priced word repairs. Only the first part
of the header's two-part transmission is identified here.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>


```text

```

</details>

The six observed changes are source **20 D→X, 23 D→X, 83 V→D, 84 D→X,
114 V→X, 126 X→D**. Source **14** is a printed dash filled as `G`;
source **90** is the literal invalid `Z`, filled as `X`. The `B` proposal

assignments under the published partial square. The conditional reference
comparison above supplies a separate documentary basis for choosing 5/6.

An optional interpretation of the `B` in `MILB` as separator `X` costs two
further observed substitutions: **13 G→V** and **113 X→V**. Its total is eight,
with the same two mask fills. The primary edition retains `MILB`.

`VDADDD` is source[80:86]; the four-coordinate `VVVG` is source[196:200]. Their
length discrepancies cancel, so the literal body already has the advertised
280 coordinates. Treating both as regular five-coordinate groups without an
explicit operation would conceal the source error.

The primary frame excludes the D at source 83 and inserts one unknown at
boundary 195 of the remaining 279-slot stream, at the start of the short group.
All other 279 observations remain unchanged and in source order. This is a
conditional reconstruction, not an OCR correction. All indices here are zero
based; ranges are half open.

There are **12 tied descriptions**: exclude any of source 83,84,85 and insert
at any boundary 195,196,197,198. A source-directed comparison checks all 30
choices within the six-coordinate and four-coordinate groups. The twelve
leaders have six disagreements against the independently observed coordinates
of the p159 B component; coordinates already supplied from another copy are
excluded from that comparison. The comparison establishes correspondence,
not a unique historical error mechanism.

## Raw and source-linked readings

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — primary frame, unchanged Nov7–9 key; 139/140 positions fixed, no coordinate substitutions or fills:**

```text
UEBER2HBAYRXGENXKDOXMUENCXENXXAN7XRSSXDIVXXLA3DSBERGEAN0EECHXXNICH2DURCH1ABELXARMEESCHLUESSELDORPELTXEMPFANGBESTXXOXHXLXRMX1ANRX11338G?HXORX
```

</details>

The four insertion boundaries give four different unfilled streams, each
fixing 139 positions. They agree at 136 positions. The repeated-D exclusions
change ownership only. The certificate retains every alias rather than pooling
its known letters into a falsely complete raw message.

Original p159 B coordinates 195–198 all read V. Under the inherited component
correspondence, the relevant V fills the added coordinate in each alias. Every
alias then produces the same completed ciphertext:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — one inserted-slot V supplied by p159 B, no changes to retained p168 coordinates; 140/140 positions fixed:**

```text
UEBER2HBAYRXGENXKDOXMUENCXENXXAN7XRSSXDIVXXLA3DSBERGEAN0EECHXXNICH2DURCH1ABELXARMEESCHLUESSELDORPELTXEMPFANGBESTXXOXHXLXRMX1ANRX11338GEHXORX
```

</details>

**Readable German — literal word excerpts from that source-linked stream; omitted passages are outside the quotation:**

> […] Gen. Kdo. […] Armeeschluessel […] Empfang best. […] O.H.L. […]

The associated order concerns routing through the Bavarian command at Munich,
army-key treatment and acknowledgment. The original contemporary reading and
later scholarly discussion are credited in the [component history](../p158.md#earlier-historical-reading-of-a-component).
The stream above retains `MUENCXEN`, `RSS`, `LA3DSBERG`, `DORPELT` and the other
remaining garbles; no new place, unit or numeral correction is supplied here.

## New coordinate support for KDO

At plaintext position 16, p168 C has the fully observed pair **VG = K**.
Its model indices 113 and 169 come from source 114 and 170. The corresponding
p159 B component has **VX = H**. Thus its `GEN HDO` can be repaired to `GEN KDO`
using the observed G from p168 source 170:

| Receiving source | Source index | Printed | Parallel-supported replacement |
|---|---:|:---:|:---:|
| p159 B | 169 | X | G |

This is one observed-coordinate substitution in p159 B, supported by a separate
printed observation. It changes exactly one plaintext letter and preserves all
other text in the established `p159B_supported_V` component layer.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — earlier p159 B supported-V component plus the single X→G substitution at source169; all other inherited repairs and garbles retained:**

```text
UEBER2XBAYRXGENXKDOXMUENCXENXXAN7XRSSXDIVXXLA3DSBERGXAN0LECHXXNICHTDURCHKABELXARMEESCHLUESSELDOWPELTXEMPFANGBESTXXOXHXLXRMX1ANRX11338GEHXORX
```

</details>

## Joint-source reconciliation

The last displayed stream also has an explicit reconciliation of the p168
witness. It follows the established p159 component at the remaining source
disagreements and uses the new p168 observation for KDO. Each selected
coordinate has a printed donor; these are recorded choices between differing
observations, not word guesses or an automatic majority vote.

| Reconciliation | p168 observed substitutions | p168 added-slot fills | p159 additional observed substitutions | Cable word |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| p159 B and p168 C | 5 | 1, V from p159 B | 1, G from p168 C | `1ABEL` retained |
| Add p158 D as third witness | 6 | 1, V from p159 B | 1, G from p168 C | `KABEL` |

The three-witness version is exactly the p159 B + KDO stream displayed above.
Its six substitutions in the primary p168 frame have the following donors:

| p168 source index | Printed | Selected | Original donor |
|---:|:---:|:---:|---|
| 5 | D | V | p159 B source 5 |
| 7 | F | V | p158 D source 7 |
| 169 | X | V | p159 B source 168 |
| 174 | V | D | p159 B source 173 |
| 175 | D | V | p159 B source 174 |
| 247 | D | X | p159 B source 247 |

At model 7, original p159 B has invalid `R`; its earlier V reconstruction must
not be counted as an independent p159 observation. The V here comes directly
from p158 D source 7, in its established prefix correspondence. The two-witness
layer therefore keeps p168's F at that position and retains `1ABEL`. Both layers
keep `DOWPELT` unchanged; no P is invented to make `DOPPELT`. The native sources,
primary raw reading and one-V source-linked layer above remain separate.

## Reproduction and credit

The [certificate](../../experiments/p168_munich_routing_witness/certificates.json)
records the literal source, every coordinate origin, all raw character domains,
the twelve ownership aliases, the copied V and the separate KDO repair. The
original PDF and a fresh source crop are authenticated by SHA-256. Two fresh
same-shape controls recover their complete source-linked streams. Both global
5/6 square completions pass full re-encryption; no choice between them is made.

**Reproduction command — verifies both source-linked streams and all frame alternatives:**

```sh
python experiments/p168_munich_routing_witness/verify.py --verify
```

Order 11338 has a wartime reading by **J. Rives Childs**, published in 1935.
**George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), §6.4**, discuss
the p168 C/D bodies. The p158 composite-source relationship, this full p168 C
source-frame certificate and the coordinate support for KDO are reviewed by
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. Earlier wording and key credit remain intact.

# p187 D1 — Aircraft connection to Mackensen currently impossible

[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source and certificate](../../experiments/aviation_connection/README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Record:** the surviving first part of message D on printed p187,
headed 13 November 1918.
**Result:** a conditional 252-coordinate frame yields a coherent
76-character closing sentence with two changes to received coordinates
and one proposed missing five-coordinate group. Twelve positions in the
opening reference fields remain unresolved.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German — body excerpt under the stated missing-group frame:**

> O.K. Mackensen. [Opening reference fields unresolved.]
> Verbindung mit R- oder G-Flugzeugen z. Zt. aus technischen Gruenden
> unmoeglich.

**Meaning:** A connection using R or G aircraft is currently impossible
for technical reasons. The message does not establish a specific aircraft
model or the purpose of the proposed connection. Its original reference
numbers and continuation have not been supplied.

## Source-framing hypothesis

The [source crop](../../experiments/aviation_connection/sources/childs_p187_D.png)
prints `RICHI-252` but contains 247 ADFGVX coordinates, plus a small
dash-like mark before the full group `GFVVV`. The edition treats that
mark as non-coordinate and inserts a missing group `DDDVV` after the
last printed complete group `DDDAA`, before final `DG`.

This is an explicit reconstruction. Those five coordinates are absent
from the source. Inserting `DDVVD` one coordinate later produces exactly
the same completed ciphertext; the two positions are equivalent aliases.

The framed baseline-key reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional five-coordinate-loss frame; unassigned square cells retained:**

```text
OXKXMACKENSENXZUXWORTXRMX?XDX?????XUXRMX?XAX?????XVERBINDUNGXMIT?RXODERXGX?LUGZEUGIN?ZXZTXAUSX?ECHNISCHE?XGRUENDENXUEMOEGLICHX
```

</details>

The proposed edition, with only the two known-coordinate repairs, is:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional loss frame, with two observed-coordinate repairs:**

```text
OXKXMACKENSENXZUXWORTXRMX?XDX?????XUXRMX?XAX?????XVERBINDUNGXMITXRXODERXGXFLUGZEUGENXZXZTXAUSXTECHNISCHENXGRUENDENXUNMOEGLICHX
```

</details>

| Decision | Exact change |
|---|---|
| Source mark | Exclude the small mark before the complete `GFVVV` group from the coordinate count |
| Missing group | Insert `DDDVV` after 245 received coordinates; the 246-boundary alias yields the same completed stream |
| Known coordinate 25, one-based | `X→V`, changing `UEMOEGLICH` to `UNMOEGLICH` |
| Known coordinate 223, one-based | `A→X`, changing `FLUGZEUGIN` to `FLUGZEUGEN` |

The 126-position frame has 109 raw fixed positions. Completing the
missing group yields 114 fixed positions after the two repairs. The
remaining 12 positions occupy five distinct unassigned square cells,
whose shared unused-symbol pool is `0123456789QY`. No digit assignments
or expansions of the raw `WORT`/`RM` reference wording are proposed.

For the same proposed 76-character suffix, exhaustive comparison of the
248 possible five-loss boundaries gives a minimum of two substitutions
only at the equivalent boundaries above. Keeping the source mark as an
erasure and inserting four coordinates requires at least 28 substitutions
over all 249 boundaries. This comparison supports the stated frame but
does not prove that every other damage model or plaintext is impossible.

## Separate conditional Y inference

The [Tiflis/pilot-name comparison](../caucasus/tiflis_appointment.md) later supports a
conditional **Nov13–15a DG = Y** assignment. Its use here additionally assumes
that the two differently keyed pilot notices contain the same correctly
copied surname. None of this message's five unresolved reference cells is
DG, so the assignment fixes no digit. It reduces their available labels to
`0123456789Q`, and their coupled possibilities from 95,040 to **55,440**.
The [propagation certificate](../../experiments/contextual_key_constraints/README.md)
checks both source-equivalent gap aliases and constructs a complete square
extension for every allowed field assignment. The baseline reading above
and its original source repairs are unchanged.

## Source and credit

Printed p187 / PDF p190: `D) NKJ v LP (03.04 a.m., November 13th);
FUER UKS 20.12 (13/11); 1 TL RICHI-252`, followed by `(Continued)`.
The multipart-total glyph is left unasserted; it is visible in the source
crop. The apparent same-date timing inconsistency is preserved rather
than silently corrected.

The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, in the [public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The published Nov13–15a key keeps its original credit in
[data/keys.json](../../data/keys.json). Source inspection, gap analysis and
this edition are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical
decipherment priority is claimed.

```sh
python experiments/aviation_connection/verify.py --verify
```

The [inputs](../../experiments/aviation_connection/inputs.json) and
[certificate](../../experiments/aviation_connection/certificate.json)
contain literal rows, source hashes, exact edits, every fixed-suffix
geometry comparison, and consistent re-encryption witnesses. The witness
square completions are not accepted historical reference numbers.

# p204 A — a radio-station handover and a conditional date digit

[Case guide](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** The unchanged published `Nov16-18` partial key fixes **69 of 70
plaintext positions** from all **140 valid source coordinates**. The only
unknown is a date digit. A separately recorded calendar inference gives a
plausible new assignment, **FD = 8**, without changing the published key.
**Source review and inference:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. The period key
retains the attribution in [data/keys.json](../../data/keys.json).

## Reading from the published key

**Readable German:**

> Hiesige Fusta wird laut S.R. Warschau Montag 1? Polen uebergeben.
> Fusta WAUM.

**Meaning:** According to S.R. Warsaw, the local radio station is to be handed
over to Polish control on Monday the 1?. `Fusta` is read as the abbreviated
radio station. `S.R.` is likely the Soldiers' Council in this context, but its
expansion is not part of the decrypted character stream. The raw ending
`FUSTAWAUM` is retained; its final `M` is not silently changed to a separator
or a different call sign.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
HIESIGEFUSTAWIRDLAUTXSXRXWARSCHAUMONTAGX1?XPOLENUEBERGEBENXXFUSTAWAUMX
```

</details>

Every fixed letter above comes from valid source coordinates and an already
established square cell. No editorial coordinate repair is proposed for this
message.

## Source date

The [source image](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/sources/childs_p204_selected.png)
is printed p204 / PDF p207, section A. The heading reads **16 November 1918**;
the intercept and internal stamps are:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
LP v WAU (3.20 a.m., November 17th)
SN AR KRIEGSMINISTERIUM 2130 (16)
RICHI-140
```

</details>

The body preserves every one of the 140 printed coordinates. The date's
unknown unit at plaintext index **41** uses the fully observed digraph
**FD**, square cell **13** in zero-based row-major indexing. Its source
coordinates are indices **92** and **63**. Under the published partial square,
its domain is `03456789`.

## Why 18 November is a strong, conditional reading

The preceding digit `1` and the word `MONTAG` are directly fixed. If the
date refers to **November 1918**, as the message heading and internal stamp
indicate, the compatible candidates are:

| Day in November 1918 | Weekday |
| ---: | --- |
| 10 | Sunday |
| 13 | Wednesday |
| 14 | Thursday |
| 15 | Friday |
| 16 | Saturday |
| 17 | Sunday |
| **18** | **Monday** |
| 19 | Tuesday |

The 11th was also a Monday, but the unknown cell cannot contain `1`: that
digit already occupies another established cell in the injective square.
The 12th is likewise excluded because `2` is already assigned. Thus
**Monday 18 November** is the unique candidate under the stated month,
weekday and square assumptions.

This is a historical inference, not an extra character supplied by the
unchanged key. It assumes that the weekday, month context and two date
coordinates were copied correctly. Source copying errors remain possible.
The repository therefore keeps `FD = 8` in the
[conditional layer](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/certificates.json),
leaving the published partial square untouched.

## Independent consequences

The same `FD` cell appears in three date fields of the three-part
[p206 A reference list](../military/p201_p206_orders.md). Under the conditional assignment,
all three read **8 November**. This is propagation of one shared key cell,
not three independent confirmations of its value.

None of the six unresolved reference digits in the
[p205 financial](../finance/p205_A.md) and [naval](../naval/p205_B.md) messages uses `FD`.
Consequently, this inference alone supplies **no new fixed p205 character**;
it only removes `8` from the domains of their other unassigned cells.
The separate p201/p206 date-link inference supplies one p205 digit under a
different, explicitly recorded assumption.

## Verification and credit

```sh
python3 experiments/open_targets_continuation/verify.py --verify
```

The verifier independently reconstructs the column offsets, checks the
plaintext domains against the project decoder, reproduces the calendar
calculation and lists every position affected by the conditional assignment.
The [inputs](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/inputs.json) preserve
the literal source, exact header, source-image hash and assumptions.
The source review and conditional analysis are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**;
no first-decipherment priority is claimed for this supplementary message.

# p211, lower B — an explicit November/December key schedule

[Case guide](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** Three source-checked parts form a readable key-handling
instruction. The unchanged published `Nov4-6` key fixes **265 of 266 raw
plaintext positions** from **532 printed coordinate slots**. **Source
assembly and edition:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. Period-key recovery
retains the attribution in [data/keys.json](../../data/keys.json); no first
historical decipherment priority is claimed.

## Reading

**Readable German:**

> November-Ringbahnschluessel nicht vernichten. Nachr.-Chef X4, B848727.
> Dezember-Ringbahnschluessel tritt vorlaeufig nicht in Kraft. Dafuer
> Schluessel erster Dezember wie zehnter November usw. bis
> einundzwanzigster Dezember wie dreissigster November.
> Empfangsbestaetigung. Nachr.-Chef Z4, B47857.

**Meaning:** Do not destroy the November Ringbahn key. The December Ringbahn
key will not yet take effect. Instead, use the 10 November key for 1 December,
continuing through the 30 November key for 21 December, and acknowledge
receipt.

The schedule itself is directly decoded in part 2 and the beginning of part
3. Three source-coordinate substitutions restore spelling in part 1; one
invalid source glyph is filled in `DREISSIGSTER` in part 3. Word spacing,
punctuation, abbreviation breaks and the omission of doubled separator `X`
characters in the reading above are editorial. The first reference
`B848727` and the difference between `NACHRCHEFX4` and `NACHRCHEFZ4` remain
literal; they are not regularized to each other.

## What this establishes

This message records an explicit reuse instruction:

| Intended December date | November key named by the instruction |
| --- | --- |
| 1 December | 10 November |
| Continuing dates (`USW`) | Corresponding continuation of the November sequence |
| 21 December | 30 November |

The first and last mappings are explicit; the intermediate daily mapping is
the ordinary interpretation of `USW` (“and so on”). This is evidence of what
was instructed. It is not independent proof that every station followed the
instruction or that a particular December intercept uses a specified key.

The earlier [p189 C instruction](../context/p189_C.md), including the raw word
`IRRTUM`, remains a separate source. The new schedule does not establish what
the earlier “error” meant. It does provide a concrete reason to examine
November/December key reuse without changing the wording of either message.

## Source identity and dates

The [source crop](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/sources/childs_p211_selected.png)
is printed p211 / PDF p214. That page contains two different `B` labels under
different headings. This case concerns the **lower B**, following a new
**19 November 1918** heading:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
POT v NKJ (09.48 a.m., November 22d)
FUER POT COS VON LP SS DD 2230 3 TLE
1 TL: RICHI-214
2 TL: RICHI-184
3 TL: RICHI-134
```

</details>

The page heading, the 22 November receipt and the undated `2230` internal
time are all preserved. The later receipt does not justify relabelling the
published `Nov4-6` key, which directly decodes all three parts. These records
are locally named `p211_B_lower1`, `p211_B_lower2` and `p211_B_lower3` to avoid
confusing them with the upper B.

## Literal plaintext and exact repair costs

Part 1, 214 slots / 107 fixed plaintext positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
NOVEMBERXGINGBAHNSC7LUESSELNICHTVERNICHTENXNACHRCHEFX4XB848727XXDEZRMBERXRINGBAHNSCHLUESSELTRITTVORLAEUFIGX
```

</details>

The proposed `GINGBAHN→RINGBAHN`, `SC7LUESSEL→SCHLUESSEL` and
`DEZRMBER→DEZEMBER` each cost one known-coordinate substitution:
source indices **89: V→A**, **128: D→G** and **209: V→F**.
All other 211 coordinates stay unchanged.

Part 2, 184 slots / 92 fixed positions, needs no repair:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
NICHTINKRAFTXDAFUERSCHLUESSELERSTERDEZEMBERWIEZEHNTERNOVEMBERUSWBISEINUNDZWANZIGSTERDEZEMBER
```

</details>

Part 3, 134 slots / 66 of 67 fixed positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
WIEDREISSI?STERNOVEMBERXXEMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNGXXNACHRCHEFZ4XBX47857X
```

</details>

The printed `R` in `FRXXX` is outside the coordinate alphabet. Filling that
one slot, source index **16**, with `V` supplies the `G` in `DREISSIGSTER` and
preserves every one of the 133 valid coordinates. The three reconstructed
parts then re-encrypt exactly to the explicitly stated repaired witnesses.

The [p145 three-part witness](nov6_ringbahn_key_witnesses.md) now supplies
independent raw support for all four proposed p211 word repairs:
`RINGBAHN`, `SCHLUESSEL`, `DEZEMBER` and the `G` in `DREISSIGSTER`.
Conversely, p211's unedited second part supports p145's declared one-slot
restoration and three substitutions; the resulting ciphertexts match
exactly. The copies retain their differing headings, reception dates and
literal reference fields. The additional witness strengthens the
transmitted wording, without establishing compliance with the key schedule.

## Verify

The [source inputs](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/inputs.json)
and [certificates](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/certificates.json)
retain the three separate geometries, all source indices, invalid glyphs and
proposed repairs.

```sh
python3 experiments/open_targets_continuation/verify.py --verify
```

The source checks and readable edition are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

# Direct-current machines: a conditional fragment on p71 A2

[Evidence and verifier](../../experiments/p71_dc_machines_fragment/README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

A 47-position technical clause can be proposed for the interrupted second part on printed page 71 without changing an observed coordinate. It is a **conditional lexical reading**: all 43 surviving constraints in this span are half-pairs, four positions have no observed coordinate, and an equally compatible wording is retained below. The remaining 49 plaintext positions are unread.

## p71 A2

**Readable German — conditional proposal:**

> [Beide Gleichstrommaschinen sind in Reihe zu schalten.] […]

**Meaning under this proposal:** Both direct-current machines are to be connected in series. The ellipsis omits the unread remainder; it does not complete it.

The [first part under the same header](../caucasus/october_caucasus.md#p71-a1--electrical-equipment-sent-to-tiflis) concerns equipment dispatched to Tiflis, including two 16-kW machine sets and a converter. Its proposed 20-kW rating includes an erasure fill. That independently established subject matter prompted the compound `GLEICHSTROMMASCHINEN`, which was absent from the generic book lexicon used by the initial search. It supplies context rather than copied ciphertext or proof of this clause.

## Source and analysis frame

The page heading is `6th OCTOBER, 1918.` The receipt header is `A) POT v OSM (01.17 a.m., October 8th)`, followed by `FÜR COS (6) 1230 2 TEILE`. This is the separately labelled `2 TL`, `RICHI-192`; the date fields are retained without reconciling them.

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — all 85 observed coordinates:**

```text
DDAFG GVVVA XAGVD XVFVF VAFXF VGFAD FGFGG FVDDG
GAFDF VGDFV FVFFF DVVVD DGDVD FDGFF GFFGF DFAGX
VAFVF
```

</details>

The source prints `(interference)` immediately afterward. The analysis frame keeps these 85 coordinates as a prefix and appends 107 unobserved coordinate slots to reach the advertised 192. It excludes no source slot and contains no printed source mask. The [original-PDF reference](../../experiments/p71_dc_machines_fragment/inputs.json) fixes the scan hash, PDF page 74 and the exact crop recipe; no new image asset is published.

The complete published October 4–6 square and its 22-column rank order are used unchanged. George Lasry's published key and the separately credited key-recovery research remain identified in the evidence file.

## Raw output

Under that frame and key, **0/96 plaintext positions** are fixed by complete observed pairs.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — all 107 unobserved-tail slots unassigned:**

```text
????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????
```

</details>

These question marks retain different domains. Of the 96 positions, 85 have one observed coordinate and 11 have none. The certificate records every domain and each coordinate's source mapping; the display is not a claim that all positions have identical uncertainty.

## Conditional edited fragment

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — conditional lexical proposal; 0 observed substitutions and 51 added-slot fills; exactly 49 unresolved positions:**

```text
BEIDEGLEICHSTROMMASCHINENSINDINREIHEZUSCHALTENX?????????????????????????????????????????????????
```

</details>

This candidate requires **0 observed-coordinate substitutions, 0 source-mask fills and 51 fills of added unobserved-tail slots**. Its first 47 plaintext positions contain 43 one-coordinate observations and four wholly unobserved positions, at plaintext indices **8, 19, 30 and 41**. No position in this prefix is fixed by a native complete pair. The remaining 56 added coordinate slots stay unassigned.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — equally compatible ERHALTEN alternative; the same 0 observed substitutions and 51 added-slot fills:**

```text
BEIDEGLEICHSTROMMASCHINENSINDINREIHEZUERHALTENX?????????????????????????????????????????????????
```

</details>

`ZU ERHALTEN` has the same coordinate price as `ZU SCHALTEN`. The latter gives a coherent electrical instruction when the two machines are connected in series; this semantic preference does not establish unique transmitted wording. Other compatible strings remain possible. Neither candidate completes the unread tail.

## Verification and limits

The verifier reconstructs all domains, the 192-slot frame and the mapping of the 43 supporting observations, then checks all assigned candidate coordinates against the source, retaining the 42 observations outside the proposed prefix. Each candidate also has a complete source-retaining re-encryption witness whose arbitrary remaining values make no historical fill claim. It also checks the actual Markdown streams and readable quotation. Optional original-PDF verification renders the declared crop with `Matrix(4, 4)` and checks its pixel hash.

Same-mask controls for the generic word and character models did not recover their complete known messages. The present fragment therefore rests on a stated technical lexical proposal with an exact coordinate account, rather than a language-model score. No exhaustive historical uniqueness claim or first-decipherment claim is made.

Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**, preserving the earlier first-part edition and the separately credited published key work.

# p84 C — German field-post fragment

[All cases](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Recovery and review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 4 November 2026.**
A source-directed frame and corpus phrase search identify **Deutsche Feldpost**
in this interrupted reception. The unchanged October 28–31 key fixes **14/122
raw positions**; the conditional word layer fixes **28/122**, with no observed
coordinate changed. Most of the message remains unread.

## Reading

**Readable German — the conditional word fragment; all surrounding passages remain unresolved:**

> […] Deutsche Feldpost […]

**Meaning:** The fragment names the German field-post service. It does not yet
establish a postal address, a post-office number, or the purpose of the message.
The raw `9` and `7` labels elsewhere in the stream remain literal.

## Source and frame

Childs, printed p84 / PDF p87, gives `C) FUER COS (4.30 a.m., November 1st)`
and `1810 (30); RICHI-244`. The page heading is October 30, and the explicit
`(30)` dating agrees with the October 28–31 key used here. The reception ends
with the annotation **Balance jammed**.

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — all 118 printed slots, including seven dash masks and the four-character FDFG group:**

```text
AFDAX AXGFD GXAVV AXDVG DAADV VXAGX GDVAA AXGGX
AAAXA FXDDG DXXGX DFDVF FAXXX FXGGA AXGFG FDFG
DADDA AVAFV XGXAD AAAAX DVXAF XAXXG FA--- ----
```

</details>

The conditional frame inserts one unknown inside or immediately beside the
short group `FDFG`, then adds 125 unknown tail slots to reach the advertised
244. All **111 observations and seven printed masks** retain their source
identities, values and relative order. Nothing is excluded.

The missing short-group coordinate can occupy any of five positions, before
zero-based source indices 75–79. All five maps are retained. They have the
same 14 raw letters and the same word-layer price; other half-coordinate
domains differ. The primary map inserts before source 76, the leading score
in the length diagnostic. Its exact position is not established.

## Raw and edited output

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — common to all five 244-slot frames; 14/122 fixed positions; no coordinate substitutions or fills:**

```text
??9????????G????????U????????E????????R????????D????????E????????7????????S????????N????????M????????N????????E????????G??
```

**Edited output — DEUTSCHEFELDPOST at zero-based positions 47–62; zero observed substitutions, two printed-mask fills and 15 added-tail fills; 28/122 fixed positions:**

```text
??9????????G????????U????????E????????R????????DEUTSCHEFELDPOST??7????????S????????N????????M????????N????????E????????G??
```

</details>

The sixteen-letter proposal has **15 observed supporting coordinates**:
`D` at 47 and `E` at 56 are already fixed; eleven further letters retain one
observed half. Three letters are wholly absent and supplied by the word
hypothesis: **H at 53, F at 55, T at 62**. The inserted short-group slot itself
remains unknown. Ninety-four plaintext positions remain unresolved.

The proposal fits all five frames without changing a source observation.
Keeping the native prefix and placing all 126 added slots at the end instead
would require four observed substitutions for the same phrase at the same
position. That comparison is word-conditioned, not proof of a unique frame.

## Search and review

The length diagnostic tested **12,617 models**: eleven complete published
keys, every even total length from 118 to 500, and either no internal loss or
one loss inside `FDFG`. October 28–31 at the advertised 244 slots ranked first.
Four fresh source-shaped controls recovered all displayed letters while
sometimes preferring another loss position or nearby length.

A separate search compared every substring alignment in **331 strictly raw
corpus streams** against the target half-coordinate domains. Its sole phrase
with at least twelve letters and twelve observed supporting coordinates was
`XDEUTSCLEFELDPOST` from [p210 C](../people/richter_aleppo.md). The donor's raw
`L` is a known textual blemish; target position 53 has no observed half, so
**H is a lexical completion**, not a copied coordinate. This is a vocabulary
match, not evidence that the two telegrams repeat one another.

One hundred frequency-preserving shuffled sources were each searched across
all five frames and the full donor corpus. Their strongest matches had at
most eleven observed supporting coordinates, versus fifteen here. This
calibration is conditional on the already selected key and 244-slot family;
it does not account for earlier searches or prove the historical wording.

[Exact domains, fills and complete witnesses](../../experiments/p84_field_post_fragment/certificates.json)
· [Search controls and replay](../../experiments/p84_field_post_fragment/README.md).
Independent review checked the original PDF pixels, every source map, all
610 plaintext domains, the repair ledger and complete re-encryption. Residual
witness fills serve only to check the arithmetic.

## Credit

Historical source: J. Rives Childs. Published October 28–31 key: George Lasry,
Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and Lasry's 2017 key list.
Source-frame search, corpus retrieval and conditional edition:
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

# p84 C — Illness and a request to come

[Evidence and verifier](../../experiments/p84_mother_illness_fragment/README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)
· [Earlier field-post fragment](p84_field_post_fragment.md)

**Recovery and review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 4 November 2026.**
An additional conditional clause fits the interrupted p84 C reception:
**Mutter schwer krank. Bitte komm.** The combined conditional proposals assign **52/122
positions**, including the previously proposed *Deutsche Feldpost*, while
retaining every observed coordinate. The unchanged key and raw source frame
still fix **14/122** positions. Seventy positions remain unassigned under these proposals.

## Conditional reading

**Readable German — conditional lexical proposal; the surrounding passages remain unresolved:**

> […] Deutsche Feldpost […] [Mutter schwer krank. Bitte komm.] […]

**Meaning under this proposal:** A mother is seriously ill, and the recipient
is asked to come. The field-post fragment supplies a plausible setting for a
personal telegram. The relationship, destination and identities are not
established by the surviving text.

**Readable German — an equally compatible lexical counterexample:**

> […] Deutsche Feldpost […] [Mittelschwer krank. Bitte komm.] […]

This alternative means approximately “moderately ill; please come.” It changes
`MUTTER` to `MITTEL`, while retaining exactly the same coordinate prices in all
five frames. At position **69**, `U` and `I` share the observed half-coordinate;
position **73**, proposed as `R` or `L`, is wholly absent. The family-message
interpretation is a contextual preference, not a unique recovery of `MUTTER`.

## Source and retained frames

Childs, printed p84 / PDF p87, labels the reception
`C) FUER COS (4.30 a.m., November 1st)` and `1810 (30); RICHI-244`.
The page heading is October 30. The source ends with **Balance jammed**.

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — all 118 printed slots; seven dash masks and the short FDFG group retained:**

```text
AFDAX AXGFD GXAVV AXDVG DAADV VXAGX GDVAA AXGGX
AAAXA FXDDG DXXGX DFDVF FAXXX FXGGA AXGFG FDFG
DADDA AVAFV XGXAD AAAAX DVXAF XAXXG FA--- ----
```

</details>

As in the earlier edition, one unobserved slot is inserted inside or beside
the four-character `FDFG` group, before source index **75, 76, 77, 78 or 79**.
Another 125 unobserved slots supply the interrupted tail and reach the
advertised 244. All 111 observed symbols and seven printed masks retain
their source identities and relative order. The published October 28–31
square and 18-column rank order are unchanged.

The new clause favors three of those existing frames without changing an
observation. The table includes the previous field-post words and the new
clause; it applies equally to the `MUTTER` and `MITTEL` alternatives.

| Insert before source index | Observed substitutions | Printed-mask fills | Added-slot fills | Observed coordinates supporting the new 27-position span |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 75 | 2 | 5 | 43 | 23 |
| 76 | 1 | 5 | 43 | 23 |
| 77 | 0 | 5 | 43 | 23 |
| 78 | 0 | 5 | 42 | 24 |
| 79 | 0 | 5 | 42 | 24 |

Frame **78** is the representative edition. Frame **79** has the same minimum
price; frame **77** also fits without an observed substitution. These are
word-conditioned comparisons. They do not establish the historical loss
position. Frames 75 and 76 remain explicit counterfactual comparisons; their
substitutions are not adopted as source corrections.

## Raw and edited outputs

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — common to all five frames; 14/122 fixed positions; no fills or observed substitutions:**

```text
??9????????G????????U????????E????????R????????D????????E????????7????????S????????N????????M????????N????????E????????G??
```

**Edited output — conditional MUTTER proposal in frame 78; 0 observed substitutions, 5 printed-mask fills and 42 added-slot fills; 52/122 fixed positions:**

```text
??9????????G????????U????????E????????R????????DEUTSCHEFELDPOST??7??MUTTERSCHWERKRANKBITTEKOMMX??????N????????E????????G??
```

**Edited output — equally compatible MITTEL counterexample; the same 0 substitutions, 5 printed-mask fills and 42 added-slot fills:**

```text
??9????????G????????U????????E????????R????????DEUTSCHEFELDPOST??7??MITTELSCHWERKRANKBITTEKOMMX??????N????????E????????G??
```

</details>

The new string occupies zero-based positions **68–94**. In frames 78 and 79,
it retains **24 observed supporting coordinates**: `S` at 74, `N` at 83 and
`M` at 92 are already fixed by complete pairs; eighteen further positions
retain one observed half. Six positions are wholly absent and supplied by
the lexical proposal: **T71, R73, K80, A82, E89 and O91**. The counterexample
supplies `L73` instead of `R73`. The final `X94` is a compatible proposed
separator with one observed half.

Compared with the previous 28-position edition, this adds **24 proposed
positions**, costing **three further printed-mask fills and 27 further
added-slot fills** in either minimum-price frame. The `9` and `7` labels in
the surrounding text stay literal and are not expanded into a post-office
number. The text after the proposed separator is unresolved.

## Discovery, verification and limits

A scan of the unchanged half-coordinate domains located the independent-book
words `MUTTER` or `MITTEL` at 68, `SCHWER` at 74, `KRANK` at 80 and `BITTE`
at 85. Examining the other retained frames then permitted `KOMM` at 90.
All five proposed words and the `MITTEL` counterexample occur in the existing
hash-pinned 53,465-word lexicon built from ten German books. Their composition
into the clause and the preference for a family message are editorial
judgments. No independent native ciphertext donor or authenticated repeat
of this clause has been identified.

The earlier `DEUTSCHEFELDPOST` corpus match, its discovery and its source
controls remain credited in the [previous edition](p84_field_post_fragment.md).
Those controls do not validate the newly composed clause. No corrected
statistical significance or exhaustive historical uniqueness is claimed.

The new verifier reconstructs the grid, all five source maps, every marginal
letter domain, both word alternatives and each separate repair ledger. It
checks that the three zero-substitution candidates retain all 111 observations,
then re-encrypts complete witnesses under one unchanged global square.
Arbitrary values in unassigned witness slots are not proposed historical
text. Optional PDF verification authenticates the original scan and the
declared crop pixels; no new image asset is required.

Historical source: **J. Rives Childs**. Published key: **George Lasry, Ingo
Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016)** and **Lasry's 2017 key list**.
Earlier fragment and new lexical extension: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

# p85 B — Telephone censorship through Budapest

[Case guide](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Source image](../../sources/excerpts/other_p85_B.png) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** A source-reviewed supplementary message. The unchanged published
`Oct28-31` key fixes **all 99 raw plaintext positions** in the 198-coordinate
source. The likely wording below corrects two raw characters and one spelling
omission; those changes are distinguished from the direct decryption.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> Fernsprechverbindung ueber [Budapest] unterli[e]gt ungarischer Censur.
> Verbindung daher nur mit [Funkspruch] moeglich.

**Meaning:** The telephone connection through Budapest is subject to Hungarian
censorship. Communication is therefore possible only by radio message.

The brackets mark editorial repairs. `BUD9PEST` most likely means Budapest,
and `FUPKSPRUCH` most likely means *Funkspruch*. Both replacements have an exact
coordinate audit below. The inserted `e` in *unterliegt* repairs the raw
`UNTERLIGT`; it is a spelling restoration, not an additional decrypted letter.
`Censur` is retained as the source's spelling. Spacing and punctuation are
editorial; the single `X` separates the two clauses.

## What the source actually yields

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FERNSPRECHVERBINDUNGUEBERBUD9PESTUNTERLIGTUNGARISCHERCENSURXVERBINDUNGDAHERNURMITFUPKSPRUCHMOEGLICH
```

</details>

All coordinates are legible and valid. This complete raw string re-encrypts
to the unchanged source. A same-length candidate correcting Budapest and
Funkspruch, while retaining `UNTERLIGT`, requires exactly these two changes:

| Source index, zero based | Printed | Proposed | Reading affected |
| ---: | :---: | :---: | --- |
| 53 | G | X | `FUPKSPRUCH` → `FUNKSPRUCH` |
| 168 | A | V | `BUD9PEST` → `BUDAPEST` |

The other **196 coordinates remain unchanged**. No coordinate is inserted,
deleted or supplied from an erasure, and no square cell is changed. This
same-length certificate does not include the extra editorial `e` in
*unterliegt*.

## Source and verification

Printed p85 / PDF p88, section B. The page heading is **30 October 1918**;
the reception header is `LP v OSM (9.42 p.m., October 31st)`, followed by
`(30) ZU 1500 UKS; RICHI-198`. These distinct dates are preserved.

The [source record](../../experiments/corpus_readings/selected_sources.json)
contains the literal grouped transcript. The
[coordinate certificate](../../experiments/corpus_readings/certificates.json)
records every plaintext position, its two source coordinates, the unchanged
key and the complete repair map.

```sh
python3 experiments/corpus_readings/verify.py --verify
```

**Credit:** George Lasry's published period key and its historical sources are
retained in [the key register](../../data/keys.json). Source inspection,
verification and this annotated reading are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.
No first-decipherment priority is claimed for this supplementary message.

# Radio contact, operating times and an unavailable key

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

These four independent records describe a broken wire connection, timed
radio calls, an embassy receiving station and the local absence of an
`OSKACHI` key. They use unchanged previously published keys and complete
source frames. They are grouped by subject, not asserted to be one exchange.

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [collected intercepts](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [inputs](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/inputs.json) and
[certificates](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/certificates.json)
retain exact source rows, headers, key provenance, image hashes, raw readings
and all local repairs. Printed page numbers are three less than PDF page numbers.

## p100 C: direct contact while the wire is broken

The [source](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p100_C.png)
is under a November 1 heading, with this November 2 reception line:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
C) UKS v ZÖN (2.03 a.m., November 2nd)
2235 (1) AN LP
RIZI-158
```

</details>

All 158 coordinates give 79 fixed plaintext labels under `Nov1-3`, without
any repair:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
WANNISTUNMITTELBARERVERKEHRMITEUCHXMUENCHENODERBRSLAUMEGLICHXDRAHTUNTERBROCHENX
```

</details>

The sender asks when direct communication with the recipient, Munich or
the place written `BRSLAU` will be possible, and says the wire connection
is interrupted. `BRSLAU` is naturally read as Breslau and `MEGLICH` as a
damaged spelling of *möglich*, but **both remain literal in the certificate**.
No missing plaintext letters are inserted. The separately printed
[p100 B](../military/budapest_wire_break.md) gives a longer wire-break report;
this does not by itself prove a single transmission or a specific route.

This is distinct from the [p100 challenge](../p100.md), whose earlier
Belgrade body remains credited to Armin.

## p137 D: the OSKACHI key is no longer here

The [source](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p137_D.png)
has `RIZI-102`. Its upper sender initial is overprinted, so the header is
conservatively retained as:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
D) ?CO V OSM (1.55 November 5th,)
RIZI-102
NF NRO V OSM
```

</details>

The page heading is November 6. Neither it nor the footer is used to resolve
the unclear upper callsign or the time's missing a.m./p.m. designation.
The two dots after the final cipher group `AX` are punctuation; the footer
is outside the 102-coordinate body.

All 51 raw plaintext positions are fixed under `Nov4-6`:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
POTSAGENDA3SSCHLUESSELOSKACHIHIERNICHTMEHRVORHANDEN
```

</details>

One observed-coordinate substitution, source **79: G→X**, changes the `3`
inside `DA3S` to `S`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
POTSAGENDASSSCHLUESSELOSKACHIHIERNICHTMEHRVORHANDEN
```

</details>

Readable German:

**Readable German:**

> POT sagen, dass Schlüssel OSKACHI hier nicht mehr vorhanden.

It asks that POT be told the `OSKACHI` key is no longer available here.
The key name itself is unchanged. The message does **not** say why it is
unavailable, identify a specific square or rank order, give its operating
period, or connect it to a separate challenge ciphertext. Its presence
inside a telegram decoded with `Nov4-6` does not make `OSKACHI` another name
for that transport key.

The raw numeral `3` remains visible in the original reading and numerical
ledger. Its local word repair does not reassign the square's digit `3`.

## p142 A: 0430 calling signal, then listen again at 0645

The [source](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p142_A.png)
is headed November 6:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) NKJ ZÖN v LP (08.25 p.m., November 6th)
FUER ZÖN 1900 (6/11)
RIZI-128
```

</details>

All 128 coordinates and 64 plaintext labels are fixed under `Nov4-6`, with
no substitutions or fills:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
GEBENSIEX0430X10XMINXVVVXDANNIHREFKSPRUNDHOERENSIEUNSWIEDERX0645
```

</details>

The instruction is to send **10 minutes of `VVV` at 0430**, then the
recipient's radiograms (`FKSPR`), and listen again at **0645**. All three
numerical fields are literal published-square readings. No extra day or
time zone is inferred from the evening reception time.

## p150 A2: receiving station in the embassy

The [source](../../experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/sources/childs_p150_A2.png)
explicitly labels this **part 2**. Its first part has not been attached or
reconstructed in this edition:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) LP v NKJ (8.55 p.m., November 7th)
PERA OSMAINE 6/11
FUER EILKESE ZU SS D (5) 2200
2 TL RICHI-180
UMGEHEND WEITERGEBEN
```

</details>

The page heading is November 6. The literal `OSMAINE` and `EILKESE` spellings
and the November 7 reception remain unchanged. The instruction separator
before `UMGEHEND WEITERGEBEN` is outside the ciphertext.

The 180-slot source contains one dash and gives 89 fixed labels out of 90
under `Nov4-6`:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
JEDOCHHOERTEMPEGSSTMTXINBOTSCHAFTAUFEUCHXNAMEXQZXXADT?SSENCHIFFRITENXINMLLENPERIDENANRUFEN
```

</details>

Six known-coordinate substitutions and one dash fill give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
JEDOCHHOERTEMPFGSSTATXINBOTSCHAFTAUFEUCHXNAMEXQZXXADRESSENCHIFFRIRENXINALLENPERIDENANRUFEN
```

</details>

The receiving station (`EMPFGSSTAT`) in the embassy listens for the
recipient. The message supplies the literal name/separator field
`NAMEXQZXX`, asks for addresses to be enciphered, and says to call in every
period. **The precise name boundary within `QZXX` is left unresolved.**
`CHIFFRIREN` and `PERIDEN` remain literal spellings; no extra plaintext
letters are claimed. The opening `JEDOCH` is retained rather than inventing
the missing preceding clause.

Known-coordinate changes, all at zero-based source indices:
**23 X→V, 80 X→V, 86 F→A, 92 X→V, 150 A→V, 167 X→V**.
The separate printed-dash fill is **112 ?→A**. Two of those substitutions
jointly change one raw `E` to `F` in `EMPFGSSTAT`; the certificate does not
collapse their cost into a single coordinate repair.

## Verify and prior credit

```sh
python experiments/radio_contacts_and_keys/verify.py --verify
```

The independent standard-library verifier rebuilds every source witness,
checks raw domains and numerical fields, and prices substitutions separately
from source-dash fills. No source coordinate is inserted or removed and no
published square is changed. Re-encryption confirms this stated arithmetic,
not the unique history of a damaged word or the identities of station names.

The keys are prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno
Wacker**, [DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
also published in George Lasry's [2017-02-24 comment 4](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1).
Earlier unreviewed OCR-derived candidates existed. The bounded author-paper
check found no explicit examples of these bodies; it does not establish
universal first-decipherment priority.

# Radio apparatus sale and estimated value

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

The two source parts concern permission to sell apparatus and an estimated value of 80 to 90 percent. The conditional reading below supplies the first part’s 21600 field; the abbreviations, 380L and 170M remain literal.

Source: Childs, printed pp.160–161 (PDF pp.163–164). [Source images and inputs](../../experiments/nov8_radio_keys_and_reports/inputs.json), [certificates](../../experiments/nov8_radio_keys_and_reports/certificates.json), [method and limitations](../../experiments/nov8_radio_keys_and_reports/README.md). All indices below are zero-based.

## Conditional digit reading

The [cross-period reference comparison](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) supports **21600** for the first part’s `21?00` field. This conditional digit interpretation adds no source edit and supplies no currency or punctuation; the opposite square gives 21500.

The same shared assignment changes the second part’s reference from `111?0?` to **`111?05`**, giving **41/42** fixed labels with no new source edit; the opposite square gives `111?06`. Its earlier question mark still depends on the invalid printed B at source 83. The selected domain there is **3458PV**, so neither a unique digit nor a complete reference is established.

## p160 B1

Header: `B) NKJ v LP (06.32 a.m., November 9th); FUER UKS (8/11) 2000 2 TLE; 1 TL; RICHI-282`.

Native 282. AVVGD is read VV, not WW. Apparate/price abbreviations, 380L, 170M and 21?00 remain literal; no currency or amount normalization.

The source has **282 slots** (282 valid coordinates). The native model has 282 slots / 141 plaintext positions: 140 fixed raw, 140 fixed after the stated edits.

**Cost:** 1 observed-coordinate substitution; 0 printed-mask fills; 0 observed-coordinate exclusions; 0 mask exclusions; no inserted coordinates.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — native source frame:

```text
0KONACHX18DZU1A11023XAPPARATEVERKGENEHMVERKFSPREISSIEMENSX21?00FERNSCHREIBERX380LXTISCHGEHAEUSEX170MXXHIERVONZEITWERTNACHSCHAETZGXANRECHNENXX
```

**Edited output** — changes and source offsets are enumerated in the certificate:

```text
AKONACHX18DZU1A11023XAPPARATEVERKGENEHMVERKFSPREISSIEMENSX21?00FERNSCHREIBERX380LXTISCHGEHAEUSEX170MXXHIERVONZEITWERTNACHSCHAETZGXANRECHNENXX
```

</details>

**Readable German** — spacing, case, punctuation and conventional umlaut rendering only; all non-`X` labels match the edited output:

> Akonach. 18 D zu 1 A 11023. Apparateverk genehm. Verkfspreis Siemens. 21?00 Fernschreiber. 380 L. Tischgehäuse. 170 M. Hiervon Zeitwert nach Schätzg anrechnen.

## p160 B2

Header: `Same p160 B header; 2 TL; RICHI-84`.

Native 84 includes printed C at 8 and B at 83, both represented as source masks. C8 is filled; B83 remains unresolved.

The source has **84 slots** (82 valid coordinates). The native model has 84 slots / 42 plaintext positions: 39 fixed raw, 40 fixed after the stated edits.

**Cost:** 0 observed-coordinate substitutions; 1 printed-mask fill; 0 observed-coordinate exclusions; 0 mask exclusions; no inserted coordinates.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — native source frame:

```text
VERMU?LICH80BIS90PROZENTXNACHCHEF3C111?0?X
```

**Edited output** — changes and source offsets are enumerated in the certificate:

```text
VERMUTLICH80BIS90PROZENTXNACHCHEF3C111?0?X
```

</details>

**Readable German** — spacing, case, punctuation and conventional umlaut rendering only; all non-`X` labels match the edited output:

> Vermutlich 80 bis 90 Prozent. Nach Chef 3 C 111?0?.

## Shared uncertainty and credit

The two missing square cells `VF` and `XA` jointly contain `5` and `6`. Both complete assignments are retained as compatibility witnesses; every occurrence of a cell shares the same digit. The displayed `?` positions therefore must not be treated as independent digit choices. In p160 B2 one additional source coordinate remains unfilled; its domain can include letters as well as digits.

The published Nov7–9 period key and earlier OCR candidates are credited in the inputs. This edition adds source inspection, separate repair costs and exact readable-text mappings. It does not claim new recovery of the period key.

cases/radio/radio_traffic_transfer_fragm.text:
# A radio-traffic transfer in a surviving second part

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

A surviving second part reports that DNZW takes over radio traffic and gives further call-name and place-like fields. The source expressly marks the first part missing. The repeated location identifies Grosswardein. One additional coordinate correction completes its opening spelling; the second occurrence keeps GROSSVARDEIN. The date and SCHWERE field retain two coupled readings.

## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p226 excerpt](../../experiments/radio_traffic_transfer_fragment/sources/p226_reviewed.png) · [Inputs](../../experiments/radio_traffic_transfer_fragment/inputs.json) · [Position and change certificates](../../experiments/radio_traffic_transfer_fragment/certificates.json)

The published `Nov28-Dec1` key is unchanged. [Original OCR records](../../experiments/radio_traffic_transfer_fragment/ocr_snapshot.json) and [reproducible comparisons with that earlier evidence](../../experiments/radio_traffic_transfer_fragment/prior_candidates.json) are preserved separately. The present edition supplies checked source framing, exact costs and readable passages; it makes no first-public-decipherment claim.

The earlier word edition has the following account; the place completion is
priced separately below.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [p226 A2](#p226-a2) | 186 | 89 / 93 | 1 | 3 |

## p226 A2

**Source transcription — header:** `A) BSL v UKS (10.27 p.m., November 30th); 1700 (11/29); (1st Tl Missing); 2 TL RICHI-186`

### A date and station field that must be read together

The [shared late-November interpretation](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/README.md)
leaves only **4/5** interchangeable. The opening `?DEZ` has the pair `F?`;
if it denotes a December day, either surviving square requires the missing
coordinate at source position 23 to be `X`. This adds **one mask fill** to
the earlier edition, giving **1 observed substitution and 4 fills**, while
leaving the day unresolved. The adjacent `SCHWERE1?` field uses the other
4/5 cell. A separate station notice on [p230 C](nov30_radio_personnel.md#p230-c)
uses that same cell for its hour.

| Opening date, if calendrical | `SCHWERE` field | p230 C hour |
|---|---|---|
| **4 December** | **15** | **5** |
| **5 December** | **14** | **4** |

Both assignments survive. The November transmission and interception
dates do not choose between them. The first place field becomes
`GROSSW7RDEIN`, still damaged; the second remains `GROSSVARDEIN`.
[Exact coordinate and branch check](../../experiments/late_november_calendar_and_units/traffic_certificate.json).

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
?DEZGROSSW0RDEINYYDNZWUEBERNIMMTVERKAHRFUEROKMSCHWEREX9RUFZYNATANADOLFUR?UL?YINGRO?SVARDEINYY
```

**Edited output — 1 observed-coordinate substitution and 3 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
?DEZGROSSW0RDEINYYDNZWUEBERNIMMTVERKEHRFUEROKMSCHWEREX9RUFZYNATANADOLFURSULAYINGROSSVARDEINYY
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> ?DEZ GROSSW0RDEIN. DNZW uebernimmt Verkehr fuer OKM SCHWEREX9 RUFZ: Natan Adolf Ursula in GROSSVARDEIN.

**Meaning:** The surviving second part states that DNZW takes over communications traffic for OKM, followed by the literal field SCHWEREX9 and RUFZ, then the proposed spoken-name sequence Natan Adolf Ursula and a place-like label. RUFZ may abbreviate Rufzeichen, or call sign. The missing first part and the exact identity of DNZW, the station and the location are not reconstructed.

**Editorial limits.**

- The source explicitly says the first part is missing. This is an edition of the complete native 186-slot second part, not a reconstruction of the missing first part.
- Four printed dashes remain occupied source positions. The earlier edition fills three in UR?UL? and GRO?SVARDEIN. The optional date interpretation above fills the fourth; its value remains 4/5 under the shared square.
- The only observed-coordinate word change is VERKAHR to VERKEHR. Natan Adolf Ursula is an explicit source-mask completion proposal, not an independently identified person or station.
- GROSSW0RDEIN keeps the numeral 0 and W in the first place-like field; GROSSVARDEIN keeps V in the second. Neither field is silently normalized to a modern or historical place name.
- Without the calendar interpretation, the opening shared-square domain is `{4, 5, D, I, J, N, U}`.
- Y is the separator label. X and 9 inside SCHWEREX9 remain literal; DNZW and RUFZ are not expanded in the exact readable quotation.

## The repeated place: Grosswardein

The opening `GROSSW0RDEIN` and closing `GROSSVARDEIN` identify the same
place with different V/W spellings. The second field's A is an unchanged
`VD` pair at source positions **57 and 149**. Applying that letter to the
opening field changes source **81 G→D**, turning its `VG` into `VD` and
giving **GROSSWARDEIN**. The original G is clearly printed: this is an
editorial repair, with no additional fill or key assignment.

The [3 August 1913 *Bácskaer Volkszeitung*, PDF p2](https://epa.oszk.hu/05600/05686/00377/pdf/EPA05686_bacskaer_volkszeitung_1913_031.pdf#page=2)
independently prints **Großwardein**. Its spelling supports the location;
the second cipher occurrence remains **Grossvardein** in the quotation.

**Conditional interpretation — readable German; the two calendar branches are paired in order:**

> {4/5}. Dez., Grosswardein. DNZW uebernimmt Verkehr fuer OKM, schwere {15/14}. Rufz.: Natan Adolf Ursula in Grossvardein.

The notice announces a transfer of radio traffic to DNZW at Grosswardein
and gives the spoken call-name sequence Natan Adolf Ursula. Reading the
opening as **4 December** gives **SCHWERE 15**; **5 December** gives
**SCHWERE 14**. Neither the place comparison nor the calendar selects
between them. The missing first part is still absent.

The complete proposal costs **two observed substitutions and four mask fills**:
VERKAHR→VERKEHR, the new place-letter repair, the three earlier word fills
and the earlier calendar fill. Both complete square branches re-encrypt
exactly; **91/93 positions** agree between them. Without the calendar
assumption, the place repair costs two substitutions and three fills in total,
with **92/93 baseline labels** fixed. This recovers a readable place word;
it does not increase the fixed-label count.

[Exact source comparison, retained branches and historical provenance](../../experiments/late_place_comparison/README.md).

## Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates independently reconstruct column positions and domains, compare them with the cipher implementation, replay every priced change, and check all readable nonseparator labels. Partial readings have one consistent injective square/source-mask completion witness that re-encrypts exactly; those witness choices are not historical identifications. Source images are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/radio_traffic_transfer_fragment/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to check the original PDF and exact source-crop pixels.

# An expected return and an attempt to obtain a vehicle

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Two complete short native bodies report an expected return and discuss obtaining a vehicle. The first is unchanged; the second has four explicitly priced coordinate substitutions. The incomplete spelling RUECKUNFT, the literal 0100 field and the elliptical sense of VERSUCHEN remain visible.


**Reviewed source crops:** [p182_reviewed.png](../../experiments/return_time_and_vehicle_attempt/sources/p182_reviewed.png) · [p189_reviewed.png](../../experiments/return_time_and_vehicle_attempt/sources/p189_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).
## Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p182 excerpt — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/return_time_and_vehicle_attempt/inputs.json) · [Reviewed p189 excerpt — source-PDF reference](../../experiments/return_time_and_vehicle_attempt/inputs.json) · [Inputs](../../experiments/return_time_and_vehicle_attempt/inputs.json) · [Position and change certificates](../../experiments/return_time_and_vehicle_attempt/certificates.json)
