[Original OCR records](../../experiments/return_time_and_vehicle_attempt/ocr_snapshot.json) and [reproducible comparisons with that earlier evidence](../../experiments/return_time_and_vehicle_attempt/prior_candidates.json) are preserved separately. The present edition supplies checked source framing, exact costs and readable passages; it makes no first-public-decipherment claim.

| Record | Source slots | Fixed raw positions | Observed substitutions | Source-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [p182 B](#p182-b) | 62 | 31 / 31 | 0 | 0 |
| [p189 B](#p189-b) | 70 | 35 / 35 | 4 | 0 |

## p182 B

**Source transcription — header:** `B) CM v CZ (20.45 p.m., November 12th); 20.20; RIZI-62`

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
RUECKUNFTVORAUSSICHTLICH0100XSX
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the unchanged raw output:**

> RUECKUNFT voraussichtlich 0100. S.

**Meaning:** The sender reports an expected return at the literal label 0100. The closing S is not expanded, and this record does not itself identify the returning person or establish a complete itinerary.

**Editorial limits.**

- All 62 printed coordinates decode directly, with no source erasures, substitutions or frame changes. The following CM UM is printed transmission control outside the body.
- RUECKUNFT is retained with only the one K visible in the decoded stream; the standard spelling Rueckkunft would require an extra plaintext letter and is not silently inserted.
- 0100 is preserved as four literal labels. Its interpretation as a time is contextual; the body does not specify a time zone or independently identify the date.
- The neighboring Seifert service exchange does not establish that the abbreviated S here is a particular person.

## p189 B

**Source transcription — header:** `B) CM v CZ (10.10 a.m., November 14th); RIZI-70`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
VERSUCHENI6GENDECNEIWWGENZUBEKOMMEN
```

**Edited output — 4 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
VERSUCHENIRGENDEINENWAGENZUBEKOMMEN
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Versuchen, irgendeinen Wagen zu bekommen.

**Meaning:** The message concerns trying to obtain a vehicle or wagon. The terse infinitive form alone does not securely distinguish a request to try from a report of an attempt, and Wagen does not by itself identify a specific car or railway wagon.

**Editorial limits.**

- All 70 native coordinates are retained and valid. High-resolution inspection reads the last group of the first row as FGXAV, including a clear X; the earlier low-resolution Y-like impression is not retained as a fictitious source erasure.
- The ordinary-word proposal costs four observed-coordinate substitutions. The literal 6 in I6GENDE… is changed only through an explicit coordinate repair, not through a global reinterpretation of the numeral label.
- The edition does not identify a vehicle, promise that one was obtained, or infer a connection to another service message merely from the word Wagen.

## Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

Partial readings have one consistent injective square/source-mask completion witness that re-encrypts exactly; those witness choices are not historical identifications. # Equipment transfer east of the Rhine, with radio service maintained

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source recovery and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This order directs equipment identified by the unexpanded label **`U.S.`**
to the nearest replacement unit east of the Rhine. It also requires wireless
station operation to be maintained. `U.S.` is preserved as a source label;
the text does not establish an American origin or a particular equipment type.

The source is Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
[printed p179 A, PDF p182](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view),
with this [visible header and ciphertext](../../experiments/november_armistice_orders/sources/p179_A.png):

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) KS CZ FG v XF (20.07, November 11th)
RICHI-266
```

</details>

## Conditional shared digits

The equipment order gains the complete reference **4B49936**, fixing **133/133 labels**. Its existing five-coordinate printed cancellation and seven word substitutions retain their separate costs. The [joint reconstruction](../../experiments/nov10_joint_completion/README.md) combines the earlier Marineamt and formation interpretations with the army-number constraint and the mobilization decree; the reversed 7/9 assignment is retained there.

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the joint square:**

> Dort befind. U S Geraete zur naechsten rechtsrhein. Ers. Abtlg. schaffen. Funkstellenbetrieb muss aufrechterhalten bleiben. Nachrichtenchef 4B49936.

<details>
<summary>Exact conditional labels</summary>

**Edited output — p179_A, conditional shared square; 133/133 fixed positions:**

```text
DORTBEFINDXUXSXGERAETEZURNAECHSTENRECHTSRHEINXERSXABTLGXSCHAFFENXFUNKSTELLENBETRIEBMUSSAUFRECHTERHALTENBLEIBENXNACHRICHTENCHEF4B49936
```

</details>


## A cancelled duplicate restores the printed frame length

The literal transcription contains **271 coordinates**. Source group 17,
at zero-based positions **80–84**, is visibly struck through. It reads
`ADADG`, exactly duplicating the immediately preceding group. Excluding the
marked copy gives the advertised **266-coordinate frame**.

The cancelled group remains in the literal transcript and in the source
image. Its exclusion counts as **five observed coordinates removed at the
printed cancellation**. It is not reported as a zero-edit source. A close
view of the damaged but readable `X` at source position 190 is also
[preserved](../../experiments/november_armistice_orders/sources/p179_A_glyph.png).

Under the unchanged published Nov10–12 square and ranks, the resulting raw
reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — frame excluding the visibly cancelled duplicate group; exclusion priced separately:**

```text
DORTBEFINDXUXSXGERAETEZURNAECHSTENRECHTSRHEINXERSXABTLGXOCHAFKENXFU?OSTELLENB2TRIEBMUSSAUFRECHTERHA?TENBLEIBENXNACHRICHTENC0EF4B4??3?
```

</details>

Seven separately recorded observed-coordinate substitutions give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same cancelled-group frame, followed by seven word repairs:**

```text
DORTBEFINDXUXSXGERAETEZURNAECHSTENRECHTSRHEINXERSXABTLGXSCHAFFENXFUNKSTELLENBETRIEBMUSSAUFRECHTERHALTENBLEIBENXNACHRICHTENCHEF4B4??3?
```

</details>

A readable expansion, with abbreviation completions in brackets, is:

**Readable German — after the cancelled-group exclusion and priced word repairs:**

> Dort befind[liche] U.S.-Geräte zur nächsten rechtsrhein[ischen]
> Ers[atz]abtlg. schaffen. Funkstellenbetrieb muss aufrechterhalten
> bleiben. Nachrichtenchef `4B4??3?`.

The three question marks in the closing `4B4??3?` are retained. They arise
from unassigned cells in the published partial square, not missing source
coordinates. The two ordinary-word question marks in the raw reading are
also partial-key outcomes; their editorial repairs change observed
coordinates, rather than filling the key with new letters.

The abbreviation `ABTLG` already includes its final G. The readable display
therefore retains that letter outside editorial brackets and preserves the
entire closing reference, including its fixed labels and three unknowns.

| Literal source slots | Analysis-frame slots | Raw fixed labels | Edition fixed labels | Observed coordinates excluded | Known-coordinate substitutions | Erasure fills |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 271 | 266 | 128 / 133 | 130 / 133 | 5 | 7 | 0 |

There are no added coordinates, block moves or baseline-key changes.
The [inputs](../../experiments/november_armistice_orders/inputs.json) and
[certificate](../../experiments/november_armistice_orders/certificates.json)
preserve both duplicate groups, the exact exclusion, every substitution,
raw domains and global re-encryption witnesses. Arbitrary completions are
marked as consistency examples, not original numerical readings.

The period key is credited to **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**. The previous unreviewed OCR stream did not yield this coherent
body. The new contribution is the source reading and priced edition;
the bounded publication check is recorded without a universal priority claim.

The other source records on this page are covered in the
[armistice and leave case](../military/armistice_and_leave_orders.md).

```sh
python experiments/november_armistice_orders/verify.py --verify
```

# November Ringbahn keys and postponed December change

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

The edited first part says to retain the November Ringbahn key and postpone the December key. Its wording continues into the unedited second part: 1 December is to use the key as on the tenth of November, continuing through 21 December as on 30 November. These are literal instructions in the traffic; they do not independently recover the secret key material or verify that the instruction was followed.

Source: Childs, printed pp.160–161 (PDF pp.163–164). [Source images and inputs](../../experiments/nov8_radio_keys_and_reports/inputs.json), [certificates](../../experiments/nov8_radio_keys_and_reports/certificates.json), [method and limitations](../../experiments/nov8_radio_keys_and_reports/README.md). All indices below are zero-based.

## Conditional digit reading

The [shared Nov7–9 digit interpretation](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) gives **Nach Chef 4 B 49859** in part 2, at no additional source edit or fill. The opposite square gives 49869; the date schedule itself is unchanged.

## p160 C1

Header: `C) NKJ v LP (03.23 a.m., November 9th); FUER RAT 2000 (8/11) 2 TLE; 1 TL; RICHI-308`.

Literal 309 versus advertised 308. FAGVGD is a six-character group at 280–285; the primary conditional frame excludes 281. Source dashes 304/305 remain separately priced fills.

The source has **309 slots** (307 valid coordinates). The conditional model has 308 slots / 154 plaintext positions: 152 fixed raw, 154 fixed after the stated edits.

**Cost:** 4 observed-coordinate substitutions; 2 printed-mask fills; 1 observed-coordinate exclusion; 0 mask exclusions; no inserted coordinates.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — under the explicitly conditional exclusion frame:

```text
NOVEMBERXRINGBAHNSCHLVESSELNICHTVERN9CHTENXNACHXCHEFX4XBX48929XDEZEMBERXRINGBAFNSCHLUESSELTRITTVORLAEUFIGNIC?TINKRAFTX?AFUERSCHLUESSEL1XDEZEMBERWIEZEHNTER
```

**Edited output** — changes and source offsets are enumerated in the certificate:

```text
NOVEMBERXRINGBAHNSCHLUESSELNICHTVERNICHTENXNACHXCHEFX4XBX48929XDEZEMBERXRINGBAHNSCHLUESSELTRITTVORLAEUFIGNICHTINKRAFTXDAFUERSCHLUESSEL1XDEZEMBERWIEZEHNTER
```

</details>

**Readable German** — spacing, case, punctuation and conventional umlaut rendering only; all non-`X` labels match the edited output:

> November Ringbahnschlüssel nicht vernichten. Nach Chef 4 B 48929. Dezember Ringbahnschlüssel tritt vorläufig nicht in Kraft. Dafür Schlüssel 1. Dezember wie zehnter

## p160 C2

Header: `Same p160 C header; 2 TL; RICHI-144`.

Native 144. The cleartext footer NF NKJ v LP UM follows the cipher body and is not encrypted input. The date relationship continues the preceding ZEHNTER word without changing its letters.

The source has **144 slots** (144 valid coordinates). The native model has 144 slots / 72 plaintext positions: 71 fixed raw, 71 fixed after the stated edits.

**Cost:** 0 observed-coordinate substitutions; 0 printed-mask fills; 0 observed-coordinate exclusions; 0 mask exclusions; no inserted coordinates.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output** — native source frame:

```text
NOVEMBERUSWXBIS21XDEZEMBERWIE30XNOVEMBERXEMPFANGSBESTGXXNACHCHEF4B498?9X
```

</details>

**Readable German** — spacing, case, punctuation and conventional umlaut rendering only; all non-`X` labels match the edited output:

> November usw. bis 21. Dezember wie 30. November. Empfangsbestg. Nach Chef 4 B 498?9.

## Earlier related schedule edition

The [p211 lower-B schedule](p211_key_schedule.md) already records the same
November/December reuse instruction in three differently worded parts. Its
published key is `Nov4-6`; these p160 parts use `Nov7-9`. The source headings,
receipt dates, abbreviations, reference fields and written-versus-numeral day
forms differ. The [parallel certificate](../../experiments/nov8_radio_keys_and_reports/parallel_witnesses.json)
compares the named raw/edited plaintext layers and preserves those differences.
It makes no ciphertext-coordinate comparison across the two keys and does not
use the older fields to complete the new unresolved reference digit.

The p211 source assembly and readable edition retain their existing
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro** attribution; the published keys retain their
original credits. These are two additional physical source parts, with no
claim to be the first identification of the key-use instruction.

## Shared uncertainty and credit

The two missing square cells `VF` and `XA` jointly contain `5` and `6`. Both complete assignments are retained as compatibility witnesses; every occurrence of a cell shares the same digit. The displayed `?` positions therefore must not be treated as independent digit choices. In p160 B2 one additional source coordinate remains unfilled; its domain can include letters as well as digits.

The published Nov7–9 period key and earlier OCR candidates are credited in the inputs. This edition adds source inspection, separate repair costs and exact readable-text mappings. It does not claim new recovery of the period key.

# Station control and the Seifert service exchange

[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All cases](../README.md) · [Source certificate](../../experiments/p170_continuation/seifert_records.json) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Nine source records, seven message groups.** The November 7–9 and November 10–12 published keys recover a sequence of radio-station reports and short service messages. Two pairs are repeated transmissions. These records are outside the original 22-entry challenge; the open p170 challenge is section **A**, not any of these neighboring records.

Source transcription, cipher checks and editorial work: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The station-control interpretations of p168 A and B were already published by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**; their author manuscript discusses both on printed p. 23 / PDF p. 24. The keys retain their recorded historical and modern provenance. This page provides a source-level edition, without claiming a first historical decipherment.

## Conditional shared digits

The paired monitoring orders each gain their hundreds digit: **500**. Both physical receptions have the same complete ciphertext; repetition preserves the value once the shared square is interpreted. No source coordinate is changed. The [joint reconstruction](../../experiments/nov10_joint_completion/README.md) combines the earlier Marineamt and formation interpretations with the army-number constraint and the mobilization decree; the reversed 7/9 assignment is retained there.

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the joint square:**

> Sofort US 500 hoeren.

<details>
<summary>Exact conditional labels</summary>

**Edited output — p172_B, conditional shared square; 20/20 fixed positions:**

```text
SOFORTXUSX500XHOEREN
```

**Edited output — p174_D, conditional shared square; 20/20 fixed positions:**

```text
SOFORTXUSX500XHOEREN
```

</details>


## Read the messages

The prior body credit for p168 A also applies to its repeated content at
**p169 A**. Identification of the repeat, its exact coordinate differences,
and the present source edition remain our contribution.

Square brackets mark supplied letters or abbreviation expansions. Punctuation, capitalization and word spacing are editorial.

| Source | Readable German | Meaning and exact qualification |
|---|---|---|
| **p168 A**; repeated with errors at **p169 A** | Stehe ab 2200 unter Aufsicht Sol[d]atenrats. Stat[ion und] Personal fest in meiner Hand. Betrieb unverändert. Seifert. | From 22:00 the sender is under the soldiers' council's supervision; station/personnel remain firmly under his control and operation is unchanged. All 92 raw positions of p168 A decode exactly; the source spells `SOLATENRATS` without `D`. The connecting words in the `STATPERSONAL` expansion are editorial. |
| **p168 B** | Soldatenrat Cöln wird bald Funkstelle besetzen. Versucht schon Funksprüche aufzugeben. | Cologne's soldiers' council is expected to occupy the radio station and is already trying to submit radio messages. The raw text has `SOLDATENRA9` and `SCKON`; the readable version requires two explicit coordinate substitutions. |
| **p172 A** | Akten [s]ämtlich vernichtet. Schlüssel in pers[önlicher] Obhut noch vorhanden. Seifert. | All records have been destroyed; the cipher keys remain in personal custody. The source fixes 67/68 plaintext positions. One invalid printed glyph leaves the initial letter of `SAEMTLICH` unresolved; `S` is a supported reading, not a source-observed letter. |
| **p174 B** | Wenn Seifert eingetroffe[n], bitte Nachr[icht]. TOF. | Please report when Seifert has arrived. The source fixes 36/37 positions. One doubtful glyph permits `N`; a `G` interpretation of that glyph instead produces separator `X` after the raw spelling `EINGETROFFE`. `TOF` is not expanded. |
| **p174 C** | Wann Rückkunft Seifert? RE. | When will Seifert return? All 24 plaintext positions decode exactly. `RE` remains unexpanded. |
| **p172 B / p174 D** | Sofort US ?00 hören. | An immediate listening instruction. The two 40-coordinate copies are identical. The unknown hundreds digit can be **5, 6, 7, 8 or 9** under a globally consistent completion of the published square. The role of `US` and the units of the number are not established. |
| **p174 E** | Seifert abgefahren. RENTE. | Seifert has departed. The raw text is `SQIFQRTABGEFAHRENXRENTE`; restoring the name requires two explicit `G → X` coordinate substitutions. `RENTE` is retained literally. |

The shared surname connects the service records, but the surviving headers do not establish Seifert's full name or a complete itinerary. The printed time expressions are preserved in the certificate, including the anomalous `17.28 p.m.` in p174 E. The day digit in p172 B is overtyped; the identical p174 D copy is explicitly dated 12 November.

## Raw decipherments

The table above does not overwrite these source-derived strings.

### p168 A — 184 coordinates / 92 positions

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
STEHEAB2200UNTERAUFSICHTSOLATENRATSXSTATPERSONALFESTINMEINERHANDXBETRIEBUNVERAENDERTXSEIFERT
```

</details>

No cipher correction is required. Supplying `D` in `Soldatenrats` and expanding `STAT` are editorial reading choices only. The source is available in the [p168 A/B excerpt](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p168_AB.png).

### p168 B — 160 coordinates / 80 positions

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
SOLDATENRA9XCOELNXWIRDBALDFUNKSTELLEBESETZENXVERSUCHTSCKONFUNKSPRUECHEAUFZUGEBEN
```

</details>

At zero-based ciphertext positions **89** and **141**, `F → V` and `G → X` give `SOLDATENRAT` and `SCHON`. The other **158 coordinates remain unchanged**. These are proposed source emendations, not alternative square assignments.

### p172 A — 136 slots / 68 positions

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
AKTEN?AEMTLICHVERNICHTETXSCHLUESSELINPERSOBHUTNOCHVORHANDENXXSEIFERT
```

</details>

The [source](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p172_AB.png) prints `DAAGC`: its final `C` is outside the ADFGVX alphabet and becomes one erasure at ciphertext position **119**. The plaintext domain at position **5** is exactly `{F,I,K,N,O,S}`. Filling that coordinate with `G` gives `S` and preserves all **135 valid received coordinates**. `PERSOBHUT` is retained; the readable expansion is *pers[önlicher] Obhut*.

### p174 B — 74 slots / 37 positions

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
WENNSEIFERTEINGETROFFE?BITTENACHRXTOF
```

</details>

The [source excerpt](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p174_BCDE.png) shows a `C`-like or defective `G` glyph at the start of group `CVXXF`, ciphertext position **20**. Its conservative analysis is `?VXXF`. The uncertain plaintext position **22** has domain `{1,5,6,7,8,9,E,N,V,X}`.

The readable `N` completion uses **D** at the source erasure and preserves all **73 certain coordinates**. Reading the doubtful glyph as **G** instead gives:

**Conditional interpretation — alternate G reading of the doubtful source glyph:**

```text
WENNSEIFERTEINGETROFFEXBITTENACHRXTOF
```

Within that single-source analysis, both alternatives are retained; the complete word `EINGETROFFEN` is an editorial inference.

An independent [p183 B witness](nov12_arrival_departure_and_car.md#p183-b)
now supplies observed `D` at source index 20 and therefore `N` at plaintext
position 22. Together the two conservative source transcriptions support
every target pair. The original C/G-like appearance and its G-reading
alternative remain in the earlier certificate and source analysis above.

### p174 C — 48 coordinates / 24 positions

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
WANNRUECKKUNFTSEIFERTXRE
```

</details>

No glyph change, erasure fill, square completion or length repair is needed.

### p172 B / p174 D — 40 coordinates / 20 positions each

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
SOFORTXUSX?00XHOEREN
```

</details>

Both copies have the same ciphertext. All 40 coordinates are legible; the unknown digit comes solely from an unassigned cell in the published November 10–12 square. The verifier constructs a full bijective square witness for **each** candidate digit 5–9. The duplicate therefore confirms the transmitted coordinates but does not select a digit.

### p174 E — 46 coordinates / 23 positions

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
SQIFQRTABGEFAHRENXRENTE
```

</details>

Changing ciphertext positions **2** and **28** from `G` to `X` gives:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
SEIFERTABGEFAHRENXRENTE
```

</details>

The other **44 coordinates remain unchanged**. The two corrections restore the same name directly present in the surrounding service traffic; the original `Q`s remain part of the raw edition.

The [p183 C witness](nov12_arrival_departure_and_car.md#p183-c) supports `X`
at source index 2, directly corroborating the second `E` of the name. Both
witnesses retain `G` at source index 28, so the first `E` remains a
separately priced contextual repair in each. The joint complete-name
proposal costs three observed-coordinate substitutions.

## The p169 A repeat

[p169 A](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p169_A.png) carries the same `SY v GK`, `2000` and `RICHI-184` metadata as p168 A, with a later intercept time. It prints **185 coordinates**, including the six-character group `DGDGGX`.

Deleting either adjacent `G` at zero-based source position **158** or **159** gives the same 184-coordinate conditional layer and this raw decipherment:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional deletion of source 158 or 159; equivalent aliases retained:**

```text
STEHEAB2200UNTEYAUFSICHTSOLATENRATWXSTATPERSONALFESTINMEIKERHANDXBETRIEBUNVERAENDURTXSEIFERT
```

</details>

It supports the repeated-message identification but is less clean than p168 A. Both deletion aliases are recorded. The untouched odd-length source is retained and is never silently decoded after dropping its last coordinate.

## Evidence and reproduction

The [certificate](../../experiments/p170_continuation/seifert_records.json) contains all nine literal source transcriptions, original headers, partial keys, raw plaintext domains, cropped-image hashes and exact proposed edits. It applies the already published keys; no unknown square cell is fixed by the prose.

```sh
python experiments/p170_continuation/verify_seifert.py
python experiments/p170_continuation/verify_seifert.py --json
```

The independent verifier checks **913 source slots**, every source-preserving fill, the four explicit coordinate substitutions, the p169 deletion aliases, both identical service copies, and all five globally attainable digit readings. A local copy of the source PDF can additionally be bound by SHA-256 with `--pdf /path/to/childs.pdf`.

### Sources and priority

- **J. Rives Childs collection:** printed pp. 168, 169, 172 and 174; PDF pp. 171, 172, 175 and 177 in the [public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view). The certificate retains its hash and the exact section headers.
- **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker:** *Deciphering ADFGVX messages from the Eastern Front of World War I*, [author manuscript](https://www.apprendre-en-ligne.net/crypto/bibliotheque/PDF/adfgvx.pdf), printed p. 23 / PDF p. 24. This earlier work explicitly identifies the p168 A/B station-control reports; it also credits Childs's wartime decipherment of the Cologne message. The present edition does not reassign that priority.
- **Published keys:** [key catalog](../../data/keys.json), entries `Nov7-9` and `Nov10-12`, retaining original table and solver provenance.

**Reviewed source crops:** [p56_reviewed.png](../../experiments/september19_pigeons_and_command/sources/p56_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).

# September: a key-destruction instruction with a masked label

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

## p61 A

Childs p61, PDF p64; [source crop](../../experiments/september_radio_instructions/sources/p61_A.png). Unchanged published **Sep19–21** key; native **176** coordinates, matching the printed length.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — received header:**

```text
21st SEPTEMBER, 1918.
A) --- v -- (10.09 p.m. September 22nd)
FEER POT COS NR 230 (19 DEN9) 1825 (19)
RIZI--176
```

**Raw output — 80/88 fixed positions; no frame change:**

```text
FUN?AX?OTIXUNDTIFLSSXSCHLUESSEL77?77X77777LI?RS?FOTTZUVETZICHTENXDA?EKANNTXFU??AXOSMANIE
```

**Edited output — 7 observed-coordinate substitutions and 7 printed-mask fills; 87/88 fixed positions:**

```text
FUNKAXPOTIXUNDTIFLISXSCHLUESSEL77?77X77777HIERSOFORTZUVERNICHTENXDABEKANNTXFUNKAXOSMANIE
```

</details>

Observed coordinate changes, with zero-based source indices: **0 G→D**, **25 X→V**, **53 G→X**, **77 G→D**, **83 V→F**, **164 G→X**, **171 X→A**.

Printed-mask fills: **4→D**, **12→G**, **54→D**, **55→D**, **56→G**, **95→D**, **96→D**.

The fixed positions satisfy their exact coordinate pairs. The remaining key-label position stays unresolved; a complete plaintext re-encryption is not claimed.

**Readable German — complete edited stream with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Funka Poti und Tiflis. Schluessel 77?77 77777 hier sofort zu vernichten, da bekannt. Funka Osmanie.

**Meaning:** The proposed message addresses the radio stations at Poti and Tiflis and instructs immediate destruction of the key bearing the labels 77?77 and 77777 because it is known. The two number labels and closing OSMANIE remain literal. HIER and several damaged words are editorial proposals; this does not prove that destruction occurred.

## What the key number does and does not establish

The source masks leave the first key label **77?77** incomplete. The second
label is directly decoded as **77777**. The baseline edited stream preserves
that distinction and the readable German retains the unresolved question
mark. It is not question punctuation.

**Conditional interpretation — repeated-number completion:**

If the two adjacent labels repeat one key number, replacing the first
`77?77` with `77777` requires one additional printed-mask fill:
**source 11 L→D** at the coordinate layer. L is outside ADFGVX, so this is a
mask fill, not a substitution of an observed valid coordinate. The optional
complete stream and its exact re-encryption are kept separately in the
certificate. No reference numeral is silently normalized or counted as a
baseline recovery.

The lexical reading **HIER** repairs raw `LI?R`, and **SOFORT ZU VERNICHTEN**
repairs `S?FOTT ZU VETZICHTEN`. These are explicit editorial proposals with
the costs listed above; another copy has not independently corroborated
them. The final **OSMANIE** stays literal. No modern place-name spelling is
substituted into the plaintext.

The heading 21 September, reception 22 September and internal 19 date fields
are preserved independently. Their difference is not resolved by changing
the ciphertext key or its labels.

## Attribution and evidence

The unchanged published key retains its original recovery credit. The frozen earlier OCR rows belong to the companion p57 edition; no p61 candidate appeared in those selected caches. The present p61 reading is derived from its checked source image, without claiming that the absence of a cached row establishes historical decipherment priority. This comparison does not establish an external first-decipherment claim.

# September radio listening and acknowledgment procedure

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Three source records on Childs printed p60 give a readable two-part instruction
to listen daily at previously stated times, followed by a separate request
to send radiograms continuously during reception of the Nauen press and
wait until afterward for acknowledgment. The unchanged published `Sep19-21`
key fixes **275 of 278 raw plaintext positions**. The readable edition uses
three observed-coordinate substitutions and four coordinate-erasure fills.

The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
[printed p60, PDF p63](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [full source page](../../experiments/september_radio_procedure/sources/childs_p60_full.png)
is headed `21st SEPTEMBER, 1918.` All three transcribed lengths exactly match
their printed `RIZI` length markers. There is no inserted, deleted or moved
ciphertext coordinate.

## A1: daily listening times

The [first-part source](../../experiments/september_radio_procedure/sources/childs_p60_A1.png)
has this header:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) COS v NKJ (10.02 p.m., Sept. 21st)
1400 (21) 2 TLE
1 TL  RIZI-176
```

</details>

The 176 source slots include a printed noncoordinate `T` and `L`. Treating
both as erasures gives the following 88-position reading, with 86 positions fixed:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
BITTEVONHEUTEABTAEGLICHZUDENVONUNSINDIESSEITX22552255VOM14X14X9XRIZI286ANGEGEBE?ENZEITE?
```

</details>

Both unknown positions have the domain `1EGNPZ`. Filling both with `N`
gives the proposed first-part ending `ANGEGEBENENZEITEN`. The rest of the
plaintext remains exactly as received. In readable form, continued by A2:

**Readable German — first-part excerpt; the continuation is separate:**

> Bitte von heute ab täglich zu den von uns in diesseit. `22552255` vom
> `14X14X9`, `RIZI286`, angegebe[n]en Zeite[n] …

The exact repeated strings **`22552255`** and **`14X14X9`**, and the reference
**`RIZI286`**, are directly fixed by the received coordinates. They are
preserved here without collapsing the repetition or supplying a normalized
telegram number or date. The abbreviation `diesseit.` is retained rather
than expanded into an unprinted document description.

## A2: a call at the beginning of every period

The [second-part source](../../experiments/september_radio_procedure/sources/childs_p60_A2.png)
is marked `2 TL RIZI-154`. All 154 coordinates are valid, and all 77 plaintext
positions are read without repair:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
AUFUNSZUHOERENXXWIRRUFENZUBEGINNJEDERPERIODEAUCHWENNNICHTSVORLIEGTANXXNKJXNKJ
```

</details>

The complete readable instruction continues:

**Readable German — second-part continuation; the opening is in the separate first part:**

> … auf uns zu hören. Wir rufen zu Beginn jeder Periode, auch wenn nichts
> vorliegt, an. NKJ NKJ.

Thus A asks the recipient to listen for the sender daily at the referenced
times. The sender will call at the start of each period even when there is
no traffic. The repeated `NKJ` signature is retained. A1 and A2 are decrypted
as their own 176- and 154-slot frames before their prose is joined.

## B: traffic during reception of the Nauen press

The [B source](../../experiments/september_radio_procedure/sources/childs_p60_B.png)
has a separate clear service annotation above its encrypted body:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
B) ASO v NKJ (1.30 a.m., Sept. 21st)
2 TL RICHI-180 NV VON GFGGV BIS SCHLUSS WH 3 TL RICHI-126
VE 2100 (21)
RIZI-226
```

</details>

The annotation is retained literally. Its references to other parts are not
counted as additional recovered records or included in the cipher frame.
`NV`, `WH` and `VE` are left unexpanded. The reception and origin-line time
strings are preserved without silently resolving their chronology.

The 226-slot body has a printed dash and one damaged group-initial glyph.
The latter looks R/E-like and may be a damaged `F`; the conservative
transcription treats it as an erasure. Both erased coordinates feed the
same plaintext position. The raw reading therefore fixes 112 of 113 positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
RITTEFUNKSPRXFUERCOSANUNSWAEHRENDAUFNAHMENAUENPRESSEIMMEROHGEUNTYRBRECHUNGGEBENXXQUITTUNGFOLGTNACHPRESSE?CHLUSSXX
```

</details>

Three coordinate substitutions repair `RITTE`, `OHGE` and `UNTYRBRECHUNG`.
Two coordinate fills supply the missing `S` in `PRESSESCHLUSS`:

<details>

**Readable German:**

The instruction asks for radiograms intended for COS to be sent continuously
to the sender while it receives the Nauen press; the acknowledgment will
follow after the press transmission ends.

### Exact repair and erasure ledger

Source indices are zero-based; printed group and within-group positions are
one-based. The source images and certificate also record the printed row.

| Record | Source index | Printed group / position | Received glyph or coordinate | Proposal | Type | Effect |

restricts that domain to `8EHISY` and reduces the fill count by one. It leaves

## Reproducibility, numerals and prior credit

The [inputs](../../experiments/september_radio_procedure/inputs.json) retain
all manual rows, glyph notes, exact headers, the published key and image
provenance. The [certificate](../../experiments/september_radio_procedure/certificates.json)

each fill and the complete re-encrypted witnesses. It counts the conditional
visual variant separately, so the corpus contribution is **three records**.

| --- | ---: |
| Source slots / valid received coordinates | 556 / 552 |
| Raw fixed plaintext positions | 275 / 278 |
| Proposed positions supported by unchanged complete pairs | 272 / 278 |
| Valid-coordinate substitutions / erasure fills | 3 / 4 |

The published `Sep19-21` key is credited to **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel,
Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**, [2016, DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),

# September: direct radio routing to Tiflis

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The original page gives one three-part instruction. Reading its actual part boundaries recovers a coherent route and monitoring order under the published key. All repeated place names and call signs remain visible. The page heading is 20 September, the internal header gives 20, and reception is 21 September; those are distinct source dates.

## p57 A1

**Readable German — complete edited stream with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Da NKJ NKJ sehr gut, ASO ASO zu leise von COS COS gehoert wird. Schnelle Uebermittlung wichtig. Zur Sicherstellung des

**Meaning:** The reason given is that COS hears NKJ very well but ASO too weakly. Rapid forwarding is important. The final words continue into part 3; every repeated call sign remains literal.

## p57 A3

Childs p57, PDF p60; [source crop](../../experiments/september_radio_instructions/sources/p57_A.png). Unchanged published **Sep19–21** key; native **176** coordinates, matching the printed length.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — 88/88 fixed positions; no frame change:**

```text
MITHOERENSVERKEHRMITXCOSXZUBESTIMMTENZEITENVORHER2NKUENDIGENXXGRUKONACH652ROEMX4XNR43908
```

**Edited output — 1 observed-coordinate substitution and 0 printed-mask fills; 88/88 fixed positions:**

```text

```

</details>

The complete edited stream re-encrypts to exactly the source plus those changes.

**Readable German — complete edited stream with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Mithoerens Verkehr mit COS zu bestimmten Zeiten vorher ankuendigen. Grukonach 652 roem 4 Nr 43908.

**Meaning:** Continuing part 2, the message asks that traffic with COS at specified times be announced beforehand to ensure monitoring. The closing labels 652, 4 and 43908 remain unchanged. The source annotation directly supports the A in ANKUENDIGEN.

## Source annotation and conservative overprint masks

Part 3 has a visible **D above the A** in typed `FGAXF`. The raw transcription
keeps the typed A at source index 132; applying the annotated D costs one
observed-coordinate substitution and changes `2NKUENDIGEN` to `ANKUENDIGEN`.
This source annotation supplies independent support beyond the readable-word
proposal. The [detail image](../../experiments/september_radio_instructions/sources/p57_A3_annotation.png)
shows the two glyphs without conflating them into one transcription.

Two other overprints are conservatively masked, not forced to a coordinate:
part 1 source 205 and part 2 source 1. Their proposed G and X fills restore
`FUNKEN` and `SEHR`, respectively. The [overprint crop](../../experiments/september_radio_instructions/sources/p57_A1_A2_overprints.png)
also confirms the clear group `FVAAX`, which directly yields `BLIND` without
an editorial coordinate change.

Part 1 `CPRUECHE→SPRUECHE` costs one substitution. Part 2 `V0N→VON` costs one
substitution: the literal zero in the raw word is visible and its proposed
letter replacement is explicitly counted. The reference digits 652, 4 and 43908
are unchanged.

Part 2 ends `ZUR SICHERSTELLUNG DES`; part 3 begins `MITHOERENS`. The complete
three-part reading therefore states the reason for announcing COS traffic
at agreed times. The words describe requested radio practice, without
establishing whether that practice was carried out.

## Attribution and evidence

The unchanged published key retains its original recovery credit. Earlier unreviewed repository OCR screens split the p57 parts across the wrong boundaries and did not produce these readable texts; the relevant prior rows are retained. This comparison does not establish an external first-decipherment claim.

[Inputs](../../experiments/september_radio_instructions/inputs.json), [positional certificates](../../experiments/september_radio_instructions/certificates.json), [earlier screens](../../experiments/september_radio_instructions/prior_candidates.json) and [reproduction](../../experiments/september_radio_instructions/README.md) preserve the complete evidence.

# Request for replies and radio priority

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This two-part telegram asks the Foreign Office in Berlin for replies to
three earlier messages and for brief instructions in plaintext. It then
suggests explicitly telling the radio station to send these telegrams
before others, because military telegrams apparently receive priority.
The signature is the literal `HORSTMANN`; no historical identity is assigned
from the name alone.

Both printed frames are complete: **226 and 282 slots**, under the unchanged
published `Nov4-6` key. Six observed-coordinate substitutions and seven
printed-dash fills give the readable edition. No coordinate is inserted,
removed or reordered, and no square cell is changed.

## Source and the first part

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [printed p128, PDF p131](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [full page](../../experiments/radio_telegram_priority/sources/childs_p128_full.png)
is headed `5th NOVEMBER, 1918.` The shared header is:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
A) LP v NKJ (7.01 p.m., November 5th)
1130 (5) 2 TLE
```

</details>

The [first part](../../experiments/radio_telegram_priority/sources/childs_p128_A1.png)
is labeled `1 TL RICHI-226`. All 226 coordinates are valid and fix all
113 raw plaintext positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
AUSWAERTIGBERLINNUMMER597XANTWORTAUFTELEGRAMME569X592UND598BISHERNICHTEINGETROFFENXZURZEWEISUNGINKLARTEXTERBETENX
```

</details>

One coordinate substitution changes `ZURZE` to `KURZE`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
AUSWAERTIGBERLINNUMMER597XANTWORTAUFTELEGRAMME569X592UND598BISHERNICHTEINGETROFFENXKURZEWEISUNGINKLARTEXTERBETENX
```

</details>

Readable German:

**Readable German:**

> Auswärtig Berlin. Nummer 597. Antwort auf Telegramme 569, 592 und 598
> bisher nicht eingetroffen. Kurze Weisung in Klartext erbeten.

The telegram says that replies to messages **569, 592 and 598** have not
yet arrived and requests brief instructions in plaintext. The message
number **597** and all three references are unchanged labels from the
published square; the edition does not infer a chronology from their order.
The source's `AUSWAERTIG` remains an abbreviation, without inserting an
encoded `AMT` into the plaintext.

## Second part: proposed radio precedence

The [second part](../../experiments/radio_telegram_priority/sources/childs_p128_A2.png)
is labeled `2 TL RICHI-282`. It contains exactly 282 printed slots, including
seven dashes. Its ordinary source frame fixes 134 of 141 positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ANH9IMGRSTELLTFDNKENSTATIONAUSDRUEK?IC7?NZUHEISENXTELEGRAMMEVORALLENANDERENZUGEBENXD?SCHEINBAR?ILITAER?SCHETELE?RAMME?EVORZUGTWERDNXHORSTMANN
```

</details>

Five observed-coordinate substitutions and seven dash fills give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ANHEIMGESTELLTFUNKENSTATIONAUSDRUEKLICHANZUWEISENXTELEGRAMMEVORALLENANDERENZUGEBENXDASCHEINBARMILITAERISCHETELEGRAMMEBEVORZUGTWERDNXHORSTMANN
```

</details>

Its meaning is: it is suggested that the wireless station be explicitly
instructed to send these telegrams before all others, because military
telegrams apparently receive preferential treatment. This is a suggestion
to the recipient, not evidence that such an instruction had already been
issued or obeyed.

The literal spellings **`AUSDRUEKLICH`** and **`WERDN`** remain in the edition.
No additional plaintext `C` or `E` is claimed. The signature `HORSTMANN`
already appears unchanged in the raw reading.

An earlier OCR extraction supplied only 281 slots. Manual source review
establishes the advertised 282-slot frame. This is an OCR transcription
correction and supplies no evidence for a historical before-transposition
coordinate loss.

## Exact coordinate costs

All source indices below are zero-based. Printed group numbers and positions
are one-based and counted separately within each part.

| Part | Source index | Printed group / position | Change | Plaintext effect |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | 156 | 32 / 2 | `V` → `F` | `ZURZE` → `KURZE` |
| A2 | 0 | 1 / 1 | `X` → `A` | Raw `9` → `E` within `ANHEIM` |
| A2 | 121 | 25 / 2 | `G` → `F` | `ZUHEISEN` → `ZUWEISEN` |
| A2 | 183 | 37 / 4 | `V` → `F` | `GRSTELLT` → `GESTELLT` |
| A2 | 184 | 37 / 5 | `F` → `V` | `FDNKEN` → `FUNKEN` |
| A2 | 203 | 41 / 4 | `D` → `G` | Raw `7` → `H` within `AUSDRUEKLICH` |

The seven A2 dash fills, separately charged, are:

| Source index | Printed group / position | Filled coordinate | Proposed plaintext label |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 26 | 6 / 2 | `F` | `A` in `DA` |
| 54 | 11 / 5 | `V` | `A` in `ANZUWEISEN` |
| 79 | 16 / 5 | `V` | `B` in `BEVORZUGT` |
| 129 | 26 / 5 | `V` | `G` in `TELEGRAMME` |
| 160 | 33 / 1 | `X` | `M` in `MILITAERISCHE` |
| 161 | 33 / 2 | `X` | `I` in `MILITAERISCHE` |
| 220 | 45 / 1 | `X` | `L` in `AUSDRUEKLICH` |

The raw numerical labels `9` and `7` in damaged A2 words remain visible in
the raw reading and the numerical ledger. Their proposed changes are local
coordinate substitutions. They do not alter the square's digit assignments.
Every actual A1 numerical reference remains unchanged.

## Verification and attribution

The [inputs](../../experiments/radio_telegram_priority/inputs.json) preserve
the exact headers, manual groups, key provenance and image hashes. The
[certificate](../../experiments/radio_telegram_priority/certificates.json)
retains every raw domain, source-coordinate origin, repair, dash fill,
numerical label and full forward witness. The standard-library verifier
independently undoes the transposition and rebuilds both witnesses:

```sh
python experiments/radio_telegram_priority/verify.py --verify
```

The period key is prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**, [DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
also reproduced in George Lasry's [2017-02-24 comment 4](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1).
Earlier unreviewed OCR-derived candidates existed. The bounded author-paper
check found no explicit p128 A body example; that does not establish
universal first-decipherment priority. Exact re-encryption certifies the
stated arithmetic and repair prices, not unique historical wording.

# Tiflis: request to repeat an encrypted telegram

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

## p77 A

Childs p77 A, PDF p80, is headed
`NKJ v LP (4.11 p.m., October 29th)` and `0110 (29/10)`.
The [source crop](../../experiments/tiflis_repetition_request/sources/p77_A.png)
contains exactly **314 source slots**, matching `RICHI-314`: **313
unambiguous coordinates and one damaged or overstruck glyph** at source 67.
It uses the unchanged published **Oct28–31** key.
Source and plaintext indices below are zero-based; printed rows and groups
are counted from one.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 314-coordinate frame:**

```text
ZUERXBXDX5XMXKAUKASUSXTIFLISXXERBITT4NXWIEDERHOLUNGXCHIFFRIERTENXTELEGRAMMSXVOMXEINUNDZWANZIGSTENXZEHNTENXCHIXZ53X12X10XUNTERSCHRIFTXX1874XSTRICHXZ?ROTX692XX
```

**Edited output — two observed-coordinate substitutions and one damaged-glyph fill:**

```text
FUERXBXDX5XMXKAUKASUSXTIFLISXXERBITTENXWIEDERHOLUNGXCHIFFRIERTENXTELEGRAMMSXVOMXEINUNDZWANZIGSTENXZEHNTENXCHIXZ53X12X10XUNTERSCHRIFTXX1874XSTRICHXZXROTX692XX
```

</details>

The observed-coordinate changes remain source **91 V→F** and **244 X→G**,
repairing `ZUER` and `ERBITT4N`. The separate fill **67 ?→X** supplies
the separator between Z and ROT at plaintext position **147**. The raw
layer fixes **156/157 positions**; the unchanged edited candidate fixes
**157/157** and re-encrypts exactly. Its cost is now **three coordinate
operations**, comprising two observed substitutions and one fill. The
former definite X was unchanged by the old candidate, so the new fill is
an additional operation, not a reclassification of either substitution.

**Readable German — spacing, punctuation and umlaut:**

> Für B. D. 5. M. Kaukasus, Tiflis. Erbitten Wiederholung chiffrierten
> Telegramms vom einundzwanzigsten Zehnten. CHI. Z53. 12. 10.
> Unterschrift: 1874 Strich Z. Rot. 692.

## Conditional interpretation and source boundaries

The text requests a repeated encrypted telegram. This edition does not
identify the earlier message or claim that it was retransmitted. The
address **B D 5 M**, reference **Z53**, separate **12 10** fields and
closing **1874 STRICH Z ROT 692** remain unexpanded. In particular, the
5 in the address is not changed into an assumed letter, and the local
repair of `ERBITT4N` establishes no global numeral mapping. The written
“einundzwanzigsten Zehnten” and the separate numerical fields are not
forced into one date.

<details>
<summary>Source 67: damaged glyph, separator fill and retained X assumption</summary>

The third glyph of the second row's sixth group is conservatively
transcribed **`DX?XF`**. The [detail crop](../../experiments/tiflis_repetition_request/sources/p77_A_source67.png)
shows X-like crossing strokes together with an additional near-vertical
or curved stroke on the right. Unlike the neighboring clear X glyphs,
the target appears overstruck or damaged. The image does not establish
which layer is original, or an unconditional X. D describes part of its
appearance; it is not adopted as a coordinate reading.

The crop comes from PDF page 80, display rectangle `[370,331,412,349]`,
at scale 16, retaining the page's native 180-degree rotation. The `?`
occupies one existing source slot, without inserting or deleting a coordinate.
Plaintext position **147** uses source indices **[242,67]** and pair
**`A?`**, whose domain is **`02HISX`**. The main template selects X as a
separator; the raw source does not independently fix that separator.

The certificate retains the previous X transcription as one explicit
assumption branch. It restores 157 raw fixed positions and the former
two-substitution account, with no further change at source 67. That
branch is a same-source glyph hypothesis, not an independent observation
or parallel copy; the primary account remains two substitutions plus
one fill. All other raw labels and the complete main candidate are unchanged.

The frozen earlier OCR already used `?` at source 67. Its complete cipher
stream and raw output match the new conservative transcription. It is an
earlier transcription of the same scan, not independent corroboration.

</details>

At source index **267**, the
[detail crop](../../experiments/tiflis_repetition_request/sources/p77_A_G_glyph.png)
shows the third glyph of **XXGGX** as G, with the same inner stroke as
the following G. An initial page-scale C reading was rejected before
publication. This clear-G check adds no coordinate edit or fill and is
separate from the damaged source 67.

The earlier unreviewed repository candidate already identified this
body; the source edition retains that credit and the published key's
provenance. It makes no historical first-solution claim. The adjacent
p77 B is a previously cataloged separate message and is not counted
again. Complete [inputs](../../experiments/tiflis_repetition_request/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/tiflis_repetition_request/certificates.json)
and [reproduction instructions](../../experiments/tiflis_repetition_request/README.md)
are available.

# Tube transmitter dispatched to TAFUNK

[Case index](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

## p87 A1

**Readable German — spacing and punctuation:**

> Akonach 18. Roehrensender an TAFUNK abgegangen. Hier 10 kW QOF-Sender Umformermotor fuer 220 Volt.

A tube transmitter has been dispatched to TAFUNK. The continuation lists a 10 kW QOF transmitter and a converter motor for 220 volts. `AKONACH 18`, `TAFUNK` and `QOF` retain their transmitted forms. This is the first of the three announced parts.

**Reading:** all 83 plaintext positions are fixed by the 166 observed source coordinates. The text re-encrypts exactly under the published Nov1–3 key, with no substitutions, fills or change of frame.

**Source:** printed p87, heading *31st OCTOBER, 1918*. Receipt: `UKS v OSM (2.02 a.m., November 2nd)`; dispatch: `SSD AUF 1330 (31/10) 3 TLE`; part label: `1 TL RICHI-166`.

![Source p87 A1](../../experiments/early_radio_and_leave_records/sources/p87_A1.png)

<details>
<summary>Transcription correction and exact text</summary>

Review of the first row's final group gives `DGAGF`. The first glyph has a closed right-hand curve and no middle bar. The earlier repository transcription read `EGAGF`, treated the out-of-alphabet `E` as a mask, and consequently displayed `AKONACH18?`. Reading source coordinate 35 as `D` fixes plaintext position 9 as separator `X`. This corrects the transcription of the visible letter; it does not alter the historical ciphertext.

**Raw output — complete native reading:**


# Warsaw control markers and radio forwarding instructions

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**ADFGVX Cipher — icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**

Four previously uncatalogued messages can be read with the published
`Nov13-15b` partial square. They describe commercial reporting from Bucharest,
LP's forwarding responsibilities, Army Group Kiev's march route, and the
`FRANZ`/`EMIL` markers used for Warsaw messages. The physical source, unresolved
symbols and exact price of each proposed repair are retained separately.

Primary evidence: J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, printed pp. 192 and 194 (PDF pp. 195 and 197). The corresponding crops,
PDF hash and literal transcriptions are in
[the source edition](../../experiments/warsaw_service_messages/inputs.json).
The published square's unknown cells and numerical labels are not changed.

## p192 A: request to Kretzschmar in Bucharest

The source header is `NKJ FUER UKS`, receipt `06.45 p.m., November 14th`,
origin `22.55 (15/11)`, and `RICHI-350`. The incompatible dates are preserved.
The 350 printed slots include an `E`-like overstrike at source index 120,
inside the group `EXAXF`. It is outside the six-coordinate alphabet and is
treated as an erasure.

Raw decryption, 171 fixed positions out of 175:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ANXOBLT0KRETZSCHMARBEIXOKMXWIRTSCHAFTSSTABABTX1XBUKARESTXNRX???XERBITTENNACHRICHTUEBERLAGENUN?AUSSICHTENSOWIEBEZUEGLICHUNSERERINTERESSENGEFASSTEBESCHLUESSEXDEUTKAUF5AUSWAERTIG
```

</details>

Filling that overstrike as `F` restores `UND`, with no change to an observed
valid coordinate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ANXOBLT0KRETZSCHMARBEIXOKMXWIRTSCHAFTSSTABABTX1XBUKARESTXNRX???XERBITTENNACHRICHTUEBERLAGENUNDAUSSICHTENSOWIEBEZUEGLICHUNSERERINTERESSENGEFASSTEBESCHLUESSEXDEUTKAUF5AUSWAERTIG
```

</details>

The message asks Oberleutnant Kretzschmar, attached to the OKM economic staff,
department 1, in Bucharest for news about the situation and prospects, and
decisions affecting the sender's interests. The literal forms `OBLT0`,
`LAGEN`, and `DEUTKAUF5` are not normalized inside the ciphertext model.
The three reference symbols after `NRX` occupy cells `VG`, `AF`, `AF`.
The [shared conditional VG=2 reading](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md#the-award-class)
gives **`2??`**, with the two unknowns still equal. This adds one label to the
existing edition, reaching **173/175**, without another source edit.

## p192 B: LP relays traffic in both directions

The header reads `NKJ v LP (06.56 p.m., November 14th)` and
`NKJ FUER ZO'N 17.30 (15/11)`. Although it advertises `RICHI-268`, the source
has **267** coordinate letters: the 22nd printed group is only `FVGA`.

Inserting one unknown coordinate immediately after that group gives this raw
reading, with 131 fixed positions out of 134:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional insertion immediately after the short printed group:**

```text
KWHXLPXUEBERMITTELTALLEVORLIEGENDENWICHTIGENNACHRICHTENFUERHEIMATDIENSTSTE?LENSOWIEXOHLXUNDUMGEKEHRTXKMXALLGXKRIEGSDEPXNRX?5?1115XANCH
```

</details>

The ordinary-word candidate is:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional missing-slot frame, with the stated repairs:**

```text
KWHXLPXUEBERMITTELTALLEVORLIEGENDENWICHTIGENNACHRICHTENFUERHEIMATDIENSTSTELLENSOWIEXOHLXUNDUMGEKEHRTXKMXALLGXKRIEGSDEPXNRX?5?1115XANCH
```

</details>

Its meaning is direct: LP transmits all available important messages for home
offices and OHL, and conversely. The ending names `KM`, the general war
department and a reference that remains literally `?5?1115` under the
published partial square.

An exhaustive check of all 268 possible insertion boundaries finds exactly
two zero-substitution fits to that ordinary-word stencil: source gaps **109**
and **110**. Both insert `F` next to the same observed `F`, producing the same
repaired ciphertext. The alternative unfilled gap moves the single erased
plaintext letter from `DIENSTSTE?LEN` to `SOWI?`; both complete to the same
candidate. No other source coordinate is altered. The two baseline unknown
reference symbols are at cells `GD` and `VG`. Applying the shared conditional
VG=2 assignment gives **`?521115`**, taking this edition to **133/134** fixed
labels; GD remains unknown. Both gap alternatives are retained.

## p194 C: which march route will Army Group Kiev choose?

The header is `IWE v WAU (2.31 a.m., November 16th)`, origin `2300 (15)`,
`RICHI-224`. All 224 printed coordinates are valid.

Raw reading, 111 fixed positions out of 112:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
HEERESGRUPPEXKIEWXXWELCHENC?MARSCNWEGWAEHLTUEERESGRUPPEKIEWXXDRINGENDBALDIGSTBESCHEIDFUNKENXPRESSEXSXRXWARSCHAUX
```

</details>

Changing source index 5 from `X` to `A`, and source index 60 from `V` to `A`,
restores the two clear ordinary words:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
HEERESGRUPPEXKIEWXXWELCHENC?MARSCHWEGWAEHLTHEERESGRUPPEKIEWXXDRINGENDBALDIGSTBESCHEIDFUNKENXPRESSEXSXRXWARSCHAUX
```

</details>

The message asks which march route the army group will choose, requesting an
urgent prompt reply by radio, and ends with the Warsaw soldiers' council's
press designation. The `C?` segment after `WELCHEN` is still unexplained.
Reading it as `XX` would require **three additional observed-coordinate
changes**; that complete but editorial candidate is priced separately in the
certificate and is not promoted to the conservative raw text.

## p194 E: FRANZ and EMIL control markers

The source is `LP v WAU (---- November 16th)`, `SSDD 2256 (15)`,
`RICHI-240`. Its first group is literally `XFYGF`, so the `Y` at source
index 2 is treated as an erasure. The other 239 coordinates are valid.

Raw reading, 119 fixed positions out of 120:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ZUKUENFTIGWERDENUNK?NTOLLIERTETELSDESXSXRXWARSCHAUDURCHXXFRANZXXXKONTROLLIERTEDURCHXXEMILXXGEKENNZEICHNETXXSXRXWARSCHAUX
```

</details>

Filling the invalid coordinate as `X` yields this complete, exactly
reencryptable candidate without changing any valid source coordinate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ZUKUENFTIGWERDENUNKONTOLLIERTETELSDESXSXRXWARSCHAUDURCHXXFRANZXXXKONTROLLIERTEDURCHXXEMILXXGEKENNZEICHNETXXSXRXWARSCHAUX
```

</details>

Future unchecked telegrams from the Warsaw soldiers' council are to be marked
`FRANZ`; checked telegrams are to be marked `EMIL`. The source plaintext spells
the first adjective **UNKONTOLLIERTE**, omitting the expected `R` from the
ordinary German word. It also puts three `X` separators after `FRANZ`. Neither
irregularity is silently changed to make the sentence look cleaner.

## Reproducibility and limits

The [verifier](../../experiments/warsaw_service_messages/verify.py) checks the
published key against `data/keys.json`, independently rebuilds the
transposition indices, records every plaintext domain, reconstructs every
candidate ciphertext from its listed edits, and exhaustively retains the two
p192 B gap minima. Its optional PDF check verifies source-crop pixels.

The four records contain 1,081 literal slots, of which 1,079 are valid
coordinates. After the one declared insertion, their models have 541 plaintext
positions, 532 fixed before repair and 535 in the conservative candidates.
The shared VG=2 interpretation adds **two** reference digits, reaching
**537/541**, as checked in the
[shared-traffic certificate](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/traffic_certificates.json).
The remaining reference symbols, the published `0` and `5`, and the
inconsistent source dates are retained.

# Warsaw station report: a conditional missing-row continuation

[Catalogue](../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Source review and conditional reconstruction: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p204 C2 prints **242 coordinate slots** but advertises **282**. Inserting a hypothetical row of eight five-coordinate groups before the terminal `GX` produces a coherent continuation of [part 1](nov16_18_command_inquiries.md#p204-c1): equipment has not arrived from home, operation is to pass to the Poles on Monday evening, and WAU is transferring personnel. The proposed words require **no change to any observed coordinate** and **36 fills in the 40 hypothesized missing slots**. Four plaintext positions remain unknown.

The longer frame and those 36 fills remain a **conditional reconstruction**. The scan does not visibly mark a lost row, and no complete independent copy supplies it. The native 242-slot decoding remains available below.

## p204 C2

[Reviewed source excerpt](../../experiments/warsaw_station_missing_row/sources/p204_C.png) · [Exact inputs](../../experiments/warsaw_station_missing_row/inputs.json) · [All gap placements and global witnesses](../../experiments/warsaw_station_missing_row/certificates.json)

**Source transcription — header:** `C) KOW v WAU (1.50 a.m., November 18th); 0115 (17), 2 TLE; 2 TL RICHI-282`.

The seven printed lines contain six lines of 40 coordinates and a final two-coordinate group `GX`. This count restores several groups omitted or damaged by OCR, but the remaining 40-slot discrepancy is in the reviewed source itself.

**Readable German — conditional interpretation**, from the edited 282-slot frame with the missing row inserted before `GX`:

> Das nicht aus Heimat eingetroffen. NO?A WAU. Festfern, Festfunk A uebergeben Betrieb Montag Abend Polen. S. R. WAU ueberweist Mannschaften Bezkdos des ?K? nach OA?.

**Meaning:** The preceding part ends with equipment; this continuation says it has not arrived from home. Under the stated lost-row hypothesis, the facilities designated FESTFERN and FESTFUNK A hand operation to the Poles on Monday evening, and S. R. WAU transfers personnel to the abbreviated Bezkdos. The opening token, final unit and destination are not identified.

The literal tokens `NO?A`, `A` after `FESTFUNK`, `DES?K?` and `OA?` are retained. `Bezkdos` is left as the transmitted abbreviation. The ending is not silently made into a fluent unit name or a plausible destination.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 282-slot frame**, before filling any missing coordinate. Every one of the 242 printed coordinates remains unchanged.

```text
DASN?C?TAUSHE?MA?EINGET?O?F?NXNO?AW?U?FEST?E?N?FEST?UN?A?EBER?E?E?BETR?EB?O?TAGA?E?D?OLEN?SX?X?AUUE?E?W?ISTM?NN?C?AFTE?B?Z?DOSXDES?K?NACHOA?X
```

**Edited output — conditional 282-slot frame:** zero observed-coordinate substitutions, zero source-mask fills, and 36 inserted-slot fills; four inserted slots remain unknown.

```text
DASNICHTAUSHEIMATEINGETROFFENXNO?AWAUXFESTFERNXFESTFUNKAUEBERGEBENBETRIEBMONTAGABENDPOLENXSXRXWAUUEBERWEISTMANNSCHAFTENBEZKDOSXDES?K?NACHOA?X
```

</details>

## What the terminal alternatives establish

The verifier checks every possible start for one contiguous 40-slot gap against the same disclosed word template. Exactly three terminal placements allow the proposed wording without changing an observed coordinate. This is a compatibility result **conditioned on the proposed wording**, not an independent identification of the lost position.

| Missing gap starts at source index | Position relative to terminal GX | Inserted-slot fills | Fixed edited positions | Remaining ending |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| 240 | Before GX | 36 | 137 / 141 | `DES?K?NACHOA?X` |
| 241 | Between G and X | 35 | 136 / 141 | `?ES?K?NACHOA?X` |
| 242 | After GX | 34 | 135 / 141 | `?ES?K?NACH?A?X` |

The before-`GX` placement preserves the printed five-coordinate group boundary. The other two possibilities are retained because the observed coordinates and the selected words do not exclude them. All three branches preserve the same substantive middle reading while leaving different terminal fields open. No global key cell is reassigned.

## Source and contextual limits

The [preceding source part](nov16_18_command_inquiries.md#p204-c1) ends with crews of two other stations lacking equipment; `DAS NICHT AUS HEIMAT EINGETROFFEN` continues that sentence naturally. The independently reviewed [p204 A telegram](p204_A.md) also reports a Monday handover to the Poles. These are useful contextual checks, but neither provides this part's missing ciphertext, final reference or destination.

<details>
<summary>Native 242-slot raw output</summary>

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — native 242-slot frame**, unchanged and without any hypothesized missing coordinate:

```text
OOXJSBN?N?NXR?MY?C?B??H2EWJ??UGH?ONGTRQEGGFWA?YSB?BT1WYU?SRD?CNTWR?E?SYCCWABOA?OCCOBNNBSTG?T?X?THG1GWJEWQSCEEBYWA?O?Q?OGW
```

</details>

This native output is not an accepted body reading. The proposed 282-slot reading is kept in its own conditional frame.

</details>

## Evidence and credit

Published Nov16–18 key: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016); George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed OCR candidates are preserved. New source review and conditional reconstruction: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates preserve all source rows, map every conditional frame position to its original source index or an explicitly inserted slot, and list every proposed fill. Separate injective global square completions and residual-coordinate fillings produce full re-encryption witnesses for all three branches. Those witnesses demonstrate consistency, not historical completeness. The readable passage maps exactly to every nonseparator label in the primary edited output, including all four question marks.

Reproduce with `python experiments/warsaw_station_missing_row/verify.py --verify`. Optional `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` regenerates the crop and checks every RGB pixel against the pinned original PDF.

# p107_D — supplementary source review

[Case index](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Original reading:** [Ayush Agarwal (@AyushAg1002), 2026-10-28](https://github.com/dbourdeau/cyphersolver/issues/181). **Current image and arithmetic review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026.

This record belongs to the wider Childs corpus and is outside the original 22-entry challenge.

Acknowledgment of operational telegrams, including numbered references, from Mackensen's headquarters to Supreme Army Command. The exact raw numbers and garbles remain visible.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German — earlier credited partial interpretation:**

> O.H.L., Op. Zu dort 1a104660 […] [Drahtungen] 1a11118 geh. Op. und 1a1?127 geh. Op. erhalten. O.K.M. 1a?116OO6.

**Meaning:** An acknowledgment of operational telegrams, with their reference numbers, addressed to Supreme Army Command and signed by Mackensen's headquarters.

**Notes:** The garbled reference strings remain literal; apparent `O` letters are not silently converted to zeroes. `[Drahtungen]` is a readable interpretation of the damaged telegram wording. Two parenthesized source coordinates admit different conservative treatments, shown below. Original reading: **Ayush Agarwal**; our contribution is the later source and arithmetic review.

86 fixed positions in 88 plaintext positions. Uncertain source annotations remain explicit.

# p187_C — supplementary source review

[Case index](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Original reading:** [Ayush Agarwal (@AyushAg1002), 2026-10-28](https://github.com/dbourdeau/cyphersolver/issues/181). **Current image and arithmetic review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026.

This record belongs to the wider Childs corpus and is outside the original 22-entry challenge.

A request for an immediate report on the connection with Mackensen's army. The natural reading is clear, but the received text still contains errors and unresolved letters.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German — earlier credited body, with later repair accounting:**

> Bitte sofort [Bescheid], ob [Verbindung mit] Armee [Mackensen] einwa[nd]frei.

**Meaning:** Please report immediately whether the connection with Army Mackensen is functioning without problems.

**Notes:** The bracketed readings normalize the raw `BE?CHEID`, `VERPINDUNG MIS`, `MAKENSEN` and `EINWA?DFREI`. They convey the likely instruction while retaining the exact source result below. In particular, the printed `FFXXV` supports the raw `M` in `MIS`; it does not itself correct `MIS` to `MIT`. Original reading: **Ayush Agarwal**; our contribution is the later source and arithmetic review.

## Conservative source reading

65 fixed positions in 67 plaintext positions. Uncertain source annotations remain explicit.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
BITTEXSOFORTXBE?CHEIDXOBXVERPINDUNGXMISXARMEEXMAKENSENXEINWA?DFREIX
```

</details>

## Review

- The original section is C, with 134 coordinates and an agreeing RICHI-134 header; p190G is the contributor's typed-log identifier.
- At group 23 the full scan reads FFXXV. The published repaired layer masks its first F as -FXXV. Both layers are kept.
- The issue's 135-symbol source count is not the count of the alphabetic source layer.

## Earlier published reading

<details>
<summary>Earlier attributed reading</summary>

**Earlier attributed reading:**

```text
BITTEXSOFORTXBE?CHEIDXOBXVERPINDUNGX?ISXARMEEXMAKENSENXEINWA?DFREIX
```

</details>

The published reconstruction is reproduced exactly. Its source differences are listed below; reproducing it does not authenticate its conjectural repairs.

| Source index (zero based) | Literal source | Published layer |
|---:|---|---|
| 110 | `F` | `?` |

[Source image](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p187_supplementary.png) · [Full certificate and attribution](../../data/supplementary_readings.json).

The first publication of these particular body readings is credited as reported by the contributor. Earlier wartime or unpublished decipherment has not been excluded.

## Exact same-length repair account

The later [aviation source package](../../experiments/aviation_connection/README.md)
adds an exact cost for the readable instruction. It preserves the earlier
Ayush Agarwal body credit and the already reviewed literal source. Four
known-coordinate substitutions produce the following 67-character edition:

<details>
<summary>Earlier attributed reading</summary>

**Earlier attributed reading — Ayush Agarwal body with the later exact four-edit account:**

```text
BITTEXSOFORTXBESCHEIDXOBXVERBINDUNGXMITXARMEEXMAKENSENXEINWANDFREIX
```

</details>

| Source coordinate, one-based | Literal | Proposed | Consequence |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 62 | X | D | BE?CHEID becomes BESCHEID |
| 86 | A | X | EINWA?DFREI becomes EINWANDFREI |
| 124 | V | F | VERPINDUNG becomes VERBINDUNG |
| 125 | F | V | MIS becomes MIT |

There are no source erasures or inserted coordinates. The two raw question
marks represent unassigned square cells; their coordinates are repaired to
the existing S and N cells, without assigning duplicate letters to the key.
The spelling `MAKENSEN` is retained in this exact-length edition. Full
reencryption reproduces the four-change ciphertext. These costs are the new
audit contribution, not a new discovery of the message's meaning.

The neighboring [p187 D1 aircraft message](../other/p187_D.md) also concerns
Mackensen's connection. The printed times do not establish a chronological
request/reply relationship.

```sh
python experiments/aviation_connection/verify_companion.py --verify
```

# p89 A2 — ship-routing clause completed conditionally

[Case index](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Original reading:** [Ayush Agarwal (@AyushAg1002), 2026-10-28](https://github.com/dbourdeau/cyphersolver/issues/181), with review by **D. Bourdeau**. **Source, arithmetic and conditional completion:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. This source belongs to the wider Childs corpus, outside the original 22-entry challenge.

This continuation concerns port capacity and the routing of ships to
Nikolayev. The native source fixes **142 of 145 positions**. The proposed
words **`WELCHE SCHIFFE`** complete the three gaps with **three source-mask
fills and no observed-coordinate substitutions**. The historical meaning
and the phrase had already been proposed; the current contribution is their
explicit source-coordinate certificate and independent word support.

## Readable message

**Readable German — conditional fills in brackets; punctuation editorial:**

> … aufnahmefähig, Nikolajew. Auf Wunsch EZ Kiew bestimmt Hptm. Joel,
> V. O. FECH, Odessa, [w]elche S[c]hi[f]fe etwa wegen Eisenbahnlage nach
> Nikolajew zugehen haben.

The [preceding part](../military/black_sea_evacuation_routes.md#p88-c1)
orders traffic other than *Siegfried* to Odessa and ends with “and if this
is no longer …”. The opening here supplies “able to receive [it],
Nikolayev”. The following clause puts the selection of ships, taking the
railway situation into account, with Captain Joel in Odessa. This sentence
division reads `BESTIMMT HPTM JOEL` as verb and subject; it does not add a
missing verb or title. The abbreviation `EZ` and office string `V O FECH`
remain literal. The earlier readable interpretation used **Ex.** for `EZ`;
that was editorial display, not a priced `Z→X` coordinate repair.

## Exact completion and its limits

The original source separately labels **`2 TL RICHI-290`**. Its header is:
